abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-yas-island.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Diploma Programme as a syllabus, not as a subject label. Each works from the current course guide, the published assessment outlines and the student's own marked work, and each session is delivered live over video to Yas Island.

intro.heading: What a Yas Island family is really asking for
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor in Yas Island looks like a logistics question and almost never is. Yas Island households sit between West Yas Academy on the island itself and the Diploma cohorts at Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and Repton School Abu Dhabi a short drive away, with Raha International School pulling students from the Al Raha corridor. A parent on Yas Acres who types that phrase has usually just read a report card with a 4 in Chemistry HL and a comment about data analysis, and wants someone who can say precisely what a 4 in Chemistry HL is made of.

That is a syllabus question. The Diploma is unusual among school qualifications because so much of the grade is specified in public documents: the number of papers, the minutes, the percentage each component carries, the criteria letters an internal assessment is marked against and the mark total under each letter. A tutor who knows those documents can look at a student's last three pieces of work and name the component that is costing the grade. A tutor who does not is guessing, however pleasant the hour is.

The honest position on delivery is this. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Teaching for Yas Island is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own scanned work on screen and the session timed to Gulf Standard Time. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature. It is the condition that makes subject specialism possible at all, because the pool of people who have taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to examination standard is small and is not distributed according to who happens to live within twenty minutes of Yas Mall.

What follows is built around the syllabus rather than around the neighbourhood. You will find the components and weightings for the courses Yas Island students most often need, the places marks are lost in each one, the criteria letters an internal assessment is judged under, and what a tutor is and is not permitted to do with a piece of assessed work. Market rates are quoted with their source so you can sanity-check any quote you receive, including ours.

If your child is in DP1 the useful work is different from DP2, and the page says so. DP1 is where a weak internal assessment topic is cheap to fix and expensive to leave; DP2 is where past-paper technique and command-term discipline move a grade. Either way the first session is diagnostic, free, and ends with a written note of what we think is actually wrong. A DP1 note usually lists two or three fixable things; a DP2 note is shorter and blunter, because there is less time to spend on anything that is not costing marks.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-yas-island.programmesIntro: Yas Island students arrive at the Diploma from several directions: the Middle Years Programme, a British Year 11, or an American high school transfer. Each route leaves a different gap, and the programme notes below describe what tutoring usually has to repair in each case.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units and inquiry rather than a fixed subject syllabus, so there is no public paper or weighting to revise towards. Tutoring at this stage is about securing number fluency, reading stamina and written structure, because those three are what the Middle Years Programme will later assume without teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Yas Island primary families tend to come to us for English reading age and times-table automaticity, not for PYP content. The practical worry is that an inquiry report can look polished while arithmetic underneath it is slow. We test calculation speed directly in the first session and tell you plainly whether there is a gap worth paying to close.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, each marked out of 8, and reported on a 1-7 scale derived from criterion totals rather than from an examination percentage. Students often collect strong criterion A marks and weak criterion C or D marks for years without anyone naming the pattern, which is exactly the pattern that later limits a Diploma grade.
programmes.countryNote: Yas Island students coming out of MYP into DP most often struggle with the move from criterion marking to component weighting. A student used to being marked out of 8 on four separate axes suddenly sits a paper worth 40% of a grade. We spend the first weeks of DP1 teaching what a mark scheme looks like and how a question is read.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component and externally assessed papers with published weightings, and the Diploma total runs to 45 points including up to 3 from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: This is the bulk of the Yas Island work. Higher Level Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics AA and Economics are the courses parents here ask about most, and the request usually arrives in DP1 term two or in the eight weeks before mocks. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, which sets the whole working backwards plan.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement and a language development portfolio. It is far less common in the UAE than the full Diploma, and the assessment load sits differently: the career-related element is moderated by the provider rather than examined by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Few Yas Island students are on the CP, but those who are often need help on exactly the DP courses they have taken alongside it, plus structure for the reflective project. We treat the DP courses with the same component-by-component approach used for a full Diploma candidate.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-yas-island.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Yas Island families ask for by name, with what each one actually assesses and the place marks most often disappear. The level column matters: Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework, it is additional syllabus and, in several subjects, an additional paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Externally assessed papers plus the scientific investigation. Marks are lost on the data-based questions where units, significant figures and uncertainty propagation are treated as decoration, and on organic mechanisms drawn without curly arrows showing electron movement.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The HL syllabus adds depth across fields, induction and quantum phenomena. The recurring failure is not conceptual but procedural: candidates do not state the model they are applying, so the examiner cannot award method marks for a line of working that happens to reach the right number.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the obvious problem and command-term discipline is the real one. Outline, explain, distinguish and suggest ask for different things and carry different mark allocations, and a student who writes one long paragraph for all four loses marks they know the content for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the HL grade. Students lose marks by abandoning working once they reach an answer, and by treating the graphical display calculator as a substitute for the analytic method the question is testing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. The common error is reporting a statistical output without interpreting it in the context of the question, which is where the interpretation marks sit rather than in the calculation itself.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, not illustrative. An axis left unlabelled or a shift drawn without an arrow costs marks on Paper 1 and Paper 2, and the HL Paper 3 quantitative work needs practised arithmetic under time pressure rather than theory revision.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis and the comparative essay reward argument structure. The weakest scripts summarise the text; the strongest make a claim about how meaning is constructed and prove it with short, precisely chosen quotation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is where marks live: a student who recalls a framework but cannot apply it to the stimulus material stalls in the middle bands. HL adds depth on operations and organisational change, and the research project needs a focused question early.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper work rewards precise pseudocode and correct trace tables, and the solution development component rewards documented testing. Students usually arrive strong on code and weak on the written justification the criteria actually reward.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for a claim, not recited. Marks are lost when a candidate describes a study accurately and never links it back to the question's command term, and HL adds the extensions and additional approaches to behaviour.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-yas-island.regionsIntro: Yas Island sits inside a cluster of Abu Dhabi communities whose students share schools, exam sessions and traffic. Because teaching is delivered over video the geography does not restrict who can teach your child, but it does shape when a session can start.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Yas Acres and the Yas Island residential districts feed West Yas Academy on the island and send Diploma students across the bridge to Saadiyat and the Al Raha corridor. Sessions here usually begin between 16:30 and 18:00.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Home to Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and a short drive from Yas. Families frequently have one child at a Saadiyat school and another on the island, which is why sibling scheduling comes up so often in this cluster.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Repton School Abu Dhabi draws Diploma students from Al Reem and the city. Apartment living here makes a quiet room at 17:00 harder to find than on Yas Acres, so headphones and a fixed desk matter more.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Al Bandar and Al Zeina residents sit between the airport road and the island. Raha International School's IB continuum is the nearest full PYP to DP route, and several Yas families chose it over an island school.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities with a long school-bus run to island schools. A student living here and schooled on Yas can be home as late as 16:45, which pushes realistic session starts towards 17:30.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Al Bateen Academy and the American Community School of Abu Dhabi sit on the older part of the island city. The drive from Yas at 16:00 is the reason very few Yas families use a tutor based here in person.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland community with a mixed school pattern across British, Indian and IB provision. Diploma students here often share a tutor slot with a sibling sitting IGCSE, which the online format makes straightforward.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Close to the airport and a straightforward run to Yas and Al Raha schools. Session timing is rarely the constraint here; subject availability is, which is why specialist coverage rather than proximity is the question that matters.

schoolClusters.city: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
schoolClusters.note: The island schools closest to Yas Acres, plus the Saadiyat Diploma cohorts most Yas families consider. Between them they cover American, British and IB routes, which is why a single household can need two different mark-scheme literacies in the same week.

sections.heading: What "IB home tutor in Yas Island" buys, in plain terms
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Yas Island, as the phrase is used in Abu Dhabi, means private one-to-one Diploma teaching arranged outside school for a student living on the island. The market splits into two models: a tutor who drives to the villa, and a tutor who teaches live over video. IB Gram sells the second. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at a Yas Acres address.

That distinction decides what you can buy. A tutor who drives is drawn from the set of people who will accept a round trip across the Sheikh Khalifa bridge in late-afternoon traffic for a single hour. That set is small, and it is not selected for having taught Chemistry Higher Level. A tutor who teaches over video is drawn from everyone qualified to teach the course, which is the whole point. For a Standard Level subject with a broad teacher pool the difference is modest. For Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Physics HL, it is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

The second thing the phrase buys is a different relationship with the student's own marked work. A private hour is the only place a student's last paper gets read closely by someone who knows the mark scheme. School marking is honest but fast; thirty scripts do not permit a line-by-line reconciliation of what was awarded against what could have been. One-to-one does, and that reconciliation is where most of the available grade movement sits in DP2.

What it does not buy is content delivery that duplicates the school. If a tutor spends the hour re-teaching the lesson your child already sat through, you are paying twice for the same material. The useful hour starts from evidence: a marked paper, a returned internal assessment draft, a topic test. If a prospective tutor does not ask for any of that before the first session, that tells you most of what you need to know.

The student's own marked work is the raw material for the session

sections.heading: Diploma components and weightings, course by course
paragraphs: The Diploma publishes how each grade is built. That is the single most useful fact available to a parent, and almost no tutoring page in this market uses it. Below is the shape of assessment for the courses Yas Island students most often need help with: what is externally examined, what is internally assessed, and roughly where the weight sits. Exact percentages are set in each subject's current guide and are revised between syllabus cycles, so treat the table as the structure and confirm the current figures with your child's subject teacher or the course guide the school works from.

Reading it changes how an hour gets spent. A student with a weak internal assessment in a subject where the internal component carries about a fifth of the grade has roughly one grade boundary of recoverable ground sitting in a document they control, on their own timetable, with no examination pressure. A student with strong internal marks and weak paper technique has the opposite problem and needs timed practice rather than coursework help. These two students look identical on a report card and need completely different tutoring.

The second use of the table is choosing which subject to fund. Families commonly buy tutoring for the subject with the lowest grade. Sometimes that is right. Often the better purchase is the subject where a single component is dragging an otherwise solid profile, because the gap between the current mark and the next band is narrower and the route to it is specified. We say which we think it is at the end of the free trial, in writing, and sometimes that answer is that the subject you asked about is not the one to buy.

sections.heading: The criteria letters your child is actually marked against
paragraphs: Every internally assessed Diploma component is marked against lettered criteria with a published mark allocation under each. A parent who knows the letters can read a returned draft and see where the marks went. A parent who does not is left with a number and a comment. This section is the one almost no competing page in Abu Dhabi carries, and it is the cheapest grade movement available in DP1.

The mechanism is the same across subjects even though the letters differ. The marker reads the work once for each criterion, places it in a band for that criterion alone, and totals. A student can therefore write something articulate and well-presented and still score poorly, because presentation is not a criterion. Equally, a student can score well with plain prose if the analysis criterion is satisfied. Teaching to the criteria is not gaming the system; it is reading the instructions the IB published.

The practical sequence we use is straightforward. The student brings whatever exists, however rough. The tutor reads it against the criteria, writes one sentence per criterion naming the current band and one sentence naming what the next band requires, and sends that to the student. The student rewrites. The tutor reads again. At no point does the tutor write, redraft or complete any part of the work, and both student and parent are told that in the first session. That line is not a disclaimer; it is what distinguishes legitimate support from the completed-coursework sellers who also rank for these searches.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, by subject group
paragraphs: Report cards describe symptoms. A 4 in Physics HL is a symptom; the cause is usually one of a small number of specific, diagnosable habits. After enough one-to-one hours the same causes recur, and naming them is faster than another term of general revision.

In the sciences the dominant cause is procedural rather than conceptual. Students who understand the physics lose marks because they do not write down the model they are using, do not quote an uncertainty, or round through a calculation and arrive at a number that cannot be awarded. The fix is mechanical and fast: a fixed layout for a calculation, a habit of stating assumptions, and ten marked data questions. Most of the recoverable marks in Chemistry and Physics sit here, not in the content.

In mathematics the dominant cause is the abandoned method. A question worth six marks is not asking for a number; it is asking for a sequence of justified steps, most of which carry marks whether or not the final line is right. Students trained on single-answer platforms stop writing once they see the answer and hand back two marks out of six. In the essay subjects the dominant cause is the command term: outline, explain, discuss, evaluate and justify each carry a different expectation and a different mark ceiling, and a student who writes the same shape of answer for all of them is capped regardless of knowledge. These are the three diagnoses we expect to make, and the first session says which one applies.
bullets: Sciences: unstated models, missing uncertainties, premature rounding
Mathematics: working abandoned once an answer appears
Essay subjects: one answer shape used for every command term
All subjects: time allocated by question length rather than by marks available

sections.heading: Online teaching versus an in-home tutor for a Yas Island household
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search implies, so here it is directly. An in-home tutor in Abu Dhabi is quoted across a wide band because the quote includes travel: published market figures put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, while qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300 and budget online providers advertise from as little as AED 33 to 65. Those are market figures from the providers themselves, not IB Gram's prices.

The money is the smaller half of the comparison. The larger half is who is in the pool. A Yas Island family hiring in person is choosing from tutors willing to make the crossing at 17:00; a family hiring online is choosing from everyone who can teach the course. For Mathematics AA at Higher Level, or Chemistry HL, or Economics HL Paper 3 work, that difference decides whether the hour is taught by a specialist or by a competent generalist. There is also a time arithmetic nobody quotes: a tutor spending ninety minutes travelling for a sixty-minute lesson has to price that time somewhere, and it is in your rate.

The honest case against online is narrow but real. A student who will not sit at a desk without an adult physically present, or who needs handwriting and physical equipment supervised, is better served in a room. For Diploma work, where the material is mostly reading, writing, calculation and marked scripts on a screen, the room adds little that a shared whiteboard and a document camera do not. We say so plainly, and if we think your child is the exception we tell you that instead of selling you sessions.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a Diploma tutor cannot cross
paragraphs: The Diploma is unforgiving about authorship. A student signs a declaration that submitted work is their own, and a breach is handled as malpractice with consequences that can reach the award of the Diploma itself. That is why this section exists on a tutoring page: some of what ranks for Abu Dhabi IB searches is sold by operators who will produce an internal assessment or an Extended Essay for a fee. One such operator advertises completed internal assessments outright. Buying that is not a shortcut; it is a risk taken entirely by the student.

The legitimate boundary is clear enough to state in a sentence. A tutor may teach the subject, explain the criteria, read a draft and say what band each criterion sits in, model a technique on a different example, and ask the questions that make a student find their own weakness. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure, proofread to completion or supply content for anything that will be submitted. IB Gram tutors work inside that boundary, and the first internal assessment session includes a short, explicit conversation with student and parent about where it sits.

There is a related point about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB and to the examination boards. We reference them and point you to the official source; we do not host or supply them. If a tutoring service offers you a library of downloaded mark schemes, that is a copyright question at best and, for unreleased material, a malpractice question. Ask where it came from.

sections.heading: Moving from MYP or Year 11 into DP1 on Yas Island
paragraphs: Two transitions dominate the Yas Island caseload. The first is MYP to DP, where a student used to four criteria marked out of eight meets components weighted as percentages of a final grade. The second is a British Year 11 into DP1, where a student used to IGCSE's tight, predictable question styles meets papers that ask for synthesis and extended argument. Both transitions are survivable and both reliably cost a grade in term one if nobody names what changed.

For the MYP student the change is in what counts as evidence. MYP criterion C or D rewards a process shown; a Diploma paper rewards an answer constructed to a command term under time. The same student who writes beautifully reflective MYP work can produce a thin Paper 2 because nobody taught them the shape of an examination answer. Four or five sessions of nothing but past-paper structure in DP1 term one is usually enough, and it is far cheaper than repairing it in DP2.

For the Year 11 student the change is in breadth of required reading and in the internal assessment. IGCSE coursework, where it exists, is tightly specified; a Diploma internal assessment asks the student to choose a question and defend the choice. Students fresh from IGCSE routinely pick a topic that cannot reach the top bands, then spend a term on it. Checking the topic before the work starts is twenty minutes that saves a grade. It is also the single most useful thing a Yas Island DP1 parent can buy in term one.
bullets: MYP to DP: learn the shape of an examination answer early in DP1
IGCSE to DP: check internal assessment topic viability before any writing
American transfer: expect the written paper load to be the shock, not the content
Term one is where a transition gap is cheap; DP2 is where it is expensive

sections.heading: Starting with a Yas Island family, and what we tell you if we cannot help
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the course, the level, the school and what the last marked piece of work said. We look at what the student actually produced rather than at the grade. A trial lesson is arranged in the slot you want to keep, free, with no card details taken. The tutor teaches for that hour and writes you a note afterwards naming the component we think is costing marks and what a term of work would target.

Where a specialist is not immediately free we say so rather than filling the slot. The courses where Abu Dhabi coverage is tightest are the ones you would expect: Higher Level Mathematics AA, Higher Level Physics, Computer Science and the less common language A options. For those the realistic answer is sometimes a wait of a few days, and sometimes a tutor based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which we disclose before you agree rather than after. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why we do.

After that it is ordinary weekly work: same tutor, same slot, one marked piece between sessions, notes to the parent. You can stop whenever you like. Sessions move in mock weeks and shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan on request. If after three or four sessions the match is not working, we change the tutor without an argument and without charging for the handover, because the alternative is a family paying for an hour nobody looks forward to.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked work between
process.description: Same tutor, same slot. One piece of the student's own work is marked between sessions and the next session opens with that marking. Parent notes after each lesson, slots moved for mocks, and Ramadan timings shifted on request.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course and level
whyPoints.description: Higher Level is a different syllabus, not more of the Standard Level one. Our matching treats it that way, so a request for Mathematics AA HL does not get answered with a general maths tutor who is strong to IGCSE and improvising above it.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus documents, used openly
whyPoints.description: Sessions work from the current course guide and the published assessment outline for the subject, and we point you to the official source rather than hosting board-owned material. You can check anything we tell you against the document the school works from.

whyPoints.title: Criterion coaching, never ghostwriting
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment support is feedback against lettered criteria on the student's own draft. Nobody writes, rewrites or proofreads to completion. That boundary is stated to the student in the first session, because the student is the one who signs the authenticity declaration.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated honestly
whyPoints.description: Teaching into Yas Island is live one-to-one video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. You will not find a page on this site implying otherwise, which is more than can be said for several rate-comparison sites in this market.

whyPoints.title: Market rates quoted with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to a published market source and dated, so you can test any quote you receive against it. We do not present market figures as our own price list, and we do not publish a rate we have not sourced.

whyPoints.title: Coverage gaps disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level course we tell you the wait, or tell you the tutor would be teaching from outside the UAE into Gulf Standard Time. You get that before you commit rather than discovering it in week three.

faqs.question: Can an IB home tutor actually visit our villa on Yas Island?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service offered only in India; teaching for Yas Island is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Independent tutors in Abu Dhabi do make house calls, and published market figures put those visits at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour with independents quoted higher. If physical presence is the deciding factor for your child, hire locally with open eyes. If subject specialism matters more, the online pool is much larger, because it is not limited to people willing to cross onto the island at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Which Diploma courses do Yas Island parents most often ask us about?
faqs.answer: Chemistry at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at both levels, and Economics including the Higher Level quantitative paper. English A: Language and Literature comes up for the comparative essay rather than for comprehension. The pattern is consistent: parents ask about the subjects where a single examined component carries a lot of weight and where the school cannot give a student much individual attention on marked scripts. Those are also the subjects where one-to-one work on a marked paper moves a grade fastest, which is why they dominate the caseload here.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's problem is content or technique?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked paper rather than at the grade. If marks were lost on questions whose topics the student can explain aloud, the problem is technique: command terms read wrongly, working abandoned, time allocated by question length rather than marks. If the student cannot explain the topic at all, it is content. The two need different hours and different money. Our free trial exists mainly to answer this question, and the written note afterwards says which it is. Buying content revision for a technique problem is the most common way families waste a term.

faqs.question: What exactly is a tutor allowed to do with my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the subject, explain the lettered criteria, say which band a draft currently sits in, explain what the next band requires, and model technique on different material. Nothing more. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or proofread to completion any part of what is submitted, because the student signs a declaration that the work is their own and a breach is handled as malpractice. Some operators ranking for Abu Dhabi IB searches sell completed internal assessments. That is a risk carried entirely by the student, and it is not a service we provide at any price.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level really harder, or just more work than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is additional syllabus, not additional homework. Higher Level courses carry extra content, and in several subjects an extra examined paper, and the questions reach further into synthesis. Economics HL adds a quantitative paper; Mathematics AA HL adds proof and deeper calculus; the sciences add topics and more demanding data work. This matters when choosing a tutor, because someone comfortable to Standard Level may be improvising above it. Ask any prospective tutor which Higher Level topics they have taught to examination standard, and listen for specifics rather than reassurance.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and nothing is urgent yet. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: DP1 is where the cheap work is. Internal assessment topic choice, the shape of an examination answer and command-term discipline all cost a few sessions in DP1 and cost a grade to repair in DP2. The most valuable twenty minutes a DP1 parent can buy is a viability check on an internal assessment topic before a term is spent on it, because a topic that cannot reach the top bands caps the mark regardless of effort. Waiting until mocks is common and it is the expensive choice. We would rather sell you four sessions now than twenty in February.

faqs.question: Who regulates the schools my child might move between in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Dubai schools answer to KHDA instead, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. That matters if you move within the country, because inspection frameworks and reporting differ by emirate. ADEK is named by almost none of the tutoring sites competing for these searches, which tells you something about how locally written those pages are.

faqs.question: Are the tutors legally permitted to give private lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. Ask any prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, and apply through MoHRE's own channels rather than an intermediary.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's own Yas Island school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Not in Abu Dhabi, and you should be cautious of any service that offers it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat this as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy if the situation affects you directly. The practical point is simple: a marketing pitch built on your child's own teacher privately is a pitch to breach a rule.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a struggling Higher Level student need?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the normal starting point and is enough when the problem is technique, because the work between sessions does most of the lifting. Two a week makes sense in a defined push: the eight weeks before mocks, or a Higher Level subject where content gaps go back a year. Three is usually a sign that something structural is wrong, such as too many Higher Levels or a subject choice that needs revisiting with the school. We would rather tell you that than sell you the third hour.

faqs.question: Does the May session or the November session apply to Yas Island students?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session, which sets the backwards plan for the whole two years. Published IB session dates should be confirmed with your child's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one; we deliberately do not print a date we have not read at source. The useful planning point is not the date anyway, it is that school internal deadlines for coursework sit months earlier than anything the IB publishes, and those are the deadlines that actually bite.

faqs.question: How does a live video lesson handle maths working and lab diagrams?
faqs.answer: A shared whiteboard both people can write on, plus the student's own scanned or photographed work on screen for annotation. For mathematics the tutor writes the working out line by line as a teacher would at a desk, which is the point: the student watches a method being constructed, not a finished answer. For a scientific investigation the tutor reads the student's own data table and graph and marks the uncertainty treatment on screen. Nothing about reading a marked script, annotating it and discussing it requires sitting in the same room.

faqs.question: What should I send before the first lesson to make it useful?
faqs.answer: The course and level, the school, the most recent marked paper or topic test, and any returned internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments. If there is a predicted grade, send that too. What we do not need is a long account of the problem: the marked script says it faster and more accurately. Twenty minutes of preparation on your side turns a diagnostic trial lesson into a specific plan rather than a pleasant conversation. Families who send the script get a better written note afterwards, every time.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's Higher Level subject on Yas Island?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a realistic wait, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. Coverage is tightest on Mathematics AA at Higher Level, Physics HL, Computer Science and the less common language A options. Sometimes the answer is a few days; sometimes it is a tutor based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which we disclose before you agree. No competing page in this market publishes a coverage limit, and the reason we do is that discovering it in week three is worse for you than hearing it now.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two Higher Level subjects for the same Yas Island student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but not at the cost of specialism. Mathematics and Physics overlap enough that one person often teaches both well. Chemistry and Biology are taught by the same person less often than parents expect, because the Higher Level content diverges sharply. Where a single tutor can genuinely cover two courses the scheduling is simpler and the student builds one working relationship. Where they cannot, two specialists beat one generalist, and we will say which situation we think you are in.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-yas-island.closingHeading: Start with one marked script and a free hour
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-in-yas-island.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Yas Island, begin with the evidence rather than the logistics. Send us the course, the level, the school and the last marked piece of work, and book a free trial lesson in the slot you actually want to keep. The tutor teaches that hour and writes you a short note naming the component costing marks and what a term of work would target. Teaching is live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time; nobody arrives at a Yas Acres address. If we do not have the right specialist free, we will tell you that too.

intro.heading: What parents are really buying when they ask for a home tutor
paragraphs: Ask an Abu Dhabi parent why they want a home tutor rather than an online one and the answer is almost never about pedagogy. It is about being able to see what is happening. A tutor at the dining table can be overheard. You can tell whether the hour was work or conversation. You can ask on the way out whether the Chemistry is actually improving. That instinct is sound: tutoring is one of the few significant purchases a family makes where the product is invisible and the result arrives months later.

The problem is that presence is a poor proxy for progress. A tutor in your house for ninety minutes a week can produce nothing you could show a subject teacher, and a tutor on a screen can produce a marked script, an annotated internal assessment draft and a six-week error log that any teacher would recognise immediately. The question worth asking a provider is not where the tutor sits. It is: at the end of six weeks, what documents will exist that did not exist before, and what will they show?

That is the question this page answers, and it answers it with the specifics of the Diploma rather than in general terms. A DP student is assessed on written papers at the end of DP2 and on eight or nine pieces of internal coursework spread across two years. Each of those has criteria with fixed mark allocations - the sciences investigation carries twenty-four marks across four criteria of six, the Extended Essay carries thirty-four with twelve of them in critical thinking alone, the mathematics exploration carries twenty with six for use of mathematics. Evidence of progress in the IB means movement against those specific numbers, not a general sense that things are going better.

Abu Dhabi families also have a scheduling reality that changes the maths. Private schools in the emirate, overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, release students between about half past two and half past three. In the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor the drive home is short. From Al Reef, Al Samha or Al Shamkha it is frequently forty minutes or more. An in-home tutor has to cross that same city, which is why the market prices in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and why in-home work is commonly sold in two-hour blocks that make the journey worthwhile.

So the honest position, stated before anything else: IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi, and in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For Abu Dhabi families, sessions run one-to-one over live video, and the accountability that a parent wanted from presence is supplied in writing instead. What follows is the detail of that - how to read a marked DP script, what an error log looks like after six weeks, how internal assessment drafts are commented on without crossing the academic-honesty line, and what can and cannot honestly be said about grade movement.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage of the IB, because the assessment looks different. A Primary Years student produces no marks at all; a Diploma student produces a marking record in nine places at once. Here is what progress can actually be shown as, programme by programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is marked against four criteria on an eight-point scale and converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. The evidence to ask for at this stage is a piece of the student's own work scored against the school's published descriptors, with the gap between the current band and the next one named in words. Movement from a 5 to a 6 in criterion C is a documentable change; "more confident" is not.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 generate most of our Abu Dhabi evidence requests, because that is where criteria marking starts deciding grades and where the personal project lands. Families in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor often arrive with a report showing four different criteria scores and no explanation of what any of them mean, which is itself the first piece of work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment worth a fifth to a third of the grade, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Evidence here is concrete: marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme beside them, drafts annotated by criterion, and a comparison between a mock script and the work produced eight weeks later on the same paper type.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session, and the school's mock window usually falls between December and February of DP2. That mock is the most valuable evidence document the student will produce before the real papers, and it is the one most families never fully read. Confirm examination and results dates with the school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external assessment, so there is no mark to track. Evidence at this stage is fluency measured directly: reading accuracy and rate on an unseen passage, number facts recalled under time, a piece of writing with its structure marked. Any provider offering exam preparation to a PYP student has misread the programme.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries in Abu Dhabi cluster in the newer mainland communities, where adding a second car journey to the afternoon is the thing families most want to avoid. Two short sessions a week produce more measurable fluency gain than one long one, and that pattern is only practical when nobody is driving.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: The grid below names, for each subject, the document that shows whether tutoring is working. It is deliberately component-level: the point of hiring a specialist is that they can tell you which eleven marks are missing and from where.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Evidence is a timed Paper 3 attempt with the method marked rather than the answer. The diagnostic signature is a student who scores well on part (a) and loses everything after it, which shows up as a mark distribution rather than as a total.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Evidence is an interpretation sentence written next to a correct calculation. The common pattern is full method marks and zero context marks, visible only when somebody reads the script against the mark scheme line by line.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Evidence is a Paper 2 extended-response answer rewritten against the command term, with the original kept for comparison. Describe-instead-of-explain is the single most common cause of lost marks and the easiest to document.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Evidence is a set of mechanism drawings with charges and lone pairs marked, and energetics cycles with the sign convention checked. Both are visual, both are gradeable, and both change within weeks when corrected consistently.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Evidence is a criterion A justification for the scientific investigation, before and after. Research design described but not justified is the most frequent cap on the 24-mark total, and the rewrite is a one-page document you can read yourself.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evidence is an evaluation paragraph added to an otherwise complete Paper 3 answer. Students reliably produce the calculation and stop, and the added paragraph is where the top band becomes reachable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Evidence is an annotated unseen text next to the essay it produced. The failure is writing about content rather than the writer's construction, and an annotation protocol makes the change visible on the page.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Evidence is a Paper 1 four-part answer with a mark-per-minute budget written on it. Overwriting part (a) and underwriting part (d) is a timing fault, and the proof it has been fixed is on the clock, not in the content.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Evidence is the justification of the statistical test in the internal assessment, which is marked on method rather than on results. A tidy experiment with a weak justification scores poorly and the rewrite is short.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Evidence is design documentation for the developed solution, which is where marks sit. Students build something functional and under-record the decisions the criteria reward, and the fix is written rather than coded.

sections.heading: The honest answer on home tutors in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: In-home tuition in the UAE is a real market with real prices, and anyone comparing options deserves the numbers rather than a redirection. The published bands for 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel included: Bestimate's rate table shows 180-350, and independent home tutors advertise between 200 and 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270.

Three things sit inside the in-home premium. Travel is the obvious one: a tutor crossing Abu Dhabi to reach Al Reef or Al Shamkha at the afternoon peak spends forty to eighty minutes in a car per visit, and that time is in the fee whether it is itemised or not. The two-hour minimum is the second, which is why in-home work is sold in blocks rather than as single focused hours. The third is scarcity pricing: inside a twenty-minute radius of any Abu Dhabi community, the number of tutors who teach a specific subject at a specific level is small, and small supply prices accordingly.

How families actually choose, in our experience, splits cleanly by what the tutoring is for. For a younger child who needs supervision and company while working, presence genuinely helps and the premium is defensible. For a Diploma student losing marks on a named component, presence does nothing that a shared screen does not do better, because the work being examined is a script and the thing being corrected is a method. The fastest way to decide is to look at the most recent marked paper: if you can see which component the marks came out of, you need a specialist. If you cannot, you may just need someone in the room to stop the phone being picked up.

IB Gram's own position is fixed and stated before any comparison: we do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi, and in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For Abu Dhabi families everything is one-to-one over live video. The table below is the comparison we give parents rather than a pitch, and the row that matters most is the last one.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Diploma script
paragraphs: Most families receive marked work and read only the total. The total is the least informative thing on the page. What matters is the distribution: which questions produced full marks, which produced method marks without answer marks, and which produced nothing. Those three patterns have different causes and different fixes, and a tutor who cannot name which one is happening is guessing.

Full marks on short questions and zeros on extended response is almost always a command-term problem rather than a knowledge problem. The student knows the content, answers in the wrong register, and the examiner has nowhere to award. Method marks without answer marks is an accuracy or units problem, often significant figures or a sign. Nothing at all on the later parts of a multi-part question is usually timing or a misread stem, and it shows up most clearly in Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, where two extended problems reward reading the whole question before starting.

The annotations themselves carry information that parents are rarely shown how to read. A tick on a working line is a method mark awarded for the approach. A mark on the answer line only is an accuracy credit. "BOD" style benefit-of-the-doubt annotations mean a borderline answer was accepted and would probably not be accepted twice. A circled command term in the question margin means the examiner is signalling the answer did not engage with the verb. None of this is secret - it is in the mark schemes the boards publish - but it is not taught to families.

This is work that is done better on a shared screen than across a table, which is worth saying plainly because it runs against the instinct this page started with. On a screen the script is scanned, enlarged, annotated by both people and saved. Six weeks later the same question type can be put next to the first attempt. In a living room, the paper goes back in the bag.

Topic repair first; technique work is wasted until the content exists

sections.heading: What six weeks of evidence looks like
paragraphs: Six weeks is the review period we set, and it is chosen because it is long enough for a pattern to appear in fresh marked work and short enough that a plan which is not working gets changed before a term is gone. The point of fixing it in advance is that families are reluctant to act on a bad match. They wait, hoping, and in a two-year programme that patience is expensive. A date in the calendar and a document to judge removes the need to have an awkward conversation based on a feeling.

What accumulates over those weeks is deliberately boring. A session note each week, written in sentences a subject teacher would recognise. An error log that carries forward rather than resetting, so that the third occurrence of the same sign-convention mistake is visible as the third occurrence. Two or three marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme beside them. Where the student is working on an internal assessment, a criterion score sheet on their own draft at each stage.

The table below is drawn from the shape of a typical Higher Level Chemistry block, which is the single most requested Higher Level science in Abu Dhabi. The detail will differ by subject. The structure should not: there should be a document at each stage, and by week six there should be a second attempt at the same task type that can be laid next to the first.

One caution about what this evidence can prove. It can show that a specific error has stopped recurring, that a criterion score on a draft has moved, and that a timed attempt now reaches the end of the paper. It cannot promise a final grade, and we do not offer one. The variables between a corrected error log in November and a Diploma grade in July include a school, a cohort, a mock season and an examination the student sits alone.

sections.heading: Internal assessment drafts: criterion letters and the honesty line
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where the largest number of recoverable marks sit and where the largest number of families get help that puts the student at risk. The criteria are public, fixed and specific. The sciences investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each, twenty-four in total, within a three thousand word limit. The mathematics exploration carries twenty marks, six of them for use of mathematics, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. The History investigation is twenty-five marks across identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself and reflection, inside 2,200 words. The Extended Essay carries thirty-four, and critical thinking alone is twelve of them, inside four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is a single ten-mark global judgement inside 1,600 words.

Useful feedback on a draft is a score against each of those letters and a sentence naming the skill the lowest-scoring criterion is asking for. "Criterion D asks you to weigh your limitations against your conclusion; you have listed three limitations without saying which one most affects your result" is teaching. It gives the student something to do and leaves the doing to them. A document returned with replacement sentences in it is not teaching, and it is not safe.

The IB treats authenticity as a condition of assessment rather than as advice, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student: a subject grade, and in serious cases the Diploma. That is worth stating bluntly in a market where one researched competitor openly advertises completed internal assessments at around AED 3,750 each. A tutor may teach the criterion, model the technique on a different question, read what the student wrote and score it, and check referencing. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into the submission, choose the research question, or hand over finished work in any state.

There is a practical reason beyond the rule. Several components involve the student discussing their own work with a supervisor or in a reflection session. A student who did not produce their own draft cannot talk about it, and the gap is obvious to anyone who has sat through one of those conversations.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what can be claimed and what cannot
paragraphs: This section exists because the market is full of grade promises and families deserve a clear statement of what is actually knowable. No tutor can promise a specific Diploma grade, a specific point total or a specific improvement, and any page that does is telling you about its marketing. The IB grade is produced by an examination the student sits alone, marked externally, against boundaries set after the session. Several large variables sit outside any tutor's reach.

What can be honestly described is intermediate and documented. A named error can be shown to have stopped recurring in the error log. A criterion score on a draft can be shown to have moved from one band to another, against the published descriptors. A timed attempt that previously stopped two thirds of the way through a paper can be shown reaching the end. A mark distribution can be shown shifting from zeros on extended response to partial credit. These are real, checkable changes and they are the mechanism by which grades move, but they are not the grade.

The second honest caveat is about timing. The amount of change available depends heavily on when the work starts. A student beginning in October of DP1 has access to content repair, internal assessment process and two mock seasons. A student beginning in March of DP2 has access to paper technique on a narrow set of components and little else, because the internal assessments are submitted and the content window has closed. Both are worth doing; they are not the same purchase, and a provider who prices and describes them identically is being unhelpful.

The third is about attribution. If a grade does move, nobody can cleanly say how much of it was the tutoring, the school, the student's own work or the cohort. We write session notes so a family can see what was taught and what changed in the evidence, and we leave the causal claim alone. That is less satisfying than a percentage, and it is the only version that survives scrutiny.
bullets: A documented change: this error stopped recurring, in this log, over these weeks

A documented change: this timed attempt now reaches the end of the paper

sections.heading: The session record, and who gets to see it
paragraphs: A parent who wanted a tutor in the house wanted oversight. The written record is how oversight works when the tutor is on a screen, and it only works if the record says something. A note reading "covered calculus, good progress" is worse than nothing, because it looks like information. A note naming the question attempted, the error that recurred, the correction taught and the practice set for the week is a document a subject teacher can act on.

Who sees it matters as much as what it contains. The parent sees the note. The student sees the note, which is not a formality: a student who reads "sign convention reversed again in question 4b" three weeks running starts checking it themselves, and that is the mechanism by which tutoring eventually stops being needed. Whether the school sees it is the family's decision, not ours, and many families do share the notes with a subject teacher productively.

Record-keeping also touches a legal duty that competitor pages in this market generally ignore. Tutoring enquiries collect personal data about a minor - name, school, year group, marks, sometimes photographs of work. Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs that. A provider should be able to tell you what it collects, why, how long it keeps it and how to have it deleted, and a privacy link should sit on every page. Never hand over a child's school, grades and photograph to a form that does not state its purpose.
Our practical rule is that nothing goes in a record that we would not be comfortable showing the student, the parent and the school simultaneously. That constraint tends to produce better notes.

sections.heading: The tutor at your child's school, and the permit question
paragraphs: Among home tutors near you, the most sought-after is the one who already teaches your child, and it is the one arrangement we will not help with. Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition work permit issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation carries a code of conduct reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Both should be verified against the current policy documents rather than taken from a tutoring page.

The evidence argument against it is simpler than the regulatory one. If the person being paid to improve the work is also the person marking it, the family has lost its only independent reading. A predicted grade cannot be questioned. A draft cannot be criticised freely. The whole purpose of the documents described on this page is to give a parent something an insider has not already shaped.

On permits generally, the position is worth stating because so many pages skip it. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit: it was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or registration from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not claim any. What we can do is explain the rules, show you where to check them, and keep producing documents you can judge us by.

sections.heading: Where the mock paper fits, and why most of them go unread
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts usually sit school mocks between December and February of DP2. By the time the scripts come back the student has moved on, the holidays have intervened, and the paper is filed. That document is the single richest piece of evidence the student will produce before the real examinations, and leaving it unread is the most common avoidable mistake we see in this emirate.

What a properly read mock produces is a ranking. Across six subjects there are a fixed number of marks available in the remaining weeks and they are not evenly distributed. A subject where fifteen marks are being lost to command-term register is a better investment than one where four marks are lost to a genuine content gap in a minor topic, because the first is a technique fix with a short feedback loop. Families almost always rank by anxiety instead, which puts the hours into the subject that feels worst rather than the one with the most recoverable marks.

The second thing a read mock produces is a comparison point. Eight weeks later the same paper type, sat to time and marked, is a measurement rather than an impression. That pair of documents is what we mean by evidence, and it is the thing we would want to see as a parent before paying for a second term.

The practical sequence we recommend is narrow. Read every returned script against the mark scheme with the student present, not alone. Sort the marks lost by cause rather than by topic. Rank the subjects by marks recoverable per hour of work. Set an end date for the block. Then repeat the measurement.

process.title: Send the marked work before the conversation
process.description: A photograph of the most recent marked paper or the returned internal assessment draft, with the teacher's comments visible, is worth more than a half-hour call. A specialist can read it in ten minutes and arrive at the trial lesson with a written hypothesis about which component is leaking marks.

process.title: Agree what will exist in six weeks
process.description: Before paying anything, settle what documents the work will produce: session notes, a carried-forward error log, marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme, and criterion score sheets where coursework is involved. If a provider cannot name the documents, there is nothing to judge them by later.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a working session on the component the script identified, not a sales call. It ends with the tutor stating, in plain words, what the next six weeks would address and in what order. No payment is taken before it happens, and a wrong match is replaced rather than defended.

process.title: Review against new marked work, not impressions
process.description: At six weeks, look at a fresh marked attempt at the same task type as week one. Check the mark distribution rather than the total. If the named error is still recurring, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we expect to reduce hours in some subjects as well as add them.

process.title: Rebuild the plan after the school mocks
process.description: Read every returned script, sort the lost marks by cause, and rank the subjects by marks recoverable rather than by how worrying they feel. The mock is the most informative document of the two years, and the block built on it is the highest-value work available in DP2.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, stated before anything else
whyPoints.description: Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs live over video with one tutor and one student. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. You can then judge the rest of this page knowing exactly what is being sold.

whyPoints.title: Accountability in documents rather than in presence
whyPoints.description: A note after every session, an error log that carries forward, marked past-paper questions with the mark scheme beside them, and criterion score sheets on coursework drafts. These are things a subject teacher can read, which is a higher standard than being overheard in a kitchen.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A Physics specialist who marks Paper 2 extended response and a general science tutor are different people. We match on the component the marked script identifies, because that is the unit in which Diploma marks are actually lost and recovered.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, and a clear statement of why
whyPoints.description: We describe documented changes: an error that stopped recurring, a criterion score that moved band, a timed attempt that now reaches the end of the paper. We do not promise a grade or a point total, because the examination is sat alone and marked against boundaries set after the session.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Tutors score criteria, name the capping skill and teach it. They do not supply prose, choose a research question or submit anything. In a market where completed internal assessments are advertised openly, that boundary is what protects the student from a malpractice finding.

whyPoints.description: Enquiries involve a child's school, year group and marks. Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs that, and a provider should be able to say what it collects, why, how long it keeps it and how to have it removed. Ours is on the privacy page linked from every page.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually come to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs one-to-one over live video, at a time set in Gulf Standard Time around your child's school run. We say this before the comparison rather than after it, because a page that lets you assume otherwise and then explains later has wasted your time. If presence in the room is genuinely the requirement - for a young child who will not work alone - an in-home provider is the right choice and the market rate for it is AED 180-500 an hour.

faqs.question: What does in-home tuition cost per hour here compared with online?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one in this market runs AED 180-500 an hour with travel inside the fee: Bestimate's 2026 table shows 180-350 and independent home tutors advertise 200-500. Monthly in-home packages run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online, a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The gap is largely travel and the two-hour minimum that a journey across the city requires. Our own fee depends on subject, level and session length and is quoted after a consultation.

faqs.question: What evidence will I actually see that my child is improving?
faqs.answer: Four documents. A written note after each session naming the task attempted, the error that recurred, the correction taught and the practice set. An error log that carries forward, so a repeated mistake is visible as a repeat. Marked past-paper questions returned every two or three weeks with the mark scheme beside them. And where coursework is involved, a criterion score sheet on your child's own draft with the gap to the next band written out. By week six there should also be a second attempt at the same task type as week one, which makes the change a measurement rather than an impression.

faqs.question: How often should marked work come back, and marked against what?
faqs.answer: Every two to three weeks is the pattern we aim for, and the marking should be against the published mark scheme for that paper, returned alongside the script rather than summarised. The reason to insist on the mark scheme is that it shows where credit was available and not taken, which is the information you are paying for. A total with a comment is not useful. What you want to be able to see is that four marks were lost to units, six to command-term register and three to an actual content gap, because those three numbers point at three different pieces of work.

faqs.question: What should a good session note say, and what is a bad one?
faqs.answer: A good note names the paper and question attempted, the specific error and whether it has appeared before, the correction in the words used with the student, and the practice set with a time limit. A bad note says "covered calculus, good progress", which looks like information and contains none. The test we apply internally is whether the note could be handed to a subject teacher who would know immediately what was done. We also write notes on the assumption that the student reads them, because a student who sees the same error named three weeks running starts checking for it unprompted.

faqs.question: Can I see the internal assessment feedback my child receives?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be a score sheet rather than an edited document. For the sciences investigation that means a score out of six against each of research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a sentence naming which criterion is capping the mark and what skill it is asking for. For the Extended Essay it means scores against the five criteria, including critical thinking, which carries twelve of the thirty-four marks. What you should not see is a draft with replacement sentences in it. That is not feedback, it is a risk transferred to your child, and the consequences of an authenticity finding fall on them.

faqs.question: How long before a grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: Honestly, it depends on which of the three problems your child has, and the marked script tells you. A command-term register problem on extended response can show measurable change in four to six weeks, because it is a short feedback loop. A timing fault on multi-part questions is similar. A genuine content gap across two topics takes a term, and technique work on top of a content gap is wasted money. We do not promise a final grade at any horizon: the examination is sat alone and marked against boundaries set after the session. What we commit to is a documented change in the evidence at six weeks.

faqs.question: Is online as effective for a child who needs someone watching them work?
faqs.answer: For supervision alone, presence in the room is genuinely better and we would say so. A tutor at the table stops a phone being picked up in a way a screen cannot. What a screen does better is diagnosis: the script is scanned, enlarged, annotated by both people and saved, so week six can be laid next to week one. If your child's problem is attention rather than method, the useful purchase may be a study supervisor locally plus a short specialist block online for the components losing marks, rather than paying specialist rates for supervision.

faqs.question: My child's mock came back two grades below the predicted grade. What happens first?
faqs.answer: The script gets read, with the student present, against the mark scheme. Before any teaching, the lost marks are sorted by cause: content, command-term register, accuracy, or timing. A two-grade gap usually turns out to be one or two causes concentrated in one or two components rather than a general collapse, and that is a far smaller problem than the grade suggests. The output is a ranking of subjects by marks recoverable per hour, which is almost never the same as ranking by how worrying each subject feels. Then an end-dated block, not an open commitment.

faqs.question: Who keeps the marked papers and the error log?
faqs.answer: The family and the student keep copies, and the tutor keeps a working copy so the log carries forward between sessions. The log is the thing most worth preserving: it is what turns a slip into a pattern, and a pattern is what can be taught against. On data, enquiries about a child collect a name, a school, a year group and marks, which Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection covers. A provider should be able to tell you what it holds, why, for how long and how to have it deleted, and that should be written down rather than described on a call.

faqs.question: Do you share progress notes with my child's school?
faqs.answer: Only if the family chooses to. The notes belong to you. Many families do pass them to a subject teacher and it tends to be productive, because the teacher can say whether the component we have identified matches what they see in class, and they set the internal deadlines any plan has to fit. What we will not do is approach a school on your behalf or present ourselves to a school as connected to it. IB Gram is independent of every school named anywhere on this site and holds no affiliation, partnership or endorsement from any of them.

faqs.question: How do you measure progress when the real examinations are months away?
faqs.answer: By using the same task types the examination uses, under the same conditions, repeatedly. A past-paper section sat to time in week one and the same section type in week six is a measurement. A criterion score on a coursework draft before and after a rewrite is a measurement. An error log showing a sign-convention mistake in weeks two and three and not in weeks five and six is a measurement. None of these is a grade, and none of them should be sold as one, but together they are the only honest answer to whether the hours are working.

faqs.question: What if the evidence shows no improvement after six weeks?
faqs.answer: Then something changes, and the change is ours to propose rather than yours to request. Either the hypothesis was wrong - the marks were not going where we thought - or the match is wrong, or the problem needs a different kind of work, such as topic repair before technique. We would rather replace a tutor than argue for the first choice, and we would rather tell you to reduce hours in a subject than keep billing them. The reason the review point is fixed in advance is precisely that families tend to wait and hope, and waiting is the expensive option in a two-year programme.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read it and score it against the five published criteria, name which one is capping the mark, and teach the skill that criterion is asking for - most often critical thinking, which carries twelve of the thirty-four marks. A tutor cannot supply prose, restructure the argument into the submission, or choose the research question. The student rewrites in their own words, which is also the only version that survives a reflection session with a supervisor. Word limit is four thousand, and going over it earns nothing. The Theory of Knowledge essay works the same way inside 1,600 words, assessed as a single ten-mark judgement.

faqs.question: Is one free trial lesson really enough to judge a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is enough to rule one out, which is most of the value. In a working trial the tutor should arrive having read the marked script you sent, teach the component it identified rather than introducing themselves, and finish by stating what the next six weeks would do and in what order. If any of those three is missing, you have learned something useful. What a trial cannot tell you is whether the plan works, which is what the six-week review against fresh marked work is for. No payment is taken before the trial happens, and a wrong match after it is replaced.

abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Ask what documents will exist in six weeks
abu-dhabi/ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IB home tutor near me in Abu Dhabi, the question that separates providers is not where the tutor sits. Ask what will exist in six weeks that does not exist now, and whether a subject teacher could read it. Then send the most recent marked paper or returned coursework draft with the subject and level, and a specialist will read it before a free trial lesson. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed in Gulf Standard Time around your community's school run, and no payment is taken before that first lesson happens.
