abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: These are coaches who work from the specification and the mark scheme outwards. Each one names the board, the paper and the component they coach, and each one marks the student's own timed work rather than talking over a textbook chapter.

intro.heading: Coaching is a cycle, not a conversation
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi households arrive at coaching after a report card that says something vague. A 5 where a 6 was expected. A B where the mocks suggested an A. The report tells you the outcome and nothing about the cause, and a tutoring hour spent re-explaining the chapter the student already half-knows changes neither. Coaching, used properly, is the opposite of that hour. It starts by finding out which marks are actually missing, in which component, for which reason, and then spends the available time on that and nothing else.

The cycle has five stages and it repeats weekly. The student sits a timed section of a real paper. The coach marks it against the published criteria and shows the marking live, cell by cell on the mark scheme. One error type is isolated. The student drills that error on three or four short items. Then the same question type is sat again, cold, a week later. What changes is recorded. Over a term that record becomes an error log: a page that shows which mistakes have been retired and which keep coming back.

This page is written for households running two boards at once, because that is common here. An older child in Diploma Year 2 and a younger one in Year 10 Cambridge IGCSE sit different papers, marked by different people, against different criteria, on different calendars. The Diploma's internal assessment is marked by the school and moderated by the board. An IGCSE paper is marked externally, in a series whose entry deadline sits months before the exam. A single coaching plan has to respect both, and the sections below set out exactly where the two diverge.

Everything here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video and timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a coach to a UAE address; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation, and the reason is in the coaching itself. A script marked on a shared screen, with the mark scheme open beside it and the whole thing recorded, is better evidence than the same hour at a kitchen table where nobody can rewatch what was said.

What you should expect from the first month is artefacts, not assurances: a marked diagnostic, an error log with at least four entries, a written note naming the component being worked on, and a second attempt at the same question type with the mark recorded. If those four things do not exist after four weeks, the coaching is not working, and the sections below say plainly what to do about that.

One practical note before the detail. Coaching works best when the household treats it as a standing appointment rather than a response to a bad week. The cycle depends on a cold re-sit seven days after a drill, and a session moved twice in a month breaks that measurement without anybody noticing. Pick the slot that survives a late bus and a long homework night, even if it is later in the evening than you would prefer.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi households rarely sit inside one programme for long. A child moves from Middle Years into the Diploma, or from Cambridge IGCSE into A Levels or the Diploma, and the coaching has to change shape at each handover. These are the four programmes coaching covers here, and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the school and moderated externally, which means part of the grade is decided months before any examination hall opens. Coaching for the Diploma therefore splits in two: the written papers, which respond to timed practice and command-term drilling, and the coursework, which responds to criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own drafts.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a concentrated Diploma market rather than a broad one, with the programme running at schools clustered on Saadiyat, in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and on Al Reem and Yas. The practical effect is that less common Higher Level courses are taught by one or two teachers in the whole emirate, so the student who needs a second opinion on Higher Level Chemistry Paper 3 often cannot find one within driving distance.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year external qualification sat subject by subject, with Cambridge and Pearson running separate specifications for the same named subject. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics and sets some sciences as single-tier. Papers are marked externally, so what the student writes on the day is the entire grade in most subjects, and command-term discipline is worth more here than in any other qualification a UAE teenager sits.
programmes.countryNote: The British curriculum is the largest single stream in UAE private education, and in Abu Dhabi it runs across the Al Raha and Khalifa City schools, Al Bateen, Al Reef and the newer Shakhbout City and Al Falah communities. Because schools choose their own board, two neighbours in the same compound can be sitting Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry in the same June series, with different paper structures and different practical arrangements.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked on an eight-point scale by the school rather than by an external board. There are no public examinations, which is why Middle Years reports are hard for parents to read and easy to under-react to. Coaching at this stage is about criterion literacy: teaching a student to read criterion B or criterion C and work out what the descriptor is actually asking for, which is the same skill the Diploma will demand two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run Middle Years into Year 11 and then hand students straight into Diploma Year 1 without an external examination in between. That gap matters: a student can reach DP1 having never sat a two-hour externally marked paper. Coaching in Middle Years Year 5 here is usually about building timed-writing stamina before the Diploma asks for it in earnest.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework with no external assessment, reported against learner-profile attributes and transdisciplinary themes. Coaching here is narrow and specific: number fluency, reading comprehension speed, and written structure. The useful work is diagnostic rather than remedial, because a primary gap in place value or in sentence construction is cheap to fix now and expensive to fix in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Primary coaching demand in Abu Dhabi is shaped by relocation. A child arriving mid-year from a different system can be a full strand behind in written mathematics method while being ahead in mental arithmetic, and the school's own baseline test will not always separate the two. A short online diagnostic in the first fortnight after arrival is usually all that is needed.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Coaching is bought by subject and level, not by programme. Below are the Diploma courses Abu Dhabi families request most, with what each one assesses and where the marks tend to go. The IGCSE grid that follows lists the specifications by code, because the code is what determines the paper structure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic, proof-heavy and calculus-dense, with Higher Level adding a third paper that rewards unfamiliar problem framing. The exploration carries twenty criterion marks. Marks are lost on unjustified steps, on notation that the marker cannot follow, and on calculator work shown as an answer with no visible method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led, with graphical display calculator fluency assumed throughout. Students who chose this course to avoid proof often underestimate the statistical reasoning in Paper 2. Marks go on misread context, on reporting a regression result without interpreting it, and on rounding before the final step.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptual questions sit alongside extended calculation, and the scientific investigation carries twenty-four marks across four criteria. The common failure is not the mathematics but the explanation: a correct number with an explanation that never names the physical principle scores a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most lost marks at Higher Level. Paper 1 penalises shallow recall of definitions; Paper 2 penalises explanations that describe a trend without giving its cause. Coaching here is mostly mechanism drawing and the discipline of answering the command term as written.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the obvious problem and data analysis is the hidden one. Extended-response questions reward structure: a named process, a stated mechanism, a consequence. Students who revise by rereading notes rather than by answering past questions plateau quickly in this subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade. A correctly drawn and fully labelled diagram with an explanation tied to the axis labels scores where a verbal answer does not. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper that rewards disciplined evaluation rather than a longer answer.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure, with marks concentrated in applying a framework to the stimulus rather than defining it. The research project rewards a tightly bounded question. Students lose marks by writing textbook definitions that the stimulus material never asked for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two externally marked papers plus an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. Analysis of how meaning is made beats summary of what the text says. The oral is the most coachable component in the course because its structure is published and its timing is fixed.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these can move the Diploma total by up to three points. Coaching is process work: narrowing a research question, planning an argument, and reading a draft against the published criteria. The writing stays the student's, start to finish, and a coach who offers otherwise should be declined.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE coaching is only as good as its specification match. Two schools in Abu Dhabi can teach the same named subject under different codes, with different paper counts and different tiering, so the first question any coach should ask is which code appears on the entry form.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers per tier, with Extended reaching grade A* and Core capped. Extended Paper 4 rewards multi-step problem solving and penalises unshown method. The most reliable gain available is accuracy under time, not extra content.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
igcseSubjects.description: Three papers including an alternative-to-practical component that tests experimental reasoning rather than content recall. Students who have never practised reading a results table against a stated aim lose marks they could keep with four sessions of focused work.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
igcseSubjects.description: Qualitative analysis, moles and organic families account for the bulk of lost marks. The alternative-to-practical paper is worth real attention because it is predictable in structure and rarely practised in school.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
igcseSubjects.description: Command terms do most of the damage here. A question that says describe and a question that says explain want different answers, and the difference is routinely worth more than the content being tested.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two equally weighted papers per tier with no coursework. The Higher tier assumes fluency in algebraic manipulation that Foundation never tests, so the tier decision taken in Year 10 sets the grade ceiling for the whole course.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers with practical skills assessed in writing. The specification's formula list differs from Cambridge's in what is given and what must be recalled, which is a cheap source of lost marks when a student revises from the wrong board's resources.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
igcseSubjects.description: Calculation-heavy by comparison with its Cambridge counterpart, with extended writing on industrial processes. Marks go missing on units, on significant figures, and on explanations that stop one step short of the reason.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and First Language English 0500
igcseSubjects.description: Two very different courses often confused by parents. Second Language rewards register and task fulfilment; First Language rewards directed writing and analysis of effect. Entering a student for the wrong one costs more than any amount of coaching recovers.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.regionsTitle: Where coaching runs across Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: Lessons are online, so a coach is never limited by a drive time. What the district does change is the realistic start time of a session, which school calendar the household is working to, and which subjects turn out to be scarce locally. These are the communities most of the coaching here serves.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short school runs and a high concentration of Diploma and A Level cohorts. Sessions here usually start at 16:30 or 17:00, and demand skews towards Higher Level sciences and the Extended Essay in the autumn of Diploma Year 2.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Bus routes from several schools converge here and arrival times vary by up to half an hour, so a fixed 17:30 slot with a recorded session works better than an earlier one. IGCSE mathematics and the double-award sciences dominate requests.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A dense British-curriculum corridor where Year 10 and Year 11 coaching demand peaks between October and February. Families often coach two subjects at once here, and the limiting factor is homework volume rather than tutor availability.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living, short commutes and a mix of Diploma and IGCSE students in the same building. Evening slots after 18:00 are common because many parents work on the island and prefer to be home for the session.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools with growing senior cohorts, which means fewer alumni cohorts to borrow past-paper culture from. Coaching here spends more time than usual on examination technique that an established school would have drilled already.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and the Corniche
regions.note: The oldest school cluster in the emirate, with established Diploma provision. Requests tilt towards individual components rather than whole subjects: Paper 3, an oral, a single internal assessment criterion.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Ghadeer and Al Samha
regions.note: Long bus journeys and a later effective start to the evening. A 19:00 slot is normal here and works perfectly over video, where a visiting coach would be arriving at the end of a long drive.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: A wide spread of curricula and the part of the emirate where a local specialist in a less common Diploma course is hardest to find. Online coverage changes that position entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Bateen and the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: The established cluster, with long-running Diploma cohorts and experienced coursework supervision. Students here usually arrive at coaching with a clear diagnosis from school and want a second specialist opinion on one component.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The largest block of British-curriculum and Diploma enrolment in the emirate. Coaching demand here is heavily IGCSE in the autumn and heavily Diploma coursework in the winter, with a real crossover in households running both.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem Island, Yas Island and the mainland communities
schoolClusters.note: Newer and fast-growing cohorts where senior provision is still thickening. Scarcity of a named Higher Level specialist is most common in this group, which is where online coverage does most of its work.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named only as the local context Abu Dhabi families live in. IB Gram claims no affiliation with, and no endorsement from, any school listed, and district groupings are approximate.
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.modesIntro: Coaching is sold in three shapes here, and the right one depends on where the student is in the year rather than on how much help they seem to need. Each shape runs one-to-one over live video, with the session recorded and a written note following it.

modes.title: Weekly cycle, one subject at a time
modes.description: The default. Sixty or ninety minutes a week on a single subject, following the five-stage cycle, with a marked script and an error-log update every fortnight. Running two subjects in parallel is possible but it halves the number of complete cycles each subject gets, which is usually the wrong trade in the first term.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes weekly, same slot, same coach
Timed section sat cold at the start of every third session
Error log updated in writing and shared with you
Fortnightly note naming the component being worked

modes.title: Coursework clinic
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions around the internal assessment, the Extended Essay or a Middle Years project. The work is read against the published criteria and commented on criterion by criterion. Authorship stays entirely with the student: a clinic produces annotated feedback on their draft and a plan for the next version, never prose that the student did not write.
bullets: Draft read against criterion letters, with marks indicated
Comments only on the student's own submitted text
Version history kept so progress is traceable
Timed to the school's internal deadlines, not ours

modes.title: Series sprint
modes.description: An intensive block in the eight weeks before a Cambridge, Pearson or IB session. The ratio inverts: less teaching, more timed papers, each one marked live. A sprint is only worth buying when the student already has most of the content and is losing marks to technique, and the diagnostic in week one says plainly whether that is the case.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week in the final block
A full paper under conditions at least once a fortnight
Marking done live, mark scheme visible on screen
Honest stop point if content gaps are too wide to close

sections.heading: The five stages of one coaching cycle
paragraphs: A coaching hour that begins with the coach talking is an hour spent on the coach's guess about the problem. The cycle inverts that. The student writes first, under time, on a question type chosen from the last marked script. Only then does anyone explain anything, and what gets explained is whatever the writing exposed.

Marking live is the part most families have never seen. The coach shares the mark scheme, reads the student's answer line by line against it, and says aloud where a mark was awarded and where it was not. This is uncomfortable for about two sessions and then it changes how the student reads questions, because they have watched an answer being judged rather than being told a score afterwards.

The drill stage is deliberately narrow. If the error was unshown method in simultaneous equations, the drill is four simultaneous-equation items with method marks the only thing being counted. The re-sit comes a week later, cold, on the same question type with different numbers, and the mark is written into the error log beside the first attempt. That pair of numbers is the only honest evidence that anything has changed.

Recording matters more here than on a conversational tutoring hour. A student who has watched a marker reject their own wording usually wants to see that moment again a day later, and a parent who was not in the room can watch the two minutes where the mark was lost rather than reading a summary of it. The recording is also how a second coach, picking up the subject later, learns the diagnosis without starting again.

A student-written script with a start and stop time
Coach reads the script against the mark scheme on screen
An annotated script with marks shown per criterion or per point

sections.heading: Two boards in one household: codes, papers and who marks what
paragraphs: The single most common avoidable problem in an Abu Dhabi household running both boards is revision from the wrong resources. A Year 11 student working from Cambridge 0625 material when the school has entered them for Pearson 4PH1 will meet a different formula list, a different practical arrangement and a different paper structure. None of that shows up until a mock paper comes back oddly.

The fix is administrative, not academic: find the entry code. It appears on the school's examination entry confirmation, on the statement of entry the student receives before a series, and usually on the department's course outline. Ask the examinations officer directly if none of those are to hand. A coach who cannot tell you which code they are coaching to is coaching to a textbook rather than to a specification.

Who marks the work matters just as much. An IGCSE grade in most subjects is decided entirely by externally marked scripts written on the day. A Diploma subject grade is part externally marked paper and part internal assessment marked by the school and then moderated by the board. That difference changes the shape of a sensible coaching plan: for IGCSE, timed technique dominates; for the Diploma, a portion of the grade is banked long before study leave begins.

There is a second administrative trap worth naming. Schools occasionally change board between cohorts, so an older sibling's textbooks and notes can be the wrong resource for the younger one in the same house. Check the code each year rather than assuming continuity, and keep the two children's material physically separate if they are on different boards for the same subject.

table.caption: THE SAME SUBJECT UNDER TWO BOARDS - WHAT ACTUALLY DIFFERS
rows: Different grade ceilings by tier and a different balance of calculator-permitted work

sections.heading: An error log that separates four kinds of lost mark
paragraphs: Every lost mark looks the same on a report card and they are not the same thing at all. A student who does not know the content needs teaching. A student who knows it and misreads the command term needs vocabulary work. A student who knows it, reads correctly, and runs out of time needs pacing. A student who does all three well and drops the mark on units or a rounding step needs a checking routine. Four different problems, four different fixes, four different costs in hours.

Sorting a marked script into those four buckets takes about ten minutes and is the highest-value ten minutes in the whole cycle. It also gives a parent something checkable. If the log says eleven of the last fourteen lost marks were command-term errors, then the next four sessions should be about command terms, and if they are not, you have grounds to ask why.

The log is kept as a running document rather than rebuilt each week, because the useful signal is which error types disappear and which keep returning. An error that has been drilled twice and still recurs is usually not the error it appears to be: unshown method that survives two drills is often a confidence problem about what counts as working, which is a different conversation.

A log also protects the household from a common billing pattern. When nobody writes down what the problem was, every session can plausibly be about something new, and a term passes with twelve plausible hours and no evidence. The log makes the plan auditable: four categories, dated entries, two marks per question type. That is a short document, and reading it takes a parent about three minutes a fortnight.

table.caption: FOUR ERROR TYPES AND WHAT EACH ONE COSTS TO FIX
columns: How it looks on the marked script
rows: Blank, or an answer unrelated to the topic tested
Teaching, then a topic test, then spaced recall
3-6 per topic, depending on how far back the gap goes
A correct fact offered where a reason was wanted

2-3, and it generalises across the whole subject

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides the mark
paragraphs: Both boards publish command-term glossaries and both expect students to have internalised them. In practice most students learn them by accident, from whichever teacher happens to enforce them. The result is a Year 11 who answers a state question with a paragraph and an explain question with a single line, losing marks in both directions on content they know perfectly well.

Coaching this is fast and the gain is unusually durable. The drill is to read twenty past questions and sort them by command term without answering any of them, then to write the first sentence only of the answer each term demands. A describe answer names features. An explain answer gives a cause. An evaluate answer reaches a judgement and supports it. A student who can produce the first sentence correctly almost always produces the rest.

The terms are not identical across boards and levels, which is another reason the specification match matters. The Diploma's analyse and the IGCSE's analyse are used with different expectations about depth, and a Diploma Higher Level discuss question wants a weighted argument where an IGCSE describe wants a list. Teaching a student the superset of terms and then telling them which board's conventions apply is more efficient than teaching one board's list twice.

Parents can run this drill themselves, which is unusual in coaching and worth saying. Take any past paper, cover the content, and ask the student only what each question is instructing them to do. A student who can answer that reliably has already recovered a meaningful share of the marks a marked script was losing, and the coaching hour can then be spent on content rather than on vocabulary.

Observable features or steps, in order
A list opening that names the first feature
A cause or mechanism, not just the effect

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma bridge, subject by subject
paragraphs: In households running both boards, the younger child's coaching is often really preparation for the older child's problem. The step from a strong IGCSE grade into Diploma Higher Level is bigger than the step from Year 10 to Year 11, and it is bigger in some subjects than others. Knowing which gaps are real saves a term of guessing in Diploma Year 1.

Mathematics is the clearest case. An Extended 0580 student who scored well has met most of the algebra that Analysis and Approaches assumes, but has met almost none of the calculus, and has never been asked to justify a step as a proof. That is roughly six to eight weeks of targeted work, best done in the summer between the two courses rather than in October when the Diploma has already started moving.

The sciences split differently. Content continuity is good, but the Diploma's internal assessment asks for an independently designed investigation, and nothing at IGCSE requires that. The alternative-to-practical paper trains experimental reasoning, not experimental design. A student who has only ever followed a given method needs explicit work on formulating a research question, and that work is cheap in the summer and expensive in Diploma Year 1.

English is the quiet exception in both directions. A student who did well on First Language English 0500 is not automatically ready for Diploma English A: Language and Literature, because the Diploma asks for analysis of how meaning is constructed across unseen text types and adds an individual oral with published criteria. Conversely a Second Language 0510 student can be stronger than expected on the Diploma's language-focused components. Neither case is predictable from the IGCSE grade alone, which is why a diagnostic matters more in English than anywhere else.

sections.heading: How far coaching may go on an internal assessment draft
paragraphs: This is the boundary that matters most and the one competitors in this market are least clear about. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by the school supervisor. A coach may teach the skills the task needs, may read what the student has written, and may comment on it against the published criteria. Authorship does not transfer, at any point, for any reason.

In practice that means feedback phrased as a question or a criterion reference rather than as replacement text. Criterion C asks for critical thinking: where in this paragraph is the counter-argument considered? Your method section does not state how the variable was controlled; the criterion requires it. That is legitimate, useful and exactly what a school supervisor also does. Supplying a paragraph for the student to paste in is not, and it puts the diploma at risk rather than the coach.

Keeping version history solves the authentication problem before it becomes one. If each draft is saved with a date and the feedback sits as comments beside the student's own text, the progression from first draft to final is visible and attributable. Any provider in this market offering finished coursework should be declined on the spot; that is an academic-integrity breach and the student carries the consequence.

The same boundary applies to past material, and it catches people out. Published syllabus documents, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and past papers belong to the boards. A coach may reference them and point you to the official page they sit on; reproducing or supplying them as downloads is a copyright problem, and in the case of unreleased material an academic-integrity one. Ask for the link, not the file.

sections.heading: What coaching costs in Abu Dhabi, and who published those figures
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for UAE queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. That is not useful to a household budgeting in dirhams, so the bands below are set out plainly with the source of each figure named. They are market rates rather than IB Gram's own: the honest answer to what we charge is that it depends on subject, level and cadence, and the free trial lesson exists so you can see the coaching before any of that is discussed.

What moves the number in this emirate specifically is scarcity rather than distance. A Standard Level Business Management coach is easy to find in Abu Dhabi and priced accordingly. A Higher Level Physics Paper 3 specialist is not, and the rate reflects it. Travel is the other multiplier: a visiting tutor is pricing the drive as well as the hour, and in this emirate the drive between the island and the mainland communities is the expensive part.

Session length is where households most often overpay. A sixty-minute slot can run one full cycle on a short question type. It cannot sit a full Diploma Paper 2, mark it live and drill the error, which needs ninety minutes or two sessions. Buying sixty-minute slots and then using them to review a paper the student sat alone is the most common way to spend money on coaching without changing anything.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what a term of coaching can honestly show
paragraphs: No coach can promise a grade and any provider who does should be treated with real scepticism. What can be shown is narrower and more useful: component marks on repeated question types, under comparable conditions, over time. A student who scored four of eleven on a question type in September and nine of eleven on the same type in December has moved measurably, whatever the report card eventually says.

Component marks move before subject grades do, and they move at different speeds. Technique errors clear in two to four weeks because the fix is a habit. Content gaps clear in six to twelve weeks because the fix is teaching plus spaced recall. A student with a wide content gap three weeks before a series will show almost no grade movement, and the honest thing to say in week one is that the available time buys partial coverage rather than a transformation.

The termly review compares the error log against the start point and says one of three things: the logged errors are retiring and the plan continues; the errors are retiring but new ones keep appearing, so the diagnosis needs redoing; or nothing is moving, in which case the coaching should stop or change hands. The third answer is given as readily as the first two, because the alternative is billing a household for a plan that is not working.

One more measurement caution. Marks only compare when the conditions do, so a paper sat at a desk with a timer against one sat on a sofa with a phone nearby are not the same data point. Keep the conditions dull and identical: same place, same time limit, no notes, no device except the permitted calculator. A term of comparable marks is worth more than a term of flattering ones.

sections.heading: Coaching to the right series: June and November
paragraphs: A surprising number of Abu Dhabi families discover the series calendar late. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Which series a student sits is the school's decision, taken at entry, months before the papers.

Cambridge does publish a February and March series as well, but it is offered to India only, so no Abu Dhabi centre enters candidates for it and any February exam window a family reads online does not apply to them. The two series that do matter here are June and November, and the published Pearson dates make the point about entry deadlines better than any explanation. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 the final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, entries closed months earlier, and results do not reach students until the following January, the way the November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026. The gap between the entry deadline and the first paper is measured in months, not weeks, in both boards and both series.

One Cambridge rule is worth knowing because getting it wrong is irreversible. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Always work from the timetable the school's examinations officer issues, not one downloaded from a search result. For IB sessions, UAE schools sit the May session; confirm any specific IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, because those dates are set by the board and revised.

The January after the series; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026
Decided in advance how a resit or a tier change would be handled
The following May or June series; Cambridge candidates use June with November as the resit
Equivalency paperwork gathered if applying to a UAE university

process.title: Send three things, not a long message
process.description: The subject, the level or tier, and one marked script or report. Those three identify the specification and give a coach something real to read. A paragraph describing how the student feels about the subject is useful later; it cannot be used to plan a first session.

process.title: A thirty-minute diagnostic, not a sales call
process.description: The student sits a short timed section while the coach watches, then the script is marked live and sorted into error types. You get a written summary of what the script showed and an honest statement of how many sessions the visible problems would need.

process.title: One free trial lesson with the coach who would teach
process.description: A full session with the person who would run the weekly cycle, at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. If the match is wrong, say so afterwards and a different coach is proposed rather than argued for.

process.title: Fix a slot around the school run, not around the coach
process.description: Tell us when the bus actually arrives and when homework realistically ends. A 19:00 slot that happens every week beats a 16:30 slot that gets moved twice a month, and in the Al Reef and Al Ghadeer corridor the later slot is almost always the right one.

process.title: Fortnightly marked work and a one-page note
process.description: Every two weeks you receive the marked script, the updated error log and a note naming the component being worked and the next target. At the end of term the log is compared with the start point and the three honest verdicts are on the table, including stopping.

whyPoints.title: Coached to the code, not to the subject name
whyPoints.description: The first question is which specification appears on the entry form: 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1, Higher Level or Standard. Everything after that, from the formula list to the paper structure to the practical arrangement, follows from that answer rather than from a textbook.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens in front of the student
whyPoints.description: The mark scheme is on screen and the script is read against it aloud. A student who has watched their own answer judged reads the next question differently, which is a change no amount of explaining produces on its own.

whyPoints.title: An error log you can audit
whyPoints.description: Lost marks are sorted into four categories and tracked across the term. If the log says the problem is command terms and the sessions are about content, you have a specific question to ask rather than a vague worry.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, measurement instead
whyPoints.description: Component marks on repeated question types under comparable conditions, recorded over time. That is what can honestly be shown, and it is more useful than a promise because it tells you in week four whether to continue.

whyPoints.title: Coursework coached inside the honesty rules
whyPoints.description: Drafts are read and commented on against the published criteria, with version history kept. The writing stays the student's from first draft to submission, which protects the diploma that the coursework is part of.

whyPoints.title: Scarcity handled before you book
whyPoints.description: If no specialist currently covers the exact component you need, that is said before the first invoice, with the realistic wait and the alternative. Coverage limits disclosed up front cost less than coverage limits discovered in week three.

faqs.question: What does IB IGCSE coaching in Abu Dhabi actually include each week?
faqs.answer: One session a week on a single subject, sixty or ninety minutes, following a fixed five-stage cycle. The student sits a timed section of a real past paper cold, the coach marks it live against the mark scheme on a shared screen, one error type is isolated and written into the error log, the student drills that error on short items, and the same question type is re-sat the following week. Every fortnight you receive the marked script, the updated log and a one-page note naming the component being worked. The session is recorded and the recording is available to rewatch.

faqs.question: Can one coach cover an IGCSE child and a Diploma child in the same family?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and it is worth being clear about why. The two qualifications are marked differently, run on different calendars and reward different habits, so a coach deep enough in Diploma Higher Level Chemistry to be useful on Paper 3 is rarely the best choice for Year 10 Cambridge 0620. What does work is two coaches on a shared schedule, with the error logs visible to you side by side. Where a single coach genuinely covers both, it tends to be in mathematics, where the content overlap is real and the bridge work is the same work.

faqs.question: How do I find out which syllabus code my child's Abu Dhabi school is entering them for?
faqs.answer: Three places carry it. The examination entry confirmation the school sends before a series lists the code against each subject. The statement of entry the student receives names it too. The department's course outline at the start of Year 10 usually states it. If none of those is to hand, email the school's examinations officer and ask directly, which takes a day. It matters because Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 Physics have different formula provision, different paper structures and different practical arrangements, and revising from the wrong board's resources costs marks that no amount of coaching recovers.

faqs.question: What is an error log, and what should actually be written in it?
faqs.answer: A running document that sorts lost marks into four categories: content gaps, command-term misreads, timing failures, and accuracy or presentation errors. Each entry names the paper, the question, the category and the mark lost, and later gets a second mark beside it when the same question type is re-sat. It should not be a list of topics to revise. The point is to show which error types are retiring and which keep coming back, because an error that survives two drills is usually not the error it first appeared to be and needs a different diagnosis.

faqs.question: What is a command term, and why does it decide so many marks?
faqs.answer: A command term is the instruction word that opens a question: state, describe, explain, compare, evaluate. Both Cambridge and the IB publish glossaries defining what each one requires, and markers award against that definition rather than against general knowledge of the topic. A student who answers an explain question by describing the effect again loses marks on content they know well. Drilling this is fast: sort twenty past questions by command term without answering them, then write only the first sentence each term demands. Students who get the first sentence right almost always produce a scoring answer.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE Extended into Diploma Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject and the difference is worth planning for. In mathematics a strong Cambridge 0580 Extended student has met most of the algebra that Analysis and Approaches assumes but almost none of the calculus, and has never been asked to justify a step as a proof: roughly six to eight weeks of targeted work. In the sciences content continuity is good, but the Diploma expects an independently designed investigation, and nothing at IGCSE requires designing a method from scratch. Both gaps are much cheaper to close in the summer before Diploma Year 1 than in the October after it starts.

faqs.question: Is coaching worth starting in Year 10, or should we wait for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the better value and almost nobody buys it then. In Year 10 the tier decision is still open, the content load is lighter, and habits like shown method and command-term discipline can be built before they are being tested under pressure. By the February of Year 11 the same habits have to be rebuilt while content revision competes for the same hours. The exception is a student with a specific wide content gap, where waiting is still wrong but the first block will be teaching rather than technique, and the honest session estimate is longer.

faqs.question: Does coaching include marking full past papers under timed conditions?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the part that cannot be skipped. In a sixty-minute slot a full Diploma Paper 2 cannot be sat, marked live and drilled in the same hour, so either the paper is sat between sessions under conditions you supervise and marked live in the session, or the slot is ninety minutes. Both work. What does not work is reviewing a paper the student marked themselves from an answer key, because the useful information is in watching the marking decisions being made, not in knowing the final score.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IB or IGCSE coaching cost in Abu Dhabi at the moment?
faqs.answer: The market runs from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium named end. A qualified subject tutor working online sits broadly in the AED 150-300 band, and a named IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist in the AED 200-450 band. In-home visits carry the drive in the rate, which is why published in-home bands reach AED 500. Those figures come from competitor and market sources published in 2026, not from IB Gram's own price list, and scarcity of the exact component moves the number more than anything else in this emirate.

faqs.question: Where do the AED rates quoted on this page come from?
faqs.answer: Each band is attributed on the page itself. The budget figures come from EdFlik and Tutopiya's own published rates, the qualified-tutor band from Unitors, the in-home band from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table and from published home-tutor rates, the specialist band from TutorChase and Bestimate, and the premium figure from BartyED. They are market observations from 2026, published so that a household budgeting in dirhams has something to compare against. They are not IB Gram's prices, and anyone quoting a rate without naming where it came from should be asked where it came from.

faqs.question: How far can a coach go in commenting on an internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: A coach may teach the skills the task needs, read what the student has written, and comment on it against the published criteria. That means feedback phrased as a criterion reference or a question: criterion C requires critical thinking, so where is the counter-argument considered? Your method does not state how the variable was controlled, and the criterion asks for it. What may never happen is authorship transferring, in whole or in part, at any stage. Supplying text for a student to paste in puts the diploma at risk, and any provider offering finished coursework should be declined immediately.

faqs.question: Which examination series will my child sit, and who decides that?
faqs.answer: The school decides at entry, usually months before the papers. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, which are the two series available to a UAE candidate; the February and March series Cambridge also publishes is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session. You can confirm which series your child is entered for from the examination entry confirmation or by asking the examinations officer, and it is worth doing early because the tier decision has to be settled before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: Why does a Cambridge entry deadline fall so long before the examination?
faqs.answer: Because entries drive timetabling, paper despatch and centre allocation. A UAE candidate sits the June series or the November series, and the gap is visible in either. Entries for the June papers close in the spring, roughly four months before the first script, and the exact day is on the statement of entry the examinations officer issues rather than on any website. Pearson works the same way: the International GCSE November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 and entries for it closed months earlier, with results reaching students the following January. The practical consequence for a household is that the Core or Extended decision, and the Foundation or Higher decision, is effectively locked a long way ahead of the papers, which is why it has to be made on mock evidence rather than on hope.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish six different timetable zones, and does it affect us?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a household this means one rule: revise and plan from the timetable your school's examinations officer issues, not from a version found through a search. It is the single highest-consequence administrative error available in the IGCSE year, and it is entirely avoidable.

faqs.question: Does coaching happen at our home in Abu Dhabi, or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video and timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a coach to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. The reason is not cost. Live marking needs the mark scheme and the script visible side by side on a shared screen, and the session needs to be rewatchable, both of which a video session does better than a kitchen table. It also means a household in Al Reef or Mussafah gets the same shortlist as one on Saadiyat, rather than whoever is willing to make the drive.

faqs.question: What would tell us, after a term, that the coaching is not working?
faqs.answer: Three things in combination. The error log shows the same categories recurring after two drills each. Component marks on repeated question types under comparable conditions have not moved. And the fortnightly notes have stopped naming a specific component and started describing sessions in general terms. Any one of those on its own can be explained; all three together mean the diagnosis is wrong or the match is wrong. At the termly review the verdict is given plainly, including the verdict that coaching should stop or change hands, because billing against a plan that is not working is worse than ending it.

faqs.question: Can coaching run through the summer between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer is the most underused block in the whole two-year course. It is the only stretch where no school deadlines compete for the hours, which makes it the right time for content teaching and for bridge work: calculus before Analysis and Approaches, investigation design before a Diploma science, timed-paper stamina before a first external series. Families who travel can keep the same slot and the same coach from wherever they are, since the session is a video call. Two sessions a week across six weeks of summer is worth considerably more than the same hours in February.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-coaching.closingBody: If you are weighing up coaching for an Abu Dhabi household running IB, IGCSE or both, the useful first step is small. Send the subject, the level or tier, and one piece of marked work. A coach will read it, sort the lost marks into categories and tell you what the script actually shows, including the possibility that coaching is not what the problem needs. The trial lesson that follows is one full session with the coach who would teach, free, with no card details and no obligation. Everything runs online, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a written note after every second session.

Session length, minimum bookings, who marks the work between lessons, the subject's scarcity and the month of the year all move it, sometimes by more than the headline rate differs between providers. This page publishes the AED bands for this market with each source named and dated, explains which variables actually change your bill, and shows how to make three quotes comparable. Lessons here run online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE at Core and Extended tier and IB at Standard and Higher Level, one to one over live video. The first session is free, and nothing is charged before you have met the tutor and received a written diagnostic.

intro.heading: Why one hourly rate tells you almost nothing
paragraphs: Ask three Abu Dhabi providers what tuition costs and you will get three numbers that cannot be compared. One quotes AED 200 for a 45-minute session with nothing set between lessons. One quotes AED 280 for a full hour with a marked past paper each week. One quotes AED 350 but insists on a two-hour minimum, so the real weekly figure is AED 700. The cheapest hourly rate in that list is the most expensive arrangement per mark gained, and nothing on any of the three websites would tell you that.

The published bands for this market are worth having in front of you. Budget online tuition, typically delivered by university students, runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with one platform listing from AED 45 to 65 and another from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit between about AED 150 and 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run roughly AED 180 to 350 in one survey, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutoring is quoted between AED 200 and 450 and above, including one UK agency at AED 270. Premium named provision reaches AED 650. Every one of those figures belongs to somebody else and was read in October 2026.

Monthly figures behave the same way. One provider in this market advertises about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, while in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions have been listed between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799. A separate cost survey estimates monthly spend for one weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Three of the six competing pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars.

What this page does is separate the headline rate from the things that actually determine your bill: the level being taught, the scarcity of the specification, whether marking happens between sessions, the minimum booking, and the month in the academic year. Those five variables explain most of the spread above. They also explain why two families in Al Raha Beach paying the same hourly rate can end a term having spent very different amounts and received very different amounts of teaching.

One point on delivery, because it changes the cost structure directly. Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and does not operate a centre anywhere in the UAE; home visits exist only in our India service. An in-home rate carries a vehicle and most of an hour's driving in the late-afternoon traffic, which is the main structural reason the in-home band sits above the online one in every survey read for this page.
bullets: Compare cost per week with session length and inclusions fixed, not cost per hour
Marking between sessions is where marks move; a rate that excludes it is a cheaper, smaller service
Scarce specifications cost more because the pool who can teach them is small, not because the subject is harder
Examination-year demand peaks between October and February in Abu Dhabi, and that peak reaches prices
Ask whether a quoted AED figure includes VAT; a provider should answer about its own pricing without hedging

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: Cost tracks level and scarcity more than it tracks subject. The three programmes below are described by what drives their price in this emirate and how many hours families typically commit to each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The widest supply and therefore the most competitive pricing of any level here. Core-tier support sits at the lower end of the qualified-tutor band; Extended-tier science and mathematics taught against the published mark scheme sits higher, because the pool who do it well is smaller. Two subjects at one hour each is the most common Abu Dhabi commitment through Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: The price pattern across an Abu Dhabi IGCSE year is predictable. Enquiries are cheap and easy to fill in September and October. From January, when mock results land and the examination series is close, specialist availability narrows and families end up paying for whoever is free rather than choosing. Booking the specialist in the autumn and reducing frequency later costs less across the year than the reverse.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive level in every published band, and the one where scarcity dominates. Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches carry the premium, and coursework supervision blocks are usually bought as a fixed number of sessions rather than a weekly slot. A two-year plan for one Higher Level subject is a serious budget line and should be planned as one.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma demand is sharply seasonal because school internal deadlines for Internal Assessments cluster between October and February. That is when specialist capacity is thinnest across the emirate and when a family that waits pays most, in money and in choice. Families on Saadiyat Island and Al Reem Island who plan the coursework block in September routinely pay less than those who call in January.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest level to support and the easiest to over-buy. With no external paper before the optional MYP 5 eAssessment, weekly year-round tuition rarely earns its cost. A short block aimed at manipulation fluency and extended-writing stamina, taken before the Diploma begins, does more for the money than a standing weekly slot through three middle years.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families often start tuition earlier than the assessment requires, which is understandable and expensive. The useful spending pattern in the middle years is diagnostic: a block of sessions, a written assessment of what is genuinely behind, then a gap. Holding budget for the Diploma years, when the hourly bands are highest and the supply tightest, is the better use of the same money.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Price varies more by scarcity than by difficulty. Each subject below carries a note on where it sits in the market band and why, which is the part no competing page in this market publishes.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The most competitively priced request in the emirate, because supply is deep. Core-tier support sits at the lower end of the qualified-tutor band. Extended-tier work, including the non-calculator manipulation drilling, is priced slightly higher but remains the easiest specialist slot to fill at short notice.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Mid-band at Core tier and noticeably higher for Extended-tier teaching that works to the mark scheme on mole calculations and organic chemistry. Demand concentrates in the eight weeks before mocks, which is also when the band tightens and choice narrows.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Priced above Cambridge 0625 support in practice, simply because fewer tutors in this market have taught the Pearson specification recently. Paying a Cambridge-trained tutor to learn 4PH1 on your time is the most common hidden cost in physics tuition here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At the top of the specialist band at Higher Level, driven by Paper 3 and the extended investigations that paper carries. Standard Level sits lower. This is the subject where families most often buy a long plan, and where planning the hours across two years saves the most.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: The scarcest common request in Abu Dhabi and consistently at the upper end of published specialist bands. The scientific investigation component, worth a fifth of the grade, is usually bought as a supervision block rather than as weekly hours, which changes the shape of the cost.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP)
subjects.description: Upper band at Higher Level. The honest cost note is that much of the early work is mathematical rather than physical, so a family paying physics-specialist rates for algebra rehabilitation is overpaying for the wrong hour. A diagnostic should establish which it is before a plan is bought.

subjects.name: Economics (IB DP)
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, with the internal assessment commentaries typically handled as a short supervision block. Higher Level quantitative content adds to the hours. Evaluation-question technique is the highest-value teaching per hour in this subject and is often skipped in favour of content revision.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Among the better-supplied subjects, so mid-band pricing with reasonable availability even late in the year. Value concentrates in marked written work between sessions rather than in the session itself, which makes the inclusions question more important here than the hourly rate.

subjects.name: Arabic (first and additional language)
subjects.description: Competitively priced and well supplied locally at school level, because the subject is mandated alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules. First-language Diploma routes are a separate, scarcer market and should not be priced from an additional-language quote.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Computer Science
subjects.description: Mid-band at IGCSE and thinner at Higher Level, where pricing reflects scarcity. In Computer Science specifically, families often pay developer rates for somebody who has never marked the written paper, which is the clearest mismatch of price to need in this market.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tuition.regionsTitle: Communities and what the local tuition market looks like in each
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Local supply differs across Abu Dhabi, and where supply is thin, in-home prices rise and choice falls. These notes describe the market in each community rather than the drive time, because price is what this page is about.

regions.name: Al Rawdah
regions.note: Central island district close to several long-established schools, with a comparatively deep local tutoring market at IGCSE level. In-home quotes here tend to sit mid-band because the travel component is small.

regions.name: Al Karamah
regions.note: Residential and central, with steady IGCSE demand and reasonable local supply. Group revision classes are more available here than in the outer communities, which makes the group-plus-targeted-one-to-one combination practical.

regions.name: Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Dense city district with a mixed school-age population and a thin specialist market of its own. Families here usually price online against a drive rather than against a local specialist, because the local specialist often is not there.

regions.name: Al Falah
regions.note: Mainland villa community some distance from the island school estate. In-home quotes include a substantial drive and commonly come with a two-hour minimum, which doubles the weekly figure regardless of the hourly rate.

regions.name: Al Ghadeer
regions.note: On the emirate boundary towards Dubai, which makes the local tutoring market unusually scattered. Some families here hold quotes from both Dubai and Abu Dhabi providers and find the travel component dominates the difference.

regions.name: Hydra Village
regions.note: Outer villa community with limited local supply at Extended tier and almost none at Diploma Higher Level. The practical choice here is an online specialist or a generalist nearby, and the price difference is usually smaller than families expect.

regions.name: Al Wahda
regions.note: Central, well connected and with good access to group classes as well as private tutors. One of the few areas where the full range of formats is genuinely available, so comparing cost per week across formats is worthwhile.

regions.name: Mussafah
regions.note: Largely industrial with residential pockets and a limited private-tuition market. Quotes for visits here reflect the distance from the island, and online pricing is unaffected by it, which is the clearest illustration of what travel costs.

schoolClusters.city: Central island schools
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's established school estate, where fee levels, examination entry costs and tuition demand are all highest. Students we support here are mostly IGCSE candidates and Diploma students needing coursework supervision blocks.

schoolClusters.note: Also under ADEK's remit, with a smaller private school market and a correspondingly thin local tutoring pool. Families here are frequently choosing between a long drive to Abu Dhabi city and an online specialist, and the cost comparison is rarely close.

sections.heading: What home tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, by level and format
paragraphs: The table below is the thing this market does not publish. Of six competing pages examined for this cluster, three quote no price at all, two quote in US dollars, and one of its own frequently-asked questions asks what tuition costs and declines to answer. Publishing a band with its source attached is therefore not a competitive claim, it is simply the first useful answer a parent gets.

Read it as a market map rather than a price list. None of these figures is IB Gram's price. Each band is drawn from named providers' published rates and from a published cost survey for this market, all read in October 2026, and all of them will drift. What the bands are good for is sanity-checking a quote: if somebody offers Higher Level Diploma Chemistry at the budget end of the range, something in the arrangement is not what you think it is, and if somebody quotes well above the specialist band, the question to ask is what the extra buys.

Two columns deserve explanation. The small-group column is a per-student figure, which is why it looks dramatically cheaper and why it is not comparable to one-to-one for a student with a specific gap: a group moves at the group's pace. The indicative monthly column assumes one session a week over four weeks, which is how most Abu Dhabi families actually buy, and it is the number worth putting in a household budget rather than the hourly rate.

The last row is the one families underestimate. Coursework supervision for an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is bought by the block, not by the term, and the block lands in the same autumn and winter weeks for almost every school in the emirate. That concentration is why September booking costs less than January booking for identical work.

sections.heading: The five variables that actually move your bill
paragraphs: Level is the obvious one and the least interesting, because every provider prices it. The four that create the real spread are scarcity, inclusions, minimum booking and timing, and none of them appear on a price page. A parent who understands those four can usually reduce a term's spend without reducing a single hour of teaching, simply by buying differently.

Scarcity first. A specification taught by many people prices competitively; one taught by few does not. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is the deepest pool in this emirate. Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, Higher Level Diploma Chemistry and Computer Science at Higher Level are the thinnest. The premium on a scarce specification is not a difficulty surcharge, it is supply, which is also why restricting the search to a driving radius raises it further.

Inclusions next, and this is where most value is won or lost. An hour that includes work set and marked against the published mark scheme between sessions is a materially different product from an hour of talking, and the two are quoted as though they were the same. The question to ask is blunt: what will you set, who marks it, and do I get the annotated script. A rate that excludes marking is not cheaper, it is smaller.

Then minimum booking and timing. A two-hour minimum doubles a weekly bill whatever the hourly figure says, and some students cannot concentrate for two hours regardless. Timing matters because Abu Dhabi demand peaks between October and February, when Diploma coursework deadlines cluster and IGCSE mocks land. Specialist capacity is thinnest then, so a family that books in September both pays less and chooses from more people. Those two decisions, session length and month, routinely matter more than which provider you pick.

sections.heading: Tuition in context: what else an examination year costs
paragraphs: Tuition is one line in a bigger examination-year budget, and families routinely plan it in isolation. Private school fees in Abu Dhabi are regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; each school publishes its own approved fee schedule, and no Abu Dhabi fee band is quoted here because no sourced figure for this page was verified. Check the school's own published schedule rather than any third-party summary, including this one.

For contrast, Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure and says nothing about Abu Dhabi fees, but it is a useful reminder that school fee policy is set emirate by emirate and changes year by year, which is why a tuition budget built on last year's assumptions drifts.

The examination entry line is the one most often forgotten entirely. Entry fees are charged by the centre, differ between Cambridge and Pearson, and rise sharply for private candidates sitting outside a school. If a student is retaking a subject or sitting one the school does not offer, that is a separate and non-trivial cost which has to be budgeted alongside the tuition hours, and the centre is the only reliable source for the figure.

The purpose is not precision, it is sequencing: seeing a two-year Higher Level plan and a four-session coursework block in the same list usually changes how a family allocates the money, and almost always moves spending earlier in the year.

sections.heading: Hourly, package or block - which model fits which problem
paragraphs: The pricing model matters as much as the price. Pay-as-you-go costs the most per hour and the least in total when the problem is undiagnosed, because you stop as soon as you know. A term-long weekly slot costs less per hour and more in total, and earns that only if the target genuinely needs months. A fixed-scope block is the right shape when the work has a deadline rather than a duration, which is exactly what coursework is.

The risk in a package is forfeiture. A monthly or termly package bought up front converts your flexibility into the provider's revenue certainty, and the question that reveals how fair it is has nothing to do with the discount: what happens to unused sessions, and what notice does a cancellation need. A package with a generous rate and no carry-over can cost more than ad-hoc booking across a term with two school trips and an examination fortnight in it.

There is a particular pattern worth naming. A family is offered a substantial discount for buying a term in advance, before any trial session has happened and before anybody has diagnosed anything. That is a commitment bought with a price cut, and in a market where a free trial is available it is unnecessary. The sequence that protects a budget is trial, diagnostic, short block, then a longer plan if the evidence supports one.

Our own structure is deliberately plain. Nothing is charged before a free trial session, no package purchase is required to start, and sessions pause during the school's own assessment weeks when a student needs revision time rather than new input. We publish no discount ladder, because a discount that depends on committing before diagnosis is a pricing tactic rather than a saving.

sections.heading: How many hours a realistic plan needs
paragraphs: Families ask how many sessions it takes, and the honest answer begins with a question back: how many weeks remain, and is the problem content or technique. Those two facts determine almost everything. A technique problem in a student who knows the content can be moved substantially in six to ten weeks of marked timed practice. A content problem spanning a year of missed teaching cannot be closed in the same window at one hour a week, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling reassurance.

No provider can promise a grade, including this one. Marking is done by the board, boundaries move between series, and a student's own work between sessions accounts for more of the outcome than the session does. What can be described honestly is what families typically book for a given situation and what has to happen outside the hour for it to be worth buying. That is the shape of the table below.

The variable most often underestimated is independent work. Beyond about two hours a week in one subject, the constraint stops being teaching time and becomes practice time: a student not completing marked work between sessions will not convert a third hour into marks, and the money is better held for the following term. This is also why adding subjects usually beats adding hours once the second hour is in place.

The variable most often overestimated is the exam-term intensive. Ten weeks of concentrated work before a series is genuinely useful for paper technique and genuinely limited for content. The best value in an Abu Dhabi examination year, repeatedly, is one hour a week from October with marked work between sessions, plus a short intensive at the end, rather than nothing until February followed by a panic block at specialist rates.
