sections.heading: The extras that make a cheap hourly rate expensive
paragraphs: The hourly figure is the part providers compete on, so it is the part that gets squeezed, and the money reappears elsewhere. The commonest mechanisms are a short session sold as an hour, a minimum booking, materials charged separately, a cancellation window that forfeits the session, and travel added for a visit. None of these is dishonest. All of them are invisible in a rate comparison.

Session length is first because it is the easiest to miss. A 45-minute session quoted at AED 200 is AED 267 an hour; a 50-minute session at AED 240 is AED 288. Both read as cheaper than a 60-minute hour at AED 280 and neither is. Ask for the session length in minutes before comparing anything, and ask whether the quoted figure is per session or per hour, because providers use both.

Materials are the second. Board syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published on the boards' own sites and are the boards' copyright; they should be referenced and linked rather than resold or redistributed as downloads. A provider charging a materials fee for board content is charging for something freely readable at source, and a provider distributing it as a download pack has a copyright problem rather than a product.

On tax, we will say only what we can stand behind. Ask any provider directly whether its quoted AED prices include VAT and get the answer in writing. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and we have no citation to publish. Similarly, the free trial is genuinely free, and its one condition is stated plainly: one session per student, no card required, no package purchase.

sections.heading: Group classes, and the economics of attention
paragraphs: Per student, a group of four is the cheapest teaching available, and for some purposes it is also the best. Revisiting content the whole group has met, working through a past paper together, drilling command terms: a competent teacher with four students does this efficiently, and the cost per student is a fraction of one-to-one. Dismissing group classes to protect a one-to-one price list would be dishonest arithmetic.

What a group cannot do is diagnose. A student losing marks because their working is disordered and another losing marks because they have never understood moles need different hours, and a group gives them the same one. The pace belongs to the group, which means the student who needs twelve minutes on a step gets four, and the student who needed none sits through all four. That is the real cost, and it does not appear in the price.

The efficient combination in Abu Dhabi, where group availability is decent in the central districts and thin outside them, is usually a group revision class for breadth plus a small number of one-to-one sessions aimed precisely at what the group cannot reach. A family buying three one-to-one hours a week is often buying two hours of content delivery that a group would have handled and one hour of genuine diagnosis.

One caution on comparing group quotes. Ask the group size, not the maximum group size, and ask what happens if the group shrinks to two or grows to eight, because both change the product. Also ask whether the class is matched by specification: a mixed Cambridge and Pearson group in a tiered science subject is teaching two different papers at once, which no amount of competence fully solves.

sections.heading: How to make three Abu Dhabi quotes genuinely comparable
paragraphs: The practical skill is normalising. Send every provider the same five facts: the board and syllabus code, the tier or level, the year group, the next assessment date, and a photograph of one recent piece of marked work. Ask every provider the same five questions: session length in minutes, hourly or per-session pricing, what is set and marked between sessions, the minimum booking, and the cancellation and carry-over terms.

Then convert everything to one number: cost per week for the arrangement you would actually buy. A 45-minute session at AED 200 with no marking, twice a week, is AED 400 weekly for 90 minutes of teaching. A single 60-minute session at AED 280 with a marked paper each week is AED 280 weekly for 60 minutes of teaching plus marking. Which is better value depends on your child, but at least the comparison is now between two real things.

Three answers should change your shortlist regardless of price. An offer to write, complete or substantially revise an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, which is academic malpractice and puts the student's diploma at risk. A claim of regulator or examination-board approval, accreditation or partnership, which no provider in this market should make without showing the permit or centre number. And a published rating or success figure with no stated sample, date or method behind it.

A last practical note. Private tutors in the UAE need a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and asking to see it is routine. It costs nothing to obtain, so there is no financial reason for an established tutor not to hold one. That single question tells you more about a provider's operating standards than any discount on the rate card.

With those, a specialist can say what the problem looks like and roughly how many hours it suggests. Without them, any figure quoted to you is a guess dressed as a price.

process.title: Free trial before any payment
process.description: One full session at no cost, no card required and no package purchase first. It runs on real questions from your child's own specification and ends with a written diagnostic you keep. The condition is one trial per student, which is stated here rather than discovered at checkout.

process.title: Agree the plan in weeks and hours, in writing
process.description: After the diagnostic we set out what the first block is aimed at, how many sessions it needs, and what has to happen between lessons for it to work. Short blocks are preferred to long commitments, because a plan that survives evidence is better than one bought on optimism.

process.title: Pay as you go, pause for school exams
process.description: Sessions are billed as they happen rather than bought in bulk, and they pause during the school's own assessment weeks, when a student needs revision time more than new input. Nothing is forfeited by pausing, which removes the main financial risk in a termly package.

process.title: Review the spend on evidence each half term
process.description: At each half term we look at marked papers and the error log and ask whether the money is doing work. If it is not, the honest answers are a different tutor, a different format, or stopping, and we will name whichever one the evidence supports rather than proposing another block.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider or survey it came from and the month it was read. Three of the six competing pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and one asks the price question in its own list and declines to answer it. An attributed band is more useful than a confident number with nothing behind it.

whyPoints.title: Cost per week, not cost per hour
whyPoints.description: Session length, minimum bookings and marking inclusions are separated out here, because those three move a weekly bill more than the headline rate does. A 45-minute session without marking and a 60-minute session with it are different products at the same apparent price.

whyPoints.title: No package purchase before a diagnosis
whyPoints.description: Nothing is charged before a free trial, and no discount is offered for committing before anybody has established what is wrong. Discounts that require a term's payment up front move risk onto the family at exactly the point when the family knows least.

whyPoints.title: Pause rather than forfeit
whyPoints.description: Sessions pause for school assessment weeks and family travel without losing value. The forfeiture clause in a termly package is the quiet cost of the lower headline rate, and across an Abu Dhabi school year with its trips and examination fortnights it is rarely a small one.

whyPoints.title: Scarce specifications stated as scarce
whyPoints.description: Where a specification has thin specialist supply, you are told the realistic wait or told plainly that we cannot cover it. Being matched at short notice with somebody learning the specification alongside your child is the most expensive hour in this market, whatever it costs.

whyPoints.title: Figures we cannot stand behind are absent
whyPoints.description: No success percentages, no star ratings, no student counts, and no VAT ruling. If a number cannot be shown with its sample, date and method, it is not published here. That includes our own: the evidence we offer is the marked work, which you can inspect.

faqs.question: How much does IB and IGCSE home tuition cost in Abu Dhabi per month?
faqs.answer: For one weekly hour, a published cost survey for this market puts monthly spend at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. In-home monthly packages of four two-hour visits have been listed at AED 1,599 to 1,799, and one provider advertises about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other companies' figures read in October 2026, not ours. The monthly number is the one worth budgeting; the hourly rate is the one that hides session length.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition priced higher than online in every survey?
faqs.answer: Because the rate carries a vehicle and most of an hour's driving. A tutor teaching one hour in an outer Abu Dhabi community and returning spends a substantial part of the late afternoon on the road, unpaid, and the hourly figure has to absorb it. That is also why in-home providers commonly impose a minimum session length or sell monthly packages rather than single hours. The published bands reflect it: in-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180 to 350 in one survey, with independent tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against about AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest hourly rate ever the cheapest arrangement?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is session length and inclusions. A 45-minute session quoted at AED 200 is AED 267 an hour. Two of them a week is AED 400 for 90 minutes of teaching with nothing set in between. A single 60-minute session at AED 280 that includes a marked past paper each week is cheaper weekly and includes work that moves marks. Convert everything to cost per week for the arrangement you would actually buy, with session length in minutes stated, and the comparison usually inverts the ranking the hourly rates suggested.

faqs.question: Which subjects carry a price premium in this emirate, and why?
faqs.answer: Scarcity rather than difficulty sets it. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 has the deepest local supply and the most competitive pricing. Higher Level Diploma Chemistry, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 and Computer Science at Higher Level are the thinnest, and sit at the upper end of published specialist bands. The premium exists because few people teach those specifications to their mark schemes, and restricting the search to a drivable radius makes it worse. If a quote for one of those subjects sits at the budget end of the market, ask directly what specification the tutor last taught.

faqs.question: Should we buy a term package up front for the discount?
faqs.answer: Not before a trial and a diagnostic. A package discount is a price cut in exchange for your flexibility, and its real terms are in two clauses: what happens to unused sessions, and how much notice a cancellation needs. Across an Abu Dhabi school year with trips, examination fortnights and travel, forfeited sessions can cost more than the discount saved. The sequence that protects a budget is a free trial, a short diagnostic block, then a longer plan if the marked evidence supports it. Any discount available only before diagnosis is a commitment device, not a saving.

faqs.question: What does a coursework supervision block cost, and when should we book it?
faqs.answer: It is priced as a block of roughly four to eight sessions within the specialist band rather than as a weekly rate, because the work has a deadline rather than a duration. Book it in September. School internal deadlines for Internal Assessments cluster between October and February across almost every Abu Dhabi school, so specialist capacity is thinnest and choice narrowest exactly when most families call. The same block of work, booked early, costs less and gets a better match. What the tutor does inside it is teach criteria, question method and give feedback on the student's own draft.

faqs.question: How many hours a week is too many in one subject?
faqs.answer: Beyond about two, the limiting factor stops being teaching and becomes independent practice. A student who is not completing marked work between sessions will not convert a third hour into marks, and the money is better held for the next term or spent on a second subject. The exception is a short, deliberate intensive before a series, where additional hours are aimed at timed papers and technique rather than new content. If a provider suggests four hours a week in one subject without asking what the student does between sessions, that is a selling decision rather than a teaching one.

faqs.question: Do your quoted prices in Abu Dhabi include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask us directly and we will answer about our own pricing in writing. What this page will not do is state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and we have no citation to publish, and a tutoring website is the wrong place to learn tax law. The same question is worth putting to every provider you approach, in writing, because a figure quoted without that answer can shift by a noticeable margin at the point of invoicing.

faqs.question: Are group classes worth it for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: For breadth, often yes. Per student, a group of four is the cheapest teaching available, and for revisiting content the whole group has met it is efficient. What a group cannot do is diagnose: the pace belongs to the group, so the student who needs twelve minutes on a step gets four. The efficient mix in central Abu Dhabi, where group availability is reasonable, is a group revision class plus a small number of one-to-one sessions on the specific gap. Ask the actual group size, not the maximum, and ask whether the class is matched by board and tier.

faqs.question: What should I ask before paying a deposit to any Abu Dhabi provider?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Session length in minutes. Whether pricing is hourly or per session. What is set and marked between lessons, and whether you receive the annotated script. The minimum booking. And the cancellation, pause and carry-over terms. Then one more that is not about money: does the tutor hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. It is free and valid for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, so an established tutor without one has made a choice, and that tells you something about the operation.

faqs.question: Can tuition fees here be compared with what the school already charges?
faqs.answer: Only loosely, and the school figure has to come from the school. Private school fees in Abu Dhabi are regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and each school publishes its own approved schedule. No Abu Dhabi fee band appears on this page because no sourced figure was verified for it. For context on how emirate-level policy moves, Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees there would not rise for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion; that is Dubai, not Abu Dhabi.

faqs.question: Is a budget online tutor at AED 60 an hour a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends entirely on the task. Platforms publishing rates from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour are generally matching university students, which can be perfectly adequate for homework supervision, basic numeracy practice or keeping a middle-years student moving. It is a poor fit for Extended-tier mark-scheme work, Higher Level Diploma teaching or anything involving assessment criteria. The expensive version of this mistake is paying budget rates for twenty sessions that do not touch the actual problem, then paying specialist rates in February anyway.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if we need to pause for school exams or travel?
faqs.answer: Here, nothing: sessions are billed as they happen rather than bought in bulk, and pausing during the school's own assessment weeks is encouraged rather than penalised, because a student in an examination fortnight needs revision time more than new input. Elsewhere, this is the clause worth reading before you pay. A termly package with a lower headline rate and no carry-over can cost more across a year than ad-hoc booking, and the arithmetic turns on how many weeks a family realistically misses.

faqs.question: Do you charge for materials, past papers or mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should anybody. Examination board syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published on the boards' own sites and are the boards' copyright: they should be referenced and linked, not resold or handed out as download packs. A materials fee for board content is a charge for something freely readable at source. What a tutor legitimately adds is the marking, the sequencing and the feedback on the student's own work, and that is what the hourly rate should be buying.

faqs.question: Where does tuition money do the most work across an IGCSE year?
faqs.answer: Early, and with marking attached. One hour a week from October, with a timed paper set and marked against the published scheme between sessions, consistently does more than nothing until February followed by an intensive block at peak rates. The second best use is sequencing: book the scarce specification first, because supply narrows from January, and leave the well-supplied subjects for later in the year when tutors are still available. The least effective pattern is three weekly hours in one subject with no independent practice between them.

The published market bands on this page give you a sanity check, with each source named and dated. Then take the free trial, read the written diagnostic, and decide. Lessons here are online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time, billed as they happen, and paused rather than forfeited when the school's own examination weeks arrive.

intro.heading: Why Abu Dhabi families search for a home tutor, and what they are really buying
paragraphs: The request is almost always the same shape. A Year 10 or Year 11 student is behind in two subjects, or a DP1 student has hit Higher Level and the evenings have become a negotiation. The parent wants somebody competent in the house at a fixed hour, because that removes the organising problem: no driving to a centre at 17:00, no supervising a screen, somebody else owning the hour. That is a reasonable thing to want, and it is worth being honest about what it costs and what it gives up.

What it costs is visible in the Abu Dhabi market. A home visit prices in the tutor's travel. Published market surveys put in-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 350 per hour, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions seen between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799. Qualified online subject tutors sit lower, with one agency listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Those are other providers' published figures with the date attached, not ours.

What it gives up is choice. A tutor who can be in Al Reef at 17:00 on a Tuesday is drawn from the set of competent people who happen to live within a drivable radius and have that slot free. For general maths support in Year 9 that pool is adequate. For Cambridge Chemistry 0620 at Extended tier, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, or Higher Level Diploma Physics, the pool of people who can teach that specification against its mark scheme is small in any one city, and geography shrinks it further.

There is also a rule most families have not been told about. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated: an individual giving private lessons needs a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anybody who tells you tutoring is unregulated, or quotes you a fine figure, is working from something other than the published position.

IB Gram's own answer to all of this is online, one to one, over live video, with a shared screen and marked scripts that the family keeps and can reread months later during revision. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits exist only in our India service. The sections below set out the comparison honestly, including the cases where a visiting tutor genuinely suits a family better, and the questions worth asking any private tutor you find independently.
bullets: In-home market rates include the tutor's travel, whether or not it appears as a line item

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for nearly every home-tutor request from Abu Dhabi. What follows is less about the syllabus content than about how each one behaves inside a weekly session plan, and where specialist supply runs thin locally.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight or nine subjects, externally examined, with the tier decision locked at entry in the Cambridge subjects that tier. Sessions divide cleanly into content teaching and paper-skills work, which makes IGCSE the easiest level to support in a weekly hour. It is also the level where parents most often hire two tutors for two subjects and need the slots to not collide.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the awkward part is the clock rather than the content. Secondary school days commonly end between 14:45 and 15:30, buses run for up to an hour in the mainland communities, and a visiting tutor has to arrive after that and before the evening collapses. Online sessions in the same window do not lose the travel margin, so a 16:15 start is realistic in Al Shamkha as well as in Al Khalidiyah.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at mixed Higher and Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Internal Assessments. Demand is concentrated and seasonal: Higher Level sciences and mathematics through the year, and coursework supervision between October and February when school internal deadlines cluster. These are the requests most likely to need somebody outside a driving radius.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma supply is the real constraint in Abu Dhabi. A home tutor who teaches Higher Level Chemistry to the current guide, in the right evening slot, in one specific community, is a narrow intersection. Families on Saadiyat Island and Al Reem Island who have tried to fill it locally usually arrive having been offered a general science graduate instead, which is how a term gets spent on the wrong problem.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with no external paper until the optional MYP 5 eAssessment, which changes what tutoring is for. The useful work is building the fluency and writing stamina the Diploma will assume, not chasing a mark scheme that does not yet exist. Parents often arrive asking for exam practice and leave with a plan about manipulation speed and extended writing instead.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run a Middle Years stream and a British-curriculum stream under one roof, so a household can have one child on criteria and another on tiers in the same term. One tutor rarely covers both well. Online matching lets a family book two different specialists into consecutive slots, which a single visiting tutor cannot replicate however willing they are.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often try to fill with a visiting tutor, with an honest note on how thin local specialist supply tends to be in each. Thin supply is the main reason a family ends up with a competent generalist instead of a specialist.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: Assessed through two papers plus a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Higher Level depth in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms is the part a generalist cannot cover. Local in-home supply for current-guide Higher Level Chemistry is the single thinnest request we see from this emirate.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP)
subjects.description: The difficulty is mathematical before it is conceptual: vector resolution, rearrangement under time pressure and the Higher Level fields topic. Students arriving from a strong IGCSE grade often stall here. A tutor who teaches Physics without the mathematics behind it produces comfortable sessions and flat paper scores.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level carries Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade, with extended investigations unlike any other paper. Proof by induction, complex numbers and series work are the usual separate-tutoring topics. Families who hire for general maths help rather than for this route end up re-hiring in the second term.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The widest supply of any subject here, and the easiest to fill locally. Extended-tier algebra and the multi-step problems that combine topics are where marks go. Current assessment includes a non-calculator component, so revision has to include timed manipulation drills rather than calculator practice alone.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry carry most of the lost marks at Extended tier, alongside the pure-recall tests for ions that get left unrevised. Reasonable local supply at Core tier, noticeably thinner for Extended-tier teaching that works to the published mark scheme.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: A different paper structure from Cambridge 0625, which matters when a tutor is working from the wrong board's past papers. Electricity, moments and the equation-selection questions are the recurring losses. Ask any prospective tutor which specification code they have taught most recently.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken by a small, able group, usually alongside Mathematics A. Local in-home supply is effectively nil in most Abu Dhabi communities, because the number of people teaching it in any city is small. This is the clearest case for matching on specification rather than on distance.

subjects.name: Arabic (first and additional language)
subjects.description: Mandated alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules, and assessed separately at IGCSE and Diploma level. Demand is steady and supply is competitive locally, but the first-language Diploma route is specialised and the two should not be treated as one subject when hiring.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Won on the extended evaluation questions, where students explain two advantages and never weigh them. Diagram accuracy is a mark-scheme item in Economics. Supply is adequate locally at IGCSE and thinner for Higher Level Diploma Economics with its own internal assessment requirements.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the written paper's precision requirements decide the grade more than programming ability does. Few students need a developer; most need somebody who has marked the paper. Local specialist supply is thin at Higher Level in particular.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Communities, commutes and what they do to a session time
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi's geography is the reason the home-tutor question is really a scheduling question. The notes below are about when a session can realistically start in each community, which online delivery resolves differently from a visiting tutor.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central island district with short school runs and an older school estate nearby. One of the few areas where a 15:45 start is genuinely workable, which widens the choice of tutors in the earlier Gulf Standard Time slots.

regions.name: Al Shamkha
regions.note: A large mainland community well outside the island, where bus journeys are long and the evening starts late. A visiting tutor here is drawn from a small local pool or prices in a substantial drive; a 17:30 online slot avoids both problems.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Villa and apartment community near the airport road, popular with families whose children travel to schools in the Khalifa City corridor. Requests from here are heavily weighted to IGCSE sciences and tend to need post-18:00 slots.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: A compact, planned community with a small resident school-age population and very limited local tutoring supply. Families here are usually choosing between a long drive and an online slot, and the specification they need decides it.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: Established central district with mixed curriculum enrolment and good access to the island schools. Short commutes make early-evening sessions straightforward and make scheduling two siblings back to back realistic.

regions.name: Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland villa community with a long run to the island and to parts of the Khalifa City corridor. The commute, rather than the subject, is the usual reason families here abandon a centre-based class and move to a fixed online slot.

regions.name: Baniyas
regions.note: An older mainland community with its own schools and a long distance to the island estate. Local in-home supply skews towards general subjects rather than Extended-tier or Higher Level specialists.

regions.name: Al Maryah Island
regions.note: Small, dense and central, with almost no resident tutoring market of its own. Families here pick a slot and a specialist rather than a radius, which is exactly the pattern online matching is built for.

schoolClusters.city: Island communities: Al Khalidiyah, Al Nahyan, Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: Short school runs and the emirate's longest-established school estate. Students we support here are mostly IGCSE candidates needing Extended-tier science and mathematics, and the early-evening slot is easy to fill.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland communities: Al Shamkha, Al Reef, Shakhbout City, Baniyas
schoolClusters.note: Long bus journeys and later evenings, with enrolment spread across the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor schools. Session times here typically start at 17:30 or later, and local specialist supply for Diploma subjects is limited.

modes.description: The closest format to what families picture when they search for a home tutor: same person, same hour, every week, through a term. It is the only format that reliably moves a grade, because the tutor sets work, marks it, and sees the same error twice. It is the wrong choice six weeks before an exam with nothing diagnosed.

sections.heading: What an Abu Dhabi home visit costs once the drive is counted
paragraphs: In-home tuition prices travel, whether or not travel appears on the invoice. Market surveys put UAE in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 350 per hour, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, while qualified online subject tutors are listed from about AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB by one agency publishing its rates. The gap between those bands is not a quality difference. It is a vehicle, a fuel bill and ninety minutes of somebody's evening.

The arithmetic becomes clearer per community. A tutor teaching one hour in Al Shamkha and returning to the island spends most of an extra hour driving, in the window when Abu Dhabi's roads are busiest. Across a week of five visits in five communities, that is several unpaid hours that the hourly rate has to absorb, which is why in-home rates sit above online ones and why most in-home providers impose a minimum session length or a package rather than selling a single hour.

That minimum matters to a parent in a specific way. If a provider sells two-hour visits only, the effective weekly cost doubles whether or not the student can concentrate for two hours. Monthly in-home packages advertised in this market have been seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, against about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions from another provider. Both are other companies' published figures, surveyed in October 2026, and both will have moved by the time you read them.

The table below sets out the travel reality by community as a planning estimate from typical road distances in the late-afternoon window, not as a measured figure. The point is not the exact number of minutes. It is that a visiting tutor's realistic weekly radius in Abu Dhabi is small, and that every minute in it is paid for somewhere in the rate.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody asks and everybody should. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on the introduction of private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

Eligibility is broader than parents expect. The published list of eligible applicants includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fees listed and a completion time of two working days.

Two things follow for a family hiring privately. The first is that asking to see a permit is a normal, answerable request, not an accusation; the permit is free and quick to obtain, so an experienced tutor who does not hold one has chosen not to. The second is that no fine amount should ever be quoted to you. Press reporting has been explicit that the ministry did not specify fine amounts or detail the penalties, and figures circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

A separate rule covers organisations rather than individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with initial approval first and a window to complete the permit and licence steps. That is a different instrument from an individual's tutoring permit, and neither one makes a provider regulator-endorsed. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or licence of any kind, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Why your child's own teacher is the wrong person to hire
paragraphs: It is the first idea most parents have, and in Abu Dhabi it runs into a conduct rule. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with teachers tutoring outside school hours required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and verify it against ADEK's current published policy before relying on it.

The reasoning holds regardless of the precise wording. A teacher who sets and marks the school assessment and is also paid privately by one family in the class is in an obvious conflict, and the student carries the consequences if anybody raises it. Families sometimes propose a workaround: a teacher from the same school but a different class, or a different year group. That is still a member of staff tutoring a student enrolled at their school, which is the thing the conduct rule describes.

What a family is actually chasing here is alignment. The school teacher knows the scheme of work, the internal deadlines and the mock paper. That knowledge is obtainable without the conflict. Share the scheme of work, the assessment calendar and the marked mock with an independent tutor, and they can teach against the same sequence. The one thing an outside tutor cannot and should not have is advance knowledge of the school's unseen assessment, which is also the thing it would be inappropriate to buy.

A second workaround worth refusing is the tutor who offers access to unreleased papers, mark schemes or boundary data. Boards' syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material and should be read on the boards' own sites rather than redistributed, and anything described as advance access to unreleased material is a malpractice exposure for the student. A tutor's legitimate edge is having marked the published papers carefully, not having obtained the unpublished ones.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group - the comparison for this emirate
paragraphs: There are three honest options and each wins somewhere. A visiting tutor wins on the organising problem: no device to supervise, no connection to worry about, and a student who will not sit still for a screen is physically in the room with somebody. For primary-age children, for students with specific attention needs, and for families who simply want the hour taken off their hands, that is a real advantage and no comparison table should pretend otherwise.

Online one-to-one wins on supply, price and record. The tutor is chosen from everyone who teaches that specification rather than everyone within a drive, the rate does not carry a vehicle, and the session leaves behind an annotated script and a set of notes the student can revisit. For Extended-tier sciences, both Diploma mathematics routes and Higher Level subjects generally, supply is the deciding factor: the right specialist is rarely the nearest one.

Group classes win on price per student and lose on diagnosis. A class of four moves at the pace of the group, which suits revision of known content and does not suit a student with a specific gap. The useful combination is often a group revision class for breadth plus a handful of one-to-one sessions on the two things actually costing marks, rather than paying one-to-one rates for content the student would absorb fine in a group.

For completeness: IB Gram does not provide in-home visits in Abu Dhabi, so the in-home column below describes what the market offers rather than something we sell. Families who conclude that a visiting tutor is right for their child should hire one, ask for the MoHRE permit, and check the specification experience as carefully as they would online. We would rather publish the comparison than win the decision by leaving a column out.

sections.heading: What a shared screen does that a kitchen table cannot
paragraphs: The strongest practical argument for video delivery is not convenience, it is the record. A student photographs a past paper attempt and sends it before the session. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, then shares the annotated script on screen and walks through where each mark was awarded and where it was lost. The marked file stays with the family. Six weeks later, during revision, the student can reread exactly why three marks went missing on a moments question.

At a table, that same conversation happens in pencil on the student's only copy and lives in memory. Nothing about it is worse in the moment; it is simply not durable. The same applies to the error log a good tutor keeps across sessions. Written down and shared, it turns into a revision list. Held in the tutor's head, it ends when the engagement does, which is a loss a family has effectively paid for.

Two more mechanics matter for these subjects specifically. Graph and diagram work is easier to assess on a shared digital canvas, where the tutor can draw a line of best fit over the student's own plotted points rather than describing what is wrong with it. And for mathematics, screen-shared working lets the tutor interrupt at the step where the method mark was lost, instead of at the end where only the answer is visible.

What is genuinely harder online is the start. A student who arrives tired and unwilling is easier to move in person, and a parent who has to set up a device and then leave the room is doing more work than one who answers the door. The honest mitigation is structure: a fixed slot, a device on a desk rather than a lap, work sent in advance so the session begins with something concrete, and a short written note afterwards so the parent knows what happened without having sat through it.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the school run, prayer times and Ramadan
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's evening is tightly packed. Secondary days commonly end between 14:45 and 15:30, bus routes to the mainland communities can run close to an hour, and families then have prayer times, younger siblings and dinner to place around whatever tutoring slot is agreed. Most of the complaints we hear about tutoring, in-home or online, turn out to be complaints about the time it was booked rather than about the teaching.

Two workable patterns exist. The early slot, from 15:45 to 17:00, suits island communities with short runs and suits younger students whose concentration fades after dinner. The late slot, from 18:30 to 20:00, suits mainland communities and older Diploma students who need the earlier evening for homework. The slot to avoid is the one immediately after a long bus journey, which looks efficient on paper and produces an hour of nothing.

Ramadan reshapes the whole plan, and it is the single most common reason for a schedule to be rebuilt mid-term. School hours shorten, concentration moves, and many families prefer sessions after Iftar. Online slots move more easily than visits, because there is no journey to recalculate, and a tutor working later in the evening does not also need to drive home afterwards. It is worth agreeing the Ramadan pattern several weeks ahead rather than in the first week.

Examination weeks need the opposite treatment. During the school's own assessment weeks, a weekly session often does more harm than good: the student needs revision time, not new input. Pausing for two weeks and resuming with a marked-paper focus afterwards is usually the better plan, and it is one of the few places where a provider's willingness to pause rather than bill is worth asking about before you start.

sections.heading: Eleven questions to ask a private tutor before the first paid hour
paragraphs: If you hire independently, the quality of the hire comes down to the questions asked before money changes hands. Most parents ask about qualifications and years of experience, which are the two least diagnostic things on the list. A good tutor answers specification questions crisply and without defensiveness, and a weak one answers them with general reassurance about rapport and confidence.

The questions that actually discriminate are concrete. Which specification code have you taught most recently, and for which board. What is the weighting of the component my child is weakest in. What will you set between sessions, and will you mark it. Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. What is your position on coursework: will you look at an Internal Assessment draft, and what exactly will you do with it. How will we know in six weeks whether this is working.

Three answers should end the conversation. An offer to write, complete or substantially revise an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, which is academic malpractice and risks the student's diploma. A claim of regulator or examination-board approval, accreditation or partnership, which no tutoring provider in this market should be making unless it can show the permit or centre number. And a promise of a particular grade or a specific number of points, which nobody can make honestly because nobody controls the marking.

One more is worth adding in Abu Dhabi specifically: is anyone in this arrangement a member of staff at my child's own school. If the answer is yes, the press-reported ADEK ethics position and the permit's code of conduct both point the other way, and the sensible move is to find somebody independent. None of these questions require expertise to ask, and a tutor worth hiring will be pleased to be asked them.
bullets: Which specification code and board have you taught most recently?
What is the weighting of the component my child is weakest in?
What will you set between sessions, and who marks it?
Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit?

What evidence will we look at in six weeks to decide whether to continue?

sections.heading: What we collect about your child, and how to have it deleted
paragraphs: A tutoring enquiry collects personal data about a minor, and that deserves stating rather than burying. A request form here asks for the student's year group, subject, board and level, the next assessment date, and a parent's contact details. That is what is needed to match a specialist and nothing else. We do not need a child's photograph, their full report card, their school's internal assessment data or their date of birth to answer the question of who can teach 0620 Extended on a Tuesday.

Marked work sent for a session is used for teaching and feedback. If a family asks for it to be removed after an engagement ends, it is removed. Session notes exist so a parent can see what was covered and a tutor can keep an error log; they are not a profile and they are not shared with anybody outside the match. The UAE's personal data protection framework, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, is the governing instrument, and a privacy link sits on every page of this site.

Two patterns worth refusing elsewhere. A provider that requires a child's photograph or school grades before giving a price is collecting more than it needs for that answer. And a provider that asks for payment before any contact with a tutor is asking a family to commit before diagnosing anything. A free trial lesson with no card required solves both: you meet the tutor, you get a written diagnostic, and you decide afterwards.

Finally, the conversion path on this page is deliberately a UAE-appropriate one. Some competing pages route Abu Dhabi parents to a +91 number or show a Dubai office address on an Abu Dhabi page. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and says so rather than implying a local presence it does not have. Delivery is online, the tutors are matched by specification, and the trial costs nothing.

process.title: Send the specification and the next date
process.description: The useful enquiry names the board and syllabus code, the tier or level, the year group and the next assessment date. Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended, Year 11, mock in five weeks is enough to match a specialist immediately. Help with science, Year 11 takes two more messages before anybody can do anything with it.

process.title: Tell us the slot that survives the school run
process.description: Give us the window that works after the bus, not the window that looks tidy. Communities outside the island usually need 17:30 or later; island districts can often take 15:45. Naming the real constraint first avoids the common failure of a perfectly matched tutor in an impossible slot.

process.title: Free trial lesson, written diagnostic
process.description: The first session is free, requires no card, and runs on real questions from the student's own specification. It ends with a written note of what is costing marks and what the first month would target. The note is yours whether or not you continue, and if the match is wrong we will match again or say we cannot.

process.title: Weekly teaching, marked work in between
process.description: A fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time, work set and marked between sessions, an error log carried across lessons and a short written note after each one. Marked scripts are shared as files the family keeps, which is the part that survives the engagement and feeds revision later.

process.title: Review on evidence, pause when school exams land
process.description: Each half term we look at marked papers and the error log rather than impressions. Sessions pause during the school's own assessment weeks, when a student needs revision time more than new input, and resume with a paper-skills focus. If the evidence shows no movement, we will say so.

whyPoints.title: The pool is national, not local
whyPoints.description: Matching happens on specification and availability, so a Higher Level Chemistry specialist or a Pearson 4PM1 teacher is reachable from Al Shamkha as easily as from Al Khalidiyah. The most expensive mistake in local hiring is accepting a competent generalist because they were the only person free within a twenty-minute drive.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider or survey it came from and the month it was read. None of them is our price. That is deliberate: three of six competing pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered in full
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit, its two-year validity, the fact that it is free, the eligible categories and the official application route are all set out here with the source named. No fine figure appears, because the ministry has not published one and the numbers circulating online cannot be verified.

whyPoints.title: A published coursework boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, question methods and give feedback on the student's own draft. No text is supplied for submission, and no board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes are redistributed as downloads. In a market where one site sells completed Internal Assessments outright, that boundary is the thing worth checking first.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can hold
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with the mark scheme applied, a carried-forward error log and a written note after each lesson. We publish no success percentages and no ratings, because any figure we cannot show you the method behind is not evidence. The marked work is the evidence.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery and about limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, operates no UAE centre and holds no regulator accreditation. Where a subject has no specialist free, you are told the wait or told plainly that we cannot cover it.

faqs.question: Can I book an IB or IGCSE home tutor to come to our villa in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for families in Abu Dhabi is delivered online, one to one, over live video with a shared screen; home visits are a service we run only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. The reason is supply rather than preference: the people who teach Cambridge 0620 Extended or Higher Level Diploma Chemistry well are not reliably the people living a twenty-minute drive from any given community. If a visiting tutor is genuinely what suits your child, hire one locally, ask to see the MoHRE private tuition permit, and check which specification they have taught most recently.

faqs.question: How much do home tutors charge per hour in Abu Dhabi right now?
faqs.answer: Market surveys read in October 2026 put UAE in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500 depending on level and subject. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been listed between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799. Qualified online subject tutors sit lower: one agency publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Those are other providers' figures with the date attached, not our price list, and they move. Treat any quote without a stated session length and inclusion list as incomplete.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi need a licence or permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the published eligible categories include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the application through its smart app, website and e-services with a two working day completion time. No fine amount has been published, so do not accept a figure from anyone.

faqs.question: Is it allowed to pay one of my child's own Abu Dhabi school teachers for private lessons?
faqs.answer: It is the wrong hire in Abu Dhabi. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current position against ADEK's published document before relying on it. The conflict is obvious in any case: the same person would be setting the assessment and being paid by one family in the class. Share the scheme of work with an independent tutor instead, which gets you the alignment without the conflict.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor better than online for a Year 11 doing Extended-tier sciences?
faqs.answer: On supply, no. Extended-tier Cambridge sciences need somebody who teaches to the published mark scheme and knows the practical or alternative-to-practical component as a format, and in any one city that group is small. Restricting it to people who can drive to your community at 17:00 usually means accepting a generalist. On organisation, a visiting tutor can be better, particularly for younger students or where a parent cannot supervise a device. The honest split is that in-home wins the logistics and online wins the specialist, and for Extended tier in Year 11 the specialist is normally the thing that moves the grade.

faqs.question: What time can sessions start if we live in Al Shamkha or Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Online, around 16:15 is realistic once the bus has run. For a visiting tutor, expect 17:15 to 17:30 at the earliest, because the drive from the island in the late afternoon runs 35 to 50 minutes each way as a planning estimate. That difference compounds across a week: the same tutor can take an earlier slot and a later one online, whereas a visit effectively consumes the whole evening. Island districts such as Al Khalidiyah and Al Nahyan can usually take 15:45 either way, which is why early slots are easier to fill there.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in different year groups?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is usually the wrong request. A tutor strong on Middle Years Programme criteria work is rarely the same person who teaches Extended-tier IGCSE chemistry against a mark scheme, and competence across both at once is less common than willingness. The better arrangement in an Abu Dhabi household is two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, which costs no extra organising online because there is no second journey. You get one point of contact for scheduling and separate session notes, so one child's progress is not blurred into the other's.

faqs.question: How do sessions change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They move, and it is worth agreeing the pattern several weeks ahead rather than in the first week. School hours shorten, concentration shifts through the day, and many Abu Dhabi families prefer sessions after Iftar. Online slots absorb that more easily than visits, because there is no journey to recalculate at either end and a tutor teaching late is not then driving home. We also recommend reducing frequency rather than cancelling entirely: one session a week kept in place is easier to restart than a month-long gap, particularly for a Year 11 or DP2 student.

faqs.question: Will the tutor mark past papers, or only teach in the session?
faqs.answer: Marking between sessions is the part that moves marks, so it should be in the arrangement explicitly. The pattern here is that the student photographs or scans their attempt and sends it before the lesson, the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, and the annotated script is shared on screen and talked through during the session. The file stays with the family and feeds revision later. Ask any prospective tutor, in-home or online, what they set between sessions and who marks it. A tutor who only teaches during the hour is selling half the service.

faqs.question: What does a free trial actually include, and is there a catch?
faqs.answer: One full session at no cost, with no card required and no package purchase beforehand. It runs on real questions from your child's own specification rather than a generic assessment, and it ends with a written diagnostic naming the two or three things costing the most marks. That note is yours whether or not you continue. The only condition is that it is one session per student, not an open-ended run of free lessons. If the tutor match feels wrong, say so and we will either match again or tell you honestly that we cannot cover the subject properly.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, question whether a research question is answerable with the available data, challenge the reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor cannot supply text, rewrite sections to completion or hand over a finished investigation. The supervising teacher authenticates the work, and IB academic-honesty rules make the alternative an expulsion risk for the student. One site in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments, which is worth knowing about before you compare prices.

faqs.question: We only want help for the last ten weeks before the exams. Is that sensible?
faqs.answer: It can be, if the goal is paper skills rather than content. Ten weeks is enough to drill command terms, fix the method-mark discipline that loses marks on work the student can actually do, and run timed papers with strict marking. It is not enough to teach a year of missing content, and a provider that tells you otherwise is selling hope. The useful first step is a diagnostic session that establishes which of those two situations you are in, because the answer changes whether the ten weeks are well spent or simply expensive.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking several providers for a quote?
faqs.answer: Five things, and the same five to everyone: the board and syllabus code, the tier or level, the year group, the next assessment date, and a photograph of one recent piece of marked work. Then ask each provider for the hourly rate, the minimum session length, what is set and marked between sessions, and the cancellation terms. Quotes become comparable the moment session length and inclusions are fixed; without them, an AED 200 hour and an AED 350 hour may be the same thing or entirely different things, and you cannot tell from the number.

faqs.question: What personal information do you need about my child to match a tutor?
faqs.answer: Year group, subject, board and level, the next assessment date and a parent's contact details. That is enough. We do not ask for a photograph, a full report card, a date of birth or a school's internal assessment data, because none of those are needed to decide who can teach a specification on a Tuesday evening. Marked work sent for a session is used for teaching and removed on request when an engagement ends. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection is the governing framework, and the privacy link sits on every page.

faqs.question: Do you have an office in Abu Dhabi we can visit?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying a local presence it does not have is worth a second look. IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, holds no regulator approval, accreditation or licence, and delivers to Abu Dhabi families online. Two competing pages in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers, and one displays a Dubai address on a page written for Abu Dhabi. Asking a provider directly where it is based, and who employs the tutor who will teach your child, is a reasonable question with a short answer.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Decide the format on supply, not on habit
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are hiring an IB IGCSE home tutor in Abu Dhabi, the decision worth making carefully is not online against in-home in the abstract. It is whether the person who can actually teach your child's specification is reachable within a twenty-minute drive of your community. For Year 9 maths they often are. For Extended-tier chemistry, both Diploma mathematics routes or Higher Level sciences, they usually are not, and that is the gap online matching closes. Send the syllabus code, the tier, the next assessment date and one piece of marked work, and the first session is a free trial that ends with a written diagnostic you keep.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE at Core and Extended tier and IB at Standard and Higher Level over live video. Each session is a working session: a paper marked in advance, a screen shared, and a written note afterwards saying what was covered and what was set.

intro.heading: The question behind the search is mechanical, not philosophical
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi who search for online tutoring have usually already decided that the subject help is needed. What they are unsure about is the delivery. Will a fifteen-year-old actually engage with a screen for an hour. What stops it becoming supervised homework. Who is watching that the time is used. How does anybody mark handwritten working remotely. What happens in a physics subject that has a practical component. These are reasonable, answerable questions, and most tutoring sites answer none of them.

The short version is that a well-run online session is more structured than an in-person one, because it has to be. There is no opening five minutes of settling in, no hunting for a textbook, no conversation with a parent at the door. Work is sent before the lesson and marked before the lesson starts, so the hour begins with something concrete on screen. That structure is also what makes the session inspectable afterwards, which an in-person session is not.

The second thing worth understanding is what Gulf Standard Time does to the tutor pool. A 17:00 slot in Abu Dhabi is 18:30 for a tutor working from India and early afternoon for one in the United Kingdom, which means the early and middle evening here draws on a wide pool of working specialists. A 20:30 slot is a different and smaller pool. Choosing a slot is therefore partly choosing how much specialist choice you have, and parents are rarely told that.

On subjects with practical work, the honest answer takes a paragraph rather than a sentence. Cambridge IGCSE sciences assess practical skills either through a practical test or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the written route is used by most international centres; that paper is examined like any other and is highly teachable remotely. In the IB sciences the internal investigation is carried out at school under the teacher's supervision and contributes a fifth of the grade. A tutor supports the design, the data handling and the write-up criteria. A tutor does not run the experiment and does not produce the report. Parents who understand that division early stop worrying about the laboratory and start asking the more useful question, which is whether the student is also losing the written practical marks that any taught candidate can secure.

Delivery here is online by design rather than by compromise. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi and operates no centre in the UAE; home visits exist only in our India service. For a family in Al Jubail Island or on the Corniche that means the choice of tutor is governed by which specialist teaches the specification, not by who can reach the building before 18:00, and the sections below set out exactly what that hour contains.
bullets: Work is sent and marked before the session, so the hour starts on evidence rather than on catching up
A shared digital canvas lets a tutor correct a line of best fit over the student's own plotted points
Session notes and annotated scripts remain with the family and feed revision months later
IB internal investigations are carried out and supervised at school, never by a tutor

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The three programmes below behave differently over video. What follows is about delivery rather than syllabus: what works well on a screen, what needs the school, and what a parent should expect to see.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The level best suited to video delivery, because the assessment is entirely written and the work divides cleanly into content teaching and paper technique. Handwritten attempts are photographed, marked against the published scheme, and talked through on a shared screen. The alternative-to-practical paper in the Cambridge sciences is taught as a format and responds strongly to remote drilling.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi IGCSE students usually have a tight evening, with secondary days ending between 14:45 and 15:30 and long bus runs to the mainland communities. Online slots from 15:45 in the island districts and from about 16:15 further out remove the travel margin at both ends, which in practice is the difference between a session that happens weekly and one that is rescheduled twice a month.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Taught well over video with one firm boundary: the internal investigation and the written core components are school-supervised and student-authored. A tutor teaches criteria, questions a method, challenges reasoning and gives feedback on the student's own draft. Higher Level papers benefit particularly from screen-shared marking, because extended responses are assessed on sustained reasoning that is visible line by line.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma specialists are the scarcest resource in this emirate, and video delivery is what makes them reachable at all for families outside the central districts. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher working to the current guide, free at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time, is a realistic match online and a thin prospect within a twenty-minute drive of Al Shamkha or Al Ghadeer.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Works online with more structure than older students need. Shorter segments, visible tasks and a clear end-of-session output hold attention better than an hour of discussion. The useful focus is the fluency and extended-writing stamina the Diploma will later assume, both of which can be set, submitted and marked between sessions.
programmes.countryNote: Middle years students in Abu Dhabi are often the ones a parent worries most about on a screen, with good reason. The practical mitigations are specific: a desk rather than a bed, a device on a stand, the camera on, work sent in advance, and a parent within earshot for the first two sessions. After that, most settle into the format faster than their parents expect.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below carries a note on how it is actually delivered over video and where the limits are, which is a more useful thing to know than a topic list before you book.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Among the strongest subjects online. Working is photographed and marked in advance, then the tutor interrupts on the shared screen at the exact step where a method mark was lost rather than at the final answer. Non-calculator manipulation drills are set as timed tasks between sessions and marked strictly.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Both papers permit a calculator, so remote work focuses on question selection, vectors, histograms with unequal class widths and iteration. A shared digital canvas is used for graph and transformation work, where the tutor can draw over the student's own plot instead of describing the error.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is taught as a written examination skill: describing a reproducible method, naming variables, identifying anomalous results and drawing a line of best fit. These are marked-scheme behaviours and are drilled effectively from past papers without a laboratory bench.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations are set to a fixed layout and marked for method rather than answer, which works better remotely than in person because the written attempt arrives before the lesson. Tests for ions and separation techniques are handled as spaced recall testing between sessions.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Command-term discipline is the main gain available, and it is taught by rewriting answers the student has already written. Genetic cross notation and osmosis explanations are drilled with annotated diagrams on the shared canvas, which the student keeps as a revision file.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: Two papers plus the internal investigation, which carries a fifth of the grade and is carried out at school under the teacher's supervision. Online work covers data-based questions, mechanism reasoning and the investigation's criteria. The experiment itself and the writing remain the student's, supervised by the school.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP)
subjects.description: Extended responses are marked against the markbands and reviewed line by line on screen, which is where the gain is: students lose Paper 2 marks on structure as often as on physics. Early work is frequently mathematical, and the diagnostic should establish that before a plan is bought.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 3 at Higher Level needs extended investigation practice under time pressure, submitted and marked rather than discussed. Proof by induction and series work are taught on a shared canvas where each line of a proof can be challenged as it is written.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: The subject where marking between sessions matters most, because the gain comes from a second and third draft rather than from explanation. Essays are annotated against the level criteria and returned as files, and the Individual Oral is rehearsed on video with the recording reviewed.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Supported against the school's own prescribed material rather than any substitute content, because published UAE guidance is explicit that different or additional content for the mandatory subjects requires prior ministry permission. Delivery is conversational practice, written structure and examination technique.

sections.heading: What the sixty minutes actually contains
paragraphs: A good online session is organised before it begins. Work goes out after the previous lesson, comes back at least a day ahead, and is marked against the published mark scheme before the student logs in. That single piece of sequencing is what separates a working session from supervised homework, and it is the first thing to ask any prospective tutor about, because a tutor who marks live is spending your paid hour reading.

The opening five minutes are a check rather than a chat: two or three questions on last week's redo task, answered on the shared canvas. If those are secure the session moves on. If they are not, the plan for the hour changes, which is a decision a tutor should be willing to make visibly. The middle forty minutes carry the teaching or the marked-paper review, and the final ten set the next task and write the note.

What a parent sees is deliberately not a live feed of the hour. It is the annotated script, the saved canvas and a short written note naming what was covered, what was set and what is still weak. Several Abu Dhabi families tell us they read the note on the way to work the next morning, which is a more realistic form of oversight than sitting in a room for an hour and hearing a conversation they cannot assess.

sections.heading: Gulf Standard Time, and the pool each slot opens
paragraphs: Choosing a session time in Abu Dhabi is partly choosing how much specialist choice you get, and almost nobody explains this. Gulf Standard Time sits an hour and a half behind the working day in India and three to four hours ahead of the United Kingdom depending on the season. A 17:00 slot here is 18:30 in India and early afternoon in Britain, which is why the early and middle evening draws on the widest pool of practising specialists.

Push later and the pool narrows in a specific direction. A 20:30 start is late evening for tutors working from India and is outside the working day for most European-based specialists. It remains perfectly fillable for well-supplied subjects such as Cambridge Mathematics 0580, and it is a genuine constraint for a current-guide Higher Level Chemistry match. Families who can take an earlier slot and choose not to are trading specialist choice for convenience without being told that is the trade.

Pull earlier and a different constraint appears: the school day. Secondary days in Abu Dhabi commonly end between 14:45 and 15:30, and bus runs to the mainland communities can take close to an hour. A 15:45 start is realistic in the island districts and unrealistic in Al Shamkha or Al Ghadeer. The UAE school week runs Monday to Friday with Friday typically shorter, which makes weekend mornings a useful and under-used option for longer sessions.

One practical note on Ramadan. School hours shorten, concentration moves through the day, and many families prefer sessions after Iftar. Online slots absorb that change far more easily than any arrangement involving travel, and the sensible approach is to agree the Ramadan pattern several weeks ahead rather than renegotiating it in the first week. Reducing frequency is better than pausing entirely, because a kept slot restarts more easily than a missing month.

sections.heading: When the connection drops, and other things that go wrong
paragraphs: Technical problems are not a reason to avoid online tuition, but pretending they do not happen is how a family loses three sessions before anybody addresses it. The failures are predictable and nearly all of them have a one-line fix agreed in advance. What matters is that the fallback is decided before it is needed, so a dropped call becomes a two-minute interruption rather than a lost hour and an argument about whether it is billable.

The most common issue is not bandwidth, it is the device. A session on a phone cannot show a marked A4 script legibly, and a student squinting at a page on a six-inch screen will disengage within twenty minutes regardless of how good the teaching is. A laptop or tablet on a stand, a desk, headphones and the camera on account for most of the difference between a session that works and one that does not.

The second most common is the submission step. Work that arrives an hour before the lesson cannot be marked properly in advance, which collapses the structure described above. Photographing a four-page attempt in reasonable light takes two minutes, and agreeing a fixed submission deadline removes the single most frequent cause of a wasted session. Where a family cannot manage advance submission reliably, the session shape should change rather than the deadline being quietly ignored.

On billing and interruptions, the position here is plain: a session cut short by a technical failure at either end is rescheduled or completed, not charged as delivered. That is worth asking any provider before booking, alongside the cancellation notice, because the answers tell you how the operation treats its own failures.
