abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi families arrive on this page from four different programmes, and the evidence that tuition is working looks different in each. A PYP parent wants to see a reading behaviour change. A DP parent wants to see a Paper 2 mark move. The programme decides what counts as proof.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year qualification most British-curriculum schools in Abu Dhabi run before Sixth Form or the Diploma. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes, Edexcel International GCSE codes begin with a digit and a subject letter pair. The tiering question matters: Cambridge maths 0580 splits Core and Extended, Edexcel 4MA1 splits Foundation and Higher, and the tier a school entered your child for caps the grade available.
programmes.countryNote: Evidence on an IGCSE subject is unusually easy to collect because past papers are plentiful and mark schemes are published. A parent in Abu Dhabi can ask for the script, the mark scheme page reference and the running total of marks lost by question type. Within a term that becomes a clear picture: a child losing marks on method rather than knowledge needs a different set of sessions from one losing marks on recall.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated by the IB. The written papers are sat in a single session, which is why a two-year plan with visible checkpoints matters more here than in any other programme.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is concentrated in a small number of schools, so a subject combination that is ordinary nationally can be rare locally. A student taking Economics HL with Chemistry HL and Spanish B may be the only one in their year group doing so. Proof of progress then has to come from the subject's own criteria and from marked papers, because there is no useful class average to compare against.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with the criteria wording doing most of the work. MYP reports often read as a wall of letters and numbers, and parents frequently cannot tell whether a 5 in Criterion C is a problem. It usually is, and it is usually a specific, fixable problem.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is where Abu Dhabi families most often ask for help, because the assessment language changes completely. We treat the criteria letters as the evidence base: a student scoring well on Criterion A knowledge and poorly on Criterion D reflection in Sciences has a writing problem, not a science problem, and the session plan says so in writing.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, so progress is recorded through observation, portfolios and conferences rather than marks. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habits that make the MYP survivable, and it is deliberately light touch.
programmes.countryNote: Because there is no mark to track, the evidence record for a PYP child in Abu Dhabi is behavioural and specific: words read per minute on an unseen passage, the number of steps a child can hold in a multi-step problem, whether they can explain a method back. Those are the numbers that go in the session notes, and a parent can check them at home in five minutes.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families bring to us most often, described by where marks actually leave the paper. Each description is the thing a tutor would write in the first session note after reading a marked script.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks leave on the non-calculator paper and on the reasoning questions where a correct answer with no visible method earns little. The recoverable pattern is almost always method presentation and algebraic fluency rather than topic ignorance, which is why a marked script is more diagnostic than a test score.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Heavy on modelling, statistics and technology use. Students lose marks by giving un-rounded answers, omitting units, or failing to interpret a result in context after calculating it correctly. The fix is a checklist habit, and progress on it is visible within three or four marked papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks at Higher Level. At IGCSE the losses cluster in mole calculations and in the practical paper's planning and evaluation questions. Both patterns show up clearly once two papers are marked by question type rather than by total.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where IGCSE candidates lose most, and the extended-response questions are where they lose silently because partial method goes unwritten. At Diploma level the loss moves to the data-analysis and uncertainty questions, which are teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The content is learnable and the marks are lost on command terms. A question that says outline, explain and discuss wants three different shapes of answer, and a student who writes the same paragraph for all three caps their own grade. Marked scripts make this obvious in one sitting.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The most requested subject in Abu Dhabi, and the one where tier matters most. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available, so the first useful question is which paper your child is actually entered for. After that, the losses are usually in algebra, bearings and compound measures.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0500 and 0475
subjects.description: Reading marks come back fastest because they depend on technique a tutor can demonstrate: annotation, question order, and using the extract rather than remembering the text. Writing marks move more slowly and need marked drafts rather than lessons about writing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation sentence carry more marks than the content. Students who can define everything and evaluate nothing sit at a predictable ceiling, and lifting it is a drilling job with a clear before-and-after on marked answers.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole game. Generic answers that never mention the stimulus material lose application and analysis marks regardless of how much theory they contain, and the correction is mechanical once a tutor shows it on the student's own script.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0478 and 0417
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the precise wording of definition questions are where IGCSE marks go. At Diploma level the internal assessment carries the risk, because a working program with a thin success-criteria record scores badly against the criteria.

sections.heading: What typing near me actually returns in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: A local search for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Abu Dhabi returns three kinds of result, and only one of them is a tutor. The first kind is a tuition centre with premises, which is a business holding a permit to operate from a location and employing whoever it has recruited. The second is a marketplace listing that sorts by distance because distance is the only field it reliably holds. The third is a blog post written to rank, with a contact form at the bottom and no named tutor anywhere on it.

None of those three tell you the thing you need. A centre two streets away may be excellent at IGCSE maths and have nobody at all for Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level. A marketplace listing ranked first for your district may be first because the tutor set their location to the city centre. And the blog post will quote a rate range without saying who charges it, which the October 2026 competitor audit found on page after page: three of six ranking pages in this cluster published no price at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars.

What a parent actually wants from a near-me search is a shortlist filtered by subject, level and syllabus code, then checked for whether the person is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE, then tested in a trial lesson. Distance belongs nowhere in that sequence once lessons are delivered over video. The table below sets out, district by district, what the map gives you and what it leaves out.

The honest conclusion is that proximity is a convenience variable that stopped mattering when the delivery moved to video, and that the variable it was standing in for, accountability, now has to be supplied directly. That is what the rest of this page is about.

sections.heading: Proximity against specialism: the twenty-minute radius problem
paragraphs: Put a compass point on any Abu Dhabi address and draw a twenty-minute drive. Inside that circle you will find people who can teach Key Stage 3 maths, people who can teach IGCSE maths, and with luck one person who has taught Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the last two years. Widen the circle to the whole emirate and the Higher Level count rises, but so does the travel time, and travel time is the thing that kills a weekly slot by November.

Now remove the circle. The pool becomes every tutor who can be on a video call at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time, which includes specialists based in the UAE and specialists based elsewhere who teach the same syllabus. For a mainstream subject such as IGCSE maths the difference is marginal, because supply is good locally. For a narrow combination such as Higher Level Economics with Higher Level Chemistry, or an Edexcel International GCSE modular route, the difference is the whole decision.

This is the trade a family makes without being told they are making it. The convenience of a nearby tutor is real and immediate. The cost of it is paid later, in a term spent with someone who knows the subject but not the syllabus, or knows the syllabus but not the tier. We publish the trade openly because the alternative, pretending a local generalist and a syllabus specialist are the same purchase, is how a parent ends up three months in with no movement and no explanation.

Availability transparency matters here too. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject and level, we say so and offer the specialist we do have, with the time zone and the rate stated before anything is booked. No competitor page in the ten query clusters we audited discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number without mentioning it.

sections.heading: The evidence pack: six artefacts and what each one proves
paragraphs: A parent cannot sit in on every lesson, and should not have to. What they can do is ask what the arrangement produces, and then read it. Six artefacts cover almost everything worth knowing, and all six are cheap for a competent tutor to produce because they are the by-product of teaching properly rather than extra administration.

The first is the diagnostic note from the opening session, which should name the error classes found and the evidence for each. The second is the weekly session note. The third is a marked script with mark-scheme references. The fourth is an error log that tracks each identified weakness from first appearance to retirement. The fifth is the dated draft history on any Internal Assessment or Extended Essay work. The sixth is a termly summary that compares the student against their own earlier papers rather than against a class.

What makes these useful is that each one has a limit. A session note proves attendance and focus, not learning. A marked script proves a mark on one paper on one day, not a trend. An error log proves a pattern, which is the closest thing to proof available before results day. Knowing the limits stops a parent over-reading a good week and panicking at a bad one, and it stops a provider using a cheerful note as a substitute for a mark.

Ask for the pack at the start rather than at the end. A provider who cannot describe what you will receive after four weeks is telling you something, and a provider who promises a specific grade in exchange for a specific number of hours is telling you something worse. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be read as making a sales claim rather than an academic one.

sections.heading: How to read a marked script when you do not know the subject
paragraphs: This is a skill, it takes about fifteen minutes to learn, and it changes the conversation with any tutor permanently. Start at the back of the script rather than the front. The final questions carry the most marks and are the ones most often abandoned, and a pattern of blank final questions is a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem. Timing problems are among the fastest things to fix, and a tutor who has not noticed is not reading the script either.

Next, look only at the command term in each question where marks were lost. Examination papers use a controlled vocabulary: state, outline, describe, explain, analyse, discuss, evaluate, justify, deduce, show that. Each one demands a particular shape of answer, and each is worth a predictable number of marks. A student who writes a description when the paper said explain has lost marks on a translation error, not on content. Group the lost marks by command term and the diagnosis usually writes itself.

Third, check whether the method is visible. In maths and the sciences, a correct final answer with no working shown earns fewer marks than an incorrect answer with full method. This single habit accounts for a large share of avoidable loss in both Cambridge and Edexcel scripts, and it is a presentation discipline rather than an intellectual one. Ask the tutor to show you three examples on your child's own paper. If they cannot find three, ask why not.

Finally, ignore the total. A total tells you where a child stood on one morning against one paper, and nothing about direction. Two scripts marked three weeks apart, grouped by question type, tell you far more than a mock percentage. This is why our marking returns the grouping rather than only the number, and why the termly summary compares a student against their own earlier scripts rather than against a cohort we have no business publishing figures about.
bullets: Read the script from the last question forwards
Group lost marks by command term, not by topic
Check whether method is written down, not just the answer
Count abandoned questions separately from wrong ones
Compare two scripts by question type before reading either total

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of a record, week by week
paragraphs: Abstract promises about progress tracking mean very little, so here is the concrete version: what a term of one weekly session on one IGCSE subject looks like on paper, with what gets filed each week. This is a model, not a guarantee, and the pace varies with the student, the subject and how much of the syllabus has been taught at school by the time the sessions begin.

The shape matters more than the specific weeks. The first three weeks are diagnostic and produce more evidence than teaching. Weeks four to eight are where error classes are worked and retired, and where the marked work starts to show movement by question type. Weeks nine to twelve are consolidation under timed conditions, where the question is no longer whether the student knows something but whether they can produce it in the time available with the method written down.

A parent reading this record should be able to answer three questions at any point: what is currently being worked on, what evidence exists that it has changed, and what is next. If the answer to the second question is a feeling rather than a document, the arrangement is not being run properly, whoever is running it and however near your home they live.

Note what is absent from the table. There is no predicted grade, no percentage improvement and no promise about results day. Those numbers are available from nobody honestly, and the competitor audit found several pages publishing exactly that kind of figure with no sample size, date or method attached to it. A record of work done and change measured is a smaller claim and a true one.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection reports and what a rating does not tell you
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge. The UAE government's own description is that ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK publishes inspection outcomes for the schools it oversees. This matters to a tuition decision in a narrower way than most parents assume, and it is worth being precise about why.

An inspection rating is a whole-school judgement built from many strands: leadership, provision, safeguarding, outcomes across phases, and progress against previous recommendations. It is a statement about an institution. It is not a statement about the Higher Level Chemistry teaching your daughter receives in a set of eleven students on a Tuesday afternoon, and it cannot be. A strongly rated school can have one subject with a staffing gap, and a mid-rated school can have an outstanding maths department.

What an inspection report is genuinely useful for is the narrative detail rather than the headline band. Reports name strands where attainment lags, and if the strand named is the subject your child is struggling in, you have independent corroboration of something you suspected. If the report names something else entirely and your child is still losing marks, the problem is more likely to be individual, which is precisely the case tutoring addresses.

The regulator map across the UAE is worth knowing if your family moves between emirates, which happens often. Dubai sits under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or endorsement from any of them, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment drafts: the record that protects the student
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and every one of them must be the student's own work. The IB's academic-honesty framework makes the student responsible for authenticity, and a school supervisor signs to confirm it. That places a hard boundary around what any tutor may do, and the boundary is not a matter of opinion or of house style.

A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss the suitability of a research question, read a draft and give feedback, and ask questions that make the student notice a gap. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sentences, restructure a section on the student's behalf, or hand over a finished piece of work. The difference is visible in the artefact: feedback keyed to criterion letters and questions for the student to answer, rather than tracked changes inside their document.

The practical protection is the draft history. Each review session works from a dated copy of what the student has produced, and the copies are retained. If authorship is ever questioned, the sequence of drafts shows a piece of work developing in one person's hands, with the tutor's comments visible as comments rather than as text. This is a defence a student can actually use, and it costs nothing to maintain.

The reason this section exists on a page about finding nearby tuition is that the UAE market contains providers selling the opposite. The October 2026 audit found a provider openly offering completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach and, for the student, an IB malpractice exposure that can end a Diploma. No IB Gram tutor supplies assessed work, edits a draft to completion, or acts as an author on any coursework.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached to it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The u.ae guidance states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the words of the same guidance, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

For an Abu Dhabi family there is a second consideration. UAE press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carrying a similar restriction. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and verify it against the current policy document if it affects a decision you are about to make. The practical upshot is simple: your child's own subject teacher is not the right person to pay privately.

A tuition business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, and in Dubai needs an educational services permit from KHDA for a training institute. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, so any provider describing itself as regulator-approved should be asked to show the permit number. This is also the single most common overstatement in the UAE tutoring market.

sections.heading: When the evidence says pause, change focus, or change tutor
paragraphs: The point of keeping a record is that it can tell you to stop. Most tutoring arrangements end because somebody loses interest, which means the decision was never made, only drifted into. A record makes the decision available, and there are three distinct versions of it that families confuse with each other.

The first is pause. Pause is right when the evidence shows the error classes have been retired and the student is working independently at the level they need. Paying for maintenance sessions after that point is buying reassurance, and it is better to stop and re-book before the next assessment block than to keep a slot running out of habit. Several of our Abu Dhabi families run exactly this pattern across a two-year Diploma.

The second is change focus. Change focus is right when the marked work shows one error class stubbornly unmoved while others have cleared. That usually means the diagnosis was wrong rather than the teaching: a student losing marks in Physics extended-response questions may have a writing problem that a Physics tutor will keep treating as a Physics problem. Moving the work to the actual weakness is cheaper than adding hours to the wrong one.

The third is change tutor. Change tutor is right when four or more weeks have produced session notes but no measurable change by question type, or when the student cannot explain what they worked on last week. Neither of those is a character judgement; some pairings simply do not work. We treat a replacement request as routine, and we do not ask a family to justify it. What we do ask is that the next tutor receives the error log, so the twelve weeks already spent are not re-spent from scratch.

whyPoints.description: Session notes, marked scripts with mark-scheme references, an error log and a dated draft history are produced as a matter of course, not on request. whyPoints.title: Built around the Abu Dhabi school day
whyPoints.description: Slots are set on Gulf Standard Time around actual school finish times and the eastern-corridor commute, with session timing shifted during Ramadan and around assessment blocks. A slot that works in October and not in March is not a slot, and a record that stops in March is not a record.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to live near us in Abu Dhabi to be useful?
faqs.answer: No. Distance affects convenience and nothing else once lessons are delivered live over video, and it has no relationship to whether a tutor has taught your child's syllabus and tier. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition online to Abu Dhabi families and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What proximity used to supply was visibility, and that is replaced here by a written record: session notes, marked scripts with mark-scheme references, and an error log you can read without knowing the subject.

faqs.question: What should I ask to see after four weeks of lessons?
faqs.answer: Four things. A diagnostic note from the first session naming the error classes found and the evidence for each. Four session notes saying what was taught and what was set. At least one marked piece of work with references to the published mark scheme beside the lost marks. An error log showing which weaknesses have moved. If all four exist and nothing has changed by question type, that is a reason to change focus or change tutor. If they do not exist at all, the arrangement is not being run properly, however good the lessons feel.

faqs.question: How do I read a marked paper if I do not know the subject myself?
faqs.answer: Start at the last question and work backwards, because abandoned final questions indicate a timing problem rather than a knowledge one. Then look only at the command term in each question where marks were lost: state, explain, analyse and discuss each demand a different shape of answer, and mismatches cluster. Then check whether method is written down, since a correct answer with no working earns less than a wrong answer with full method. Ignore the total. Two scripts a few weeks apart, grouped by question type, tell you far more than any single percentage.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a few streets away better than a specialist on a video call?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject. For IGCSE maths, local supply in Abu Dhabi is good and a nearby centre may be a reasonable choice. For Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Economics or an Edexcel modular route, the nearest centre is unlikely to hold a specialist, and you would be paying for convenience rather than expertise. Ask the centre which syllabus code and tier the assigned tutor has taught, and how many times. A centre that cannot answer at subject level is selling rooms and hours rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What counts as evidence that tuition is working rather than just a feeling?
faqs.answer: Movement in lost marks grouped by question type, measured across at least two marked papers sat under similar conditions. Everything else is a leading indicator: fewer abandoned questions, method written down without prompting, the student able to explain last week's work unprompted. Those are real and they usually arrive first. What is not evidence is a cheerful session note, a child who enjoys the lessons, or a single good mock. A term that produces three marked scripts and an error log gives you something you can actually read a trend from.

faqs.question: How long before any of this shows up in a school report?
faqs.answer: School reports are slow instruments. They are usually written on data gathered weeks earlier, they aggregate several components, and they compare a student against a cohort rather than against their own earlier work. A change visible in marked papers in week six may not appear in a report until the following term. That is why we track against the student's own previous scripts. If you want an earlier signal, ask the subject teacher directly what has changed in class, which is quicker and more specific than waiting for a report cycle.

faqs.question: Can we see what the tutor writes about our child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should read it rather than filing it. The session note is written for a parent, not for a teacher audience, and it names the error class worked on, the material used, and what the student should attempt before the next lesson. The diagnostic note and the error log are the same. Nothing is written in the record that we would not say to you directly. If a note is vague enough that you cannot tell what happened in the hour, that is worth raising, and it is usually a sign the hour was vague too.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection band tell me about my child's lessons?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents expect. An inspection outcome is a whole-school judgement covering leadership, provision, safeguarding and outcomes across every phase. It is not a judgement about the teaching your child receives in one subject set. The useful part of a report is the narrative: if it names a strand where attainment lags and that is the subject your child is struggling in, you have independent corroboration. If the report praises that department and your child is still losing marks, the problem is probably individual, which is the case one-to-one work addresses.

faqs.question: My child says the sessions are useful but the marks have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnosis problem before treating it as a teaching problem. Pull the error log and check whether one class has stayed unmoved while others cleared. A common pattern is a student losing marks in extended-response questions across several subjects, which is a writing and structure issue that each subject tutor keeps treating as their own subject's issue. Moving the work to the real weakness is cheaper than adding hours. If the log shows no movement anywhere after four weeks of notes, ask for a different tutor and send the log with the request.

faqs.question: What record should exist of Internal Assessment supervision?
faqs.answer: A dated copy of each draft the student produced, plus the tutor's feedback keyed to criterion letters and kept separate from the student's text. That sequence demonstrates a piece of work developing in one person's hands, which is a defence the student can use if authenticity is ever questioned. What should not exist is tracked changes inside the document from the tutor, or a version where sentences appeared that the student cannot explain. No IB Gram tutor supplies text, edits to completion or acts as an author on any assessed component, and the school supervisor's process always takes precedence.

faqs.question: Should we compare our child to the class average or to their own last paper?
faqs.answer: To their own last paper, for tutoring purposes. A class average tells you about a cohort, which changes between sets, between years and between schools, and tells you nothing about which marks your child can recover. Self-comparison by question type tells you exactly that. The cohort comparison does matter for one decision, which is whether a subject choice or tier is right in the first place, and that is a conversation for the school. Our termly summaries deliberately compare a student only against their own earlier scripts.

faqs.question: How many past papers should be marked before a June series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, marked far more carefully than most families imagine. Three or four full papers sat to time and marked properly against the published scheme, with lost marks grouped and then actually worked on, beats a dozen papers skimmed for a percentage. The marking is where the value sits, not the sitting. The one thing worth adding in the final fortnight is a timed paper with no marking attached, purely to practise pacing, because pace under pressure is a separate skill from accuracy.

faqs.question: What does a weak evidence trail from a tutoring provider look like?
faqs.answer: Session notes that could describe any student, feedback expressed only as encouragement, no marked work returned, no reference to a mark scheme, and no record of what has changed. Add to that any promise of a specific grade, any published satisfaction percentage without a sample size and date, any claim of regulator approval, and any offer to help produce coursework. Each of those is a sales artefact rather than an academic one. Ask what you will receive after a month before you pay for a month, and compare the answer with what arrives.

faqs.question: Does the free trial lesson produce anything we can keep?
faqs.answer: Yes. The trial is a full-length working lesson with the matched tutor, not a sales call, and it produces the diagnostic note whether or not you continue. If nothing marked has been available to send in advance, the tutor sets a short unseen paper during the session and marks it, so the note has evidence behind it. No card details are taken and there is no obligation to book. If the pairing does not feel right, tell us and we will match a different tutor, which costs you another trial lesson and nothing else.

faqs.question: When is adding hours the wrong answer?
faqs.answer: When the error log shows the diagnosis is wrong, when the student cannot use the work already set, or when fatigue is the actual limiting factor. A Year 11 student in Al Reef who leaves home before seven and gets back after four has a finite amount of attention left, and a second weekday session can reduce output rather than increase it. In those cases the better moves are to change focus, move the session to a weekend block, or stop and re-book closer to the assessment. More hours is the easiest thing to sell and often the least useful thing to buy.

Lessons run one to one and live online on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Abu Dhabi school day. If we do not have the right specialist for your child's subject and level, we will tell you that instead of taking the booking.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IGCSE at Core and Extended tier and IB at Standard and Higher Level. Each one works to a named syllabus version rather than a generic subject outline, and the first session produces a written list of the topics and paper skills that are actually costing marks.

intro.heading: Two exam systems, one timetable, one child
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families often run both curricula at once. A British-curriculum school takes a student to IGCSE in Year 11, then a sibling or a school move puts the next child into the IB Middle Years Programme and on towards the Diploma. Parents end up holding two assessment vocabularies in their heads: tiers, grade scales and command words on one side, Higher Level, Internal Assessments and the three core components on the other. Searching for an IB IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is usually what happens when those two vocabularies stop making sense together.

The honest position is that the two systems reward different habits. IGCSE rewards precision against a mark scheme: the right command term, the unit written in, the working shown in the order the marker expects. The Diploma rewards extended reasoning and a tolerance for being partly wrong on the way to being right. A student who has spent five years learning to produce the exact phrase an IGCSE marker wants can struggle in a Diploma essay that asks for an argument. A tutor who knows both assessments can name that gap in one session instead of circling it for a term.

This page does not open with the usual list of reasons tutoring is good. It opens with the exam. Below you will find the grade scales side by side, the Core and Extended tier decision with its grade ceiling stated plainly, a paper-by-paper breakdown of where IGCSE marks are lost in the subjects Abu Dhabi students take most, a comparison of Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for the same subject, and the entry deadlines that sit months before the exam window and catch private candidates every year.

Delivery is the one thing to settle early. Tuition for families in Abu Dhabi is delivered online, one to one, over live video with a shared screen and a marked-up paper the student keeps. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a subject like Chemistry at Higher Level or Pearson Further Pure Maths 4PM1 that matters more than it sounds, because the pool of people who can teach that specification well is not the pool of people who live a twenty-minute drive from Al Reem Island.

Every figure on this page is either from an examination board's own published material or from a named market source with its date. Where a number could not be verified, it is not here. That applies most sharply to IB session dates: the IB does not permit automated reading of its site, so this page describes the May session as the one Abu Dhabi schools sit and asks you to confirm specific dates with your child's Diploma coordinator.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every request that arrives from Abu Dhabi: the IB Middle Years Programme, the IB Diploma Programme, and IGCSE under Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Each is described below with what it actually assesses and what that means for a student sitting it in this emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 and reported on a 1-7 scale after a grade boundary conversion the school sets. There is no external paper until the optional eAssessment at MYP 5. Students are graded on investigation, communication and reflection as much as on content recall, which is why a strong MYP report does not always predict a strong first Diploma term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the MYP alongside a British-curriculum stream in the same building, so cousins and neighbours in the same community can be sitting entirely different assessments in the same school year. Families on Yas Island and in Al Raha regularly ask us to compare an MYP criterion report against an IGCSE predicted grade, which cannot be done directly: one measures process against descriptors, the other measures marks against a boundary.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, each graded 1 to 7, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge which together contribute up to three additional points. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework: in the sciences it adds further topics and a longer second paper, and in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches it adds Paper 3, a two-problem extended-response paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session, in line with the northern-hemisphere calendar most private schools here follow. The practical consequence is that Internal Assessment deadlines land in the same autumn and winter weeks across almost every school in the emirate, so specialist tutoring capacity for Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics is tightest between October and February. Confirm your own school's internal deadlines with its Diploma coordinator rather than assuming the published external ones.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate qualifications that parents treat as one. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different papers and different grade ranges. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is largely untiered in its science and English specifications but tiers Mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Both are externally examined, and in most subjects the final grade comes entirely from written papers with no coursework component.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi student may sit Cambridge in one subject and Pearson Edexcel in another within the same school, because departments choose their own specification. Check the syllabus code on the statement of entry, not the school prospectus. A tutor working from 0625 material when the student is entered for 4PH1 will teach competently against the wrong paper structure, and the first time anyone notices is the mock.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about most, described by what the assessment actually demands. Each line names where marks are commonly lost rather than listing topics, because the topic list is on the board's website and the failure pattern is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Extended tier carries the full grade range. Marks are lost in two predictable places: algebraic manipulation under time pressure on the non-calculator paper, and the multi-step problems that combine trigonometry with bearings or similar shapes. Working shown out of order scores zero on method marks even when the final answer is right.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, both calculator-permitted, which changes revision strategy against Cambridge entirely. Higher tier questions on vectors, histograms with unequal class widths and iterative methods are the usual sticking points. Students coming from Cambridge often over-practise non-calculator arithmetic they will not need.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper carries roughly a fifth of the total and is the most teachable component on the whole specification: it rewards knowing how to describe a method, identify a variable and read a results table. Electricity and the thermal physics definitions are where theory marks disappear.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the mole calculations account for most of the lost marks at Extended tier. Students can usually balance an equation and still fail to convert between moles, mass and concentration under exam conditions. Separation techniques and the tests for ions are pure recall and are routinely left unrevised.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: A recall-heavy specification where the command words decide the mark. Describe, explain and suggest each require a different answer shape, and a student who writes a description when the paper asks for an explanation loses marks on content they know. Osmosis experiments and genetic crosses need drilling, not reading.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade, with two extended investigations that resemble no other paper the student has sat. Standard Level is examined over two papers plus the exploration. Proof by induction, complex numbers and the Maclaurin series are the Higher Level topics that most often need separate tutoring.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: Under the current guides both levels are assessed through two papers plus a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Higher Level depth in equilibrium, energetics and organic mechanisms is where the HL-only questions sit. The data-based section rewards practice with unfamiliar graphs rather than more content revision.

subjects.name: Physics (IB DP)
subjects.description: The step from IGCSE to Diploma Physics is mathematical before it is conceptual. Students who were comfortable with 0625 often stall on vector resolution and the use of calculus-adjacent reasoning in the HL fields topic. Paper 2 extended responses need structured practice against the markbands, not more reading.

subjects.name: English Language (Pearson Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing, assessed against level-based criteria rather than point-scoring. The common failure is a strong writer producing an unfocused answer because the question's audience and purpose were skimmed. Anthology texts reward annotation drills more than rereading.

subjects.name: Economics and Business (0455 and 4BS1)
subjects.description: Both specifications are won on the eight- and twelve-mark evaluation questions, where students lose marks by explaining two advantages and never weighing them. Diagram accuracy in Economics is a mark-scheme item: axes labelled, curves shifted the right way, the new equilibrium marked.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi changes the school cluster, the commute and the hour a session can realistically start. Because lessons run online, it does not change which tutor is available, but it does change the timetable we build around.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A dense residential island a short causeway from the city centre, with a heavy mix of British and IB enrolment in the schools families commute to. Sessions here usually start at 16:30 or later once the school bus has run.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding several of the emirate's larger British-curriculum schools. Parents here often ask for two siblings in different year groups on consecutive evening slots, which online scheduling makes straightforward.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Low-rise apartments and townhouses on the Dubai-side corridor. Families frequently split the week between Abu Dhabi and Dubai, so a fixed online slot that survives the drive matters more than proximity to a tutor.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A cluster of premium schools with a high proportion of Diploma candidates. Requests from here skew towards Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and towards Internal Assessment support in the autumn term.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: An older island district with established schools and short school runs. Younger IGCSE students can take a 15:45 slot here, which widens the choice of tutors available earlier in the Gulf Standard Time evening.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer family housing with a growing school intake and a long causeway commute. Evening traffic back from the island is the usual reason a parent abandons a centre-based class and moves to a fixed online slot.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland community with mixed curriculum enrolment and longer distances to the island schools. The practical effect is late starts: a 17:30 or 18:00 session is normal rather than exceptional.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Central, close to several long-established schools, and a common base for families running one child in a British stream and another in an IB stream. Cross-curriculum questions arrive from this area more than most.

sections.heading: What a parent actually means by an IB and IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is a subject specialist who can teach to a named syllabus version in either system and who knows how that syllabus is marked. That is the whole definition. It is not a general academic coach, and it is not somebody who knows the subject at university level but has never read a mark scheme. The second kind of tutor can explain electromagnetic induction beautifully and still leave a student scoring four out of seven on a question about it.

The reason the two systems get searched together is practical rather than academic. A family typically has one child finishing IGCSE and another starting or inside the Diploma, or a single child who has just moved from an IGCSE Year 11 into DP1 and lost their footing. Those are different problems. The first needs two tutors working to two specifications. The second needs one tutor who can diagnose which habits learned for IGCSE are now actively costing marks, which is a narrower skill than it sounds.

There is a third case that arrives regularly from Abu Dhabi. A student is partway through the Diploma, has chosen a Higher Level subject on the strength of an excellent IGCSE grade, and is now finding that the IGCSE grade predicted very little. A grade 8 or an A in Cambridge Chemistry 0620 says a student can recall and apply a bounded body of content accurately. Higher Level Chemistry asks for mechanistic reasoning across topics. The gap between those two things is where most of the autumn-term panic in DP1 comes from.

What a tutor does about it is specific. First session: a diagnostic on real questions from the actual specification, not a chat. Second session: the two or three habits that are costing the most marks, named and drilled. After that, a weekly rhythm of taught content, timed practice and marked feedback against the published criteria. Everything on this page is organised around making that diagnostic accurate, because a tutor working on the wrong problem is an expensive way to feel reassured.

sections.heading: The grade scales, side by side, and the floor that matters in the UAE
paragraphs: IGCSE grading confuses Abu Dhabi parents for a good reason: two scales are in active use. Cambridge reports some syllabuses on the 9 to 1 numeric scale and others on A* to G, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. The scales are not interchangeable at every point, and the mapping that matters most to families here is not the one between the two scales but the one between either scale and the UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency floor.

The ministry's British-track requirement, as reported in July 2026, is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competing tutoring site currently publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

That matters for tier choice and for subject count. A family entering a child for the Core tier in several sciences is capping the grade available in each, and while Core-tier grades can clear the equivalency floor comfortably, they may not clear a university's subject prerequisite. The sensible order of decisions is: check the university destinations first, then the subject prerequisites, then the tier. Doing it in the other order is how a student ends up with five perfectly adequate grades that do not open the door they wanted.

A tutor's job in this conversation is informational, not administrative. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry of Education runs, and nobody at IB Gram performs them, influences them or speeds them up. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the school's university counsellor before making a tier or subject decision on the strength of anything written on a tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects, the entry decision made months before the exam fixes the highest grade the student can be awarded. Core-tier papers do not contain the questions that separate the top grades, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded them however well they perform. This is the single most consequential administrative choice in an IGCSE year, and it is routinely made on the basis of a mock result taken before half the specification has been taught.

Schools in Abu Dhabi generally take a defensible view: enter a borderline student at Core and secure a solid grade rather than risk an Extended paper the student cannot access. For a student whose next step needs a strong grade in that subject, the calculation is different. Extended tier with eight months of targeted work is often a better bet than a capped grade that closes a Higher Level or A-Level route. The deciding question is not confidence; it is how much of the Extended-only content is genuinely out of reach and how many weeks remain.

A tutor earns their fee in this conversation by being specific. Extended-only material in the sciences is identifiable and finite. In Mathematics 0580 it is the algebraic and trigonometric work that Core never reaches. A diagnostic that tests exactly those topics gives a family evidence instead of a feeling, and it gives the head of department something concrete to respond to when a tier change is requested. Tier decisions can usually be revised before the final entry deadline, which is why the deadline dates in the calendar section below matter.

Pearson Edexcel works differently and parents should not assume the Cambridge pattern. Its International GCSE sciences and English specifications are largely untiered, while Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher. A student entered for 4MA1 Foundation faces the same capped-ceiling logic as a Cambridge Core candidate; a student entered for 4CH1 Chemistry faces no tier decision at all. Read the specification code on the statement of entry before having this argument with anybody.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing, paper by paper
paragraphs: Lost marks are not randomly distributed. In every cohort the same components leak the same marks for the same reasons, and most of those reasons are procedural rather than conceptual. A student who knows the content can still lose a fifth of the available marks on a paper by answering the wrong question type, omitting units, or writing a description where the command word asked for an explanation. This is the cheapest ground a tutor can recover.

The alternative-to-practical paper is the clearest example. In Cambridge physics and chemistry it carries roughly a fifth of the total mark and tests a narrow, predictable set of skills: describing a method so another person could repeat it, identifying independent and dependent variables, spotting an anomalous result, reading a scale correctly, and drawing a line of best fit. Almost none of that requires new content knowledge. Students lose marks there because nobody has ever taught them the paper as a paper.

The second pattern is command terms. Describe, explain, suggest, state, calculate and compare each have a defined answer shape in the mark scheme, and the difference between describing a trend and explaining it is the difference between one mark and three. Diploma students meet the same issue in a harsher form, because markbands reward sustained reasoning and a bullet-point answer cannot reach the top band however correct its content.

The third is arithmetic under pressure, which is where the non-calculator component in current Cambridge mathematics bites. Students who have practised exclusively with a calculator lose method marks on manipulation they can do slowly. The fix is drills, timed and marked, not more explanation. sections.heading: The step from MYP 5 into DP1, and why August is late to start
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme and the Diploma are both IB, which leads families to assume the transition is gentle. For the students who struggle, it rarely is. MYP assessment is criterion-referenced: a student is judged against descriptors for investigating, communicating and reflecting, with marks out of eight converted to a 1 to 7 grade by boundaries the school sets. Diploma assessment is externally examined against mark schemes and markbands, with a fixed syllabus and a fixed exam window.

That difference shows up in three places. Content coverage, because the MYP does not prescribe content in the way a Diploma subject guide does, so two students arriving in the same DP1 class from different MYP schools can have genuinely different starting knowledge. Mathematical fluency, because the Diploma sciences and both mathematics routes assume manipulation speed the MYP never tested under time pressure. And writing stamina, because an MYP task is usually shorter than a Paper 2 extended response.

The route choice compounds it. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation are different courses, and the choice has consequences for university applications in engineering, mathematics, economics and some sciences. A student who picks Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because it sounds more serious, without the algebraic fluency to carry it, spends two years in difficulty. Check the specific entry requirements of the universities the student is aiming at before the choice is locked, because requirements differ by institution and by year.

The practical advice is to use the months before DP1 rather than the first term of it. A short block of sessions in the spring or summer before the Diploma starts, aimed at manipulation speed, the specific content gap between the student's MYP subject and the Diploma guide, and extended-writing structure, is worth more than twice as many sessions in November when the first Internal Assessment deadlines are already moving. Diagnosing this needs the subject guide and the student's own work, not a general assessment.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel - the same subject, two different exams
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools choose specifications department by department, so a single student can hold a Cambridge entry in one subject and a Pearson Edexcel entry in another. Parents sensibly treat IGCSE as one qualification; examiners do not. The structures differ in ways that change how a student should revise, and a tutor working from the wrong board's past papers will produce good work that does not fit the paper the student will sit.

The differences worth knowing are concrete. Tiering: Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, while Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher and leaves most sciences untiered. Practical assessment: Cambridge offers a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres use the written route. Calculator policy in mathematics: current Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component, while Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which changes revision priorities substantially.

Series availability matters too. Cambridge runs its International GCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, which are the two series a UAE centre can enter candidates for, and it holds Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which are not IGCSE examinations and should not be mistaken for a series. Cambridge does also run a February and March series, but it is offered to India only, so an Abu Dhabi family who finds a February exam window online is reading a timetable that does not apply to their child. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Both publish provisional timetables ahead of each series, and both expect candidates to work from the correct official timetable rather than a restated date on a third-party site.

Cambridge adds one administrative trap that catches private candidates and new families. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school or the examination centre which zone it sits in, and work from that timetable only.

sections.heading: The deadlines that sit months before the exam
paragraphs: Every year a family discovers that the decision they wanted to make in the spring was locked months earlier. Examination entries, tier choices and private-candidate registrations all close well before the exam window, and the boards publish those dates openly. This is the single most useful planning fact on this page, and no competing tutoring page in the research set names a single session, deadline or results date.

For a UAE candidate the sequence runs from one of two series, June or November, and the gap is wide in both. Take the June series and count it backwards. The written papers run through May and June on the timetable issued for the centre's administrative zone. Forecast grades are wanted by the school before that, on the school's own schedule. Final entries close in the spring, several months ahead of the first paper, and the governing date is the one printed on the statement of entry rather than any figure restated on a website. Read that sequence backwards and the planning implication is obvious: a tier change argued after the entries have gone in is an argument about the November resit, not about June.

Pearson's dates for its own series show the same shape. The November 2026 final International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can still be revised.

IB dates are deliberately absent from the table below. The IB's own site does not permit automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified examination date on a page parents plan around would be worse than publishing none. Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session; for the exact window, your school's Diploma coordinator and ibo.org are the only sources worth using.
