process.title: Name the school, not just the group
process.description: Schools inside a group can run different curricula, serve different age ranges and use different boards for the same subject. Say which school, which stage and which assessment is next. Those three sentences are the difference between a matched specialist and a general subject tutor, and they cost nothing to supply.

process.title: Confirm the curriculum from a primary source
process.description: The school's own site and the regulator's school listing are the authoritative places to check curriculum, year groups and programmes. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the emirate including Al Ain. Do not take a tutoring page's word for what a school offers, including this one.

process.title: Request one match per child
process.description: For a two-school household, ask for separate matches rather than one tutor for both. Two correctly matched arrangements at a shorter frequency usually outperform one shared arrangement at a longer one, because a session aimed at the wrong assessment produces very little regardless of how long it runs.

process.title: After a transfer, audit before you tutor
process.description: Go through the specification topic by topic and mark each one covered, partly covered or not met, using the new school's teacher and the student's own books from the previous school. The gaps are specific and finite, which makes them cheap to close, and tutoring without the audit spends sessions finding them.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson to test the assessment fit
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, no payment and no card. Ask them to do the specific thing your child's assessment requires: name the recurring loss on a marked script, or band a piece of work against a descriptor and justify it. General enthusiasm is not evidence of a match.

whyPoints.title: Matched on school, stage and assessment
whyPoints.description: A group name is not a curriculum. Matching works from the individual school's licensed curriculum, the student's stage and the named assessment coming next, which is why a request naming only the group and the subject gets sent back with three questions rather than a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Honest about two-school households
whyPoints.description: Two children on two assessments usually need two matches, not one compromise, and this page says so even though the shared-tutor version looks cheaper. A session aimed at the wrong mark scheme produces very little, and the allocation table sets out which trade-offs actually work.

whyPoints.title: Transfer gaps named by subject
whyPoints.description: Content sequencing differs between schools even on the same board, so a mid-course transfer commonly leaves one topic untaught and another doubled. The audit method and the typical session counts are published here rather than discovered during a first term that gets written off as settling in.

whyPoints.title: Al Ain treated as a distinct market
whyPoints.description: Al Ain sits under the same regulator as Abu Dhabi city but has a smaller pool of local component specialists, which is where online matching changes the available choice most. Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain return zero mentions across the competitor corpus measured for this project; Al Ain is barely better served.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated before payment
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where delivery happens.

whyPoints.title: No claimed relationship with any school or group
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and presents no school or group as a client, partner or endorser. Several competitors list more than twenty schools as trusted partners with no relationship at all.

faqs.question: Our children attend two schools in the same group. Can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and the reason is the assessment rather than the subject. Lower-secondary work is teacher-assessed against curriculum objectives, IGCSE is terminal components on a named code, and the Diploma is criterion and weighting based. A tutor fluent in one can be ineffective in another, and the gap is invisible for several sessions. Two correctly matched arrangements at a shorter frequency usually outperform one shared arrangement at a longer frequency for the same monthly figure.

faqs.question: What should a tutoring request about a group school actually specify?
faqs.answer: Three things. The curriculum the particular school is licensed for, because schools inside a group can differ. The stage the student is at: primary, lower secondary, the IGCSE years or post-16. And the named assessment coming next, which might be a syllabus code, an internal criterion task or a school-set examination. Those three sentences turn a general enquiry into a specific one and determine whether the match is a specialist or a generalist.

faqs.question: Where do we verify what curriculum a particular school actually runs?
faqs.answer: The school's own site and the regulator's school listing, and nowhere else. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the emirate including Al Ain, and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Aggregator sites carry stale information and tutoring pages, including this one, should not be the source for what a school offers. Across the competitor pages measured for this project, ADEK was named by nobody at all.

faqs.question: When is the worst time to transfer between schools inside a group?
faqs.answer: During the two IGCSE years. The course is linear, the board may differ between schools, and content sequencing almost certainly does, so a student can arrive having covered a topic the class finished last term and never having met one the class did first. Nothing in the enrolment process surfaces that. Lower secondary is the least damaging point to move, because nothing is externally examined and the sequencing gaps have time to close.

faqs.question: How do we find out what a transferring student has actually missed?
faqs.answer: An audit before any tutoring. Take the specification, go through it topic by topic, and mark each one as covered, partly covered or not met. Two sources give most of the answer: the subject teacher at the new school on what the class has done, and the student's own exercise books from the previous school on what they actually studied. The gaps that emerge are specific and finite, usually four to six sessions of work rather than a term.

faqs.question: Is a first-term dip after a move just settling in?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the shape of the losses tells you. A genuine settling-in dip is broad and shallow: slightly worse across everything, improving slowly, with no topic conspicuously absent. A mismatch dip is narrow and deep: one topic answered as though it had never been taught, because it had not, or a whole paper approached with the wrong conventions. Settling in resolves itself; a mismatch does not, and waiting a term to find out wastes the cheapest available time.

faqs.question: What changes when a student moves between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Most of the subject content transfers; the examination does not. Paper splits differ, formula-sheet provision differs, and question phrasing differs noticeably even where the underlying physics or mathematics is identical. The commonest error after such a move is assuming a formula will be provided when it is not. Four to eight sessions of convention work usually closes it, and the first step is getting the new specification code from the examinations officer in writing.

faqs.question: With one budget and two children, which one should get the sessions?
faqs.answer: Weight it towards the child closer to a terminal assessment with marks at stake. A Year 11 twelve weeks from a June series has a harder deadline than a Year 8, and the Year 8 work is cheaper to buy later while the Year 11 work is not. If both are in terminal years, keep sessions full length and reduce frequency rather than shortening them, because a short session loses its first ten minutes to reconnecting with where the student was.

faqs.question: Can two children share one tutoring hour to save money?
faqs.answer: It halves both, and it is the one arrangement we would discourage outright at any level above lower secondary. Even for two lower-secondary students on close content, the sensible version is the same tutor and the same method in two separate shorter sessions rather than two children inside one hour. Once either child is on a terminal course with its own mark scheme, a shared hour stops being a compromise and becomes two inadequate half-sessions.

faqs.question: Does a family in Al Ain have the same tutoring options as one in Abu Dhabi city?
faqs.answer: The same regulation, a noticeably smaller local market. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools across the emirate including Al Ain, so the inspection framework and vocabulary are identical. What differs is the pool of local tutors with marking experience on a named specification, which is smaller in Al Ain, so a family seeking a component specialist may find no realistic driving radius contains one. That is where matching nationally online changes the available choice most.

faqs.question: Which exam series can a UAE candidate in either city sit?
faqs.answer: June and November for Cambridge International, and May and June plus November for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so guidance pointing an Abu Dhabi or Al Ain family at a spring sitting describes another country's timetable. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone version of the timetable is essential, so confirm the zone with the examinations officer.

faqs.question: How do we manage an IGCSE calendar and a Diploma calendar in one house?
faqs.answer: By knowing where they clash. The IGCSE pressure points are the entry deadline months before the paper, the mock window the term before, and the series. The Diploma pressure points are internal: several internal assessment deadlines and the Extended Essay converging in one stretch of the second year. Early spring is the genuine collision. Front-load the Diploma research work in the autumn, protect the mock diagnosis in winter, and reduce subject count rather than session length in the spring.

faqs.question: Why are there no IB dates on this page when the Cambridge ones are given?
faqs.answer: Because the Cambridge and Pearson dates could be verified at source and the IB ones could not. The International Baccalaureate's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project is confirmed, and publishing an unverified date across hundreds of pages would be a liability rather than a service. UAE candidates sit the May session; for every specific date, the school's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative calendar.

faqs.question: If one tutor works with both our children, is there an academic honesty issue?
faqs.answer: There can be, and it is worth naming rather than assuming it will not arise. Work produced for one child's assessment must not reach the other's, and a tutor who has coached one sibling's coursework on a topic should be careful with an overlapping piece from the other. The obligation sits with the tutor, but a family that knows about it is less likely to create the situation by accident, for instance by sharing a drive folder between children.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost across this emirate, and who publishes those figures?
faqs.answer: Online, a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and a named-component specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Entry-level online rates run lower, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the fee. Each figure belongs to the provider named.

faqs.question: Do schools in a group need to be named as partners for a tutor to support students there?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying such a relationship should be treated carefully. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any school, group, regulator or examination board, and names no school as a client or endorser. Students supported by tutors attend schools across the emirate, and that is the whole of the relationship. Several competitors measured for this project list more than twenty schools as trusted partners with no relationship at all.

A request naming an Advanced Placement course or an IB subject and level reaches someone who has taught that specific assessment.

intro.heading: Four claims a tutoring provider makes, and how a parent checks each one
paragraphs: Almost everything an agency says about itself is unverifiable by design. A satisfaction percentage with no sample size, a star rating with no countable reviews, a claim of regulatory approval that no regulator would confirm: competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026 carried all three, and one showed two different review totals on the same page. This page therefore takes the opposite approach and sticks to claims a parent in Abu Dhabi can check against a primary source within about fifteen minutes.

There are four worth checking before paying anyone. First, the rate. Market rates are published by several providers, so a quote can be tested against them: online entry tutors run roughly AED 33 to 150, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; a qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; a named-course specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270; and AED 650 is the highest published figure found in this market, from BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the fee.

Second, the permit. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The ministry's own service page for it lists no fee and a two working day completion time. A parent can ask a tutor directly whether they hold one, and can read the eligibility rules themselves rather than taking anyone's word on them.

Third, the school. Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its outcomes. Read the inspection on ADEK's own site and nowhere else, because aggregated ratings go stale and the band vocabulary differs between emirates. Across the competitor pages measured for this project, ADEK was named by nobody at all, which tells you how much local checking went into them.

Fourth, the equivalency rule, which matters more at an American-curriculum school than anywhere else and is set out in its own section below. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and names no school on this page as a client or partner. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-american-co.programmesIntro: An American-curriculum school running the IB Diploma alongside its own diploma gives a family two genuinely different post-16 routes and one earlier decision point. These four blocks set out what each stage assesses and what that means in this emirate.

programmes.name: Elementary school
programmes.description: Standards-based reporting rather than percentage marks, which makes specific gaps hard for a parent to see. The skills that matter later are number fluency, reading stamina and the ability to produce a structured paragraph without a template. A standards report can show consistent attainment while one of those three is quietly missing, and it usually shows up two years later as a middle-school writing problem.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi these years also carry the mandatory UAE subjects, which run in private schools alongside the licensed curriculum under the federal requirement overseen by the Ministry of Education. Arabic is normally the first subject where the report carries a conventional grade, and in expatriate households on the island it is frequently the only one a parent cannot help with at the kitchen table.

programmes.name: Middle school
programmes.description: Grade point averages begin to accumulate here in most American-curriculum schools, which changes the purpose of tutoring: a weak semester is now a permanent entry on a transcript rather than a bad term. Algebra readiness is the single highest-leverage thing to fix in these years, because it carries both the high-school maths sequence and the quantitative science courses that follow it.
programmes.countryNote: Middle school is also where an Abu Dhabi family starts weighing the two post-16 routes, and the earlier decision is whether to stay in the American sequence or move towards a British-curriculum school for IGCSEs. That second route brings its own equivalency rule, counting five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education.

programmes.name: High school and Advanced Placement
programmes.description: Course grades build a transcript and a grade point average, and Advanced Placement courses sit on top as externally examined single subjects scored one to five. The structure is modular in a way the IB Diploma is not: a student can take one Advanced Placement course or six, and can drop one without affecting the diploma. That flexibility is the main argument for the route and also its main risk, since nothing forces breadth.
programmes.countryNote: The American track for Ministry of Education equivalency has published thresholds that catch families out. English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are specific numbers with a specific source, and they are worth knowing in Grade 10 rather than Grade 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service. Unlike the Advanced Placement route it is all or nothing: the Diploma is awarded on the whole package, so a collapse in one subject has consequences across it. Internal assessment runs in every subject, and five of those deadlines plus a four-thousand-word Extended Essay land inside one stretch of the second year. UAE candidates sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: No IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency appears on this page, because none could be verified against the Ministry's own publication, and repeating an unverified figure across hundreds of pages would be a liability rather than a service. A Diploma family should confirm the current requirement with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority before planning around any number they read anywhere, including here.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-american-co.subjectsIntro: The courses Al Bateen and island families most often ask about, across both post-16 routes. What moves the rate is the level and the proximity to an external assessment, not the subject label.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the course, and students arriving from an American sequence often find the non-calculator demands unfamiliar rather than hard. The commonest avoidable loss is a correct method never written down, because the mark scheme credits the working and the student recorded only the answer. Higher Level adds proof and complex numbers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Students lose marks reporting a calculator output without naming the command that produced it, and treating a regression line as an answer rather than a model with limits. The internal assessment rewards data the student actually collected and can defend.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · AP Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms separate grades at Higher Level. Students moving from an American course often have stronger stoichiometry and weaker mechanism reasoning than the Diploma expects. Data-based questions reward reading axis labels before the question stem, which under time pressure almost nobody does.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · AP Physics
subjects.description: Definitions carry marks that calculations cannot recover. A student who cannot state what a field is in one sentence loses the explanation marks that follow it. Electromagnetic induction and circuit analysis produce the heaviest losses at both levels, and drawing the circuit before writing anything is the reliable correction.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · AP Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes it feel like a memory test and students revise it as one. The marks live in command terms: outline, explain, evaluate and discuss each want a different answer shape, and a well-learned paragraph scores two of five when the verb asked for a comparison. Internal assessment statistics is a routine weak spot.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis won in the reading rather than the writing. The Individual Oral usually fails on the global issue, not on the texts, because students choose something too broad to evidence in ten minutes. Higher Level adds an essay that needs a sustained argument rather than a tour of the text.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · AP Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks, and candidates drawing from memory rather than from the question routinely shift the wrong curve. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and is the clearest separator between a five and a seven. The Advanced Placement equivalent rewards short precise definitions in a way the Diploma does not.

subjects.name: History
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · AP World History
subjects.description: Source work is the examinable skill, not the narrative. Students lose marks describing what a source says instead of assessing its value and limitations. The Diploma internal assessment is a historical investigation with its own structure, and a research question that is too wide caps the mark before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Relevant where a sibling or a transfer places a student on a British-curriculum track. Extended opens A* to E and Core caps at C, a ceiling set by the school at entry. Pearson 4MA1 covers similar ground with a different paper split and its own formula-sheet conventions, so past-paper practice must match the board entered.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed guidance and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between streams. The non-Arab stream is the one usually tutored in expatriate households and has its own realistic ceiling.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-american-co.regionsIntro: Where island families actually live, and what that does to a session time rather than to a rate. Al Bateen sits on the western side of the island, and the commute pattern around it is the reason the travel premium in the tables below is real.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: An established island neighbourhood with a mix of villas and low-rise apartments, a short school run and a slow exit onto the main corniche roads at the end of the working day. Households here are more often long-term residents than short postings, which makes multi-year weekly arrangements more common than crash blocks.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah and the Corniche
regions.note: Apartment living along the island's western edge, where a large share of students travel by bus rather than by car. The bus timetable rather than a parent's diary sets the earliest realistic session, and that routinely pushes weekday arrangements later than families expect.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Villa neighbourhoods inland from Al Bateen with several long-standing schools nearby. Two-school households are common here, with one child on an American track and a sibling on a British one, which is the usual reason a family needs two different kinds of tutor at once.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense residential towers with a large school-age population commuting outward in several directions. The exit onto the crossing in the late afternoon is the slowest part of the day, so families here ask for the latest practical weekday slot more often than anyone else on the island.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short crossing north, with several newer international schools of its own. Families appear here when a sibling attends one of those schools, and the two different school calendars are what makes a shared tutoring schedule difficult and a per-child video slot straightforward.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The mainland villa corridor, roughly thirty to forty-five minutes from Al Bateen at peak. For families who moved outward but kept the island school place, this is exactly the journey a travelling tutor prices into an in-home rate, and the reason the online figure sits well below it.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland residential area with longer average commutes and a mixed school profile. Households here most often run two children at two schools on two timetables, which makes an evening driving route impractical and a scheduled video session the only arrangement that reliably holds.

schoolClusters.city: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif
schoolClusters.note: The western and central island neighbourhoods hold several of the emirate's longest-established international schools, drawing from overlapping villa and apartment communities. Students move between them more often than between island and mainland schools, so local course sequencing is familiar across the group.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Yas and the mainland corridor
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools on the islands and the villa-corridor schools on the mainland. An Al Bateen family frequently has a sibling in this group, which is the most common reason a household carries an American-track course and an IB or IGCSE course at the same time.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-american-co.modesIntro: Three shapes of arrangement, each suited to a different part of an American-curriculum or Diploma year. The choice is set by the assessment coming next rather than by preference.

modes.title: Semester-long weekly session
modes.description: One fixed session a week across a semester, which matches the American-curriculum reporting cycle rather than a British term structure. Because a semester grade lands on a transcript permanently, the value of steady support here is higher than the equivalent at a British-curriculum school, where a weak term is recoverable. The session runs alongside the course, not ahead of it.
bullets: Same tutor and slot across a whole semester
Aimed at the semester grade, not just the next test

modes.title: External assessment block
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions before an Advanced Placement examination, an SAT sitting or an IB May session, built on timed questions and marked work. Content teaching stops; the hour becomes technique, command terms and the recurring losses. Availability tightens sharply in the spring for all three, because the windows overlap, so this is the block that most rewards early booking.

modes.title: Internal assessment and research supervision support
modes.description: Scheduled sessions through an IB internal assessment, Extended Essay or an extended research piece, working only on what the student has written. The tutor maps the draft against the published criteria and names the criterion costing marks. The tutor does not contribute text, redraft into a final version or supply data, and that boundary is stated before the first session.

sections.heading: What you can actually verify about a tutoring quote in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Verification is the whole point of this section, because the alternative is trust in claims nobody can test. The competitor corpus measured for this project is full of them: one page shows a rating of 4.92 out of 5 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page; another shows 5.0 from 20 reviews next to a claim of 2,500 students. Both are structured-data violations and, as commercial representations in the UAE, consumer-protection exposures. Neither is checkable.

What is checkable, from a primary source, in roughly fifteen minutes: the market rate band, the tutor's permit obligation, the school's regulator and inspection, the examination board's own timetable and specification, and the Ministry of Education's published equivalency requirements. That is five things, and they cover most of what actually matters in a tutoring decision. The table sets each one against the authority that publishes it.

The practical use of this is in an initial conversation. Ask a provider what their rate is, which band that puts them in, whether their tutors hold the MoHRE permit, which specification or course code they teach, and which authority inspects the school they claim to support. A provider who can answer all five without hesitation is operating in a different way from one who answers with a satisfaction percentage. That is a better signal than any rating. None of those five questions is rude, and a provider who treats them as rude has answered the most important one already.

sections.heading: The AED bands, and the four questions that test a quote
paragraphs: A rate on its own is not information. A rate with a band, a format and a date attached is. The Abu Dhabi market splits into roughly four bands online, and the useful move for a parent is to work out which band a quote belongs to and then ask whether the service matches it. A quote at the specialist rate that cannot name a course-specific recurring loss is mispriced, and a quote at the entry rate for Higher Level work is mismatched in the other direction.

The four questions that test any quote are simple. Which band does this sit in, against the published market figures? Is it per hour or per session, and how long is the session? Does the figure include any written feedback, marking or reporting between sessions, or is that extra? And what happens to the rate in exam term, when demand is at its peak and availability at its lowest? A provider who answers all four plainly is one you can budget against.

The table lists the bands with their sources and what each one should include at that price. Every figure belongs to the provider or survey named and none of them is an IB Gram quotation; IB Gram's own commercial terms are set in a consultation after the free trial lesson rather than published as a rate card. The in-home row appears because it is the comparison families make, not because it is on offer: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: Two routes out of Grade 10, and what each one asks of a student
paragraphs: A school offering both an American diploma with Advanced Placement courses and the IB Diploma presents a genuine choice at the end of Grade 10, and it is a choice about the student's working style as much as their ability. The routes are not harder and easier versions of each other. They are structurally different, and a student who thrives in one can struggle badly in the other for reasons that have nothing to do with intelligence.

The Advanced Placement route is modular. A student takes courses individually, each externally examined and scored one to five, and can take one or six. A weak result in one does not threaten the others. The diploma itself comes from the school's own transcript and grade point average, so consistency across semesters matters more than performance in a single examination window. This suits students who work steadily and prefer depth in chosen subjects to enforced breadth.

The IB Diploma is a single package. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service, awarded as a whole. Breadth is compulsory, internal assessment runs in every subject, and five internal deadlines plus a four-thousand-word essay converge inside one stretch of the second year. It suits students who are organised and broad, and it punishes poor time management more severely than weak content. The table sets the two side by side on the dimensions that actually decide which fits, and the last row is the one worth reading first, because it says where the tutoring money tends to go on each route.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency on the American track
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that converts a foreign school certificate into something the UAE system recognises, and it is where an American-curriculum family meets specific numbers for the first time. The published requirements for the American track are concrete. English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

Those are the thresholds, and two things follow from them. The first is timing: an SAT Math score of 450 is not a demanding target for a student who has taken the test seriously once, but it has to exist before an application, which makes Grade 11 the right time to deal with it rather than Grade 12. The second is that this is a test-preparation problem rather than a course-content problem, and it is a different tutoring purchase from subject support.

The British track is included in the table for the common case of a family with children on both routes. It requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB there is a deliberate gap: no points threshold is published here because none could be verified against the Ministry's own site. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and it is not a reason to buy tutoring.

sections.heading: Online delivery and the Al Bateen commute, costed honestly
paragraphs: An in-home rate in Abu Dhabi contains a journey. A tutor reaching Al Bateen at five in the afternoon spends a meaningful part of their evening on the corniche roads, and that is why the local in-home band reaches AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to 450 online. The difference is not quality. It is distance, and it is paid for whether or not the invoice itemises it.

There is a reliability cost on top. A session dependent on a journey fails for reasons unconnected to teaching, and families with travelling tutors commonly lose two or three sessions across a twenty-eight-session term to traffic, weather or an overrun. In the spring, when Advanced Placement examinations, SAT sittings and an IB May session overlap, those are the least replaceable hours in the year, which makes the proportional loss worse than it looks.

The decisive cost, though, is choice. Travel restricts the tutor pool to whoever drives to this part of the island at that hour. For a specific Advanced Placement course, for Higher Level Physics or for Economics Paper 3, that radius may contain nobody with the right experience at all. Online delivery is not offered here as a convenience; it is offered because a national pool contains the specialist and a twenty-minute driving radius in one emirate does not. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: Transcripts, grade point averages and why the tutoring target differs
paragraphs: An American-curriculum school and a British-curriculum school measure success differently, and that changes what tutoring is for. In a British system the terminal examination is almost everything, so a weak term is recoverable and tutoring is aimed at a single event months away. In an American system the transcript accumulates, semester by semester, and a weak semester grade is permanent. The target is therefore continuous rather than a single peak.

The practical consequence is that the standing weekly session is worth more at an American-curriculum school than the equivalent at a British one, and the crash block is worth less. A family that tutors heavily for three months before an examination and not at all during the semesters has optimised for the wrong measure, because the grade point average was being built the whole time. That is the single most common misalignment in this market for American-track families.

The second consequence is about Advanced Placement scores, which sit alongside the transcript rather than inside it. An Advanced Placement examination is a one-off external event scored one to five, and it behaves like a British examination: technique, timing and command words decide it, and a short preparation block is genuinely effective. So a family on this route is usually buying two different things at two different times of year, and confusing them is why some arrangements feel expensive and ineffective at once. Budgeted separately, one is a modest standing monthly line and the other is a finite block with a date on it, and both become easier to justify.
bullets: Transcript and grade point average accumulate; a weak semester is permanent

sections.heading: The IB May session counted backwards from a Grade 11 start
paragraphs: A Diploma student beginning in Grade 11 has roughly two years, and the deadlines that matter are nearly all internal. UAE candidates sit the May session. The external papers are the visible endpoint, but the work that decides the grade starts much earlier: an Extended Essay research question, five or six internal assessment proposals, and a Theory of Knowledge essay all have school deadlines set inside board deadlines, and those are the dates a family should be working from.

No specific IB session or results date appears on this page. The International Baccalaureate's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified date across hundreds of pages would be exactly the error this page is written against. Confirm every IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative internal calendar.

What can be stated is the sequence, which is the useful part anyway. The table works backwards from the examination window through the internal deadlines to the point in Grade 11 where decisions are still cheap. Reading it the other way round, the single highest-value action for a Grade 11 family is to get the Extended Essay research question settled early, because a question that is too broad caps the mark before any writing begins and is expensive to fix in the second year. The second highest-value action is to stagger the internal assessment proposals deliberately, because the school's deadlines will cluster them whether or not the student has prepared for that.

One further note on reading the sequence. The dates in the right-hand column are deliberately relative rather than absolute, and that is not vagueness: internal deadlines differ between schools by weeks, and a family acting on a generic calendar found online will be a fortnight out in either direction.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a household runs two assessment systems
paragraphs: A school offering both routes produces several kinds of assessed work that must be the student's own, and the rules differ in detail while the principle does not. An IB internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, a research paper carrying a course grade: in every case the submission has to be the student's work, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student rather than on anyone selling help.

The permitted work is wide and genuinely valuable. A tutor can read the published criteria with the student and explain what each descriptor awards. They can press on a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. They can teach the statistical test, the laboratory technique, the citation convention or the economic model the piece needs. They can read a draft the student wrote and name the criterion costing marks. They can rehearse the supervisor conversation.

The prohibited work is equally clear. No contributed text, no redrafting into a final version, no data supplied for the student to present as collected, no editing that leaves the submission substantially someone else's work. One operation ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price; that purchase risks the student's whole qualification and risks nothing for the seller. The self-test a student can apply is whether they could explain every sentence of their own submission, unprompted, to the person who supervised it. If they could not, the line has been crossed whoever crossed it, and the honest repair is to return to the last point where the work was genuinely theirs.

process.title: Name the course and the assessment, not the subject
process.description: A request that says Chemistry gets a generalist. One that says IB Chemistry Higher Level, Paper 2, currently a 4, or an Advanced Placement course by name, reaches someone who has taught that assessment. At a school running two routes this matters more than usual, because the same subject label covers two different examinations.

process.title: Say which band you are shopping in
process.description: This page publishes the market bands and what each should include. Tell us which one you are aiming at and we will say honestly whether it covers what you are asking for. An entry-band budget for Higher Level coursework support is a mismatch, and it is better identified in a first message than in a third session.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson to run the checks
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, no payment and no card. Ask them in it to name the recurring loss on the last piece of marked work, to say which course or specification they teach, and whether they hold a MoHRE permit. Three verifiable answers in one hour is a better basis than any published rating.

process.title: Separate the transcript work from the exam work
process.description: At an American-curriculum school these are two different purchases: a standing weekly session that protects the semester grade, and a short block before an Advanced Placement examination or an SAT sitting. Budgeting them as one line is why some arrangements feel expensive and ineffective simultaneously.

process.title: Get the availability answer before you commit
process.description: If no specialist in that course is free at the time you need, you are told in advance and given the alternatives: a different slot, a different tutor, or a specialist outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time. No competitor page measured for this project publishes a coverage limit of any kind.

whyPoints.title: Claims you can check against a primary source
whyPoints.description: Every rate here is attributed to its publisher, every regulatory point to the authority that published it, and every historical date to the source that reported it. No satisfaction percentage, review count or star rating appears on this page, because none could be evidenced with a sample size, a date and a method.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course and assessment, not by grade level
whyPoints.description: At a school running an American diploma alongside the IB Diploma, the same subject name covers two different examinations with different mark schemes. A tutor matched to the named course and level knows which one, and a tutor matched to a grade level does not.

whyPoints.title: The American-track equivalency numbers published
whyPoints.description: SAT Math 450, IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450: specific published thresholds that families usually meet at Grade 12 and should have handled in Grade 11. Zero competitors in four of the ten query clusters measured for this project mention equivalency at all.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated before any payment
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where delivery actually happens.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals of any kind
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson or the College Board, and names no school on this page as a client or partner. The phrase a parent should treat as a warning is any provider calling itself regulator-approved.

whyPoints.title: A coursework boundary set out in writing first
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads, questions and gives feedback on work the student wrote, and does not contribute text, redraft to a final version or supply data for any internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or graded research paper. The line is stated before the first coursework session because the qualification at risk is the student's.

faqs.question: How can a parent in Abu Dhabi verify that a tutoring rate is reasonable?
faqs.answer: Compare the quote against published market figures rather than against a feeling. Online entry rates run roughly AED 33 to 150, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Course specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and AED 650 is the highest published figure found. Each belongs to the provider named.

faqs.question: What should a tutor be able to tell me in the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Five things, all verifiable. Which market band their rate sits in. Whether the figure is per hour or per session, and the session length. Whether marking and written feedback between sessions are included or extra. Which course, level or specification code they teach. And whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A provider who answers all five plainly is operating differently from one who answers with a satisfaction percentage, and that contrast is more informative than any published rating.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require from an American high school diploma?
faqs.answer: The published requirements include specific test thresholds. English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those numbers are concrete and they need to exist before an application, which makes Grade 11 the right time to deal with them. Confirm the current requirements with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority.

faqs.question: Is the Advanced Placement route or the IB Diploma easier for our child?
faqs.answer: Neither is simply easier; they ask for different things. The Advanced Placement route is modular, so a weak result in one course stays contained, and the school transcript and grade point average carry most of the weight. The IB Diploma is a single package with compulsory breadth, internal assessment in every subject and an Extended Essay, and it punishes poor time management more than weak content. A steady, deep worker often prefers the first; an organised, broad worker often prefers the second.

faqs.question: Should tutoring at an American-curriculum school be continuous or before exams?
faqs.answer: Mostly continuous, which is the opposite of the British-curriculum answer. The transcript and grade point average accumulate semester by semester, so a weak semester grade is permanent rather than recoverable, and a standing weekly session protects the measure that actually counts. A pre-examination crash block is still worth buying for an Advanced Placement examination or an SAT sitting, because those behave like external papers. Treating the two as one budget line is the commonest misalignment for American-track families in this market.

faqs.question: When should SAT preparation start for a student aiming at UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Grade 11 rather than Grade 12. The Ministry's American-track mathematics requirement is at least 450 in the SAT Math test, which is not a demanding target for a student who has prepared properly once, but it must exist before the application. English can be satisfied by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. Leaving all three to the final year stacks them against university deadlines and against the Advanced Placement examination window in the same spring.

faqs.question: Does an Advanced Placement tutor need to be different from a subject tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. An Advanced Placement examination is externally set and scored one to five, and like any external paper it is decided by timing, command words and answer shape rather than by broad subject knowledge. A tutor who has prepared students for that specific course knows what the scoring guidelines reward. A strong subject teacher who has never seen the course can teach the content accurately and still leave two or three points on the table through unfamiliarity with the format.

faqs.question: Why does the in-home rate in Al Bateen reach AED 500 an hour?
faqs.answer: Because the fee contains a journey. A tutor reaching Al Bateen at five in the afternoon spends a substantial part of the evening on the corniche roads, and that time sits inside the rate whether or not the invoice itemises it. Travel also loses sessions: families with travelling tutors commonly lose two or three of a twenty-eight-session term. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at any rate, and the figures are published only so a family can see what the extra money buys.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects schools in Abu Dhabi and where is the report published?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Read them on ADEK's own site rather than on an aggregator, because aggregated ratings go stale and band vocabulary differs between emirates. Across the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026, ADEK was named by nobody at all. Dubai sits with KHDA, Sharjah with SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and three emirates with the federal Ministry.

faqs.question: Is a private tuition permit actually required, and does it cost the tutor anything?
faqs.answer: Required, and free. An individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time, with applications through its smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone quoting a permit fee at you has it wrong. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supply data or sources for an internal assessment that is running late?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor can teach the statistical test or laboratory technique the investigation needs, explain the citation convention, read a draft the student wrote and name the criterion costing marks, and rehearse the supervisor meeting. A tutor cannot supply data for the student to present as collected, contribute text, or redraft a passage into its final form. One operation ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments; the thing that purchase risks is the student's entire qualification, not the seller's business.

faqs.question: At what point in Grade 11 should the Extended Essay question be locked down?
faqs.answer: Mid Grade 11 at the latest, and earlier if possible. A research question that is too broad caps the achievable mark before any writing happens, and fixing it in Grade 12 means rewriting rather than editing. The highest-value single hour a Diploma family can buy in Grade 11 is a session that interrogates the question until it is answerable in four thousand words. Confirm every internal deadline with the school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative calendar rather than any published summary.

faqs.question: Why are there no specific IB session dates anywhere on this page?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the International Baccalaureate itself. The organisation's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project is confirmed at source, and publishing an unverified date across hundreds of pages would be the exact failure this page is written against. UAE candidates sit the May session; for every specific date, ask the school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative internal and external calendar.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both a Diploma subject and an Advanced Placement course?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The content overlap between, say, an Advanced Placement science course and the equivalent Diploma subject at Higher Level is real but partial, and the assessments differ substantially in format and scoring. A tutor who has taught both can be efficient for a household running two children on two routes. A tutor who has taught one and read about the other will be noticeably weaker in the second, and the trial lesson is where to test that.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for the course and slot we need?
faqs.answer: You are told before paying. The alternatives are a different time in the week, a different tutor at the same level, or a specialist based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, which is how scarcer courses usually get covered. No competitor page measured for this project discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where delivery happens. A planable availability answer is worth more than an unconditional yes.

faqs.question: Can sessions move for Ramadan, travel and the spring assessment pile-up?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the spring pile-up is the real reason it matters here. Advanced Placement examinations, SAT sittings and an IB May session fall close together, so a schedule has to flex within a few weeks rather than across a term. During Ramadan, timings commonly shift to after Iftar, which a video arrangement handles by changing a calendar entry rather than a driving route. A student travelling for a fortnight keeps the slot instead of losing a month of continuity.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-american-co.closingHeading: Run the five checks, then take a free trial lesson
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-american-co.closingBody: If your child is at the American Community School of Abu Dhabi, the useful first message names the course and assessment, the market band you are shopping in, and the window in the week that genuinely works. You will get a straight answer on availability for that course, the market context for the rate, and a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor before anything is charged. Use that hour to run the checks on this page: ask for the recurring loss on a marked script, the course or specification taught, and the permit position. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Read the market from the bottom, not the top
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market introduces its prices from the top down. The premium tier appears first, the mid tier follows as the sensible compromise, and the budget tier arrives last as a warning. That ordering is a sales device rather than information, because it makes the mid tier feel like restraint when it may be twice what a particular job needs. Reading the same market from the bottom up produces different and more useful decisions.

So this page starts at AED 45 an hour, which is the lowest advertised figure in the researched market, and climbs. At each step it asks a single question: what does the additional money actually buy, and is that thing relevant to your child's problem? Sometimes it is, decisively. A pupil who needs an Extended-tier script marked against a real mark scheme is not well served at the bottom of the market. Sometimes it is not, and a family pays specialist rates for content coverage a careful graduate could have delivered.

The figures used are published by the providers and surveys named, not by IB Gram. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above, while BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named premium tutor. None of these providers publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method.

Abu Dhabi then adds a layer that Dubai families do not encounter. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct is also reported to bar serving students affiliated with their own school. Those reports should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as ADEK's exact wording, and they are enough to make one arrangement a parent might think convenient the wrong one.

ADEK appears on none of the researched competitor pages, which is a remarkable gap on pages targeting Abu Dhabi families. So this page covers it, along with how to verify a rate, what group classes can and cannot do, and what the travel premium looks like across an emirate where the distances are genuinely long. Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

programmes.description: The thinnest specialist pool and therefore the firmest rates. The published AED 200 to 450 specialist band applies, and premium named tutors advertise up to AED 650. subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)

subjects.description: A genuinely thin pool, particularly for Cambridge pseudocode conventions, so expect longer match times and upper-band rates. Worth asking about availability before building a budget around it.

subjects.description: Mandatory provision alongside any international curriculum in UAE private schools under the federal baseline. A thin specialist pool at first-language level, and support must follow the prescribed content rather than substitute an alternative.

sections.heading: Starting at AED 45 and working up
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor in the UAE market costs between about AED 33 and AED 650 an hour, and the honest way to present that is from the bottom. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both drawing largely on university students and overseas graduates. That is the floor, and it is a real floor rather than a loss-leader: these providers deliver sessions at those prices.

The next step up is Unitors, publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which roughly triples the floor. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai puts qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 and subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above. The top of the market is BartyED at AED 650 for a named premium tutor. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 350 in the Bestimate survey and up to AED 500 among independent home tutors.

Read upwards, each step has to justify itself against the step below. From AED 45 to AED 150 the justification is specification knowledge: a trained teacher who has taught the syllabus rather than studied the subject. From AED 150 to AED 250 it is diagnostic capability: the ability to mark a timed script against the published scheme and say where the marks went. From AED 250 to AED 650 the justification is scarcity and reputation, and that is where the argument gets weakest.

It gets weakest because nothing in this market is measured. Not one of the researched providers publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a stated method. Competitor pages carry satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and claims about the proportion of students reaching top grades, with nothing checkable attached. A rate above the specialist band is therefore a claim about positioning, and a family paying it should be clear that is what they are buying.

sections.heading: What the bottom of the market actually does well
paragraphs: It is worth being specific rather than dismissive, because the floor of this market is genuinely useful for several real jobs. A pupil who understands the content and will not sit down to revise alone benefits from somebody competent in the room keeping the session moving. A Key Stage 3 pupil who needs arithmetic drilled to fluency needs repetition under mild time pressure, not a specialist. A Core-tier candidate covering content needs coverage.

In each of those cases the extra AED 150 an hour buys nothing the job requires. A family paying specialist rates to have a confident graduate keep their Year 8 company through maths homework has paid for diagnostic capability they are not using. That is the single most common overspend in this market and it happens because the market is presented top-down, making the floor look like a risk rather than a fit.

What the floor does not do reliably is diagnosis. Marking a timed Extended-tier script against the published mark scheme, separating method losses from content losses, and knowing that a six-mark explanation question wants six ideas in sequence are things that come from having taught the specification and ideally from having marked it. A tutor learning the syllabus alongside your child cannot do that, however able they are.

The practical test is a question rather than a credential. Ask a prospective tutor at any rate: which specification code and tier is my child entered for, and what are the components? Then: having read this marked script, how many marks went to method as against content? A tutor who answers both concretely is worth their rate whatever it is. A tutor who answers in general terms about building confidence is a floor-level service, and should be priced as one.

sections.heading: When the specialist band is genuinely justified
paragraphs: There are four situations where paying the AED 200 to 450 band is defensible on the evidence rather than on reassurance, and they are narrower than the market implies. The first is Extended-tier script diagnosis, where a marked timed paper has to be read properly and the lost marks categorised. The second is the top end of a subject, where a pupil already at a 7 is chasing the marks that separate a 7 from an 8 or 9 and the questions involved are genuinely demanding.

The third is a scarce specification. Cambridge Computer Science 0478 with pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, or an unusual literature text list. Here the rate reflects supply rather than any claim about quality, and a family is paying for availability. That is a legitimate thing to pay for, and it should be understood as such rather than as access to better teaching.

The fourth is a specific internal assessment brief at Diploma level, where scoring a draft against lettered criteria with stated mark allocations requires familiarity with those criteria. A tutor who knows what criterion B wants in a particular subject is scarce, and the work they do is not available at the floor. Again, that is supply and specificity rather than general excellence.

Outside those four, the honest answer is often that the mid band is sufficient and the floor may be. The useful discipline is to name the job before the rate: content coverage, habit installation, script diagnosis, top-end stretch, or scarce specification. Each has a band attached, and matching the two prevents both kinds of error - paying specialist rates for coverage, and buying coverage when diagnosis was what was needed.

sections.heading: The ADEK layer that Dubai parents never meet
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi has its own regulator and it appears on none of the researched competitor pages, which is a striking omission on pages aimed at Abu Dhabi families. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's equivalent is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority; Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The part with direct consequences for a tutoring arrangement is professional ethics. ADEK's rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct is also reported to bar serving students affiliated with their own school. Those reports should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being quoted as ADEK's exact wording.

The practical advice follows regardless of the precise wording: do not arrange paid tutoring with your child's own class teacher, however convenient and however well they know the pupil. It puts the teacher in a position they should not be in, and it is the one arrangement in this market that is explicitly discouraged by both an emirate regulator and a federal permit's code of conduct. Any provider marketing a pupil's own teacher privately is marketing a problem.

Nothing in any of this gives a tutoring platform standing to claim regulatory approval. A parent can name a regulator and explain what it does; a provider cannot imply endorsement. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and makes no such claim. It has no office or centre in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and nobody should describe its tutors as regulator-approved.

sections.heading: Five things a parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Most claims in this market cannot be checked and a few can. The permit can. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit is free, any provider citing licensing costs as a reason for its rate has misread its own paperwork. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any amount circulating online should be treated as unverified.

The specification code can be verified too, with the examinations officer rather than the provider. So can a sixth form's published entry grades, which are public. So can the claim that a rate is a market rate, by checking it against the published figures on this page. What cannot be verified is any satisfaction percentage, star rating or proportion-reaching-top-grades claim in this market, because none of them arrives with a sample size, a date and a method.

A premises-based operation is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, and that is checkable as well. A tutoring business with premises and staff in the UAE needs an educational services permit from the relevant emirate authority - in Dubai a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An online matching platform holds no such permit and should not imply one.

sections.heading: Group classes in Abu Dhabi, and what they cannot do
paragraphs: Group tuition sits between the floor and the mid band on price and is genuinely good value for one job. Small-group rates in this market run around AED 100 to 150 per pupil, against AED 200 to 450 for one-to-one specialist work. For content coverage across a group of pupils at the same tier in the same subject, the economics are hard to argue with and the social element helps some pupils work.

What a group cannot do is diagnose. A session pitched to a group addresses the average of several pupils' gaps, which means it addresses none of them precisely. Your child's specific pattern of lost marks - method unshown in three questions, a precision error in two, the back page unreached - is invisible in a group and cannot be worked on there. The entire argument for paying one-to-one rates is that the hour targets one pupil.

There is a second limitation that matters more in an examination year. A group cannot mark one pupil's timed script against the published scheme and categorise the losses, because that is individual work done between sessions. Some group providers offer it as an add-on and some do not, and asking is worth the thirty seconds. Where it is not offered, the group is a content service and the diagnostic has to come from elsewhere.

The sensible combination for a budget-conscious Abu Dhabi family is often a hybrid: group content coverage at AED 100 to 150 per pupil, plus a small number of one-to-one diagnostic sessions at the specialist band at the start and before the series. That buys the thing the group cannot do without paying specialist rates for the thing it can. Nobody in this market packages it that way, which does not mean a family cannot assemble it.

sections.heading: The travel premium in an emirate with long distances
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's geography makes the in-home premium behave differently from Dubai's. A tutor travelling from the island districts out to Al Reef or Al Shamkha is committing a substantial round trip, and villa communities like Khalifa City and Al Raha have internal distances that add time after the arrival. Yas and Saadiyat have single access routes that behave badly at peak. The published AED 180 to 500 in-home band is priced against journeys of exactly this shape.

The second cost is selection, and it does not appear on any invoice. An in-home tutor must live within a drivable radius, so the pool of people who both specialise in Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 and happen to live twenty minutes from Al Reef is small and sometimes empty. When it is empty the arrangement becomes whoever is available rather than whoever is right, and a family has paid the in-home premium for a generalist. That is the worst value combination available.

The third is cancellation. A tutor held up on the Shamkha corridor or caught behind an incident on an island access route either arrives twenty minutes late and teaches forty, or cancels. Across a term that is real money that bought nothing, and the replacement slot competes with homework that has already moved. None of this is anyone's fault; it is a consequence of distance.

Removing the car removes all three. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Abu Dhabi households over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which means the tutor is selected for the specification and tier rather than for a postcode. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered in India only. The table sets out what each format gives and what it gives up.

sections.heading: What no rate should include, at any band
paragraphs: Some things should not appear at AED 45 or at AED 650. Written, edited or supplied coursework is the clearest. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger rather than a service, and the exposure falls on the candidate whose certificate is at stake. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work.

Nor should anybody supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as files. Those belong to the boards, and the correct behaviour is to link the official page so a family reads the current version. A provider offering a folder of mark schemes as part of a package has told you how it treats rules in general, which is worth knowing at any price point.

Claims nobody can substantiate should not be in a rate either. No provider in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method, so a satisfaction percentage or a claim about the proportion of pupils reaching top grades is a marketing figure. A promise of a specific grade, score or improvement is a reason to decline. Self-asserted star ratings shipped in schema are against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure.

Examiner status deserves a note because it is used loosely. Describing a tutor as an IB or Cambridge examiner is only appropriate where current examiner status can be evidenced, and it should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it confers none. A family hearing that claim should ask what evidence supports it and what difference it is supposed to make, and should expect both answers to be modest.
