sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, at any distance
paragraphs: Distance changes nothing about the rules and arguably makes them easier to enforce, because everything happens in documents. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece, including a school practical write-up contributing to an internally assessed mark or a Diploma internal assessment.

One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is a malpractice trigger rather than a service, and the exposure falls on the candidate whose whole qualification is at stake rather than on the provider taking the fee. A useful test for any prospective arrangement is to ask plainly what they would do if asked to write a paragraph, and the answer is more informative than anything on a profile.

Board material should not be handed over as files. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides, and the right behaviour is to link the official page so a family reads the current version. That is also practically better in a screen-based arrangement, because a family that knows where the documents live can check a mark scheme during a session if they want to.

On claims: no satisfaction percentages, no self-asserted star ratings, no claims about the proportion of pupils reaching top grades, and no grade promises. None of the researched providers in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method, so any such figure is marketing. And no tutor should be described as an IB or Cambridge examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced, nor should that status be used to imply access to marking or boundaries, because it confers none.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and the first session
paragraphs: Mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered in this set, and a match is usually quick regardless of where a family lives, because the pool is not geographic. Thinner briefs still exist: Computer Science 0478 with pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, and unusual literature text lists. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free.

Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies. The brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days. The brief is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than concealed behind a local-looking telephone number - and that disclosure matters, because two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying so. Or the brief is not currently covered, in which case it is named rather than filled.

Parents are entitled to check the one credential that exists. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure circulating online is unverified.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful thing to bring is your child's last marked script rather than a description of the problem, because the session should be spent annotating it. By the end of the hour you should have an annotated file, a mark count by category, and a stated target - which is three of the five artefacts on this page, produced before anything has been paid for.

process.title: Decide the trade explicitly
process.description: Presence or specialism. For a Year 7 pupil who will not sit down alone, presence may genuinely win and that is worth saying. For a Year 10 or 11 pupil who needs a script read properly, the specialism wins and insisting on a local visit in Al Ain usually means losing it without the rate falling.

process.title: Require the five artefacts from session one
process.description: The annotated script, the dated mark count by category, the work produced between sessions, the re-answered question, and the monthly note in the school's vocabulary. Ask for all five at the start, not at the twelfth session. A provider who will not maintain them has told you how this will be assessed later.

process.title: Get the brief from the subject teacher
process.description: In a smaller school the teacher knows a pupil's work in detail, so ask which component is costing marks, what the mock split between method and content was, and what one thing they would have the pupil practise. That last answer is a precise brief, given free, by the best-informed person available.

process.title: Check the pupil can state what changed
process.description: At the end of a session they should be able to say, unprompted, what they will do differently: write the method, name the effect on a reader, attach the unit. If they cannot, the session was a lecture. Thirty seconds of that question is the most reliable quality control available at a distance.

process.title: Keep the annotated scripts together
process.description: Six annotated scripts from a term is a revision resource built entirely from your child's own errors, and it is the most useful document a candidate can hold in the final quarter. Almost nobody has one, because almost nobody saves the files. Put them in one folder from the first session.

whyPoints.title: The availability problem stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Al Ain's specialist pool is small and for a specific brief it can be empty. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a telephone number. Where a brief is not covered, it is named rather than filled with a generalist at the same rate.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what distance costs
whyPoints.description: Presence keeps a younger pupil at the table and lets a tutor read unspoken confusion. Those are real and they matter most at eleven and least at seventeen. A page claiming there are no trade-offs is a page that should not be trusted on anything else.

whyPoints.title: Five artefacts instead of reassurance
whyPoints.description: The annotated script, the dated mark count, the work produced between sessions, the re-answered question and the monthly note. A parent in the next room during an in-home lesson has less information than any of those, and none of them exists unless it is required.

whyPoints.title: Chosen from the specialism, not a radius
whyPoints.description: Selection starts from the specification code and tier on the exam entry. A pupil in Zakher can work with an Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 specialist who would never be available to drive there, at the published online band rather than the in-home one.

whyPoints.title: ADEK named, and the one arrangement to avoid
whyPoints.description: ADEK regulates private schools in Al Ain as well as Abu Dhabi city, and its reported ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled pupils. In a thin market that is exactly the arrangement that looks most convenient, and it should not be pursued.

whyPoints.title: No claim that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no satisfaction percentages, no self-asserted ratings, no unevidenced examiner claims, and no suggestion that ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB has approved or partnered with IB Gram. There is no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: Why is it hard to find a specialist tutor in Al Ain for a Brighton College Al Ain pupil?
faqs.answer: Market size, not school quality. Al Ain is smaller than Abu Dhabi city or Dubai, so the number of people living within driving distance who hold a particular specialism is correspondingly small. For general Key Stage 3 maths the local pool is reasonable. For Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 it is scarce, and for Cambridge Computer Science 0478 with pseudocode conventions or Additional Mathematics 0606 it may be empty in a given month. When the pool is empty, what disappears is the specialism rather than the arrangement.

faqs.question: What actually happens if we insist on a tutor who can come to our villa?
faqs.answer: Usually you get somebody local and general rather than the specialist you wanted, and the rate does not fall to match. The published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour is priced against the journey, not the expertise, so a family ends up paying a travel premium for content coverage. It is also invisible: a confident generalist going through a textbook with a competent pupil looks exactly like tutoring, the grade does not move, and the explanation tends to be attributed to the child.

faqs.question: Is there any case where a tutor in the room beats a specialist on screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth saying clearly. For a Year 7 or 8 pupil whose binding constraint is attention rather than expertise, presence matters: somebody in the room keeps them at the table and reads unspoken confusion before it is admitted. For that pupil a competent local tutor in person may genuinely be the better arrangement. By Year 10 or 11 the balance inverts, because the binding constraint becomes whether the person can explain why a six-mark question scored three.

faqs.question: What should replace being able to hear the lesson from the next room?
faqs.answer: Documents, not reassurance. Five do most of the work: the pupil's own marked script annotated on a shared screen and saved; a dated mark count by category; the piece of work produced between sessions; a question re-answered in the session; and a monthly note written in the school's own vocabulary. A parent in the next room hears tone and engagement, which is comforting and tells them nothing about whether marks are moving. Ask for all five at the first session rather than the twelfth.

faqs.question: What does a good online session actually consist of?
faqs.answer: The pupil's own marked paper on a shared screen, worked through question by question. The pupil reads a question aloud and says what they thought it wanted. The mark scheme is opened beside it and the gap is examined rather than explained. The pupil rewrites the answer while the tutor marks it clause by clause, then rewrites again. Three or four questions handled that way fills an hour and is where marks actually move, because the pupil ends with a skill rather than a note.

faqs.question: How long would a tutor spend travelling to a session in Zakher or Al Maqam?
faqs.answer: Thirty-five to forty-five minutes each way at peak from central Al Ain, so a one-hour lesson becomes a two-and-a-half-hour commitment. Across a thirteen-week term that is roughly nineteen hours of travel inside thirteen hours of teaching, which is the ratio the in-home band is priced against. Some families consider a tutor commuting from Abu Dhabi city at around ninety minutes each way; no rate makes that sustainable weekly, and such arrangements tend to become fortnightly, which breaks the frequency.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, the same body that regulates Abu Dhabi city, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The wider map is genuinely confusing and worth knowing: Dubai has KHDA, Sharjah has SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah has a Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Naming a regulator is not the same as being approved by one, and no tutoring provider should imply otherwise.

faqs.question: Could one of our child's own teachers tutor them privately in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: It should not be pursued, and in a thin market that is exactly the arrangement that looks most convenient. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct is also reported to bar serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current ADEK policy wording, but the practical advice holds either way.

faqs.question: Does a smaller school cohort help or hurt a pupil needing support?
faqs.answer: Both, in different ways. In a small set a teacher knows a pupil's work in genuine detail, so the questions that produce facts - which component is costing marks, what the mock method-against-content split was, what one thing to practise - tend to get precise answers. Against that, a pupil whose needs sit away from the middle of a small set gets less differentiation, and the school may not run a route such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or all three separate sciences for a handful of pupils.

faqs.question: Can the examined science practical work be prepared for online?
faqs.answer: Entirely, because it tests written precision rather than laboratory skill. The paper asks for a method with quantities, instruments and intervals stated, variables identified, scales read to the right precision, data tabulated and plotted, a trend interpreted and a specific improvement suggested. All of that is writing marked against a scheme, which makes it ideal shared-screen work. It is also the best-value science block available, because six to eight sessions on it raises marks across every science a pupil is taking at once.

faqs.question: Does the rate change if the tutor is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. The published band for the subject and tier applies whether a specialist is working from inside the UAE or into Gulf Standard Time from outside it. What does change is that the fact is disclosed, which matters because two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to telephone numbers outside the country without saying so, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. A family is entitled to know where the person teaching their child is before the first session.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Al Jimi, Zakher or Falaj Hazzaa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Al Ain families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The benefit is specific to this city: the tutor is selected from everyone who holds the specialism rather than from the handful willing to drive across Al Ain at five in the afternoon, and no session is lost to a long cross-city run.

faqs.question: How do we know the sessions are not just being talked through?
faqs.answer: Ask your child one question afterwards: what are you doing differently next time? A useful answer is specific - 'I write the method even when I can see the answer', 'I name the effect on the reader', 'I attach the unit'. A vague answer about going through topics means the session was a lecture. That check takes thirty seconds and it is the most reliable quality control available at a distance, more reliable than sitting in the next room ever was.

faqs.question: What should we keep from a term of online sessions?
faqs.answer: The annotated scripts, in one folder. Six scripts from a term, each worked through on screen with the lost marks named and the better answers written in, is a revision resource built entirely from your own child's errors. In the final quarter before the June series that is the most useful document a candidate can hold, and almost nobody has one because almost nobody saves the files. Start the folder at the first session rather than realising in April that it would have been useful.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-brighton-co.closingHeading: Choose the specialism, then require the evidence
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-brighton-co.closingBody: Work out which trade you are actually making. If your child is eleven and will not sit down alone, presence may win and that is a fair conclusion. If they are fifteen and losing marks nobody has categorised, the specialism wins, and in Al Ain that almost certainly means a screen. Then require the five artefacts from the first session: the annotated script, the dated mark count, the weekly piece of work, the re-answered question and the monthly note. A free trial lesson is one session with no card details required, and the right thing to bring is a marked script. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-british-sch.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below is matched to a named component: a specific paper on a specific syllabus code, or a specific coursework task. That is the level at which IGCSE marks are won and lost, and it is the level a request should be written at.

intro.heading: The question that decides a tutoring plan: which papers is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Most families cannot answer it, and that is not a criticism of the families. Schools report by subject, parents think in subjects, and tutoring is advertised by subject. The examination, though, is a set of components, each with its own weighting, duration, question style and mark scheme, and each with its own characteristic way of losing a candidate three marks. A plan built on the subject name attacks the wrong thing roughly half the time.

The first concrete step is therefore to ask the school's examinations officer for the syllabus code of every subject your child is entered for. It will look like 0580 or 0980 for Cambridge Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0625 for Physics, 0610 for Biology, or 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 for the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents. That single list changes a tutoring conversation from general to specific, and it takes one email to obtain.

The codes matter more than they look. Cambridge 0580 and 0980 are both Mathematics and are graded on different scales, so a student practising from the wrong set of past papers is reading boundaries that do not apply to them. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, which sets the highest grade available before the exam hall. The sciences carry separate practical arrangements, and the two routes through them are assessed quite differently. None of that is visible from a report card.

There is a second, purely administrative risk specific to candidates outside the United Kingdom. Cambridge International allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A family working from a timetable found online rather than from the centre's own zone version is carrying a real and avoidable risk, and the cost of resolving it is one email to the examinations officer rather than anything more elaborate.

Two things to be plain about before the components. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India. And every syllabus document, past paper and mark scheme referred to here belongs to Cambridge International, Pearson or the International Baccalaureate, and is referenced and linked rather than reproduced, because copying them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. A provider offering a folder of downloadable mark schemes is taking a risk on your family's behalf rather than giving you something useful, and the school's own legitimate materials cover the same ground.
bullets: Ask the examinations officer for every syllabus code, in writing
Cambridge 0580 and 0980 are graded on different scales
Core and Extended set the grade ceiling before the exam
The sciences have two different practical routes, assessed differently
Cambridge centres sit in one of six zones; the wrong timetable can lose a paper

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-british-sch.programmesIntro: A British-curriculum school in Abu Dhabi runs four stages that matter to a tutoring plan, and the assessment logic changes completely between the third and the fourth. These blocks say what each one actually measures.

programmes.name: Primary, Years 1 to 6
programmes.description: Teacher assessment against curriculum objectives, with no external examination and no syllabus code. The things that matter later are narrow and identifiable: number bonds and times tables to automaticity, reading stamina sufficient for a page of unfamiliar text, and the ability to write a paragraph with a point and support. A primary report can look settled while any one of those is missing.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi these years carry the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the British curriculum, under the federal requirement overseen by the Ministry of Education. Arabic appears on the report with a conventional grade attached, usually before anything else does, and for a non-Arabic-speaking household it is the first line where a parent has no independent way of judging whether the mark is fair or the progress real.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Three years of no external assessment, ending in the option choices that fix the IGCSE set. The most consequential tutoring in a British-curriculum education happens here and almost nobody buys it, because nothing is at stake visibly. Rearranging a formula, writing a method line, and structuring a written argument are the three transferable skills that the IGCSE years will test in nine subjects at once.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 option choices in the UAE carry a regulatory consequence most families only meet years later. Ministry of Education equivalency for British-curriculum students counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. A page currently ranking in this market states the figure as six; it is five, and that is a whole option slot.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two linear years assessed by terminal examination, built from components with published weightings. The paper set is determined by the syllabus code, the available grade range by the tier, and the practical assessment by which route the school uses. Each of those three is a decision made by the school before the course begins, and each one changes what useful tutoring looks like for that subject.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi candidate sits the June series or the November series with Cambridge, and the May and June or November series with Pearson Edexcel. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only. The centre's administrative zone determines which version of the timetable applies, and that question should be answered by the school rather than inferred from any published summary.

programmes.name: A Level, and the IB Diploma as the alternative route
programmes.description: A Level narrows to three or four subjects studied in depth, with no enforced breadth and no compulsory extended research piece. Some Abu Dhabi families move to an IB Diploma school for the sixth form instead, taking six subjects with three at Higher Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service. The two routes ask genuinely different things, and the choice is about working style as much as ability.
programmes.countryNote: Equivalency on the A Level route requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than grade E, or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE or GCSE passes. No IB points threshold is published on this page because none could be verified against the Ministry of Education's own site, so confirm that directly before planning a Diploma route around any figure.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-british-sch.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the components rather than the content, because the component is the unit a session should target. The losses described are the ones that recur on marked scripts rather than the ones that feel most difficult.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and 0980)
subjects.description: Two codes on different grading scales covering comparable content, so the first job is confirming which one is on the entry. Extended losses cluster in bearings, upper and lower bounds, similar-shape ratios and premature rounding. The single largest avoidable loss across both codes is a correct answer with no method written beside it.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: A different paper split from Cambridge and its own formula-sheet conventions, which is why a student drilled on Cambridge papers meets unfamiliar phrasing. The commonest specification error is assuming a formula is provided when it is not. Confirm the specification before buying any past-paper work for this subject.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Multiple-choice, theory and practical components, with the practical arrangement differing by school. Marks are lost on explain questions where no definition was stated first, and on circuit questions attempted without drawing the circuit. Electromagnetic induction is the single heaviest topic for lost marks at Extended level.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a practical component, and the practical is where the clearest separation between candidates happens, because it rewards a method somebody could actually follow. Units omitted from mole calculations cost marks the arithmetic had already earned. Organic naming and the reactivity series are recall and can be banked a year early.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content volume invites memorisation and the assessment rewards command-term discipline. Describe, explain, compare and suggest each want a different answer shape, and a well-learned paragraph earns two of five when the verb wanted a mechanism. Graph interpretation and experimental design make up most of the remaining recoverable marks.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Two papers testing different things that students revise as one. Reading comprehension rewards precise retrieval and inference under time pressure; directed writing rewards audience, form and purpose being addressed explicitly. Candidates who write well but ignore the form specified in the task lose marks that have nothing to do with their prose.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Essay marks depend on a sustained argument rather than coverage of the text, and the single most common loss is a well-informed tour of the plot. Quotation handling is marked: embedded, brief and analysed scores above long and unexamined. Marking essay plans rather than full essays produces faster progress and a weekly artefact.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Relevant for families moving to an IB Diploma sixth form. Algebraic fluency carries the course, the paper without a calculator concentrates the losses, and Higher Level adds proof and complex numbers where a missing justification line costs more than an arithmetic slip.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools alongside the British curriculum. Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed public guidance and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between streams. The non-Arab stream has its own syllabus and its own realistic ceiling.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Runs alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools. Content is prescribed, and KHDA's published guidance states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support here means working with the school's own material rather than substituting anything for it.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-british-sch.regionsIntro: The neighbourhoods families travel from, with the detail that affects scheduling rather than price. Al Mushrif sits inland on the island, and the afternoon pattern around it sets what time a weekly session can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: An established inland island neighbourhood with several long-standing schools nearby and a predominantly long-term resident population. Short school runs, but the roads around the school cluster are slow at pick-up, which pushes a dependable session start past half past four rather than at four.

regions.name: Al Karamah and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Villa and low-rise neighbourhoods adjoining Al Mushrif, where households often have children at two different schools in the same area. Two fixed slots on two evenings is the usual arrangement, and both can be held because neither depends on a tutor's driving route.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: The western island neighbourhoods, a short drive away, with a mix of villas and apartments and a high proportion of settled families. Multi-year arrangements are more common here than crash blocks, which suits the Key Stage 3 work that pays off at IGCSE.

regions.name: Corniche and Markaziyah
regions.note: Apartment living in the island core, where a large share of students travel by bus and the bus timetable sets the earliest realistic session. Families here are the most likely to need a slot after seven, which a travelling tutor can rarely offer at a sensible rate.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense towers at the eastern end with a large school-age population and a slow exit onto the main crossing in the late afternoon. Weekday sessions here work from five o'clock onwards, and weekend blocks are popular for full timed papers that need more than an hour.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The mainland villa corridor, roughly thirty to forty-five minutes from Al Mushrif at peak. For families who moved outward and kept the island school place, this crossing is precisely what a travelling tutor prices into an in-home rate.

regions.name: Saadiyat and Yas Islands
regions.note: Island communities a crossing away, where a sibling at a newer school is common. Two schools with two different assessment calendars in one household is the usual reason a family needs both IGCSE component work and Diploma criterion work in the same week.

schoolClusters.city: Al Mushrif and the inland island
schoolClusters.note: A cluster of long-established schools within a few minutes of one another, drawing from overlapping villa neighbourhoods. Students move between them more often than across to the mainland, so a tutor familiar with one school's examination calendar usually recognises the others.

schoolClusters.note: Newer schools on Saadiyat and Yas and the villa-corridor schools inland. A family here frequently has a sibling in this group on a different board, which is why one household often needs both paper-based and criterion-based tutoring.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-british-sch.modesIntro: Three arrangements built around components rather than hours. The right one depends on which component is losing the marks and how long there is before it is sat.

modes.title: Single-component work
modes.description: Sessions targeting one named paper on one syllabus code: Cambridge 0620 Paper 4, for instance, or Pearson 4MA1 Paper 2. Each session uses questions from that component only, under its own time constraints, and works on its characteristic losses. This is the most efficient arrangement available when a family knows which paper is pulling the grade down, and the mock usually tells them.

The work is specific: describing a method somebody could follow, identifying variables precisely, handling anomalous results honestly, and drawing a graph to the conventions the mark scheme requires.

This is the cheapest and least popular tutoring in the market and the highest return on cost.

sections.heading: Which papers your child sits, and what each one actually tests
paragraphs: An IGCSE subject grade is assembled from components, and the components are not interchangeable. A multiple-choice paper tests breadth of recall under speed. A structured theory paper tests whether a candidate can produce the specific thing a command term asked for. A practical or alternative-to-practical component tests experimental reasoning, which is a different skill from knowing the science. A candidate can be strong in one and weak in another within the same subject, and the overall grade hides that completely.

This is why the mock paper breakdown is worth more than the mock grade. A student with a C overall may be sitting on an A in the theory paper and a D in the practical, in which case the useful six weeks of work is entirely practical technique and none of it is content revision. The opposite case exists just as often. Either way, the subject-level grade points at nothing specific, and acting on it means guessing.

The table sets out the component types and what each one rewards, which is the framework to apply to whichever specification your child is entered for. The exact component list, durations and weightings must come from the current syllabus document for that code, via the school, because they differ between subjects, between codes and between boards, and they are revised. What transfers is the question to ask: which components, in what proportion, and where did the marks go on each? A school that cannot answer the third part of that question has not marked the paper properly, which is itself worth knowing.

sections.heading: Syllabus codes: why 0580 and 0980 are not the same entry
paragraphs: Cambridge runs more than one code for some subjects, and the codes differ in ways that matter to a candidate. For Mathematics, 0580 and 0980 cover comparable content but are reported on different grading scales. A student who has been practising from past papers and grade boundaries belonging to the other code has been measuring themselves against numbers that do not apply, which is a demoralising and entirely avoidable experience.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE adds a second axis of confusion, because its codes look nothing like Cambridge's: 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4PH1 for Physics, 4BI1 for Biology. The paper splits differ, the formula-sheet conventions differ, and the question phrasing differs noticeably even where the physics is identical. A student drilled on the wrong board has practised the right subject for the wrong examination.

The fix costs one email. Ask the examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject on the entry, and keep the reply. Everything downstream depends on it: which past papers to buy, which boundaries to read, which revision guide is the right one, and which specialist to ask for. A tutor who starts work without that list is working on assumptions, and in a two-year linear course those assumptions are expensive to discover late. The same email should ask for the centre's administrative zone, because that is the other piece of information nobody volunteers and everybody needs. Two answers, one message, and the whole plan rests on solid ground instead of inference.

sections.heading: The science practical component, and the two routes through it
paragraphs: Science subjects assess experimental skill, and schools reach that assessment by different routes depending on the arrangement at the centre. The component is worth a meaningful share of the grade and it is the one families most often leave entirely unprepared, partly because it feels like something only school can teach and partly because it is invisible in a report that gives one grade per subject.

What it actually rewards is communicable reasoning rather than laboratory dexterity. A candidate has to describe a method in enough detail that a reader could repeat it, identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables precisely, explain how a measurement was made and why that way, handle an anomalous result honestly rather than quietly, and draw a graph to the conventions the mark scheme specifies. All of those can be taught and practised without equipment.

That is why practical preparation works online as well as it does. The marks are in the writing and the reasoning, not in the manipulation, and a tutor can mark a method description as rigorously as an examiner will. The first useful exercise is always the same: the student writes a method, the tutor tries to follow it exactly as written, and the gaps become obvious to the student rather than being pointed out to them. Confirm with the school which practical route applies before buying any preparation for this component, because the routes are assessed differently and preparing for the wrong one is work that earns nothing.

sections.heading: The six-zone timetable rule, and the question that resolves it
paragraphs: This is the most consequential administrative detail on the page and almost nothing in this market mentions it. Cambridge International allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones. It states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. A UAE candidate working from a timetable found online is therefore carrying a risk that nobody has told them about.

The resolution is a single question to the school's examinations officer: which administrative zone is our centre in, and may we have the correct timetable version. Keep the reply. Use that document for every date, and treat any other summary, including this page, as unreliable for timing purposes. This also matters when a family is planning around a return flight or a family commitment, because the same paper can sit on different days in different zones.

Pearson Edexcel operates differently but with a comparable caution. It publishes provisional timetables ahead of a series and then finalises them, which means a date read early can be revised. The correct practice is to work from the live official timetable rather than from any restatement of it. The historical anchors are checkable: the November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the day after, and November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: The five-subject equivalency rule, and why Year 9 options decide it
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency converts a foreign school certificate into something the UAE system recognises, and for British-curriculum students the published requirements are specific. A candidate must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects.

That exclusion is the part families miss, and it has a direct effect on an option sheet. A student taking nine subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has seven that can count, which is comfortable. A student taking a narrower set, or one whose accredited subject list is shorter than it appears, can find the margin uncomfortably thin. The decision point is Year 9, which is years before anyone thinks about attestation.

One further correction is worth stating because it is live in this market: a page currently ranking tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required. The published figure is five. Publishing the correct number is a small thing that beats a ranking page on accuracy, and acting on the wrong one costs a family a genuine option slot. Equivalency is also not a process a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and it is not a reason to buy tutoring; it is a rule to know early and to verify with the official channel.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside the IGCSE set
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE teach mandatory UAE subjects regardless of the licensed international curriculum. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's requirement, and it is the reason an IGCSE timetable in Abu Dhabi is fuller than the same timetable in England.

The most detailed published guidance comes from Dubai's regulator and is worth reading even by an Abu Dhabi family, because it describes the structure that the federal rule produces. It requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It sets the language of instruction for each stream, and it requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval to teach those subjects.

Two practical consequences follow for tutoring. The first is that the non-Arab Arabic stream is a different course with a different ceiling from the first-language stream, and a tutor should be matched to the right one. The second is a constraint on material: the published guidance states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited for these subjects. Support therefore means working with the school's own material rather than importing an alternative course, which is a narrower and more honest offer than most of this market makes.

sections.heading: What a session fixes in one hour, and what it does not
paragraphs: The honest unit of change in tutoring is not an hour, and pretending otherwise is how families end up disappointed by something that was working. Some things genuinely shift within a single session, and they are all conventions: reading the command term before the question, stating a definition before an explanation, writing units on every line, drawing the circuit first, writing the method line the mark scheme credits. Those transfer immediately across every paper the student sits.

Other things take weeks. Algebraic fluency is built by short daily practice and cannot be installed in a session. Timed-paper pacing improves over four or five full papers, not one. Reading stamina and essay structure move across a term. And a missing conceptual foundation, in energetics or in mechanics or in the behaviour of fractions, has to be rebuilt in sequence, which means starting earlier in the syllabus than the student expects and is the least popular correct answer in this business.

This matters commercially as well as educationally. A tutor who promises that six sessions will move a grade from a D to an A is describing a sale. A tutor who says that two sessions will eliminate a unit-omission habit, four will fix command-term discipline, and a term will rebuild algebraic fluency is describing a plan, and the second is checkable against the next marked paper. Ask which category each item falls into during the free trial lesson; the answer tells you what the next six months would look like.

sections.heading: Coursework and controlled assessment: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some specifications carry coursework or a non-examined assessment, and a sixth form produces more of it. In every case the submission has to be the student's own work, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student rather than on anyone selling assistance. This section states the boundary in advance so that no session of this kind starts with it unclear.

What a tutor can do is substantial and is the actual service being paid for. Read the published assessment criteria alongside the student and explain what each descriptor awards. Press on a research question or investigation title until it is answerable within the limit. Teach the statistical test, the laboratory technique, the referencing convention or the model the task requires. Read a draft the student wrote and name the criterion that is costing marks. Rehearse the conversation the student is about to have with their teacher or supervisor.

What a tutor cannot do is contribute to the submission: no text, no redraft into a final version, no data presented as collected, no edit that leaves the work substantially someone else's. One operation ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student rather than the seller. The test a student can apply unaided is whether they could explain every sentence of their own submission, without prompting, to the person who marks it. If they could not, the line has been crossed whoever crossed it, and the honest repair is to go back to the last version that was genuinely theirs.

process.title: Get the code list from the examinations officer first
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier for every entered subject, in writing, plus the centre's administrative zone. One email produces the single most useful document a family can hold, and everything downstream depends on it: which past papers, which boundaries, which revision guide, which specialist.

process.title: Send the mock breakdown, not the mock grade
process.description: A subject grade points at nothing. A component breakdown shows that the theory paper was fine and the practical was not, or the reverse, and that determines where the next six weeks go. If the school does not provide a breakdown, ask for one; the marks exist per component.

process.title: Name the component in the request
process.description: A request that says Chemistry reaches a generalist. One that says Cambridge 0620 Extended, Paper 4 and Paper 6, currently a C, reaches someone who has marked both. At this level the component is the unit of work, and matching on the subject name alone wastes the first two sessions.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson to sort conventions from foundations
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, no payment and no card. Ask them to list which losses on the script are conventions fixable in a session and which are foundations needing a term. A tutor who can separate the two is describing a plan; one who cannot is describing a sale.

process.title: Check the practical route before preparing for it
process.description: Science practical arrangements differ between centres, and preparing for the wrong route is wasted work. Ask the science department which arrangement applies, then prepare specifically: method writing, variable identification, anomaly handling and graph conventions, all of which can be marked rigorously online.

whyPoints.description: A tutor allocated to Cambridge 0625 Paper 4 or Pearson 4MA1 Paper 2 knows the paper structure, the formula conventions and the characteristic losses. faqs.question: How do we find out which syllabus codes our child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer in writing for the board, syllabus code and tier of every subject on the entry, and keep the reply. The codes look like 0580 or 0980 for Cambridge Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0625 for Physics and 0610 for Biology, or 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 for the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents. Everything downstream depends on that list: which past papers to use, which grade boundaries apply, and which specialist to ask for.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge 0580 and 0980 Mathematics interchangeable for revision?
faqs.answer: No. They cover comparable content but are reported on different grading scales, so past papers and grade boundaries from one do not translate cleanly to the other. A student measuring themselves against the wrong boundaries gets a misleading and usually demoralising picture of where they stand. Confirm which code is on the entry before buying any materials, and check that any tutor you engage is working from the same code rather than from the version they happen to know.

faqs.question: What is the six-zone timetable rule and does it affect Abu Dhabi candidates?
faqs.answer: It affects every Cambridge candidate outside the United Kingdom. Cambridge International allocates each examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone is essential, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Ask your examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and work only from that timetable version. A date found online is not a safe substitute.

faqs.question: Why does the mock component breakdown matter more than the mock grade?
faqs.answer: Because the grade hides the diagnosis. A candidate with a C overall might be sitting on an A in the theory paper and a D in the practical component, in which case the next six weeks should be entirely practical technique and none of it content revision. The reverse case is just as common. The subject grade points at nothing specific, so acting on it is guessing. If the school does not issue a breakdown, ask for one; the marks exist per component.

faqs.question: Can the science practical component really be prepared for online?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the marks are in the reasoning and the writing rather than in handling apparatus. The component rewards describing a method someone could repeat, naming independent, dependent and controlled variables precisely, explaining how a measurement was taken, treating an anomalous result honestly, and drawing a graph to the conventions the mark scheme specifies. The most effective first exercise is the tutor following the student's written method exactly as written, which makes the gaps the student's own discovery.

faqs.question: Which practical route does our school use, and why do we need to know?
faqs.answer: Science practical arrangements differ between centres, and preparing for the wrong one is wasted work. Ask the science department which arrangement applies to each science subject before buying any preparation for that component. It is a short question with a definite answer, and it determines what the session should contain. Families most often leave this component entirely unprepared because it feels like something only the school can teach, which is not true of the parts that carry the marks.

faqs.question: For equivalency, how many accredited IGCSE passes must appear on the certificate?
faqs.answer: Five. A British-curriculum student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. There is a post-16 requirement too: one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade. A page currently ranking in this market says six subjects; it is five, and the difference is a real option slot at Year 9.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the equivalency total?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification states explicitly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. They are still mandatory in UAE private schools under the federal requirement, so a student takes them and they appear on the certificate, but they do not contribute to the five. That is worth knowing when counting accredited subjects on a Year 9 option sheet, which is where the margin is actually set.

faqs.question: What are the rules on tutoring Arabic and Islamic Education in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Published guidance requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It also states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited for these subjects. Practically, tutoring means working with the school's own material rather than importing an alternative course, and the tutor must match the correct stream.

faqs.question: Which Arabic stream should a non-Arabic-speaking family ask for?
faqs.answer: Arabic as an additional language, which is a separate course from Arabic as a first language with its own expectations and its own realistic ceiling. The two are taught in separate classes by requirement, and a tutor matched to the wrong stream will either pitch far above the student or cover material the school is not assessing. Ask the school which stream the student is in and request a tutor for that stream specifically rather than for Arabic in general.

faqs.question: What can a single session actually change for a Year 11 candidate?
faqs.answer: Conventions, and they transfer immediately. Reading the command term before the question, stating a definition before an explanation, writing units on every line of a calculation, drawing the circuit before attempting the question, and writing the method line the mark scheme credits. Each of those can be installed in an hour and shows up on the next paper. What cannot change in a session is algebraic fluency, timed pacing or a missing conceptual foundation, and an honest plan says which is which.

faqs.question: Is Key Stage 3 tutoring worth paying for when nothing is examined?
faqs.answer: It is the highest return on cost in the whole market and the least purchased. Three transferable skills decide the IGCSE years in nine subjects at once: rearranging a formula, writing method, and structuring a paragraph with a point and support. Building them in Years 7 to 9 costs the lower end of the market bands, roughly AED 65 to 150 an hour, because it is content teaching rather than diagnosis. Fixing the same gaps in Year 11 costs the specialist rate and competes with exam preparation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a non-examined assessment that is due next week?
faqs.answer: With the student's own draft, yes; with the writing, no, regardless of the deadline. A tutor can explain what each criterion descriptor awards, narrow the title until it is answerable, teach the method the task requires, mark the draft the student wrote and name the criterion costing marks, and rehearse the conversation with the teacher. A tutor cannot contribute text, redraft into a final version or supply data. One operation ranking in this market sells completed coursework, and the student carries that risk alone.

faqs.question: Why will a tutor not supply past papers and mark schemes directly?
faqs.answer: Because they belong to Cambridge International, Pearson or the International Baccalaureate, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter rather than a service. For unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. The correct approach is to reference the official document, link to it on the board's own site, and work from materials the school has legitimately provided. A provider offering downloadable mark schemes and grade-boundary tables is taking a risk on the family's behalf.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost for a British-curriculum student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and a specialist in a named component at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Entry-level online tutors sit lower, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the fee. Each figure belongs to the provider named.

faqs.question: Can a weekly session near Al Mushrif realistically start straight after school?
faqs.answer: Usually not at four o'clock. The roads around the inland island school cluster are slow at pick-up, and a dependable weekly slot starts from about half past four onwards, later for families whose children travel by bus from the island core. That is the practical argument for video delivery here rather than a marketing one: the slot can be set where it actually works and moved by an hour when something intervenes, without anyone redrawing a driving route.

Send those with the window in the week that genuinely works. You will get back a specific view of which component is losing marks, an honest separation of what a session can fix from what needs a term, and a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor before any payment is taken. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-cranleigh-a.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here work on named specifications rather than year groups, which is what matters for a school running IGCSE into a sixth form. A request for Pearson 4PH1 Physics or for Diploma Economics Paper 3 reaches someone who has marked that component.

intro.heading: Working up from the cheapest rate instead of down from the dearest
paragraphs: Every agency page in this market quotes from the top. The premium figure goes first because it anchors expectations, and the cheaper options get described as compromises. That is a sales technique, not information, so this page inverts it. Below is what the Abu Dhabi market charges, starting with the least, and the honest answer to the question parents actually ask: at what point does the cheap option stop working?

The floor of this market is around AED 33 to 65 an hour. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52; EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that rate the tutor is typically a university student or a recent graduate, the lesson is content explanation rather than diagnosis, and the preparation between sessions is minimal. For a Year 8 student who missed three weeks of algebra and needs someone to re-teach it patiently, that is a genuinely good purchase and the rest of this page is irrelevant. Nothing about a higher price buys a better explanation of how to expand brackets.

The next band up, roughly AED 150 to 300, is a qualified subject teacher working online. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Here the difference is not the explanation but the diagnosis: this tutor reads a marked script and can say which four marks the student drops repeatedly and why. That is the service a Year 11 candidate in a linear two-year IGCSE course needs, because the content is largely known by then and the losses are technique. Above that, AED 200 to 450 and beyond buys a specialist in one named specification, and AED 650 is the top published figure in this market, from BartyED.

In-home visiting rates sit separately at AED 180 to 500 an hour, because a travelling rate is a teaching rate with a driving rate folded in. On Saadiyat Island that folded-in portion is substantial: the island is reached by a single bridge corridor, and a tutor crossing at the end of the working day is committing an evening to deliver an hour. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons here run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, and the comparison table further down sets out what that trade actually gains and costs.

One more thing before the tables. The bands above are jobs, not quality tiers, and the most common purchasing error in this market is buying the wrong job rather than buying too cheaply. A Year 7 who needs patient re-teaching is overpaying at the specialist rate and will get no more from it. A Year 11 four months from a June series is underpaying at the entry rate and will get an explanation of content they already half-know. Deciding which job you need comes before deciding what to spend on it, and that is what the next two sections are for.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-cranleigh-a.programmesIntro: Cranleigh Abu Dhabi runs a British-curriculum pathway into a sixth form, so the programmes that matter are the lower secondary years, the IGCSE block, and the two post-16 routes. Each needs a different kind of teaching, and the rate bands above apply differently to each.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, Key Stage 3
programmes.description: Three years with no external examination, which makes it the cheapest place in a school career to fix something and the easiest place to let it slide. The subjects that decide IGCSE grades are settled here: algebraic manipulation, written argument in English, and the habit of showing method. A Year 9 who cannot rearrange a formula will meet that same gap in Physics, Chemistry and Maths simultaneously two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Key Stage 3 in Abu Dhabi carries the mandatory UAE subjects alongside it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, under the federal requirement overseen by the Ministry of Education. For a Saadiyat family on a short posting, Arabic is usually the first subject where the report card and the parent's ability to help diverge.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, almost entirely terminally assessed, with syllabus codes that determine the paper set: Cambridge 0580 or 0980 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, which caps the grade available. The tier decision is made by the school a year before anyone sits a paper.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE set matters beyond the sixth form for a UAE resident. Ministry of Education equivalency for British-curriculum students counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that five. One page ranking in this market states the figure as six subjects; it is five, and a Year 9 option choice should be made against the correct number.

programmes.name: A Level sixth form
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, with no breadth requirement and no compulsory extended research piece. The step up from IGCSE is steepest in Mathematics and the sciences, where the questions stop testing recall and start testing whether the student can apply an idea to an unfamiliar context. Students who coasted to an A at IGCSE on memory meet that wall in the first term and often need help identifying what changed.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency the A Level route requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than grade E, or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, in addition to the five IGCSE passes. That makes the A Level set a regulatory document as well as a university application, which is a point sixth-form families in Abu Dhabi often discover at the attestation stage rather than at the option stage.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service. The Diploma keeps breadth that A Level drops, and adds internal assessment in every subject. The hardest part is rarely the content; it is that five Internal Assessment deadlines and a four-thousand-word Extended Essay land inside one stretch of the second year. UAE candidates sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: No IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency appears on this page, because none could be verified against the Ministry's own publication, and an unverified threshold repeated across hundreds of pages is a liability. A Diploma family in Abu Dhabi should confirm the current requirement with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly before planning around any figure.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-cranleigh-a.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where Saadiyat and island families most often ask for help, with what each component actually tests. The level moves the rate more than the subject does, so use these notes to decide what you need rather than what it costs.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Extended reaches A* to E; Core stops at C, and that ceiling is set by the school's tier entry, not by the exam. Extended losses cluster in bearings, similar-shape ratios, upper and lower bounds, and in rounding a surd that should have been left exact. The non-calculator demands are lighter than at A Level but the method marks are not.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Covers similar ground to Cambridge with a different paper split and its own formula-sheet conventions, which matters because a student drilled on Cambridge past papers will meet unfamiliar question phrasing. Students lose marks assuming a formula is given when it is not. Check which specification the school entered before buying any past-paper preparation.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 and 4PH1)
subjects.description: Definitions carry more marks than calculations at this level. A student who cannot state what a field is in one sentence cannot earn the three marks for the explanation that follows. Electricity, circuits and electromagnetic induction produce the heaviest losses, and the reliable fix is drawing the circuit before writing a word, every time.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 and 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations presented without units lose marks that the arithmetic had already earned. The practical paper separates candidates sharply, because it rewards describing a procedure someone could actually follow rather than one that sounds plausible. Organic naming and the reactivity series are pure recall and are worth banking early.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 and 4BI1)
subjects.description: Students revise it as a memory test and are assessed on command terms. Describe, explain, compare and suggest each want a different shape of answer, and a well-learned paragraph scores two out of five when the verb asked for a mechanism. Graph interpretation and experimental design are the two recoverable weak spots.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency decides this course. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and a longer calculus reach, and the paper without a calculator is where the damage concentrates. The commonest avoidable loss is a correct method that was never written down, because the mark scheme credits the working and the student only recorded the answer.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · A Level
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks, and students who draw from memory rather than from the question routinely shift the wrong curve. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is quantitative and is the single clearest separator between a five and a seven. At A Level the equivalent separator is the extended evaluation paragraph that most candidates run out of time to write.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IGCSE · DP HL and SL · A Level
subjects.description: The unseen analysis is won in the reading, not the writing: students who annotate for five minutes outscore those who start writing immediately. At Diploma level the Individual Oral usually fails on a global issue that is too broad to evidence in ten minutes, and that choice can be fixed in a single session.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written paper, not the coding, is where grades are lost. Students who can program fluently still drop marks on trace tables, logic gate completion and on explaining an algorithm in prose. At Diploma level the Internal Assessment needs a client with a real problem, and a weak client choice limits the mark ceiling from the start.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed guidance and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two streams. The non-Arab stream is the one most commonly tutored in expatriate households on the island.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-cranleigh-a.regionsIntro: Saadiyat Island and the communities around it have a particular logistics problem, and it is the reason the travel premium in the tables below is not a rounding error. These are the areas Cranleigh families most often travel from.

regions.name: Saadiyat Beach
regions.note: Villa and townhouse communities within a few minutes of the school, which makes the morning run short and the afternoon one unpredictable only on event weekends. Households here are disproportionately on two to four year postings, so demand skews towards bridging a student into a British curriculum rather than long-run support.

regions.name: Saadiyat Cultural District
regions.note: Apartment buildings and newer towers with a younger resident profile and a smaller secondary-age population. Families here commonly want evening slots after a working parent is home rather than straight after school, which is the timing a travelling tutor can least afford to offer.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods a short crossing away, with several long-standing schools of their own. Households here often keep one child at a school on the island and send another to Saadiyat, which produces the two-timetable problem that makes a fixed weekly slot per child valuable.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense residential towers with a large school-age population and no single dominant school, so students commute outward in several directions. The exit onto the main crossing at half past three is the slowest part of the day here, and a five o'clock start is far more reliable than a four o'clock one.

regions.name: Al Raha and Khalifa City
regions.note: The mainland villa corridor, roughly thirty to forty-five minutes from Saadiyat at peak. For families who moved outward but kept the school place, this crossing is exactly the journey a travelling tutor prices into an in-home rate, and the reason the online figure undercuts it so clearly.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Residential clusters with a growing secondary population and a commute that is short in distance but hostage to the event calendar. Families here ask most often for a schedule that survives disruption, which a video slot does and a driving route does not.

regions.name: Mangrove Village and Al Zeina
regions.note: Waterfront communities where a high proportion of students travel by school bus, so the bus timetable rather than a parent's diary sets the earliest possible session. Weekend blocks are requested more often here than weekday evenings.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat Island and the cultural district
schoolClusters.note: A concentration of newer international schools built within a decade of each other, drawing from the same villa and apartment communities. Students move between these schools more often than between island and mainland ones, which means a tutor who knows one school's sequencing usually recognises another's.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island and the mainland corridor
schoolClusters.note: The older established schools and the newer villa-corridor ones. Families at Cranleigh frequently have a sibling in this group, which is the most common reason one household needs both an IGCSE and a Diploma tutor at the same time on different schedules.

modes.title: Fixed weekly slot across a term
modes.description: One or two sessions a week held in the same place in the week for a whole term, running alongside the school's own scheme of work. This is the lowest effective cost per unit of progress, because no part of the session is spent rediscovering where the student is. For a Year 10 student in the first half of a two-year IGCSE course it is also the only mode that prevents the Year 11 scramble.

This is the dearest mode per hour because specialist availability is at its scarcest, and it is the one families most often buy too late. sections.heading: What each AED band actually buys in the hour
paragraphs: Price bands in tutoring are usually described by who the tutor is. That is the wrong axis, because a parent cannot verify it. The useful axis is what happens inside the hour, and that differs sharply band to band. At the bottom of the market the hour is explanation: the tutor teaches a topic the student has not understood, in a way the classroom did not land. Nothing about a higher fee improves that service for a Year 8.

In the middle band the hour becomes diagnosis. The tutor arrives having read something the student produced, identifies a repeating error, and spends the session on that rather than on the syllabus. That is a different product and it needs a different person. At the top of the market the hour is component-specific: a tutor who knows how Paper 4 of a named specification is marked, what the examiner report said about last series, and where candidates at this grade typically stall.

The table below sets the bands out with what the hour contains and where it runs out. Read the last column carefully, because the point of this page is that each band has a real failure point. A Year 11 candidate four months from a June series is poorly served at the bottom of the market, and a Year 7 who needs patient re-teaching is overpaying at the top. The bands are not quality tiers; they are different jobs.

sections.heading: The cheapest option that is genuinely worth buying, and when it stops
paragraphs: The honest cheapest purchase in this market is a session or two a month at the entry band for a lower secondary student who has fallen behind on one topic. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, a Year 8 who missed three weeks of algebra can be caught up by somebody patient with good explanations, and paying three times that would buy nothing extra. Any page that tells a parent otherwise is selling.

It stops working at a specific and predictable point: when the problem is no longer what the student knows but how they answer. That transition usually happens in the second half of Year 10 and is fully arrived by Year 11. A candidate who understands the content but keeps dropping four marks a paper does not need another explanation; they need someone who can look at their script and name the pattern. That requires a tutor who has marked that specification, which is the AED 150 to 300 band at minimum.

It also stops working for anything criterion-assessed. An Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or an A Level coursework piece is marked against published descriptors, and a tutor who has not read those descriptors against real student work cannot say which criterion is losing marks. The second failure point is subject reach at Higher Level: entry-band tutors can usually handle Standard Level content and run out somewhere inside the Higher Level syllabus, often mid-session, which is worse than not starting.

sections.heading: Saadiyat Island logistics and what the travel premium pays for
paragraphs: Saadiyat is reached by a bridge corridor, which makes the travel component of an in-home rate unusually visible here. A tutor living on the island and teaching on the island has a short journey. A tutor living anywhere else and teaching on Saadiyat at five in the afternoon is committing roughly ninety minutes of road time to deliver sixty minutes of lesson, and that is why the local in-home band reaches AED 500. The driving is not a surcharge; it is most of the gap.

The second cost is reliability. A session that depends on a journey fails for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching: a slow crossing, an event on Yas, a sandstorm, a tutor's own schedule running over. Across a twenty-eight-session term, families with travelling tutors commonly lose two or three sessions to logistics, and in exam term those are the least replaceable hours of the year. A video slot fails only if the student or the tutor is genuinely unavailable.

The third cost is choice, and it is the one that actually matters for a sixth-form candidate. Travel restricts the tutor pool to whoever lives within a sensible drive of Saadiyat. For Pearson 4PH1 Physics or Diploma Economics Paper 3, that radius may contain nobody with the right experience. The whole argument for online delivery in this emirate is not convenience; it is that a national pool contains the specialist and a twenty-minute radius does not.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers several IGCSE subjects, and the tier a student is entered for decides the highest grade available to them before they sit anything. Extended opens the A* to E range. Core stops at C. That is not a prediction; it is an administrative ceiling, and it is applied by the school at entry, typically a year or more before the exam. Parents discover it late because nothing on a report card announces it.

The decision is not always wrong. A student genuinely working at a D or E on Extended material may score better and be less damaged by a Core entry, and there are subjects where that is the right call. What makes it a problem is when it is made from a weak Year 9 baseline for a student who then improves, or when the family did not know the ceiling existed. Changing tier after entries close is at best difficult and at worst impossible.

Pearson Edexcel runs a comparable structure under different names, with Higher and Foundation tiers on some specifications. The practical advice is identical: ask the school, in writing, which tier each subject has been entered for and when the final decision point falls. Then ask what the student would need to demonstrate to be moved up. That is a concrete, answerable question, and the answer tells a family how many weeks of work the move requires and therefore what tutoring is actually for.
