sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, a different exam
paragraphs: A family buying past-paper practice needs to know which board their child is entered with, and a surprising number do not. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs in the same subjects, and the content overlap is high, but the paper structure, the formula-sheet conventions and the question phrasing differ. A student drilled on the wrong board's papers has practised the right physics and the wrong exam.

The structural differences are worth knowing concretely. Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended on many subjects; Pearson uses Higher and Foundation on some specifications and no tier on others. Cambridge publishes a six-zone timetable structure and states that it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of a series, which means dates can be revised and the live official timetable is the only one to work from.

Session availability also differs. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March main series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate's options are June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. For a resit decision, that difference in structure is the whole question, so get the specification code from the school before planning anything.

sections.heading: The deadline before the deadline, and who actually holds it
paragraphs: The exam date is not the date that matters. Final entries close months before any paper is sat, and they are submitted by the school or examination centre rather than by the parent. The most expensive mistake available to a family here is assuming someone will ask them. If a student intends to sit an extra subject, change tier, or take a paper as a private candidate, that intention has to reach the examinations officer before entries close, and the officer will not chase it.

Backward-looking dates are the only ones worth stating precisely, because they can be checked. Pearson Edexcel's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and reached students the day after. November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026. Those are real, dated anchors for how long a results wait actually is.

Forward-looking windows are named by month here and nowhere by year, because provisional timetables are revised and a page that pins a future date is wrong a year later with nobody having touched it. The useful output of this section is the sequence rather than the dates: find the entry deadline, work backwards to the mock window, work backwards again to the point at which a tier change is still possible, and put a tutoring plan on that timeline rather than on a term structure. A plan built on terms discovers the coursework deadline a fortnight before it falls; a plan built on the entry sequence does not.

sections.heading: Is the tutor permitted to teach in the UAE, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted but regulated. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone who should hold one and does not is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted at you as unverified.

The eligibility list is broader than most parents expect. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, under the service named for private tutor licensing, with a stated completion time of two working days and no listed fee. That is the official route and the one to point anybody at.

There is a separate and more important restriction for an Abu Dhabi family. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify the wording against ADEK's own publication, but the practical reading is unambiguous: an offer of your child's own teacher privately is a problem, not a shortcut. A tuition operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again and needs a KHDA educational services permit in Dubai.

sections.heading: Coursework, feedback, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: A British-curriculum sixth form produces assessed work that must be the student's own: a Diploma Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, an A Level coursework piece or a non-examined assessment. The rules governing them are the board's and the school's, and the consequence of breaching them falls on the student. This section states the boundary in advance so that no coursework session begins with it unclear.

What a tutor can do is substantial. They can read the published assessment criteria alongside the student and explain what each descriptor is awarding. They can press on a research question until it is narrow enough to answer inside the word limit. They can teach the statistical test, the lab technique or the economic model the piece needs. They can read a draft the student wrote and identify which criterion is costing marks. They can rehearse the meeting the student is about to have with their supervisor.

What a tutor cannot do is contribute to the text. Not a paragraph, not a redraft into final form, not data for the student to present as collected, not an edit that leaves the submission substantially someone else's work. One operation ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one puts a student's entire qualification at risk and the seller's business at none. The test a student can apply unaided is whether they could explain every sentence of their own submission to their supervisor without prompting.

process.title: Send the specification code, not the subject name
process.description: A request that says Physics gets a generalist. A request that says Pearson 4PH1, Paper 1, currently a 5, sixth form wants a 7 reaches someone who has marked that paper. If you do not know the code, the school's examinations officer does, and it is the single most useful thing to ask them for.

process.title: Say which band you want, and why
process.description: This page sets out the market bands and where each one runs out. Tell us which you are aiming at. A family that wants entry-band topic catch-up for a Year 8 should not be quoted a specialist rate, and a Year 11 four months from a series should not be offered the cheapest option.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson first
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, no payment and no card required. The session is used to diagnose rather than to sell, and afterwards you receive a written view of where the marks are going. If the tutor is wrong for the student, you have lost an hour and nothing else.

process.title: Get the availability answer in writing
process.description: If no specialist in that specification is free at the time you need, you are told before you commit, with the alternatives spelled out: a different slot, a different tutor, or a specialist outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time. No competitor page measured for this project publishes a coverage limit.

process.title: Put the exam calendar in before the term calendar
process.description: Entry deadlines, mock windows, coursework submission dates and the series itself go into the plan first. Weekly subject work is then built around them. A plan built on terms rather than deadlines consistently discovers the Internal Assessment two weeks before it is due.

whyPoints.title: Prices from the bottom up, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, and the bands run cheapest first so that a family can find the lowest honest option rather than be anchored to the dearest. Three of six competitor pages measured for this project published no rate at all.

whyPoints.title: Matched on specification, not on year group
whyPoints.description: A tutor allocated to Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 knows the paper split, the formula-sheet conventions and the question phrasing. A student practising the wrong board's papers has prepared the right subject for the wrong exam, and that is a mistake no amount of hours fixes.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool wider than a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Saadiyat sits behind a bridge corridor, and a travelling tutor can only come from a limited area around it. Online delivery means the choice is everyone available on Gulf Standard Time, which in scarce components like Higher Level Physics or Economics Paper 3 is the difference between the right person and an available one.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated before you pay, not after
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where delivery actually happens.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals, no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and names no school on this page as a client. No satisfaction percentage or star rating appears here, because none can be evidenced with a sample and a method.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary written down first
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads, questions and gives feedback on work the student wrote. A tutor does not contribute text, redraft to final form or supply data for any Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or A Level coursework. The line is stated before the first coursework session, because the qualification at risk is the student's.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest tutoring that is actually worth paying for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The entry band, roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, is a genuinely good purchase for a lower-secondary student who has fallen behind on a specific topic. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that rate the tutor explains content clearly and nothing more expensive explains algebra any better. It stops being the right purchase when the problem shifts from what the student knows to how they answer, which usually happens in the second half of Year 10.

faqs.question: At what point does a cheap tutor stop being enough for a Cranleigh Year 11?
faqs.answer: At the point where the losses are technique rather than knowledge. A candidate who understands the content but drops four marks on every paper needs someone who can read their script and name the repeating pattern, which requires a tutor who has marked that specification. That is the AED 150 to 300 band at minimum. The second failure point is anything criterion-assessed, because a tutor who has not worked against the published descriptors cannot say which criterion is costing marks. The third is Higher Level reach, where entry-band tutors often run out mid-session.

faqs.question: Why does the in-home rate on Saadiyat Island reach AED 500 an hour?
faqs.answer: Because the fee is a teaching rate with a driving rate folded into it, and Saadiyat is reached by a bridge corridor. A tutor coming from the mainland villa communities at five in the afternoon commits around ninety minutes of road time to deliver sixty minutes of lesson, and that time is paid for whether or not it appears on the invoice. Travel also loses sessions: families with travelling tutors commonly lose two or three out of a twenty-eight-session term. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at any rate.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE Core and Extended, and who decides?
faqs.answer: Extended opens the A* to E grade range; Core stops at C. The school decides at final entry, typically a year or more before the paper is sat, and nothing on a report card announces the ceiling. The decision is not always wrong: a student genuinely working at D or E on supplementary content may score better on Core. It becomes a problem when it was made from a weak Year 9 baseline for a student who then improved. Ask the school in writing which tier applies and what would change it.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer for the specification code, in writing. It will look like 0620 or 0625 for Cambridge, or 4CH1 or 4PH1 for Pearson Edexcel. This matters more than parents expect, because the content overlap between boards is high while the paper structure, formula-sheet conventions and question phrasing differ. A student drilled on the wrong board's past papers has practised the right subject for the wrong exam, and that is an expensive error no number of extra hours repairs late in Year 11.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge offer a spring exam series our child could use?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate sits the June series and the November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests running in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Any guidance pointing an Abu Dhabi family at a spring Cambridge sitting is describing a different country's timetable, and acting on it would mean missing an entry deadline for the series the child can actually sit.

faqs.question: Who submits the exam entries and what happens if we want to add a subject?
faqs.answer: The school or examination centre submits final entries, months before any paper is sat, and nobody will chase a parent for a change. If a student wants an extra subject, a tier change or a private-candidate paper, that has to reach the examinations officer before entries close. Ask for the date entries lock and treat it as the real deadline. After it passes, adjustments are difficult and sometimes impossible, which is the most expensive avoidable mistake available to a sixth-form family in this emirate.

faqs.question: How long is the wait between sitting a paper and getting the result?
faqs.answer: Weeks rather than days, and the historical anchors are the useful guide. Pearson Edexcel's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and reached students the following day. November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Future windows are not dated here because provisional timetables get revised; work from the live official timetable through the school's examinations officer rather than any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor at the entry rate handle Higher Level Diploma content?
faqs.answer: Sometimes for part of it, and that partial coverage is the trap. Entry-band tutors generally manage Standard Level content and then run out somewhere inside the Higher Level syllabus, often mid-session and often in front of the student. For Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level Chemistry or Economics Paper 3, the market band is AED 200 to 450 and upwards because the pool of people who can teach it to the top of the range is genuinely small in this emirate, not because the rate is padded.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Cranleigh student need a UAE licence?
faqs.answer: An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system, with a stated two working day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Could we simply hire one of the school's own teachers for evening lessons?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi that is specifically restricted. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than taken from the policy text, so verify the current wording with ADEK directly. The practical position is that such an offer is a compliance problem for the teacher and should be declined rather than negotiated.

faqs.question: Will a tutor read and improve our child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor will read it and tell the student which criterion is costing marks, and will not improve it on their behalf. The distinction is the whole of academic honesty here. Allowed: reading the published descriptors together, narrowing the research question, teaching the method the essay needs, marking the student's own draft, rehearsing the supervisor meeting. Not allowed: contributing text, redrafting into a final version, or supplying data. One operation ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments, and the qualification it risks is the student's, not the seller's.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a sixth-form candidate on Saadiyat usually take?
faqs.answer: One ninety-minute session a week in each subject that is genuinely behind, which is usually one or two subjects rather than three or four. In the final year, a coursework block of eight to twelve sessions often runs alongside. Families who tutor four subjects at once typically have a scheduling problem rather than an academic one, and the honest advice is to fix the weakest subject properly before adding another. Spreading hours thinly across subjects dilutes exactly the work that moves a grade.

faqs.question: Which regulator inspects schools on Saadiyat Island, and where is the report?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi's private schools, including those on Saadiyat, are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Read inspection outcomes on ADEK's own site rather than on an aggregator, because aggregated ratings go stale and the band vocabulary differs between emirates. Dubai sits with KHDA, Sharjah with SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: Can a session be moved when the Yas event calendar wrecks our evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a practical advantage of video delivery rather than a marketing point. A video slot can shift by an hour or move to another evening without anyone having to redraw a driving route, which is exactly the flexibility a travelling tutor cannot offer at short notice. The same applies during Ramadan, when timings commonly move to after Iftar, and during family travel, when a student abroad for a fortnight keeps the slot rather than losing a month of momentum.

faqs.question: Is a group revision course better value than one-to-one for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: On price, clearly: local centre group rates sit around AED 85 to 160 per student an hour against AED 150 to 450 for one-to-one. On outcome it depends on the student. A group works through the syllabus on a fixed schedule regardless of whether a given student needed that topic this week, which suits someone broadly on track who wants structure and deadlines. It does not suit a candidate dropping the same marks every paper, because diagnosing that needs a tutor looking at their script and nobody else's.

intro.heading: Two tracks, two sets of requirements, one certificate process
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families on the American track meet a question British-curriculum families never do, and they usually meet it late. The question is what the Ministry of Education requires for certificate recognition, because the answer is completely different from the British-track answer and turns on standardised test scores rather than on subject grades. Nobody at a parents' evening in Grade 9 explains this, and by Grade 12 the window to act on some of it has narrowed.

The published American-track requirements are specific. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. Those are the figures as published, and the guidance they come from does not mention EmSAT as an alternative route for this purpose. Confirm the current position on moe.gov.ae before relying on any of it, because requirements are revised.

The British track works on a different logic entirely. It requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. So one track counts subjects and the other counts test scores, which is why advice written for one is misleading for the other.

No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in the sources available here, so none is published on this page. That gap is worth noting rather than filling: a figure circulating on tutoring pages is not a figure read from the Ministry, and an IB family should confirm theirs on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority. The same applies to any number quoted for a track this page does not cover.

Beyond equivalency, the American track differs from IGCSE in a way that matters for how a pupil is taught. It assesses continuously, through coursework, quizzes, projects and tests across a semester, with a grade point average accumulating over years. IGCSE assesses terminally, in one window, with nothing banked. A pupil moving between those systems is changing how they are measured rather than only what they study, and the behaviours that earned them a strong record in one are not the behaviours that earn one in the other.

So this page covers three things in turn: what each track actually assesses and what that means for preparation, the published equivalency thresholds for both, and what changes on each of the common transfers within Abu Dhabi. Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: What the American track assesses, and why that changes preparation
paragraphs: The American high school diploma is credit-based and continuously assessed. A semester grade is built from coursework, quizzes, projects, tests and participation, and those semester grades accumulate into a grade point average across four years. The structural consequence is that consistency matters more than peak performance: a poor semester lowers a cumulative figure permanently rather than being superseded by a stronger examination later.

IGCSE and A Level work the other way. Nothing accumulates. A pupil can have a difficult Year 10 and sit an excellent paper in Year 11, because the paper is the assessment. The IB Diploma sits between the two, with internal assessment components contributing alongside terminal examinations, which is why pupils used to coursework deadlines often adapt to it more comfortably than to a purely terminal system.

That difference changes what preparation means. Supporting a continuously assessed pupil is largely about never falling behind: understanding each unit as it is taught, submitting work on time, and treating every assessment as contributing rather than as practice. Supporting a terminally assessed pupil is largely about diagnosis and timed practice, because the only assessment that counts has not happened yet and the current gap can still be closed.

Families who move a child between systems frequently import the wrong habit. A pupil arriving on the American track from IGCSE may treat early-semester work as practice and find the grade point average already compromised. A pupil arriving at IGCSE from the American track may revise steadily all year and never sit a full timed paper, then discover in the examination that timing is itself assessed. Both are predictable and both are avoidable by naming the difference early.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency for the American track, stated exactly
paragraphs: This is the section an American-track family in the UAE most needs and is least likely to find. The Ministry of Education's published requirements for the American curriculum track turn on standardised test scores. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying.

Two things about that are worth noticing. The English requirement offers three alternative routes, which means a family can choose the test their child is most likely to clear rather than assuming one is compulsory. And the mathematics requirement is stated as needing to be in place before applying, which is a sequencing instruction rather than a general standard: it means the test has to have been sat and scored by the point of application, not during it.

The guidance these figures come from does not mention EmSAT as an alternative route for this purpose, and it states no International Baccalaureate points threshold. That second absence is why no IB figure appears on this page. A number circulating on tutoring pages is not a number read from the Ministry, and an IB family should confirm theirs on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority rather than acting on a page like this one.

Two cautions to state plainly. Requirements are revised, so every figure here should be checked against moe.gov.ae before it is relied on for an application. And IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency or attestation; the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate authority, and the right action is to use the official channel. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, admission or progression, and any page implying otherwise has made a false claim about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: The SAT thresholds, and when to sit the tests
paragraphs: A threshold expressed as a number invites a specific question: how far is my child from it, and how long would closing the gap take? For the SAT that is answerable quickly, because full-length practice tests exist and the test is designed to be practised. A pupil who sits one under timing has a score within a few points of what they would get on the day, which is more than can be said for most school assessments.

What SAT preparation consists of is mostly not new content. The mathematics section tests material a pupil on the American track has already met; what it tests additionally is pacing, question-type recognition and arithmetic fluency under pressure. The reading and writing section tests careful reading under timing. In both cases the gap between a pupil's capability and their score is usually procedural, which is why preparation produces visible movement relatively quickly.

Timing the sittings is the part families get wrong. A single attempt scheduled close to an application deadline leaves no room for a disappointing result, and a disappointing result happens for ordinary reasons - illness, nerves, a bad morning. The sensible plan allows for two sittings with a gap between them, which means working backwards from the application and placing the first attempt early enough that a second is possible.

The English requirement deserves its own decision rather than a default. A pupil who reads quickly under timing may find the SAT reading and writing route easiest. A pupil whose spoken and listening English is strong but whose timed reading is slower may do better on IELTS or TOEFL, which assess differently. Trying one practice version of each is a couple of hours well spent and it frequently redirects a preparation plan entirely.

sections.heading: AP courses, and the part of the track that behaves like an exam
paragraphs: Advanced Placement courses are the element of the American track that most resembles a British or IB external examination. Each one ends in an externally marked paper scored on a scale from 1 to 5, administered by the College Board rather than the school. Nothing about a pupil's grade point average changes the AP score, and nothing about the AP score changes the grade point average. They are separate instruments.

That separateness is useful and it is also where pupils are caught out. A pupil who has maintained a strong semester record through consistent coursework arrives at an AP examination and finds that consistency is not what is being tested. What is being tested is performance in one window, under timing, on content from a whole course - which is the terminal-examination skill their track has not otherwise required them to develop.

Preparation for an AP paper therefore looks like preparation for an IGCSE or A Level paper rather than like preparation for a semester. Past papers from the official source, sat under timing, marked against the published standard, with the lost marks categorised into content, method, precision and timing. The habit is diagnosis and practice rather than steady completion, and a pupil meeting it for the first time in Grade 11 needs it named for them.

For a pupil heading to a competitive university, AP results are also the clearest externally verifiable evidence the American track produces. A grade point average is a school's own judgement, honestly made and not directly comparable between schools. An AP score is an external mark on a known scale. That asymmetry is worth understanding when deciding where preparation effort should go in Grades 11 and 12.

sections.heading: Grade point average, transcripts and the cost of a bad semester
paragraphs: A grade point average is cumulative, which is the single most important thing about it and the thing families from terminal systems underestimate. Every semester grade enters a running figure that follows a pupil to the end of Grade 12. A difficult Grade 9, caused by a move between countries or a settling-in year, is not erased by a strong Grade 11; it is averaged with it.

The practical consequence is that support in the American track is most valuable early, which is the opposite of the pattern in a terminal system. A pupil struggling in Grade 9 should be helped in Grade 9, because that semester's grade is permanent. A pupil struggling in Year 10 of an IGCSE course has a whole further year before anything is assessed externally. Importing the second assumption into the first system is expensive.

There is a related point about what to work on. In a continuously assessed system, the highest-value intervention is frequently organisational rather than academic: understanding each unit as it is taught, submitting work on time, and treating every quiz as contributing. A pupil losing marks to late submissions and missed assignments is not short of understanding, and no amount of subject teaching fixes it.

Transcripts carry more than grades, too. They record courses taken, which matters because a pupil who has not taken the mathematics or science sequence a university expects cannot retrofit it in Grade 12. Checking what the intended destination requires - whether a UAE university, an American one, or a British one reading an American transcript - in Grade 9 or 10 rather than Grade 12 is the single most useful piece of planning available on this track.

sections.heading: Moving between the American track and IGCSE or the Diploma
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families move between systems more than most, because the emirate has mature American, British and IB provision within a few kilometres of each other. A transfer is usually described as a change of school, and it is also a change of how a pupil is measured, which is the part nobody briefs them on. The academic content overlaps substantially; the assessment logic does not.

Moving from the American track into IGCSE, a pupil meets three new things. Tiering, where a Cambridge entry at Core tier caps the grade scale regardless of performance. Terminal assessment, where nothing done before the series counts. And specification codes, where practice has to match the exact paper being sat. None of those exists in the system they came from, and all three need explaining in the first fortnight rather than the first report.

Moving the other way, a pupil meets a cumulative grade and continuous deadlines. The habit that served them at IGCSE - working steadily and performing in one window - is not what is rewarded, and the transition shows as a weak first semester produced by a capable pupil. Naming it in advance is most of the remedy, because the behaviours required are simple once they are understood.

Moving into the IB Diploma from either is a third case. Breadth becomes compulsory, so a subject a pupil hoped to leave behind may need carrying. Writing becomes load-bearing in every subject because internal assessments are written in all six. And one mathematics decision - Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level - gates specific degree routes, so it should follow the intended destination rather than perceived difficulty.

sections.heading: What an American-track pupil actually needs from a tutor
paragraphs: Three different things, and conflating them wastes money. The first is subject support inside a continuously assessed course, which is mostly about keeping pace with units as they are taught and never arriving at an assessment unprepared. That is ordinary teaching, and it works best as a short regular arrangement during the semester rather than as a block before a test.

The second is standardised test preparation, which is not subject teaching at all. The SAT tests pacing, question-type recognition and application of content already met. Preparation is full-length timed practice with every wrong answer explained back, and the gap is usually procedural rather than knowledge-based. A tutor who approaches SAT mathematics as a syllabus to teach has misunderstood the instrument.

The third is terminal-examination technique, needed for AP courses and for any transfer into IGCSE or the Diploma. This is diagnosis and timed practice: a past paper under timing, marked against the published standard, with lost marks sorted by category and the largest category targeted. It is a different habit from both of the other two and it has to be taught explicitly to a pupil who has never needed it.

The honesty line applies throughout and is worth stating because the American track is coursework-heavy. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted coursework, project or essay. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the student rather than on the provider taking the fee.
bullets: Semester subject support: short, regular, paced to the units being taught
SAT preparation: timed practice and pacing, not syllabus teaching
Terminal technique: diagnosis and marked timed papers, taught explicitly
No submitted coursework written, co-written or edited to completion, at any price

sections.heading: The UAE mandatory subjects still apply
paragraphs: An American-curriculum school in the UAE delivers the same federally required subjects as every other private school. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies sit alongside the American diploma exactly as they sit alongside a British or IB programme.

The detail is set by the emirate regulator, which for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain is the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai gives the clearest public illustration of how specific these requirements are: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited, and prescribed languages of instruction by group.

Two points connect this to the rest of the page. KHDA's guidance states that for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so any support in these subjects must reinforce the school's prescribed material rather than run a parallel course. And time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with at least 25 minutes advised per lesson, which tells a parent that these subjects are not short of taught time.

The equivalency connection is specific to the British track rather than the American one, and it is worth knowing in case a family transfers. On the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the Ministry requires. A family moving a child from the American track to IGCSE should count their prospective subject list with those two struck out.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and the first session
paragraphs: American-track subject support, SAT preparation, AP courses, and Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE across mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects are all covered in this set, and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist: specific AP subjects with smaller cohorts, Arabic as a first language, and mid-transfer reconciliation between two particular systems. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free.

Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies. The brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days. The brief is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than concealed behind a local-looking telephone number - and two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying so. Or the brief is not currently covered, in which case it is named.

Parents are entitled to check the one credential that exists. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. ADEK's reported professional-ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful things to bring are your child's current transcript or semester report, any practice test score they have, and the destination they are aiming at. With those the session can produce a written timeline against the published thresholds, which is the single most useful document an American-track family in the UAE can hold. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoE, Cambridge, Pearson, College Board or IB approval or partnership and claims none.

process.title: Look up the thresholds that apply to your track
process.description: For the American track the published requirements are SAT Mathematics at least 450 before applying, and English proficiency via IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. Check the current position on moe.gov.ae, because requirements are revised and this page is not the authority on them.

process.title: Sit one diagnostic practice test early
process.description: A full-length timed practice test gives a score within a few points of a real one, which no school assessment does. That tells you whether a gap exists at all before any preparation is bought, and it also lets you compare the three English routes by trying one practice version of each.

process.title: Plan two sittings, not one
process.description: Work backwards from the application deadline and place the first attempt early enough that a second is possible. A disappointing score happens for ordinary reasons, and a single attempt scheduled close to a deadline leaves nowhere for it to go. The mathematics requirement specifies being scored before applying.

process.title: Name which of three jobs you are buying
process.description: Semester subject support paced to the units being taught, standardised test preparation that is pacing rather than syllabus teaching, or terminal-examination technique for AP and any transfer. They are different jobs needing different work, and conflating them is the commonest waste on this track.

process.title: Check the transcript, not just the grades
process.description: A transcript records courses taken as well as grades, and a pupil who has not taken the mathematics or science sequence a destination expects cannot retrofit it in Grade 12. Check what the intended universities require in Grade 9 or 10. On a cumulative system, early checking is worth considerably more than late effort.

whyPoints.title: Both tracks' thresholds quoted from the source
whyPoints.description: The American requirements - SAT Mathematics 450 before applying, English via IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450 - and the British ones, five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 plus one A Level at E or two AS at E. Four of the ten researched competitor clusters mention equivalency not at all.

whyPoints.title: No IB figure invented
whyPoints.description: No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in the sources available here, so none is published. A number circulating on tutoring pages is not a number read from the Ministry, and an IB family should confirm theirs on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority.

whyPoints.title: Assessment logic, not just content
whyPoints.description: A cumulative grade point average and a terminal paper reward different behaviours, and a pupil moving between them imports the wrong habit unless somebody names the difference. That naming is the most valuable thing a transferring family can be given in the first fortnight.

whyPoints.title: Three distinct jobs kept distinct
whyPoints.description: Semester support, standardised test preparation and terminal-examination technique need different work. A tutor approaching SAT mathematics as a syllabus to teach has misunderstood the instrument, and a family paying for that is paying for content a pupil has already met.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are an India-only service. Where a brief such as a smaller-cohort AP subject has no specialist free, it is named rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: No role claimed in a regulatory process
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency or attestation, which belong to the Ministry and the emirate authority. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, admission or progression, and no regulator, exam board or the College Board has approved or partnered with IB Gram.

faqs.question: What does the UAE require from a GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi pupil for certificate recognition?
faqs.answer: On the American track the published requirements are standardised test scores rather than subject grades. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. Those are the figures as published, and the guidance does not mention EmSAT as an alternative for this purpose. Check the current position on moe.gov.ae, because requirements are revised and no tutoring page is the authority.

faqs.question: Which English test should we choose out of the three accepted routes?
faqs.answer: Whichever your child is most likely to clear, and the way to find out is to try one practice version of each. A pupil who reads quickly under timing often finds the SAT reading and writing route easiest, since 450 in that section is accepted. A pupil whose spoken and listening English is strong but whose timed reading is slower may do better on IELTS at 5 or TOEFL iBT at 61, which assess differently. Two hours spent comparing them frequently redirects a whole preparation plan, and it costs nothing but the time.

faqs.question: Why does the mathematics requirement say 'before applying'?
faqs.answer: Because it is a sequencing instruction as well as a standard. The published requirement is at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying, which means the test has to have been sat and scored by the point of application rather than during the process. Practically that pushes the whole timeline earlier than families expect: a diagnostic practice test, a preparation block, a first sitting early enough that a second is possible, and the score in hand before the file goes anywhere. Confirm the current wording on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: How are the British-track requirements different?
faqs.answer: They count subjects instead of test scores. The published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. That is why advice written for one track misleads on the other, and why a family transferring between systems should read the rules for the one they are joining.

faqs.question: Our other child is on the Diploma. What points total does the Ministry want?
faqs.answer: Not in the sources available here, which is why no figure appears on this page. The guidance that supplies the American and British thresholds states no International Baccalaureate points requirement, so publishing one would mean inventing it. Numbers do circulate on tutoring pages, and a number on a tutoring page is not a number read from the Ministry. An IB family should confirm theirs on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly, and should treat any other source as unverified until they have.

faqs.question: Why does a weak Grade 9 matter so much on the American track?
faqs.answer: Because the grade point average is cumulative. Every semester grade enters a running figure that follows a pupil to the end of Grade 12, so a difficult Grade 9 - caused by a relocation or a settling-in year - is averaged with a strong Grade 11 rather than superseded by it. That inverts the pattern families from terminal systems expect, where a poor Year 10 is recoverable because the paper has not happened yet. On this track, support is most valuable early and least valuable late.

faqs.question: What should we actually work on if assignments are being handed in late?
faqs.answer: Organisation, not subject content, and this is the commonest misdiagnosis on a continuously assessed track. A pupil losing marks to late submissions and missed quizzes is usually not short of understanding, and no amount of subject teaching fixes it. The useful work is unit-by-unit pacing, treating every assessment as contributing rather than as practice, and a simple submission routine. That is cheaper than tutoring and it affects a permanent cumulative figure, which makes it the better purchase.

faqs.question: How is an AP examination different from the rest of the American track?
faqs.answer: It is terminal and externally marked, scored on a scale from 1 to 5 by the College Board rather than by the school. Nothing about a grade point average changes an AP score and nothing about an AP score changes the average; they are separate instruments. The consequence is that a pupil who has succeeded through consistent coursework arrives at an AP paper needing a skill their track has not otherwise required - performance in one window, under timing, on a whole course's content.

faqs.question: Should SAT preparation be taught as a syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who approaches it that way has misunderstood the instrument. The mathematics section tests material a pupil on the American track has already met; what it additionally tests is pacing, question-type recognition and arithmetic fluency under pressure. The reading and writing section tests careful reading under timing. The gap between capability and score is therefore usually procedural, which is why full-length timed practice with every wrong answer explained back produces visible movement relatively quickly.

faqs.question: What changes if our child transfers from the American track to IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Three things that do not exist in the system they are leaving. Tiering, where a Cambridge entry at Core tier caps the grade scale regardless of performance on the day. Terminal assessment, where nothing done before the series counts towards the grade. And specification codes, where practice has to match the exact paper being sat, since Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations. All three need explaining in the first fortnight rather than appearing on the first report, and the tier question should be settled first.

faqs.question: What changes moving the other way, into an American school?
faqs.answer: The reward structure. A pupil who has worked steadily and expected to peak in one window meets a cumulative grade point average and rolling deadlines, and the habit that served them produces a weak first semester despite real capability. Naming it in advance is most of the remedy, because the behaviours required are simple once understood: understand each unit as it is taught, submit on time, treat every quiz as contributing. Expect roughly a semester of adjustment, less if the difference is explained early.

faqs.question: Do the UAE mandatory subjects apply at an American-curriculum school?
faqs.answer: Yes, identically. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, so those subjects sit alongside the American diploma as they do alongside a British or IB programme. Detail is set by the emirate regulator, which for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain is ADEK. Any support in these subjects must reinforce prescribed content, since different or additional content requires prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with American-track coursework or a capstone project?
faqs.answer: With the thinking, the method and the feedback, yes. With the writing, no. A tutor may teach the skills, model the technique on a different example, and read a draft and say which section fails to meet the rubric. A tutor may not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece to completion, and no price makes that acceptable, particularly on a track where coursework feeds a permanent cumulative grade. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the student.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Khalifa City, Al Raha or Yas Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For a Grade 11 pupil juggling AP courses and standardised test preparation, the practical gain is the travel time: two or three sessions a week is achievable without a journey and would not be with one, and a full-length timed practice sitting needs an undisturbed morning rather than a visitor.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-americ.closingHeading: Check the thresholds, then sit one practice test
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-americ.closingBody: Look up the current Ministry requirements for your child's track on moe.gov.ae: on the American track that means SAT Mathematics at least 450 before applying, and English via IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. Then have your child sit one full-length timed practice test, which gives a score within a few points of a real one and tells you whether a gap exists at all. Plan two sittings rather than one. A free trial lesson is one session with no card details required, and the useful things to bring are a transcript and any practice score. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-.tutorsIntro: These tutors are matched to a component rather than a subject: a named paper, a criterion, an oral or an internal assessment. That matters at a continuum school, where the same subject is assessed one way in the Middle Years Programme and an entirely different way in the Diploma.

intro.heading: Marks are awarded by a scheme, and the scheme is knowable
paragraphs: Most tutoring is sold as more practice. More practice helps a student who does not know the content. It does very little for the much commoner case, which is a student who knows the content and loses marks on the shape of the answer. Those losses are systematic, they are described in the published assessment criteria and examiner commentary, and they are fixable in a handful of sessions once somebody has read the student's actual script against the actual scheme.

At a school teaching the full International Baccalaureate continuum, that reading has to happen twice over, because the two programmes assess in incompatible ways. The Middle Years Programme marks against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with no past paper to drill and no mark total to accumulate. The Diploma marks against papers with published weightings, plus an internal assessment in every subject. A student who was excellent at the first can be mediocre at the second for purely structural reasons, and the transition between them is the most under-taught moment in the whole continuum.

The IGCSE in this page's title matters for the families who need it. A household may have a sibling at a British-curriculum school in Khalifa City working towards Cambridge 0580 Mathematics or 0620 Chemistry, or a child who arrived mid-course from a British-curriculum school abroad and is deciding whether to finish the qualification as a private candidate. IGCSE is a linear, terminally assessed course with published component weightings, which makes it the easiest of the three to analyse mechanically and the most responsive to technique work.

What this page therefore does, section by section, is set out the mechanics: the paper weightings, the criterion letters and what each credits, the command terms that cost the most marks and what each demands, the word and page limits that silently cap a grade, and the series calendar counted backwards. None of this is in the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026: not one of them named a single internal assessment criterion by letter, and five of six carried no table at all.

Two things before the mechanics. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India. And every mark scheme, past paper and subject guide referenced here belongs to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson, and is referenced and linked rather than reproduced, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. A provider offering downloadable mark schemes is taking a risk on the family's behalf rather than providing a service.
bullets: MYP marks four criteria per subject, each one to eight, with no mark total
The Diploma marks published paper weightings plus internal assessment in every subject
IGCSE is linear, terminally assessed and the most responsive to technique work
Command terms, not content gaps, cause most avoidable losses at every level
Mark schemes and past papers are linked from the board, never reproduced here

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-.programmesIntro: At a continuum school the same child meets three different assessment logics in sequence. These blocks describe what each one actually measures, which is the only basis on which a tutoring plan makes sense.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against unit outcomes and learner-profile attributes, with no external examination and no numerical total. The absence of a mark makes specific weakness hard to see from a report, and the gaps that matter later are narrow: number fluency, reading stamina and the ability to produce a structured paragraph unaided. Those three carry the entire Middle Years Programme, which begins assessing them formally within weeks.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi these years also carry the mandatory UAE subjects, which run in private schools alongside the licensed curriculum under the federal requirement overseen by the Ministry of Education. Arabic is usually the one subject on a Primary Years report with a conventional grade attached, and in expatriate households it is frequently the only line a parent cannot act on without help.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with the total converted to a one-to-seven grade using published boundaries. There is no past paper and no cumulative mark, so the only way to improve is to read the criterion wording against the student's own work until they can predict their own score. The final-year Personal Project is assessed on process rather than product, which students consistently underestimate.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years Programme is where Abu Dhabi families most often weigh a board change, because a move to a British-curriculum school at Year 10 means joining a linear two-year IGCSE course partway through. Students leaving for Khalifa City or the island typically need bridging in mathematical notation and in science practical write-ups, both of which IGCSE expects in a format the Middle Years Programme never taught.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service. Each subject has published component weightings and an internal assessment carrying a fixed share of the grade. The structural difficulty is convergence: five internal assessment deadlines and a four-thousand-word essay land inside one stretch of the second year. UAE candidates sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: For an Abu Dhabi Diploma student the two pressure points are that convergence and the mandatory Arabic requirement sitting alongside six Diploma subjects. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site, and every date should come from the school's Diploma coordinator rather than from any published summary.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year linear course with terminal examinations and syllabus codes that determine the paper set: Cambridge 0580 and 0980 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology; Pearson 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, which caps the available grade before anyone sits a paper. Component weightings are published per specification and are the basis for any sensible revision plan.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE set is also a regulatory document for a UAE resident. Ministry of Education equivalency for British-curriculum students counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five. One page ranking in this market states the figure as six; it is five, and that difference is a whole subject on a Year 9 timetable.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by its assessment rather than its content: what the components are, what they credit, and where the marks actually leave. That is the level of detail a session plan has to work at.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Papers split by calculator access, and the paper without one concentrates the losses. The dominant avoidable error is a correct method never written down, because the scheme awards method lines and the student recorded only a final answer. Higher Level adds proof and complex numbers, where a missing justification line costs more than a numerical slip.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led with the graphic display calculator assumed. Marks go on reporting an output without naming the command that produced it, and on treating a regression line as an answer rather than a model with stated limits. The internal assessment credits data the student collected and can defend under questioning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms separate Higher Level grades. At IGCSE the recurring loss is units omitted from a mole calculation and a practical description nobody could follow. Data questions reward reading the axis labels before the stem, which under time pressure is the first habit to disappear and the easiest to rebuild.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Definitions carry marks that calculation cannot recover: a stated definition before an explanation routinely earns the first of three marks. Electromagnetic induction and circuit analysis produce the heaviest losses at both levels. Drawing the circuit before writing is a technique fix rather than a content fix, and it works within two sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Revised as recall, assessed on command terms. Outline, explain, compare, evaluate and suggest each demand a different structure, and a well-memorised paragraph earns two of five when the verb wanted a mechanism. Internal assessment statistics is the single most consistent weak point across both programmes.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The unseen guided analysis is decided in the reading, and students who annotate deliberately for five minutes outscore those who begin writing immediately. The Individual Oral fails on a global issue too broad to evidence in ten minutes. In the Middle Years Programme the equivalent loss is ignoring the criterion wording while writing good prose.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns credit prose cannot recover, and candidates drawing from memory rather than from the question shift the wrong curve. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and is the clearest single separator between a five and a seven in this subject at any school.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Extended opens A* to E; Core stops at C, a ceiling set at entry rather than in the exam hall. Extended losses cluster in bearings, upper and lower bounds, similar-shape ratios, and premature rounding of a value that should have stayed exact. Pearson 4MA1 covers similar ground on a different paper split.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Four criteria covering knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Students lose most heavily on the investigating criterion, because a research question set too wide cannot be evidenced within the task, and on communicating, where referencing conventions are marked explicitly and are usually treated as a formality.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed guidance and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the streams. The non-Arab stream has its own syllabus and its own realistic ceiling.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-.regionsIntro: The communities families travel from, with the detail that changes when a session can start rather than what it costs. Abu Dhabi's geography affects scheduling far more than pricing.

regions.name: Al Maryah and Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense residential towers with a large school-age population and no single dominant school, so students commute outward in several directions. The exit onto the main crossing in the late afternoon is the slowest stretch of the day, which pushes a realistic weekday start to five o'clock or later.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established western island neighbourhoods with a high proportion of long-term resident families. Multi-year weekly arrangements are more common here than crash blocks, which suits criterion work in the Middle Years Programme, where improvement is cumulative rather than event-driven.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The mainland villa corridor, with a dense cluster of secondary-age students and households frequently running two boards at once. School-bus timings rather than parent diaries set the earliest session here, and the afternoon traffic onto the main road makes a later slot more durable.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short crossing from the island, with several newer international schools. Families appear here when a sibling attends one of them, and two different assessment calendars in one household is the usual reason a family needs both criterion-based and paper-based support simultaneously.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Residential clusters with a growing secondary population and a commute that is short in distance but unpredictable around the event calendar. Households here value a schedule that survives disruption more than one that is convenient in an ordinary week.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland residential area with longer average commutes and a mixed school profile. Two children at two schools on two timetables is the norm rather than the exception, which makes an evening driving route impractical and a fixed video slot per child straightforward.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah

The aim is narrow: the student should be able to read a criterion descriptor and predict their own score within a point. Once they can do that, they can self-correct a draft without a tutor present, which is the only version of this that lasts.

sections.heading: What a paper weighting is, and why effort should follow it
paragraphs: A Diploma subject grade is built from components with published weightings, and students almost never revise in proportion to them. The commonest pattern is a candidate who spends most of their revision on the component they find most comfortable, which is frequently the one worth least. Reallocating that effort is free, requires no extra hours and is often worth more than the tutoring itself, which is why this is the first thing a session plan should establish.

The internal assessment is the clearest example. It carries a fixed share of the final grade in every Diploma subject, it is completed under conditions the student controls, and it is marked against criteria published in advance. In mark-per-hour terms it is the single most efficient part of the course, and it is also the part most often left until the deadline forces it. A student who treats the internal assessment as the first priority rather than the last is using the structure of the qualification rather than fighting it.

The table below sets out how to work out the allocation for any subject, because the specific weightings differ by subject and by level and should be read from the current subject guide rather than from a page like this one. The method is what transfers: list the components, find the weighting for the student's level, divide the available revision hours in that proportion, and then check what the student actually did last month against it. The gap is usually startling.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses, not different difficulties
paragraphs: Families routinely describe Higher Level as the harder version of a Standard Level subject. Structurally it is more than that: it usually adds content, adds an assessed component, changes the weighting of the components that are shared, and raises what the same command term expects of an answer. A student moving between levels is therefore changing the assessment, not just the volume, and a tutoring plan that treats it as volume will miss the part that costs marks.

The practical differences show up in three places. The additional Higher Level content is the visible one and the easiest to teach. The extra component is the one students underprepare, because it appears late in the course and has no Standard Level equivalent to compare against. And the raised expectation on shared components is the invisible one: the same question stem at Higher Level wants more justification, more precision in terminology, and a willingness to qualify a claim rather than assert it.

The table compares the two on the dimensions that decide a tutoring plan, and the last row is the one worth acting on. The decision about level is usually made a year or more before it is tested, often on the basis of a single report, and it is far more reversible early than late. A family uncertain about a level should ask the subject teacher what the student would need to demonstrate to be secure at Higher Level, which is a concrete and answerable question.

sections.heading: Criterion letters: what each one is actually paying for
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme marks four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, and this is where the competitor corpus is emptiest: across every page measured for this project, not one named a single criterion by letter or explained what it awards. For a parent that absence is the whole problem, because a report showing a five on criterion C is unreadable without knowing what criterion C is for.

The criteria are labelled A to D in each subject, and the labels mean different things in different subjects while following a consistent logic. Criterion A is typically knowledge and understanding. The middle criteria usually cover the process of investigating or applying, and the final criterion typically covers reflection, evaluation or critical thinking. A student scoring well on A and poorly on D is not a weak student; they are a student who has not been taught to evaluate, which is a teachable skill with a known method.

The useful work in a session is narrow and repeatable. Read the descriptor for the criterion that scored lowest, in its exact published wording. Read the student's own submitted work beside it. Ask the student to award themselves a band and justify it against the words in the descriptor. Then rewrite one paragraph to move it up one band. A student who can do that unaided has acquired the skill that the whole programme is built on, and will keep it into the Diploma, where the same habit applied to an internal assessment is worth considerably more.

sections.heading: Command terms are the single largest source of avoidable loss
paragraphs: Across every level in this page, the most consistent source of lost marks is answering the wrong verb. A student who writes a precise, accurate description when the question said explain has produced good work that scores badly. This is not carelessness and it is not a knowledge gap; it is an untaught convention, and it is the cheapest thing to fix in the whole of exam preparation.

The reason it persists is that command terms are taught once, early, as a list to memorise, and then never practised as a discipline. The discipline is simple: circle the verb before reading the rest of the question, decide the answer shape it demands, and write to that shape. Students who adopt it typically recover marks within two or three sessions, across every subject at once, which makes it the highest-leverage single habit available.

The table maps the common command terms to the answer shape each one requires. The specific terms and definitions should be read from the current subject guide, because they are defined formally by the board and the definitions matter. What transfers is the mapping itself: each verb corresponds to a structure, and a student who can name the structure before writing has solved most of the problem before the first sentence. The habit also survives the transition between programmes, which is rare: a student who installs it in the Middle Years Programme carries it into Diploma papers and into any IGCSE they sit.

sections.heading: Word limits, page limits and the grade they quietly cap
paragraphs: Assessed coursework across both programmes carries limits, and exceeding them has consequences that students treat as administrative and examiners treat as assessable. The Extended Essay limit of four thousand words is the one everybody knows. The limits on internal assessments, reflections, project reports and process journals are the ones that catch people out, because they differ by subject and are easy to find only if you know to look.

The failure mode is predictable. A student writes to the word limit as though it were a target, fills it with description, and then has no room for the evaluation that carries the highest band. The result is a long piece scoring in the middle. The correct approach is to budget the limit by criterion before writing: decide how many words the evaluation needs, protect them, and compress the description into what remains.

The table sets out the structure of that budgeting exercise. The exact limits must come from the current subject guide and the school's own instructions, because they change and they differ by subject, and no page should be the source of a figure a student writes to. What this page can give is the method, which nobody else publishes: treat the limit as an allocation across criteria, not as a finishing line. Done properly, the allocation is written down before the first draft and checked against the actual word count at every stage, which turns an invisible cap into a planning constraint the student controls.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Pearson calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: For the IGCSE side of a household, the calendar is both knowable and routinely misreported. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March main series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sits June and November and nothing else. Any guidance pointing an Abu Dhabi family at a spring Cambridge sitting is describing another country's timetable.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone is essential, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after reading the wrong one. That is a real operational risk and it is resolved by one question to the school's examinations officer. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of a series, which means dates can be revised.

The dates worth stating are the ones already past, because those are checkable. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026. Future windows are named here by month only, deliberately, since a pinned future date makes a page wrong a year later with nobody having edited it.
