sections.heading: What one session can realistically repair, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Honesty about the unit of work matters, because families buy sessions and improvement does not arrive one session at a time in equal portions. Some things genuinely change in sixty minutes: a command-term habit, a definition set learned verbatim, a circuit-drawing routine, a unit-writing discipline, the narrowing of a research question. These are conventions rather than knowledge, and once installed they transfer across every paper the student sits.

Other things do not change in a session and should not be sold as though they might. Algebraic fluency is built over weeks of short daily practice, not in an hour. A missing conceptual foundation in energetics or in mechanics needs rebuilding in sequence. Reading stamina and essay structure improve over a term. A tutor who promises any of those in a few sessions is describing a sale rather than a plan.

The honest version of a first session is therefore diagnostic: read the marked work, identify which losses are convention and which are foundation, fix one convention immediately so the student leaves with something that works, and set out an accurate timescale for the rest. That is what the free trial lesson is for, and it is also why a tutor who cannot name a specific recurring loss from a script is not worth the mid band regardless of what they charge. The separation also lets a family decide how long to commit: a convention block is four sessions, a foundation rebuild is a term, and knowing which one you are buying is the difference between a plan and an open-ended arrangement.
bullets: Changeable in one session: command terms, definitions, units, method lines, a research question

sections.heading: Academic honesty across the Personal Project and the internal assessment
paragraphs: Both programmes produce work that must be the student's own, and both have formal consequences for a breach that fall on the student rather than on anyone selling assistance. The Personal Project in the Middle Years Programme and the internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay in the Diploma are all in this category, and so is a school-assessed task that contributes to a reported grade.

What a tutor may do is substantial and is the actual service. Read the published criteria alongside the student and explain what each descriptor awards. Press on a research question until it is answerable within the limit. Teach the statistical test, the laboratory technique, the referencing convention or the model required. Read a draft the student wrote and name the criterion costing marks. Rehearse the supervisor conversation. Keep the process journal honest by asking about it every week.

What a tutor may not do is contribute to the submission: not text, not a redraft into final form, not data presented as collected, not an edit that leaves the work substantially someone else's. One operation ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price, and the thing that purchase puts at risk is the student's qualification while risking nothing for the seller. The self-test is whether the student could explain every sentence of their own submission, unprompted, to the person supervising it. If they could not, the line has been crossed whoever crossed it, and the only honest repair is to go back to the last point where the work was genuinely theirs and continue from there.
bullets: Explaining descriptors, narrowing a question, teaching a method: allowed

process.title: Send a piece of marked work, not a description of the problem
process.description: A parent's account of what is going wrong is usually accurate about the symptom and wrong about the cause. One marked script or one returned criterion task tells a specialist more in five minutes than a long conversation does, because the losses are visible and countable rather than inferred.

process.title: Name the component and the level
process.description: At a continuum school the same subject is assessed one way in the Middle Years Programme and another in the Diploma, and a request naming only the subject reaches the wrong specialist. Say the programme, the level and the component: Higher Level Paper 2, criterion D, the internal assessment, the Individual Oral.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson as a diagnosis
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, no payment and no card. Ask them to name the recurring loss from the marked work and to say which of it is convention and which is foundation. A tutor who can separate those two is worth paying; one who offers general revision is not.

process.title: Agree the weighting allocation before the schedule
process.description: Before deciding how many sessions, decide which components they are for, using the published weightings from the current subject guide. Most revision plans over-serve the lowest-weighted component, and correcting that costs nothing and often matters more than the sessions themselves.

process.title: Get written feedback that names the target
process.description: After each session you receive what was covered, what was set and what loss is being targeted next. That record makes a term-long arrangement reviewable against something specific, and it is the same document a student can take into a supervisor or subject-teacher meeting.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and components named explicitly
whyPoints.description: This page sets out criterion positions, command-term structures and how to allocate revision by weighting. Across the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026, not one named a single internal assessment criterion by letter, and five of six carried no table at all. The mechanics are knowable and publishing them is the whole differentiator.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a component, not a subject label
whyPoints.description: A tutor allocated to Higher Level Paper 3, to criterion D in one subject, or to Cambridge 0620 Paper 6 knows what that component credits. At a school running the full continuum, the same subject name covers two incompatible assessment systems, and matching on the label alone reaches the wrong person.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a session can change
whyPoints.description: Conventions change in an hour. Fluency changes in weeks. Conceptual foundations change in a term. This page says so explicitly, including the things no tutoring arrangement can supply, which is the student's own practice between sessions. No grade, score or improvement is promised anywhere on this page.

whyPoints.title: Official material referenced, never reproduced
whyPoints.description: Mark schemes, past papers, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. They are referenced and linked here rather than copied, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure for everyone involved.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated plainly, before payment
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated on this page, on the UAE hub and on every country page, so nobody discovers it afterwards.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and names no school here as a client or partner. No satisfaction percentage or star rating appears, because none can be evidenced with a sample size, a date and a method.

faqs.question: What does a criterion letter on a Middle Years Programme report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each scored one to eight, with the total converted to a one-to-seven grade using published boundaries. Criterion A is typically knowledge and understanding; the middle criteria usually cover investigating and communicating or applying; the final criterion usually covers evaluation and critical thinking. A student strong on A and weak on D has not been taught to evaluate, which is a teachable skill rather than an ability ceiling. Read the exact descriptors in the subject guide.

faqs.question: Why does my child write good work in the Middle Years Programme and still score five?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the work answers the task rather than the descriptor. The criteria are marked on specific wording, and a well-written piece that never addresses what criterion C or D asks for will sit in the middle bands no matter how good the prose is. The fix is narrow and repeatable: read the descriptor in its exact wording, have the student award themselves a band and justify it, then rewrite one paragraph to move up a band.

faqs.question: How should revision hours be split between the papers in an IB subject?
faqs.answer: In proportion to the published component weightings for the student's level, which should be read from the current subject guide via the school. The usual finding when a family does this honestly is that the lowest-weighted component has been absorbing the most revision time, because it is the most comfortable one. Reallocating costs nothing, adds no hours, and frequently matters more than the tutoring itself. The internal assessment is normally the most efficient marks in the course and the most often postponed.

faqs.question: Structurally, what actually changes when a subject moves from SL to HL?
faqs.answer: No. It usually adds content, adds an assessed component, weights the shared components differently, and raises what the same command term expects. The additional content is the easiest part to teach. The extra component is the most underprepared, because it arrives late with no Standard Level equivalent to compare against. And the raised expectation on shared components is invisible without marked work: the same stem wants more justification, tighter terminology and a qualified claim rather than an asserted one.

faqs.question: Which command term costs the most marks in practice?
faqs.answer: Evaluate, followed by compare. A student who answers evaluate with a list of advantages and disadvantages loses the entire top band, because judgement supported by weighed evidence is what the term requires. Compare answered as two separate descriptions in sequence typically loses half the available marks, since the credit is in the point-by-point linking. Both are conventions rather than knowledge gaps, and both are usually fixed within two or three sessions across every subject at once.

faqs.question: What is the fastest change a tutor can make for a GEMS World Academy student?
faqs.answer: Installing a command-term discipline, which means circling the verb before reading the rest of the question and naming the required answer shape before writing. That single habit recovers marks in every written subject simultaneously and usually takes two or three sessions to stick. Close behind it are learning a definition set verbatim in physics, writing units on every line in chemistry, and narrowing a research question that is currently too wide to evidence.

faqs.question: Why do word limits matter if the examiner is reading for quality?
faqs.answer: Because the limit is an allocation and students treat it as a finishing line. The usual failure is that description expands to fill the space and the evaluation, which carries the highest band, gets whatever is left over. The result is a long piece scoring in the middle. Budget the limit by criterion before writing: decide how many words the evaluation needs, protect them, and compress the description into the remainder. Read the exact limits from the current subject guide.

faqs.question: How does the Personal Project differ from the work my child is used to?
faqs.answer: It is assessed on process rather than product, which students consistently misread. The process journal is the evidence, and a journal written retrospectively in the final fortnight cannot show the thinking that the criteria credit. The habit that makes it work is a short weekly entry from the beginning, recording decisions, dead ends and changes of direction. A tutor can ask about the journal every week, which is often the whole of the useful intervention.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE student need a different kind of tutor from a Middle Years student?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and this is where households at continuum schools get caught. IGCSE is linear and terminally assessed, so technique, timing and published component weightings decide it, and past-paper work is central. The Middle Years Programme has no past paper and marks four criteria against published descriptors, so the work is reading the student's own tasks against the wording. A tutor strong at one can be ineffective at the other, and the trial lesson is where to test it.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge series can an Abu Dhabi candidate sit, and when are checkpoints?
faqs.answer: June and November for the main series. Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not available to a UAE candidate, and any guidance suggesting a spring sitting describes another country's timetable. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone version of the timetable is essential, so ask the examinations officer which zone applies.

faqs.question: How long does an IGCSE result actually take to arrive?
faqs.answer: Weeks, and the checkable anchors are historical. Pearson Edexcel's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Future windows are not dated here because provisional timetables get revised; work from the live official timetable through the school's examinations officer rather than any summary.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's internal assessment draft and tell them what to change?
faqs.answer: A tutor can mark the draft and name which criterion is costing marks, and cannot make the changes. The permitted work is wide: explaining each descriptor, narrowing the research question, teaching the statistical test or laboratory technique, marking the student's own draft and rehearsing the supervisor meeting. The prohibited work is contributing text, redrafting into a final version or supplying data. One operation ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments, and that purchase risks the student's whole qualification.

faqs.question: Why will a tutor not just send us the mark scheme and past papers?
faqs.answer: Because they belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson, and reproducing or supplying them is a copyright matter rather than a service. For unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure for the student. The correct position is to reference the official document, link to it on the board's own site, and work from what the school has legitimately provided. A provider offering downloadable mark schemes and grade-boundary tables is taking a risk on the family's behalf.

faqs.question: What can a tutor not fix, however many sessions we buy?
faqs.answer: The practice between sessions. Beyond that, some things take longer than a purchase implies: algebraic fluency builds over weeks of short daily work, a missing conceptual foundation has to be rebuilt in sequence, and essay structure and reading stamina improve over a term. Conventions, by contrast, change in an hour. An honest plan separates the two and gives a realistic timescale for each, rather than implying that everything moves at the speed of the fastest item.

faqs.question: Does Abu Dhabi's regulator publish anything that helps us judge a school?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Read them on ADEK's own site rather than on an aggregator, because aggregated ratings go stale and band vocabulary differs between emirates. Across the competitor pages measured for this project, ADEK was named by nobody at all. Dubai sits with KHDA, Sharjah with SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and three emirates with the federal Ministry.

faqs.question: Can a weekly criterion session continue through Ramadan and the holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and continuity matters more here than for paper-based work, because criterion improvement is cumulative rather than event-driven. During Ramadan, timings commonly shift to after Iftar, which a video arrangement handles by moving a calendar entry rather than redrawing a driving route. Over holidays families often reduce frequency instead of stopping, which keeps the habit of self-marking against descriptors alive. A student travelling for a fortnight keeps the slot rather than losing a month of momentum.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IGCSE and IB Diploma subjects Al Raha and Khalifa City families ask for most often. Each one teaches a named syllabus rather than a year group, so a request for 0620 Chemistry or DP Maths AA SL reaches someone who has marked that paper.

intro.heading: Start with the number, not the brochure
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages aimed at Abu Dhabi families hide the price. Of the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026, three of six published no hourly figure at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars, which is not the currency any Abu Dhabi parent transacts in. One agency's own frequently-asked-questions block asked what tutoring costs and then declined to answer it. That is the standard this page is written against, so the rates come first and the sales argument comes after.

Here is the shape of the Abu Dhabi market. A university-student tutor working online sits roughly between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist in IB, IGCSE or A-Level sits at AED 200 to 450 and upwards; TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's Abu Dhabi and Dubai rate survey tops out past AED 450. A named premium or examiner-led tutor can reach AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure. Every one of those numbers belongs to the provider named beside it, not to IB Gram.

In-home one-to-one visits are the expensive option, quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour once travel is in the figure. That band is wide because it is really two numbers added together: the teaching and the driving. A tutor crossing from the island to the Al Raha corridor at five in the afternoon spends forty minutes in traffic each way, and that time is billed whether the parent sees it on the invoice or not. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. What a family here buys instead is the teaching without the travel, which is why the arithmetic in the tables below works out the way it does.

Raha International School runs the IB continuum, which changes what the money buys. A student in the Middle Years Programme is being assessed against criteria, not papers, and a tutor who only knows how to drill past questions will not move an MYP grade. A Diploma student needs something different again: paper technique, command-term discipline, and a supervisor-safe process for the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay. Families who arrive here searching for an IGCSE tutor are usually either joining Abu Dhabi from a British-curriculum school mid-stream, or running two children on two different boards in the same house. Both of those cases are priced below, because both are common in Al Raha Gardens.

The last thing worth saying before the tables: price and value separate quickly in exam year. A cheap tutor who has never seen a marked script will spend a session re-teaching content the student already half-knows. A specialist spends the same hour on the four marks the student drops every single time, because they recognise the pattern from thirty other scripts. That difference is what the top of the AED band is actually selling, and a parent can test it in a single free trial lesson before committing to anything.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.programmesIntro: Raha International School teaches the IB continuum, so a tutoring plan has to match the programme the student is actually in rather than their age. The four blocks below set out what each programme assesses and what that means for a family in the Al Raha corridor specifically.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with no external examination at any point. Progress is reported against learner-profile attributes and unit outcomes rather than marks out of a hundred, which is why a PYP report card can look reassuring while a specific skill gap sits underneath it. The gaps that matter later are number fluency, written structure and reading stamina, because those three are what the Middle Years Programme immediately starts assessing.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi adds a layer the PYP does not: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in private schools across the UAE regardless of the licensed curriculum, and the federal rule behind that sits with the Ministry of Education. A PYP family in Al Raha often finds Arabic is the only subject with a conventional mark on the report, and the only one where a parent cannot help at the table.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, and converts the total to a one-to-seven grade. There is no past paper to drill. A student who writes good content but ignores the criterion wording loses marks that look invisible to them, and the fix is reading the rubric aloud against their own draft until they can predict their own score. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed on process, not product.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where Abu Dhabi families most often consider a board change, because a move to an IGCSE school at Year 10 means picking up a linear two-year syllabus halfway through. Students leaving the Al Raha corridor for a British-curriculum school in Khalifa City or on Al Mushrif typically need bridging in maths notation and in science practical write-ups, where IGCSE expects a format MYP never taught.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a fixed share of the final grade, and the external papers carry the rest. The Diploma punishes poor time management more than weak content, because five Internal Assessment deadlines and an Extended Essay land inside the same four months of the second year. UAE candidates sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: For an Abu Dhabi DP student, the two pressure points are the Internal Assessment calendar and the Arabic requirement running alongside six Diploma subjects. Tutoring demand in the Al Raha corridor spikes twice a year: once in the autumn when Extended Essay first drafts are due, and again after the mock results in the second year, when the gap between a predicted five and a required six becomes a university problem.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year linear course assessed almost entirely by terminal examination, with syllabus codes that matter: 0580 and 0980 for Cambridge Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0625 for Physics, 4MA1 for Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A. Cambridge splits many sciences and maths into Core and Extended, which caps the grade available. Pearson runs a modular structure on some specifications that Cambridge does not, and the difference changes when a resit is possible.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE student in Abu Dhabi matters for a reason beyond the grade: the Ministry of Education equivalency route for British-curriculum students counts five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included in those five. That makes subject choice at Year 9 a decision with a regulatory consequence, not only an academic one.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Raha and Khalifa City families request most, with what each one actually assesses and the place marks go missing. Rates for all of them sit inside the same market band; the subject does not change the hourly figure as much as the level and the proximity to an exam series does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. The Higher Level paper set adds proof, complex numbers and a longer calculus reach, and the non-calculator paper is where most of the damage happens. Marks go missing in method lines that are correct but unwritten, because the mark scheme awards the working and the student only wrote the answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Students lose marks by reporting a calculator output without the command that produced it, and by treating a regression line as an answer rather than as a model with limits. The Internal Assessment here rewards a dataset the student collected and can defend.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate grades at Higher Level. At IGCSE 0620 the recurring loss is in mole calculations presented without units and in the practical paper, where students describe a procedure they could not actually follow. Data-based questions reward reading the axis labels before the question stem, which almost nobody does under time pressure.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The gap is rarely the maths. It is the definition: students who cannot state what a field is in one sentence cannot answer the three-mark explain question that follows. Circuits and electromagnetic induction produce the most dropped marks at both levels, and the fix is drawing the circuit before writing anything, every time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content makes this feel like a memory test, and students revise it as one. The marks sit in command terms: outline, explain, evaluate and discuss each want a different shape of answer, and a well-memorised paragraph scores two out of five when the verb asked for a comparison. Statistics in the Internal Assessment is a routine weak point.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis and it is won in the first ten minutes of reading, not the last ten of writing. The Individual Oral fails on the global issue, not on the texts: students pick something too broad to evidence in ten minutes. Higher Level adds the essay, which needs a line of argument rather than a tour of the novel.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns credit that prose cannot recover, and students who draw from memory rather than from the question routinely shift the wrong curve. Paper 3 at Higher Level is quantitative and is the single biggest differentiator between a five and a seven in this subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Extended opens grades A* to E; Core caps at C, and that cap is set by the school's entry decision long before the exam. The recurring Extended losses are in bearings, similar-shape ratios and anything requiring a surd left unrounded. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 covers similar ground with a different paper split and its own formula sheet conventions.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools alongside any international curriculum, and the subject where expatriate families most often feel unable to help. KHDA guidance requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, so the non-Arab stream has its own syllabus and its own realistic ceiling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study is released ahead of the Higher Level paper and students under-prepare it, treating it as background rather than as the examined material. Marks are lost in tools applied without the company's actual numbers. The Internal Assessment requires real organisational data and a research question narrow enough to answer in the word limit.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi changes the logistics of tutoring more than the price of it. These are the communities Raha International School families most commonly commute from, with the detail that actually affects when a session can start.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: The villa community immediately beside the school, which is why the afternoon school run here is short and a four o'clock session start is realistic. Families in Al Raha Gardens are the one group in Abu Dhabi for whom an in-home tutor would cost least in travel, and even here the specialist pool within a twenty-minute drive is thin.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Apartment towers along the Khor Al Raha channel, with a different rhythm from the villas: more single-child households, more families on two-year postings, and more mid-year arrivals who need bridging rather than long-term support. Sessions here often start later because both parents commute to the island.

regions.name: Khalifa City A
regions.note: A large villa catchment feeding several British-curriculum and IB schools, so households here frequently run two boards at once. Traffic onto the Abu Dhabi-Dubai road at half past three makes a five o'clock start more reliable than four, which matters when a tutor is holding a fixed weekly slot.

regions.name: Al Bandar and Al Zeina
regions.note: Waterfront communities on Al Raha Beach with a high proportion of secondary-age students travelling to school by bus. Bus timings rather than parent timings set the earliest session, and families here are the most likely to ask for weekend blocks instead of weekday evenings.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer residential clusters with a growing school-age population and a commute that is short in distance but unpredictable around event weekends. Families on Yas often want a schedule that survives travel, because event-driven and holiday-driven absence is common.

regions.name: Masdar City and Zayed City
regions.note: Closer to the airport corridor, with households attached to the research and government sectors. Demand here skews towards Higher Level sciences and maths, and towards university-application support in the second Diploma year, because university route decisions are made early in these families.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short crossing from the island, home to several of the emirate's newer British and American schools. Saadiyat families appear on this page when a sibling is at Raha and another is on a different board, which is the single most common reason one household needs both an IB and an IGCSE tutor.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Raha and Khalifa City corridor
schoolClusters.note: This corridor holds the densest cluster of secondary-age international students outside the island itself, which is why a tutor advertising travel to homes here can fill a diary on geography alone. The schools below sit within a few minutes of one another and draw from overlapping villa communities, so students often know each other across school lines.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island and Al Mushrif
schoolClusters.note: The older established schools sit here, and families who moved outward to the villa communities frequently keep a child enrolled on the island rather than change schools mid-programme. That produces the long afternoon commutes that make a fixed in-home slot hard to hold and an online slot easy to hold.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.modesIntro: Three ways to buy the same teaching, with different cost structures. The choice is usually decided by how many weeks remain before an assessment rather than by preference, so each block below says what it is actually for.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-long
modes.description: One or two fixed sessions a week across a term, running with the school's own scheme of work rather than ahead of it. This is the cheapest route per unit of improvement because nothing is wasted on re-establishing where the student is each time. For a Diploma student it also means the Internal Assessment gets touched every week in small increments instead of in one panicked block.

modes.title: Exam-series intensive
modes.description: A compressed block of sessions in the eight to ten weeks before a Cambridge June series or an IB May session, built entirely around timed questions and marked scripts. Content teaching stops; everything becomes technique, command terms and the recurring four marks the student drops. Abu Dhabi demand for this concentrates sharply in the second half of the spring term and availability tightens with it.

modes.title: Coursework process support
modes.description: Scheduled sessions through the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project cycle, working on the student's own draft. The tutor reads what the student wrote, maps it against the published criteria, and names the criterion that is costing marks. The tutor does not write, redraft to completion, or supply text. That boundary is stated in the first session and it is not negotiable.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE or IB tutor costs for a Raha International School family
paragraphs: A qualified online subject tutor for an IGCSE or Diploma student in Abu Dhabi is priced in the AED 150 to 300 band, with specialists in Higher Level sciences, Higher Level maths and Internal Assessment supervision sitting from AED 200 up past AED 450. Those are market figures, drawn from providers' own published rates and from the Bestimate tutoring rate survey for the 2026-27 year. They are not an IB Gram price list.

The table below splits the market by level and by format, because those two variables move the number far more than the subject does. Read the in-home column as what the market quotes, not as something available from IB Gram; tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visits are offered only in India. The small-group column is per student, which is why it looks cheap until you notice the tutor is dividing attention four ways through a session that an exam-year student needs undivided.

Two patterns are worth naming before the rows. First, the gap between the budget band and the specialist band is not experience, it is diagnosis: a specialist arrives knowing what a Chemistry 0620 candidate at a given grade typically gets wrong, and spends the hour there. Second, the monthly figure is the one families actually budget against, and it hides the session count. AED 799 a month for eight online sessions is a different product from AED 1,599 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, and the second is not twice the teaching.

sections.heading: What moves the number in Abu Dhabi specifically
paragraphs: Four things push an Abu Dhabi quote from the bottom of its band to the top, and three of them have nothing to do with teaching quality. The first is travel. An in-home rate is a teaching rate plus a driving rate, and the driving rate in this emirate is set by the crossing between the island and the mainland villa communities. A tutor who lives on Al Reem and teaches in Khalifa City at five o'clock is selling two hours of their evening for one hour of lessons, and prices accordingly.

The second is the calendar. Specialist availability in the eight weeks before a June Cambridge series or an IB May session is the scarcest commodity in this market, and scarcity is priced. A family booking an Extended Level Chemistry specialist in September pays the middle of the band; the same family booking in April pays the top of it, if a slot exists at all. This is the single most avoidable premium on the page.

The third is subject scarcity. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches, Economics Paper 3 and the Internal Assessment supervision work all have fewer qualified people than demand, and in a city the size of Abu Dhabi that shortage is real rather than theoretical. The fourth is session length: a sixty-minute slot and a ninety-minute slot are rarely priced proportionally, and the longer block is usually better value per unit of work done, because the first ten minutes of any session are spent reconnecting with where the student left off.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a tuition centre: the Abu Dhabi arithmetic
paragraphs: This is the comparison the whole page turns on, so it gets a table rather than an argument. The honest position is that in-home tutoring buys one real thing an online lesson cannot: a tutor physically beside a student who will not engage with a screen. For a Year 4 student with attention difficulties, that is decisive. For a Diploma candidate working on a Higher Level Chemistry paper, it is worth considerably less than having a tutor who has marked that paper, and the second is what a national online pool makes possible.

The travel premium is not only money. A tutor arriving at half past five because the Sheikh Zayed bridge was slow is teaching a tired student in a shortened session, and the cancellation rate for weather, traffic and travel is materially higher than for a video call. Over a term of twenty-eight sessions, a family with a travelling tutor typically loses two or three to logistics. That is roughly one per cent of a Diploma year's tutoring, lost to the road.

The tuition centre is the third model and it is genuinely cheaper, because the cost is divided. What divides with it is attention. A centre group of six running an IGCSE maths revision course covers the syllabus on a fixed schedule regardless of whether a given student already understands the topic that week. For a student who is broadly on track and needs structure, that is good value. For a student who drops the same four marks every paper, it is the wrong purchase at any price.

sections.heading: Raha teaches the IB continuum, so why search for an IGCSE tutor?
paragraphs: This page carries both boards in its title for a reason that is worth being straight about. Raha International School is an IB continuum school, so a student enrolled there is in the Primary Years, Middle Years or Diploma Programme, not sitting IGCSEs. Families who search for an IGCSE tutor for Raha students are almost always in one of three situations, and each needs something different.

The first is a mid-stream arrival. A family moving to Abu Dhabi from a British-curriculum school in another country has a child who has started a two-year IGCSE course, and the question is whether to finish it as a private candidate or move into the Middle Years Programme. That is a decision with real consequences, because the Ministry of Education equivalency route for British-curriculum students counts five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and a half-finished IGCSE set counts for nothing. Arabic and Islamic Education sit outside those five.

The second is a two-board household: one child at Raha in the Middle Years Programme, a sibling at a British-curriculum school in Khalifa City or on Al Mushrif working towards 0580 and 0620. One tutoring arrangement has to cover both, and the criteria-based and paper-based worlds need different teaching. The third is a family planning a move outward, considering a British-curriculum school for the sixth form and wanting to know what the gap looks like before they commit. All three are served below, and none of them is served by pretending Raha runs an IGCSE programme.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context against the rest of the education bill
paragraphs: A tutoring number means little on its own. Set against the other lines on an Abu Dhabi family's education budget it becomes a proportion, and proportions are what parents actually decide on. The context worth knowing is that Dubai's regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi runs its own fee-approval process through its own regulator, so that freeze does not transfer, but it sets the direction of travel in the market families are comparing against.

The private-candidate exam route is the line most families have never costed, and it matters specifically for the mid-stream arrival case above. Sitting IGCSEs as a private candidate means paying an examination centre's own entry fees per subject, which are set by the centre rather than by the board, and those fees are separate from any tutoring. A family deciding between finishing IGCSEs privately and converting to the Middle Years Programme should get a written per-subject entry quote from a local centre before they decide, because it changes the arithmetic materially.

Every figure in it is a market band rather than a quotation, and the tutoring rows assume the online one-to-one rates from earlier on this page. Nothing here includes an IB Gram price, because IB Gram's own commercial terms are set in the consultation after a free trial lesson rather than published as a rate card.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a session calendar. Across the competitor pages fetched for this project, the word November returned zero hits, meaning not one of them told a parent when their child's resit opportunity falls. That gap is filled here, with one correction that matters more than anything else on the page: Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate sits the June series and the November series. Any page telling an Abu Dhabi family about a spring Cambridge sitting is describing a different country's timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and keep their dates, which is what makes them checkable. Forward-looking windows are named by month only here, because a published provisional timetable can be revised and a page that pins a future date goes wrong without anyone touching it.

The operational point is that the deadlines a family can miss sit months before the exam. Entry closes long before the paper, and the entry is made by the school or the centre, not by the parent. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after reading the wrong version. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in, and work from that timetable rather than from any summary, including this one.

sections.heading: ADEK and who regulates what across the Emirates
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. This matters to a Raha family for a practical reason: the inspection framework, the rating vocabulary and the complaints route are all ADEK's, not Dubai's, and advice written for a Dubai audience routinely points parents at the wrong authority. Across the competitor pages measured for this project, ADEK was named by nobody at all.

The full regulator map for UAE private schools has five bodies. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah sits with its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in those three. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum approval and not only inspection sits locally.

What a parent does with this: read the inspection report on the regulator's own site rather than on an aggregator, because the aggregators carry stale ratings. Check which authority covers the school before asking anyone a question about it. And treat any tutoring provider claiming to be approved, accredited or licensed by one of these bodies with suspicion. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and says so plainly rather than implying otherwise.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or Personal Project
paragraphs: This section exists because one page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for a published AED figure. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student, whose Diploma is the thing at risk, not the seller's. The boundary is simple to state and worth stating in writing before any coursework session happens: the work must be the student's own, and a tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback.

In practice that means a tutor can read the published criteria with the student and explain what each criterion letter is awarding. They can interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to answer inside the word limit. They can teach the statistics or the lab technique the investigation needs. They can read a draft the student wrote and say which criterion is costing marks and why. They can rehearse the conversation the student is about to have with their supervisor. Every one of those is teaching.

What a tutor cannot do is write any part of the submission, redraft a passage into its final form, supply text or data for the student to use, or edit the work to completion. The distinction a student should be able to apply themselves is whether they could explain every sentence in their own submission to their supervisor without help. If the answer is no, the line has been crossed, whoever crossed it. A tutor who offers to produce the work is not offering a shortcut; they are offering to put the student's entire Diploma on the table.
bullets: Teaching, questioning, reviewing and feedback on the student's own draft: allowed
Writing, redrafting to completion, supplying text or data: not allowed, at any price
Official syllabus guides, mark schemes and past papers: linked from the board, never reproduced
The test a student can apply: could they explain every sentence unaided?

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and what a UAE university will want to see
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that converts a foreign school certificate into something the UAE system recognises, and it is the step families discover late. For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five subjects.

That five-subject rule is worth repeating because a competitor page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents the figure is six. It is five, and the difference is one subject's worth of a teenager's Year 10 timetable. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the IB there is a deliberate gap in this page. No IB points threshold for equivalency is published here, because none could be verified against the Ministry of Education's own site, and an unverified threshold repeated across hundreds of pages is a liability rather than a service. A Diploma family should confirm the current IB requirement directly with the Ministry or with the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and it is not a reason to buy tutoring; it is a process to understand early and use the official channel for.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: A request that says Chemistry gets a generalist. A request that says Cambridge 0620 Extended, Paper 4 and Paper 6, currently a C, aiming for an A, reaches someone who has marked those papers. The same applies at Diploma level: name the programme, the level, and whether the Internal Assessment is the pressure point.

process.title: A free trial lesson, before anything is paid
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, at no cost and with no card required, so the student decides whether this person explains things in a way that lands. The tutor uses it to diagnose rather than to sell, and afterwards you get a written view of where the marks are actually going.

process.title: An honest answer on availability
process.description: If no specialist in that exact subject and level is free at the time you need, you are told that and offered the alternatives, including a different slot or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit; a provider that hides one is a provider you find out about in exam term.

process.title: A plan with the school's calendar in it
process.description: Sessions are scheduled against the school's own deadlines and the board's series, not a generic term structure. For a Diploma student that means the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay dates go into the plan first and the weekly subject work is built around them, because those are the deadlines that cannot move.

process.title: Written feedback every session, visible to you
process.description: After each session you receive what was covered, what was set, and what the tutor thinks is still weak. That record is what makes a six-month arrangement reviewable rather than a matter of faith, and it is the same document a student can take into a supervisor meeting.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page are sourced, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, and none of them is presented as an IB Gram price. Three of six competitor pages measured for this project published no rate at all, and the two that did used US dollars. A parent who can see the market can judge a quote against it.

whyPoints.title: Specialists by syllabus code, not by year group
whyPoints.description: A tutor matched to Cambridge 0620 Extended or to Diploma Maths Analysis and Approaches Higher Level knows the paper structure, the command terms and the recurring losses. That is different from a good teacher who has never seen the specification, and the difference shows up in the first marked script.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated plainly, everywhere
whyPoints.description: Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is said on this page, on the UAE hub and on every country page, so nobody discovers it after paying.

whyPoints.title: A coursework boundary written down in advance
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work and does not write, redraft to completion or supply text for any Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. The boundary is stated before the first coursework session, because the student's Diploma is what is at risk.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and names none of the schools on this page as a client or partner. No satisfaction percentage, star rating or success figure appears here, because none could be evidenced with a sample size and a method.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool that is not limited by driving distance
whyPoints.description: A family in Al Raha Gardens looking for a Higher Level Physics specialist is choosing from everyone available online rather than from whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive. In a subject with a genuine shortage of qualified teachers in this emirate, that is the whole difference between the right tutor and an available one.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE or IB tutor cost per hour for a Raha International School family?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Abu Dhabi for a qualified online subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a specialist in a Higher Level subject or in Internal Assessment supervision. Those figures come from providers' own published rates and from the Bestimate tutoring rate survey for 2026-27; they describe the market, not an IB Gram price list. In-home visits in the emirate are quoted at AED 180 to 500 once travel is included. IB Gram's own terms are set after a free trial lesson rather than published as a rate card.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home rate in Abu Dhabi so much higher than the online rate?
faqs.answer: Because an in-home rate is two charges added together: the teaching and the driving. A tutor crossing between Abu Dhabi island and the Al Raha or Khalifa City villa communities at five in the afternoon commits around ninety minutes of their evening to deliver sixty minutes of lesson, and that time is in the price whether the invoice itemises it or not. Travelling arrangements also lose more sessions to traffic and weather than video calls do. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at any rate; the figures are quoted here so a family can compare them honestly.

faqs.question: Raha runs the IB continuum, so does an IGCSE tutor make any sense for us?
faqs.answer: It makes sense in three situations, all of them common in this corridor. A child arriving mid-stream from a British-curriculum school abroad may be part-way through a two-year IGCSE course and needs a decision about finishing it as a private candidate or converting into the Middle Years Programme. A household may run two children on two boards at once. Or a family may be planning a move to a British-curriculum sixth form and want to know what the bridging costs in weeks. If none of those applies, Diploma or Middle Years support is what you actually want.

faqs.question: Does a tutor charge more for Higher Level than Standard Level, and by how much?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the gap in this market is roughly AED 40 to 130 an hour between Standard and Higher Level for the same subject. Two things cause it. Higher Level content reaches further, so fewer tutors can teach it to the top of the grade range. And the pool of people who have actually marked Higher Level scripts is small in an emirate this size, which is scarcity rather than snobbery. The practical consequence is that Higher Level specialists book out earliest, so a family that needs one in exam term should be arranging it two terms ahead.

faqs.question: When do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi go up, and can we avoid that?
faqs.answer: Rates firm up and choice narrows in the eight to ten weeks before a Cambridge June series or an IB May session, which is the most avoidable premium in this market. A family booking a specialist in the autumn pays mid-band and picks from a real list. The same family booking in April pays the top of the band and takes whoever is left, if anyone is. Booking early costs nothing extra and buys the tutor rather than a tutor, so the sensible move is to arrange exam-year support before the autumn term finishes.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series do UAE candidates actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so any guidance pointing an Abu Dhabi family at a spring Cambridge sitting is describing a different country's timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, so ask your school's examinations officer which zone applies before working from any published dates.

faqs.question: Is the November series a real resit route for an Abu Dhabi student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the one nobody writes about. Across the competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026, the word November returned zero hits, so not one of them told a parent when their child's second chance falls. For Cambridge in the UAE, November is the resit series after June. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, November is a full series in its own right; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Confirm current dates with the centre.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one ninety-minute session a week per subject that is genuinely behind, which is one or two subjects rather than six. In the second Diploma year, the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay cycle often adds a separate block of eight to twelve sessions. A student taking three or four tutored subjects at once is usually a scheduling problem rather than an academic one, and the honest advice is to fix the weakest subject properly before adding a second. More hours in more subjects dilutes the work that moves a grade.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish the Internal Assessment for us if time runs short?
faqs.answer: No, and the refusal is the point. A tutor can read the published criteria with the student, narrow a research question, teach the statistics or technique the investigation needs, read a draft the student wrote and name the criterion costing marks, and rehearse the supervisor conversation. A tutor cannot write any part of it, redraft a passage to its final form, or supply text or data. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger, and the thing at risk is the student's Diploma, not the seller's business.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates Raha International School and where do we read its report?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi's private schools sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Read the report on ADEK's own site rather than on an aggregator, because aggregated ratings go stale and the vocabulary differs between emirates. Dubai's schools sit with KHDA, Sharjah's with SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Guidance written for Dubai parents routinely points Abu Dhabi families at the wrong authority.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE tuition permit required for a tutor teaching an Al Raha student?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Ask the tutor directly and check against the MoHRE service page.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at school tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need that permit. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify the current wording against ADEK's own publication, but treat any offer of your child's own teacher privately as a problem rather than a perk.

faqs.question: What do Arabic and Islamic Education mean for a Raha family's tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the federal baseline behind that requirement sits with the Ministry of Education. KHDA's Dubai guidance, the most detailed published version, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For an expatriate family in Al Raha these are often the only subjects a parent cannot help with at the table, and the non-Arab Arabic stream is the one most commonly tutored alongside the IB programme.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free in the subject and slot we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, before you pay anything. The alternatives are a different time in the week, a different tutor at the same level, or a specialist based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, which is how the scarcer Higher Level subjects usually get covered. No competitor page measured for this project discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without mentioning where delivery happens. An availability answer you can plan around is worth more than an unconditional yes you find out about in exam term.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class cheaper than one-to-one, and is it worse?
faqs.answer: Cheaper, yes: centre group rates in this market sit around AED 85 to 160 per student an hour against AED 150 to 450 for one-to-one. Worse depends entirely on the student. A group covers the syllabus on a fixed schedule whether or not a given student needed that topic this week, which suits someone broadly on track who wants external structure. It does not suit a student dropping the same four marks on every paper, because diagnosing that pattern needs someone looking at their script and nobody else's.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Abu Dhabi school hours, Ramadan and family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the practical advantage of video delivery in this emirate. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and can be set after the school bus arrives, which for Al Raha Beach and Al Bandar families is often later than the villa communities. During Ramadan, timings commonly shift to after Iftar, and a video slot moves without a tutor having to redraw a driving route. Family travel is the same problem solved the same way: a student abroad for two weeks keeps the slot rather than losing a month of momentum.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.closingHeading: Start with a free trial lesson and a straight answer on cost
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raha-intern.closingBody: If your child is at Raha International School and either the Diploma deadlines or a half-finished IGCSE set is the problem, the next step is a single free trial lesson with the tutor we propose. No payment, no card. Tell us the programme and level, the specific papers or criteria that are costing marks, and the realistic window in the week after the school run. You will get a written view of where the marks are going, an honest answer on whether a specialist in that exact subject is available in that slot, and a plan built around the school's own deadlines. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-reach-briti.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE across mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects, one-to-one over live video into Gulf Standard Time. Every block runs for six weeks against one named target and ends in a decision.

intro.heading: Six weeks, one target, one decision
paragraphs: The standard tutoring offer in this market is a term, sometimes a year, with progress reported in adjectives. That shape suits providers and it is not the shape a family needs. Six weeks is long enough for honest work on a narrow target to show movement, short enough that being wrong costs a manageable amount, and exactly the right length to end in a decision rather than a renewal. Nothing about that is complicated; it is simply not how the market sells.

The protocol below has four parts and they have to happen in order. A baseline measured with a repeatable instrument before anything is bought. One narrow target chosen from that baseline, not three. Four weeks of work aimed only at that target, with the pupil's own written work produced every week. Then the same instrument again, under the same conditions, and a decision based on what the comparison shows. If any part is skipped the rest stops meaning anything.

The repeatability of the instrument is the part most often got wrong, and it is the part that does all the work. A baseline taken from a school assessment and a re-test taken from a different school assessment cannot be compared, because the two papers differ in difficulty, coverage and conditions. A Cambridge or Pearson past paper, downloaded from the official board site, sat under timing, marked against the published scheme, can be compared with another one. That is the whole technical requirement.

The narrowness of the target is the part families resist. A pupil with three shaky subjects wants all three addressed, and a provider is happy to oblige. But a six-week block aimed at three things produces a result that cannot be interpreted: if the marks move, nobody knows which intervention did it, and if they do not, nobody knows which one failed. One target per block is not stinginess; it is what makes the block informative. The second target gets the next six weeks.

And the decision at week six has to be a real decision, including the option to stop. A block that ends with the target met should stop or move to a new target. A block that ends with the target unmet should end with an honest account of why - wrong diagnosis, wrong match, or work not done between sessions - and those are findable rather than mysterious. No ranking competitor page in this market publishes a stop rule, which is understandable from a provider's position and not from a family's. Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

The baseline and the re-test must use the same instrument under the same conditions

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-reach-briti.programmesIntro: The protocol is the same at every stage; what changes is the instrument available. Below is what can be used as a repeatable baseline at each point.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: No external papers exist, so the repeatable instrument has to be constructed: a fixed set of fluency or comprehension tasks, timed, used identically at week zero and week five. Crude but comparable, which is the only property that matters. Six-week blocks work especially well here because the targets are narrow by nature.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools set and stream in most cases, and the set a pupil occupies at the end of Year 9 often informs the IGCSE tier a department later proposes. A documented six-week block showing movement is exactly the kind of evidence a department can act on in a set review.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: The best-instrumented stage anywhere in school, because past papers and published mark schemes exist in quantity on the boards' own sites. A pupil can sit comparable papers repeatedly under identical conditions and the marks are directly comparable. Almost no family uses this, and it is free.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used, so ask the school which zone applies.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The measurable unit shifts from a paper mark to a criterion letter, because internal assessments are scored against lettered criteria with stated mark allocations. A draft can be scored criterion by criterion at week zero and week five, which is a genuinely repeatable instrument for work that is not examined by paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a substantial International Baccalaureate presence alongside its British and American curriculum schools. For a Diploma pupil the six-week block often maps naturally onto an internal assessment window, which makes the timing easier rather than harder.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Past papers remain the instrument, with one complication: content accumulates quickly, so a paper sat in week zero covers less of the course than one sat in week five. The fix is to use the same paper sections rather than whole papers, or to accept that the comparison is of question types rather than totals.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms publish IGCSE entry grades and often a mathematics requirement alongside for the sciences. A documented six-week block is a useful thing to have when making a case to a department, because it shows a trajectory rather than a single snapshot.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-reach-briti.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with the repeatable instrument that works for it and the kind of target a six-week block can realistically close.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The cleanest instrument available: a full past paper at the entered tier, timed, marked against the published scheme. Realistic six-week targets are written method, non-calculator fluency, or precision on final answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Same instrument, different papers and calculator permissions. The comparison is only valid if both the baseline and the re-test come from the board on the entry, which is worth confirming in writing before week zero.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Measure the theory and practical components separately, because they move independently. A realistic six-week target is extended-response explanation marks, or written method on the practical paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Moles give a binary instrument that takes two minutes: three Extended-tier calculations and whether the pupil writes a balanced equation first. A six-week block is ample for that target if that is the one chosen.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: The instrument is a set of extended-response questions marked for terminology precision. A six-week target is command-term discipline, which is one of the fastest-moving targets in any subject.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: The instrument is one reading answer and one directed writing task, timed, scored against the assessment objectives. A realistic six-week target is the analysis sentence, or form and register in directed writing.

subjects.name: Literature in English (Cambridge 0475 and 0992)
subjects.description: Timed essays on the school's own set texts, scored against the real criteria. The six-week target is argument structure or quotation economy; learning a new text is not a six-week target and should not be sold as one.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge IGCSE 0470)
subjects.description: Source questions make an excellent instrument because they score on select, attribute, infer and evaluate. A six-week target is usually one of those four, and improvement transfers into English reading at the same time.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Separate data-response marks from evaluation marks in the baseline. The six-week target is almost always evaluation writing, which is where pupils who know the content lose an entire mark allocation.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory provision alongside any international curriculum under the federal baseline for UAE private schools. Reading fluency and script accuracy are both easy to instrument and move visibly inside six weeks.

sections.heading: Week zero: a baseline that can be repeated
paragraphs: Everything in this protocol depends on one property of the baseline: that it can be run again identically. That rules out most of what families naturally reach for. A school report is a judgement, not an instrument. A mock result is one performance under conditions that will not recur. A topic test written by a teacher cannot be re-sat without the pupil remembering it. None of these can produce a before-and-after comparison.

What can is a board past paper. Cambridge and Pearson publish past papers and mark schemes on their own sites, in quantity, across years and series. Two papers from different series at the same tier are close enough in difficulty to be compared, and far enough apart that a pupil will not recall the second from the first. Sat under the same timing, in the same kind of room, marked against the published scheme, they produce numbers that mean something.

The conditions matter as much as the paper. A baseline sat at four in the afternoon in a quiet room and a re-test sat at eight in the evening with a sibling's music audible are not comparable, and the difference will be larger than the intervention. Pick a slot and a setting at week zero and reuse both. In Abu Dhabi, where commutes from the Shamkha corridor or Khalifa City are long, that usually means a weekend morning for both sittings.

The marking standard is the third requirement. The same person marking against the same published scheme both times, with no generosity in either direction. A re-test marked more kindly than the baseline manufactures progress, which is worse than no measurement because it leads to a wrong decision at week six. The simplest protection is for the family to keep both scripts and both mark counts, which is why the log in a later section exists.

sections.heading: Weeks one and two: the target has to be narrow
paragraphs: A baseline usually shows losses spread across several categories, and the instinct is to address all of them. That instinct destroys the block. If four weeks of work targets method, arithmetic, precision and timing simultaneously, then whatever the week-five result shows, nobody can say which part worked. A null result is uninterpretable and a positive result is unrepeatable, so the next six weeks begins with no more information than the first.

One target per block is therefore a technical requirement rather than a commercial limitation. Choose the category holding the most marks, aim everything at it, and leave the others visibly alone. A pupil losing fourteen marks to unshown method and six to precision should spend six weeks on method. The precision marks are still there in six weeks' time, and they will be the next block's target, measured against a baseline that now includes a known method improvement.

The narrowness also changes what a session looks like. Work aimed at written method is not a lesson about a topic; it is the pupil doing questions with the method written out, every time, with the tutor refusing to accept an unshown answer however correct. Work aimed at the analysis sentence in English is the pupil writing that sentence, having it marked clause by clause, and writing it again. These are drills rather than lectures, and they are uncomfortable for about a fortnight.

Two things have to happen outside the session for the block to work. The pupil produces one piece of relevant written work between sessions, which is marked and returned. And nobody introduces a second target halfway through because a school assessment went badly in another subject. That second thing is where most blocks fail, and it fails for understandable reasons. Holding the line for six weeks is the single hardest part of this protocol.
