sections.heading: Weeks three and four: what should be visible in the pupil's work
paragraphs: By the middle of a block the indicator is behavioural rather than numeric, and this is where families get anxious unnecessarily. Marks will not usually have moved by week three, because a habit has to become automatic before it shows up under timing. What should have changed is the pupil's unprompted behaviour on their own written work: method appearing without being asked for, units attached, the question re-read before answering, the analysis sentence present.

That is checkable by a parent without any subject knowledge. Look at a piece of the pupil's work from week three next to a piece from week zero and ask whether the targeted behaviour is there. If method was the target, is working written out? If the analysis sentence was the target, is there a short quotation followed by an effect? The presence or absence of that behaviour is the mid-block signal, and it is more informative than any verbal report.

If the behaviour is absent at week three, something specific is wrong and it is usually one of three things. The target was not actually agreed with the pupil, so they do not know what they are supposed to be doing differently. The between-session work is not being done, so the habit has four opportunities a month rather than fifteen. Or the sessions have drifted onto content because content is more comfortable to teach than a drill is.

All three are addressable at week three and much harder to address at week six. This is the one checkpoint worth actively intervening at: ask the pupil to state the target in their own words, ask what they did differently this week, and look at the work. Three minutes of that is worth more than a monthly progress email, and it is the difference between a block that produces a decision and one that produces an excuse.

sections.heading: Week five: the re-test, under identical conditions
paragraphs: The re-test is the point of the whole exercise and it is the easiest part to compromise. A different paper from a different series at the same tier, from the official board site. The same timing. The same room, the same time of day, the same absence of interruptions. The same marker, using the same published scheme, with no allowance made for effort. Any deviation from that list weakens the comparison, and a weak comparison produces a wrong decision.

What is compared is not the total. Totals move for reasons unrelated to the intervention: a paper that happened to feature a strong topic, a question style the pupil likes, a good or bad morning. What is compared is the marks lost in the targeted category. If the target was written method, count the method marks in both scripts. If it was precision, count precision losses. That number is the result of the block and everything else is noise.

Two patterns are worth naming because they are easy to misread. A total that has fallen while the targeted category has improved is a successful block: the pupil has installed a habit and happened to meet a harder paper. A total that has risen while the targeted category is unchanged is not a successful block; the pupil had a better day and nothing has been learned that will survive June. The category is the result, every time.

The pupil should sit the re-test knowing it is a practice paper rather than a test of them, which is a presentation matter and not a trivial one. A fifteen-year-old told that six weeks of work is about to be judged will perform worse than one who has been asked to do a practice paper. The measurement belongs to the adults. The pupil's job is to sit the paper the way they would sit any paper.

sections.heading: Week six: three outcomes, and one of them is stop
paragraphs: The decision at week six has exactly three legitimate outcomes, and a provider who offers only one of them is not running a protocol. The target is met, in which case the block ends and either a new target begins or the arrangement stops. The target has moved but not enough, in which case one further block on the same target is reasonable with a stated expectation. Or the target has not moved at all, in which case something structural is wrong and continuing on the same basis is not an option.

The third case is the informative one. A target that has not moved after four weeks of focused work and a clean re-test has one of three causes. The diagnosis was wrong, meaning the marks were not actually being lost where the baseline suggested. The match was wrong, meaning this pupil and this tutor are not working. Or the between-session work did not happen, meaning the habit had too few repetitions. Each of those has a different response and all three are findable by asking.

What is not a legitimate response is another term on the same basis in the hope that more of the same produces a different result. That is the default in this market and it is the mechanism by which a six-week question becomes an eighteen-month arrangement. The stop rule exists precisely so that the conversation happens at the point where it is cheap, rather than at the point where somebody is angry.

Stopping is also sometimes the right outcome for reasons that have nothing to do with the tutoring. A pupil whose baseline reveals a content gap across a third of the specification in the spring of Year 11 cannot be rescued by six-week blocks, and the honest plan is to protect the subjects that can still move. A provider who says that has behaved well, and a provider who takes the money anyway has sold comfort at a specialist rate.

sections.heading: Why six weeks rather than a term
paragraphs: Six weeks is not arbitrary. It is four weeks of work with a measurement at each end, which is the shortest period in which a habit can become automatic enough to appear under timing. Shorter than that and a null result means nothing, because the intervention has not had time to land. Much longer and the cost of being wrong rises without the information improving, because a habit that has not formed in four weeks of focused drilling is unlikely to form in twelve.

A term has a different logic, and it is an institutional one rather than an educational one. Terms exist because schools are organised that way and because a term is a convenient billing period. Nothing about the way a fifteen-year-old acquires the habit of writing out method corresponds to a thirteen-week cycle. The term is the unit of the seller; the block is the unit of the question.

The six-week shape also fits a Dubai or Abu Dhabi school year better than a term does. It maps onto the gap between a mock and a report, onto the window before an internal assessment deadline, onto the stretch between a half-term and a holiday. And it survives the interruptions that a UAE calendar guarantees: trips, examination weeks, and in some years a Ramadan reshaping of the evening when sessions move to a post-Iftar slot.

There is one period where the block length should shorten rather than lengthen. In the eight to twelve weeks before the June series, the useful unit is two or three weeks: a timed paper, the errors re-worked, another timed paper. Nothing is being installed at that point; what remains is practice and immediate correction. A six-week block begun in April finishes after the examination, which is a plan with no purpose.

sections.heading: What the pupil should be able to say at each point
paragraphs: The pupil is the best available instrument for checking whether a block is real, and almost nobody asks them anything specific. At week zero they should be able to say what the target is, in their own words, without being prompted with the phrasing. 'I have to write the working out even when I can see the answer' is a target. 'I need to get better at maths' is not, and a pupil who says the second has not been given a target.

At week three they should be able to say what they are doing differently. Not whether the sessions are good - a fifteen-year-old will say yes to be polite - but what has changed in their own behaviour. 'I write the method now' or 'I check the units at the end' is the right kind of answer. 'We went through the stuff on circuits' describes a session and says nothing about whether a habit is forming.

At week five, before the re-test, they should be able to predict roughly where the marks will go. Pupils are better at this than adults expect, and a pupil who says 'I think I'll still lose the long explanation ones' has given you the next block's target before the paper is even marked. A pupil who has no view at all has not been engaged with the measurement, which is usually a presentation problem rather than an attitude one.

And at week six they should be present for the decision, or at least told it in terms they recognise. A pupil who learns that the method marks they have been drilling for six weeks did in fact appear has been given something no amount of encouragement provides, which is evidence that effort maps onto outcome. A pupil who is simply told that sessions will continue has learned that adults buy things and nothing more.

sections.heading: Recording it: the one-page log
paragraphs: A block that is not written down does not exist by week six, because memory reconstructs it favourably. The whole record fits on one page and the family keeps it, not the provider. Week zero: the paper used, the date, the conditions, the total, and the marks lost by category. Weeks one to four: the date, the work produced between sessions, and whether the targeted behaviour was present. Week five: the same fields as week zero. Week six: the decision and the reason.

That page does three things. It makes the week-six decision mechanical rather than negotiated, because the numbers are already written down and nobody is reconstructing them under social pressure. It makes a second block's baseline meaningful, because the first block's result is recorded rather than remembered. And it is a document a head of department can read in two minutes if a set review or a tier conversation becomes relevant.

The log also protects against the commonest soft failure in this market, which is scope creep. An arrangement that began with one target in one subject and is now general support across three has drifted, and the drift is invisible without a record. A page showing a target in week one and a different target in week three has shown you the problem without anybody having to raise it as a complaint.

It should belong to the family in a literal sense. A log the provider holds is a log the family cannot check, and an arrangement where the evidence lives only in the tutor's notes cannot be evaluated by the person paying for it. Ask for it at week zero rather than at week six, because a provider who will not maintain it is telling you something about how the block is going to be assessed.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and coverage
paragraphs: The protocol does not change the rules about what a tutor may do. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece, including a school assessment or a Diploma internal assessment, and no price makes that acceptable. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate rather than the provider taking the fee.

Board material should not be handed over as files either. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and the right behaviour is to link the official page. That matters practically for this protocol, because the baseline and re-test papers must come from the official site anyway, and a family that knows where they live can check the comparison for themselves at any point.

On credentials, parents are entitled to check the one that exists. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules are reported to bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, so that arrangement should not be sought.

On coverage: mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist, and in a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free. Where a specialist is working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, that is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number, and the rate does not change. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval or partnership, and has no office in the UAE.

process.title: Download two comparable past papers
process.description: From the official Cambridge or Pearson site, at the tier on your child's entry, from two different series. One is the week-zero baseline and one is the week-five re-test. Keep both, and keep both mark schemes. This step costs nothing and it is the whole technical foundation of the protocol.

process.title: Fix the conditions and reuse them
process.description: Same time of day, same room, same timing, no interruptions. In Abu Dhabi, where runs from Al Shamkha or Khalifa City are long, that usually means a weekend morning for both sittings. A re-test under different conditions produces a difference larger than any intervention and makes the block meaningless.

process.title: Agree one target with the pupil present
process.description: Phrased in words the pupil can repeat back without prompting. One category, not three. Write it on the log. A pupil who cannot state the target at week three has not been given one, and that single check catches most failing blocks while they can still be redirected.

process.title: Check behaviour at week three, not marks
process.description: Put a piece of work from week three beside one from week zero and ask whether the targeted behaviour is present. That takes no subject knowledge. If it is absent, the cause is the target, the between-session work or session drift onto content, and all three are fixable at week three.

process.title: Decide at week six using the category, not the total
process.description: Count the marks lost in the targeted category in both scripts. A total that rose while the category is unchanged is not progress; a total that fell while the category improved is. Then take one of three outcomes: met, partial, or structural problem. Another term in hope is not one of them.

whyPoints.title: Six weeks, not a term

whyPoints.title: One target, deliberately
whyPoints.description: A block aimed at three things produces a result nobody can interpret, whichever way it goes. One category per block is a technical requirement rather than a commercial limit, and the second target gets the next block measured against a better baseline.

whyPoints.title: A repeatable instrument from the official site
whyPoints.description: Board past papers and published mark schemes, downloaded from Cambridge or Pearson, under identical conditions both times. School reports, mocks and teacher-written tests cannot be repeated and therefore cannot measure anything over time.

faqs.question: Why six-week blocks rather than a term for a Reach British School pupil?
faqs.answer: Because six weeks is the shortest period that produces an interpretable answer, and a term is a billing convention rather than an educational unit. Four weeks of focused work with a measurement at each end is long enough for a habit to become automatic enough to appear under timing, and short enough that being wrong about the diagnosis costs an affordable amount. A habit that has not formed in four weeks of deliberate drilling rarely forms in twelve, so the extra weeks add cost without adding information.

faqs.question: What makes a baseline repeatable, and why does that matter so much?
faqs.answer: It has to be an instrument that can be run again identically, which rules out most of what families reach for. A school report is a judgement. A mock is one performance under conditions that will not recur. A teacher-written topic test cannot be re-sat without the pupil remembering it. What works is a board past paper from the official Cambridge or Pearson site: two papers from different series at the same tier are close enough to compare and different enough that nothing is recalled. Without that property, nothing before and after means anything.

faqs.question: Why only one target when my child is weak in several areas?
faqs.answer: Because a block aimed at four things produces a result nobody can read. If the marks move, nobody knows which intervention did it; if they do not, nobody knows which one failed, so the next six weeks begins with no more information than the first. One category per block is a technical requirement rather than meanness. The other categories are still there in six weeks and they become the next block's target, measured against a baseline that now includes a known improvement.

faqs.question: What should we see by week three if the block is working?
faqs.answer: Behaviour, not marks. A habit has to become automatic before it appears under timing, so week three is usually too early for the numbers to move. What should have changed is the pupil's unprompted behaviour in their own written work: method written out without being asked, units attached, the question re-read, the analysis sentence present. A parent can check that with no subject knowledge by putting a week-three piece beside a week-zero one and looking for the targeted behaviour.

faqs.question: What if the targeted behaviour is missing at week three?
faqs.answer: Then one of three specific things is wrong, and all three are fixable at week three rather than week six. The target was never actually agreed with the pupil, so they do not know what to do differently - test this by asking them to state it unprompted. The between-session work is not being done, so the habit gets four repetitions a month rather than fifteen. Or the sessions have drifted onto content, because teaching a topic is more comfortable than running a drill. Ask about all three.

faqs.question: How should the week-five re-test be set up?
faqs.answer: Identically to the baseline in every respect except the paper itself. A different past paper from a different series at the same tier, from the official board site. The same timing, the same room, the same time of day, the same absence of interruptions, the same marker using the same published scheme with no allowance for effort. In Abu Dhabi that usually means a weekend morning both times, because weekday evenings after a long run from Al Shamkha or Khalifa City are not comparable to anything.

faqs.question: Should we compare the paper totals or something else?
faqs.answer: The marks lost in the targeted category, every time. Totals move for reasons unrelated to the work: a paper that happened to feature a strong topic, a question style the pupil likes, a good or bad morning. Two patterns catch families out. A total that fell while the targeted category improved is a successful block - the pupil installed a habit and met a harder paper. A total that rose while the category is unchanged is not, because nothing has been learned that will survive June.

faqs.question: What are the legitimate outcomes at week six?
faqs.answer: Exactly three. The target is met, in which case the block ends and either a new target begins or the arrangement stops. The target has moved partially, in which case one further block on the same target is reasonable with a stated expectation. Or the target has not moved at all, which means something structural is wrong - the diagnosis, the match, or the between-session work - and continuing on the same basis is not an option. Another term in hope is not one of the three.

faqs.question: Does the pupil need to know they are being measured?
faqs.answer: They should know the target and not feel judged by the instrument, which is a presentation matter rather than a trivial one. A fifteen-year-old told that six weeks of work is about to be assessed will perform worse than one asked to sit a practice paper. The measurement belongs to the adults. What the pupil should own is the target, stated in their own words, and the knowledge at week six that the marks they were drilling for did in fact appear, which is evidence that effort maps onto outcome.

faqs.question: Why does the log have to be written down?
faqs.answer: Because memory reconstructs a block favourably by week six, and the decision then becomes a negotiation rather than a reading. One page covers it: the baseline paper and conditions with losses by category, the target in the pupil's own words, one line a week on whether the behaviour appeared, the re-test in the same fields, and the decision with its reason. It also catches scope creep, which is invisible without a record, and it is readable by a head of department in two minutes.

faqs.question: Should the block shorten close to the exams?
faqs.answer: Yes. In the eight to twelve weeks before the June series the useful unit is two or three weeks rather than six: a timed paper, the errors re-worked immediately, another timed paper. Nothing is being installed at that point, so the long shape has no purpose, and a six-week block started in April finishes after the examination. The other calendar point worth planning around is Ramadan, where it overlaps revision: sessions move to a post-Iftar slot rather than pausing for six weeks.

faqs.question: Can this protocol be used for a Diploma internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the criterion letters as the instrument instead of a paper. A draft scored against the lettered criteria and their stated mark allocations at week zero, four weeks of feedback and the student's own redrafting, and a re-score at week five using the same criteria. The rule that makes it legitimate is absolute: nothing the tutor writes enters the draft at any point. Feedback names what a criterion wants and is missing; it does not supply the text. The student redrafts, the tutor re-scores.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Mohammed Bin Zayed City or Al Shamkha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For this protocol the format helps: the marked script is annotated together on a shared screen, and a session is never lost to a Shamkha corridor delay, which matters when the comparison depends on the re-test happening in the week it was planned for.

faqs.question: What should we ask for before the first block starts?
faqs.answer: Four things, all before any money is agreed. The two past paper references that will serve as baseline and re-test, from the official board site. The conditions both will be sat under, written down. The single target, phrased in words your child can repeat. And the log, shared with you rather than held by the provider. A provider who will not supply all four at week zero has told you how week six is going to be assessed, and it will not be with numbers.

intro.heading: How a parent can tell whether tutoring is working, before the results arrive
paragraphs: Tutoring is bought on hope and reviewed on results, which leaves a gap of several months in which nobody actually knows anything. That gap is where most of the money in this market is wasted. A family paying AED 250 an hour for six months has committed a substantial sum on the strength of a child saying the sessions are helpful, which is not evidence and is not the child's fault. The alternative is to decide in advance what evidence would count and then collect it weekly.

This is not a hard problem, and the materials already exist. A marked paper has a mark, a mark scheme and a set of specific losses. An internal assessment has a criterion grid and a sequence of drafts. A weekly session can produce a one-paragraph written record naming what was targeted and what was set. Put together, those three give a family something to review at week six rather than at results day, and they make the decision to continue or to stop a decision rather than a guess.

The pattern of losses is remarkably stable, which is what makes the evidence readable. A candidate who drops marks on explain questions in Biology drops them on explain questions in Chemistry too. A student who omits units in one mole calculation omits them in all of them. A Year 11 who never writes the method line loses the same two marks on every structured question in every paper. Those are countable, they are visible on a script, and they either reduce over six weeks or they do not.

What is not evidence, and is routinely presented as though it were, deserves naming. A satisfaction percentage with no sample size, a star rating with no countable reviews, a claim about typical grade improvement with no method: competitor pages measured for this project in October 2026 carried all of those, one showing two different review totals on the same page. None of it tells a parent anything about their own child. No statistic of that kind appears anywhere on this page.

Two things to state plainly before the detail. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India. And no grade, score or improvement is promised here, by any amount of evidence; what is promised is that the evidence will exist and will be shown to you whether it is flattering or not. That is a lower claim than most of this market makes and a considerably more useful one, because it is the only claim a parent can check for themselves at week six.

An internal assessment carries a criterion grid and a draft sequence

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-repton-scho.programmesIntro: Repton School Abu Dhabi runs a British-curriculum pathway with post-16 routes, so three stages carry evidence in different forms. What counts as proof of progress differs sharply between them.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external examination, so the evidence has to come from school assessments and from work the student produces at home. This is the stage where a weekly written record matters most, because a report card arriving twice a year is not a feedback loop and cannot show whether something changed in October. The skills to watch are formula rearrangement, written structure and the habit of showing method.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi these years carry the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the licensed curriculum, under the federal requirement overseen by the Ministry of Education. Arabic is frequently the first line on a report where an expatriate parent cannot judge whether progress is real, which makes a tutor's written record more useful there than in any other subject on the timetable.

programmes.name: GCSE and IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Terminal assessment with published component weightings and syllabus codes that decide the paper set: Cambridge 0580 and 0980 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, and Pearson 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Because the assessment is a paper, the evidence is also a paper, which makes these the easiest two years in which to measure whether tutoring is doing anything. A mock is the single most valuable document a family holds.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE set carries a regulatory consequence for a UAE resident. Ministry of Education equivalency for British-curriculum students counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five. One page ranking in this market states the figure as six subjects; it is five, and acting on the wrong number costs a real option slot.

programmes.name: A Level sixth form
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, where the step up from GCSE is steepest in Mathematics and the sciences and is usually misread as a motivation problem. The evidence here is the first marked assessment of the autumn term, which is genuinely diagnostic because it is the first time the new style of question has been tested. Families who wait for a January report have lost a term of readable signal.
programmes.countryNote: Equivalency on the A Level route requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than grade E, or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, in addition to the five GCSE or IGCSE passes. Abu Dhabi families most often meet this at the attestation stage, which is late enough to be a problem rather than a choice, so it belongs in a Year 11 conversation.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity-Activity-Service. The evidence trail here is richer than anywhere else in school education, because every subject has an internal assessment marked against published criteria and every internal assessment has drafts. A family that keeps the drafts has a documented record of exactly what improved and when. UAE candidates sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site, which returns an error to automated checking. Every IB date should come from the school's Diploma coordinator rather than from a published summary, including this one. The internal deadlines matter more to a family than the external ones in any case.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-for-repton-scho.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by the loss that shows up on a marked script, because that is the thing a session targets and the thing a six-week record should show reducing.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: The visible loss is the unwritten method line: a correct answer with no working scores less than the scheme allows. Behind it sit bearings, upper and lower bounds, similar-shape ratios and premature rounding. All four are countable on a script, which makes this the easiest subject in which to prove or disprove progress over six weeks.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: The loss is a missing stated definition before an explanation, which costs the first of three marks every time it happens. Circuits and electromagnetic induction concentrate the rest. Counting the explain questions on a mock and the marks earned on each gives a baseline that can be re-measured on the next paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: The loss is units omitted from calculations and practical descriptions nobody could follow. Both are binary on a script: either the unit is there or it is not. That makes chemistry the clearest evidence subject of the three sciences, because the first fortnight of work either eliminates the error or it does not.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The loss is answering the wrong command term, which is measurable by going through a marked paper and separating losses into content and verb. Most students are surprised by the split. Graph interpretation and experimental design make up the remainder and respond to a short block of targeted work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper concentrates the evidence, and the dominant loss is again method never written down. Higher Level adds proof and complex numbers, where a missing justification line costs more than an arithmetic slip. A marked paper with the method marks circled is the cheapest diagnostic available.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms separate Higher Level grades, and data-based questions reward reading the axis labels before the stem. The internal assessment produces the richest evidence trail in the subject, because each draft can be scored against the published criteria and the movement between drafts is visible.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: A Level · DP HL and SL
subjects.description: A mislabelled or wrongly shifted diagram is the countable loss, and it recurs because students draw from memory rather than from the question. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is quantitative and is the clearest separator between a five and a seven. The evaluation paragraph is the other measurable item: written or not written.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IGCSE · A Level · DP HL and SL
subjects.description: The loss is structural rather than linguistic, and it is visible in an essay plan: a tour of the text rather than a sustained argument. Progress is measurable by marking plans rather than finished essays, which is faster and gives a weekly artefact instead of a fortnightly one.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Business Management
subjects.levels: IGCSE · A Level · DP HL and SL
subjects.description: The countable loss is a tool applied without the organisation's own figures, which can be marked by circling every number the student used from the case. At Diploma Higher Level the pre-released case study is the evidence item, and under-preparation of it shows up immediately in a timed answer.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools alongside the licensed curriculum. Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed guidance and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. For a parent who does not read the language, the tutor's written record is the only available evidence.

sections.heading: What evidence of progress actually looks like week by week
paragraphs: Evidence has to be decided in advance or it will not exist. The useful move at the start of an arrangement is to agree three things: what artefact each week will produce, what will be counted on it, and when the review happens. Without that, week six arrives with nothing to look at except a child's opinion and a tutor's reassurance, and neither is a basis for spending another three thousand dirhams.

The artefacts are ordinary and already exist in the school's own cycle. A marked class assessment, a homework task returned with comments, a timed question done in the session, a draft of an internal assessment, a set of past-paper answers with the losses circled. What turns any of these into evidence is counting something consistently: the number of explain questions answered as descriptions, the number of calculations missing units, the number of method lines absent, the criterion band awarded on a draft.

The table sets out a six-week shape for a typical arrangement. It is a format rather than a case study, and no claim is made about what any particular student achieves, because an outcome claim without a sample size and a method is not information. What the table does show is what a family should expect to be able to read at the end of six weeks, and what to ask for if it is not arriving. If week four produces no comparable paper and week six produces no written summary, the arrangement is not evidence-led regardless of how the sessions felt.

sections.heading: The marked paper is the only unit of evidence that settles arguments
paragraphs: Everything else in this market is contestable. A child says the sessions are useful. A tutor says the student is engaging well. A report says progress is satisfactory. None of those three statements can be checked against anything, and all three are routinely true while a grade stays exactly where it was. A marked paper is different: it has a number, the number came from a published scheme, and the losses are individually visible.

Using it properly means marking for categories rather than for a total. A total tells you where the student is; the categories tell you why. Go through the script and label every lost mark as one of four things: content the student did not know, a verb they answered wrongly, a convention they omitted, or time they ran out of. Add them up. Most families find the content column is the smallest of the four, which is both surprising and useful, because the other three are faster to fix.

The second discipline is comparability. Two papers from the same specification and tier, marked the same way, six weeks apart, give a readable comparison. A class test against a past paper does not, and nor does a paper the student had seen before. This is why an early mock matters so much: it is the first genuinely comparable baseline a family gets, and treating it as a rehearsal rather than a diagnostic wastes the most useful document of the year.
bullets: Label every lost mark: content, verb, convention or time

sections.heading: Grade movement, and how to tell it from noise
paragraphs: A mark that goes up is not automatically progress. Papers differ in difficulty, a student can have a good day, a familiar topic can inflate a result, and a single assessment carries real random variation. Families who treat every mark as a signal end up changing tutors, subjects and strategies on noise, which is both expensive and demoralising for the student.

The way through this is not statistical sophistication; it is counting the right thing. A loss category is far less noisy than a total mark. If a student omitted units in nine calculations in week one and in one calculation in week four, that is a real change regardless of what the overall marks did, because the behaviour is directly observable and not subject to paper difficulty. Loss counts move before totals do, which is also why they are the better early signal.

The table sets out what to treat as signal and what to discount. The practical rule underneath it is that two consistent movements in the same direction, on comparable material, mean something, and one does not. Six weeks is long enough to see the first and short enough to be worth reviewing at. A family unwilling to stop an arrangement at week six on the evidence is not really collecting evidence; they are collecting reassurance. The uncomfortable corollary is that a tutor should be willing to say when the evidence is flat, and the ones who do are the ones worth keeping.

sections.heading: The internal assessment draft trail as documented progress
paragraphs: An internal assessment is the richest evidence item in a Diploma or a coursework-bearing A Level, because it is marked against published criteria that both the student and the family can read. Scored at each draft, it produces a record of exactly which criterion moved and when, and that record is far more informative than any grade prediction.

The method is simple and it is the student's own work throughout. Draft one is scored honestly against the descriptors, usually badly, and the lowest criterion is identified. The student revises that criterion and only that criterion. Draft two is scored again. The movement, or the absence of it, is the evidence. Doing this across three drafts typically moves two criteria substantially and makes the remaining weakness obvious, which is a far better position than a single panicked rewrite in the final fortnight.

The trail matters for a second reason that is worth stating plainly. A documented sequence of the student's own drafts, each with the tutor's criterion-level feedback and the student's own revisions, is also the evidence that the work is theirs. That protects the student if a question is ever raised, and it is exactly what a purchased internal assessment cannot produce. A tutor who contributes text destroys the trail as well as breaking the rules, which is why the honest method and the defensible method turn out to be the same method here rather than a compromise between two.

sections.heading: The reporting you should receive, and what to do if it does not arrive
paragraphs: A written record after every session is not an administrative nicety; it is the mechanism by which a family holds an arrangement accountable. It needs four things and nothing more: what was covered, what loss was being targeted, what was set for the week, and what the tutor still considers weak. Four sentences is enough. A paragraph of encouragement is not a record and should be identified as what it is.

What to do if it does not arrive is the useful half of this. Ask for it once, in writing, specifying the four items. A tutor working from marked scripts will produce it without difficulty, because they already know all four answers. A tutor who cannot produce it is either not reading the student's work or is working without a plan, and in both cases the arrangement is less than a family is paying for. That is a decision available at week two rather than week twenty.

The same principle applies to the school side. A family is entitled to ask the subject teacher what specifically changed in the student's work, rather than whether progress is being made. The second question gets a courteous non-answer; the first gets a usable one. Between the school's answer and the tutor's weekly record, a parent in Abu Dhabi can assemble a genuinely informative picture without waiting for a report cycle. Neither request is unreasonable and neither takes anybody more than a few minutes to answer, which is why the refusal rather than the answer is the informative outcome.

sections.heading: Online delivery and the Al Reem evening, costed honestly
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement depends on a slot that actually holds every week, which is where the logistics of this part of Abu Dhabi matter. Al Reem's exit onto the main crossing in the late afternoon is slow, and a tutor driving in to a five o'clock appointment is committing a large part of their evening to one hour of teaching. That is why the local in-home band is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, against a market band of AED 150 to 450 for qualified to specialist work online.

The cost that matters more for evidence, though, is the lost session. Families with travelling tutors commonly lose two or three sessions in a twenty-eight-session term to traffic, weather or an overrun. Each loss breaks the chain of comparable weekly artefacts, which is exactly the thing the whole method depends on. A video session fails only when the student or the tutor is genuinely unavailable, and it can move by an hour rather than being cancelled.

The third cost is the tutor pool. Travel restricts the choice to whoever drives to this part of the island at that hour, and for a particular specification or component that radius may contain nobody with marking experience. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. What a family here buys instead is a specialist matched nationally, teaching on Gulf Standard Time, with the weekly record intact.

sections.heading: The series calendar read as a set of evidence deadlines
paragraphs: Exam calendars are usually presented as dates to fear. Read as evidence deadlines they are more useful, because each milestone is a point at which a family either has a readable document or does not. The entry deadline is the last moment at which the evidence can change a decision about tier or subject. The mock is the first comparable baseline. The coursework submission is the end of the draft trail.

The calendar facts for a UAE candidate are specific. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not an option here, and guidance suggesting a spring sitting describes another country's timetable. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone version of the timetable is essential, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

The dates worth citing precisely are historical, because those can be checked. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the day after; November 2025 results arrived with students on 22 January 2026. Future windows are named by month only here, deliberately, since provisional timetables are revised and a pinned future date makes a page wrong without anyone editing it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why the draft trail is also the protection
paragraphs: Assessed work has to be the student's own, and the consequences of a breach fall on the student rather than on anyone selling help. That is the principle. The practical version, on an evidence-led page, is that the draft trail which proves progress is the same document that proves authorship, so the honest method and the defensible method are identical.

What a tutor can do is the whole of the service. Read the published criteria with the student and explain what each descriptor awards. Press on a research question until it is answerable within the limit. Teach the statistical test, the laboratory technique or the referencing convention the piece requires. Score a draft the student wrote and name the criterion costing marks. Rehearse the supervisor conversation. Every one of those leaves the student's work untouched and the trail intact.

What a tutor cannot do is contribute to the submission: no text, no redraft into final form, no data presented as collected, no edit that leaves the work substantially someone else's. One operation ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price. Beyond the rule, that purchase destroys the only evidence the student has that the work is theirs, which is a bad trade at any price. The self-test is whether the student could explain every sentence of their own submission, unprompted, to the person supervising it. If they could not, the line has been crossed whoever crossed it, and the repair is to return to the last draft that was genuinely theirs and continue from there.

process.title: Send a marked script with the enquiry
process.description: One mock paper, class assessment or returned homework tells a specialist more in five minutes than a long description does. A parent's account is usually right about the symptom and wrong about the cause, and the script shows the cause. It also means the first session starts from a named loss rather than from introductions.

process.title: Agree what will be counted, before session one
process.description: Decide which loss category is being tracked and on what artefact. Units omitted, explain questions answered as descriptions, method lines missing, criterion band on a draft: one of these, counted consistently, is worth more than a general plan to improve. It also makes a week-six review possible rather than theoretical.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson to test the diagnosis
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor, no payment and no card. Ask them to name the recurring loss from the script and to separate what is convention from what is foundation. A tutor who can do both is worth paying for; one who offers general revision has told you what the next six months would look like.

process.title: Review at week six, with the records in front of you
process.description: Six written notes, two comparable marked papers and a loss count. Read them together and make a decision: continue, change focus, change tutor, or stop. The point of the evidence is that stopping is a live option, and an arrangement where it is not is not being reviewed.

process.title: Keep the drafts, every one of them
process.description: For any internal assessment, Extended Essay or coursework piece, keep each dated draft with the feedback attached. That sequence is the record of progress and the record of authorship simultaneously, and it is the one document that cannot be reconstructed afterwards if a question is ever raised.

whyPoints.title: A written record after every session
whyPoints.description: What was covered, what loss was targeted, what was set, and what is still weak. Four sentences, every week, so that a six-week review has something specific to read. A paragraph of encouragement is not a record, and this page says so rather than leaving a family to work it out at month five.

whyPoints.title: Progress measured on loss counts, not on impressions
whyPoints.description: A loss category is far less noisy than a total mark, because the behaviour is directly observable and independent of paper difficulty. Counting units omitted or verbs answered wrongly gives an early signal that a mark total cannot, and it is the one measure a parent can verify themselves on a script.

whyPoints.title: No outcome claims of any kind
whyPoints.description: No grade, score or improvement is promised here, and no satisfaction percentage, review count or star rating appears, because none could be evidenced with a sample size, a date and a method. Competitor pages measured for this project carried all three, one showing two different review totals on the same page.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a specification, by someone who marks it
whyPoints.description: An evidence-led arrangement needs a tutor who can mark against the scheme that actually applies, which means matching on the specification and component rather than the subject name. A good teacher who has not seen the specification can teach the content and still misread the script.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery keeps the weekly chain unbroken
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Beyond the rate, the practical gain is that a video slot can move by an hour rather than being lost, which is what protects a comparable weekly record.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and names no school here as a client. Mark schemes, past papers and subject guides are referenced and linked rather than copied.

faqs.question: How will we know whether the tutoring is working before results come out?
faqs.answer: By deciding in advance what would count and collecting it weekly. Three things do the work: a short written note after every session naming the loss being targeted, two comparable marked papers six weeks apart, and a count of one specific loss category on each artefact. Read together at week six, those give a decision rather than an impression. An arrangement where stopping is not a live option at week six is not being reviewed, it is being hoped for.

faqs.question: What exactly should be in the written note after each session?
faqs.answer: Four items and nothing else: what was covered, what loss was being targeted, what was set for the week, and what the tutor still considers weak. Four sentences is sufficient. A paragraph of general encouragement is not a record. A tutor working from marked scripts produces this without difficulty because they already know all four answers, which is why asking for it once in writing is itself a useful diagnostic at week two.

faqs.question: How should we mark a mock paper to get something useful out of it?
faqs.answer: Mark for categories, not for a total. Go through the script and label every lost mark as one of four things: content the student did not know, a command term answered wrongly, a convention omitted such as a unit or a method line, or marks lost to running out of time. Then add the columns up. Most families find the content column is the smallest of the four, which is useful because the other three are faster to fix.

faqs.question: A mark went up on one paper. Is that progress?
faqs.answer: Probably not on its own. Papers differ in difficulty, students have good days, a familiar topic inflates a result, and a single assessment carries genuine random variation. One movement is not a signal. Two consistent movements in the same direction on comparable material are. Loss counts are the better early measure because they are directly observable and independent of paper difficulty, and they move before totals do, which makes them the useful thing to track.

faqs.question: Which marked work is worth comparing and which should be discounted?
faqs.answer: Compare like with like: two papers from the same specification and tier, marked the same way, several weeks apart. Discount anything the student had seen before, because recall is not what is being measured, and treat a class test against a past paper as non-comparable. This is why an early mock matters so much: it is the first genuinely comparable baseline a family holds, and treating it as a rehearsal rather than a diagnostic wastes the best document of the year.

faqs.question: How does scoring an internal assessment draft actually work?
faqs.answer: The student writes draft one unaided. The tutor scores it honestly against the published descriptors, usually finding a low band somewhere, and names the single lowest criterion and why. The student revises that criterion and only that criterion. Draft two is re-scored against the same descriptors, and the movement is the evidence. Across three drafts this typically shifts two criteria substantially and makes the remaining weakness obvious, which is a much better position than one rewrite in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Why does keeping every draft matter beyond the marks?
faqs.answer: Because a dated sequence of the student's own drafts, each with criterion-level feedback and the student's own revisions, is simultaneously the record of progress and the evidence of authorship. It protects the student if a question is ever raised about whose work it is, and it is precisely what a purchased piece of coursework cannot produce. A tutor who contributes text destroys that trail as well as breaking the rules, which makes it a bad trade twice over.

faqs.question: What should we ask our child's subject teacher at Repton to get a usable answer?
faqs.answer: Ask what specifically changed in the work, rather than whether progress is being made. The second question gets a courteous non-answer because it invites a judgement; the first invites an observation and usually gets one. Follow it with what they would want to see in the next piece of work. Between that answer and a tutor's weekly written record, a parent can assemble an informative picture without waiting for a report cycle to come round.

faqs.question: Does an in-home tutor make the weekly record harder to maintain?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality. Families with travelling tutors commonly lose two or three sessions in a twenty-eight-session term to traffic, weather or an overrun, and each loss breaks the chain of comparable weekly artefacts that the method depends on. Al Reem's exit onto the main crossing is slow in the late afternoon. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at all; a video slot can move by an hour rather than being cancelled.

faqs.question: What do in-home and online tutoring actually cost in this part of Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market in-home rates are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is inside the fee, with Bestimate's survey at AED 180 to 350 and local home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Online, a qualified subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and a specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Each figure belongs to the provider named, not to IB Gram.

faqs.question: When is the first point at which evidence can still change an exam decision?
faqs.answer: The final entry deadline, which falls months before any paper is sat and is held by the school's examinations officer rather than the parent. Up to that point, marked work on supplementary content can support a case for an Extended rather than a Core entry, or for adding a subject. After it closes, changes are difficult and sometimes impossible. Ask the school for the date entries lock and treat that as the real deadline rather than the exam itself.

faqs.question: Which exam series is available to a UAE candidate for a resit?
faqs.answer: November, for both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates; its February and March series is offered to India only, so any guidance pointing an Abu Dhabi family at a spring sitting describes another country's timetable. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, so confirm the zone with the examinations officer before working from dates.

faqs.question: How quickly should a convention error disappear from the evidence?
faqs.answer: Within two or three weeks if it is genuinely a convention. Units omitted from calculations, method lines absent, a definition not stated before an explanation: these are habits, and a student who is shown the cost and given a checking routine usually stops within a fortnight. If the same convention error appears in week one and week six, something is wrong with the method or the tutor, and that is a decision the evidence has made for you rather than a judgement call.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of a coursework piece if the deadline is tomorrow?
faqs.answer: No, at any price and under any deadline pressure. A tutor can score the draft against the published criteria, name the criterion costing marks, teach the method the piece needs and rehearse the supervisor meeting. A tutor cannot contribute text, redraft into a final version or supply data. One operation ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments; the thing that purchase risks is the student's entire qualification, and it also destroys the draft trail that proves authorship.

faqs.question: What should a six-week review conclude if the evidence is flat?
faqs.answer: That something must change, and the options are specific rather than general. Change the loss being targeted, because the wrong one may have been chosen. Change the artefact, because the measure may be too noisy. Change the tutor, if a convention error has not shifted in six weeks. Or stop, if the honest reading is that the student is not doing the work between sessions, which no arrangement can purchase on their behalf. All four are better than continuing unexamined.

faqs.question: Does Abu Dhabi's regulator publish anything a family can use as evidence?
faqs.answer: Yes, about the school rather than the child. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Read them on ADEK's own site rather than an aggregator, since aggregated ratings go stale and band vocabulary differs between emirates. Across the competitor pages measured for this project, ADEK was named by nobody. Dubai sits with KHDA, Sharjah with SPEA, and three emirates with the federal Ministry.

From there the arrangement produces a written note each week, so week six is a decision rather than a guess. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Distance is the one variable that stopped mattering
paragraphs: A parent in Al Reef searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Abu Dhabi is asking a reasonable question that the search engine answers badly. What comes back is a distance-sorted list: directory entries, tuition centres with a map pin, agency landing pages that mention the district without covering it, and individuals advertising on classified sites. Sorted by kilometres. None of those columns is the one that predicts whether a grade moves.

The variables that do predict it are the exam board and syllabus code, whether the tutor teaches the specific component failing, whether they can hold a recurring evening slot through February to April, and whether they mark the student's own written work against the published scheme. Proximity correlates with none of them, and in an emirate this spread out it actively works against them. Abu Dhabi runs from the island through Khalifa City and Al Raha out to Al Shamkha, Al Samha and Al Reef. A ten-kilometre radius around Al Reef contains very few people who teach Higher Level Chemistry.

That is the practical case for the delivery model on this page, and it is a trade rather than a free gain. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi — that is a service we run only in India — and lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. What a family gives up is an adult physically in the room, which matters for a nine-year-old and matters very little for a Year 11 student working on Pearson 4PH1 Paper 1. What a family gets back is the whole pool instead of the nearby slice of it.

So this page spends its length on the things distance was standing in for. It maps the districts against commute reality, because the school run is what actually decides when a session can start. It names the subjects with thin coverage across the UAE rather than promising everything. It explains what the Department of Education and Knowledge governs in this emirate, because ADEK is mentioned by none of the competitor pages researched for this project and parents are regularly told things about it that are not true.

It also covers two things families searching this phrase usually have further down the list and will need: the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement that runs alongside an international curriculum in UAE private schools, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether a set of IGCSE grades is recognised here. Neither has anything to do with how near a tutor lives, and both change decisions about subject choice that are made in Year 10 and cannot easily be undone in Year 11. One of them is published incorrectly by a site currently outranking this one, which is the sort of gap worth filling properly.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Which programme your child is on changes what a local search should be looking for. These are the four running in Abu Dhabi private schools, with the staffing reality behind each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The best-supplied level in the emirate. Maths, English, Biology, Business Studies and Economics can all be covered by tutors who live within a short drive of most Abu Dhabi districts. The harder asks are Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606 and the top end of Physics and Chemistry Extended, where local supply thins quickly outside the island.
programmes.countryNote: The board matters more than the postcode. Abu Dhabi schools split between Cambridge and Pearson, sometimes within one science department, and a tutor who assumes the wrong one will drill an alternative-to-practical paper a Pearson candidate never sits. Establish the code on the entry sheet before anything else, including location.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where proximity breaks down completely. Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, means a student may need two or three specialists rather than one generalist. The probability that all of them live near you is low in any city and very low across Abu Dhabi's geography.
programmes.countryNote: Most Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates sit the May session, which concentrates demand into January to April. A family that books a nearby generalist in September and discovers in February that Higher Level Maths needs a specialist is competing for slots at the worst possible moment.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with no external paper in most schools. Supply is reasonable because the work is criterion-matching rather than board-specific. A tutor needs the school's own assessment task and the published criterion descriptors, not a past paper archive.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, so those students never sit an IGCSE paper. Searching for an 'IGCSE tutor near me' for such a child produces the wrong match entirely; what they need is exam-condition practice before Year 12 begins.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The one level where proximity has a genuine argument behind it, because a young child often needs an adult physically present rather than on a screen. No external assessment applies, so the work is number fluency, reading stamina and written structure rather than paper technique.
programmes.countryNote: Families with a primary-age child should treat the free trial lesson as the decisive test rather than as a formality. Some children engage with a screen for thirty minutes and some do not, and no amount of tutor quality changes that. Where the answer is no, an in-person arrangement locally is the better route and we will say so.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: What each Diploma subject needs from a tutor, and how easily that is found in the UAE. The scarcity column is the one a distance-sorted search cannot show you.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs someone fluent in Higher Level Paper 3, where two extended problems build on each other and an early slip propagates through both. Supply across the UAE is reasonable at Standard Level and noticeably thinner at Higher Level, which is the single most-requested specialism in Abu Dhabi.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs organic pathway fluency and the ability to question an Internal Assessment research design before data collection. Higher Level supply is thin across the whole country, not just this emirate, which is the clearest case on this page for ignoring distance entirely.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Needs someone who marks for units, significant figures and uncertainty rather than for the final number, and who insists a principle is stated before any algebra. Higher Level supply is thin; Standard Level is manageable within Abu Dhabi.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The best-supplied Diploma science in the emirate. Command-term work and data-based question technique do most of the grade movement here, and both are widely taught, so a local match is realistic if that is what a family wants.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Needs diagram discipline — labelled, titled, referred to in the prose — plus evaluation technique and, at Higher Level, quantitative handling. Supply is good on the island and thinner in the mainland communities, which is a district-level gap rather than a national one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Needs case-study application rather than definitions, and drilling on the quantitative content: ratios, break-even and cash-flow forecasting. Reasonably supplied across Abu Dhabi, including the Khalifa City corridor.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Needs unseen analysis technique and Individual Oral preparation, where a precisely stated global issue has to be traced through both an extract and a literary work. Well supplied in this emirate at both levels.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The thinnest supply of any Diploma subject in the UAE. Needs pseudocode convention work, documented testing in the solution development stage, and a Higher Level case study read months ahead. Searching by distance for this subject returns essentially nothing useful.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Needs calculator-evidence discipline and statistical interpretation in context, since an unexplained output earns the calculation mark and nothing more. Supply sits between Analysis and Approaches and the sciences.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandated alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools and ignored by almost every tutoring site in this market. Local supply is the strongest of any subject here, which makes it the one case where a near-me search genuinely works.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same scarcity question at IGCSE level, where supply is generally better and the gaps are narrower but still real.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980, Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The deepest supply in the emirate; a local match is entirely realistic. What a tutor must know is which code and which tier, because the grade ceilings differ and the 2025 Cambridge revision added a non-calculator paper that caught out a cohort.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Reasonable supply for Core, thinner for Extended at the top of the range. The tutor needs to know whether the student sits Cambridge's separate practical component or Pearson's papers, which examine practical skills internally with no separate component.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Similar to Physics. The qualitative-analysis tables and the alternative-to-practical paper are the coachable parts and the parts most commonly taught badly, so ask a prospective tutor to describe how they teach them.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Good supply across Abu Dhabi. Extended physiology answers need sequence and named structures, and magnification and surface-area calculations appear almost every series while being routinely skipped in revision.

igcseSubjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Good supply. The constraint is marking capacity rather than availability — this subject generates the heaviest marking load at IGCSE, so confirm whether marking between sessions is inside the rate.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Adequate supply on the island and thin in Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Shamkha. Short engagements work here: diagram labelling and evaluation technique recover marks faster than content coverage does.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Adequate supply emirate-wide. The calculation questions are the fastest marks to recover and the ones most often left blank, which makes the first three sessions the most productive of any engagement.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Thin supply at IGCSE as well as Diploma. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are quick wins; the programming component justifies a longer engagement. Distance-based searching for this subject in Abu Dhabi returns little.

regions.note: Central island addresses with the shortest school runs in the emirate. A 16:30 or 17:00 start genuinely works here, and those are the easiest slots to book because fewer families compete for them. Local tutor supply is the densest in Abu Dhabi for Maths and English.

regions.note: High-rise living with short runs and a high rate of mid-cycle curriculum changes. Families here frequently arrive mid-year from another system, so the first session is usually a syllabus audit against the new specification rather than teaching.

regions.note: Newer international enrolment weighted heavily towards the Diploma. Internal Assessment and Extended Essay supervision dominates the requests, and those are usually booked as weekend daytime blocks rather than weekday evening slots.

regions.note: The longest bus runs in Abu Dhabi, with a working window from 18:30 to 20:00. In-home specialist supply here is close to nonexistent for Higher Level sciences and Computer Science, which makes this the catchment where removing distance from the equation changes the most.

sections.heading: What an IB IGCSE tutor near me search returns in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: The results page for this search is not a list of tutors. It is a mixture of five different things wearing the same clothes, and separating them is the first useful step a parent can take. Directory listings rank on how much a provider paid the directory. Tuition centre pages rank on having a verified map pin, which tells you about premises rather than about teaching. Agency landing pages rank on mentioning the district by name, often with no tutor in it. Classified adverts rank on recency. Blog posts with a district in the title rank on domain authority and frequently exist only to collect enquiries and sell them on.

None of those five is sorted by anything that predicts a grade. The research behind this project fetched and dissected sixty-odd competitor pages in October 2026, and the pattern was consistent: three of six commercial pages published no price at all, five of six carried no data table, one page's structured data was unparseable by Google, and one listed a school that appears not to exist. The best page in the set was 2,294 words and still refused to answer its own question about cost.

The honest reframing is to search for the component rather than the place. A parent whose child is losing marks on Cambridge 0620 mole calculations wants someone who teaches Cambridge 0620. A parent whose Year 12 child is stuck on a Higher Level Maths Exploration wants someone who has supervised Explorations against the published criteria. Those are findable. 'A good tutor nearby' is not a specification and cannot be matched against.

sections.heading: The commute, not the bell, decides when a session starts
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families book sessions at times their children cannot attend, and the cause is arithmetic rather than optimism. A school finishing at 15:00 on the island releases a student who lives in Al Reef into a bus route that can run an hour and a quarter in evening traffic. Add food and the change of clothes and the earliest honest start is 17:30, often 18:30. A 16:00 slot booked in September becomes a 16:25 start by October and a cancelled session by November.

The consequence is worse than a late start. A tutor holding a 16:00 slot that consistently begins at 16:25 either runs over into the next student's time or delivers thirty-five minutes for a sixty-minute fee, and the second is what usually happens. Across a term that is several hours of paid teaching that did not occur, and the family concludes that tutoring does not work. The fix is to book the slot the child can actually reach.

The second scheduling reality is capacity rather than time. A Year 11 student with three subjects under support cannot absorb three sessions stacked on a Tuesday, and a Diploma student cannot absorb two hours of Higher Level Maths after a full school day plus a bus. Spreading sessions across the week and keeping each one short enough to finish well is a better plan than maximising contact hours, and the family is better placed to judge that than any provider.

sections.heading: Where the specialists are not: subject coverage across the emirate
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market implies it covers everything. None of the sixty-odd competitor pages researched for this project discloses a single coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an Indian telephone number rather than stating where the tutor sits. That is the gap this section fills, because a disclosed limit is more useful to a family than an undisclosed promise.

The pattern is consistent and not specific to Abu Dhabi. Maths and English at IGCSE are deeply supplied everywhere. Biology and the commercial subjects are adequately supplied. Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches, and Computer Science at any level are thin across the whole country, and within Abu Dhabi they are concentrated on the island. Arabic is the exception that runs the other way — local supply is excellent and almost no tutoring site in this market treats it as a subject at all.

What a family should do with that depends on the subject. Where coverage is deep, a local in-person arrangement is a genuine option and we will say so rather than arguing against it. Where coverage is thin, the realistic choice is a specialist outside your district or outside the UAE, delivered over live video, with the location stated. Where nothing fits the slot you have, the answer should be that nothing fits — not a general science teacher booked against a Higher Level Paper 3 problem.
The table states the position subject by subject. It is a coverage statement, not a sales argument, and the fallback column is the part most providers would prefer not to publish.
