sections.heading: Who regulates what: ADEK, and the other four
paragraphs: Parents in this emirate are told a great deal about regulators that is not accurate, and the research behind this project found ADEK named by none of the competitor pages fetched. The position is straightforward and comes from the UAE government's own private-schools page. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge 'supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate'. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education'. In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority 'regulates private education in the emirate', as does the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the Ministry of Education 'plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools'.

What that means practically: the regulator decides whether a school may operate, which curricula it may offer, how it is inspected and what rating it publishes. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities also 'approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods', so curriculum approval sits with the emirate rather than only inspection. What the regulator does not do is set your child's grades. Cambridge Assessment International Education, Pearson Edexcel and the International Baccalaureate write the papers, publish the mark schemes and set the boundaries. A regulator rating tells you about a school; it tells you nothing about a syllabus.

Two claims to treat as warnings. First, no tutoring provider should describe itself as approved, accredited or endorsed by ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson unless it can produce the permit number, and the research for this project found claims of that kind circulating in this market with nothing at all behind them. IB Gram holds no such status and claims none. Second, a tuition business with premises and staff is licensed differently from an individual tutor — in Dubai that is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute — so a centre asserting approval can be asked for the number.

IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. It is a matching platform delivering one-to-one lessons over live video, and the regulators are described on this page as context for how Abu Dhabi schooling works rather than as any kind of endorsement.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside an international curriculum
paragraphs: Families searching for an IGCSE or IB tutor in Abu Dhabi usually arrive with an international subject in mind and then discover, often in Year 10, that their child also carries UAE-mandated subjects that will not go away. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

Across the border in Dubai, KHDA's published guidelines make the operational detail explicit, and while they are Dubai's rules rather than Abu Dhabi's, they show what the federal baseline looks like in practice. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies — combined classes for both groups are, in KHDA's words, 'strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction'. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary the length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

Two further points from the same source matter for anyone tutoring these subjects. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools must hold the relevant KHDA approval to teach them, which is a credential question a parent can ask about. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, 'the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited' — which constrains what tutoring material in these subjects may be. A tutor offering an alternative curriculum for Islamic Education is offering something the rules do not permit.

For an Abu Dhabi family the practical consequences are three. These subjects consume timetable hours that the international subjects do not get. A student weak in Arabic as an additional language carries that into a report regardless of their IGCSE grades. And, as the equivalency section below sets out, Arabic and Islamic Education sit outside the five subjects the Ministry of Education counts, which changes how a family should think about subject choice.

sections.heading: UAE equivalency: the five subjects that actually have to count
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that makes a foreign school certificate usable in the UAE, and it is one of the eighteen gaps the research for this project found competitors leaving entirely empty. It matters to a near-me search because it changes subject choice, and subject choice is settled in Year 10 — long before anybody is looking for a tutor.

On the British track, as reported when the UAE clarified its requirements, students must pass 'five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3', and must additionally submit proof of 'one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E' or 'two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade'. The detail families miss is that Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'. One site ranking in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong — publishing the correct rule is a straightforward accuracy win over a page currently outranking us.

On the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at 'a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test', '61 in the TOEFL iBT test', or '450 in the reading and writing section in the SAT test', with mathematics requiring 'at least 450 in the SAT Math test' before applying. For the IB there is no figure here to publish. The article states no IB points threshold, and ibo.org blocks automated fetching, so any IB equivalency number has to be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the emirate's attestation authority before it is relied on. We would rather print that gap than fill it with a number we cannot stand behind.

Three cautions. Equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry of Education, not something a tutoring provider performs, arranges or guarantees — descriptions of it belong on a page like this, applications belong on the official channel. Tutoring is not required for equivalency and nobody should tell you it is. And the rule as set out here was reported in July 2026, so verify the current version before making a subject decision on it.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is who the listing says they are
paragraphs: A distance-sorted list carries no verification at all, so the checking falls to the family. Four questions do most of the work, and a tutor who cannot answer them in writing has told you something useful.

Ask for the permit. A tutor based in the UAE providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing' service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, there is no cost excuse for not holding one. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount quoted at you.

Ask about the school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is understood to bar the same. That reporting is press-sourced rather than read here from the current ADEK policy document, so verify it with ADEK directly — but treat 'your child's own class teacher, privately' as the arrangement to avoid regardless.

Ask about the syllabus and ask about examiner claims. A tutor should be able to name the code they teach, describe how the components are weighted, and say where students lose marks on it; vagueness there is the only credential test that matters. On examiner status, be sceptical: nobody should be described as an IB or Cambridge examiner without current evidence, and examiner status should never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Finally, ask what happens to prepaid hours if the match changes, and ask for the cancellation terms in writing before any payment — Abu Dhabi school calendars generate clashes constantly and a loose policy becomes an argument in month two.

process.title: Replace the place with the component
process.description: Instead of a district, send the board, syllabus code, tier and the component going wrong — Cambridge 0620 Paper 4, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, or a Higher Level Maths Exploration stuck on Criterion E. That is a specification a match can be made against. 'A good tutor nearby' cannot be matched at all.

process.title: Send the window your child can actually attend
process.description: Take the earliest honest start from the regions table for your district rather than the school finish time. A 16:00 slot in Al Reef becomes a 16:25 start and then a cancellation, and the sessions lost that way are usually blamed on tutoring rather than on scheduling.

process.title: Hear the coverage answer before paying
process.description: For Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics or Computer Science, ask directly whether a specialist is free in your slot and where they are based. If the answer is nobody, that is the answer. Matching a general science teacher to a Higher Level Paper 3 problem wastes a term.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per student, no payment, no card, no commitment. It runs as a working session: the student writes something under time and the tutor marks it against the published scheme. For a primary-age child it also answers whether the format works for them at all, before any money moves.

process.title: Fix the slot and keep it through the crunch
process.description: Demand concentrates between January and April for the May and June series. A recurring slot booked in the autumn survives that; week-by-week arrangements do not, and the tutor still free in March is rarely the specialist you wanted in October.

process.title: Review against the marked evidence
process.description: Every half-term, look at the annotated scripts: which error types stopped recurring and which did not. If the marks have not moved, change the plan or end the engagement. A quiet renewal with no evidence behind it is how a year of tutoring produces nothing.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the kilometre
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the syllabus code and the failing component. A distance-sorted list optimises for the one variable that has no bearing on a grade, and in an emirate running from the island to Al Shamkha it actively narrows the pool to whoever can drive to you.

whyPoints.title: Commute reality built into the slot
whyPoints.description: The session time is set from the bus route rather than the school bell, because an Al Reef student does not reach a desk at 16:00 no matter what the timetable says. Booking the slot a child can actually attend is the difference between sixty minutes and thirty-five.

whyPoints.title: Coverage gaps published
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Physics and Computer Science are thinly supplied across the UAE, and that is written on the page. None of the sixty-odd competitor pages researched discloses a single coverage limit, and several hide non-UAE delivery behind a foreign telephone number.

whyPoints.title: ADEK explained, not invoked
whyPoints.description: The regulator table cites the UAE government's own private-schools page and separates what a regulator governs from what an awarding body decides. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or endorsement from ADEK or anyone else, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch.

whyPoints.title: The equivalency rule stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five. A site currently ranking in this market publishes six, which is wrong, and no IB points figure appears here because none could be read from an official source.

whyPoints.title: Verification questions handed to you
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE permit, the rule against tutoring a teacher's own students, naming the syllabus code, and written cancellation terms. Four questions, all answerable in writing, and a provider's reluctance to answer any of them is itself the result you were looking for.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Abu Dhabi return so few real options?
faqs.answer: Because the results are sorted by distance and most of them are not tutors. The page mixes paid directory listings, tuition centres ranking on a map pin, agency pages naming your district without staffing it, classified adverts and blog posts that exist to collect and resell enquiries. None of those columns predicts a grade. The variables that do — board, syllabus code, the specific failing component, and whether a recurring evening slot can be held — are invisible in a distance ranking. Searching for the component instead of the place produces a specification that can actually be matched.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi districts have the thinnest IGCSE subject coverage?
faqs.answer: Al Reef, Al Samha, Al Shamkha and the outer parts of the Khalifa City corridor, measured by how many subject specialists live within an evening's drive. Maths and English are fine almost everywhere in the emirate. Physics and Chemistry Extended thin out noticeably off the island, and Computer Science 0478 is close to unavailable locally in those districts. The island — Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif — is the only part of Abu Dhabi where a genuinely local specialist match is realistic across most subjects, and that is the honest version of the coverage picture.

faqs.question: Does living on Saadiyat Island or in Al Reef change which tutors we can reach?
faqs.answer: For an in-home arrangement, enormously. Saadiyat has campus-based schools and moderate runs; Al Reef has the longest bus routes in the emirate and almost no local specialist supply for Higher Level sciences. For a live video session, the district changes nothing about which tutor is available — only the slot time differs, because an Al Reef student realistically starts at 18:30 while a Saadiyat student can start at 17:00. That difference between the two answers is the clearest practical argument on this page for ignoring distance in the search.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after an Abu Dhabi school run?
faqs.answer: It depends on the district rather than on the school bell. On the island, in Al Khalidiyah or Al Bateen, 16:30 genuinely works. In the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor the earliest honest start is 17:30 and the slot that actually gets kept is 18:30. In Al Reef, Al Samha and Al Shamkha the working window is 18:30 to 20:00. Booking a 16:00 session for a child who arrives home at 16:20 produces a thirty-five-minute lesson at a sixty-minute price, every week, and the family usually blames the tutoring rather than the timetable.

faqs.question: My child's school teaches MYP rather than IGCSE. Does this page apply to us?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the difference matters enough to flag. Several Abu Dhabi schools run the IB Middle Years Programme to Year 11 and then move students straight into the Diploma, so those students never sit an IGCSE paper and searching for an IGCSE tutor produces the wrong match. MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, usually with no external paper. What that cohort needs most is exam-condition practice before Year 12 begins, because their first external timed paper will otherwise be a Diploma one in Year 13.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE and DP subjects are hardest to staff locally in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Computer Science at either level is the thinnest, followed by Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Physics, then Higher Level Maths Analysis and Approaches. Those gaps are national rather than specific to this emirate, and within Abu Dhabi the available specialists are concentrated on the island. Running the other way, Arabic as a first or additional language has the strongest local supply of any subject here and is treated as a subject by almost no tutoring site in this market. Where coverage is thin, the realistic answer is a specialist outside your district with their location stated.

faqs.question: Is a tutor fifteen minutes away better than a specialist in a different time zone?
faqs.answer: For a primary-age child, usually yes — a young student often needs an adult physically in the room, and no screen substitutes for that. For a Year 11 student losing four marks a paper on Cambridge 0620 mole calculations, no. The nearby generalist will re-teach moles pleasantly; the specialist will mark the student's own script against the published scheme and show them the line where the marks were available. A UK-based tutor finds an Abu Dhabi 18:30 a convenient mid-afternoon, so the time zone is frequently less of an obstacle than the drive.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in another emirate teach my child in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, over live video, and it is common for the scarcer subjects. The permit position is the same wherever in the UAE the tutor sits: the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 applies nationally and is granted free of charge for two years. What differs between emirates is school regulation — ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, KHDA in Dubai, SPEA in Sharjah — and that governs schools rather than tutors. A tutor in Dubai teaching an Abu Dhabi student needs the same permit as one in Al Mushrif.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor really knows my child's exam board?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the syllabus code and describe its components. Someone who teaches Cambridge 0625 will tell you there is a separate practical component worth a fifth of the grade and that it can be sat as the alternative-to-practical paper; someone who teaches Pearson 4PH1 will tell you practical skills are examined inside the written papers with no separate component. Then ask where students lose marks on that paper. Specific answers to both questions are the only credential test that matters, and vagueness on either is decisive.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi school teachers tutor their own students privately?
faqs.answer: They should not, and this is the one rule parents here most often try to work around. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct is understood to bar the same arrangement. That reporting is press-sourced rather than read here from the current ADEK document, so verify it with ADEK before relying on the exact wording. Either way, treat an offer of your child's own class teacher privately as a reason to decline.

faqs.question: What does ADEK actually do, and does it regulate private tutors?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, in the UAE government's own words. It decides whether a school may operate, which curricula it offers, how it is inspected and what rating it publishes. It does not set your child's grades — Cambridge, Pearson and the IB do that — and it does not license individual private tutors. Tutors sit under the MoHRE permit regime instead. No tutoring provider should describe itself as approved or accredited by ADEK; IB Gram holds no such status and claims none.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not towards the five subjects on the British track. When the UAE clarified its equivalency requirements, the rule was that students must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'. Those subjects remain compulsory in UAE private schools regardless, because the federal rule requires Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum. They simply sit outside the equivalency count, which is worth knowing before Year 10 subject choices are made.

faqs.question: How does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency work for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or grade 3 or better, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, and must additionally show one A Level at no less than grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One site ranking in this market tells UAE families they need six IGCSE subjects, which is incorrect. For the IB there is no points figure we can publish, because the source we read states none — check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: How long does matching a subject specialist take once we ask?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot rather than on paperwork. A Maths or English request in a 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time window is usually quick, because supply is deep. A Higher Level Chemistry or Computer Science request pinned to one weekday at 18:30 in March can take considerably longer, and in that case you hear it before paying rather than being matched with the nearest approximation. The free trial lesson comes first regardless, so the first contact is a working session rather than a commitment.

faqs.question: Does my child need Arabic alongside IGCSE in an Abu Dhabi private school?
faqs.answer: Yes. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, and every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement follows from that. The subject consumes timetable hours the international subjects do not get, and a weakness there appears on a report regardless of IGCSE grades. Local tutoring supply for Arabic is the strongest of any subject in this emirate, which makes it one case where searching near you genuinely works.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Search for the component, send the real slot
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Abu Dhabi, swap the two inputs. Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component that keeps losing marks, and send the evening window your child can genuinely sit a session in once the bus has arrived. Those two pieces of information produce a match that distance never could. The free trial lesson follows — one per student, no payment, no card, no commitment — and it runs as a working session: the student writes under time, the tutor marks against the published scheme, and you get the breakdown. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and no tutor travels to a UAE address.

intro.heading: Thirty plausible names, sorted by the wrong variable
paragraphs: Al Bandar sits in Al Raha Beach, minutes from several of Abu Dhabi's better-known schools and inside the deepest pool of teaching staff on the mainland. A near me search here returns plenty, and it sorts what it returns by distance. Distance is the one factor in this purchase with no effect on an outcome: the syllabus is set by the board, the mark scheme is published by the board, and the grade boundaries apply identically to every candidate in the emirate. Sorting by proximity is sorting by convenience and calling it a recommendation.

The second problem is that the profiles are indistinguishable. Experienced, qualified, patient, results-focused, flexible, familiar with the UAE curriculum. None of that is false and none of it is decisive. What a parent needs is a filter that eliminates most of the list quickly on evidence rather than on impression, and then a way to compare the final two or three on the same basis. That is a process problem, not a judgement problem, and process problems have published answers.

So this page is the process. It gives a four-stage funnel that takes thirty names down to two, a scorecard for running two trial sessions and comparing them on identical evidence, and a week-one checklist that surfaces a poor match inside the first two sessions rather than in the spring. It also covers the particular complication of this community, which is households running two systems at once: one child in the Diploma at a school in the Al Raha or Khalifa City belt, another sitting IGCSE, with two assessment calendars colliding in the same week.

A note on what the funnel filters for. Stage one is the fact base: the syllabus code or the IB subject and level, which comes from the school rather than from a tutor. Stage two is the permit, which is checkable in a minute. Stage three is syllabus knowledge, tested with three questions. Stage four is the trial, scored against a short list of observable behaviours. Nothing in the funnel requires a parent to know the subject, which is deliberate: a process that only works for parents who are themselves mathematicians is not a process.

And the model, stated plainly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In this part of Abu Dhabi an in-home arrangement is genuinely easy to organise, so the case for online here is selection rather than logistics, and the published rates favour it too: in-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Our trial lesson is free with no card required, and the funnel below works on us as well as on anyone else.

sections.heading: The four-stage funnel: from thirty names to two
paragraphs: Stage one is not about tutors at all. It is an email to your child's school asking for the syllabus code and tier for each IGCSE subject, or the IB subject and level, plus the exam centre and its Cambridge administrative zone where relevant. Without those facts no filtering is possible, because every subsequent question depends on knowing the right answer. This stage takes one message and eliminates nobody, which is why it is skipped and why skipping it wastes the rest.

Stage two is the permit, and it eliminates quickly. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Ask to see it. Anyone who quotes a fee for the permit itself, or who is evasive about holding one, has removed themselves from the list. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so disregard any page quoting an amount.

Stage three is three questions and it does the heavy lifting: what is each component of this course worth, name the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations where the subject has one, and where do candidates lose marks on this specific paper. Precise, immediate answers indicate someone who has prepared candidates. Generalities about confidence and motivation indicate someone who has not. Stage four is the trial, scored against the behaviours in the next section. A thirty-name list usually reaches stage four with two or three survivors, and the whole funnel costs an email, two short conversations and a free session.

sections.heading: Scoring two trial sessions on the same evidence
paragraphs: One trial produces an impression. Two trials in the same week, on the same material, produce a comparison, and a comparison is a decision. Give both tutors the same thing to work from: a marked paper, a returned piece of coursework, or a specific topic the student is stuck on. Then watch for the same behaviours in each and write down what you saw rather than how you felt.

The behaviours worth scoring are observable and require no subject knowledge. Did the tutor ask what the student already understood before explaining anything? Did they look at the actual evidence, the script or the draft, rather than talking generally about the topic? Did they watch the student work, or do the work themselves while the student watched? Did they name a specific next step, with a reason? Did they say anything they would not do, which is the test of a boundary? Did the student speak more in the second half of the session than the first?

That last one is the most reliable single indicator and the easiest to miss. A session in which the tutor's share of the talking falls as the hour progresses is a session in which the student is being made to think. A session that ends with the tutor still explaining is a lecture, and lectures are available free from a school. Score both trials on these points within an hour of each ending, while the detail is fresh, and the choice usually makes itself.

sections.heading: What the two systems demand of a tutor, and why one person rarely does both well
paragraphs: Families here often ask whether one tutor can cover a Diploma student and an IGCSE sibling. Occasionally yes, usually not, and the reason is structural rather than about talent. IGCSE mathematics on Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 is assessed entirely by written papers, so the skill being bought is paper technique: visible method, pacing, answer form, and mark-scheme fluency on a specific component. The work is short, measurable and intense.

The Diploma places about a fifth of each subject grade in work produced at home across months, which demands a different capability: supervising a piece of independent writing against published criteria without touching it, over a long period, while also teaching two or three papers. A tutor strong at one of these is not automatically strong at the other, and the second requires patience with a process rather than fluency with a mark scheme.

The calendars compound it. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in June and November, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. The Diploma's internal deadlines sit at intervals across two years and frequently land in the same weeks as an IGCSE sibling's mock season. The table sets out what each system asks of a tutor, which is also the list of things to test for separately at stage three if you are hiring for two children.

sections.heading: The week-one checklist
paragraphs: Most families discover a poor match in the spring, which is the most expensive moment to discover it. The purpose of a week-one checklist is to move that discovery forward to session two, when switching costs almost nothing. The items are deliberately concrete and all of them are things a parent can verify without sitting in the session.

After the first two sessions, you should be able to answer: has the tutor named, specifically, what is costing marks? Has that been written down anywhere? Did the student do work between the sessions, and was it marked at the start of the second? Can the student say what the next session will cover? Has the tutor mentioned the assessment calendar, whether that is the June series or an internal deadline? Has anything been measured, in units you could check against your child's own papers?

If more than two of those answers are no, raise it immediately rather than waiting. In our arrangements the tutor changes at our cost, and the review at six sessions exists as a formal backstop rather than as the first opportunity. In this community, where tutors frequently arrive by recommendation from a neighbour, the awkwardness of switching is the main reason families stay in a mismatch, and a checklist agreed in advance removes the awkwardness by making the question procedural. It also protects a good tutor, because a parent with a checklist raises specific points early instead of accumulating a vague dissatisfaction that surfaces as a cancellation three months later.

sections.heading: What a near me search cannot sort for
paragraphs: A distance sort cannot see the four things that decide whether an arrangement works. It cannot see whether the tutor has prepared candidates on your child's specific syllabus and level, which is the only form of experience that affects marks. It cannot see whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It cannot see where they will draw the line on coursework. And it cannot see whether they will make your child do the work or do it for them, which is visible in a trial session and in nothing else.

It also cannot see availability honestly. Minority Higher Level Diploma subjects, Arabic A Literature, Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Computer Science, Digital Society and Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are thin in this market, and thinner at a particular evening slot. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit, which does not mean they do not have one. Our position is to name the limit and the expected wait, and where the specialist teaching your child's syllabus is based outside the UAE we say so rather than concealing it behind a phone number, which two of the researched pages do.

One further thing the sort cannot see is what the household actually needs. Sometimes the right recommendation is not a tutor at all: a physics student losing marks to algebra needs a mathematics block, a Diploma student with secure paper technique and a weak exploration needs supervision hours, and a Year 11 student who has never sat a full past paper under time needs a weekend rather than a term. Those recommendations are worth less to a provider than a long booking, which is a fair test of whether you are being advised or sold to.

sections.heading: Two children, two systems, one protected evening
paragraphs: This is the practical problem a household in this belt most often brings. School runs here are short, so children are home early and a 16:30 or 17:00 session is viable, which gives more usable evening than most Abu Dhabi communities have. It still has to serve two students with different needs, and the usual error is to split it evenly.

The better approach allocates by where marks are being lost rather than by fairness. An IGCSE candidate eight weeks from the June series needs weekly sessions and a full timed paper at the weekend. A Diploma student in Year 1 needs fortnightly sessions with a concentrated block around an internal deadline. Those two patterns fit together in one evening slot across alternating weeks, with the weekend carrying the long work. Splitting the slot equally every week serves neither.

Two scheduling notes specific to this belt. The weekend is where full papers and coursework reviews belong, because both are two-hour jobs that no school night will hold, and in a household with two students the weekend is the only place both can have one. And frequency should fall during each school's own assessment weeks, which in a two-school household means two separate quiet periods rather than one. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan on request, and nothing renews automatically, so a planned pause costs nothing. The one arrangement to avoid is booking both children into the same hour with one tutor alternating between them, which produces half a session each and a tutor who never sees either student work for long enough to diagnose anything.

sections.heading: What we measure, and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: The unit of measurement depends on the system. For an IGCSE student it is timed questions with every lost mark classified as a method error, an accuracy error, a missed independent mark or genuine unknown content. For a Diploma student it is work marked against the published criteria, by letter. In both cases the report at six sessions names what has moved and what is still costing marks, in units you can check against your child's own papers. A report that says the student seems more confident is not a measurement, and confidence is the easiest thing in the world to manufacture.

If the match is wrong the tutor changes at our cost, and both the week-one checklist and the six-session review exist to make that routine rather than awkward. Nothing renews automatically. A family can take a free trial, keep the diagnosis, and never speak to us again, which is a legitimate use of the process on this page.

The claims we will not make matter on a page about verification. No grade or points promise, because both systems are externally assessed and the result belongs to the student on the day. No satisfaction percentage, score-improvement figure, student count or star rating, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method; in the pages researched for this project one provider displayed two contradictory review totals on a single page. No examiner description for anyone whose status we cannot evidence. No accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE premises. And on coursework, a tutor teaches the criteria, works comparable examples and gives feedback on your child's own drafts, and never produces the work; one provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments, and the malpractice consequences of that fall on the candidate.

faqs.question: How do I shortlist an IB or IGCSE tutor near Al Bandar when every profile looks the same?
faqs.answer: Use a four-stage funnel. Stage one, email the school for the syllabus code and tier or the IB subject and level, because every later question depends on it. Stage two, ask each tutor for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge for two years. Stage three, ask three questions: component weightings, Internal Assessment criteria by letter, and where candidates lose marks on this paper. Stage four, take two free trials and score them. Thirty names usually becomes two.

faqs.question: Is it worth running two trial sessions before choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in the same week on the same material, because one trial gives an impression and two give a comparison. Hand both tutors the same marked paper or returned draft and watch for the same behaviours: whether they ask what the student already understands, whether they work from the actual evidence, who does the work, whether a specific next step is named, and whether the student speaks more in the second half. Our trials are free with no card required, and the student does genuine work in both.

faqs.question: What is the single best indicator in a trial session?
faqs.answer: Who is talking by the end. A session in which the tutor's share of the talking falls as the hour progresses is a session in which the student is being made to think, and that pattern predicts the next six months better than any credential. A session that ends with the tutor still explaining is a lecture, and a lecture is available free at school. Watch also for whether the tutor demonstrates while the student watches, since marks are earned by the student's own working.

faqs.question: How quickly should I expect to know whether the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: After two sessions. By then a specific diagnosis should exist, it should be written down, work should have happened between the sessions and been marked, the student should be able to say what comes next, the assessment calendar should have been mentioned, and something should have been measured in units you can check. If more than two of those are missing, raise it immediately. We change the tutor at our cost, and switching at week one costs almost nothing.

faqs.question: Should we hire one tutor for both systems, or two specialists?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and usually not, for structural reasons rather than talent. IGCSE is assessed by written papers, so the skill is paper technique and mark-scheme fluency on specific components. The Diploma puts about a fifth of each subject grade in coursework produced at home over months, which demands patient supervision against published criteria without touching the work. Strength in one does not imply strength in the other, so test for each separately at stage three and expect to match two people.

faqs.question: How do I compare two children's assessment calendars in one household?
faqs.answer: Map them side by side before committing to any weekly pattern. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Diploma internal deadlines fall at intervals across two years and frequently land in an IGCSE sibling's mock season. Expect two separate quiet periods if the children attend two schools, since each school's assessment weeks differ.

faqs.question: Should the evening be split evenly between two children?
faqs.answer: No, allocate by where marks are being lost. An IGCSE candidate eight weeks from the June series needs weekly sessions plus a full timed paper at the weekend. A Diploma student in Year 1 needs fortnightly sessions with a concentrated block around an internal deadline. Those patterns interleave in one evening slot across alternating weeks, with the weekend carrying the long work. Splitting the slot equally every week serves neither child, and in this belt early school finishes make the interleaving easier than elsewhere.

faqs.question: What should I ask to check a tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A quoted permit fee or evasiveness about holding one removes a candidate from the list at stage two.

faqs.question: Why does proximity matter so little in this purchase?
faqs.answer: Because the syllabus is set by the board, the mark scheme is published by the board, and the grade boundaries apply identically to every candidate in the emirate. Distance affects convenience and the in-home price, where published rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. It has no effect on whether a tutor has prepared candidates on your child's paper, which is the variable that moves a grade and the one a distance sort cannot see.

faqs.question: A neighbour recommended someone. Is that a shortcut through the funnel?
faqs.answer: It is a shortcut through stage two and no further. A recommendation tells you about reliability and manner, both of which matter, and nothing about whether the tutor has prepared candidates on your child's syllabus and level. In this belt the same well-liked generalist often teaches several households across different boards and year groups. Take the name gratefully, then run stage three and the scored trial anyway, because your child may sit a different paper from the neighbour's.

faqs.question: What if stage three eliminates everybody on my list?
faqs.answer: Then the specialism is scarce rather than your standards being high. Minority Higher Level Diploma subjects, Arabic A Literature, the arts, Computer Science, Digital Society and Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are thin in this market, and thinner at a specific evening slot. Our answer in that situation is to name the expected wait and the nearest alternative with the difference explained, and to say plainly where a specialist is based outside the UAE. An approximate match discovered in session four is worse.

faqs.question: Could the right answer be no tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. A physics student losing marks to algebra needs a mathematics block rather than a second subscription. A Diploma student with secure paper technique and a weak exploration needs supervision hours rather than teaching hours. A Year 11 student who has never sat a full past paper to time needs a weekend, not a term. Those answers are worth less to a provider than a long booking, so whether you are offered one is a reasonable test of the advice.

faqs.question: What will a progress report from you contain?
faqs.answer: For an IGCSE student, classified losses: every mark lost on a timed paper recorded as a method error, an accuracy error, a missed independent mark or genuine unknown content, with the same question types re-sat after the targeted work. For a Diploma student, work marked against the published criteria by letter. At six sessions you receive a written statement of what has moved and what is still costing marks, checkable against your child's own papers. If the match is wrong we change the tutor at our cost.

faqs.question: Do you publish success rates or ratings I can compare?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately, and you should be wary of those that are published. In the pages researched for this project, one provider displayed two different review totals on the same page and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a far larger claim about students taught. Self-asserted rating markup breaches Google's structured-data policy and is a consumer-protection exposure as a commercial representation. We publish no rating, student count or satisfaction figure, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method.

intro.heading: Ask for the numbers before you ask about experience
paragraphs: Both the IB Diploma and the two International GCSE boards publish their component weightings. That means a parent can test any tutor in about ninety seconds without knowing any mathematics or science themselves. Ask what Paper 2 is worth in your child's subject at their level. Ask how many marks the Internal Assessment or coursework component carries, and how they are divided. A specialist answers instantly, because these figures are the architecture of the grade they work on every week.

The figures are worth having in front of you because they frequently contradict how revision is being done. A Cambridge IGCSE science theory paper is fifty per cent of the grade while the multiple-choice paper is thirty, yet most students spend most of their revision on recall. A Diploma science investigation is twenty per cent, marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each, and the criterion students neglect is worth exactly as much as the one they over-prepare.

Al Bateen is an established mainland district with long-standing schools nearby, which means households here commonly run both systems. One child on the Diploma at an IB school, another on the British pathway at a school in Al Mushrif or Al Bateen itself. The same subject name then means two different courses, and a single tutor across both is almost always a compromise rather than an efficiency. Two specialists in consecutive online slots cost the same hours and match each child properly.

The second thing worth knowing is that one skill genuinely transfers. Command terms are defined by the IB and used in parallel form by both IGCSE boards, and they are the largest single source of avoidable loss in either system. A student who learns the difference between describe, explain and evaluate once improves in Diploma theory papers and IGCSE extended answers at the same time, which is unusually good value for three or four sessions of work.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Al Bateen is one-to-one teaching over live video, matched by syllabus code and component, with your child's own school material on screen. In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted in the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in.

What follows is the detail: weightings in both systems set side by side, the command-term vocabulary that serves both, Internal Assessment and coursework criteria with their mark allocations, where marks go subject by subject, why syllabus codes matter when buying anything, the local school mix, and the boundary a tutor does not cross on assessed work. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is examined through three components at thirty, fifty and twenty per cent, with an alternative to practical paper carrying its own conventions. Diploma Chemistry runs thirty-six, forty-four and twenty, with an investigation marked out of twenty-four across four criteria. A tutor fluent in one is not automatically useful in the other, and a tutor claiming both at an equal standard is usually claiming too much.

sections.heading: Component weightings in both systems, side by side
paragraphs: This is the table to keep. It sets the published weightings for both systems next to each other, which is the fastest way to see why a revision plan built on recall underperforms. In Cambridge IGCSE sciences, half the grade sits in the theory paper's extended written answers. In the Diploma sciences, forty-four per cent sits in Paper 2. In both cases most students spend most of their revision on the component worth least.

Pearson International GCSE takes a structurally different route in the sciences, examining each through two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than as a separate component. The board publishes the exact weightings on the specification page, and that is where they should be read from rather than from any third party, including this page.

The Diploma's internal components are where the sharpest planning gains sit. An Internal Assessment is typically twenty per cent of a subject grade, produced over months in conditions the student controls, and marked against criteria published with their mark allocations. It is the most recoverable part of the qualification and the part most commonly left to run itself.

Use the table as an audit rather than a plan. Take your child's six subjects in whichever system, write the weightings next to each, and compare that against where revision time has actually gone over the last month. Most families find at least one component worth forty per cent or more that has had no attention at all, and that discovery is usually worth more than the first month of tutoring.

sections.heading: Command terms: one vocabulary for both systems
paragraphs: This is the single highest-return teaching available to a two-system household, because the vocabulary is shared. The IB defines its command terms and examiners mark to them; both IGCSE boards use parallel wording. A student who learns the difference between describe, explain and evaluate once improves in Diploma theory papers and in IGCSE extended answers at the same time, and the improvement holds for years.

The default error is identical in both systems. Students describe, because describing is what they can always do. A six-mark explain question answered descriptively collects perhaps a third of the available marks, and the student leaves the paper believing they answered it well. The gap between what was written and what was asked is invisible to them, which is why it survives two years of revision.

The fix is mechanical. Underline the command term before reading the rest of the question. Write the structure it demands before any content. For explain, a statement followed by a because. For evaluate, a claim, evidence for, evidence against, and a judgement with a reason. Three or four supervised attempts and the habit holds under pressure, which is the only test that matters.

Reading the mark allocation belongs with it and takes thirty seconds. A two-mark question wants two distinct points rather than one expressed twice. A six-mark question in a science theory paper usually wants six separable statements, and a student writing a flowing paragraph of three ideas scores three. Counting the marks, then counting your own points, is a habit almost nobody is taught explicitly in either system.

sections.heading: Criteria by letter, and what each is actually worth
paragraphs: Diploma Internal Assessments are marked against published criteria with published allocations, and students lose marks here more cheaply than anywhere else in the qualification because they lose them in criteria they never read. A tutor who does nothing but make a student mark their own draft against the descriptors, letter by letter, usually finds two or three marks sitting in plain sight before any new content is taught.

In the current science investigation, the report is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a three-thousand-word maximum. Students over-invest in method and under-invest in evaluation, which is worth exactly as much. A conclusion comparing a result to a cited accepted value scores where one restating the result does not.

The mathematics exploration is twenty marks: presentation four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Personal engagement and reflection together carry six of the twenty and are won by writing about choices and abandoned approaches rather than by producing more mathematics.

IGCSE coursework, where a specification includes it, works differently: it is marked by the school against board criteria, and in mathematics it does not exist at all. What both systems share is that the criteria are published and the student is entitled to see them. Ask for the criteria document in writing if nobody has handed it over; it is the single most useful page in the whole process.

sections.heading: Where marks go, subject by subject, in each system
paragraphs: The losses are patterned rather than random, which means they can be diagnosed from one marked paper and then worked on deliberately. In mathematics the IGCSE pattern is reverse percentages, similar shape scale factors, bounds and unshown working, while the Diploma pattern is unjustified steps, chain-rule errors and calculator fluency. Those are different lists requiring different sessions.

In the sciences the two systems converge on command terms and diverge on data. Both punish a description answering an explain question. The Diploma then demands considerably more of its data-based work, where uncertainty propagation and gradient interpretation decide a large share of the marks, while Cambridge IGCSE asks for instrument reading, precision and specific error sources in its practical component.

In English the IGCSE loss is answering the wrong task well: a polished essay in response to a question asking for a speech cannot reach the top band. The Diploma loss is the Individual Oral, worth twenty or thirty per cent and prepared worst because it feels informal. It is a rehearsed ten-minute argument with a global issue at its centre and it needs practising aloud.

In Economics and Business both systems reward the same thing and students skip it. A correctly labelled diagram earns credit before prose is read, and a tool applied to the stimulus firm scores where a tool described in the abstract does not. In the Diploma the commentary portfolio adds the easiest marks in the course and the ones most routinely wasted on unlabelled axes.

sections.heading: Syllabus codes, and why they decide what you should buy
paragraphs: Before buying any resource, check the code. A four-digit number starting with zero is Cambridge International: 0580 mathematics, 0625 physics, 0620 chemistry, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English. A code of the form 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 or 4EA1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. For the Diploma, what matters is the subject, the level, and for mathematics which of the two courses.

The codes matter because the courses genuinely differ. Cambridge 0580 separates its papers so a candidate sits one without a calculator and one with; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both. Cambridge assesses practical science through a practical test or the alternative to practical; Pearson assesses the same skills inside its written papers. Buying a revision guide for the wrong code teaches the wrong difficulty.

In a two-system household the risk compounds, because resources get shared between siblings who are not on the same courses. A Diploma Chemistry textbook is not a 0620 revision guide and will not help a Year 11 student, however reassuring it looks on a shelf. Keep the two sets of material separate and labelled by code.

A note on official material. We reference and link board syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes rather than supplying them, because reproducing them is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school holds legitimate copies of everything needed. A provider advertising a downloadable archive of mark schemes is distributing material it has no right to distribute.

sections.heading: Past papers, honesty, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A past paper teaches nothing until it is marked against the official scheme by somebody who can explain why a mark was withheld. The method that works in both systems is one timed section rather than a whole paper, marked aloud with the student present, with every lost mark classified as content, command term, unshown working or timing. The tally after five or six sessions tells you what to teach, and it is almost never what the student guessed.

On assessed work the boundary is identical in both systems and worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach content, explain what the criteria reward, question whether a plan or a research question is answerable, suggest reading and say why a section is weak. No tutor at IB Gram will write an Internal Assessment, draft an Extended Essay, compose a Theory of Knowledge essay or produce coursework in any subject.

That line matters commercially as well as ethically, because this market contains operations that cross it. One openly sells completed Internal Assessments. The consequence of that falls on the student as a malpractice finding rather than on the seller, which is the whole reason to say so on a page like this rather than leave it implied.

What this page does not claim: no regulator, examination board or school endorses or accredits IB Gram. We hold no ADEK, MoHRE, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval of any kind. process.description: 0620 Extended, or Diploma Chemistry Higher Level. Those are different courses needing different tutors. For a two-system household send both children's details separately rather than as one request, because they produce two different searches and two different matches.

process.title: Name the component you think is failing
process.description: The theory paper, the multiple-choice paper, the Internal Assessment, the Individual Oral. Component-level requests are matched faster because they are narrower searches, and if you are not sure the marked paper will show it within twenty minutes.

process.title: Test the tutor on published figures
process.description: In the free trial lesson, ask what Paper 2 is worth at your child's level and how many marks the internal component carries. Those are published facts, so hesitation is the answer. One trial lesson per family, before payment and with no card details taken.

process.title: Audit the weightings against the revision
process.description: Write your child's subjects down with their component weightings and compare that against where revision time has actually gone this month. Most families find a component worth forty per cent or more that has had no attention, which is usually worth more than the first month of tutoring.

process.title: Review against a fresh marked section
process.description: At eight weeks, run a new timed section and compare the error list. If the recurring errors have stopped, continue. If they have not, we change the tutor, the component focus or the diagnosis rather than adding hours. Re-matching is free and the diagnosis carries across.

whyPoints.title: Weightings published so you can test us
whyPoints.description: Cambridge IGCSE sciences split thirty, fifty and twenty. Diploma sciences run thirty-six, forty-four and twenty. The investigation is twenty-four marks across four criteria. Those figures are on the page so you can ask any tutor, including ours, and judge the answer.

whyPoints.title: Two systems, two specialists
whyPoints.description: The same subject name means different courses across the Diploma and the IGCSE boards. We staff each child separately rather than offering one tutor for both, because specification knowledge is the part that moves grades and nobody holds two at an equal standard.

whyPoints.title: One vocabulary taught once
whyPoints.description: Command terms are shared across both systems, so three or four sessions on question wording improve Diploma theory papers and IGCSE extended answers at the same time. In a two-system household that is the one genuine efficiency available.

whyPoints.title: Criteria read with the student, not at them
whyPoints.description: Internal components are marked against published criteria with stated allocations, and students lose marks in criteria they never read. We make the student mark their own draft letter by letter, which usually finds marks before anything new is taught.

whyPoints.title: Codes checked before anything is bought
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are different courses with different calculator rules. We ask for the code first, which prevents the commonest avoidable waste in this market: a term of revision against the wrong specification.

faqs.question: How do I test an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Bateen in one phone call?
faqs.answer: Ask three published questions. What is Paper 2 worth in my child's subject at their level. How many marks does the internal or coursework component carry, and how are they divided. What does an examiner want from evaluate that they do not want from describe. A specialist answers all three immediately, because those figures are the architecture of the grade they work on weekly. A tutor who moves the conversation to rapport has told you what you needed to know.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both an IGCSE and a Diploma child in Al Bateen?
faqs.answer: Rarely well. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is examined across three components at thirty, fifty and twenty per cent, with an alternative to practical paper carrying its own conventions. Diploma Chemistry runs thirty-six, forty-four and twenty with an investigation marked out of twenty-four across four criteria. Those are different bodies of knowledge. What can be shared is command-term discipline, timed-practice habits and the scheduling, and the scheduling is where the real saving sits.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes in Al Bateen?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one to one over live video, matched by syllabus code and component, with your child's own material on screen. In Al Bateen the usual obstacle to a visit is building access and parking rather than distance, which is a cost nobody quotes for and which online delivery removes entirely.

faqs.question: Why is the Cambridge science theory paper the one to work on?
faqs.answer: Because it is half the grade. Cambridge examines each separate IGCSE science through a multiple-choice paper at thirty per cent, a theory paper at fifty, and a practical component at twenty. Most students spend most of their revision on recall, which serves the thirty per cent paper. The fifty per cent paper is extended written answers, where command-term discipline and mark-allocation reading decide the outcome. That mismatch is the commonest planning error in the British pathway.

faqs.question: What is the DP science investigation marked out of?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four, across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a three-thousand-word maximum, and it carries twenty per cent of the subject grade. Students over-invest in method and under-invest in evaluation, which is worth exactly as much. A conclusion that compares the result against a cited accepted value scores where one that restates the result does not, and that is a writing decision rather than a scientific one.

faqs.question: Which part of the maths exploration carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: Use of mathematics, at six of the twenty available. Presentation and mathematical communication carry four each, personal engagement three and reflection three, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. The pair students neglect is engagement and reflection, which together carry six marks and are earned by writing about the choices made and the approaches abandoned. Treating that writing as padding around the mathematics costs nearly a third of the Internal Assessment mark.

faqs.question: Do command terms work the same way in both systems?
faqs.answer: Closely enough that teaching them once serves both, which makes this the best value available to a two-system household. The IB defines its command terms and both IGCSE boards use parallel wording. Describe wants features, explain wants a mechanism with a because, analyse wants parts and relationships, evaluate wants a judgement with evidence on both sides. A student who learns the distinctions once improves across every subject in both systems simultaneously.

faqs.question: Why does reading the mark allocation change the answer?
faqs.answer: Because the number of marks tells you how many separable points are wanted. A two-mark question wants two distinct points, not one expressed twice. A six-mark question in a theory paper usually wants six separable statements, and a student writing a flowing paragraph containing three ideas scores three however well written it is. Counting the marks and then counting your own points takes thirty seconds and almost nobody is taught to do it explicitly in either system.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my Al Bateen child sits?
faqs.answer: Check the front of any past paper. A four-digit code starting with zero is Cambridge International, so 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610 or 0500. A code of the form 4MA1 or 4PH1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The schools around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif sometimes use different boards for different subjects in the same building, so check each one. An email to the school office will confirm the board and code in writing within a day.

faqs.question: Can my Diploma child use a sibling's IGCSE revision guide?
faqs.answer: No, and the reverse is equally unhelpful. A Diploma Chemistry textbook is not a 0620 revision guide and will not serve a Year 11 student however reassuring it looks on the shelf. The courses differ in content, in component structure and in what the questions ask for. Keep the two sets of material separate and labelled by code. Resource sharing between siblings on different systems is a common and quietly expensive mistake in two-system households.

faqs.question: Where should we start if the report just says the grade is a 5?
faqs.answer: With a marked paper rather than the report. Write the component weightings for that subject next to the paper and look at where the lost marks sit. A grade of 5 in a Cambridge science can mean a weak multiple-choice paper, a theory paper losing marks on command terms, or a practical component nobody rehearsed, and those are three different fixes. Twenty minutes with the script and the weightings usually produces a brief you can act on.

faqs.question: Is the Individual Oral worth preparing properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the Diploma component prepared worst. It carries thirty per cent of English A Language and Literature at Standard Level and twenty at Higher Level, which is more than most students realise, and it feels informal because it is internal and spoken. In practice it is a rehearsed ten-minute argument built around a global issue, with extracts chosen deliberately. It needs practising aloud several times, which is one of the few things video delivery handles better than a notebook ever could.

faqs.question: Should we buy a mark-scheme archive from a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: No. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the examination boards, and reproducing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. Your child's school holds legitimate copies of everything needed and a tutor can work from those. A provider advertising a downloadable archive is distributing material it has no right to distribute, which is a reason for caution about everything else it tells you.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write part of an Internal Assessment if the deadline is close?
faqs.answer: Not here, at any price and at any point in the calendar. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own in both systems. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the research question is answerable, and say why a section is weak so the student can fix it. Nobody at IB Gram writes, drafts or edits assessed work. If a deadline is genuinely unreachable, the conversation to have is with the school.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff both systems at the hours we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than putting one tutor across both. Common subjects in either system usually match within a few days. The constraint is narrow combinations at fixed hours: a specific Diploma Higher Level component at 19:00 competes with Corniche, Al Reem and Saadiyat households for the same window. Where consecutive slots on one evening cannot be staffed we will offer two different evenings instead, which is a worse schedule and a better match.

intro.heading: A list of names near you verifies nothing. Here is what does
paragraphs: A near me search is a proximity query answered by directories, and proximity is the one variable in this market that has no effect on a grade. Al Falah sits out towards the airport road, well away from the Khalifa City and Al Raha school belt, so the list such a search returns is short, and the short list is reassuring in exactly the wrong way: it looks like a vetted set when it is a geographic one. Nothing on it has been checked against the syllabus your child is actually sitting.

The useful question is narrower and entirely answerable. Has this person taught Cambridge 0580 Extended, or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, to examination, and when? Do they hold the UAE private tuition work permit? What will they refuse to do with an Internal Assessment? How will they report progress, and in what units? Every one of those can be asked and answered before any money moves, and none of them requires a parent to know the subject. This page is a verification manual rather than a sales page, and it is written that way because the alternative in this market is a list of adjectives.

Households in Al Falah often run two systems at once, which complicates the question. One child may be in the Diploma at a school in the Al Raha belt while a younger sibling sits IGCSE closer to home, and the two require different things from a tutor: the Diploma is a two-year course in which about a fifth of each subject grade is produced at home across months, while IGCSE is externally assessed in written papers where technique carries the result. A provider who treats those as interchangeable has not understood either, and that is testable in one conversation.

There is also a layer most tutoring pages skip entirely. Private schools in Abu Dhabi are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project. Alongside the licensed international curriculum, UAE private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies, under a federal baseline requiring adherence to those subjects regardless of the curriculum licensed. Those lessons occupy real timetable space and a revision plan that ignores them overstates the hours available.

Finally, the model, stated before anything else is read. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Al Falah families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We hold no accreditation, licence or partnership from any regulator or examination board and have no premises in the UAE, and this page will show you how to check that kind of claim on anyone, including us.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE

Verification turns on the syllabus code and the tier: Cambridge 0580 has a Core route graded C to G and an Extended route graded A* to E, while Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 caps Foundation at grade 5 and runs Higher from 9 to 4. A tutor who cannot discuss the difference has not prepared candidates for either.

programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, ending in the Personal Project. The verification question is whether the tutor can explain how criterion marks differ from percentages, because a parent reading an MYP report as a percentage grade will make the wrong purchase and a tutor who does not correct that misunderstanding is not paying attention.

sections.heading: How to verify a tutor's claims before you pay
paragraphs: Almost every claim that matters here is checkable, and the checks are quick. Subject expertise is verified by asking for component weightings and Internal Assessment criteria, in that order, and by asking which syllabus and level they have taught to examination and when. Those three answers separate syllabus knowledge from subject knowledge, which is the distinction the published AED bands are really pricing.

Permit status is verified by asking to see the permit. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified.

Institutional claims are verified differently. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a regulated entity: in Dubai that means a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. So a claim of regulator approval should come with a permit number, and a claim of partnership with a school or board should come with a document. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same arrangement; treat that as press-reported and verify against the current ADEK policy. The practical rule: decline any offer of your child's own class teacher privately.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it changes the answer
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised that the regulator depends on the emirate rather than on the curriculum. Dubai private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate, and Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, which does the same. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The practical consequences are real. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval, not only inspection, sits at emirate level there. For an Al Falah family the relevant body is ADEK, and any inspection outcome should be read on the regulator's own site rather than on a tutoring page. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project, which is a notable gap on pages written for Abu Dhabi parents.

Why this belongs on a verification page: a regulator's name is the most commonly misused word in this market. Naming ADEK, KHDA or the Ministry of Education and explaining what each does is legitimate and useful. Implying that any of them has approved, accredited, licensed or partnered with a tutoring provider is a claim that requires a document, and in most cases that document is a permit issued to a premises-based institute rather than anything a platform or an individual can hold. IB Gram holds no such approval from any of these bodies, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no premises in the UAE.
