sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects, and what they do to a timetable
paragraphs: This is the section competitor pages leave empty, and it affects every revision plan in the country. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why a school licensed for the IB or for Cambridge still teaches those subjects, and why they occupy timetable space that a parent planning Year 11 or Diploma Year 2 revision has to account for.

Dubai's published guidance, issued by KHDA, is the most detailed public statement of how this works and is useful as an illustration even for an Abu Dhabi family, with the caveat that the Abu Dhabi regulator is ADEK and its own requirements should be confirmed directly. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is required as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details matter to a tutoring conversation. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which is a concrete credential point and a reason to be careful with any tutoring claim in this area. And instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and an advised minimum of at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. The use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring material for these subjects may honestly be described.

sections.heading: Two systems in one household: what differs and what does not
paragraphs: Many Al Falah families are running an IGCSE student and a Diploma student at the same time, and the instinct is to treat them as the same problem at different ages. They are not. IGCSE mathematics on Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 is assessed entirely by written papers, with no Internal Assessment on the main mathematics syllabuses, so the whole of the preparation value sits in technique and the interventions are short and measurable. The Diploma puts about a fifth of each subject grade in work produced at home across months, which means supervision months before any exam.

The calendars differ too. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in June and November, and UAE candidates sit those two series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. The Diploma has its own internal deadline structure for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word ceiling and the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 words, and those internal deadlines frequently land in the same weeks as a sibling's mock season. A household planning both at once should map the two calendars side by side before committing to any weekly pattern.

What does not differ is the verification question. In both systems the thing worth checking is whether the tutor knows the specific assessment, what each component is worth, and where marks are lost. In both systems the coursework boundary is identical in principle: a tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on the student's own work and never produces it. And in both systems the regulator and the permit position are the same, because they attach to the person and the premises rather than to the curriculum.

Our position is to disclose it. If a combination is not covered, you are told that, given the expected wait, and offered the nearest alternative with the difference explained. Where the specialist teaching your child's syllabus is based outside the UAE, we say so plainly; the lesson still runs in Gulf Standard Time and the syllabus is the same syllabus, but you should know where the person sits rather than discovering it later. Two of the competitor pages measured for this project route UAE parents to a phone number in another country without ever stating that.

Sometimes the better answer is a different intervention entirely. A physics student losing marks to algebra benefits more from a mathematics repair block than from waiting for a physics specialist. A Diploma student with a weak exploration and secure paper technique needs supervision hours rather than teaching hours. Those recommendations are worth less to us than a long weekly booking, which is precisely why a page about verification should contain them.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across both boards, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: The boundary is identical in both systems and worth setting before any deadline tests it. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, works comparable examples, sets practice, marks it and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce your child's coursework, does not supply submittable text, and does not edit a draft until the thinking has stopped being theirs. That covers an IB Internal Assessment in any subject, the Extended Essay at its 4,000-word ceiling, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 words, and the Cambridge 0607 investigation.

The reason to publish it rather than discuss it privately is that the exposure is asymmetric. An authenticity problem is a malpractice matter for the candidate, with consequences for their diploma, while the person who supplied the work faces nothing. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. On a verification page, that is the single most important thing to be able to check: ask any tutor what they will refuse to do, and listen to whether the refusal is specific.

We also do not publish or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source. And we claim nothing that cannot be checked. IB Gram holds no licence, approval, certification or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. It has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. It publishes no satisfaction percentage, student count, score-improvement figure or star rating, because none of those could be evidenced with a sample size, a date and a method. Those are the claims this page has spent its length teaching you to test, so it would be strange to make them.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Al Falah who knows my child's exact syllabus?
faqs.answer: It depends on the syllabus, and it is checkable rather than a matter of hope. Al Falah itself holds very few resident subject specialists, and the mainland pool sits around Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt, twenty to forty minutes away. For common IGCSE subjects and the main IB sciences and mathematics the answer is usually yes. For minority Higher Level subjects, Arabic A Literature, the arts or Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, often nobody nearby teaches it at any price, which is where online delivery stops being a compromise.

faqs.question: What three questions will tell me whether a tutor really knows the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask what each component of the course is worth. Ask for the Internal Assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations. Then ask which syllabus and level they have taught to examination, and when. Someone who has planned and delivered the course answers all three immediately and specifically. Someone who knows the subject in general will generalise, talk about motivation and confidence, or reach for a document. None of this requires you to know the subject yourself, which is the point of asking in that order.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is allowed to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and applications go through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A quoted permit fee is a warning sign, since the permit costs nothing.

faqs.question: A tutoring provider claims regulator approval. How would I verify that claim?
faqs.answer: Ask for the permit number and the issuing body, then check it with that body. In Dubai, a tutoring operation with premises and staff requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal; that permit is issued to premises-based operations rather than to platforms or individuals. A provider using the word approved with no document is making the single most dangerous claim available in this market. IB Gram holds no such approval from any regulator or examination board and has no UAE premises.

faqs.question: Who regulates the schools an Al Falah family would use?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. Across the rest of the country, Dubai sits with KHDA, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve fees, curricula, courses and assessment methods. Read any inspection outcome on the regulator's own site rather than on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher be hired privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It has been reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against the ADEK policy document, since press reporting is not the policy itself. The practical answer for an Al Falah household is to decline such an offer and to ask instead for a tutor with no connection to the school your child attends.

faqs.question: Why do Arabic and Islamic Education matter to an IB or IGCSE revision plan?
faqs.answer: Because they occupy timetable space that a plan built only around the international curriculum ignores. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations, so these subjects run alongside the licensed programme. Published KHDA guidance calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any such lesson. A Year 11 or Diploma Year 2 plan that overlooks them overstates the hours a student actually has.

faqs.question: Are separate Arabic and Islamic Education classes really required?
faqs.answer: In Dubai, published KHDA guidance requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Abu Dhabi schools are regulated by ADEK, so confirm its requirements directly, but the federal baseline behind both is the same.

faqs.question: We have one child on IGCSE and one in the Diploma. Does that need two different plans?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the grades are earned differently. IGCSE mathematics is assessed by written papers with no Internal Assessment on the main syllabuses, so short well-aimed technique work moves the result. The Diploma places about a fifth of each subject grade in coursework written at home across months, which means supervision long before any exam. Map both calendars side by side before committing to a weekly pattern, because Diploma internal deadlines frequently land in the same weeks as an IGCSE sibling's mock season.

faqs.question: What should I ask about a tutor's willingness to help with coursework?
faqs.answer: Ask directly what they will refuse to do, and listen for whether the refusal is specific. The correct answer involves teaching what the criteria reward, working a comparable example on a different topic, and giving feedback on your child's own drafts. Any version that involves producing, drafting, polishing to completion or supplying text should end the conversation. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the malpractice consequences of that purchase fall on the candidate rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: Do the star ratings on tutoring websites in this market mean anything?
faqs.answer: Treat them as decoration unless they come with a sample size, a date and a method. In the pages researched for this project, one provider displayed two different review totals on the same page and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a far larger claim about students taught. Self-asserted rating markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, it is a consumer-protection exposure. We publish no rating, student count or satisfaction figure for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: What happens if the specialist teaching my child's subject is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: We tell you, before you book. The syllabus is the same syllabus, the lesson runs in Gulf Standard Time, and for a minority Higher Level subject or Further Pure Mathematics the non-UAE specialist may be the only person who teaches it. What should not happen is a provider concealing delivery location behind a foreign phone number, which two of the competitor pages measured for this project do. Knowing where the tutor sits is part of what you are verifying, not an administrative detail.

faqs.question: Does distance from the island change what my child's tutoring costs?
faqs.answer: For in-home arrangements, yes. Published figures put in-home one-to-one across Abu Dhabi at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the quotes sit lower around Khalifa City where drives are short and higher out towards the airport road. That geographic pattern is the clearest evidence that distance is being billed rather than expertise. Online rates do not change with distance, which is why Al Falah benefits from them more than most communities.

faqs.question: If the honest answer is that nobody covers my child's subject, what then?
faqs.answer: We say so, name the expected wait and explain the nearest alternative with the difference stated. Sometimes a different intervention is the better recommendation: a physics student losing marks to algebra gains more from a mathematics repair block than from waiting for a physics specialist, and a Diploma student with secure paper technique and a weak exploration needs supervision hours rather than teaching hours. Those answers are worth less to us than a long booking, which is a reasonable test of whether a provider is being straight with you.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-g.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE subjects and IB Diploma courses at both levels. For a family deciding how much to commit, the useful question is not the hourly rate but what arrives each week in return for it, which is set out further down this page.

intro.heading: Start with the annual figure, not the hourly rate
paragraphs: Nobody buys an hour of tuition. Families buy a term or a year, usually without ever seeing that number written down, and the hourly rate is a poor guide to it because the rates in this market span more than a factor of ten and the inclusions differ at every level. The honest way to start a conversation about cost is to annualise it, and that is what the first table on this page does, using published monthly estimates rather than our own figures.

Al Ghadeer sits on the boundary between Abu Dhabi and Dubai, a mixed community of townhouses and apartments on the corridor, with many households working on the Dubai side and some using schools there. That position produces a specific cost effect: families here are routinely quoted against both emirates' markets, and Dubai rates are the ones most visible online. A parent comparing a Dubai-advertised home tutor against an Abu Dhabi school fee cycle is comparing two different markets without realising it.

The second thing worth establishing early is what the money actually buys, because that varies more than the price does. At the budget end an hour is typically a review of homework the student has already attempted. In the middle band a tutor teaches the specification and marks written work between sessions. At specialist level the fee buys judgement: which tier, which topics to abandon, which papers to sit, what the mark scheme rewards. Those are three different products and all three are advertised in the same language.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Ghadeer or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The relevant cost point is that published in-home visiting rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and from a boundary community the difference is substantially a journey.

This page also sets out the options that cost nothing or almost nothing, because a cost page that only discusses paid options is a brochure. A school's own intervention class is free, taught by somebody who knows the specification and has seen the student's work, and for a procedural or terminology gap it is frequently the best available option at any price. Retrieval practice costs nothing. Reading a mark scheme costs nothing. All three should be exhausted before a family commits several thousand dirhams a year.

Every AED figure here belongs to the market, is attributed to a named published source, and was read in October 2026. Where an annual figure appears it is our own arithmetic on a published monthly estimate and is labelled as such. None of it is IB Gram's price list, and on the VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE we state no position, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority.

sections.heading: A year of tuition, costed
paragraphs: The table annualises published monthly estimates over a nine-month school year, which is our own arithmetic on somebody else's figures and is labelled as such. The monthly estimates come from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from packages advertised in this market, all read in October 2026. None of it is our price list.

Two things become visible once the numbers are annual. First, the range is enormous: a weekly hour at budget level and a weekly hour of specialist examination-year support differ by roughly a factor of four over a year, and in-home delivery adds a further layer. Second, the bounded block sits in a completely different bracket from everything else. Three to five sessions aimed at a diagnosed procedural fault costs less than a single month of a weekly arrangement, which is why the diagnosis matters more than the rate.

The sensible way for an Al Ghadeer family to use the table is to decide what kind of problem they have before deciding what to spend. A procedural fault, a command-term problem or an unpractised Paper 3 is a bounded-block purchase in the lowest row. A content gap or a fluency problem is a term, in one of the middle rows, and should be entered into knowing that it is months rather than weeks. There is no version of this market in which a fluency problem is cheap.

One further observation on the in-home rows. The loading over online delivery is real and from a boundary community it is largely transport: a visiting tutor is committing to a long round trip for a single lesson. What it buys is physical presence in the room, which genuinely helps some students, particularly younger ones and those who need supervision rather than teaching. For a Diploma student working on criteria-based assessed pieces it is usually the least valuable thing on the invoice.

sections.heading: The border effect: two markets, one household
paragraphs: Al Ghadeer's position on the Abu Dhabi and Dubai boundary creates a pricing confusion that families elsewhere do not have. Much of the published tutoring rate information in the UAE is Dubai-facing, because that is where the search volume is, and a household here is routinely quoted against both markets without being told which is which.

The practical consequences are small but real. A Dubai-based home tutor quoting for a visit to Al Ghadeer is pricing a journey across the emirate boundary, and that journey is in the rate. An Abu Dhabi-based tutor is doing the same from the other direction. Online, the geography disappears and the quote is for teaching. If you are comparing three quotes and one is a visit, you are not comparing like with like, and the difference is not quality.

The second border effect concerns schools. Some Al Ghadeer households use Dubai-side schools, which means a different regulator, a different fee approval process, potentially different term dates and a different inspection framework. Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate; Abu Dhabi's sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Confusing published news between the two is easy and consequential.

A dated example of why that matters. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure. A family with a child in an Abu Dhabi school should not plan a budget around it, and a family with a child on the Dubai side should read the regulator's own announcement rather than a summary of it.

sections.heading: What you are entitled to receive for the money
paragraphs: If the price range is wide and the inclusions vary, the useful consumer question is not how much but what arrives. This is the part of the transaction families almost never specify in advance, and specifying it is the single best protection against spending a term on something unmeasurable.

The minimum defensible set is short. A written diagnosis in the first week, naming the specific faults found and the category of each. Written work set every week with an explicit instruction about what to show. That work returned marked against the published scheme or criteria, with marks rather than ticks. An error log maintained across papers showing whether the named faults recur less often. And a review at a fixed date at which the question is whether the marks moved, not whether the lessons were enjoyable.

All five of those are checkable by a parent with no subject knowledge, which is the point. A marked script showing eleven marks lost to command-term misreads in October and three in December is evidence. A cheerful message after each lesson is reassurance, generated by design, and in our experience that language appears precisely when the written work has quietly stopped being set.

The table sets out each item with what it looks like done well, what it looks like done badly, and how to check. Take it to any provider, including us. A provider who treats the list as reasonable is describing a service; one who finds it intrusive is describing something else.

sections.heading: Free, nearly free, and cheap: what to try before paying
paragraphs: A page about cost that only lists paid options is advertising. There are three or four interventions that cost nothing or almost nothing, and for a meaningful share of students they are sufficient. They should be exhausted before a household commits several thousand dirhams a year, and no provider has an incentive to tell you so.

The school's own intervention or support class is first. It is free, it is taught by somebody who knows the exact specification and has seen your child's work, and they have access to the department's assessment data. For a procedural gap, a terminology problem or a command-term habit, that is a strong combination at any price. Ask whether such a class exists and whether your child is in it, and treat a negative answer as the first question for the school rather than a reason to buy.

Second is reading the mark scheme. Published schemes are free on the boards' own sites and almost no student has read one. A student who reads three, with their own marked script alongside, changes the shape of their written answers permanently. A parent can supervise that in an evening without understanding the subject, simply by checking that the required elements named in the scheme appear in the student's answer.

Third is retrieval practice, which is free and better than the method most students use. Reading notes produces recognition; writing an answer without notes produces recall, which is what examinations require. Twenty minutes a day on a topic covered three weeks ago, marked against the scheme afterwards, outperforms two hours of rereading. The table sets these out with what each fixes and, importantly, what it cannot.

sections.heading: Hidden extras and the billing questions worth asking
paragraphs: The published rate is rarely the whole figure, and the gaps are predictable enough to ask about in advance. None of these questions is awkward and all of them are cheaper to ask than to discover.

Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, because a sixty-minute rate quoted against a forty-five minute lesson is a different price. Ask what happens if a session is cancelled, by either side, and how much notice is required. Ask whether marking of written work between sessions is included or billed separately, since that is the component that does the work. Ask whether a first payment commits you to a block, and whether anything renews automatically. Ask what happens if the match is wrong and a replacement is needed.

Ask about the free trial's conditions on the same screen as the offer, because an offer described as free with an undisclosed condition attached is not free. Ours is one lesson, with no card required and nothing starting automatically, and that is the whole of it. If a provider's trial requires card details, requires a block commitment afterwards, or is only free if you continue, those are conditions and you are entitled to see them before giving your details.

Ask about data, too, since tuition involves information about a minor. A provider should tell you what it collects, why, and how to have it deleted, and should keep a privacy link on every page. The UAE has a federal personal data protection law, and a lead form gathering a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose is a problem regardless of intent. It is reasonable to ask what happens to the marked work and the diagnosis when you stop.

sections.heading: Tuition against school fees: the context
paragraphs: Tuition spending makes more sense viewed against the rest of a household's education budget than in isolation. For most families in this corridor, school fees are the dominant figure and tuition is a marginal addition — which argues for spending it precisely rather than broadly, since the marginal dirham has to work harder than the fee does.

The published context worth knowing is dated and checkable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Those are Dubai figures; Abu Dhabi's fee process sits with ADEK.

Against that backdrop, the annualised tuition figures in the first table are a modest proportion of a typical private school fee and a large absolute number in their own right. The decision that most affects value is therefore not how much to spend but on what: one subject properly funded with marked work, or a core component nobody else is buying, against three or four subjects funded thinly enough that the written practice stops happening in all of them.

There is one figure in this market that belongs in a cost discussion for a different reason. A provider advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750 — roughly three months of genuine specialist tuition. We decline to produce assessed work at any price. The number is useful because it shows what is being sold in this market and at what scale, and because buying one is academic malpractice whose consequence falls on the student's whole entry rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: When money cannot buy the outcome
paragraphs: A cost page should say where spending stops working, because that is the information a family cannot get from anybody selling. There are four situations in which more money produces less than it appears to, and recognising them saves real sums.

The first is a load problem. A competent student carrying three Higher Levels, the Diploma core, mandatory subjects and a long daily journey may simply lack the hours the courses assume. Adding a weekly session to that week displaces the written practice that makes sessions work, so the intervention makes the situation worse. The honest next step is a conversation with the school about level or subject load, and we will say so rather than taking the booking.

The second is lateness. Tuition bought eight weeks before a terminal series reliably improves timing, command-term discipline, rounding and question selection, and reliably cannot rebuild two years of fluency or teach untaught content. Both are true at the same time. A family who knows which they are buying will spend the eight weeks well; a family who has been told it can fix everything will be disappointed in a way that was predictable from the start.

The third is breadth. Tuition works through marked written practice between lessons, and a student's free evenings do not multiply when subjects are added. By the third or fourth subject the lessons are the only work happening and nothing consolidates. The fourth is a structural problem at a school — a course not taught by a specialist this year, or a Higher Level combination that did not run — which tuition can palliate and cannot fix, and which should be raised with the school directly.

sections.heading: The permit, our status and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years — so a tutor who tells you the permit is costly is mistaken — and the ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published and press reporting states that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure quoted to you as the penalty is invention — a useful test of whether the rest of a provider's claims are sourced. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school. Verify the current document before relying on the wording.

An operation with premises is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs its own permit from the emirate regulator; in Dubai that is an educational services permit for a training institute issued by KHDA. IB Gram holds none, because it has no premises: it is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. Describing a tutoring service as approved by one of those bodies without the document to show is the most dangerous sentence available in this market.

On claims and figures: we publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic, because stating one honestly requires the sample size, the date and the method alongside it. Every AED figure on this page is attributed to a published source and dated October 2026, and the annualised figures are labelled as our arithmetic on those published monthly estimates. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university outcome, and we decline to produce assessed work of any kind at any price.

faqs.question: What does a year of IB or IGCSE tuition cost from Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: Annualising published monthly estimates over a nine-month school year: roughly AED 2,200 to 5,400 for a weekly hour at budget level, AED 5,400 to 10,800 mid-market, and AED 9,000 to 18,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. An advertised in-home package of four two-hour sessions a month annualises to roughly AED 14,400 to 16,200. Those monthly figures come from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and market packages read in October 2026; the annualisation is our arithmetic.

faqs.question: Why are we quoted different rates from Dubai and Abu Dhabi tutors?
faqs.answer: Because Al Ghadeer sits on the boundary and most published UAE rate information is Dubai-facing, so a household here gets quoted against two markets without being told which is which. More importantly, a visiting tutor from either direction is pricing a journey across the emirate boundary into the rate. If one of three quotes is for a visit, you are not comparing like with like, and the difference is transport rather than quality.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing that actually works?
faqs.answer: The school's own intervention or support class, which is usually free, taught by somebody who knows the exact specification and has seen your child's work, and backed by the department's assessment data. For a procedural gap, a terminology problem or a command-term habit that is a strong combination at any price. Ask whether such a class exists and whether your child is in it. After that, reading three published mark schemes and twenty minutes of daily retrieval practice, both free.

faqs.question: How cheap can a useful paid arrangement be?
faqs.answer: A bounded block of three to five specialist sessions aimed at one diagnosed fault costs roughly AED 600 to 2,300 in total at published specialist online rates read in October 2026, which is less than a single month of a weekly arrangement at the same level. Where the diagnosis is a procedural fault, a command-term habit or unpractised Paper 3 technique, that block is frequently the whole of what a student needs and we would rather sell it than a term.

faqs.question: What should I receive each week for the money?
faqs.answer: Five things, all checkable without subject knowledge. A written diagnosis in week one naming the faults and their categories. Written work set with an explicit instruction about what to show. That work returned marked against the published scheme, with marks rather than ticks. An error log kept across papers. And a review at a fixed date measured on marked evidence. Cheerful messages after each lesson are reassurance by design, and usually appear when the written work has stopped.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT, and are tuition fees taxed in the UAE?
faqs.answer: On the general tax treatment of tuition fees we state no position, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority and we would rather say so than publish something unsourced. What a family can and should do is ask any provider directly whether a quoted figure includes VAT, and ask for that in writing before committing. A provider who cannot answer clearly about their own pricing has told you something about their administration.

faqs.question: What hidden extras catch Al Ghadeer families out?
faqs.answer: Five recurring ones. Whether the price is per hour or per lesson, since a sixty-minute rate against a forty-five minute session is a different price. Cancellation terms and notice periods on both sides. Whether marking between sessions is included or billed separately, which matters because the marking does the work. Whether a first payment commits you to a block or renews automatically. And what happens if the match is wrong and a replacement is needed.

faqs.question: Is a free trial lesson really free?
faqs.answer: Ours is: one live video lesson, no card required, no block commitment afterwards, and nothing renewing automatically. That is the whole of the condition. Elsewhere, ask for the conditions on the same screen as the offer, because an offer described as free with an undisclosed requirement attached is not free. If a trial requires card details, a subsequent commitment, or is only free if you continue, those are conditions you are entitled to see first.

faqs.question: Should we fund three subjects or one for our Al Ghadeer student?
faqs.answer: One, properly, and then review. Tuition works through the marked written practice between lessons, and your child's free evenings do not multiply when subjects are added. By the third or fourth subject the lessons become the only work happening and nothing consolidates. One subject with a specialist and marked work reliably moves a grade; three funded thinly cost three times as much and move none. For a terminal examination year with two genuinely failing subjects, two is defensible.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze apply to our Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure for Dubai schools. Abu Dhabi's private school fee process sits with ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation in that emirate. On a boundary like Al Ghadeer's the two are easy to confuse and the difference is consequential.

faqs.question: When is spending more on tuition pointless?
faqs.answer: In four situations. When the student has a load problem rather than a learning one, because adding sessions displaces the practice that makes sessions work. When tuition starts eight weeks before a terminal series and the fault is fluency or untaught content rather than technique. When the budget is spread across three or four subjects until the written work stops in all of them. And when the underlying problem is structural at the school, which tuition can palliate and cannot fix.

faqs.question: Why is Theory of Knowledge the best value thing to buy?
faqs.answer: Because it carries twenty marks — ten for the essay and ten for the exhibition — against published instruments with strict word limits of sixteen hundred and nine hundred and fifty words, and most students receive very little structured teaching on how those instruments are applied to what they have written. Three to five sessions aimed exactly at that often returns more per dirham than the same money added to a fourth subject. Almost no household budgets for it.

faqs.question: What is the AED 3,750 figure some providers advertise?
faqs.answer: A completed Internal Assessment, sold outright by a provider in this market. It belongs in a cost discussion for two reasons. It is roughly three months of genuine specialist tuition, which puts the price of the shortcut in perspective. And buying one is academic malpractice whose consequence falls on the student's whole Diploma entry rather than on the seller. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind at any price.

faqs.question: Does the permit a tutor needs add to what we pay?
faqs.answer: It should not, because the permit is free. The UAE private tuition work permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with the ministry's own service page listing no fee and a two working day completion time. A tutor who tells you the permit is costly is mistaken, and anyone quoting you a specific fine for tutoring without one is inventing it, since no schedule of amounts has been published.

intro.heading: Five different things come back from one search
paragraphs: Typing tutor near me from an address on Al Jubail Island produces a list that looks homogeneous and is not. Somewhere in it are specialist agencies with a vetted panel, international marketplaces listing tutors in several countries, tuition centres with premises on the mainland running group classes, individual tutors advertising informally in residents' groups, and, invisibly, the support your child's own school already provides and has not been asked for. Those five things have different prices, different strengths and different failure modes, and a parent choosing between them is usually not told that they are choosing at all.

That matters more from this address than from most. Al Jubail Island is a low-density residential development laid out among mangroves, with no school on the island, so every school run crosses a bridge to Saadiyat, Yas, Al Raha or the main island. The informal local network that does most of the tutoring work in a dense Abu Dhabi district is thin here, and the mainland tuition centres are a drive away in the evening. The usual defaults do not apply.

So this page is a comparison rather than a pitch. It sets out what each of the five options is genuinely good at, what each tends to get wrong, and what to ask before committing to any of them. It includes the two options a tutoring company has no commercial reason to recommend, which are the school's own support and a well-chosen group class, because for a good number of students those are the right answer and saying so is more useful than pretending otherwise. A comparison is only worth reading if the writer's own option appears in it on the same terms as everybody else's, so ours does.

It also deals with something specific to households running both systems at once, which is common here: an IB report and an IGCSE report are written in different languages about different things, and parents comparing two children's progress are frequently comparing nothing at all. Criterion levels, a one-to-seven subject grade, letters and numbers all mean different things, and the differences are not intuitive. Getting that wrong leads directly to spending money on the child whose report simply looks worse, which is a surprisingly common outcome.

On delivery, so nothing is implied: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Jubail Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is the model this page is describing when it describes an online one-to-one provider, and its limitations are set out alongside everybody else's. Where a group class or the school's own department is the better answer, this page says so.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects with terminal papers and a tier per subject. Because the content is standardised and widely taught, this is the stage where group classes and tuition centres are most viable, and where an individual tutor hired informally is least likely to be fatally mismatched, though specification differences still bite.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series, with the February and March series offered to India only. Campuses around Saadiyat, Yas and Al Raha use both Cambridge and Pearson specifications, sometimes within one school for different subjects.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject with a Personal Project in the final year. Group provision is weak here because there is no standard terminal paper to teach towards, and the useful work is specific to how the student's own school interprets the criteria.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with an Internal Assessment in each, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The stage where group and marketplace models break down most often, because the work is individual, deadline-driven and specific to a course and level rather than to a subject.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level cohorts at Abu Dhabi IB campuses are small, so the pool of teachers with repeated experience of a given course and level is small too. From an address requiring bridge crossings, that is the practical argument for matching on course rather than on proximity.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Standardised and widely taught, so a group class at a tuition centre can work if everyone in it is on the same specification and tier. One-to-one earns its premium where a tier decision is live or where a specific error pattern needs diagnosing from a script.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics AA and AI
subjects.description: Course and level specific, with an exploration worth 20% and at Higher Level an extended-response paper. Group provision rarely works because two students in the same room are frequently on different courses. Specialist one-to-one is close to the only sensible model.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences
subjects.description: Good group candidates for content coverage, less good for the practical-method questions that need a student's own work examined. Mark loss in units, significant figures and method description responds best to individual script review.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry, Physics and Biology
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment is individual by definition and cannot be taught in a group. Content work at Standard Level can be, but Higher Level extension material is where the scarce specialist teaching sits and group settings dilute it.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature, both systems
subjects.description: Extended writing improves through feedback on the student's own work, which groups deliver poorly and school teachers often deliver well. This is a subject where asking the department for additional feedback should precede paying anybody.

subjects.name: Business, Economics and the humanities
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and case-study specificity respond well to small-group drilling, so these are among the better value group subjects. Internal Assessment commentaries in the IB remain individual work with firm word limits.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Provision is uneven across every provider model, and the school itself is often the strongest resource because its teachers hold the specific permissions required to teach these subjects. A specific request beats a general one.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay coaching
subjects.description: Individual, deadline-driven and bounded by academic-honesty rules. Criteria taught with their mark allocations, topics interrogated, feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing written for them. Group settings cannot do this at all.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A genuinely small specialism across every model, so availability rather than price is the limiting factor. Families should ask early in Year 12 rather than in the term the essay is due.

subjects.name: Study skills and organisation
subjects.description: Often the real problem behind a request for subject tuition, particularly in a Diploma year where four internal deadlines collide. Worth diagnosing before buying subject hours, because subject hours do not fix a planning failure.

sections.heading: The five things a near me search returns, compared
paragraphs: A tutoring search produces results that differ more in kind than in quality, and the first useful step is to sort them. Specialist agencies maintain a panel and match a tutor to a request, which works well when the panel is deep in the subject you need and poorly when it is not; the question to ask is how many tutors they have on your child's exact course and level, not how many in total. International marketplaces list large numbers of tutors across countries, which gives breadth and shifts all the verification work onto the parent, who has to judge experience from a profile.

Tuition centres have premises and run mostly group provision on a fixed timetable, which is efficient for standardised content and awkward for anything individual. Individuals advertising informally in a residents' group are usually the cheapest and the least verifiable, and in a thin market like this island the pool is small. And the school's own support is free, delivered by someone with full context, and consistently the least asked for of the five.

The table compares them on the terms a parent actually needs rather than on the terms each prefers to be judged by. Note the verification column particularly: the amount of checking a parent has to do varies enormously between models, and the models that ask least of a parent are not necessarily the ones that deliver most. IB Gram sits in the online one-to-one row, and its limitations are in that row alongside everybody else's.

sections.heading: Ask the department before you pay anybody
paragraphs: The cheapest useful option in this entire comparison is the one no tutoring company has a reason to mention. Your child's own teacher knows the student, the scheme of work, the mark scheme and the school's assessment calendar, and in most Abu Dhabi schools will give additional feedback or run a clinic if asked directly. The number of families who buy private tuition without ever having asked is remarkable.

Four specific requests are usually available and rarely made. Will you mark one extra past paper and tell us where the marks went, rather than giving a grade? Which specific topics are weakest, in syllabus language? Is there a lunchtime or after-school clinic, and would you recommend our child attend it? And what tier or level is our child on, what does it cap, and when is the entry submitted? Those four answers together are worth more than the first month of paid tuition, and they cost an email.

What school support generally cannot provide is a weekly hour of individual teaching, because departments do not have the capacity, and that is where paid tuition earns its place. But the sequence matters: ask first, then buy what the answers show is actually needed. A family that starts with the department arrives at a tutor knowing the specification, the tier, the weak topics and the assessment dates, which makes the first paid hour three times more useful than it would otherwise have been.

sections.heading: Group classes, honestly assessed
paragraphs: Group tuition is cheaper per hour and is routinely dismissed by one-to-one providers, which is a self-interested position rather than an analysis. A well-matched group of two to four at AED 80 to 180 per student is genuine value for standardised content, and for some students it is better than one-to-one because the pace is less relentless and hearing another student's wrong answer is instructive.

The condition is matching, and it is a hard condition. Every student in the group has to be on the same specification, the same tier and at roughly the same point, or the session divides into fractions. A group containing one student stuck on non-calculator algebra and another needing help with an Internal Assessment is two students receiving half a lesson each. That is why groups work for IGCSE content coverage and fail for IB Diploma work, where two students in the same room are frequently on different courses entirely.

From Al Jubail Island there is a second condition, which is the journey. Most centres sit around Al Raha, Khalifa City or the main island, twenty-five to thirty-five minutes away at the hour classes run, which turns a ninety-minute class into a three-hour commitment for the household. For a weekend class that may be acceptable. For a weekday evening it usually is not, and families from this island who try it tend to stop by half term. The table sets out when each format wins.

sections.heading: Two systems, two grading languages
paragraphs: Households running an IB child and an IGCSE child face a problem that has nothing to do with tutoring and distorts every decision about it: the two systems describe progress in languages that do not translate, and parents compare them anyway.

An IGCSE report gives a subject grade, either letters from A star to G on the Cambridge scale or numbers from 9 to 1 on the Pearson scale, and those two do not map onto each other cleanly either. An MYP report gives criterion levels per subject, usually out of eight per criterion, plus an overall subject level out of seven, and criterion levels are not percentages. A Diploma report gives a subject grade from 1 to 7 plus predicted points and, separately, criterion feedback on internal assessments. A 5 means something entirely different in the MYP and the Diploma.

The practical consequences are real. Parents conclude that one child is doing better than the other on no evidence. A Diploma 5 sounds mediocre and is a solid pass. An MYP 6 sounds strong and may conceal weak technical fluency, because criterion marking rewards communication and process. An IGCSE grade 6 is respectable and is below the common entry requirement for A-Level Mathematics. The table translates the vocabulary, and the point of it is to stop families spending tutoring money on the child whose report simply looks worse. The useful discipline is to stop comparing children and compare each child against the requirement they are actually heading towards. That is a fixed target with a published number attached, and it makes the question answerable.

sections.heading: The tutor hired through a residents' group
paragraphs: In most Abu Dhabi neighbourhoods the single largest tutoring channel is informal: a name passed between parents in a building or community group, hired directly, paid in cash, often excellent and entirely unverified. It deserves a fair assessment rather than dismissal, because the model has real strengths.

The strengths are trust, continuity, price and convenience. Somebody you know has used them, the rate is usually below agency rates, and the arrangement is flexible in a way an institution cannot be. For Key Stage 3 support, homework supervision and primary-age work, this is frequently the sensible choice and paying agency rates instead would be paying for a qualification the task does not use.

The weakness is specification mismatch and it is invisible. Reputation in these networks is built on a different child sitting a different paper. A tutor who was excellent for a Foundation-tier IGCSE student two years ago may be the wrong person for an Extended-tier candidate now, and nobody in the chain has done anything wrong. On this island the pool is also small, so the same two or three names circulate regardless of subject. Four questions fix most of it: which specification and tier, which paper allows a calculator, how many cohorts of this exact course have you taught, and do you hold a current MoHRE private tuition permit. Asking those four questions of somebody a neighbour recommended feels awkward and takes two minutes. A good tutor will not mind, and the ones who bristle at being asked what they have taught have answered the question anyway.

sections.heading: Checking what a provider claims
paragraphs: Every model in this comparison makes claims, and they vary from verifiable to meaningless. Sorting them takes a few minutes and is the single most protective thing a parent can do, because the claims that cannot be checked are the ones most often used.

A MoHRE private tuition permit is verifiable: ask to see it. It is granted free of charge for two years and is a legal clearance rather than a quality judgement. A tutor's taught cohorts are semi-verifiable: a specialist answers with a number and the tiers, a generalist answers with years of experience. A claim of regulator approval is not verifiable at all, because no UAE regulator approves individual private tutors on teaching merit; in Dubai, KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to a training institute with premises, which is a specific permit and not an endorsement of anyone's teaching.

Two claim types deserve particular scepticism. Examiner status, unless currently evidenced, implies nothing about access to marking, boundaries or paper content and is widely asserted. And self-published star ratings are not evidence: competitors in this market have shown two different ratings on the same page, and self-serving review markup is against Google's structured-data policy. For completeness: IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, publishes no self-asserted rating, and no school named on this page is a client or partner. None of this requires suspicion as a default posture. It requires asking the better question once, early, when the answer still has time to change a decision rather than explain a disappointment.

sections.heading: Which requests are genuinely hard from this address
paragraphs: A comparison is incomplete without a statement of limits, and no provider researched for this project publishes one. Here is ours, for a household on Al Jubail Island.

Comfortably covered at Abu Dhabi evening hours: IGCSE subjects at every tier on both specifications, Diploma Standard Level maths, biology, economics, business management and English A, and Middle Years support across the main subjects. These are requests we can normally fill within days at a slot after 6.30pm.

Genuinely tight: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Diploma chemistry and physics at Higher Level, the smaller Group 2 languages, Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision support in unusual subjects, Arabic as a first language, and weekend mornings in the fortnight after mocks when every family in the emirate wants one. A request in that group gets one of three answers: a waiting time with a date attached, a named tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist with that stated plainly, or an honest statement that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need. From an island where the local alternative is thin, a straight no in September is more useful than a yes that becomes a problem in February. The list changes through the year, too. A request that is comfortable in September can be tight in February, which is why we answer it at enquiry rather than publishing a permanent promise. Ask again in a different term and the answer may genuinely differ.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the limits of any credential
paragraphs: Whichever model a family chooses, two layers of regulation apply and it is worth knowing which does what, because the claims made about them are frequently wrong.

Schools are regulated by emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge. Dubai's are overseen by KHDA. Sharjah has its own Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies cover the whole country, and reading your own school's inspection report alongside its own reporting is a useful and free exercise.

Tutors are regulated federally. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, any specific figure is unverified. One condition matters especially in Abu Dhabi: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit carries a comparable restriction. Neither layer of regulation tells a parent whether somebody teaches well. That remains a question about taught cohorts, specifications and what happens in a trial lesson, and no credential substitutes for it.

faqs.question: What kinds of provider come back when I search for a tutor near this island?
faqs.answer: Five quite different things that look alike in a list. Specialist agencies that match a tutor from a panel. International marketplaces listing tutors across countries with no vetting of specification knowledge. Tuition centres with premises on the mainland running mostly group classes. Individuals advertising informally in residents' groups, which is the cheapest and least verifiable channel. And, invisibly, your child's own school, which is free and almost never asked. Each has a different price, a different strength and a different failure mode, and sorting them is the first useful step.

faqs.question: Should we ask the school for help before paying a tutor?
faqs.answer: Almost always, and very few families do. Four requests are usually available and rarely made: will you mark one extra past paper and say where the marks went rather than giving a grade; which topics are weakest, in syllabus language; is there a clinic and should our child attend; and what tier or level is our child on, what does it cap and when is the entry submitted. Those four answers are worth more than the first month of paid tuition and they cost one email. They also make any later paid hour considerably more productive.

faqs.question: Is a small group class worse than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Not inherently, and one-to-one providers who say so are arguing their own case. A matched group of two to four at AED 80 to 180 per student is genuine value for standardised IGCSE content, and some students do better in a group because the pace is less relentless and hearing another student's wrong answer is instructive. The condition is strict: everyone must share the specification, the tier and roughly the same position. Groups fail for IB Diploma work, where two students in a room are often on different courses entirely.

faqs.question: Can we get to a tuition centre from Al Jubail Island on a weekday?
faqs.answer: In principle, and most families who try stop by half term. The centres a household here might consider sit around Al Raha, Khalifa City or the main island, twenty-five to thirty-five minutes away at the hour classes run, which turns a ninety-minute class into a three-hour household commitment on a school night. For a weekend class that can work. For a weekday evening, after a school run that already crossed a bridge twice, it is a lot of driving for a lesson that is not individually aimed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send anyone to the island?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Jubail Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The honest limitations of that model are that it needs a quiet corner and a reliable connection, and that a very young primary child sometimes works better with somebody physically present. For IB and IGCSE work the trade is strongly favourable, because the tutor is chosen for the course rather than the journey.

faqs.question: How do I compare an MYP report with an IGCSE report?
faqs.answer: Carefully, because they measure different things in different units. An IGCSE report gives a tier-capped subject grade, either A star to G on the Cambridge scale or 9 to 1 on the Pearson one. An MYP report gives criterion levels, usually out of eight per criterion, plus an overall subject level out of seven, and criterion levels are not percentages. A Diploma grade is also out of seven but means something different again. Comparing two children across these scales produces confident conclusions from no evidence, which then misdirects the tutoring budget.

faqs.question: Why does a Diploma 5 feel disappointing when it is not?
faqs.answer: Because the number looks like a school mark and is not. A Diploma subject grade runs from 1 to 7, is awarded against externally moderated standards, and a 5 is a solid pass that satisfies a great many university requirements. Meanwhile an MYP 6 sounds strong and can conceal weak technical fluency, because criterion marking rewards communication and process alongside content. And an IGCSE grade 6 sounds respectable and sits below the common entry requirement for A-Level Mathematics. None of these scales translates, and all of them get translated anyway.

faqs.question: Is a tutor recommended in our community group a safe bet?
faqs.answer: A good starting point that still needs checking. The strengths of that channel are real: trust, continuity, a lower rate and flexibility, and for Key Stage 3 or primary work it is frequently the sensible choice. The weakness is invisible specification mismatch, because reputation in these networks is built on a different child sitting a different paper. On an island with a thin pool, the same two or three names circulate for every subject. Four questions settle most of it: the specification, the tier, how many cohorts of that exact course, and the MoHRE permit.

faqs.question: Which tutoring claims can I actually verify?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition permit, by asking to see it, remembering that it is a free legal clearance valid for two years rather than a judgement on teaching. A tutor's taught cohorts, semi-verifiably, because a specialist answers with a number and the tiers while a generalist answers with years of experience. What cannot be verified is regulator approval of an individual tutor, because no UAE regulator grants it, nor examiner status without current evidence, nor a self-published star rating, which in this market has appeared in two different versions on one page.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA training institute permit actually mean?
faqs.answer: It is the permit a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs, issued by KHDA as an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. It is a specific commercial licence for a specific kind of business. It is not an endorsement of anybody's teaching, and it does not apply to an individual tutor or to an online provider without premises there. Describing any provider as approved on the strength of it is a misreading, and IB Gram holds no such permit and claims none.

faqs.question: Which of our two children should the budget go to?
faqs.answer: Decide it from the calendar rather than from the reports, since the reports are written in incomparable languages. The questions that settle it are about closing deadlines: is an IGCSE tier entry still open, because that cannot be reopened; has an Internal Assessment topic been chosen, because the mark ceiling is set in the first fortnight; is a Year 11 or Year 13 technique problem heading into February unaddressed. Those outrank everything. One diagnostic hour per child, each ending in a written gap list, usually makes the answer obvious.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest for you to cover from this island?
faqs.answer: The tight group is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Diploma chemistry and physics at Higher Level, the smaller Group 2 languages, Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision in unusual subjects, Arabic as a first language, and weekend mornings in the fortnight after mocks. Comfortably covered are all IGCSE tiers on both specifications and Diploma Standard Level maths, biology, economics, business management and English A. For the tight group you get a date, a named alternative with its limits stated, or an honest no.

faqs.question: Does the regulator that inspects our school matter when choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and mostly because its report is free information. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK; Dubai's are overseen by KHDA; Sharjah has its own Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah has a Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. An inspection report comments on teaching quality by subject against a published framework, which sometimes shows that a department rather than a child is the weak link, and that changes where tutoring money should go.

faqs.question: Could the real problem be organisation rather than a subject?
faqs.answer: Frequently, particularly in a Diploma year, and it is worth diagnosing before buying subject hours. Most Diploma students who struggle are not defeated by the difficulty of a subject; they are defeated by four internal deadlines colliding in one month with nothing started early. Subject tuition does not fix that, and six weeks of it can be spent while the underlying problem continues. A single diagnostic session that identifies planning rather than content as the issue is the cheapest useful thing a family can buy in that situation.

faqs.question: Which campuses do the students you support near this island attend?
faqs.answer: Households on and around Al Jubail Island travel to campuses on Saadiyat Island and Yas Island and across to Al Raha and Khalifa City. The names that recur include Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, West Yas Academy, Repton School Abu Dhabi, Raha International School, Al Yasmina Academy and Reach British School, which between them run both the IB and British-curriculum programmes. Those names describe the local education map and nothing else. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them, and none of them is a client.

intro.heading: Where are you in the year? Everything follows from that
paragraphs: The honest first question for an Al Karamah family looking for a tutor is not which subject or which district, but what month it is and what has already happened. A request in September and the identical request in March describe completely different problems. In September almost everything is still available: content can be taught and consolidated, an internal assessment can be planned properly, a tier decision is still open. In March the content window has closed, several deadlines have passed, and what remains is examination technique and the cheapest available marks.

That is why this page is built around the calendar. Al Karamah households frequently run two of them at once, because siblings sit different systems: an IGCSE Year 11 facing a single terminal series, and a Diploma student facing two years of internal deadlines with no external examination at all in the first of them. The two calendars peak at different moments and compete for the same evenings, and the DP1 student is usually the one quietly neglected because nothing visible is due. By the time anything visible is due, in the first half of DP2, a fifth to nearly a third of each subject grade has already been settled by work produced in that quiet year.

There is a second reason to start with the calendar. Eight weeks of one session a week is eight to twelve hours of teaching, and that quantity has a ceiling. It can close one diagnosed content gap and re-test it. It can rebuild examination technique across a subject the student broadly knows, which is where most recoverable marks sit. It cannot teach two years of untaught content, and any service implying otherwise is selling a feeling rather than a plan. Knowing where you are in the year is what makes the difference between buying the first thing and buying the third.

Boards matter to the calendar in specific ways. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series, with the February and March series offered to India only, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session with November as the alternative route, and no IB date appears on this page because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than none.

One thing does not depend on the month. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which in practical calendar terms means a slot that does not move when island traffic is slow, and that reliability is what makes a counted eight-session block actually deliver eight sessions.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks actually have to achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks at one session a week is eight to twelve hours of teaching. Being blunt about that quantity is the most useful thing a tutoring page can do, because the gap between what a family hopes for and what the hours allow is where disappointment is manufactured. Within that envelope three things are reliably achievable and two are not.

Achievable: one diagnosed content gap closed and re-tested. For IGCSE mathematics that is usually a cluster such as histograms with unequal class widths or circle theorem reasoning. For Diploma chemistry it might be energetics sign conventions and uncertainty treatment. Also achievable: examination technique rebuilt across a subject the student broadly knows, which covers reading the question, allocating time by mark value, showing method where the scheme awards it separately and answering the command term asked. Most students lose a meaningful number of marks to process rather than ignorance, and that is recoverable in two months. Third: an internal assessment taken from a vague idea to a workable draft, provided the school's deadline allows it.

Not achievable: two years of untaught Higher Level or Extended content. If a DP2 student arrives in March with a third of the syllabus unmet, the honest plan targets the highest-value accessible topics and the papers where marks are cheapest, and says plainly that full coverage is unavailable in the time. Also not achievable: any promised grade, from anyone, at any price. A grade depends on the student's own work across two years, on internal assessment already submitted, and on boundaries nobody controls.

Setting the measure is what makes the eight weeks accountable. A timed paper in session one, marked against the published scheme with losses sorted by cause rather than topic. The same style of paper at session eight. An error log in between so nothing is taught twice. If the second script has not moved, either the plan targeted the wrong gap or the match is wrong, and both are ours to fix rather than the student's to absorb.

sections.heading: The year, term by term, across both boards
paragraphs: An Al Karamah household running an IGCSE Year 11 and a Diploma student is running two clocks that tick at different rates. Setting the two calendars side by side shows where they collide and which one is being silently deprioritised.

The autumn term is the quiet and valuable period for both. The IGCSE student is finishing content and should be starting full-length timed practice by the end of it. The Diploma student has no external examination pressure at all in DP1, which is exactly why the Exploration or Scientific Investigation should be planned and drafted now. Work done in the autumn is the cheapest work in the year, and almost nobody buys it.

January and February are the collision. IGCSE mocks land, Diploma mocks land, Diploma internal assessment deadlines land, and the Extended Essay final submission is usually due around the same stretch. Demand for specialist tutors across the emirate peaks in exactly these weeks, which means a family starting to look now is competing for whatever remains. The spring is then almost entirely revision for the IGCSE student and a sprint for the DP2 student.

After the papers the calendars diverge again. IGCSE results arrive in the summer for a June series, with a November resit route producing a result the following January. Diploma results arrive in the summer for a May session. For a DP1 student, the summer between the two Diploma years is the most under-used window in the whole programme: four to six sessions aimed at a specific weakness cost less and achieve more than the same hours bought in March of DP2.
