faqs.question: What should a month of IB or IGCSE tutoring cost in central Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package prices in this market put eight online sessions at around AED 799 a month and four in-home two-hour visits at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Those are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list, and they are the right numbers to check a quote against, because a monthly figure for a defined plan is the only comparable thing in this market.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tutoring in Abu Dhabi so much more expensive per hour?
faqs.answer: Because the rate includes a journey. A tutor crossing Abu Dhabi island to reach a flat in Al Manaseer at seven in the evening may spend close to an hour travelling for one hour taught, and somebody pays for that. It arrives as a higher hourly figure, quoted in this market at AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online, or as a two-hour minimum booking, or both. The two-hour minimum is the more expensive of the two, because the second hour of a weeknight double is rarely productive.

faqs.question: Do your tutors visit homes in Al Manaseer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Other Abu Dhabi providers do offer in-home tuition and it is a legitimate service with real advantages for younger children. For IB and IGCSE work the trade is usually poor value: you pay the travel premium and accept a shortlist limited to specialists who live within a drive of Al Khalidiyah. Our Al Manaseer lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Where do families with two children in two curricula usually waste money?
faqs.answer: Four places. Running three or four subjects at once, so each receives a third of an already short week, when sequencing them one per term would cost a third as much and work better. Keeping an older sibling's tutor for a younger child on a different specification, which is a mismatch nobody notices until a mock. Buying packages before anybody has diagnosed the gap, so paid hours go on topics the student already holds. And buying Internal Assessment support after the mark ceiling has already been set by the topic choice.

faqs.question: Is a package cheaper than paying for single sessions?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually yes. Per useful hour, often not. A ten-hour block looks like a discount, but if six of those hours cover material the student already holds, the effective rate on the four that mattered is more than double the sticker price. The sequence that actually saves money is one diagnostic hour first, with the child's marked work in front of the tutor, producing a written gap list, and only then hours bought against that list. Packages also tend to have the least flexible exit terms, which is where they hurt.

faqs.question: How much does tutoring cost compared with school fees?
faqs.answer: Usually a small fraction of the same year's school fee, which is context rather than permission. For scale, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total, and Dubai's sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25. Abu Dhabi fees are regulated separately by ADEK, so those figures are background. The argument is for deliberate spending: one well-aimed hour often returns more than anything else in the budget.

faqs.question: Which tutoring work genuinely needs an expensive specialist?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Diploma teaching, Internal Assessment and Extended Essay coaching, the extended-response Paper 3, an IGCSE tier diagnosis while the entry decision is still live, and mock-script dissection, where all the value depends on the reader knowing the mark scheme. What does not need the specialist band is supervised practice in a subject the student basically understands, Middle Years consolidation, arithmetic fluency and routine coverage in a Standard Level subject already sitting at a 5. Paying specialist rates for those is paying for a qualification the task does not use.

faqs.question: What is the least effective thing a family can spend tutoring money on?
faqs.answer: General revision bought in the final fortnight before an exam. By that point the limiting factor is almost never knowledge, the student has no capacity to absorb new content, and the hours mostly provide reassurance at a specialist rate. Close behind it: two-hour weeknight blocks, where the second hour is usually the least productive time bought all year, and homework supervision at specialist rates, which is something a quiet room and a worked-solutions file would do for nothing.

faqs.question: How do I compare quotes from three different Abu Dhabi providers?
faqs.answer: Send all three the same six-line brief, or the replies will not be comparable. State the curriculum, course and level precisely, the year group and school, what you want help with, your two workable evening windows, how many weeks you expect to run, and a direct request for a monthly figure for a defined plan with session length stated. Then ask every provider the same three closing questions: does the price include VAT, what happens if we stop after one session, and who by name will teach, with the courses and levels they have taught.

faqs.question: Should I expect an Abu Dhabi tutoring quote to be VAT-inclusive?
faqs.answer: That can only be answered by each provider for their own pricing, and any page that states a general rule about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees without a Federal Tax Authority citation is guessing at your expense. So the practical instruction is to ask in writing, from every provider you are comparing, whether the quoted AED figure includes VAT, and to ask for a tax registration number from any provider that says it charges it. A clear written answer makes a quote comparable; a verbal assurance does not.

faqs.question: Is there a licence fee built into what tutors charge in the UAE?
faqs.answer: There should not be, because the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Any provider implying that a government licence cost sits inside their rate is describing something that does not exist. Working without a permit does attract fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no official fine schedule has been published, so figures circulating online for that are unverified.

faqs.question: What conditions should I check on a free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Five. How long the trial is, and whether it is a full session or a shortened one. Whether a card is required to book it. Whether it is a genuine teaching session or a consultation with a coordinator who introduces a tutor afterwards. Whether the tutor who teaches the trial is the one who continues. And whether anything is owed or renews automatically if it does not suit. Our trial is a full free session with the continuing tutor, named in advance with their taught courses and levels, ending in a written gap list, with nothing owed and nothing renewing.

faqs.question: Do rates rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Published rates do not generally change, but what you can buy at them does. The specialists with capacity in September are the people families want in March, and by then they are committed. So a Year 11 or Year 13 request made in April is often met with either a waiting time or a tutor who covers the course rather than specialising in it, at the same price. The effect is a quality reduction rather than a price rise, which is harder to see on an invoice and more expensive in outcome.

faqs.question: Which campuses do your students around Al Manaseer attend?
faqs.answer: Families on the western island come from campuses in Al Bateen and nearby, and from the IB and British-curriculum schools further out, including the American Community School of Abu Dhabi, Al Bateen Academy, Cambridge International School Abu Dhabi, Repton School Abu Dhabi, Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and Raha International School. Those names are given to describe the local education map and nothing else. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any school named, and none of them is a client of ours.

faqs.question: If our budget only covers one child, which one should it go to?
faqs.answer: Whichever has the decision closing soonest rather than the louder complaint. An IGCSE tier entry closes and cannot be reopened, so it outranks almost everything. A Diploma Internal Assessment topic sets a mark ceiling in its first fortnight. A Year 11 or Year 13 technique problem has to be addressed before February. General consolidation, a Standard Level subject sitting comfortably and a Year 9 wobble can all wait a term at no cost. One diagnostic hour per child, each producing a written gap list, usually makes the answer obvious.

intro.heading: What a proximity search gets wrong on Al Maryah Island
paragraphs: Al Maryah Island is a financial and healthcare district with residential towers on top of it. Abu Dhabi Global Market sits here, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi sits here, The Galleria sits here. What does not sit here is a school. Not an IB World School, not a Cambridge centre, not a British-curriculum primary. Every child living on the island crosses a bridge to get to class, which means the phrase parents type into Google when they want help has no local answer to return.

That matters more than it sounds. A search built on distance assumes the thing you need is evenly distributed, the way pharmacies or dry cleaners are. Tutoring is not. An IB Diploma Chemistry HL teacher who understands how the internal assessment is marked against criteria, or an IGCSE Physics specialist who knows why Paper 6 wrecks otherwise strong candidates, is a narrow specialism. There are not many of them in any emirate, and the odds that one happens to live within a fifteen-minute drive of a tower on Al Maryah Island are poor.

So families end up making a trade without noticing they made it. They pick the nearest available person, who turns out to teach a different board, or teaches the right board at the wrong level, or teaches maths generally rather than the specific route the school entered the child for. The lessons happen. The paper the child actually sits is not the paper being practised. Three months later the mock result has not moved and nobody can say why.

IB Gram was built to remove that trade entirely. Lessons run over live video, one student and one teacher, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past papers on screen. Because nobody is driving, the pool a family on Al Maryah Island can reach is the whole pool rather than the slice inside a traffic radius. That is the entire argument, and it is an argument about syllabus coverage, not convenience.

This page answers the honest version of the question. Where the IB and IGCSE schools near Al Maryah Island actually are. What tutoring costs across Abu Dhabi, in dirhams, with the sources named. What the permit rules say about who may legally teach your child privately. Which exam series a UAE candidate sits, counted backwards from the paper. And what happens when no specialist is free, because that happens and pretending otherwise is how trust gets lost.

One thing to state plainly before anything else, because it shapes everything that follows: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at an island address. Every lesson described below happens online, one student and one teacher, over live video.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.programmesIntro: Al Maryah Island children are spread across boards, because the island has no catchment school to funnel them. A family in one tower may have a Diploma candidate at a Saadiyat IB school and a Year 10 sibling sitting Pearson Edexcel across the bridge. These are the programmes that come up most.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two separate boards, often confused. Cambridge uses four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics, with a Core and Extended split in several subjects. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1 and does not tier the same subjects the same way. The paper structure differs, the formula booklets differ, and the mark schemes reward different things.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. One competitor page ranking for Abu Dhabi queries states six subjects. Five is what the official clarification says, and it is worth checking your child's option block against it in Year 9 rather than Year 11.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at higher level, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject and is marked against published criteria identified by letter. Most of the damage in a Diploma year is done by the coursework calendar, not by the final papers, because the deadlines land while teaching is still running.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families usually meet the Diploma at a school on Saadiyat Island, Al Reem Island or in the Khalifa City corridor, which from Al Maryah Island means a bridge crossing twice a day. The practical effect is that a Diploma student here has less usable evening time than a classmate who walks to school, so we front-load coursework coaching into the autumn rather than the spring.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with command terms that do most of the work. Students who have only ever been marked on right answers find criterion-based marking disorienting, because a correct answer with no justification scores badly. The MYP personal project in the final year is the first piece of independent extended work most of these students meet.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is where Abu Dhabi tutoring demand spikes, and it is a different problem from ordinary catch-up. A student can finish the Middle Years Programme with strong criterion scores and still be short of the algebraic fluency that Analysis and Approaches assumes from week one. That gap is diagnosable in a single lesson and usually takes six to ten weeks to close.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.subjectsIntro: Requests from the island skew towards the subjects that decide university applications: maths at both IB routes, the three sciences, economics and English. Each subject below is taught against a named specification, and the first lesson starts from your child's own last assessment rather than from a generic diagnostic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy IB route. Higher level adds Maclaurin series, differential equations and more demanding integration, and Paper 3 asks students to extend an unfamiliar idea under time pressure. Marks are lost on justification rather than arithmetic: a correct answer with no working attracts method marks it never earns.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work. Students assume it is the easy route and then meet hypothesis testing, chi-squared and graph theory at higher level. The calculator is part of the assessment, so a student who cannot drive their own handset efficiently loses marks that have nothing to do with mathematics.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended opens the A* to C range and is what any student aiming at a Diploma or A-level maths route needs. The usual damage sits in algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs and the multi-step problems late in Paper 4, where candidates abandon a question rather than secure the first two marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, no coursework, and a formula sheet that differs from Cambridge. Students moving between the two boards mid-course are the group most at risk, because the topics overlap while the question style and the expected layout of a solution do not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits do most of the harm at IGCSE; at IB it is the data-analysis and uncertainty work. Cambridge Paper 6 on practical skills is answered badly by candidates who have done plenty of experiments and never been taught how to write up error analysis for a marker.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate grades at higher level. The internal assessment is where Diploma candidates lose the most, usually by choosing a question that cannot generate enough quantitative data to analyse properly. That is a conversation to have in September, not in February.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap, and the command terms are the fix. Students who write everything they know about a topic score below students who answer the verb in the question. Extended-response practice against the published mark scheme moves grades faster than any amount of re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and most candidates draw them incompletely: no axis labels, no shifted curve, no indication of the new equilibrium. The higher-level paper three quantitative work is mechanical once practised and is the cheapest set of marks available on the course.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time, and the individual oral asks students to connect a global issue to two texts. Structure beats insight here: a clear line of argument held across ten minutes scores better than a cleverer reading delivered without shape.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in UAE private schools by federal requirement, and it is frequently the subject nobody plans for. Support here is about the school's own scheme of work and the assessment it sets, since additional or different content needs Ministry permission.

sections.heading: What "IB IGCSE tutor near me" actually returns on Al Maryah Island
paragraphs: A proximity search on Al Maryah Island returns agencies registered elsewhere in Abu Dhabi, marketplace profiles with no board named, and a handful of independent tutors whose adverts list every subject from Year 1 to A-level. None of that tells you whether the person can teach Cambridge 0580 Extended or IB Applications and Interpretation SL, which is the only question that matters.

The reason is structural rather than anyone's fault. Tutoring supply in the emirate is thin at the specialist end and thick at the generalist end. Plenty of people can help a Year 7 with fractions. Far fewer can mark an IB internal assessment against criterion C and explain why the sample scored what it did. When you filter by distance first, you are filtering on the abundant variable and ignoring the scarce one.

Island geography makes this sharper than it would be in Khalifa City. There is no school on Al Maryah Island, so there is no local teacher population attached to one. In a villa community, the person two streets away may well teach at the school your child attends. On Al Maryah Island, the person two floors down works in banking or healthcare. Proximity is not even a weak proxy here; it is noise.

The practical move is to invert the filter. Decide the board and the syllabus code, decide the level, then ask who can teach it and when they are free. Distance drops out of the problem once the lesson is over video, and the pool of people who can genuinely teach your child's paper stops being a handful and becomes the whole set.

sections.heading: The schools near Al Maryah Island, and which board each one means
paragraphs: Because the island has no school of its own, the question of which syllabus your child sits is settled by whichever bridge the family crosses each morning. That makes the school map practically useful rather than decorative: it is the thing that determines which specification a tutor needs to know.

The island cluster, which in practice means Saadiyat, Al Reem and the Al Bateen side of the mainland, carries both the IB continuum and the English National Curriculum through IGCSE and A-level. The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor carries most of the emirate's Diploma capacity along with British and American provision. Those two clusters cover the overwhelming majority of Al Maryah Island children.

Every school in the table is licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate of Abu Dhabi. ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, and a parent choosing between two schools should read the most recent published rating on the authority's own site rather than relying on a tutoring company's summary of it.

One caution worth stating. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars the same thing. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document. Either way, the lesson for parents is clear: do not arrange private lessons with your child's own classroom teacher in Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Abu Dhabi, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest option and work upwards, because that is the order a budget actually gets built in. A university-student tutor working online is the floor of this market: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That buys homework supervision and someone to keep a student company through a problem set. It does not buy internal-assessment criteria or Paper 6 technique.

A step up, a qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which makes it the only competitor in this cluster to print an hourly rate at all. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-level teaching runs roughly AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table showing AED 200 to 450 plus. At the top, BartyED quotes AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Now the comparison the island makes relevant. An in-home visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. Against a qualified online tutor at AED 150 to 300, the gap is the travel premium, and for an Al Maryah Island address that premium is buying bridge crossings and parking. It is not buying better teaching, and it narrows the pool to people willing to make the drive.

Monthly packages give a cleaner planning number than hourly rates. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one hour a week run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year support. Every figure here is a market rate published by the named provider, not an IB Gram price; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson, when we know what the work actually involves.

sections.heading: Why a fifteen-minute radius is the wrong filter, in numbers
paragraphs: Work through what a distance filter does to the candidate pool. Begin with every private tutor in the emirate who can teach secondary mathematics. Remove those who teach only the American or Ministry curriculum, and the set shrinks. Remove those who do not teach IB at all, and it shrinks again. Now split the remainder between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and between higher and standard level, and the set that matches one particular Diploma student is small.

Then apply geography on top. Require that this person be willing to drive to an island tower twice a week at a time that fits around a school run that already crosses a bridge. Each of those conditions is independent of teaching ability, and together they cut harder than any of the subject filters did. What survives is not the best match; it is the match that happens to be convenient.

Online delivery removes the last filter and leaves the subject filters intact. That is the whole mechanism, and it is worth being precise about what it does not do. It does not make a mediocre tutor good. It does not remove the need to check credentials. It does not suit every child, and a student who genuinely cannot hold attention on a screen for an hour needs a different plan. What it does is stop distance from deciding who teaches your child.

There is a second-order effect that island families notice quickly. Because no travel time is being paid for, a session can be 45 minutes when 45 minutes is what the work needs, or two short sessions in a week rather than one long one. An in-home tutor crossing two bridges will not sell you half an hour, which means the format quietly dictates the pedagogy.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition compared for an island address
paragraphs: The honest comparison has four variables: what you pay, what the logistics cost you in time, how wide the tutor pool is, and what happens when something changes. For a family on Al Maryah Island, the second and fourth matter more than they would elsewhere, because the island is reached by bridge and because a tower address makes a last-minute reschedule harder for anyone driving.

Group tuition at a centre is the cheapest per student and the least adaptable. It works when a cohort is genuinely at the same point on the same syllabus, which is unusual once students are inside a Diploma or a tiered IGCSE. For an island family it also adds a round trip at the worst hour of the day, which is the thing the format was supposed to save.

In-home one-to-one is the format parents instinctively trust and the one the market prices highest, because the price includes a car. The teaching can be excellent. The constraint is supply: you are choosing from people who will travel to you at a given hour, and in a specialist subject that set may contain nobody at all. Note again that IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; this row describes what the market charges, for comparison.

Online one-to-one costs less than the in-home equivalent, draws on the whole pool, and makes the screen itself useful. A past paper can be annotated by both people at once, the session can be recorded for revision, and a graph can be built live instead of copied. The real trade is that it demands a quiet room and a working connection, and the parent has to make the first one happen.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in the Abu Dhabi tutoring market answers in writing, and it is easy to answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no fee listed.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody, and a figure circulating online could not be verified. If a provider tells you a specific penalty number, treat that as a signal about the provider.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. IB Gram does not hold a regulator permit of any kind and does not claim one. We are a matching platform delivering lessons online, and we say so rather than borrowing authority we have not earned.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Families on Al Maryah Island plan around flights, school holidays and work calendars, so the exam calendar needs reading in reverse: not when the paper is, but what has to be true eight weeks earlier. The fixed points differ by board, and getting them wrong is expensive in a way that no amount of tutoring fixes afterwards.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so an Abu Dhabi parent reading a tutoring page that quotes February dates is reading a page written for a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. For the most recent completed cycle, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and they are what makes the pattern checkable; the live timetable for an upcoming series should always be read from the board's own provisional timetable page, because dates can be revised.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session. We do not publish a specific IB examination or results date on this page: the IB organisation blocks automated checking, and a date we cannot verify is not worth printing for a parent to act on. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed calendar, including internal coursework deadlines, and those internal deadlines are usually the ones that decide a grade.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops: academic honesty on internal assessment
paragraphs: This matters more in Abu Dhabi than the local market admits, because the same search results that return tutors also return services selling finished coursework. One operator in this space advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. Buying one puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding, which in a Diploma year can cost the whole qualification rather than one grade.

The boundary is not vague and it is worth knowing precisely. A tutor may teach the subject content an assessment draws on, explain how the published criteria are applied and what distinguishes one band from the next, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, teach data handling and referencing, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. That is teaching.

A tutor may not supply text that ends up in the submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, produce the analysis, or hand over a worked exemplar to be adapted. IB Gram does not write, finish or supply assessed coursework of any kind, and a tutor asked to will decline and tell us. We would rather lose the booking than have a student face a malpractice panel over an hour of our help.

There is also a copyright line. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them, cite the official source, and teach from material the student legitimately has through their school. If a provider offers you a library of mark schemes, that tells you something about how they handle rules generally.

sections.heading: Coverage, waiting time, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is strange, because every tutoring network has one. Demand is not evenly spread across subjects: maths and the sciences at IGCSE and Diploma level are requested constantly, while a Diploma higher-level subject in a smaller group can go weeks without a request and then need a specialist within days.

What that means for an Al Maryah Island family is a realistic expectation rather than a promise. For core maths and science at IGCSE and Diploma level, a match is normally arranged within a few days, with the trial lesson in the same week. For a narrower higher-level subject, or for a specific combination such as Applications and Interpretation HL plus economics with one tutor, it can take longer, and we will tell you that at the enquiry rather than after you have waited.

When no UAE-based specialist is available for a subject, we say so and offer the alternative explicitly: a specialist elsewhere in our network teaching the same specification over the same video platform, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time so your child's evening is unaffected. That is disclosed before you book, never discovered afterwards. Several providers in this market route UAE families to numbers in other countries without mentioning it, and the concealment is the problem rather than the geography.

If a match turns out to be wrong after the trial, say so and we change it. That is what the free trial lesson is for: a specific, no-obligation hour whose only purpose is to tell you whether this particular teacher and this particular child work together. A platform that cannot be told no is not worth using.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it affects a tutoring plan
paragraphs: Five bodies cover private schooling in the UAE, and knowing which one applies to your child changes what you can look up. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. In Dubai it is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there.

Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same in its own. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority goes further still, approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits at emirate level.

The practical use for an Al Maryah Island parent is narrow and real. ADEK publishes inspection outcomes, so a tutoring plan can be built against what the regulator says about a school rather than what a prospectus says. If a school's published report flags attainment in mathematics, that is a reason to look harder at your own child's maths data rather than a reason to panic.

There is also a federal baseline worth knowing. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the mandatory subjects running alongside your child's international curriculum, and it explains why a Diploma or IGCSE timetable in the UAE is fuller than the same programme would be elsewhere.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB or IGCSE tutor based on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it is the wrong thing to search for. Al Maryah Island is a financial and healthcare district with residential towers and no K-12 school, so there is no local teacher population attached to a campus the way there is in Khalifa City or Al Bateen. Anyone advertising as near you is near you by accident rather than because they teach your child's syllabus. The better question is who can teach Cambridge 0580 Extended or Analysis and Approaches HL, and that question is answered by a video link rather than a postcode.

faqs.question: Will a tutor be sent to an apartment on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Al Maryah Island family is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We target the home-tutor search because it is what parents type, and then we answer it honestly: the market does sell in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and we think a specialist on a screen at AED 150 to 300 is the better purchase for an exam course. The comparison table above sets out both sides.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student living on the island?
faqs.answer: For core maths and the three sciences at IGCSE or Diploma level, usually within the same week, including the free trial lesson. For a narrower higher-level Diploma subject, or for a request that one tutor covers two subjects, it can take up to a fortnight at peak times. We tell you which case you are in at the enquiry rather than after you have waited. If nobody suitable is available at all, we say that too and you lose nothing but an email.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Maryah Island children usually attend?
faqs.answer: Because no school sits on the island, families cross a bridge. In practice that means the island cluster of Saadiyat, Al Reem and the Al Bateen side, or the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor where most of the emirate's IB Diploma and British-curriculum capacity sits. All of them are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which publishes its inspection outcomes. We name schools as context for the local education ecosystem and claim no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Does the bridge crossing change what time a lesson can start?
faqs.answer: It does, and it is the most practical scheduling fact for island families. A child at a Reem Island school can be ready for a 16:30 start. A child commuting from Khalifa City or Saadiyat realistically needs 18:00 or later on a weekday, because a 15:30 school finish becomes a 16:45 arrival on a normal afternoon and worse on a bad one. We set the slot to survive the bad afternoon, since a lesson the student arrives at exhausted is wasted money.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour for a family in central Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the range. Budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and IB teaching runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Those are the market's figures, named by source; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with an Al Maryah Island family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you can ask to see it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own smart app and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine amount is officially published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own classroom teacher tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: You should not arrange it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK document, but the direction is unambiguous. Using an independent specialist avoids the conflict entirely and has a side benefit: a second teacher explains a topic differently, and that different explanation is often what makes it land.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit if they are in an Abu Dhabi Cambridge school?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series for UAE centres, with the November series acting as the resit route. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so any page quoting February dates to a UAE parent is written for a different country. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so ask your exams officer which zone applies.

faqs.question: If my child sits Pearson Edexcel, when does the results date fall?
faqs.answer: The board runs May and June and November series. Looking at the most recent completed cycle gives the pattern: the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are citations rather than forecasts. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so for an upcoming sitting read the official timetable page rather than any tutoring company's summary.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry equivalency count need on the British track?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A ranking competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring company performs, and you should confirm the current requirement on the official channel.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do on an IB internal assessment, and where do they stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the subject content the assessment draws on, explain how each published criterion is applied, press on a research question until it is answerable, teach data handling and referencing, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor cannot supply text for the submission, rewrite a paragraph into final form, produce the analysis or hand over an exemplar to adapt. IB Gram does not write or finish assessed coursework, and a tutor asked to will decline. Services selling completed internal assessments put the candidate at risk of malpractice.

faqs.question: Is online one-to-one genuinely as effective as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For an exam course at IGCSE or Diploma level, usually yes, and sometimes better, because the screen is working for you. Both people annotate the same past paper, graphs are built live, and the session can be recorded for revision. Two conditions have to hold: a quiet room and a stable connection. For a younger child who needs physical supervision to stay on task, the honest answer is different, and we will say so rather than sell you a format that will not work.

faqs.question: What if we try a tutor and my child does not get on with them?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the match. That is the purpose of the free trial lesson: one hour, no payment, no package, designed to find out whether this teacher and this student work together. Your child's view counts, because an hour a week with someone they cannot talk to achieves very little regardless of how strong the subject knowledge is. There is no obligation after the trial and no penalty for saying the match was wrong.

faqs.question: Can an Al Maryah Island slot shift during Ramadan or a month of family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most island families need both. Lessons can shift to later evening timing through Ramadan, and because nobody is travelling to you, a slot can follow a family that is out of the country for a fortnight as long as the time zone difference is workable. We ask for notice when a slot moves permanently so the tutor's week can be rebuilt, but a one-off change is routine. Scheduling defaults to Gulf Standard Time and stays there unless you ask otherwise.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking for a quote for two children in different programmes?
faqs.answer: Each child's board and syllabus code, their current level or tier, the most recent marked assessment for each, and the two time windows that genuinely work after the school run. Siblings in different programmes is common on Al Maryah Island because there is no catchment school funnelling everyone into one syllabus. We schedule a household rather than a student, usually back-to-back slots on the same evening, which keeps one quiet room doing double duty.

intro.heading: Why nearness is the wrong thing to optimise in Al Muroor
paragraphs: A search for a tutor near me is a search for a solved logistics problem. In Al Muroor that instinct is sound, because the neighbourhood is dense, the school runs go in four directions and nobody has a spare hour in the car. The difficulty is that nearness and suitability are not the same variable, and in IB and IGCSE teaching they pull in opposite directions.

Consider what a short radius actually contains. Al Muroor sits inland behind Muroor Road, with Al Mushrif, Al Nahyan, Al Wahda and Al Karamah within a few minutes and Airport Road along one side. Draw a five-kilometre circle and you capture a large resident population and a modest number of qualified subject teachers who tutor privately in the evenings. Narrow that to people who teach IB Chemistry Higher Level, or Cambridge 0580 Extended specifically rather than maths generally, or the mathematical exploration, and the circle usually contains one or two candidates. Narrow it again to those free at 7pm on the evening your household can hold, and it frequently contains nobody.

That is the trade every Abu Dhabi family makes without seeing it. They choose a tutor who can reach the building and accept whatever subject depth comes with them. For a Year 9 top-up that is fine. For an IB Diploma subject at Higher Level, or an IGCSE Extended entry with a tier decision riding on it, it is the whole quality question, and it is being decided by geography. Nobody chose that trade deliberately. It happens because the search began with a map rather than with a syllabus, and the map answered first.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Every Al Muroor lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the shortlist for your child's actual subject and level is the whole shortlist rather than the part of it that lives nearby. It also means the slot can be late enough to work after a school run from Al Reem Island or Al Raha, because nobody is adding a tutor's drive to the end of yours.

The other thing this page is about is the household rather than the student. Al Muroor families frequently run two children on two curricula, one sitting IGCSEs and one in the Diploma, with three or four subjects between them that need help in the same school year. That is a scheduling problem, a cost problem and a consistency problem all at once, and it is handled very differently from a single weekly session for one child. Treating it as one child's problem four separate times is how a household ends up with four commitments, three of which are not the one that mattered.

The Diploma's distinctive load is not the difficulty of any one subject but the number of internal deadlines running at once, which is where most students actually come unstuck.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Muroor commute to campuses on Al Reem Island, Saadiyat Island and the Al Raha corridor, where Higher Level cohorts are small. That is exactly the situation in which a nearby generalist is the wrong answer and a subject specialist on a screen is the right one.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Muroor households most often need across both curricula, with an honest note on which are well covered and which are genuinely scarce in this market.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics AA and AI
subjects.description: Both Diploma maths courses, including the exploration worth 20% of the grade and, at Higher Level, the extended-response Paper 3. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the single scarcest teaching skill in Abu Dhabi and the clearest case for widening the search beyond a short radius.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 sets a non-calculator and a calculator paper per tier; Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator on both. Most recoverable marks sit in non-calculator fluency and in showing method on questions the student can already answer.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and the data-based questions that reward precise language. The Internal Assessment is where most Diploma chemistry marks are won or lost, and tutors who can coach it without touching the writing are in short supply.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves account for most mark loss, and the practical-skills questions assume laboratory experience a student cannot acquire from a textbook. Describing an experimental method precisely is a trainable, heavily rewarded skill.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides grades here more than content recall: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate are marked differently and students answer all four the same way. Statistical analysis in the Internal Assessment is the common weak point.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry and Biology
subjects.description: The science triple and double award routes diverge in content and in grade ceiling, and families frequently do not know which their child sits. Marks cluster in recall precision and in correct use of units and significant figures.

subjects.name: IB English A and English B
subjects.description: Two very different courses, one for first-language study of literature and language and one for acquisition, with different assessments including the Individual Oral. Choosing the wrong one is a common and expensive error in an international cohort like Abu Dhabi's.

subjects.name: IB Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation command terms carry the marks, not the breadth of real-world reading. The Internal Assessment commentaries have strict word limits, and the commonest avoidable loss is exceeding them.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay coaching
subjects.description: Criteria taught explicitly with their mark allocations, topics interrogated for depth, and written feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is written, supplied or restructured for the student, and that boundary is stated before the first session.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, and the subject most likely to be ignored until a report arrives. It is also one where provision is uneven, so a specific request is better than a general one.

sections.heading: What a short radius around Al Muroor actually contains
paragraphs: Nearness buys convenience, and convenience is worth something. What it does not buy is subject depth, and the mathematics of that is worth setting out because almost nobody does it before hiring. The pool of private tutors around any dense Abu Dhabi district is reasonably large for general secondary work and shrinks sharply with every condition you add.

Add a curriculum and it halves. Add a specific syllabus code and it halves again. Add a level, Higher rather than Standard, Extended rather than Core, and it halves once more. Then add the only time your household can actually hold, which after a school run from Al Reem Island or the Al Raha corridor is 6.30pm or later, and the set is frequently empty. At that point a family either changes the subject they ask for help with or accepts a tutor who covers the course rather than specialising in it, usually without being told which has happened.

The table below works through the narrowing for the subjects Al Muroor families ask about most. The point is not that local tutors are poor; many are excellent. It is that geography is a filter with no relationship to teaching quality, and applying it first means the quality filter runs second on whatever is left. Removing the geography filter reverses the order, which is the entire argument for one-to-one delivery over live video in a city laid out like this one. There is a simpler version of this test. Ask the question you would actually want answered, then count how many people in your district could answer it. If the answer is one, geography has already chosen your tutor for you.

sections.heading: Two children, two curricula, one evening
paragraphs: The household rather than the student is the right unit of planning in Al Muroor, because the common case here is two children in two systems. One sitting IGCSEs at a school in Al Mushrif, one in the Diploma on Al Reem Island. Different finish times, different report formats, different assessment vocabularies, and deadlines that land in the same fortnight without anybody having coordinated them.

Run that badly and you get four tutoring sessions a week spread across two children and three subjects, a diary nobody can hold, and a parent arbitrating between competing claims on the dining table. Run it deliberately and the same money does considerably more. The central decision is sequencing: which subject needs the hour now, and which can wait a term without a cost.

Some things cannot wait. An IGCSE tier decision cannot wait, because the entry closes. A Diploma Internal Assessment topic cannot wait, because the mark ceiling is set in the first fortnight. A mock-paper technique problem in Year 11 cannot wait past February. Other things can. General consolidation in Year 10, a Standard Level subject sitting comfortably at a 5, or a Year 9 wobble are all legitimately deferrable. The table sets out how a two-child household typically sequences a year, which is a more useful planning document than any list of subjects. Write the sequence down in September and keep it where both parents can see it. Households that hold a written plan spend less and argue less, because the question in February is no longer which child shouts loudest but what the sheet said in September and whether the evidence has changed it.

sections.heading: What an IB week and an IGCSE week demand of a household
paragraphs: Parents moving a second child from IGCSE into the Diploma are regularly surprised by how different the load feels, and the difference is structural rather than about difficulty. An IGCSE year is dominated by terminal exams. Nearly all the marks arrive in one window, so the work is cumulative and the pressure is concentrated at the end.

A Diploma year is the opposite shape. Six subjects each carry an Internal Assessment, and the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service sit on top. Those deadlines are set internally by the school and they land throughout the two years. A Diploma student rarely fails because a subject is too hard; they fail because four internal deadlines coincide in November and nothing was started early. That is a planning problem, and it responds to a planning intervention rather than to more teaching hours.

This changes what a tutor is for. For the IGCSE child, a tutor is mostly closing knowledge and technique gaps against a terminal paper. For the Diploma child, a tutor is often doing that plus holding a line on an Internal Assessment timetable the school set and nobody is tracking. Both are legitimate. They are not the same purchase, and a household buying the same thing twice usually underserves one child. One further consequence worth planning for: a Diploma child needs an adult looking twelve weeks ahead, while an IGCSE child mostly needs one looking at last week's script. If the same tutor is asked to do both jobs for both children, one of those two jobs is quietly not being done.

sections.heading: Which subjects are easy to cover here, and which are genuinely scarce
paragraphs: Every tutoring site in this market implies that every subject is always available. None of them disclose a coverage limit, which makes the claim worth less than an honest answer. Some subjects are straightforward to staff well at an Abu Dhabi evening hour. Others are not, and a family planning a year deserves to know which is which before committing to a plan that depends on the scarce one.

Broadly, IGCSE maths and the IGCSE sciences at either tier are well covered, as are Diploma Standard Level maths, biology and business management. The pressure points are Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Diploma chemistry and physics at Higher Level, the less common Group 2 languages, and specialist Extended Essay supervision in unusual subjects. Arabic as a first language is uneven. Theory of Knowledge is a genuinely small field.

What we do with that is state it. A request for a scarce combination gets one of three answers: a waiting time with a date attached, a named tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist available with that limitation spelt out, or an honest statement that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need. The third answer is sometimes the right one and it is always better than a mismatch that consumes a term. What never happens is a silent substitution: you know who is teaching your child, and what they have actually taught, before the trial lesson rather than after it.

sections.heading: What a nearby tutor knows about your child's school, and what they do not
paragraphs: One real argument for a local tutor deserves a straight answer rather than dismissal. A tutor who lives in the area and has taught several children from the same school knows things a stranger does not: which teacher sets which kind of homework, how that department sequences topics, which mock paper gets reused, how a report is phrased when a child is drifting. That is genuine local knowledge and it has value.

It is also replaceable, and it is narrower than it looks. The knowledge is about the school, not about the neighbourhood, and a tutor who has taught six students from a Reem Island campus online has it in exactly the same measure as one who drives there. Meanwhile the parts of a child's situation that actually decide the grade, which syllabus they sit, which paper is non-calculator, which criteria the Internal Assessment is marked against, where their own scripts lose marks, are not local knowledge at all. They are subject knowledge, and they are what a short radius most often forces a family to compromise on.

The practical answer is to ask for both and insist on the second. Ask any tutor how many students they have taught on that specific course and level, and how many from schools like your child's. A tutor who can answer the first question precisely is worth more than one who can only answer the second, because what your child is assessed on is set by the IB, by Cambridge or by Pearson, and none of them vary by district.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor near you
paragraphs: A search for a tutor near me in Abu Dhabi will surface a mix of agencies, platforms, tuition centres and individuals advertising informally, and they are not all operating on the same legal footing. This is checkable and most parents never check it.

Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page for the permit lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure quoted online is unverified.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. In Dubai, that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. Nothing in either route amounts to a regulator endorsing anybody's teaching, and the phrase approved tutors, in whatever form you see it, should be treated as marketing rather than as a credential. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and any page in this market that claims one is worth a second look.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in an already full week
paragraphs: Any plan for a nearby tutor has to fit a school week that is fuller than the international curriculum alone. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects run alongside IB or IGCSE rather than replacing part of it.

The detail in the published guidance shows the scale of the commitment. KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements for Dubai, the fullest document of its kind in the country, calculate instructional time in forty-minute lesson units and advise that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. They require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes outright because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA permission, and using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is not allowed.

For a household in Al Muroor the consequences are entirely practical. A Year 11 carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies has no slack in the week, and a Diploma student has less. That argues for one well-aimed session rather than two vague ones, for sixty minutes rather than two hours, and for honesty about which subject genuinely needs the hour. It is also worth knowing that for Ministry equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required IGCSE subjects, which surprises many parents who assumed the opposite.
bullets: Arabic, Social Studies and Islamic Studies are the federal baseline in every private school

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, for whichever track your child is on
paragraphs: A household running both curricula will eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and the requirements differ by track. This matters for UAE university applications and for some employment routes, and it is handled by the Ministry rather than by any school or tutoring provider. Nobody should present it as something they perform or guarantee on your behalf.

On the British track, the published requirement is a pass in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which contradicts the published rule, and it is the kind of error a family can plan a year around.

On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB there is no published points threshold that could be verified for this page, so no figure appears here. Confirm all of it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on any of it, including this summary, and note that tutoring is not a requirement of the process.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a tutor actually lives near Al Muroor?
faqs.answer: Less than the search implies. Nearness buys convenience, and in a district with school runs going four directions that is worth something. What it does not buy is subject depth, and the two conditions conflict. A five-kilometre circle around Muroor Road holds plenty of competent general tutors, a handful who teach a specific IGCSE syllabus and tier, and often one or two who teach a Diploma subject at Higher Level. Once an evening slot is added, the set is frequently empty. Removing the distance condition is what lets the subject condition be met properly.

faqs.question: Can one arrangement cover an IGCSE child and a Diploma child at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Al Muroor that is the normal case rather than the unusual one. Two children in two systems means different finish times, different report formats and deadlines landing in the same fortnight. The workable pattern is one weekly session each, in the subject with the widest gap, both from 6pm or later, with the rest of the year sequenced rather than run at once. Tier work in the autumn, Internal Assessment coaching in the winter, whole papers from February. Four concurrent subjects is what makes a household plan collapse.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building near Muroor Road?
faqs.answer: Some Abu Dhabi providers do offer that, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs the journey. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Muroor lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gains are a slot late enough to work after a long school run, a tutor chosen for the subject rather than the postcode, and an hour of teaching with no commute inside it.

faqs.question: Which IB and IGCSE subjects are hardest to staff at an Abu Dhabi evening hour?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the tightest, followed by Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Diploma chemistry and physics at Higher Level, the smaller Group 2 languages, specialist Extended Essay supervision in unusual subjects, and Theory of Knowledge, which is a genuinely small field. Arabic as a first language is uneven. IGCSE maths and sciences at either tier are comfortable, as are Standard Level Diploma maths, biology and business management. A request in the tight group gets a date, a named alternative with its limits stated, or an honest no.

faqs.question: How do I judge whether a tutor really knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask two specific questions and listen for precision rather than enthusiasm. First, which specification and which papers, by code: Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. Second, how many cohorts they have taught on that exact course and level. A tutor who can name which paper is non-calculator, what the Internal Assessment criteria are worth and where students typically lose marks is demonstrating knowledge. A tutor who answers in general terms about experience and rapport is demonstrating something else.

faqs.question: Is a local tutor who knows my child's school worth paying more for?
faqs.answer: School knowledge is genuinely useful, and worth asking about. A tutor who has taught several students from the same campus knows how that department sequences topics, which mock papers recur and how its reports are phrased. The catch is that this is knowledge about the school, not about the neighbourhood, and a tutor who has taught six students from that campus online holds it in exactly the same measure. The things that decide the grade, the syllabus, the paper structure, the criteria and where the child's own scripts lose marks, do not vary by district at all.

faqs.question: We have three subjects we are worried about. Where should the money go first?
faqs.answer: Into whichever decision closes soonest. An IGCSE tier entry closes and cannot be reopened, so it comes first. An Internal Assessment topic sets a mark ceiling in its first fortnight, so it comes next. A Year 11 technique problem must be fixed before February. General consolidation, a Standard Level subject sitting at a 5, or a Year 9 wobble can all wait a term without cost. Four short diagnostic sessions across the candidate subjects, each ending in a written gap list, is a far cheaper way to decide than booking packages in all three.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Abu Dhabi regulated, and how do I check a tutor's position?
faqs.answer: It is. Individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Ask the tutor whether they hold a current permit. Treat it as a legal clearance, not evidence of teaching quality or of any regulator endorsing anyone.

faqs.question: What does it mean when a tutoring site says its tutors are approved?
faqs.answer: Usually nothing verifiable, and it is worth probing. No UAE regulator approves individual private tutors on teaching merit. MoHRE issues a work permit to the individual. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to a training institute with premises in Dubai. Neither amounts to an endorsement of anyone's teaching, and claiming regulator approval without holding the specific permit is the most common overstatement in this market. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and says so rather than implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Why does my Diploma child seem more overwhelmed than my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Because the two years are shaped differently. An IGCSE year concentrates nearly all its marks into one terminal window, so the pressure builds towards the end. A Diploma year spreads it: six subjects each with an Internal Assessment, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service, on internal school deadlines running throughout. Most Diploma students who struggle are not defeated by a subject's difficulty; they are defeated by four internal deadlines colliding in one month. That responds to planning and sequencing rather than to additional teaching hours.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education load affect a tutoring schedule?
faqs.answer: It removes most of the slack. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's detailed guidance for Dubai counts that instructional time in forty-minute units and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in several of those subjects. A Year 11 carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus three mandatory ones has a full week and a Diploma student has a fuller one. In practice that argues for one well-aimed sixty-minute session rather than two longer vague ones.

faqs.question: Is equivalency something a tutoring provider can arrange on our behalf?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry process based on qualifications achieved, and tutoring is not part of it. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB no points threshold could be verified for this page, so none is quoted. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, and be wary of any provider presenting equivalency as something it performs for you.

faqs.question: What happens at the trial lesson, and what do we owe if it does not suit?
faqs.answer: The trial is free and it is a working session rather than a sales call. You are told who the tutor is and what they have taught, by course and level, before it begins. The tutor teaches something, tests a hypothesis about where the gap sits, and writes down what they found. You receive that written gap list afterwards in syllabus language. If the fit is wrong, the match changes and nothing is owed. A mismatch caught in week one costs an hour; one tolerated until half term costs a term.

faqs.question: Which schools do the students you support in central Abu Dhabi attend?
faqs.answer: Families in this part of the island come from British-curriculum and IB campuses in Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan and from schools on Al Reem Island, in Khalifa City and along the Al Raha corridor, including The British School Al Khubairat, Abu Dhabi International School, Repton School Abu Dhabi, GEMS World Academy Abu Dhabi and Al Yasmina Academy. Those names describe the local school map and nothing more. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them, and no school named is a client.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue when we travel out of Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Al Muroor households that travel is one of the main reasons online delivery works better than the alternative. An in-home arrangement cancels whenever the family leaves the city, which during a Diploma year can mean a three-week gap at exactly the wrong point. A live video session follows the student, so the only adjustment is the time zone. Families usually thin sessions out rather than stopping them over long summers, because the fluency that decides an IGCSE tier is the first thing to decay in a ten-week break.

intro.heading: A near-me search is a location filter pretending to be a quality filter
paragraphs: Search engines answer near-me queries with whatever is physically closest and has done enough local marketing to be found. For a restaurant that is a good trade. For a tutor it is close to meaningless, because the thing that decides whether the tuition works is not within two kilometres of Al Mushrif, it is whether the person has taught the exact component your child is failing. A Diploma student losing marks on a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches exploration and an IGCSE student mishandling frequency density need different people, and neither need is served by geography.

Al Mushrif makes this sharper than most districts. It sits inland between Airport Road and Karamah Street, a settled villa area with families whose children have often been in the same school since Foundation Stage. Those children are spread across at least three qualification routes: IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, the Diploma Programme in Years 12 and 13, and the Middle Years Programme for anyone in an IB continuum school. Three routes, one postcode. No local tutor covers all three at depth, and the ones who claim to are usually describing confidence rather than coverage.

There is a second thing proximity cannot tell you. The UAE regulates private tutoring by permit. Anyone teaching your child privately needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and Abu Dhabi has its own layer on top, because ADEK's professional-ethics rules restrict what school staff may do outside school hours. A search result does not surface a permit. A conversation does, and it is a reasonable question to ask anybody before the first lesson, including us. Nor does a result page show whether the person is free in the only hour your child's week leaves open, which in Al Mushrif is usually later than a parent would choose.

So this page answers the near-me question in two parts. First, what the search is actually useful for: knowing which schools the district feeds, when the school day ends, which emirate regulator publishes the inspection report you are reading. Second, what has to be matched deliberately: programme, level, component, and the specific place marks are being lost. The first part is local knowledge, and this page carries it. The second part is why delivery is online.

Being plain about that: IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Al Mushrif address. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. That removes the radius without removing the relationship, and it is the only way a family here can work with somebody who has taught their child's component through several sessions rather than somebody who lives nearby.
