abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.programmesIntro: The same household often has children on two of these at once, which is why a single tutor is rarely the answer for a whole family. Each route is listed with the Abu Dhabi detail that changes how it is taught.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, marked out of eight each, with no external papers until the optional eAssessment. Students arriving from a British lower school find the criteria language unfamiliar, and marks are lost on command terms rather than on content. Tuition here is mostly teaching a student to read a task sheet properly and to write to the criterion the task is actually assessing.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Abu Dhabi often sit alongside peers heading to IGCSE in a different school, so comparisons between households are misleading. The useful comparison is against the criteria descriptors, which parents can read. Ask the school for the subject's criteria rubric; it is the single most helpful document for an MYP parent and it is rarely handed out unprompted.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations, tiered into Core and Extended for Cambridge or Foundation and Higher for Edexcel, with the tier decision usually taken late in Year 10. Grades here set Diploma and A Level options, so a weak Year 10 narrows Year 12 before anybody has discussed it. The work that moves a grade is timed papers marked to the published scheme, not more textbook reading.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; Cambridge offers its February/March series to India only. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the exams officer which zone your school is in.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard Level courses, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the creativity, activity, service requirement. Internal assessments run through both years and the deadlines are internal, which means they move and then collide. Most Diploma students who ask for help in Year 13 need deadline management as much as subject teaching.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB session or results date appears on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a family plans travel around must come from the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly. Several schools within reach of Al Mushrif run the Diploma alongside A Levels, so Year 11 here is a genuine choice.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.subjectsIntro: Requests from this district cluster in a predictable set of subjects, split across the two boards. Each entry names what the subject actually assesses and where a tutor's time is best spent.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with the exploration worth a fifth of the grade. Higher Level adds a third paper that rewards unfamiliar problem-solving rather than recall. Students who arrived from a comfortable IGCSE Extended grade are the ones most often caught out, because the step up is in reasoning rather than in content volume.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. The common error is treating it as the easier route; the Higher Level course is demanding and some university courses prefer Analysis. Check the prerequisite for the intended degree before the option form is signed.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge or Edexcel
subjects.description: Two examined papers, with the calculator policy differing by board. Marks go on method lines and rounding instructions far more often than on misunderstood topics. Three-dimensional trigonometry and frequency density are the two reliable repair jobs, and both take a session each.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Unit handling, graph interpretation and the extended-response questions that ask for an explanation rather than a number. At IGCSE the electricity topic produces the widest spread of marks. At Higher Level the practical and data-analysis skills carry weight that students consistently underprepare for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, moles and the energetics calculations where arithmetic slips cost more than conceptual gaps. The internal assessment is where Diploma students lose most, usually on methodology and the evaluation rather than on the chemistry. A tutor teaches the criteria; the student does the work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: Volume of content plus precise command-term discipline. The difference between describe, explain and outline is worth several grades across a paper. Students who revise by rereading notes plateau quickly; the fix is answering past questions against the mark scheme and seeing which verb was actually being tested.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation. A perfectly drawn diagram with no explanation of the shift scores poorly, and so does an eloquent paragraph with no diagram. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper that rewards structured judgement. The internal assessment commentaries are a deadline problem as much as an economics one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper one guided analysis are the two components where preparation pays most. Students often know the texts and cannot build an argument under timed conditions. Tuition is spent on structure and on reading an unseen text quickly enough to say something specific about it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The essay and exhibition are assessed on the quality of the question as much as the answer. A weak research question cannot be rescued by good writing. Support means interrogating the question, teaching the referencing conventions and giving feedback on the student's own drafts, never producing text for them.

sections.heading: What a near-me search can tell you, and what it cannot
paragraphs: A proximity search is genuinely informative about place. It will tell you which schools sit near Al Mushrif, roughly when the local school day ends, and which tuition centres have premises on the island. Those facts matter: they decide whether a four o'clock slot is realistic and whether a sibling's pickup collides with it. Use the search for that, and it earns its place in the planning.

What it cannot do is rank teaching. Search results are ordered by relevance signals and local prominence, neither of which knows whether a tutor has taught Higher Level Chemistry through more than one session or has ever marked an IGCSE Extended paper against the published scheme. A well-optimised listing from a centre two streets away outranks a specialist in another emirate every time, and the parent reading it has no way to see the difference from the result page.

The practical consequence is that the near-me search should be step one of two. Step one establishes the local facts. Step two is a conversation in which you ask three specific questions: which programme and level has this person taught, which component of it, and how recently. Those three answers do more work than any map. The table sets out which of the two steps each piece of information belongs to. Treat anything in the right-hand column as something you have to ask for, because no listing, review count or map pin will volunteer it, and a parent who asks gets a straight answer far more often than a parent who assumes.

sections.heading: IB or IGCSE: the decision Year 11 in this district actually faces
paragraphs: Families in Al Mushrif are unusually likely to have a real choice at sixteen, because the schools within reach offer the Diploma and A Levels in roughly equal measure. That makes the Year 11 decision a genuine one rather than an administrative default, and it is made with less information than it deserves. The usual framing, that the Diploma is broader and A Levels are deeper, is true and almost useless on its own.

The more useful framing is workload shape. The Diploma spreads six subjects plus three core components across two years with internally set deadlines that land continuously. A Levels concentrate three or four subjects into terminal papers with fewer internal deadlines. A student who manages their own time well and dislikes being examined on everything at once is better served by the Diploma. A student who works in intense bursts and wants to drop subjects they are weak in is better served by the linear route.

Grades at IGCSE then act as the filter. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is hard to recommend to a student who found Extended maths a struggle, and that conversation is far better had in March of Year 11 than in October of Year 12, when the option form has already been signed and the first internal assessment is due. If one block of tutoring is worth buying in this district, it is often the diagnostic one that informs this choice rather than the remedial one that follows it.

sections.heading: Five regulators, one country, and the report you are reading
paragraphs: Parents in Al Mushrif read inspection reports written by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. Families who move within the UAE often assume the report format travels with them, and it does not. Dubai schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there.

Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which also regulates private education in that emirate, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete map. It is worth knowing because the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate regulator there.

None of this makes any tutoring platform approved by anybody. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Sharjah authority, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked to show the permit number. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit of its own, which is a specific document issued to training institutes. Explaining a regulator is useful. Borrowing it as a badge is not.

sections.heading: The honest answer about who is available, and when
paragraphs: Coverage is not uniform and pretending otherwise is the standard failure of this market. Mainstream Diploma subjects and IGCSE maths and sciences are matched within days in term time. Smaller Higher Level courses, Theory of Knowledge specialists and the less-entered IGCSE options take longer, and in the weeks before a series the queue for exam-year support lengthens for everybody. None of this is a secret worth keeping from a parent who is trying to plan.

When the right person is not free, the alternatives are better than a poor substitute. A later weekday slot with the correct tutor usually beats an immediate slot with the wrong one. A single diagnostic session on a marked paper gives the student a ranked list they can work through alone, which is genuinely useful and cheap. A waiting list with a date on it lets a family make other arrangements. A tutor from an adjacent specialism, named as such before booking, is sometimes the right call and should always be the parent's decision.

What we will not do is take a booking and let the mismatch surface in session two. That pattern is why so many families in this district describe a first tutor who was pleasant and changed nothing. Pleasantness is not the variable. Whether the person can look at a marked paper and name, in one sentence, the three things costing seven marks is the variable, and if nobody who can do that is free this week, the useful answer is to say so.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more on the IB side than almost anywhere else in school education, because so much of the Diploma grade is work the student submits as their own. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, every internal assessment, and the Middle Years Programme personal project are all authenticated by the school. A tutor who crosses the line does not get caught instead of the student; the student carries the consequence, and it can reach the whole diploma.

The boundary is workable and clear. A tutor may teach the skills a component needs, explain the published criteria, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, demonstrate referencing conventions, and read a draft the student has written and say where it does not yet meet the criterion. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure in their own words, supply paragraphs, invent data, or edit a draft to completion. The test is whether the words and the thinking remain the candidate's.

This is also a live commercial issue in this market. At least one page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright. That is not an alternative service with a different risk profile; it is a malpractice trigger with the student's qualification attached. If a provider offers to produce assessed work, that is the end of the conversation. We would rather lose the enquiry than be in that business, and we say so on the page rather than in the small print.

sections.heading: What tuition costs in this market, read from the monthly line down
paragraphs: Most families decide on the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, so start there. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Published packages in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits. Those figures belong to the providers who published them.

The hourly bands behind those monthlies are worth seeing, because they explain the spread. Budget online tuition runs about AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is around AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Named specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-branded tuition at AED 500 to 650, where BartyED quotes AED 650.

Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote US dollars at families who transact in dirhams. That is the gap this table fills. It is a market picture rather than an IB Gram price list: our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and the rate is confirmed in the match conversation, which is the honest way to quote something that depends on subject, level and frequency.

sections.heading: Timing a session into a real Al Mushrif week
paragraphs: The slot is where good intentions die. A household in this district typically has a school day finishing between two and three, a bus or car run of fifteen to forty minutes depending on which campus, and then the mandatory UAE subjects' homework alongside everything else, because federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for. That is real timetable space, and it is often invisible in a parent's planning.

Add activities. Swimming, football and music in Abu Dhabi tend to run early evening, which is exactly when tutoring wants to happen. The result is that the only genuinely free hour in many weeks is later than a parent would choose or at the weekend. Choosing the awkward hour at the start is better than choosing the convenient one and rescheduling it twice before it quietly stops. An online slot survives this better than a travelling tutor does, because a six-thirty start costs nobody a drive.

Ramadan reshapes the week again, and it moves earlier each year. School hours shorten, families eat late, and the useful tutoring window often sits after iftar rather than in the afternoon. Sessions can move to post-iftar timing for the month and back afterwards, and planning that in advance is better than losing four weeks of momentum. Families who travel over Eid or the summer can keep the same tutor across time zones, which is the one scheduling advantage online delivery has outright.

sections.heading: Equivalency, and why tutoring is not part of it
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the process by which a UAE authority recognises a foreign school certificate, and it is a step families here meet when applying to UAE universities. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

On the American track the published position is different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB there is no points threshold any page should publish without reading it on the Ministry's own site, and this one does not. At least one page ranking for these searches states that six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced figure is five.

Two cautions follow. First, equivalency is a regulatory process run by the authority, not a service a tutoring platform performs, submits or guarantees, and this page describes it only so a parent knows what to ask. Second, tutoring is not a requirement of equivalency, university admission or school progression, and any provider framing it that way is manufacturing urgency. Verify every requirement with the Ministry before you act on it; wording changes and a page is only as current as its last review.

process.title: Say which programme, not which year
process.description: Diploma, Middle Years Programme or IGCSE, then the level and the component. A Higher Level internal assessment and an Extended Paper 4 are different jobs needing different people, and the year group alone does not distinguish them. One sentence here saves a week of mismatching.

process.title: Send one marked piece of work
process.description: A mock paper, a criterion-marked task or a draft with teacher comments. A specialist reading a marked piece tells you more in twenty minutes than any amount of description, because the marks show where the loss is rather than where it feels like it is.

process.title: Take the free trial with that work open
process.description: The trial session is at no charge and is spent on the diagnostic rather than on introductions. You should finish it with a short, ranked list of what is costing the most marks, and that list is yours to use whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Fix the slot against the real week
process.description: Include the school finish, the bus run, the mandatory UAE subjects and the activity that owns a weekday evening. Then choose the hour that survives all of them. Ramadan timing is agreed in advance rather than improvised when the month arrives.

process.title: Review when new evidence arrives
process.description: A mock, a criterion mark or a teacher comment is better evidence than four weeks of session impressions. The topic sequence is revised when one lands, and if the error log has flattened, fewer sessions are the honest recommendation and we will make it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the map
whyPoints.description: The first question is which programme, level and component a tutor has taught and how recently. Distance from Al Mushrif is not a criterion, because online delivery makes it irrelevant, and that is what allows a specialist rather than a neighbour to take the lesson.

whyPoints.title: Both boards handled by one process
whyPoints.description: A household with a Year 11 on IGCSE and a Year 13 on the Diploma does not need two platforms. The matching logic is the same in both cases: name the component, read the marked work, find the person who has taught it recently.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model said once, plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for this district are online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that service exists only in India. Stating it on the first screen is better than letting a parent find out at booking.

whyPoints.title: Figures with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED number here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the market framing kept separate from our own arrangement. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, which is the gap worth closing.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line held in public
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody here produces an essay, an internal assessment or a personal project. Competing pages sell exactly that, and saying no to it on the page is more useful than saying it in terms and conditions.

whyPoints.title: Regulators explained, not borrowed
whyPoints.description: ADEK, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE are described here because knowing what each does helps a parent ask better questions. IB Gram claims no approval or accreditation from any of them, and any provider that does should be asked for the document.

faqs.question: Does a near-me search actually find the best tutor in Al Mushrif?
faqs.answer: It finds the closest and the best-marketed, which are not the same thing. Search ranking knows about local prominence and relevance signals; it does not know whether a tutor has taught Higher Level Chemistry or marked an IGCSE Extended paper to the published scheme. Use the search for local facts, such as which schools the district feeds and when the school day ends, then ask three direct questions of any shortlist: which programme and level, which component, and how recently. Those answers decide the outcome.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both my IGCSE child and my Diploma child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, within one subject family, and usually it is better not to. The two routes assess differently: IGCSE is terminal papers against a mark scheme, while the Diploma mixes examinations with internally assessed work judged on published criteria. A tutor fluent in both for the same subject does exist and is uncommon. For a household with children on each route, two matched specialists generally outperform one generalist, and the matching process is identical for both, so arranging it is no more work.

faqs.question: Which programme should my child take after Year 11 in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Decide on workload shape rather than prestige. The Diploma runs six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and service across two years with internal deadlines landing continuously. The linear route concentrates three or four subjects into terminal papers and allows a weak subject to be dropped after the first year. Self-managing students who dislike being examined on everything at once tend to prefer the Diploma. Have the conversation in March of Year 11, with IGCSE grades in hand, rather than in October of Year 12.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school if we move from Abu Dhabi to Sharjah?
faqs.answer: A different body with a wider remit. Abu Dhabi schools sit under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its own Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The report format and the fee approval route both change.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by ADEK or by the IB?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring platform should imply that it is. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Those bodies are described on this page because understanding them helps a parent ask better questions. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit of its own, which is a specific document with a number. If a provider claims regulator approval, ask to see it.

faqs.question: How far in advance should we arrange Diploma support in this area?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. Mainstream Diploma subjects are matched within days during term time, but the queue for exam-year support lengthens in the weeks before a sitting, and the smaller Higher Level courses and core specialists are thinner year round. The practical advice is to book the diagnostic session in the autumn term rather than the remedial block in the spring. A ranked list of where marks are going is useful in October and close to useless three weeks before a paper.

faqs.question: Where is the line between Extended Essay coaching and writing it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can interrogate the research question until it is answerable, explain the published criteria, teach referencing conventions, and read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of a criterion. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, restructure in their own words, supply paragraphs or edit a draft to completion. The school authenticates the work, so the student carries any consequence. Any provider offering to produce the essay should be ruled out on that basis alone.

faqs.question: What does an online IB or IGCSE tutor cost a month in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Published market packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are the providers' own figures rather than ours. IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and confirms the rate in the match conversation, because it depends on subject, level and how often you want to meet.

faqs.question: My daughter is in the Middle Years Programme and the marks make no sense. Why?
faqs.answer: Because they are criterion marks, not percentages. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and a task usually assesses only one or two of them. A strong piece of work can score modestly if it answers a different criterion from the one being marked. Ask the school for the subject's criteria rubric, which is rarely handed out unprompted. Most of the early progress in Middle Years tutoring comes from teaching a student to read the task sheet and write to the criterion in front of them.

faqs.question: Does the tutor hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: It is the right question to ask anybody, including us. The permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Anyone tutoring privately without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with caution.

faqs.question: Can my son's own subject teacher tutor him privately after school?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, you should assume not. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also restricts serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it. There is also a practical reason to look elsewhere: the person who marks the coursework and sets the mocks should not also be paid to prepare the student for them.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE and IB exams happen for a candidate based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: IGCSE candidates here sit the June and November series. Cambridge offers its February/March series to India only, so an Indian revision site's deadlines do not apply. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, and this page publishes no IB dates because the IB's own site blocks automated verification. Take any date you plan around from the board's live timetable or from your school's IB coordinator, and confirm the Cambridge zone with the exams officer.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the tutoring schedule here?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, family routines move later, and the useful study window often sits after iftar rather than in the afternoon. The month also moves earlier in the calendar each year, so it lands at a different point in the academic cycle each time. Sessions can shift to post-iftar timing for the month and return afterwards, which keeps momentum instead of losing four weeks. Agree the change before the month begins; improvising it in the first week is how a block of sessions quietly stops.

faqs.question: Is an online session really equivalent to a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For secondary students working on papers and drafts, it holds up well, because the gain from choosing the right specialist is larger than the loss from the screen. Both people see the same document, working is written live on a shared whiteboard, and a written note follows each session. Physical presence matters most for much younger children who need an adult managing attention. For Diploma and IGCSE work the binding constraint is the tutor's grasp of the criteria and the mark scheme.

faqs.question: What do we do if the first Al Mushrif match turns out to be wrong?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than giving it a term. The usual sign is that sessions feel pleasant and nothing in the marks moves, which generally means the tutor is supervising rather than diagnosing. A good match produces a specific, ranked account of where marks are being lost within the first two sessions. If that has not happened, a change is reasonable and the diagnostic does not need repeating from scratch, because the marked work and the error log carry over to the new tutor.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.closingHeading: Use the search for the place, and a conversation for the teaching
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-m.closingBody: The near-me search has done its job once you know which schools Al Mushrif feeds and when the school day ends. The rest is a conversation: which programme, which level, which component, and how recently the tutor has taught it. Send one marked piece of work, take the free trial with it open, and finish that session with a ranked list of where the marks are going. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to the Abu Dhabi school week and shifted after iftar during Ramadan. If the right specialist is not free, we will tell you and give you a date.

intro.heading: Why 'near me' is the least useful word in this search
paragraphs: A search for a tutor nearby is a search for a short drive. It made sense when tuition meant somebody arriving at the door, and in Al Nahyan it produces a list filtered by geography rather than by whether anyone on it has taught your child's course. That filter throws away the thing you actually need. There is no shortage of competent maths graduates within ten minutes of Al Nahyan. There is a real shortage of people who have marked a Cambridge Extended paper against the published scheme and also know what a Diploma mathematics exploration scores at criterion E.

The households that type this phrase in Al Nahyan tend to look the same. Two or three children, one still in the IGCSE years on a Cambridge or Pearson specification, one in DP1 or DP2 having crossed over, and a parent trying to find one point of contact rather than three. The district is apartment living between Airport Road and Al Karamah, which means siblings often attend different schools on different finish times, and the family calendar is the binding constraint on when anything can happen.

The honest answer to the proximity question is this: IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons over live video, and does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi — home visiting is an India-only service. Independent tutors in the emirate do travel, and the market prices that at a premium we set out further down. What online delivery changes for a two-board household is the match. The Year 11 child gets a 0580 or 4MA1 specialist; the DP2 child gets someone who has supervised explorations and knows the criteria by letter; and both can be booked into the same evening without anyone driving between them.

The rest of this page deals with the two problems that actually bring Al Nahyan parents here. The first is the crossing from IGCSE to the Diploma, which is the single most underestimated transition in international schooling and which bites in specific, nameable ways per subject. The second is running two boards in one house: different command-term vocabulary, different reporting scales, different exam series, different internal deadlines. Both are manageable once they are written down, and most of this page is simply writing them down.

Three further sections cover ground this search ignores entirely. One sets out the Diploma's internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations and word limits, because those are published, knowable and routinely unread by the students they govern. One covers the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies layer that runs alongside every international curriculum in the Emirates and quietly consumes the homework capacity parents assume their child has. The last covers the honesty boundary across both boards, which matters because at least one site competing for this phrase sells completed assessments to families who think they are buying help.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-n.programmesIntro: An Al Nahyan household running both boards is usually touching three programmes at once. Each has a different assessment logic, and a tutor who treats them as the same subject taught at different speeds will be wrong about what to practise.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal written papers, tiered as Core and Extended by Cambridge and Foundation and Higher by Pearson. Assessment is almost entirely by examination, with practical skills examined on paper in the sciences. The grading scale differs by board, which matters when a family tries to compare two children's reports.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, the IGCSE years are also where the Ministry of Education equivalency rules start to apply. The British track requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. Subject choices made in Year 9 therefore have an administrative consequence years later.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria by letter, and those marks are a meaningful fraction of the grade. The written papers reward justified judgement rather than recall.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the fastest-growing route in Abu Dhabi private schooling and several schools in the emirate run it alongside a British lower school, which is exactly how a two-board household appears. No Ministry of Education equivalency points figure for the Diploma should be quoted to you without a reference on the ministry's own site.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, graded one to eight against four criteria per subject rather than by percentage. Students arrive in the Diploma fluent in reflection and inquiry language but often short of the procedural fluency that terminal written papers demand, particularly in mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Al Nahyan child moves from MYP into DP1 maths, the gap is almost always algebraic stamina rather than understanding. That is diagnosable in a single trial lesson and repairable over a term of weekly work, which is far cheaper than discovering it in the DP1 mock.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route several Abu Dhabi schools run beside the Diploma, with narrower subject choice and staged AS and A2 assessment. Content depth per subject is greater; breadth is lower. Families comparing the two routes for a Year 11 child are usually weighing exactly that trade.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects. Verify the current requirements through the official channel before acting on them.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-n.subjectsIntro: The courses below are the ones Al Nahyan households most often need covered at the same time, with the specific thing that goes wrong in each. Several appear in both systems and are not the same subject twice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Diploma's proof-heavy maths route. Students arriving from Extended IGCSE meet radians, formal proof and calculus at pace. HL adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards stamina and penalises students who abandon a question early.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work. The common error is treating it as the easier course; the graphic display calculator fluency and the modelling vocabulary are genuine demands and are examined precisely.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers, one without a calculator. Extended-only topics include functions, vectors and harder trigonometry. Marks go to scale factors in similar solids, frequency density and early rounding more often than to anything conceptual.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Maths A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers, calculator permitted on both, formula sheet supplied, graded on the numerical scale. The skill is fast formula selection rather than recall, which changes how revision should be spent.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: At Diploma level the step is uncertainty treatment and the data-based paper; at IGCSE it is the alternative-to-practical paper, where students who have done the experiments still lose marks describing a method precisely enough to be repeated.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the Diploma marks; moles and ionic equations carry the IGCSE ones. The reasoning demanded in Diploma Paper 2 is a different genre of writing from an IGCSE structured answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of specific terminology at IGCSE, and command-term discipline at Diploma level. Students who revise by reading lose marks that students who practise written answers against mark schemes keep.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure decide the grade. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on real published articles, and the most common fault is commentary that summarises the article rather than applying a theory to it.

subjects.name: English A Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen text analysis, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, the HL essay. Strong IGCSE English candidates often stall here because the Diploma rewards argument about how a text works rather than comprehension of what it says.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, quantitative content and an internal assessment grounded in a real organisation. Students lose marks by describing a business rather than answering the question asked about it, which is a correctable habit.

sections.heading: What 'near me' actually returns for an Al Nahyan household
paragraphs: A proximity search ranks by distance and reviews. Neither signal says anything about whether a tutor has taught Cambridge Extended mathematics or supervised a Diploma exploration. The result is a list of people who are close, which is a solved problem in a district as dense as Al Nahyan, and silence on the question that matters.

Test it with one question. Ask any prospective tutor which criterion of the mathematics exploration carries six marks, or how many marks the Extended Essay's critical thinking criterion is worth. Those are facts, published by the board, and a specialist answers immediately. Somebody who teaches general maths will not, and that is useful information obtained in ten seconds rather than after four paid lessons.

The second thing proximity hides is availability. Specialist Diploma tutors in Abu Dhabi concentrate their hours in the same late-afternoon window every family wants, and the scarcer the course, the tighter that window. Higher Level sciences, Economics and the less common languages run thin. A family filtering by driving distance first and specialism second is choosing from the intersection of two small sets, and will usually end up compromising on the one that matters.

What this page offers instead is a specification-first match delivered over live video, with the honest statement attached: IB Gram runs no home visits in Abu Dhabi, because that is an India-only service, and we think the trade favours the family. The alternative — a generalist who is nearby — is the quiet reason a great deal of tuition money produces no measurable change in a report card.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma crossing, subject by subject
paragraphs: The gap between Year 11 and DP1 is the most consistently underestimated step in international education, and it is not uniform. It is specific per subject, and naming it converts a vague anxiety into a plan with a number of weeks attached.

In mathematics the jump is formal: proof as a genre, radians instead of degrees, and calculus arriving faster than most students expect. A student with a strong Extended 0580 or Higher 4MA1 grade still has to learn a new kind of writing, because Analysis and Approaches asks for argument and not just the correct value. In the sciences the shift is methodological: uncertainty treatment, the data-based paper, and an internal assessment that is marked on the design of the investigation rather than on how neatly the results came out. In the humanities it is evaluative, because the Diploma rewards a justified judgement with a counterargument where IGCSE rewarded a complete and accurate answer.

The table below sets out the common routes with the gap that actually bites and a realistic span of support. These are typical spans, not promises, and they assume weekly one-to-one work with marked written output between lessons. A student who does no written work between sessions should expect the longer end of every range.

Timing matters more than volume here. Work done in the months before DP1 starts is worth considerably more than the same hours spent in DP1 term two, because the student is not simultaneously trying to keep up with six new courses, Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay. For an Al Nahyan family whose child finishes IGCSE in the June series, the window between the last paper and the start of the new year is the cheapest and most productive one available.

sections.heading: Command terms: the same word means different things on different boards
paragraphs: Both Cambridge and the IB publish lists of command terms with definitions, and both expect students to treat them as instructions rather than synonyms. Students who do not read those lists write answers that are correct and unrewarded, which is the most demoralising way to lose marks there is.

The clearest example is 'show that'. A question that says show that the answer is a particular value wants a derivation that arrives at the printed result. A student who substitutes the printed value back in and demonstrates that it works has verified the answer and scored nothing, because verification is not derivation. Similarly, 'comment on' asks for interpretation of a result already obtained, not a restatement of it, and 'justify' requires the evidence to be named rather than implied.

The vocabulary shifts as a student crosses into the Diploma. IGCSE answers reward completeness and accuracy; Diploma answers in the humanities and sciences reward a judgement, supported, with its limitations acknowledged. A Year 12 student still writing good IGCSE answers will be marked down for exactly the quality that earned them a top IGCSE grade, which is bewildering unless somebody explains the change.

The table lists the terms that cost the most marks in Abu Dhabi scripts, with what the examiner is looking for. The mark weights are typical rather than fixed; read the current published command-term list for the subject, since boards revise them. The exercise worth doing at home takes twenty minutes: open a marked script, underline the command word in every question that lost marks, and check it against the published definition. In most scripts two or three terms account for the bulk of the damage, and both children in a two-board household usually have different ones.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria by letter, and what each is worth
paragraphs: This is the part of the Diploma that Abu Dhabi families understand least and that carries the most recoverable marks. Every internal assessment is marked against published criteria, each criterion has a letter and a maximum, and the student can read them before writing a word. Most do not. A student who writes with the criteria open beside them scores differently from one who writes an essay and hopes.

The mathematics exploration is the cleanest example. Twenty marks, split across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation. A technically immaculate exploration with no reflection loses marks that were available for free. The Extended Essay works the same way across thirty-four marks, with critical thinking worth twelve of them — more than a third of the essay — which tells a student exactly where to spend their final fortnight.

Word limits are part of the specification rather than a guideline, and Abu Dhabi students lose marks to them routinely. The Extended Essay stops at four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay stops at sixteen hundred, and the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty. Markers stop reading at the limit; everything after it is unmarked, which turns an over-length conclusion into no conclusion.

A tutor's role here is specific and bounded. We teach what each criterion rewards, question a student's draft against it, and point at the criterion a paragraph is failing to address. We do not write any part of an assessment, edit it to completion, or supply text for submission. The work is the student's, the entry is the student's, and a tutor who offers otherwise is creating a malpractice exposure for your child rather than saving them time.

sections.heading: Running two boards in one Al Nahyan household
paragraphs: A family with a Year 11 IGCSE student and a DP2 student is managing two different calendars, two reporting scales and two kinds of homework, and the two children will tell you the other one has it easier. The practical problems are mundane and solvable once they are separated out.

Calendars first. The IGCSE child's year ends in a terminal exam series with almost everything riding on a fortnight of papers. The Diploma child's year is a chain of internal deadlines — exploration drafts, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge submissions — spread across eighteen months, any one of which can swallow a weekend. Those two shapes need different tuition patterns: steady weekly work for the IGCSE child, lumpier blocks timed to deadlines for the Diploma child.

Then the reporting scales, which cause more domestic friction than anything else. Cambridge reports A* to G, Pearson reports nine to one, the Diploma reports one to seven per subject with a forty-five point total, and the MYP reports one to eight against criteria. None of these translates cleanly into another and attempting the translation at the dinner table helps nobody. The useful comparison is progress against the same child's previous work, not against a sibling on a different scale.

On cost, the figure parents usually want is monthly rather than hourly. For a single weekly one-hour session, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts monthly spend at roughly AED 240 to 600 at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Two children on weekly sessions therefore means doubling whichever band applies, and the honest planning advice for an Al Nahyan household is to fund the child in an exam year properly rather than funding both thinly. Those bands are the market's, read in October 2026, and not our price list.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the international curriculum
paragraphs: This is the layer almost no tutoring site in the UAE mentions, and it affects every family on this page. Private schools in the Emirates are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects run alongside the Cambridge or IB timetable, not instead of it, and they appear on the report card.

The requirements are detailed where they have been published. KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance for Dubai, which is the clearest public statement of how these subjects are organised in the UAE, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It sets Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with a recommendation that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes.

Two consequences follow for an Al Nahyan family. First, these subjects consume timetable space that parents often forget when they calculate how much homework capacity a child has, which is why a Diploma student with six subjects plus Arabic is genuinely busier than the subject count suggests. Second, the content is tightly controlled: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited. That is a real constraint on how any Arabic or Islamic Education tutoring can honestly be described, and anyone offering a bespoke alternative syllabus for them is describing something they should not be doing.

There is a third point worth knowing, because it is checkable. Schools are required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval from the regulator to teach those subjects. That is a question a parent can ask the school directly, and the answer is a matter of record.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection ratings, and what a school report does not tell you
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. That makes ADEK the first place to look when a family is comparing schools, and it is named by almost none of the tutoring sites competing for this search, which is a strange omission given how much weight parents put on it.

The regulator map across the Emirates is worth knowing because families move. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates the regulator's remit extends well beyond inspection.

What an inspection rating tells you is how a school performs overall against the regulator's framework. What it does not tell you is whether that school's Higher Level Chemistry set has a specialist teacher this year, whether the maths department is short-staffed, or whether your particular child is on the right tier. Those are the questions that determine whether tuition is needed, and none of them is answerable from a published band. Read the rating, then ask the subject-level questions separately.

IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or approval from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and is not a registered centre of any kind. The regulators are named here so that an Al Nahyan parent can ask better questions of their school, not to imply any of them endorses this platform.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across both boards, and what a tutor will not do
paragraphs: Both systems treat authorship as non-negotiable, and the Diploma treats it as a condition of the award. An internal assessment submitted with material a student did not produce puts the whole entry at risk, not just that component. This is the point at which some of the websites competing for this search become actively dangerous: at least one in this market sells completed internal assessments outright, at a four-figure price in dirhams. Buying one is not a shortcut; it is an offence against the regulations that the student carries, not the seller.

The boundary a legitimate tutor works inside is clear and we state it to students at the first session. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion rewards, question a draft, point out where an argument is unsupported, model an unrelated worked example, and mark practice work against the published scheme. A tutor may not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, provide answers to live assessed tasks, or sit beside a student during an assessment. We decline those requests and will say why.

There are two related boundaries worth stating because competitors cross them. We do not reproduce or distribute board material. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB and are published on their own sites; a tutor works through them with a student from the official source rather than handing over copies. And we do not describe tutors as current examiners for any board unless that status can be evidenced, nor use examiner experience to imply any access to marking or unreleased papers.

The last boundary is about outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university place, and nobody should sell you one. What good tuition offers is a correct diagnosis, teaching aimed at it, written work marked against the real criteria, and an honest statement about how much of the gap the time remaining can close. If a provider will not say what their plan cannot achieve, that silence is the most informative thing about them.

faqs.question: Is there an IB and IGCSE tutor actually based in Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: There are certainly tutors living in and around the district, and several visit homes independently. IB Gram is not one of them: we deliver one-to-one lessons over live video and do not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because home visiting is an India-only service for us. The reason we think that is the better trade for an Al Nahyan household is specialism. A Diploma Higher Level Chemistry specialist or a 4MA1 examiner-trained maths teacher is scarce in the emirate, and filtering by driving distance first removes most of them from consideration.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my Year 11 child and my DP2 child in Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and we would rather say so. Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE and the IB Diploma are different assessment systems with different command vocabulary, different internal assessment rules and different exam calendars. A tutor who genuinely covers both at depth exists but is uncommon. What we do instead is match each child to a specialist and put the sessions back to back on the same evening, so the household keeps one schedule and one point of contact without compromising either child's match.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from Extended IGCSE maths to Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Larger than the grade suggests. A student with a strong Extended 0580 or Higher 4MA1 result still has to absorb radians, formal proof as a style of writing, and calculus arriving at a pace no IGCSE course prepares for. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper that rewards persistence. Typical weekly support for this crossing runs to a term alongside DP1, and the same work done before DP1 begins is worth noticeably more because the student is not also juggling five other new courses.

faqs.question: Which criterion carries the most marks in the Diploma Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Critical thinking, at twelve of the thirty-four available marks. The others are focus and method, knowledge and understanding, presentation, and engagement. Knowing that allocation changes how a student spends their last fortnight: polishing the presentation criterion returns four marks at most, while strengthening the analysis and the handling of counter-evidence reaches into the largest pot on the sheet. The essay also stops at four thousand words, and anything written beyond that limit is simply not marked.

faqs.question: What are the word limits on Diploma internal assessments?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay stops at four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay stops at sixteen hundred, and the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty. The sciences scientific investigation runs to three thousand words and the History internal assessment to two thousand two hundred. The mathematics exploration has no fixed word count but is expected to be a short report. Markers stop at the limit, so an over-length conclusion is an unmarked conclusion, which is the most avoidable way to lose marks in the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Abu Dhabi IGCSE candidates sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two open to UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, as it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who sit the wrong version. Read the live official timetable rather than any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, no. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. They must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. At least one ranking tutoring site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Verify the current rules through the official ministry channel before acting.

faqs.question: Why does my Al Nahyan child's school teach Arabic alongside the IB or IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Because it is required. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects run alongside the international timetable rather than replacing any of it. The practical effect on a household is capacity: a Diploma student carrying six subjects plus the mandatory subjects has less homework headroom than the subject count implies, which is worth factoring into any tuition schedule.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection rating tell me about my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Very little at subject level, which is the limitation parents most often miss. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, and a rating describes whole-school performance against the regulator's framework. It cannot tell you whether this year's Higher Level Chemistry set has a specialist teacher, whether the maths department is carrying a vacancy, or whether your child is entered at the right tier. Read the rating, then ask those questions of the school directly.

faqs.question: How much do two children in Al Nahyan cost per month in tuition?
faqs.answer: Double whichever band applies, which is why the planning question is which child to fund properly. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Our honest advice is to fund the child in an examination year at specialist level rather than funding both children thinly. Those figures are the market's, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my DP2 child finish their Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor will teach the criteria, read what your child has written, ask the questions that expose a weak argument, and point at the criterion a section is failing. A tutor will not supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece, or produce any part of it for submission. We decline that, because the entry belongs to the student and material they did not produce puts the whole Diploma at risk. At least one provider in this market sells completed assessments; that is a trap for the student, not a service.

faqs.question: Does my child's own teacher in Abu Dhabi count as a legal private tutor?
faqs.answer: Not for your own child. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates private and charter school staff are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Any paid private tutor in the UAE needs that permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued free of charge for two years. Verify current ADEK policy before relying on the detail.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start tuition for the move into DP1?
faqs.answer: The weeks between the last IGCSE paper and the start of the new academic year. A student in that window has no competing coursework, so content taught then is absorbed rather than crammed alongside six new courses, Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay. For an Al Nahyan family whose child sits the June series, that is a genuine opportunity and it is also the period when specialist tutors have the most availability, because everyone else has stopped thinking about school.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist covers our subject combination in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with someone close enough. Availability is thinnest in Higher Level sciences, Economics and the less common languages, and tightest in the late-afternoon Gulf Standard Time window every family wants. The options are usually a different weekday slot, a weekend session, or a short wait for a named tutor. Where no specialist covers the combination at all, we say that plainly and explain what the realistic alternative looks like before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: How do we compare an IGCSE grade with a Diploma subject grade at home?
faqs.answer: Do not try. Cambridge reports A* to G, Pearson reports nine to one, the Diploma reports one to seven per subject against a forty-five point total, and the Middle Years Programme reports one to eight against criteria. None of those scales converts cleanly into another, and attempting the conversion between siblings causes more friction than information. The comparison that means something is each child against their own previous marked work on the same course, which is also the only comparison a tutor can usefully act on.

intro.heading: What a 'near me' search actually returns, and what it costs
paragraphs: Typing a tutor search with 'near me' on the end tells a search engine to prioritise proximity, and proximity is a weak proxy for everything a parent in Al Raha Beach actually cares about. The results that come back are a mixture of agencies with a local landing page, marketplaces listing anyone within a radius, blog posts written to rank, and a handful of independent tutors with good local reputations. The one thing the list does not do is sort by value.

Price is the clearest illustration. The published spread in this market runs from AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium end, which is a fourteen-fold range for something described by the same two words. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from the equivalent of AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650. Bestimate's rate work puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

Those figures are not five providers charging differently for the same thing. They are five business models with different cost bases, and a parent who understands the models can read a quote in about thirty seconds. A university student tutoring part-time under a private tuition permit has no overheads. An agency has a matching team and a replacement policy. A tuition centre has premises, a licence and staff. A home tutor has a car and an hour of unpaid driving. The rate reflects the model, not the teaching.

The second thing a 'near me' search hides is the extras. The hourly figure is rarely the whole invoice. Minimum blocks, cancellation windows shorter than a school's own notice period, charges for a written report, a travel surcharge to communities on the airport side of Abu Dhabi, and material fees all appear after the decision has been made. There is also the question of whether a quoted price includes VAT, which a provider should answer in writing for their own prices and which this page does not attempt to settle as a general rule.

So the structure of this page is a pricing audit. Five models priced with sources, the extras checklist, what the travel premium buys in this particular corridor, and how a household running one IB and one IGCSE student can share a budget instead of running two. subjects.description: Three specifications in common Abu Dhabi use, with different paper structures and calculator rules. The code on the exam entry statement decides which tutor is useful; a general IGCSE maths label does not.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Heavily mathematical, with uncertainty treatment and graph interpretation carrying marks throughout. The internal assessment rewards a well-controlled investigation rather than an ambitious one, and students lose marks on the evaluation section most often.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Formula rearrangement, standard form and gradient reading account for a large share of lost marks. A maths-literate tutor can move this grade without teaching new physics content, which matters when a household is buying hours for two children.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics carry the difficulty, and the internal assessment needs a defensible treatment of uncertainty. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, which changes what revision looks like in the final term.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, empirical formulae, percentage yield and the qualitative analysis tables. The tables are learnable in a few hours and are routinely left to the last fortnight, which is a predictable and avoidable loss.

subjects.name: IB English A and English B
subjects.description: English A assesses response to literature through individual oral and written tasks; English B assesses language acquisition across four skills. Students confuse the two courses' demands, and the individual oral is the component most often under-rehearsed.

subjects.name: IGCSE English
subjects.levels: First Language and as a Second Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition task carry the heaviest weighting, and the reading questions reward precise quotation over general comment. Second Language candidates lose marks on the summary task more than on anything else.

subjects.name: IB Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, labelling and the quantitative questions at Higher Level separate grades. Both subjects carry an internal assessment that must be the student's own work, with a tutor's role limited to questioning and feedback.

subjects.name: IGCSE Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Data response and calculation questions on elasticity, break-even and index numbers. Candidates who comment on a table in context rather than restating its figures pick up the marks most frequently left behind.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Personal Project
subjects.description: All three must be the student's own work. A tutor may discuss a research question, explain a criterion and respond to a draft with questions. Writing, completing or supplying text is malpractice under IB rules and carries consequences for the student.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools regardless of the international curriculum, with the language of instruction and class organisation set by published regulatory guidance rather than by the school's own preference.

sections.heading: The five ways tuition is sold in Abu Dhabi, priced
paragraphs: Comparing an agency quote with a freelance quote is comparing two different products, and most pages in this market avoid saying so because the comparison makes their own model look expensive. The table below compares the models rather than the brands, with each rate attributed to the provider or rate study that published it, read in October 2026.

What varies between the models is not teaching quality but what happens around the teaching. A freelance tutor found through a community group is the cheapest route and carries the most risk: no replacement if the match is wrong, no record if they stop answering, and no third party to raise a problem with. An agency costs more and exists largely to solve those three problems. Whether that is worth the difference depends on how much a failed match would cost your child in a given term.

Tuition centres sell something different again. A centre with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a licence issued to training institutes rather than to individuals, and the overhead shows in the price. A centre class also means a fixed slot, a set curriculum and a drive, and for some families the structure and the peer pressure are the point rather than the cost.

Platforms sit between the two. The honest description of IB Gram's own model is a matching platform: we hold no premises in the UAE, lessons are one-to-one over live video, and the value is in the matching, the specialist pool and the disclosure. IB Gram does not operate an office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and we do not send tutors to UAE homes.

sections.heading: The extras that catch Al Raha Beach parents off guard
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the number a family compares and the invoice is the number they pay. The gap between them is made of six things, and all six are answerable in one message before any money moves. Asking costs nothing and routinely changes which provider looks cheapest.

The first is the minimum block. Some providers quote per hour and sell only in packages of eight or twelve, which converts a trial into a commitment. The second is the cancellation window. A school gives a term's notice of a change; a tutor may require twenty-four hours and charge in full inside it, which collides awkwardly with a child who is genuinely ill. The third is report charges: a written summary of progress is sometimes an extra line rather than part of the service.

The fourth is the travel surcharge, which is specific to communities like Al Raha Beach and Al Reef on the airport side of Abu Dhabi. It may be quoted as a flat addition or folded silently into a higher hourly rate for the area. The fifth is materials. Printed workbooks, platform licences and mock paper packs are sometimes charged separately, and a provider offering a bundle of official past papers as a download is also doing something the boards' copyright does not permit.

The sixth is VAT. Whether a given tuition service is subject to UAE VAT depends on the provider's own circumstances, and this page does not attempt to state the treatment as a general rule. What a parent should do is ask the provider in writing whether their quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive, and ask for the tax registration number if they are charging it. A provider who cannot answer that clearly has told you something useful.

sections.heading: What the distance premium actually buys in this corridor
paragraphs: Break the in-home premium into its parts and it becomes easy to judge. Market in-home rates in Abu Dhabi run roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's rate work, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. On the same tier of teacher, the difference is the journey. For a tutor coming to Al Raha Beach from the city or from Khalifa City, that journey is twenty to forty-five minutes each way in the late afternoon, plus community access.

What the premium buys is a person in the room. For a younger student, or one who disengages the moment a screen is involved, that is worth paying for and should be said plainly. Supervision is easier. Written work on paper is easier to see. A tutor can notice a student's posture change when a topic appears.

What the premium does not buy is choice, and this is where the Al Raha Beach geography bites. The pool shrinks to people willing to make that drive at that hour. For a mainstream IGCSE subject the pool is still adequate. For Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 with its investigation paper, Further Pure Mathematics, or a Diploma language B at Higher Level, it shrinks to a handful or to nobody, and a family ends up choosing availability over suitability without quite realising they have done it.

The decision is therefore different for different children in the same household. A Year 7 student who needs supervision as much as teaching may genuinely be better served by a person in the room. A Diploma student working on a Paper 3 question needs the best specialist available and a whiteboard they can rewatch. IB Gram serves UAE families online for both cases and does not run home visits in the UAE, so for the first case we say what the honest trade-off is rather than pretending it does not exist.
