sections.heading: Running one IB and one IGCSE student on a single budget
paragraphs: Households in this corridor frequently have a Diploma student and a Year 10 or 11 candidate at the same time, and the instinct is to split the tutoring budget evenly. That is almost always the wrong allocation, because the two stages have very different marginal returns on an hour of tuition.

The Diploma student's hours are worth more per hour and should be fewer. Higher Level component work, Paper 3, and internal assessment feedback genuinely require subject-level specialism, and the top of the market band is justified for them. But the Diploma student also has school support, a coordinator, and a structured deadline calendar, so a targeted block beats a standing weekly slot.

The IGCSE student's hours are cheaper and often need to be more numerous, because the common losses are habit-shaped rather than concept-shaped: rounding, units, missing method steps, unattempted final pages. Those take repetition rather than brilliance to fix, and a competent mid-tier tutor will do it as well as a premium one. Spending the premium rate here is a waste of the household's money.

The practical structure that works is consecutive slots on one evening, separate specialists, one point of contact, and one termly review covering both children. The administration cost collapses, the disruption is confined to a single evening, and each child keeps a tutor matched to their actual specification. sections.heading: Who regulates the schools, and why a parent should know
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi deal with ADEK and often do not realise that the authority differs by emirate, which matters the moment a family moves within the UAE or compares a school across emirates. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate.

Sharjah's private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools, and it is worth knowing that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so their remit extends beyond inspection.

None of these authorities regulates private tutoring rates, which is the single clearest explanation for why school fees have a controlled structure and tutoring prices span a fourteen-fold range. What does govern individual tutors is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, under which the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a different thing from an individual's tutor permit, and neither should ever be presented as an endorsement of a platform.

sections.heading: What to send when you ask three providers for a quote
paragraphs: Most quotes a family receives are vague because the request was vague. A message that says a Year 10 student needs help with maths produces a price for an hour of generic tuition, and the quotes cannot be compared because nobody is pricing the same thing. Six lines of information changes that entirely.

Send the board and the specification code with tier: Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Higher, IB Analysis and Approaches Standard Level. Send the year group and the school's own assessment calendar. Send the most recent marked assessment, which is worth more than any description of the problem because the losses are visible on it. Name the component that is going wrong rather than the subject.

Then ask the six extras questions in the same message: minimum block, cancellation window, whether a written report is included, whether a travel surcharge applies to Al Raha Beach, whether materials are charged separately, and whether the quoted figure includes VAT. Ask what happens if the match is wrong in week three. Ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit and under which category.

The answers sort the market faster than any amount of browsing. A provider who prices a named component, answers the extras in writing, and discloses where the tutor is based has given you a comparable quote. A provider who returns an hourly rate and a paragraph about confidence has not, and the gap between those two responses is a better predictor of the next thirty hours than any rate on this page.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and when the tutoring year actually works
paragraphs: Scheduling is a cost too, because a slot that keeps getting missed is money spent on nothing. The UAE academic year has a distinctive rhythm, and a family planning a term's tuition should plan around it rather than discover it.

Ramadan shortens the school day across the UAE and shifts the shape of an evening completely. Study after Iftar works well for many families and badly for others, and the only sensible approach is to agree the Ramadan arrangement in advance rather than to cancel week by week. Some students do their best concentrated work in the quiet late evening of that month; others need the block moved out of it altogether. Both are legitimate and both need deciding before it starts.

The long summer break is the other structural feature, and it is the most under-used tuition window in this market. Transition work belongs here: the non-calculator fluency block between IGCSE and post-16 maths, the MYP to Diploma algebra bridge, the Extended Essay research question settled before DP2 starts. Buying those hours in the summer costs the same as buying them in October and is worth considerably more, because nothing else is competing for the student's attention.

Within a term, the pattern worth avoiding is the fortnight before a school's own internal deadline, when a student is least able to absorb new teaching and most in need of time. Plan intensive blocks either side of those deadlines. And where a family travels between Abu Dhabi and abroad during holidays, online delivery on a stated time zone means the schedule can follow them rather than pause, which is a practical advantage over any visiting arrangement.

sections.heading: How IB Gram answers the 'near me' question
paragraphs: The honest answer to a 'near me' search is that we are not near you, and that this is deliberate rather than a limitation we are apologising for. IB Gram matches Al Raha Beach families with tutors who teach their child's exact course, and delivers lessons one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India.

What replaces proximity is specificity. You tell us the board, the course, the level and the component. We propose a tutor who teaches that, and say where they are based before you book rather than after. The first lesson is a free trial with no card details collected, which is the point at which you can test whether the tutor can name your child's papers and their weightings without looking them up.

Matching takes a couple of working days for mainstream IGCSE subjects and for Diploma courses with deep supply. It takes longer for thin ones, and where nobody suitable is free we give one of three answers: a waiting date, a disclosed tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on the same clock, or an admission that we cannot cover it well. The third answer loses the booking, which is why so few pages in this market contain it.

On the two things this page has been about, the position is simple. Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate study that published it, with the month it was read, and none of them is an IB Gram price list. And every extra on the checklist is a question we will answer in writing before you commit, because a quote a parent cannot compare is not really a quote.

process.description: One marked mock or internal assessment is worth more than a page of description, because the losses are visible on it. It also lets a tutor say in the trial lesson which two topics to attack first and why those two, which is the test of whether they know the specification.

process.description: Minimum block, cancellation window, report charges, travel surcharge, materials, VAT position. Ask all six of every provider you approach, including us. The answers reorder the shortlist more often than the hourly rates do.

process.description: One lesson at no charge, no card details collected. Count how much your child speaks. Ask the tutor afterwards which two topics they would start with. A tutor who answers in named topics is worth their rate; one who answers in adjectives is not.

process.title: Book a block with an end date, then review
process.description: Hours bought against a named component with a defined finish, rather than an open weekly slot. At the end, check whether the named problem closed. If it did, the hours move or stop. That single discipline is what stops a tutoring budget drifting upwards unexamined.

whyPoints.description: Each AED figure is attributed to the competitor page or rate study it came from, with the month it was read. No ranking page in this market cites a source for a single rate, and an unsourced number is not something a parent can act on.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write, complete or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. That boundary protects the student's qualification.

faqs.question: Why do IB and IGCSE tutor rates in Abu Dhabi vary from AED 45 to AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: Because the figure reflects a business model rather than a level of skill. A university student tutoring under a private tuition permit carries no overheads and advertises from the low end; EdFlik quotes from AED 45 to 65. An agency funds matching, vetting and a replacement policy, which is where Unitors' AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB sits. A visiting tutor prices in a car and an unpaid hour of driving, which Bestimate puts at AED 180 to 350. A premium brand charges for reputation; BartyED quotes AED 650. Read the model, then the rate.

faqs.question: What extra charges should I ask about before booking a tutor in Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: Six, and all are answerable in one message. The minimum block, because some providers quote hourly and sell only in eights or twelves. The cancellation window and what is charged inside it. Whether a written progress report is included or extra. Whether a travel surcharge applies to Al Raha Beach or Al Reef, which is common on the airport side. Whether materials, platform licences or mock packs are billed separately. And whether the quoted AED figure includes VAT, which should be confirmed in writing by the provider for their own prices.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor actually worse for my child?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the question is better asked per task. Habit-shaped losses, which is most of what costs IGCSE candidates marks, respond to repetition rather than to brilliance: rounding, missing units, unattempted final pages, working that skips the step the mark scheme needed. A competent mid-tier tutor fixes those as well as a premium one. Where the premium genuinely buys something is Diploma Higher Level component work, internal assessment criteria and thin specifications, because those need subject-level depth that the budget tier generally does not have.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office or centre in Abu Dhabi I can visit?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and we would rather state that than let a footer address imply otherwise. Tuition for UAE families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We also do not send tutors to UAE addresses; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If a provider competing for this search shows a UAE address, it is worth checking whether they actually occupy it, because at least one ranking page shows a Dubai footer on an Abu Dhabi page.

faqs.question: How should I split a tutoring budget between a Diploma child and an IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Not evenly. The Diploma student's hours should be fewer and more expensive, because Higher Level component work, Paper 3 and internal assessment feedback need real subject depth, and the school already provides structure around them. The IGCSE student's hours should be cheaper and more numerous, because the common losses are habits that respond to repetition. A worked allocation at market rates might be ten specialist hours plus a four-hour assessment clinic for the Diploma student, and fourteen mid-tier hours split between topic repair and timed papers for the IGCSE candidate.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share a tutor to save money?
faqs.answer: Only where the content is genuinely shared. Two students on the same specification and tier can work together productively on timed paper practice and mark-scheme technique, and the per-student rate is substantially lower. It does not work for diagnostic or gap-closing work, because two students' gaps are by definition different and one of them ends up watching. The arrangement that usually serves a two-child household better is consecutive one-to-one slots on the same evening with separate specialists and a single point of contact.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. The authority differs elsewhere in the UAE: KHDA in Dubai, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods. None of them regulates private tutoring rates, which is why tutoring prices spread so much more widely than school fees do.

faqs.question: Do I need to check whether a tutor has a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it takes one question. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified. Ask which category the tutor holds it under.

faqs.question: How do I write a tutoring request that gets comparable quotes?
faqs.answer: Six lines. The board and specification code with tier. The year group and the school's assessment calendar. The component that is going wrong, named rather than described. The most recent marked assessment attached. The six extras questions asked in the same message. And a question about what happens if the match is wrong in week three. Providers who price a named component and answer the extras in writing have given you something comparable. Providers who return an hourly rate and a paragraph about confidence have not, which is itself informative.

faqs.question: When in the UAE school year is tutoring money best spent?
faqs.answer: The summer break is the most under-used window in this market and often the most valuable, because transition work belongs there: non-calculator fluency between IGCSE and post-16 maths, the MYP to Diploma algebra bridge, an Extended Essay research question settled before DP2 begins. Within term time, the twelve weeks before an exam series return the most per hour on technique and timed papers. The period to avoid for new teaching is the fortnight before a school's own internal deadline, when a student needs time rather than more input.

faqs.question: How does tutoring work during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The school day shortens and the evening changes shape, so the arrangement should be agreed before the month starts rather than negotiated week by week. Post-Iftar sessions work well for many students, who find the quiet late evening their most productive concentrated time. Others do better having the block moved out of Ramadan entirely and resumed afterwards. Both are reasonable. What wastes money is a standing slot that gets cancelled four weeks in a row, since a missed session is the one cost with no educational return at all.

faqs.question: Will lessons continue if we travel between Abu Dhabi and abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one practical advantage of online delivery over any visiting arrangement. Lessons are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time by default, and where a family is travelling the slot can move to suit the time zone they are in rather than pausing for the trip. It does need stating in advance so the tutor's own week can accommodate it. Families who travel frequently often keep a lighter but unbroken schedule through holidays rather than a heavy term-time one with month-long gaps, which works better for retention.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right match after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. A mismatch is usually visible by the third session, and the signals are consistent: your child speaks very little, the sessions cover ground rather than fixing anything named, and there is no running record of what has closed. We rematch on request, and the information from the first attempt makes the second one better because the component and the loss pattern are now documented. Ask any provider what their replacement policy is before booking, not after.

faqs.question: Are tutors allowed to give me past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: They should reference and link them rather than distribute them. Past papers, mark schemes, specifications and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing or supplying them as downloads is a copyright matter rather than a grey area. Your child's school has legitimate access, and the boards publish material through their own channels. A provider offering a bundle of papers as a selling point is doing something that should make a parent cautious rather than pleased, and it says something about the rest of their practice.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student in Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: For mainstream IGCSE subjects and Diploma courses with deep supply, usually one to two working days. For thinner courses, longer: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Further Pure Mathematics and some Diploma language B courses can take up to a week. Where nobody suitable is free we give one of three answers rather than a vague reassurance: a waiting date, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time and disclosed as such, or an admission that we cannot cover it well.

intro.heading: One household, two examination calendars
paragraphs: Al Raha Gardens is a community where this situation is common. The school at its centre runs the full IB continuum, while families wanting the British pathway commute to Khalifa City and sometimes as far as Al Bateen or Al Mushrif. A single household can therefore contain a Middle Years student, a Year 11 IGCSE candidate and a Diploma student, on three different assessment systems, none of which shares a deadline. That is not an unusual arrangement here; it is close to the default for a family of three children.

The two examined calendars work in opposite ways, and this is the fact that makes planning hard. The IGCSE calendar is external and dated: entry deadlines, zone timetables, published results days. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; its February and March series is India-only. Pearson runs May, June and November, and June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026.

The IB calendar is internal and school-set for most of its length. Internal Assessment drafts, the Extended Essay milestones, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay deadlines are all fixed by your school rather than published nationally, and they cluster into a nine-month stretch of the Diploma. A family planning around the May examination session alone has planned around the least demanding part of it.

Because the IB dates are school-set and because no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and nothing more precise. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative version for your child's cohort. A date restated on a website, this one included, is a guide to structure rather than a source to act on.

The collisions are predictable once you have both calendars on one page. IGCSE mocks and Diploma Internal Assessment drafts tend to land in the same winter weeks. IGCSE study leave and Diploma examination preparation overlap in the spring. Results seasons sit weeks apart in the summer, which means two sets of decisions in one holiday. And the Year 11 to Diploma first year bridge, which nobody schedules, falls in the gap between them.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Al Raha Gardens is one-to-one teaching over live video, which makes a two-system household materially easier to run: two different specialists, back-to-back on the same evening, with no travel to co-ordinate between them. One night of the week is committed rather than three, and neither session begins late because somebody was held up between two addresses.

sections.heading: The two calendars, side by side
paragraphs: Getting both calendars onto one page in September is the highest-value hour a two-system household spends, and almost nobody does it. The reason is structural: the IGCSE calendar is published and dated by the examination boards, while the Diploma calendar is mostly set internally by your child's school and exists only in a document the student was given in the first week and has not looked at since.

The published side is straightforward. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson runs May, June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the family's risk.

The internal side is denser and less visible. Four or five Internal Assessments, each typically worth around twenty per cent of its subject, with school-set draft deadlines. An Extended Essay with supervisor meetings and milestone dates. A Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay. Creativity Activity Service requirements running alongside. None of it is published nationally and all of it is compulsory.

Ask your Diploma child's school for its internal deadline list in writing. Most schools issue one. Put it beside the IGCSE child's mock and study-leave dates, and the collision weeks appear immediately. In most Abu Dhabi households they are the same three or four weeks every year, and knowing which ones they are lets you front-load support instead of reacting to it.

sections.heading: Why the Diploma's internal deadline chain is the harder calendar
paragraphs: Parents plan Diploma support around the final papers and the pressure does not land there. It lands in the middle, in a nine-month stretch where four or five Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay and two rounds of mocks arrive in an order nobody has written down for the student in one place.

The chain matters because the links are sequential. A science Internal Assessment needs data collected while laboratory access exists, which puts the method decision months before the write-up. The mathematics exploration needs a topic narrow enough to finish, which is a decision rather than a task, and students defer decisions far longer than tasks. The Extended Essay needs a supervised first draft before Internal Assessments start arriving, because afterwards there is no spare week.

The weightings explain why this is worth the attention. Internal Assessments are typically twenty per cent of a subject grade. Across six subjects that is a substantial share of the Diploma, produced in conditions the student controls, marked against criteria that are published. It is the most recoverable part of the qualification and the part most commonly left to chance.

A tutor's most useful contribution here is refusing to let a deadline be a surprise. The first session of a Diploma engagement should produce a single sheet: every internal deadline the school has published, every external component, and the three weeks in the year where two of them collide. Everything after that is teaching against a known map rather than reacting to whatever arrived on Sunday.

sections.heading: The bridge summer nobody schedules
paragraphs: Between the end of Year 11 and the start of the Diploma sits a gap that decides a surprising amount, and in Al Raha Gardens it often coincides with a change of school because British-pathway students commuting to Khalifa City may move to a Diploma school afterwards. Nothing in Year 11 prepares a student for what arrives, and Diploma induction does not cover it either.

Three specific things are missing. First, unstructured problems: IGCSE questions tell a student which method to use, and Diploma questions frequently do not. Second, criterion-marked writing, where a student is assessed against published descriptors rather than a mark scheme of right answers. Third, the mathematics course decision, between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, which has university consequences and is usually made on instinct.

The good news is that the gap is narrow and the work is cheap. Three to five sessions in that summer, on open problem work and criterion reading, with one session on the mathematics decision, materially changes the first Diploma term. It is also the only tutoring in the six years that competes with nothing: no deadlines, no mocks, no coursework, no other subject demanding the same hours.

It is worth saying what the gap is not. It is not a content gap. An IGCSE student arriving in the Diploma generally knows enough content; what they lack is the way the questions are posed and the way the internal work is judged. A provider offering a summer content course is solving a problem the student does not have, which is a common and expensive misdiagnosis.

sections.heading: Two results seasons in one summer
paragraphs: A two-system household gets two sets of post-results decisions within a few weeks, which is harder than it sounds because each has its own short window and its own options. For the IGCSE side the dates are published: Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The IGCSE options after a disappointing grade are three. An enquiry about results, submitted by the school within a board deadline, which is a clerical and marking review rather than a general appeal. A November series resit, producing a grade the following January. Or a full retake in the next June series. For a UAE candidate the February and March series is not available, being offered to India only.

On the IB side, results reach candidates in July according to the school confirmation each cohort receives, and the options are different in kind: an enquiry upon results through the school, a retake in a subsequent session, or acceptance. Because no IB date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, every IB date and deadline should be taken from your school's Diploma coordinator rather than from any website.

The practical move for a two-system family is to have both conversations in the spring, before either result arrives. Decide in advance what grade would trigger a remark request, what would trigger a resit, and what would simply be accepted. Decisions made calmly in March are better than decisions made in the forty-eight hours after a result, when nobody in the house is thinking clearly.

sections.heading: One tutor or two across a household
paragraphs: Families ask whether one tutor can cover both children, usually for budget reasons, and the honest answer is almost never. The same subject name means different things in the two systems: IGCSE Mathematics is two timed papers with no coursework, while Diploma mathematics adds a twenty per cent exploration and, at Higher Level, a third paper worth a fifth of the grade.

What can genuinely be shared across a household is narrower and still worth having. Command-term discipline transfers, because the same verbs appear in both systems and a student who learns the difference between explain and evaluate improves in both. Study technique transfers. Timed-practice habits transfer. Pacing arithmetic transfers. None of those requires the same person to teach both children.

What cannot be shared is specification knowledge, which is the part that moves grades. A tutor who teaches Cambridge 0620 weekly knows where the qualitative analysis marks are. A tutor who teaches Diploma Chemistry weekly knows how the investigation's four criteria are allocated. Those are different bodies of knowledge and a tutor who claims both at an equal standard is usually claiming too much.

The practical arrangement that works in Al Raha Gardens households is two specialists in consecutive online slots on the same evening. One evening is committed rather than three, each child gets somebody who teaches their system, and because nobody is travelling neither session starts late. That is the clearest operational benefit online delivery gives a two-system family.

sections.heading: ADEK, equivalency, and the paperwork after results
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Two-system households deal with ADEK twice over, once per school, and the schools' fee approval and calendar arrangements both run through the regulator rather than being set freely.

The paperwork that catches families out later is certificate equivalency, administered by the Ministry of Education. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail most often got wrong is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. At least one competitor ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. That matters because it changes the subject list a Year 10 student should be entered for, which is a dated decision.

For the IB track, no points threshold for equivalency has been read on a Ministry source, so this page publishes none. Publishing an unverified figure would be worse than publishing nothing. Equivalency is a Ministry process rather than something a tutoring service performs or guarantees; verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own site or with the attestation authority, and treat any provider claiming to secure it for you with caution.

paragraphs: Running support for two children in two systems costs roughly double running it for one, and the only real saving available is in scheduling rather than in price. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270 and premium named tutors quoted as high as AED 650 at BartyED. The allocation that works in a two-system household is to protect the Diploma child's Internal Assessment windows and the Year 11 child's final twelve weeks, and to be modest everywhere else. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, we hold no ADEK, MoHRE or board approval, and there is no Abu Dhabi office. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback; nobody here writes an Internal Assessment, drafts an Extended Essay, composes a Theory of Knowledge essay or produces coursework in any system.

faqs.question: Can one IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Raha Gardens cover both of my children?
faqs.answer: Almost never usefully. The same subject name means different things: IGCSE Mathematics is two timed papers with no coursework, while Diploma mathematics adds a twenty per cent exploration and, at Higher Level, a third paper worth a fifth of the grade. Specification knowledge is what moves grades and nobody holds two systems at an equal standard. What can be shared is command-term discipline, timed-practice habits and the scheduling, which is where the real saving sits.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to Al Raha Gardens for either system?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Both children's lessons are one to one over live video. For a two-system household that is a practical advantage rather than a compromise: two different specialists can take consecutive slots on the same evening, so one night is committed instead of three and neither session starts late because nobody is driving.

faqs.question: Why do the IB and IGCSE calendars clash so badly in the winter?
faqs.answer: Because the IGCSE mock season and the Diploma Internal Assessment draft deadlines land in the same weeks, and they demand opposite kinds of work. Mocks need timed revision; Internal Assessment drafts need sustained writing. A household with one child in each is trying to supply both at once in late November and December. Getting both calendars onto one page in September lets you front-load one of them instead of discovering the clash while it is happening.

faqs.question: Where do I get the Diploma internal deadline dates from?
faqs.answer: From the school, in writing. Most Diploma schools issue a list of internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge in the first term, and most students never show it to a parent. Ask your child for it, and if it has gone missing email the Diploma coordinator. Those dates are school-set rather than published nationally, which is precisely why they are easier to miss than the IGCSE ones.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my Year 11 child sit in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: June or November with Cambridge International, and May, June or November with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so no candidate in Abu Dhabi sits it whatever a generic revision site suggests. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Check your school's own zone timetable on the board's site, since Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones.

faqs.question: In a two-system household, which child has more recoverable marks?
faqs.answer: Typically around twenty per cent, and in some subjects more. The science investigation is twenty per cent, marked out of twenty-four across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation with a three-thousand-word maximum. The mathematics exploration is twenty per cent, marked out of twenty across five criteria. The Economics portfolio can reach thirty per cent at Standard Level. It is the most recoverable part of the Diploma and the part most often left to chance.

faqs.question: What does my Year 11 child actually need before starting the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them content. Practice with unstructured problems, because IGCSE questions tell a student which method to use and Diploma questions frequently do not. Experience of criterion-marked writing, where work is judged against published descriptors rather than a mark scheme of right answers. And a decision on the mathematics course, between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, which has university consequences. Three to five summer sessions cover all three.

faqs.question: Is a summer content course a good idea before the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because it solves a problem most students do not have. An IGCSE student arriving in the Diploma generally knows enough content; what they lack is the way questions are posed and the way internal work is judged. A provider offering a summer content course is misdiagnosing the gap, which is a common and expensive mistake. Spend the summer on open problem work, criterion reading and the mathematics decision instead.

faqs.question: Does my Al Raha Gardens child need five or six IGCSE passes for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, on the published British-track rule: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. At least one site ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry before acting.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points figure for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not one this page will publish, because no IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on a Ministry of Education source. The British-track numbers are sourced and quotable; the IB figure is not, and publishing an unverified number on a page a parent might act on would be worse than publishing nothing. Equivalency is a Ministry process rather than something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees. Verify it with the Ministry or the attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: When do the two sets of results arrive, and what are the options?
faqs.answer: The IGCSE side is published: Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, with options of an enquiry about results, a November resit producing a grade the following January, or a retake in the next June series. On the IB side, results reach candidates in July according to each cohort's school confirmation, with options of an enquiry upon results, a retake in a later session, or acceptance. Take all IB dates from the coordinator.

faqs.question: Should we decide about resits before results arrive?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the spring, and it is the single most useful conversation a two-system household can have. Agree in advance what grade would trigger a remark request, what would trigger a resit, and what would simply be accepted. Decisions made calmly in March are considerably better than decisions made in the forty-eight hours after a result lands, when nobody in the house is thinking clearly and the windows for acting are short.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with both an IA draft and IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: Within the same boundary in both systems, yes, and it is the same boundary. A tutor may teach content, explain what the criteria reward, question whether a plan is answerable, suggest reading, and say why a section is weak. Nobody at IB Gram writes an Internal Assessment, drafts an Extended Essay, composes a Theory of Knowledge essay or produces coursework. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, in either system, at any price.

faqs.question: What does supporting two children in two systems cost here?
faqs.answer: Roughly double supporting one, because two specialists are needed. Published Abu Dhabi bands run from about AED 33 to 65 for student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists. The saving available is in scheduling rather than price: consecutive online slots commit one evening a week. The spending that works is protecting the Diploma child's Internal Assessment windows and the Year 11 child's final twelve weeks.

faqs.question: Can you staff two specialists in consecutive slots on one evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the arrangement most two-system Al Raha Gardens households settle on. Common subjects in both systems match within a few days. The constraint is narrow combinations at fixed hours: a specific Higher Level component at 19:00 competes with Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas households for the same window. Where we cannot staff both consecutively we will say so and offer two different evenings rather than putting one tutor across both systems.

intro.heading: Two systems in one household, and the comparison nobody makes properly
paragraphs: Plenty of Al Rawdah families are running both systems at the same time. An older child is in the Diploma managing internal assessment deadlines and a 45-point total; a younger one is in Year 10 heading for a terminal IGCSE series with a tier already decided. The two need different kinds of help at different points in the year, and a single search for a tutor nearby tends to produce providers who treat them as the same request.

Other families are standing at the decision itself. A British-curriculum school has taken the child to Year 11 and now offers either A-Levels or the Diploma; or an IB continuum school is the alternative to an IGCSE route at 14. That decision is usually made on reputation and anecdote, which is a shame, because the two systems differ in documented ways that suit different students, and the differences can be set out plainly.

The headline difference is the assessment culture. The Diploma spreads consequence across two years: six subjects, three at Higher Level, internal assessments carrying substantial weight in most subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay worth up to three points, and a final examination session on top. IGCSE concentrates consequence into a terminal series, with tiering that caps the grade available and no coursework in most mainstream syllabuses. One rewards sustained organisation; the other rewards performance in a window.

The second difference is reversibility. IGCSE tier entry can sometimes be changed before the school's deadline, and a student who struggles in Year 10 can recover in Year 11 because the marks come at the end. Diploma course and level choices become effectively fixed within a term because the content diverges, and internal assessment marks banked early cannot be revisited. A family choosing between the systems is choosing between a late decision point and an early one.

There is a third group searching this phrase: families who are happy with both schools and simply want one subject fixed. For them the comparison between systems is irrelevant and the only question is whether the tutor has taught the exact course or syllabus code. That is worth separating out early, because a page like this can make a simple request feel like a decision. If your child needs help with Diploma Chemistry or Cambridge 0580 and nothing else is in question, skip to the sections on provider models and verification, which are the two that matter for a single-subject booking.

IB Gram teaches both as live one-to-one video tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a household running two systems that arrangement has an obvious practical benefit: two matched specialists on consecutive slots on one evening, with no travel between them and nothing lost when the week moves.

sections.heading: The IB and IGCSE compared as assessment systems
paragraphs: Comparing the two systems on difficulty produces an argument. Comparing them on structure produces something usable. The Diploma distributes consequence: internal assessments in most subjects, core components worth up to three points, six subjects to keep moving, and a final session. IGCSE concentrates it: a terminal series, tiered entry, and almost nothing banked along the way in mainstream syllabuses.

That difference decides which student each suits. A student who organises well, works steadily and writes fluently thrives in a system that rewards sustained output across two years. A student who works in bursts, performs under pressure and resents coursework often does better where the marks arrive at the end. Neither is a better student; they are suited to different assessment cultures, and matching the student to the culture produces better grades than pushing either into the other.

The reversibility point matters too. An IGCSE student who has a poor Year 10 can still produce a strong terminal result, and a tier change is sometimes possible before the school's deadline. A Diploma student whose internal assessment mark is banked in DP1 carries it, and a course or level chosen in Year 11 is effectively fixed by the end of DP1 term one because the content diverges. Families who like keeping options open should know which system keeps them open longer.

Finally, the documentation. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track the requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so a family planning around UAE university entry should verify the IB position on moe.gov.ae rather than accept a figure from any commercial page, including this one.

sections.heading: MYP or IGCSE at fourteen, and what each leaves the student holding at sixteen
paragraphs: Families at an IB continuum school sometimes ask whether their child should sit IGCSEs at all. It is a fair question with a practical answer. Both routes lead into the Diploma, and schools running MYP prepare students for it directly. The difference is what the student holds at sixteen and what habits they have built.

MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked 0 to 8, with a Personal Project in the final year. The student leaves with strong investigation and communication skills, experience of extended independent work, and relatively little practice at timed written examinations. IGCSE leaves the student with an externally examined certificate, considerable practice at papers under timing, and less experience of sustained independent projects.

The consequence appears in DP1 term one. MYP students meet timed technical writing and sustained algebra under pressure for the first time; IGCSE students meet independent project work and the internal assessment culture for the first time. Both gaps are real and both are closeable in a term, but they are different gaps requiring different work, which is why a tutor should ask where a DP1 student came from before proposing anything.

For families who may apply to UAE universities, there is one asymmetry worth weighing. The IGCSE certificate counts towards Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, where the published requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded. That is a documented pathway. The equivalency treatment of the IB route should be verified directly with the Ministry rather than assumed, and that verification is worth doing before the decision rather than after it.

sections.heading: Switching systems: the transition map, subject by subject
paragraphs: Mid-stream curriculum changes are common in Abu Dhabi because families relocate within the city and between countries. The useful thing is a map rather than reassurance: for each common move, what carries across, what does not, and roughly how long the gap takes to close with support.

IGCSE into the Diploma is the most frequent. Algebra, trigonometry and data handling carry across well. Calculus does not exist yet, independent project work is unfamiliar, and the pace of written technical work is faster. Eight to twelve sessions in DP1 term one normally covers it, concentrated on algebraic fluency at speed and on how an internal assessment is actually structured.

MYP into the Diploma carries across investigation skill, reflection and communication, and lacks timed examination technique and formal proof. A term of weekly work started in September covers it; the same gap addressed in February does not, because by then the student has a year of unfamiliar habits layered on top. CBSE or Indian-curriculum transfers often arrive with more calculus than the course needs, no experience of a graphical display calculator and little exposure to command-term question styles. American high school transfers arrive comfortable with technology and breadth and short on algebraic manipulation at speed.

The move nobody plans for is a transfer in the middle of DP1 or Year 11. It is the hardest because internal assessment deadlines and tier entries are already in motion at the receiving school. The first job there is administrative rather than academic: establish from the new school what has already been banked, what deadlines are live, and whether the course or tier the student was on is even offered. Tutoring that starts before that information is in hand is guessing.

sections.heading: What each kind of tutoring provider is actually selling
paragraphs: Every tutoring site compares itself favourably with an unnamed set of other platforms. A more useful comparison is between the models themselves, including the model we belong to, because each has a structural advantage and a structural weakness that no amount of marketing changes.

A specialist agency vets its tutors, charges accordingly and usually publishes least about price. An international marketplace offers volume and choice with little localisation; one such site in this market quotes in US dollars, names no UAE school, no area and no regulator. A freelance tutor found through word of mouth is often excellent and often cheapest, with no replacement if the match fails and no continuity if they leave the country. A tuition centre offers premises and group rates, and in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute to operate as one. An online matching platform, which is what IB Gram is, offers course-level matching and replacement at the cost of physical presence.

Knowing the structural weakness of your chosen model is what protects you. With a freelancer, ask what happens if they leave. With a marketplace, ask who vetted the tutor and against what. With an agency, ask what the rate includes and whether the person who sells is the person who teaches. With a centre, ask the group size. With an online platform, including ours, ask what happens when the specialist you need is unavailable and whether the tutor is based in the UAE.

One rule applies across all five. A provider that compares itself to a straw man, publishes a star rating it cannot evidence, or implies a regulator endorsement is telling you how it will behave later. Competitor pages in this market show two different review totals on the same page, and one shows a self-asserted rating against a student count that does not reconcile. Treat unverifiable social proof as a negative signal rather than a neutral one.

sections.heading: Comparing cost across the models rather than across the tutors
paragraphs: Rates differ by model more than by individual, so comparing two tutors from different models tells you less than comparing the models. The published bands, read in October 2026, map onto the models fairly clearly, and the cheapest band is not automatically the wrong choice.

Budget online tuition, often delivered by university students through platforms, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online, the band an online matching platform usually occupies, run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Independent in-home tutors and agency visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel included, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tuition runs AED 200 to 450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led work reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, BartyED publishing AED 650.

For a two-system household the arithmetic compounds, which is why the model choice matters more here than for a single child. Two children at the qualified online band for one hour a week each is a different monthly commitment from two children at the specialist in-home band, and the difference over a school year is substantial. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is a useful pair of anchors.

Two notes. These are market rates from named published sources, not IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson, when the course or code and session length are known. And one competitor's own frequently asked questions in this market pose the price question and then decline to answer it, while another's structured data contradicts the price shown on the page. A provider willing to publish a band with its source is giving you something you can check.

sections.heading: Verification compared: what you can actually check before paying
paragraphs: Across every model there are four checks a parent can make, and they take minutes rather than hours. The first is the tutor's permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE grants the private tutor work permit free of charge for two years to a defined set of applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. It is free, so ask to see it.

The second is the school's regulator. For Al Rawdah that is ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes its own inspection ratings. Dubai has KHDA, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Read ratings there, not on a tutoring page.

The third is any accreditation claim. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. If a provider implies a regulator relationship, ask for the permit number.

The fourth is any statistic. A satisfaction percentage, a tutor score average or a success rate means nothing without a sample size, a date and a method, and should be read as marketing rather than evidence. The same applies to star ratings that differ between a page and its structured data, which happens in this market. None of these checks requires expertise, and together they filter out most of what is wrong with this SERP.

sections.heading: Honest limits, availability and what a first lesson should settle
paragraphs: A page comparing everything should compare its own weaknesses too. Online delivery has no physical presence, which matters for young and distractible students. Our pool is finite, and Diploma Higher Level specialists fill up before mock windows and internal assessment deadlines. We hold no regulator accreditation. We cannot guarantee a grade, because the outcome depends on a student's own work on a specific morning, and no honest provider can.

What we can do is disclose. When no specialist is free for a course or code, you are told, given an expected wait, and offered the alternatives in writing: a different qualified tutor on the same course in another slot, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course on Gulf Standard Time and disclosed before booking, shorter and more frequent sessions until the preferred slot clears, or waiting. Several sites in this market route UAE families to non-UAE numbers without mentioning it.

On assessed work the line is firm in both systems. A tutor teaches, explains and gives feedback on work the student wrote. No internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project is produced here, and one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which exposes a student to a malpractice finding reaching the whole Diploma. We also cite board materials rather than redistributing syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes.

The free trial lesson is the place all of this becomes concrete. One full lesson per child, no card required, no block of hours bought first. It should settle three things: where the marks are actually going, whether the course, level or tier looks right on the evidence, and how many sessions the work genuinely needs. For a two-system household it should also produce one view of both children's plans, which is often the first time anybody has looked at them together.

faqs.question: We have one child in the Diploma and one in Year 10. Can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, but it is usually a compromise. The two systems need different things: the Diploma child needs seasonal support shaped around internal assessment deadlines and mocks, while the Year 10 child needs steadier work aimed at a terminal series and a tier ceiling. Two matched specialists on consecutive online slots cost the same as two separate bookings, save the scheduling, and give each child somebody who has taught their actual course. Ask what any single tutor has genuinely taught before agreeing.

faqs.question: Which system suits a student who works in bursts rather than steadily?
faqs.answer: Generally the IGCSE route, because the marks arrive at the end and a poor Year 10 can still be followed by a strong terminal result. The Diploma distributes consequence across two years through internal assessments and core components, which rewards sustained organisation and punishes a student who works only under pressure. Neither is the better system; they suit different working styles, and matching the student to the assessment culture produces better grades than forcing either into the other.

faqs.question: Is the Diploma harder than A-Levels for a student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is broader rather than straightforwardly harder. The Diploma runs six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with internal assessments in most subjects. A-Levels run three or four subjects deeply with no core and pressure concentrated in the examination series. A student certain of their direction who dislikes breadth often performs better on A-Levels; an undecided or broadly capable student often performs better on the Diploma.

faqs.question: Should our child sit IGCSEs if their school runs the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: Both routes lead into the Diploma, so the academic answer is that neither disadvantages them. The practical difference is what they hold at sixteen. IGCSE produces an externally examined certificate that counts towards Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, where the published requirement is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded. MYP produces no external certificate. Families who may apply to UAE universities often weigh that heavily.

faqs.question: What actually changes when a student moves from IGCSE into DP1?
faqs.answer: Algebra, trigonometry and data handling carry across well. What is new is calculus, independent project work on the scale an internal assessment requires, and a faster pace of written technical work. Eight to twelve sessions in DP1 term one normally covers it, concentrated on algebraic fluency at speed and on how an internal assessment is actually structured. The same gap addressed in DP2 costs considerably more, because a year of newer content now sits on top of it.

faqs.question: Our child is transferring schools mid-year. Where do we even start?
faqs.answer: With an administrative audit rather than tutoring. Establish from the receiving school what internal assessment marks have already been banked, which deadlines are live, whether the course or tier your child was on is offered there, and what the entry position is for the current series. Tutoring arranged before that information is in hand is guessing. Mid-DP1 and mid-Year 11 transfers are the hardest moves precisely because deadlines and entries are already in motion.

faqs.question: How do agencies, marketplaces, freelancers and centres actually differ?
faqs.answer: Each has a structural advantage and a matching weakness. An agency offers vetting at the highest price and often publishes no rate. A marketplace offers volume with little localisation, sometimes pricing in other currencies. A freelancer is often excellent and cheapest with no replacement if the match fails. A centre offers premises and group rates, with group size diluting attention. An online matching platform, which is what we are, offers course-level matching and replacement but no physical presence in the room.

faqs.question: What question should I ask an online tutoring platform before paying?
faqs.answer: What happens when the specialist I need is booked, and where is the tutor based. Those two expose the weaknesses of the model. A platform should be able to tell you the expected wait, offer named alternatives in writing, and disclose a tutor located outside the UAE before you book rather than after the first invoice. Several sites in this market route UAE families to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it, which is a trust failure rather than a logistics detail.

faqs.question: Why does a star rating on a tutoring site mean so little?
faqs.answer: Because it is often unverifiable and sometimes internally contradictory. Pages in this market show two different review totals on the same page, and one shows a self-asserted rating alongside a student count that does not reconcile with it. Self-serving review markup also breaches Google's structured-data policy. Treat any rating without countable, attributable, dated reviews as marketing rather than evidence, and the same for any satisfaction percentage published without a sample size and method.

faqs.question: Does tutoring cost more for two children in two different systems?
faqs.answer: It costs twice as much per hour, and the model you choose matters more than it would for one child because the arithmetic compounds. Published bands read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Advertised monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which are useful anchors for a household budget.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Extended Essay or a Personal Project?
faqs.answer: With process and feedback only. A tutor can help narrow a research question, explain a method the student then applies, discuss structure, and give feedback against the published criteria on a draft the student wrote. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or edit any part of it to completion, and no part may be produced for the student. The supervisor signs to authenticity, so a breach puts the student's own declaration in question and can affect the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: Which regulator do I contact about a school problem in Al Rawdah?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes its own inspection ratings. Dubai families go to KHDA, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and families in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the Ministry of Education. Read inspection ratings and policies on the regulator's own site rather than on any commercial page.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education optional if my child is in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No. Private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and in Dubai KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. These subjects sit on the timetable in both systems and cannot be dropped to make room for extra Higher Level study.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful thing a first lesson should produce?
faqs.answer: A named list of where the marks are going, plus an honest estimate of how many sessions it takes to recover them. For a two-system household it should also produce one view of both children's plans, which is often the first time anybody has looked at them together. If a first lesson produces only enthusiasm and a package recommendation, it has not diagnosed anything, and the most useful finding is sometimes that a child needs three sessions rather than thirty.

intro.heading: The question is distance; the answer is the monthly figure
paragraphs: A household in Al Reef Villas with one child in Year 11 and another in Diploma Year 1 is not shopping for a tutor. It is deciding how much of the month belongs to tutoring. That decision gets made badly in this market because almost nobody publishes a number. Three of the six pages ranking for searches like this one quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency anyone in Abu Dhabi pays rent in.

So the figures come first here, and they come monthly rather than hourly, because that is the unit a household budget uses. The cheapest route into tutoring in this market, online group or university-student support, is estimated at AED 240 to 600 a month for a weekly one-hour session. A qualified subject teacher online sits at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on the same cadence. Specialist exam-year support runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward. In-home packages of four two-hour visits are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month. Those bands come from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai rate table and from the published rates of EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and BartyED, each named where its figure is used.

The second thing a household needs is the difference between those bands. The step from the budget band to the qualified band buys somebody who has taught the paper. The step from the qualified online band to the in-home band buys driving, and from Al Reef that is thirty to forty minutes each way. Nothing about the drive improves a Diploma physics grade. The step into the premium band buys scarcity - a named specialist in a subject few people teach - and that step is worth taking for Higher Level Chemistry or a Theory of Knowledge essay, and not worth taking for Year 10 maths.

The third thing, and the one this market hides, is the extras. Registration fees. Minimum session blocks. Cancellation windows that charge for a lesson missed because a child had a fever. Assessment fees for the diagnostic that should have been free. Materials charges for past papers that belong to the boards and should be cited and linked rather than sold. A quote that does not mention any of these is not a complete quote, and the list of questions that gets you a complete one is printed further down this page.

On delivery, the honest version: home visits are not something IB Gram sells anywhere in the UAE, because that is an India-only service, and nobody will arrive at an Al Reef address from us. What this household gets instead is a tutor chosen from everyone who teaches the relevant syllabus rather than from the few willing to make the drive, a session that can begin at 17:00 because there is no traffic in it, and a rate with no travel component inside it. Where no suitable tutor has a slot, you are told so and told when one is expected, rather than being matched with whoever was free.
