Every subject carries internally assessed coursework, and that coursework is where a two-year timetable either holds or collapses.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the most expensive programme in this community to support, because six subjects plus coursework supervision is a wide front and the specialist bands apply. The budget discipline that works is to buy Higher Level subject help and Extended Essay process coaching, and to leave Standard Level subjects the student is managing alone. A household trying to tutor all six subjects at once will spend at the top of the specialist band and still not finish the coursework on time.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria on a one-to-eight scale rather than by examination, with a Personal Project in the final year. Marks come from criterion-referenced tasks, so a student can know the content and still score poorly by failing to meet the criterion wording. The transition from criterion marking into Diploma examinations is a real step and is often the reason a strong Year 11 struggles in Diploma Year 1.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Reef family the Middle Years Programme is usually the cheaper half of the budget, because the help needed is interpretation of criteria rather than examination technique. A short block before each reporting cycle, aimed at how the criteria are worded, does more for a Middle Years grade than a standing weekly slot. The Personal Project needs process coaching only, never content production.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject examinations with syllabus codes on the statement of entry: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450 and the rest. Tiering varies by subject, with Core and Extended options in several. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and has no bearing on an Abu Dhabi child.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge entries dominate the schools Al Reef children travel to in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. Because entries are per subject, the budget can be per subject too, which makes this the easiest programme to spend sensibly on: pick the two subjects where the mock grade is furthest from the target and leave the rest. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so the school's own version of the timetable is the only one that counts.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other major IGCSE route, with its own codes: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Examinations run in May/June and November each year. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable ahead of each series, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which is a useful indication of the shape of that window.
programmes.countryNote: Mixing boards within one household is common in Abu Dhabi, because siblings at different schools sit different entries. The budget consequence is that a single tutor rarely covers both well in the same subject, and a provider who claims otherwise without naming the specification codes is guessing. Pearson results timing also matters locally: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit means waiting into the new year.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-r.subjectsIntro: Subject choice drives cost more than board does. The grid below ranks by what the Abu Dhabi market charges for cover rather than by popularity, because scarcity is what moves a rate from the qualified band into the specialist band.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1; IB AA and AI at HL and SL
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in this community and therefore the easiest to buy at a sensible rate. Cover is deep at IGCSE and thinner at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, where Paper 3 and the exploration push a tutor into the specialist band.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1; IB DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Cover is reasonable at IGCSE and scarce at Higher Level, where the practical and data-analysis component plus the internal assessment narrow the field. Expect specialist-band pricing for Diploma Higher Level and qualified-band pricing for Year 10 and 11.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1; IB DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the internal assessment are where households end up paying specialist rates. At IGCSE the subject is well covered. The step from 0620 to Diploma Higher Level is one of the largest in the Diploma and is worth budgeting for before Year 12 starts.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1; IB DP HL and SL
subjects.description: Content-heavy rather than conceptually difficult, which makes it cheap to support well: structured recall work and command-term discipline rather than a specialist. The internal assessment is the part that needs a trained eye, and that is a short block, not a year.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0455 and 0450; IB DP Economics HL and SL
subjects.description: Diploma Economics carries internally assessed commentaries on published news articles, which is process work a tutor can coach without ever touching the student's writing. At IGCSE the marks sit in command terms - explain, analyse, evaluate - rather than in content.

subjects.name: English
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0500, 0510 and 4EA1; IB DP Language A and Language B
subjects.description: Diploma English includes an Individual Oral assessed on a global issue through two extracts, which is the single most coachable component in the Diploma because it rewards structure. IGCSE English divides into First Language and Second Language routes that demand different preparation.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0478 and 0417; IB DP Computer Science
subjects.description: Thin cover across the whole emirate, so this is reliably specialist-band work. The IGCSE pseudocode and trace-table questions are mechanical and teachable quickly; the Diploma internal assessment solution needs supervision across months rather than hours.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, and taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Often absent from a household's tutoring budget until a report arrives, and then needed urgently. Material is tightly prescribed.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Worth up to three bonus points combined, which is the difference between a conditional offer and a rejection. Support here is process coaching: question framing, source selection, structure, meeting the assessment criteria. Nobody writes any part of it for the student, ever.

subjects.name: Further and Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths entry by students heading for A Level or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Schools usually run it as an option set with thin teaching time, so the support burden lands at home. A short block on calculus notation is better value than a weekly slot.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-r.regionsTitle: Where Al Reef sits in the Abu Dhabi tutoring market
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-r.regionsIntro: Al Reef is far enough from the island that proximity stops being a sensible way to choose. The communities below are the ones whose rates and availability set the price an Al Reef household is quoted.

regions.name: Al Reef Villas and Downtown
regions.note: Lower housing cost than the island, which is exactly why households here notice tutoring cost. Evening sessions start realistically at 17:00 or later once buses have returned, and that is the slot every other community wants too.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The nearest real concentration of tutors and tuition centres. A centre class here adds a second car journey to the week, which is a cost even when the per-hour figure is the lowest on offer.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Quoted higher in-home rates than Al Reef for the same tutors, which tells a household how much of a local quote is about driving distance rather than about teaching quality.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense towers where a visiting tutor can fit three sessions into an evening. The per-session economics there are better than anything available in a villa community, and rates reflect it.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: The top of the emirate's school and tutoring market, and a useful benchmark. A Saadiyat-level quote offered to an Al Reef household is a statement about mileage, not about specialism.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A deep pool of resident teachers across several curricula, and the closest thing to local supply. Cover thins quickly for Diploma Higher Level sciences and Computer Science.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Competes directly for the 17:00 to 19:00 window. A tutor with a Yas booking will offer Al Reef a later slot or a higher rate, and both are forms of the same travel cost.

regions.name: Al Bateen and the Corniche
regions.note: Island districts with long-established schools and short walking distances between them. Tutors based there rarely accept an Al Reef weekday run at any price, which is the practical ceiling on local matching.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reef and the airport corridor
schoolClusters.note: Closest to home, and the schools that set the end-of-day time for most children in this community. Session planning starts from the bus timetable rather than from the tutor's calendar.
schools: GEMS Cambridge International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and Al Raha
schoolClusters.note: Where most Al Reef secondary students actually sit their examinations, across both Cambridge and Pearson entries and both IB programmes. A household with two children here can easily need two boards covered.

schoolClusters.city: The island and the bridges
schoolClusters.note: Schools students we support travel to from the mainland. Also the benchmark for premium tutoring rates in the emirate, which is why their fee and rate levels appear in this page's comparisons.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-r.modesIntro: Three purchasing shapes exist, and they differ mostly in how much of the month they commit. The right one depends on whether the problem is a known gap or an unknown one.

modes.title: Pay-per-session, no retainer
modes.description: Sessions booked and paid for individually, with no annual commitment and no minimum block. This is the shape to start in, because it costs nothing to stop. A household that is unsure whether tutoring is the answer should never begin with a term-long package, however much the per-hour figure improves.
bullets: No registration fee and no minimum block to begin
Cancellation terms stated in writing before the first session
Stop after one session with nothing further owed
Rate does not change if you later move to a weekly slot

modes.title: A named block against a named problem
modes.description: Six to ten sessions aimed at a specific component - the Chemistry internal assessment, 0580 non-calculator accuracy, the Individual Oral - with a defined end. Costs a fraction of a year-long arrangement and is the correct purchase whenever the problem can be named precisely.
bullets: Scope agreed before the first session, in writing
Ends when the component is addressed, not when a term ends
Sized from a marked script or a returned criterion sheet
Extendable, but not automatically renewed

modes.title: Two children, two boards, one schedule
modes.description: The common Al Reef case: a Year 11 on Cambridge entries and a Diploma student on IB, needing different specialists in the same week. Scheduled together so the evenings work, with the heavier subject placed earlier and sibling slots arranged back to back where it helps.
bullets: Separate specialists per board, one coordinated timetable
Billed per session per child, never bundled into an opaque family rate
Shared skills - graph work, command terms - taught once
Shifts to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan

modes.title: Exam-season intensives
modes.description: Concentrated work in the weeks before a series, or in the gap between results and a resit entry. Priced the same per hour but compressed, so the monthly figure rises while the total falls. Built backwards from the entry deadline rather than forwards from the enquiry.

sections.heading: What proximity is actually worth from Al Reef
paragraphs: The phrase near me assumes that distance is the constraint worth optimising. For tutoring delivered to a community thirty kilometres from the island, it is close to the least useful constraint available, and the table below prices it.

Start with what proximity gives you. A tutor who can reach the house can sit at the table with a child who will not engage on a screen, can take a book out of a bag, and can be physically present in a way a younger student sometimes needs. That is real and for some children it decides the outcome. It is the honest case for an in-home visit and it is why the service exists in this market at AED 180 to 500 an hour.

Now price what it costs. Thirty to forty minutes of driving each way is inside that rate whether or not it is itemised. The pool of tutors willing to make the run on a weekday evening is small, and the subset of that pool who teach Diploma Higher Level Chemistry, Computer Science or Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 is smaller again. A household optimising for proximity is choosing a specialist from a shortlist of people whose main qualification is a tolerance for the Sweihan road at six in the evening.

There is a scheduling cost too. A tutor with a Yas Island or Al Raha booking earlier in the evening will offer Al Reef the late slot, which for a Year 11 means the session lands after the point at which anything is retained. Removing the drive moves the session earlier, and an earlier session on a school night is worth more than a better tutor at nine o'clock. That is the trade, stated plainly, and a household can reasonably decide either way once it is stated.

sections.heading: The monthly figure, cheapest first
paragraphs: Households budget monthly, so this is the band set a household should be given. Read it from the bottom up, because the useful question is how little will do rather than how much is available.

At the bottom, a weekly one-hour session with a budget online provider or a university-student tutor is estimated at AED 240 to 600 a month. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, which is where those monthly figures come from. For a Year 9 who needs company while doing homework, this band is honestly adequate and nobody should talk a household out of it.

In the middle, a qualified subject teacher online on the same weekly cadence is estimated at AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. This is the band that suits most Year 10 and 11 work and most Standard Level Diploma subjects. Above it, specialist exam-year support is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 a month and upward, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270 an hour and BartyED around AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. Online package pricing around AED 799 a month for eight sessions appears repeatedly in this market; in-home packages of four two-hour visits are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799.

The practical rule that follows is to buy the lowest band that can do the job and to escalate only where scarcity forces it. One Higher Level science at the specialist band plus two subjects at the qualified band is a coherent monthly budget. Four subjects at the specialist band is a household paying for insurance it will not use. All of these figures are market observations with their sources named; none is an IB Gram price list, and the first session is a free trial precisely so that the right band can be identified before money moves.

sections.heading: Covering two boards in one household without paying twice
paragraphs: The Al Reef case that recurs is two children, two schools, two boards. One sits Cambridge entries in Year 11; the other is in Diploma Year 1 with Higher Level sciences and an Extended Essay to start. Treated as one problem this gets expensive fast, and the mistake is almost always the same: buying breadth where depth was needed.

Separate the two children's needs by type rather than by subject. The Year 11 problem is examination technique against a known paper structure, diagnosable from a marked mock and fixable in a defined number of hours. The Diploma problem is a two-year timetable with coursework deadlines inside it, where the risk is not a weak topic but a missed internal deadline. Those need different purchases: a block for one, light supervision over months for the other.

Then decide where a single tutor can genuinely serve both. Shared skills exist and are worth paying for once - graph interpretation, standard form and significant figures, the command-term vocabulary that runs from IGCSE through to Diploma papers, writing enough method to earn marks when an answer is wrong. What does not transfer is specification knowledge. A tutor who has taught 0620 Chemistry is not thereby a Diploma Higher Level Chemistry tutor, and a provider who implies otherwise without naming codes and levels is selling convenience as expertise.

The budget version of this is simple arithmetic. Two children at the qualified band, one session each per week, lands around AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month. Adding one Higher Level specialist for the Diploma child takes the top of that range higher. Adding a standing slot for every subject in both households' timetables produces a figure nobody intended and no better outcome. Bill per session per child, see the lines separately, and cut the ones that are not producing a change in marked work.
bullets: Diagnose by problem type - technique, content, or deadline - before choosing a tutor
Pay once for shared skills; never assume specification knowledge transfers between boards
Insist on per-session, per-child billing so the useless lines are visible
Light supervision across months beats a weekly slot for Diploma coursework

sections.heading: Availability, and what you should be told when there is none
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas telephone number and let a parent discover it later. That is the gap this section fills, because an honest answer about availability is worth more to a household than an optimistic one.

Cover is not uniform. Mathematics and the IGCSE sciences are deep, and a suitable tutor with an evening slot is usually available quickly. Diploma Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are thinner. Computer Science at Diploma level, Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, Language B at Higher Level and the less common Group 6 subjects are thin everywhere in the Gulf, not only in Abu Dhabi. Arabic and Islamic Education cover exists but is in demand because the subjects are mandatory in private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

What should happen when the match does not exist is that you are told, told when it is expected, and offered the nearest sensible alternative with its limits stated. What should not happen is a slot filled by whoever was free. A household that is given an honest no in week one and a specialist in week three is better served than one given a generalist in week one and a wasted month.

Two further questions get a household a straight answer about any provider. First, where is the tutor physically, and in which time zone will the sessions actually be scheduled. Second, does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A provider who cannot discuss it is telling you something about how carefully they recruit.

sections.heading: Tutoring inside the whole education budget
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest education line in an Al Reef household, and reading it against the others changes how it gets decided. Dubai's private school sector, the best-documented in the country, enrolled 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, teaching 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum schools at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Abu Dhabi's sector is supervised separately, by ADEK, which handles licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes.

Fee movement matters to this calculation. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure rather than an Abu Dhabi one, but it sets the context every family in the country reads fee letters against. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after enrolment rose 6 per cent in 2025-26.

Against a school fee, a tutoring line of AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one subject is a real commitment but a comprehensible one. Against two Higher Level specialists plus two Year 11 subjects, the same household can find itself spending a meaningful fraction of a term's fees on support that was never diagnosed. The discipline is to attach every line to a named problem and a marked piece of evidence, and to remove the line when the evidence changes.

Two costs that households forget belong here too. Private-candidate examination entry carries a fee set by the centre rather than by the board, and it applies whenever a school will not enter a resit. And the mandatory UAE subjects sit outside the international curriculum budget entirely until a report arrives: Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education for Arab students.

sections.heading: The permit question, and why the cheapest tutor can be expensive
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, to government and private-sector employees, to unemployed individuals, to university students and to school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to a household, and any page quoting one should be treated with suspicion. The position to hold is that the permit is required rather than optional, and that a provider who treats it as paperwork is a provider who has not checked.

Abu Dhabi adds a specific restriction a household should know. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable bar. So the arrangement that feels most convenient - the child's own subject teacher, privately, for cash - is the one to decline. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before treating that summary as final.

A business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no permit of that kind, claims no accreditation from any regulator or examination board, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. It is an online matching platform. Saying so is the point: a household that knows exactly what it is buying can price it properly.
bullets: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge and valid for two years
No fine amount for unpermitted tutoring is published, so no figure should be quoted to you
Abu Dhabi school staff are reported as barred from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students
IB Gram claims no regulator or board accreditation and occupies no UAE premises

sections.heading: What nobody should be charging an Al Reef household for
paragraphs: A quote becomes comparable only once the extras are visible. Five lines recur in this market and all five are negotiable or avoidable, which is why they are worth naming before the first session rather than after the second invoice.

Registration and assessment fees come first. A diagnostic session that establishes what a student needs is work the provider does in its own interest, and in a market with free trials it should not carry a charge. Second, materials. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the examination boards; they should be cited and linked, not reproduced and sold. A provider offering a pack of papers for a fee is selling something that is not theirs to sell.

Third, cancellation terms that charge in full for a lesson missed because a child was unwell. A notice window is reasonable; an unconditional charge is not, and it should be read before anything is signed. Fourth, minimum blocks. A twelve-session minimum sold before a single lesson has happened transfers all the risk to the household. Fifth, the word free used with a condition attached that appears only later - a trial that requires card details, or a discount tied to a commitment that is not stated on the same screen.

Two claims belong in the same bin. Any guarantee of a grade, a score or a points total should end the conversation, because no tutor can make one and a provider who does is describing their sales process rather than your child's prospects. And any review score shown without a countable, attributable set of reviews behind it is decoration. Competitor pages in this market have shown two different ratings and review counts on the same page, and one shows a rating drawn from a handful of reviews beside a student-count claim far larger than that.
bullets: Ask in writing: registration fee, assessment fee, minimum block, cancellation window, materials charge
Board materials should be linked and cited, never sold as a pack
A guarantee of a grade or a points total is a reason to leave, not a reassurance
Any rating shown must come with a countable, attributable set of reviews

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects and where they land in the budget
paragraphs: Every household covering IB or IGCSE in the UAE is also covering a second curriculum it did not choose, and it usually appears in the budget late. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is the rule behind each emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

The requirements are specific. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Classes must be organised separately for Arab and non-Arab students for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Two further details affect what tutoring can honestly offer here. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met and advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. A tutor therefore works within prescribed material rather than bringing a parallel syllabus, and any provider promising their own improved Arabic programme has not read the rules.

The budget consequence for an Al Reef household is to treat these subjects as a standing small line rather than an emergency. A short block before each reporting cycle, inside the prescribed material, costs a fraction of the panic purchase that follows a weak report in the final year. It also matters later: Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five subjects required for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, so the reason to support them is the school report and the child's own progress, not the equivalency file.

process.title: Say which board, which level, which component
process.description: The first message that helps contains board, level and the specific component in trouble: Cambridge 0620 Paper 4, Diploma Higher Level Physics internal assessment, Analysis and Approaches Paper 3. That narrows the specialist search immediately and prevents the generic weekly slot that costs a household the most.

process.title: Take the free trial before anything is paid
process.description: One trial session per student, booked without card details. It is spent on diagnosis: working problems while the student explains the reasoning aloud, which separates fluency gaps from content gaps. You leave it knowing which band of tutor the problem actually needs.

process.title: Get the full quote in writing
process.description: Hourly rate, whether the quoted figure includes any applicable tax, registration or assessment fees, minimum block, cancellation window, materials charges, and what happens if the match fails. A provider who will not put that in a message is a provider to leave at this step rather than the next one.

process.title: Buy the smallest thing that can work
process.description: A named block against a named component, at the lowest band that can do the job, billed per session. Escalate to a specialist only where scarcity forces it. Households almost never regret starting small; they regularly regret a term-long package bought in the first week.

process.title: Review against marked work, then cut or continue
process.description: After the block, compare marked work from before and after and decide line by line. Anything not producing a change in marked evidence gets removed. That is the only progress report worth paying attention to, and it is the step that keeps the monthly figure honest.

whyPoints.title: The numbers are on the page
whyPoints.description: Monthly and hourly AED bands are published here with each source named, which almost nothing ranking for this search does. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars - a currency no Abu Dhabi household transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed first
whyPoints.description: Where no suitable specialist has a slot that works from Al Reef, that is stated along with the expected wait. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE enquiries to overseas numbers without saying where delivery happens.

whyPoints.title: Per session, per child, no retainer
whyPoints.description: Billing stays itemised so a household can see which lines are producing a change in marked work and remove the ones that are not. Nothing requires an annual commitment, and the rate does not improve as a reward for signing one.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run online, the tutor is chosen from everyone teaching that specification rather than from the few willing to drive out past the airport. For scarce components - Higher Level Chemistry, Computer Science, Paper 3 - that is the difference between a specialist and a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is printed
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work and produce none of it. At least one operator in this market sells completed internal assessments outright, so the boundary is worth stating rather than assuming, for the student's sake more than ours.

whyPoints.title: No claimed accreditation, no UAE premises
whyPoints.description: IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and occupies no office or centre in the UAE. Knowing precisely what a provider is lets a household price it correctly.

faqs.question: What does searching for a tutor near me actually get an Al Reef household?
faqs.answer: It gets you the subset of tutors willing to drive thirty to forty minutes each way on a weekday evening. For deep subjects like IGCSE maths that subset is adequate. For Diploma Higher Level Chemistry, Computer Science or Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 it is very small, and the people in it are selected partly for their tolerance of the drive. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour carry that travel inside them. If your child will work on a screen, dropping the proximity requirement widens the choice enormously and lowers the rate.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use one tutor for an IB child and an IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Only for the skills that genuinely transfer - graph interpretation, significant figures, command-term discipline, writing enough method to earn marks. Specification knowledge does not transfer. Someone who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry is not thereby a Diploma Higher Level Chemistry tutor, and a provider who suggests otherwise without naming codes and levels is selling convenience. Expect two specialists and one coordinated timetable, billed per session per child. That is usually cheaper in the end than one tutor covering both adequately and neither well.

faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly tutoring budget for a household in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Market estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 with a qualified subject teacher online, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A sensible shape for two children is one qualified-band slot each, plus one specialist component where scarcity forces it. Those are market figures with sources named, not an IB Gram price list. Start with the free trial, identify the band the problem needs, and buy that rather than the band that sounds reassuring.

faqs.question: Do IB and IGCSE tutoring cost different amounts in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the gap is driven by scarcity rather than by prestige. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, which reflects how many people can teach each. IGCSE cover is deep across maths and the sciences, so rates sit in the qualified band. Diploma Higher Level sciences, Computer Science and the core components push into the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above. Within the Diploma, Standard Level subjects are cheaper to cover than Higher Level for the same reason.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to find a tutor for near Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Diploma Computer Science, Analysis and Approaches Paper 3, Higher Level Language B and the less common Group 6 subjects are thin across the whole Gulf rather than just locally. Diploma Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are thinner than their IGCSE equivalents. Arabic and Islamic Education cover exists but is in demand, because those subjects are mandatory in private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for. For these, insisting on a tutor within driving distance of Al Reef usually means accepting a generalist, which is the expensive outcome.

faqs.question: What should a provider tell me if no specialist tutor is available?
faqs.answer: The honest wait, before any money moves, and the nearest alternative with its limits stated plainly. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal where delivery actually happens behind an overseas telephone number. A household given a straight no in week one and a specialist in week three is better served than one given a generalist immediately and a wasted month. Ask where the tutor is physically located and which time zone sessions will be scheduled in.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi rise closer to the exam season?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than headline rates rising, and the effect on a household is the same. In the weeks before a series the evening slots that suit a child go first, and the tutors left are the ones with the most capacity rather than the most relevant experience. Scarce components feel this hardest: a Higher Level Chemistry specialist who was free in October may have nothing in March. Booking a named block early costs the same per hour and buys the slot, which is the part that actually becomes scarce.

faqs.question: Does a quoted hourly rate include tax?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing rather than verbally. A quote that does not state whether the figure is inclusive is not a complete quote, and the difference matters across a term. IB Gram does not publish an hourly rate on this page, so the question belongs to the consultation after the free trial. On how tuition fees are treated for tax purposes generally, the Federal Tax Authority is the only authority worth citing, and no tutoring page including this one should state the position as settled fact.

faqs.question: What hidden extras appear on tutoring invoices in this market?
faqs.answer: Five recur. Registration or assessment fees for a diagnostic that should be free. Materials charges for past papers and mark schemes that belong to the examination boards and should be linked rather than sold. Cancellation terms that charge in full for a lesson missed through illness. Minimum blocks sold before a single lesson has happened. And the word free attached to a condition that appears only later, such as card details for a trial. Ask about all five in writing before the first session and the quotes become comparable.

faqs.question: How long does matching a tutor from Al Reef usually take?
faqs.answer: For deep subjects - IGCSE mathematics, the IGCSE sciences, Standard Level Diploma subjects - a suitable tutor with a workable evening slot is normally available quickly, and you will often have a choice. For thin components the wait is real and you should be told its length rather than offered a substitute. Because delivery is online there is no search radius to satisfy, so the constraint is the tutor's calendar in Gulf Standard Time rather than their distance from the Sweihan road.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education need separate tutoring from the main curriculum?
faqs.answer: They are separate subjects with separately prescribed content, so yes. They are mandatory in private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and classes must be organised separately for Arab and non-Arab students, with combined classes prohibited because the expectations and the language of instruction differ. Content is tightly controlled: using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. A tutor therefore works inside the prescribed material. Anyone offering their own improved Arabic programme has not read the requirement.

faqs.question: Can we pay per session instead of committing to a monthly package?
faqs.answer: You should be able to, and it is the right way to start. Packages improve the effective hourly rate - around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions appears repeatedly in this market - but they transfer the risk to the household before anyone has established that the tutoring works. Begin per session with no minimum block, see a change in marked work, then move to a package if the arrangement is clearly worth continuing. A provider who only sells blocks before a first lesson is asking you to decide without evidence.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre class in Khalifa City cheaper than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and it is the lowest figure available in this market. The full cost is higher than it looks for an Al Reef household: a second car journey each week, a room moving at the median student's pace, and a tutor rostered by the centre rather than chosen for your child's specification. It works well for broad coverage before mocks. It works poorly for a named weakness, because most of the hour is spent watching other students' problems being solved rather than your child's.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: You should be able to change without penalty and without re-paying for the diagnostic work already done, and the terms for doing so should be in writing before the first session. Ask specifically what happens to any unused sessions in a block. Mismatches are normal and not always about competence - timing, pace and manner all matter to a teenager. What is not normal is a provider who treats a change as a renegotiation, which is one more reason to start per session rather than per term.

faqs.question: Should tutoring pause during the examination fortnight itself?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with one exception. During the papers themselves a student's time is better spent on the next paper's own revision than on a scheduled session, and the sensible plan pauses and resumes. The exception is a short, specific session between two papers in the same subject when a predictable weakness is about to be tested again. Agree the pause in advance so it does not become a cancellation charge, which is one of the five extras worth settling in writing before anything starts.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-r.closingHeading: Decide the band first, then the tutor
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-r.closingBody: The useful order for an Al Reef household is band, then component, then tutor. Work out from the monthly figures above which band the problem actually needs, name the component precisely, and only then ask who is available to teach it. That sequence keeps the budget attached to evidence and makes the quotes comparable, which is most of what goes wrong in this market. Book the free trial, bring the marked work and the board and level, and the first conversation will be about which band and which component rather than about how many hours to sell. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Two curricula, one search box
paragraphs: The phrase "IB IGCSE tutor near me" is what a parent types when they are not certain which of the two labels applies to their own child, or when they have one child on each. It is a reasonable search and it hides the most consequential comparison in UAE schooling: the IB Diploma and the British International GCSE route are assessed on different principles, lead to different sixth-form shapes, and meet the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements by different paths.

The distinction that matters for tutoring is where the grade comes from. The British track places almost everything in terminal written papers sat at the end of two years, with little or no coursework in most subjects. The IB Diploma distributes the grade: written papers plus one internally assessed component per subject, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Creativity, Activity, Service requirement on top. One route rewards examination technique concentrated into a few weeks. The other rewards sustained work against published criteria over two years.

That single difference changes what a tutor should be doing. For an International GCSE candidate, the highest-value tutoring is timed-paper discipline and mark-scheme literacy in the final terms. For a Diploma student, the highest-value tutoring is internal assessment coaching against published criteria, scheduled months before the school's own deadline. A tutor who treats both the same way is wrong for at least one of them, and the rate they charge tells you nothing about which.

Now the geography. Does the answer change between Al Reem Island, Saadiyat, Yas, Khalifa City or Al Raha? For the curricula, no. The IB subject guides and the Cambridge and Pearson specifications are identical documents everywhere, grade boundaries are set across the whole candidate entry, and ADEK regulates the entire emirate on the same terms. What changes between communities is the commute, the travel component of an in-home quote, and how many suitable tutors happen to live nearby.

Does it change between emirates? Slightly, and only on the regulatory side. Dubai answers to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection alone. None of that changes what your child sits.

So the honest answer to "near me" is that the useful comparisons are curricular and regulatory rather than local, and that is what this page sets out. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, which makes the proximity question a scheduling question and nothing more.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two years with three at higher level, each assessed by written papers plus one internal component, on top of the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The internal components have published criteria with stated mark allocations and months-long timelines, which makes them the most tractable and least prepared part of the course.

This page publishes no IB session or results date: the IB's own site blocks automated access, nothing has been confirmed at source, and a date a family plans around should come from the school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Named specifications sat as terminal written papers, with Core and Extended routes at Cambridge and Foundation and Higher tiers at Pearson. The codes matter: 0580, 0606, 0625, 0620, 0610 and 0455 at Cambridge; 4MA1, 4MB1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and 4EA1 at Pearson. Almost all marks are terminal, which makes timed-paper work non-negotiable in the final terms.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's own risk.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's pre-Diploma route, assessed against four criteria per subject with level descriptors rather than by terminal paper. Students arrive in DP1 fluent in criterion-based work and often inexperienced at sitting a timed paper, which is the mirror image of the International GCSE leaver's profile.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has both continuum schools and Diploma-only schools, so a DP1 class in this emirate typically mixes Middle Years Programme leavers with International GCSE leavers. The two groups need different first terms, and a tutor who treats them identically wastes half the hours on each.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation of the British track where a school does not run the Diploma. Narrower than the Diploma by design: three or four subjects studied in depth, with no compulsory core. The jump in reading load and mathematical fluency from Extended tier to AS is the steepest in the British route.

sections.heading: The IB Diploma and the British track, compared where it counts
paragraphs: A great deal is written about which of these routes is harder, and almost none of it helps a parent choose a tutor. The useful comparison is structural: where the marks sit, when they are earned, and what a student has to be able to do to collect them. On that basis the two routes are genuinely different products rather than two versions of the same thing.

The British track concentrates the grade into terminal written papers sat at the end of the course, with little or no coursework in most subjects. Everything therefore depends on examination performance within a few weeks, and the skills that matter are mark-scheme literacy, timing, and the ability to produce under conditions. A strong student can underperform here purely on technique, and a well-prepared average student can outperform their classwork.

The Diploma distributes the grade across papers and an internal component in every subject, then adds the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge on top as a separate points contribution. A student therefore accumulates their result across two years, and the components with published criteria and long timelines are the most controllable part of it. The failure mode is different too: Diploma students more often lose marks to criteria they never read than to examinations they could not sit.

For a family choosing, the practical question is not difficulty but fit. A student who performs well under pressure, prefers depth in fewer subjects and has clear subject preferences is well served by the British track and its AS and A Level continuation. A student who works steadily, writes well and benefits from breadth is well served by the Diploma. Neither answer is improved by living in one Abu Dhabi community rather than another.

sections.heading: The regulator map: Abu Dhabi beside the other emirates
paragraphs: Families comparing communities often end up comparing emirates, usually because a job or a lease is moving. The regulatory picture is worth knowing because it is the one genuine difference, and because ADEK is named by none of the competing tutoring pages we examined for this market, which is a strange gap on pages aimed at Abu Dhabi parents.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete map.

The remit is wider than inspection in some emirates. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sit with the emirate regulator rather than only with the school. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the baseline every emirate builds on.

What none of this changes is the examination. A Cambridge 0580 paper is the same paper in Sharjah as in Abu Dhabi, an IB subject guide is the same document in Fujairah as on Al Reem Island, and grade boundaries are set across the whole candidate entry. A family relocating within the UAE changes regulator, school and commute. They do not change curriculum content, which means they do not need to change tutor if the tutor was chosen for specification knowledge in the first place.

sections.heading: Equivalency compared by curriculum
paragraphs: If a UAE university application is a possibility, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements are the one place where the choice between curricula has an administrative consequence. The British-track rule is published and specific. The IB figure is not something we will publish, because we have not read it on the Ministry's own site, and an unsourced points threshold on a tutoring page is the sort of number a family plans around and should not have to.

On the British track, as reported in July 2026, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. The exclusion is the part families miss: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A student with Arabic, Islamic Education and three others has three towards the count rather than five.

On the American track the same source gives different gates: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not the published rule, and publishing the correct five-subject rule is a straightforward accuracy win over a page that outranks us.

Two cautions apply regardless of route. Equivalency and attestation are processes carried out by the Ministry and the relevant authority, not by a tutoring platform, and nothing described here is performed or guaranteed by IB Gram. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; anyone implying otherwise is selling urgency about a regulatory process. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry's own channel before building a subject list around it.

sections.heading: The transition map: where the gaps actually are
paragraphs: Families on Al Reem Island move campuses and routes more often than the brochures imply, and every move creates a specific, bounded gap. Nobody publishes a structured version of these gaps, which is odd, because they are predictable and short to close. One competitor has a single subheading on the International GCSE to Diploma step and nothing else.

International GCSE into the Diploma is the most common move in Abu Dhabi. The student arrives with terminal-paper experience and usually with sound content, and is short of two things: the criterion literacy the internal assessments require, and in mathematics the algebraic fluency that Analysis and Approaches at higher level assumes from the first month. Both are closable in a short block and both are cheaper to close in the summer before DP1 than in DP2.

Middle Years Programme into the Diploma is the mirror image. The student is fluent in criterion-based work and often has never sat a timed paper of any consequence. The gap is exam behaviour: timing, working under pressure, and writing method rather than performing it mentally. Again a short block, again best taken before the first Diploma term rather than after the first set of mock results.

Cambridge into Pearson or the reverse, mid-course, is the cheapest gap to close and the one most often left open. The content overlaps heavily; the question architecture does not. The fix is an immediate switch of the past-paper diet plus an audit of the handful of topics present in one specification and absent from the other. It takes a few sessions. Left undone, a student revises competently for a slightly different examination and nobody can explain the result.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor is rarely the right one
paragraphs: Having established that the curricula are identical everywhere and the regulators differ only administratively, the proximity question answers itself. A tutor selected for being near is selected on the one variable that has no bearing on whether they know your child's route, level, board, code or tier. On a dense island with growing but limited provision, the set of nearby adults who teach any particular specification every week is small.

Consider the narrow cases, which are where this bites. A Diploma student in Analysis and Approaches at higher level needing Paper 3 work. A Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics candidate. A student on Pearson 4MB1 rather than 4MA1. A Diploma student whose internal assessment is in a subject the local market barely covers. In each case the number of suitable tutors living within a short drive of Al Reem Island may be zero, and the number available over video is not.

The counter-argument is that a local tutor understands local schools. Sometimes true, and worth separating from the claim being made. Useful local knowledge is about campuses: which school enters which board, which offers 0606 as an extra, when a given school's internal deadlines fall. All of that is available by asking the school, requires no residency, and is not the same thing as knowing a specification.

IB Gram makes the separation structural rather than advisory. We do not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, so there is no version of our service in which proximity is a selection criterion. Published market bands, for context, put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 for in-home and Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and International GCSE from AED 150. Those are attributed market figures, not our prices.

sections.heading: Coverage and what happens when we cannot help
paragraphs: No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal the fact that delivery is not local at all. Ours is stated. For mainstream Diploma subjects at higher or standard level, and for mainstream International GCSE codes, a match at a common evening slot is usually available within a few days. For narrower combinations the answer is longer, and occasionally the answer is no.

The variables are the route, the level, the specification and the time. An International GCSE science code at 18:00 Gulf Standard Time is an easy match. A Diploma higher level subject at an early slot that only suits a student at a campus near the island is harder. Cambridge 0606 is the scarcest specialism in this market. Where we cannot staff a combination properly, we say so and give you the code or route written down so you can look elsewhere with precise information.

That is a deliberate policy rather than a courtesy. A tutor who does not know the route or the code costs a family the fee and a term of misdirected effort, and the second cost is much the larger. A disclosed waiting time is a better outcome than a fast placement with the wrong person, and it is the one piece of information this market systematically withholds.

Two checks are the same whoever you engage. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. And treat any claim of regulator approval as a numbered permit to be produced rather than an adjective. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do on assessed work, on either route
paragraphs: Both routes place some marks inside work the student must author, and both treat authorship as the student's responsibility. In the Diploma that means the internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition. On the British track it means any coursework or controlled assessment component where a school enters one. The boundary is identical and worth stating in writing.

A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, discuss topic ideas the student has proposed, teach techniques the student has chosen to use, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is substantial and it is where a bounded coaching block earns its cost, because most marks in these components are lost to criteria nobody read rather than to content nobody knew.

No tutor may write the work, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion, or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price. The risk in that transaction falls on the student, whose Diploma is what a malpractice finding costs. We state our position because in this market it is not universal and because a parent should be able to read it before paying anyone.

The same limit applies to materials on both routes. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. They belong to the boards, are published through the boards' own channels, and reach students through their school. The skill worth teaching is how to use those documents critically, which outlasts any file a student could be handed.

faqs.question: Is my child on the IB or the IGCSE route, and how do I tell?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, and ask for it in writing. The quick indicators are these: an International GCSE student in Year 10 or 11 is entered for named syllabus codes such as Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 and sits terminal written papers. An IB Diploma student in Year 12 or 13 takes six subjects at higher and standard level with an internal assessment in each, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. A Middle Years Programme student is assessed on four criteria per subject rather than by paper.

faqs.question: Which route is better for a family on Al Reem Island?
faqs.answer: Neither, and the choice should not be made on location. The structural difference is that the British track concentrates the grade in terminal papers while the Diploma distributes it across papers, internal assessments and a written core accumulated over two years. A student who performs well under pressure and prefers depth in fewer subjects suits the British route. One who works steadily, writes well and benefits from breadth suits the Diploma. The community you live in does not change that.

faqs.question: Does tutoring for the two routes actually differ?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and at the same point in the year they need opposite things. For an International GCSE candidate the highest-value work in the final terms is timed-paper discipline and mark-scheme literacy, because almost all the marks are terminal. For a Diploma student the highest-value work is internal assessment coaching against published criteria, scheduled months before the school's own deadline. A tutor who treats both identically is wrong for at least one, and the hourly rate tells you nothing about which.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school in Abu Dhabi, and does it differ in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain private schools sit under ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation in the emirate. Dubai's answer to KHDA, Sharjah's to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. The remit differs: in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. None of it changes the examination.

faqs.question: On the British track, how many IGCSE passes does UAE equivalency actually require?
faqs.answer: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, as reported in July 2026, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One page currently ranking in this market states six subjects, which is not the published rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process, so verify the current requirement through the Ministry's own channel before planning a subject list.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the IB points requirement for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Because we have not read it on the Ministry's own site, and a threshold a family plans a child's two years around should be checkable at source. The British-track numbers on this page are sourced to a July 2026 report and we publish them with that attribution. The IB figure is not, so it is absent. On a set of pages this large, an unsourced number is not one liability but thousands, and the correct response is silence plus a pointer to the authority.

faqs.question: What is the gap when a student moves from IGCSE into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Two things, both bounded. The first is criterion literacy: the Diploma's internal assessments are marked against published criteria with stated mark allocations, and a student who has only ever sat terminal papers has no habit of reading them. The second, in mathematics, is the algebraic fluency that Analysis and Approaches at higher level assumes from the first month. Both close in a short block, and both are much cheaper to close in the summer before DP1 than in the second Diploma year.

faqs.question: What is the gap when a student moves from MYP into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The mirror image: exam behaviour. A Middle Years Programme student is fluent in criterion-based work and has often never sat a timed paper of any consequence. The gap is timing, working under pressure, and the habit of writing method down rather than performing it mentally, which is what earns method marks. It is a short block and it belongs before the first Diploma term rather than after the first set of mock results makes it visible.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to Al Reem Island homes?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. On a comparison page this is the cleanest consequence of the argument: with no journey involved, the service, the arrangement and the rate are the same in Al Reem Island, Saadiyat, Yas, Khalifa City or another emirate entirely.

faqs.question: If we move to Dubai or Sharjah mid-course, does the tutoring change?
faqs.answer: Only if the school changes the curriculum or the board. The regulator changes, the fee rules change and the commute changes, but a Cambridge 0580 paper is the same paper in Sharjah as in Abu Dhabi and an IB subject guide is the same document everywhere. If the new campus enters a different board, that is a transition block of a few sessions: switch the past-paper diet immediately and audit the handful of topics present in one specification and absent from the other.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both an IB child and an IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: For mathematics at International GCSE and Diploma standard level there is a reasonable case, because the content adjoins. For most other combinations there is not. A Diploma higher level specialist teaching Extended International GCSE content is being paid a specialist rate for generalist work, and a generalist supporting a Diploma internal assessment will not know how the criteria are awarded. A better saving is to stagger the two children's intensive phases, which fall at different times anyway.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for our route and time?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give you the route or code written down so you can look elsewhere with precise information. Mainstream Diploma subjects and International GCSE codes at a common evening slot are usually matched within a few days. Narrow combinations take longer, and Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is the scarcest specialism in this market. A disclosed waiting time is a better outcome than a fast placement that costs you a term as well as a fee.

faqs.question: Is there any real advantage to a tutor who lives nearby?
faqs.answer: Not one that affects teaching. Useful local knowledge is about campuses: which school enters which board, which offers Additional Mathematics as an extra entry, when a given school's internal deadlines fall, and how long the afternoon run takes. All of that is available by asking the school and requires no residency. What proximity does not supply is specification knowledge, which is the only variable that reliably changes a grade, and on a dense island the nearby pool for a narrow specification can be empty.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with Diploma or IGCSE assessed work?
faqs.answer: On both routes, the same things. Teach the skills the task assesses, explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, discuss topic ideas the student has proposed, teach the techniques the student chose, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write the work, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments, and the risk in that transaction falls entirely on the student.

faqs.question: What should a first message to a tutoring platform contain?
faqs.answer: Six things, which together prevent almost every mismatch: which child, which route, which subject, the level or the board and syllabus code and tier, the campus the child attends, and the time they are realistically home. Add one marked paper or draft and the first session can open with teaching rather than with questions you have already answered. Platforms that do not ask for these before quoting are not matching on anything that determines the outcome.

intro.heading: The arithmetic, before the adjectives
paragraphs: Al Samha sits at the northern edge of Abu Dhabi, out past Al Bahia and Al Rahba, close enough to the emirate boundary that some households here look towards Dubai for schooling and some look back towards the city. It is a long way from the island school belt, and that single geographic fact drives the economics of tutoring for families here. Anybody travelling to a home in Al Samha is pricing in the travel, and the pool of people willing to make the journey at five in the afternoon is small.

So the search for somebody near me is, in practice, a search for a short list that barely exists. This page takes the opposite approach and starts from the money. What does this market actually charge, who publishes those figures, what does each price point buy, and where does a family's spending leak away without producing anything visible on a paper? Those four questions are answerable with real numbers, and almost nobody in this search result answers them at all.

Three of the six strongest competing pages for this cluster of queries publish no price whatsoever. Two quote United States dollars at families who transact in dirhams. One publishes an hourly rate in its page copy that contradicts the figure in its own structured data. That is the state of pricing transparency in this market, which is why this page attributes every figure to whoever published it and states the month it was read.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a household out here, that is the cost argument as well as the logistics argument. Nobody is driving an hour each way, so nobody is charging for it, and the tutor is selected from everyone who teaches your child's course rather than from the handful prepared to come this far north.

The rest of this page is arithmetic. A price ladder running cheapest first, with what each tier genuinely delivers and what it cannot. A two-year spend map for a household running both an IGCSE child and a Diploma child. The five specific places money leaks. The free support worth exhausting before anything is paid for. And the scarcity premium, which is real, and which deserves explaining rather than hiding.

One principle underneath all of it: the cheapest purchase that fixes the identified problem is the correct purchase. That sounds obvious and it is routinely violated, usually by a family buying a term of general support when the marked paper pointed at one topic and three sessions. Everything below is designed to make that mistake harder to make.

sections.heading: What "near me" costs a household in Al Samha
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor near me, searched from Al Samha, is a request with a hidden price tag. The northern suburbs sit a long way from the emirate's school belt, and anybody prepared to drive here for a weekday session is pricing that journey into the rate, explicitly or otherwise. The market numbers bear this out: in-home one-to-one visits including travel are advertised in this market from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350. Online qualified subject tutors publish from roughly AED 150 to 300.

The gap between those two bands is, in large part, the travel. It is worth asking what it buys. A person physically in the room, which some students genuinely respond to, particularly younger ones. And a narrower choice of tutor, because the only candidates are those within driving distance at the hour your child is free. For a Year 9 maths top-up that trade can be reasonable. For Diploma Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, it is a poor one, since the specialists are scarce across the whole Gulf and are not concentrated near the emirate boundary.

IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we offer only in India. So the travel premium does not arise here at all, and neither does the narrowing. A household in Al Samha chooses from everyone who teaches the relevant course, at whatever hour the commute actually permits, which this far north is often a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening.

There is a second cost nobody prices, which is the family's own time. A visiting tutor consumes the arrival, the settling and the departure out of an evening that already contains a long bus run, dinner and homework. Over a term of weekly sessions that is several hours of household time, and out here it is more than it would be closer in.

sections.heading: The price ladder, cheapest first
paragraphs: Most pricing discussions in this market start at the premium end and work down, which flatters the expensive option. Starting at the bottom is more useful, because it makes clear what the cheapest tier actually delivers and at what point paying more starts to buy something a family needs.

At the entry level, EdFlik advertises online sessions from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. This tier buys supervision, company and structure. For a disorganised student who works better with somebody present, that has genuine worth and it is not a trick. What it does not buy is a diagnosis against a mark scheme, because that requires somebody who has the scheme in front of them and knows what the examiner rewards.

The qualified tier is where specification knowledge begins. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Here you are paying for somebody who knows the course, can answer a content question properly and can set sensible practice. The specialist tier, from AED 200 to AED 450 and above with TutorChase at around AED 270, buys knowledge of the paper rather than the course: the mark scheme, the command terms, where the marks go, and what a mock paper actually means. Premium named or examiner-led provision has been advertised as high as AED 650.

The ladder below is the one to work down rather than up. Identify the problem from marked work, find the cheapest tier that can address it, and buy that. The commonest expensive error in this market is buying the specialist tier for a supervision problem — or, more often, buying the supervision tier for a mark-scheme problem and then buying it again for a second term.

sections.heading: Two years of spending, written out
paragraphs: Families almost never plan tutoring across two years, which is why the total comes as a surprise. Writing it out changes decisions, because it exposes how much of the spend typically lands in the most expensive and least effective months rather than in the cheap and effective ones.

The pattern in households running both systems is consistent. Very little is spent in Years 8 and 9 and in DP1, where support is cheap and compounds. A great deal is spent in the spring of Year 11 and the spring of DP2, where it is expensive and where what it can achieve is narrowest. Reversing that distribution does not increase the total; it moves it, and the same money buys more.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions provide a usable frame: AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Advertised monthly packages in this market have included AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.
