sections.heading: Five places the money leaks
paragraphs: Waste in this market is rarely fraud. It is almost always a mismatch between what was bought and what the problem required, and it repeats in five identifiable ways. Naming them is more useful than any amount of advice about choosing a good tutor.

The first is buying length instead of accuracy: a term of general weekly support bought because a report card was poor, when the marked paper pointed at one topic and three sessions. The second is buying the wrong board's practice, which happens whenever nobody confirmed the syllabus code, and which feels productive right up to results day. The third is spreading a small number of sessions across three subjects in the spring of DP2, which reliably produces no visible movement anywhere.

The fourth is paying for explanation when the student needs marking. A student who understands the content and loses method marks does not need more teaching; they need their own work marked against the scheme and three answers rewritten. Explanation is more pleasant for everyone and changes nothing. The fifth is continuing a block that is not working because stopping feels like giving up, which is the most expensive of the five and the easiest to prevent with a midpoint review that is genuinely allowed to end things.

Each of these has a cheap counter. Ask for the smallest option first. Confirm the code in writing. Triage rather than spread. Insist that work is marked, not discussed. And agree at the outset what evidence would justify stopping.

sections.heading: What to exhaust before paying anybody
paragraphs: A page that charges for tutoring ought to be honest about the free support that comes first, because a family who exhausts it sometimes discovers they do not need to buy anything. In the northern suburbs, where households are often managing long commutes and two or three children, that matters more than usual.

Start with the school. Ask for the marked script rather than the grade. Ask the subject teacher which three topics they would prioritise. Ask whether a departmental revision session or clinic exists, because many schools in this emirate run them and attendance is often poor simply because families do not know. Ask the examinations officer for the syllabus code, the tier and the study-leave date in writing. All of that is free and it is the material any competent tutor would want anyway.

Then use the boards' own published material. Cambridge, Pearson and the International Baccalaureate all publish specification documents and support material on their own sites, and the official timetable for your centre's zone is published too. We do not reproduce or supply any of it, because it belongs to the boards; we cite and link it. A provider offering a library of copied mark schemes is offering a copyright problem rather than a service.

Only then does paying make sense, and the purchase should be the smallest one that addresses what the free material revealed. If after all of that the answer is three sessions on circle theorems, that is a good outcome and it costs a fraction of a term.

sections.heading: The scarcity premium, explained rather than hidden
paragraphs: Some subjects cost more, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Diploma Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, and minority languages at either level are thinly staffed across the whole Gulf. A family asking for one of those at a specific hour is asking for an intersection that may have very few people in it, and the rate reflects that.

This is where concealment is common in this market. A provider takes the booking, places the nearest available person, and the family discovers in week three that the tutor is a subject generalist. The cost of that is not the fee; it is the term. In DP2 particularly, three wasted weeks cannot be recovered at any price, which makes a mismatched placement the single most expensive purchase available.

Our position is to disclose before the trial rather than after. Where no specialist is free at your preferred hour, you get three options stated plainly: a different time with the right person, which is usually the correct answer; a wait with an actual date attached; or a tutor based outside the UAE with their location and working hours disclosed in advance. Nobody is placed into a course they do not teach.

There is also a legitimate way to reduce the premium, which is flexibility on timing. A family in Al Samha willing to take a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening opens up a much larger pool, often at the lower end of the specialist band, and gets a student with more energy into the bargain. Out here that trade is almost always worth making.

sections.heading: Permits, guarantees and the claims to walk away from
paragraphs: Spending money on tutoring in this country involves a regulatory question most families do not know to ask. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any page quoting an amount has invented it.

A rate far below the market is sometimes a sign that this question has not been answered. It is reasonable to ask an independent tutor directly whether they hold the permit, and the fact that it costs nothing to obtain removes the usual excuse. Abu Dhabi adds a further rule: ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction.

Then there are the claims that should end a conversation. Any guarantee of a grade, a points total or a university place. Any claimed approval, accreditation or licence from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or an examination board. Any school presented as a partner or client. Any satisfaction statistic without the number, the date and the method behind it. Any star rating that is not backed by real, countable, attributable reviews. And any offer to write, complete or finish a piece of assessed coursework.

IB Gram makes none of those claims. We hold no regulator or board approval and say so. We publish no ratings. We do not describe any school as a partner. And we do not write assessed work: a tutor teaches the criteria, questions the reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote, which is the only defensible position under board rules and the only one that protects the student.

faqs.question: Why would an in-home tutor charge more to come out to Al Samha?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is part of what you are buying. Published in-home rates in this market run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts the common in-home band at AED 180 to 350. This far north the drive is long and the pool willing to make it at five in the afternoon is small, which pushes both the rate and the waiting time up. Online delivery removes both effects.

faqs.question: What is the smallest sensible amount to spend on a first attempt?
faqs.answer: Three sessions: one reading a marked paper and naming the error types, and two fixing the biggest one, ending with your child attempting that question type unaided. At published qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour that is a few hundred dirhams rather than a few thousand, and it produces a written diagnosis you keep whatever you decide next. Most families are never offered this and are quoted a term instead, which is worth noticing.

For a disorganised student who works better with somebody present that is real value and not a trick. For a student losing method marks on long questions it will not help, because diagnosing that needs somebody with the published mark scheme in front of them. Also worth asking whether they hold the MoHRE permit, since it costs nothing to obtain.

faqs.answer: Less than most families do, if the spending is placed well. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. The pattern that wastes money is spending almost nothing in Years 8 and 9 and in DP1, then a great deal in the spring of Year 11 and DP2. Moving the same total earlier buys considerably more.

faqs.question: Where do families in this corridor most often waste money?
faqs.answer: Five places, in order of frequency. Buying a term of general support when the marked paper pointed at one topic. Practising from the wrong board because nobody confirmed the syllabus code. Spreading a handful of sessions across three subjects in the spring of DP2. Paying for explanation when the student needed their own work marked against the scheme. And continuing a block that is not working because stopping feels like giving up. Each has a cheap counter, and the first is simply asking for the smallest option.

Out in the northern suburbs that is also the cheaper arrangement, because nobody is pricing in a long drive, and it widens the choice of tutor from those prepared to travel this far to everyone who teaches your child's course.

faqs.question: Why are Diploma Higher Level subjects more expensive than IGCSE ones?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty of delivery. Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, and minority languages are thinly staffed across the whole Gulf, so a request for one at a specific hour may have very few people in it. The premium reflects that scarcity. The risk to watch is a provider concealing it by placing a near-match: the fee is recoverable and the term is not, which makes a mismatched placement in DP2 the most expensive thing a family can buy.

faqs.question: Can we lower the rate by being flexible about timing?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and for a household this far north it is the trade worth making. Insisting on a weekday evening slot narrows the pool to whoever is free at the one hour everybody wants. Accepting a weekend morning opens it considerably, frequently at the lower end of the specialist band, and gets a student with energy rather than one who has just finished a forty-minute bus run. Ask what is available across the whole week before fixing a time.

faqs.question: What free help should we use before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of which any good tutor would want anyway. The marked script rather than the grade sheet. The subject teacher's view of the three topics they would prioritise. Any departmental revision clinic the school runs, which in this emirate is often under-attended simply because families do not know it exists. And the syllabus code, tier and study-leave date in writing from the examinations officer. Then use the boards' own published material on their own sites, which we link rather than copy.

faqs.question: Is a prepaid package better value than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Only where the diagnosis genuinely supports a block of that length, and only where you can stop. A package bought before anybody has read marked work is a commitment made without information, and the discount rarely compensates for being locked into the wrong plan. The question to ask about any package is what happens at the midpoint if the evidence says stop. If the answer is nothing, the discount is being paid for with your optionality.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a student in Al Samha need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so a page quoting a figure is not citing anything.

faqs.question: What claims should make us walk away from a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Any guarantee of a grade, points total or university place. Any claimed approval, accreditation or licence from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or an examination board. Any school described as a partner or client. Any satisfaction figure or star rating without the number, date and method behind it. And any offer to write, finish or complete a piece of assessed coursework, which is academic malpractice and puts the student at risk rather than the provider.

faqs.question: What evidence should justify stopping a block rather than extending it?
faqs.answer: Agree this before the first session. A reasonable standard is a second timed paper at the midpoint, marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic, plus your child being able to name their own weakest area without prompting. If neither has moved after four weeks, something is wrong with the plan or the match and continuing is paying for a hope. A provider who cannot describe a stopping condition is selling a subscription.

faqs.question: Does paying a higher rate produce a better grade?
faqs.answer: Not by itself, and anybody saying otherwise is selling. What a higher rate reliably buys is mark-scheme level knowledge and experience of the specific paper, which matters enormously for a technique problem and hardly at all for a motivation problem. The relationship that does hold is between accuracy of diagnosis and outcome. A cheap, correctly targeted three sessions beats an expensive term aimed at the wrong thing, which is why this page starts with the marked paper rather than the rate card.

intro.heading: Work backwards from the deadline, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Almost every tuition plan is built forwards. A family decides to start, books a weekly slot, and the arrangement runs until something interrupts it. Plans built that way collide with the calendar at predictable points: a coursework deadline nobody wrote down, a mock week that swallows a fortnight, Ramadan arriving with the existing session time intact, an entry deadline that has already passed when the conversation about tiering finally happens.

The alternative is to start from the dates and plan backwards. That requires three or four facts from the school, all of which are freely available if you ask: when the final examination entry is submitted, when the internal coursework and exploration deadlines fall, when the mock window sits, and when the syllabus is scheduled to finish being taught. With those four, a tuition plan writes itself and the surprises largely stop.

Al Shamkha is a mainland villa district on the south-eastern side of Abu Dhabi, around half an hour from the island on a clear afternoon run. The calendar matters more here than in the island communities for a mundane reason: an hour a day on the road is roughly five usable hours a week, so there is less slack to absorb a badly planned fortnight. A family with a long commute and a plan built backwards from the dates is in a better position than a family nearer the schools with a plan built forwards from a phone call.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Shamkha or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Where the calendar is the organising constraint, that matters practically — a video session can move to a different evening in mock week, run post-Iftar during Ramadan, or happen at all during a week when nobody in the household can drive anywhere.

Two factual notes that govern everything below. Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two available to UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered in India only, and a page telling a UAE parent otherwise is giving them a date to act on that is wrong for their country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. For the IB, the session UAE schools sit is the May one, and no specific Diploma examination or results date appears on this page because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one.

What follows is the calendar in usable form: an eight-week programme with weekly outputs, the year counted backwards, Ramadan and the revision clock, what a mock is actually for, which weeks of the year genuinely exist for sustained work, how the Diploma's deadline chain differs from the IGCSE run, and an honest account of what six weeks can and cannot do.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE

The calendar has one cliff edge and two hard administrative dates before it: the school's final entry submission, and the mock window that informs it. Everything else is teaching and revision.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong version.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Eighteen months of internally assessed work running alongside the taught courses, then a terminal examination session. The calendar is a chain rather than a cliff: exploration and investigation drafts, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge submissions, each with its own school deadline and word limit.

The session UAE schools sit is the May one; for the exact windows, deadlines and results dates, the Diploma coordinator is the only reliable source.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-s.subjectsIntro: Different subjects have different calendar pressure points, and knowing which ones load up when prevents a household planning as though all eight are identical.

subjects.name: Mathematics, IGCSE
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Steady through both years with no coursework pressure, which makes it the subject most amenable to a timed-paper intensive in the final weeks. The pressure point is the tiering decision, which sits at the entry deadline rather than at the examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Diploma
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: The exploration deadline is the calendar event, typically in DP1 or early DP2 depending on the school. Higher Level students also need Paper 3 practice, which is the component most often pushed into the final fortnight and least suited to it.

subjects.name: Sciences, IGCSE
subjects.description: Practical or alternative-to-practical components concentrate the pressure late, and the terminology load means revision must start earlier than in mathematics. Students who leave the sciences until the final six weeks run out of time rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Sciences, Diploma
subjects.description: The scientific investigation carries its own deadline chain with a three thousand word limit, and it is marked on the design of the investigation rather than on how neatly the results came out. Design decisions made late cannot be undone.

subjects.name: English, First Language and Language A
subjects.description: Diploma English carries the Individual Oral, a specific assessed task with its own window, and at Higher Level an essay. IGCSE English loads onto the examination series, which makes it a candidate for late, feedback-driven work on the student's own writing.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Diploma commentaries are tied to published articles and carry internal deadlines across the course. Leaving them late produces summaries of articles rather than applications of theory, which is the single most common mark loss in both subjects.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Twenty marks across the essay and the exhibition, with word limits of sixteen hundred and nine hundred and fifty respectively, and deadlines that sit in the middle of the busiest term. Routinely the last thing planned and the easiest to plan.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Thirty-four marks with critical thinking alone worth twelve, and a four thousand word ceiling beyond which nothing is marked. Its milestone chain — question, research, first draft, final — spans a year and is the clearest argument for backwards planning.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: These run alongside the international timetable throughout, which is the reason a student's real weekly load exceeds a count of their examined subjects. Content for them is tightly prescribed by the authorities.

subjects.name: Any subject being resat
subjects.description: The calendar here belongs to the centre rather than the board, because internal entry deadlines fall earlier than the board's. A resit decision made after results day is usually a race against an administrative date, not a teaching one.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can actually deliver
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the period most families buy, usually after a mock, and it is long enough to produce a measurable change if it is structured and nearly useless if it is not. The failing pattern is familiar: sit a paper, check the total, feel bad, sit another. Papers used that way measure a student repeatedly without changing them.

A structured eight weeks does three things in sequence. It diagnoses, using one full paper sat under conditions and marked strictly against the published scheme, with every lost mark categorised. It repairs, driven entirely by that categorisation rather than by working through the syllabus from the top. Then it rehearses, with full papers to the clock and a hard rule that no question is abandoned before the given working is attempted.

The table sets out a workable shape. The last column is the one that makes it honest: each week has a check that either passed or did not, which means the plan fails visibly and early rather than invisibly and late. A family in Al Shamkha with a long commute cannot afford to discover in week seven that weeks two through five did not land.

Two rules make or break it. Papers must be sat to time, because the fault most students discover under the clock is that they spent twelve minutes on a four-mark question and left eighteen marks unattempted. And papers must be marked against the published scheme rather than self-assessed, because students systematically award themselves credit for answers that would earn none and miss method marks they genuinely earned.

sections.heading: The academic year counted backwards
paragraphs: This is the table no competitor in this market publishes, and it is the most useful thing on the page. Read it from the bottom upwards. The examination is not the organising date; the entry deadline is, because that is the moment tier and subject decisions stop being changeable.

The pattern it reveals is that the administrative dates fall far earlier than families expect. A school's final entry is submitted months before the papers. Its internal coursework and exploration deadlines are spread across the preceding year. The mock window usually sits a full term before the series. By the time most families start looking for a tutor, two of those four dates have already passed.

The consequence is specific. A conversation about moving a student from Core to Extended, or from Higher Level to Standard, has to happen before the entry is submitted — and before that, early enough for the content the other class covered to be taught. A conversation about an exploration topic has to happen before the draft deadline, not after it. Neither is a teaching constraint. Both are calendar constraints, and both are routinely discovered too late.

For Pearson the published schedule illustrates how far ahead the machinery runs. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well in advance of each series, which is exactly why a tutoring page should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

sections.heading: Ramadan and the revision clock
paragraphs: Ramadan is part of the UAE academic calendar and most tuition providers handle it by ignoring it until the cancellations start. School days shorten, late-afternoon energy drops, and the hours in which concentrated work is possible move. A plan that leaves a four o'clock weekday slot in place through the month will lose most of those sessions and the family will conclude that the arrangement stopped working.

Two patterns work. The first is to move sessions to a post-Iftar time in the evening, agreed in advance as a matter of routine rather than negotiated in week two. For many households this is the single best study window of the whole year: quiet, unhurried and after the day's obligations. The second is to reduce the cadence for the month and maintain contact through short written work, then resume fully afterwards. Which suits a household depends on the family rather than on the student, and it is worth asking the question before the month rather than during it.

The timing interaction that matters for examination years is that Ramadan's position in the Gregorian year moves, so its relationship to a given series changes from one year to the next. In some years it sits well clear of the papers and in others it lands in the final revision run. That is a reason to check the calendar each year rather than assume last year's plan applies, and a reason the school's published calendar is the document to work from.

There is a wider point here about designing round the household rather than the syllabus. A tuition arrangement that has been fitted to a real week — including prayer times, Ramadan, sibling collections and an hour a day on the road from Al Shamkha — survives the year. One booked at a nominally convenient time is being rescheduled by week four and abandoned by week eight, which is a planning failure that gets attributed to the tutor.

sections.heading: Mock season: what a mock is for, and how to use the script
paragraphs: A mock is a diagnostic instrument that most families treat as a verdict. The grade on the front is the least informative part of it. The script underneath is the most valuable educational document a household will hold all year, and in the great majority of cases nobody reads it question by question.

Reading it properly takes about forty minutes and requires no subject knowledge. Go through every question where marks were lost and assign one of five categories: content never learned, method known but misapplied, notation or calculator error, command word misread, or ran out of time. Then count the categories. In most scripts three or four recurring faults account for the bulk of the loss, and typically at least two of them are technique rather than knowledge.

That count is the plan. A script showing eleven marks lost to misread command words and nine to early rounding does not need the syllabus re-taught; it needs two specific interventions and some marked practice. A script showing marks lost evenly across every topic needs something quite different, and probably more time than remains. Knowing which of those you have is the difference between a well-aimed eight weeks and an expensive guess.

One further use of mock season that families miss: it is the last reliable evidence before the entry deadline in many schools. If a tiering or level conversation is going to happen, the mock script is the document that supports it, and the window to have that conversation closes with the entry. A family that reads the script in the week it comes back is in a position to act; one that files it is not.

sections.heading: Which weeks of the year genuinely exist
paragraphs: A year looks like forty teaching weeks and behaves like considerably fewer. Breaks, mock fortnights, internal deadline weeks and the final run-in all consume time that a naive plan assumes is available for sustained new work. Writing down which weeks actually exist is a twenty-minute exercise that changes how a family spends several thousand dirhams.

The table gives the shape. The pattern worth noticing is that the genuinely productive stretches are the autumn term and the spring term's first half, plus the long summer break, and that the periods families instinctively target — the weeks immediately before a series — are the least suited to anything other than rehearsal. The summer in particular is the most under-used asset in the whole calendar, especially for a student crossing from IGCSE into DP1, because there is no competing coursework and nothing else to displace the work.

For an Al Shamkha household the commute compounds this. Five hours a week lost to travel is roughly a sixth of a secondary student's usable study time, which means the available weeks are not only fewer than they look but thinner. The honest planning response is to be more selective about what the tuition is for rather than to add sessions, since adding sessions to an already full week displaces the written practice that makes the sessions work.

The practical instruction is to get the school's published calendar in the first week of the year, mark the four dates from the backwards table on it, cross out the breaks and the mock fortnight, and look at what remains. That remaining set is the plan's real capacity. Almost every disappointed tuition arrangement we see was built on a calendar that had never been looked at.

sections.heading: The Diploma chain against the IGCSE run
paragraphs: A household running both systems is running two incompatible calendars, and the mistake is to treat them as one. The IGCSE student's two years are teaching and revision with a single cliff edge at the end and two administrative dates before it. The Diploma student's two years are a chain of internally assessed deadlines running continuously alongside the taught courses.

That produces a different tuition shape for each. The IGCSE child benefits from steadiness: a weekly slot, marked written practice, and a timed-paper intensive at the end. The Diploma child benefits from lumpiness: concentrated sessions at the exploration draft, the Extended Essay first draft, the Theory of Knowledge submissions, and the Paper 3 practice that nobody schedules. Running both children on a single steady pattern underserves the Diploma student at exactly the moments that carry marks.

The word limits are part of the calendar, because they are what makes a late draft unsalvageable. The Extended Essay stops at four thousand words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at sixteen hundred and the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty, and the sciences investigation at three thousand. Markers stop reading at the limit. A student compressing a finished argument into the limit in the final week is cutting the parts that carry the critical thinking marks, which at thirty-four marks for the Extended Essay means twelve of them.

The boundary applies throughout and we state it to students directly. A tutor teaches the criteria, discusses topic viability, reads the student's own draft, questions it and names the criterion a section is failing to address. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, or produce any part of an assessment. We decline that at any price, because work the student did not produce puts the whole entry at risk rather than one component.

sections.heading: Six weeks left: the honest version
paragraphs: A large share of the families who find this page have about six weeks and a bad mock. The useful thing we can offer is an honest account of what that period does, because the alternative — implying it can do everything — produces a disappointed family and a fair conclusion that tutoring does not work.

Six weeks reliably improves four things. Timing, through full papers sat to the clock with per-question timings recorded. Command-term discipline, which is a vocabulary problem solvable in two sessions. Rounding and accuracy habits, which are a single instruction consistently enforced. And question selection, including the rule that no question is abandoned before the given working is attempted. Together those routinely produce a double-digit mark swing on a paper where the content is broadly known.

Six weeks does not rebuild algebraic fluency, teach content that was never taught, or change a tier. Fluency is a volume problem requiring months; untaught content requires teaching time the week no longer contains; and tier is fixed at an entry deadline that has already passed. A provider who takes money for six weeks while implying otherwise is selling hope, and the specific harm is that the family stops looking for interventions that might actually help, such as a conversation with the school.

So the sequence we recommend with six weeks is: read the script and categorise every lost mark, pick the two or three technique faults that account for most of the loss, attack those with marked practice and timed papers, and ignore the rest. Narrow and well-aimed beats broad and reassuring. And where the script shows the problem is content rather than technique, we will say that the honest purchase is a plan for the next series rather than this one.

sections.heading: Dates we will not publish, and limits we will not cross
paragraphs: A calendar page carries a specific obligation: not to publish a date a parent might act on unless it can be stood behind. So two things are absent here deliberately. No IB examination or results date appears, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one and automated access to it is blocked, which means any site quoting you a Diploma results date is passing on something unverified. And no future-dated examination window appears for any board, because a page naming a specific year goes stale without anybody touching it.

What is stated is checkable. Cambridge runs June and November series, with the February and March series offered in India only, and allocates centres to six administrative zones each with its own timetable version. Pearson runs May/June and November, published provisional timetables ahead of each series, and the past dates cited on this page — the November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026, November 2025 results to students on 22 January 2026 — are backward-looking citations kept with their dates precisely because that is what makes them checkable.

On status: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform. It holds no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. It is not a registered examination centre, cannot enter a candidate for anything, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Any paid private tutor in the Emirates needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years.

And on promises: no tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university outcome, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism. We publish no star rating or satisfaction figure, because stating one honestly requires the sample size, the date and the method. Board material is referenced and linked rather than reproduced. What we commit to is a written diagnosis, marked written work, a stated review date, and a straight answer about what the time remaining can and cannot achieve.

process.title: Collect four dates from the school
process.description: When the final examination entry is submitted, when the internal coursework and exploration deadlines fall, when the mock window sits, and when the syllabus finishes being taught. Those four facts are freely available and they determine everything a tuition plan can usefully do.

process.title: Read the last script and categorise it
process.description: Forty minutes, no subject knowledge needed. Assign every lost mark to one of five categories: content never learned, method misapplied, notation or calculator error, command word misread, or ran out of time. The counts are the plan.

process.title: Free trial lesson against the real calendar
process.description: One live video lesson with a matched specialist who has read the script, scheduled at a time that survives a bad traffic day from Al Shamkha. You decide afterwards, no card is required, and nothing starts automatically if you do not continue.

process.title: Write the interruptions in from the start
process.description: Mock fortnight re-timed rather than cancelled, Ramadan sessions agreed post-Iftar in advance, holiday pauses covered by short written work, and extra sessions placed around each internal deadline rather than spread evenly across the year.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts at the entry deadline
whyPoints.description: Tier and level decisions stop being changeable when the school submits its entry, months before the papers. We build backwards from that date rather than forwards from the first phone call, which is why fewer surprises arrive.

whyPoints.title: Every week has an inspectable output
whyPoints.description: An eight-week programme with a named focus, a marked artefact and a check each week. A plan built this way fails visibly in week three rather than invisibly in week seven, which is the only kind of failure a family can act on.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan is planned, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Post-Iftar timing or a reduced cadence with written work, agreed before the month rather than negotiated after two cancellations. Its position relative to a series moves year to year, so we check the school's calendar rather than repeating last year's plan.

whyPoints.title: The mock script is treated as the main document
whyPoints.description: Not the grade on the front. Every lost mark categorised, the counts used to pick the two or three faults worth attacking, and the rest deliberately ignored. Narrow and well-aimed beats broad and reassuring in a short window.

whyPoints.title: An honest account of six weeks
whyPoints.description: Timing, command terms, rounding and question selection improve reliably. Fluency, untaught content and tier placement do not. We say which you are buying, because the alternative is a family that stops looking for help that might work.

whyPoints.title: Live video, which the calendar rewards
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in Al Shamkha or anywhere in the UAE because home visiting is an India-only service, and a video session can move to another evening in mock week rather than being lost.

faqs.question: Which four dates should an Al Shamkha family get from the school?
faqs.answer: When the final examination entry is submitted, when the internal coursework and exploration deadlines fall, when the mock window sits, and when the syllabus finishes being taught. All four are freely available if you ask, and together they determine what a tuition plan can usefully do. Most families start looking for a tutor after two of those dates have already passed, which is why conversations about tiering or level arrive too late to change anything.

faqs.question: Is an eight-week programme long enough to change a grade?
faqs.answer: If it is structured, often yes; if it is just eight papers, almost never. A workable shape is one diagnostic paper marked to the published scheme with every lost mark categorised, three weeks of repair driven entirely by that categorisation, a mid-point retest, then timing and endurance work, with the final week consolidating only. Each week should produce a marked artefact and a check that either passed or did not, so the plan fails visibly rather than late.

faqs.question: How should tuition be timed around Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Decide before the month, not during it. School days shorten and late-afternoon energy drops, so the two workable patterns are a post-Iftar evening session, which for many households is the best study window of the year, or a reduced cadence with short written work maintaining contact. What fails is leaving an existing four o'clock weekday slot in place and watching the cancellations accumulate. Ramadan's position relative to a series also moves year to year, so check the school calendar.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with a disappointing mock script?
faqs.answer: Read it question by question, which takes about forty minutes and needs no subject knowledge. Assign every lost mark to one of five categories: content never learned, method known but misapplied, notation or calculator error, command word misread, or ran out of time. Then count them. In most scripts three or four faults account for the bulk of the loss and at least two are technique rather than knowledge, which makes the next eight weeks a targeting problem rather than a guess.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the school year are genuinely usable for new work?
faqs.answer: The autumn term and the first half of the spring term, plus the long summer break, which is the most under-used asset in the calendar. Mock fortnights yield nothing for new teaching, winter breaks are short and often travelled through, and the final six weeks are for rehearsal only. For a household losing around five hours a week to the Al Shamkha commute, the available weeks are both fewer than they look and thinner than they look.

faqs.question: What can six weeks before the papers realistically fix?
faqs.answer: Four things reliably: timing, through full papers sat to the clock with per-question timings recorded; command-term discipline, which is a vocabulary problem solvable in two sessions; rounding and accuracy habits; and question selection, including never abandoning a question before attempting the given working. Together those often produce a double-digit swing. Six weeks does not rebuild fluency, teach untaught content or change a tier, and a provider implying otherwise is selling hope.

faqs.question: Why is the entry deadline more important than the exam date?
faqs.answer: Because it is the moment decisions stop being changeable. A school's final entry is submitted months before the papers, and the tier or level is fixed at that point. Before it, there is a second practical limit: moving a student up requires content the other class covered months earlier, so a change needs teaching time as well as an administrative form. Ask when entries close and how much of the higher-tier content has been taught, and work from the earlier of the two.

faqs.question: How does a Diploma calendar differ from an IGCSE one at home?
faqs.answer: One is a cliff, the other is a chain. The IGCSE student has two years of teaching and revision with a single terminal series and two administrative dates before it. The Diploma student has eighteen months of internally assessed work running alongside the courses, each piece with its own criteria, word limit and school deadline. So the IGCSE child benefits from a steady weekly pattern and the Diploma child from concentrated blocks at each deadline.

faqs.question: Do word limits really matter that much in Diploma assessments?
faqs.answer: They decide marks, because markers stop reading at the limit. The Extended Essay stops at four thousand words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at sixteen hundred, the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty, and the sciences investigation at three thousand. A student compressing a finished argument into the limit in the final week cuts the analytical passages, and for the Extended Essay the critical thinking criterion alone carries twelve of the thirty-four available marks.

faqs.question: When do Pearson timetables and results actually fall?
faqs.answer: On a schedule published well ahead of each series. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables for future series, which is precisely why any page should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

faqs.question: Can an Al Shamkha student sit the February series if they miss June?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and a page telling you otherwise is handing you a date that is wrong for your country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we plan the summer before DP1?
faqs.answer: From the spring, because specialist availability in that window is the widest of the year and it fills once results arrive. For a student crossing from IGCSE into the Diploma, those weeks are the most productive tuition period in the whole programme: no competing coursework, nothing to displace the work, and content absorbed rather than crammed alongside six new courses, Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay. For a DP1 student it is when an exploration can be thought about properly.

faqs.question: Will sessions be cancelled during our mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Re-timed rather than cancelled, and written into the plan from the start. A mock fortnight produces nothing for new teaching because the student is sitting papers, but the week immediately afterwards is the most valuable in the term, since the scripts are the freshest diagnostic evidence available. So we move sessions out of the fortnight and put extra time into the week after it, with the script reading done together.

faqs.question: What dates will you not give us, and why not?
faqs.answer: No IB examination or results date, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one and any site quoting you one without citing it is passing on something unverified. The session UAE schools sit is the May one; ask your Diploma coordinator for the windows. We also avoid naming a specific future year for any series, because a page dated to one year goes stale without anybody touching it. Past dates we cite keep their dates, which is what makes them checkable.

intro.heading: The calendar is the real problem, not the distance
paragraphs: A search for a tutor near Al Wahda is almost never about geography. It is about timing. Term one has three weeks left and a Diploma internal assessment draft is due. The January mock window is close enough to matter and the predicted grade comes out of it. A Year 11 student has entries made for the June series and has not yet completed a whole past paper. Each of those is a scheduling problem with a deadline attached, and a tutor five minutes away who starts next month solves none of them.

Abu Dhabi private schools run three terms, with the long break in summer, a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in the second half of the year. Inside that, each term has a job. Term one covers new content and ends with the first serious internal assessment evidence. Term two carries the mock window, the predicted grades and the bulk of coursework deadlines. Term three is examinations, and by then the room for improvement has narrowed to technique rather than content. A family who understands which term they are standing in makes better decisions about how much tutoring to buy.

The Diploma and the IGCSE calendars overlap but are not the same. A Diploma student is managing internal deadlines the school sets for the Exploration, the Extended Essay and subject internal assessments, all of which sit well before the IB's own submission dates. An IGCSE student is managing a single terminal series with entries made by the school as the examination centre. A household with one of each is managing both, which is a real administrative load and the reason a shared plan on one page is worth more than two separate conversations.

On the exam series themselves, there is one fact that a surprising amount of online advice gets wrong for this country. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. A student in Al Wahda sits June, with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Any revision timetable built on a February window belongs to a different country's candidates.

IB Gram delivers this as live one-to-one online tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. When the constraint is the calendar, that is the useful arrangement rather than the compromise: a session happens at the minute it was booked, it does not depend on anyone's drive across the island at five in the afternoon, and it can be scheduled for the week it is needed rather than the week a travelling tutor has a gap.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-w.subjectsIntro: Different subjects bite at different points in the year. The notes below are organised by when the deadline lands rather than by faculty, because that is the order a family actually meets them.

subjects.name: Mathematics, DP and IGCSE
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL; Core, Extended, Foundation, Higher
subjects.description: Content-heavy and cumulative, so gaps compound across terms. The Diploma Exploration deadline lands in term one or two; the IGCSE series is terminal. Most recoverable marks sit in technique: written setups, units, bounds, and calculator discipline rather than new understanding.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: DP SL and HL; Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: The internal assessment and practical skills carry weight through the year, and the DP investigation deadline is usually a term-one or term-two matter. Marks are lost in uncertainty handling, graph treatment and the gap between a calculation and an explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: DP SL and HL; Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and energetics generate the most late-term panic, and the DP internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to produce usable data. Students who choose an investigation in week two of a term finish; those who choose in week eight usually do not.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: DP SL and HL; Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: Volume of content makes this a long-run subject rather than a crammable one. Command terms are the hidden examiner: describe, explain, outline and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and students lose marks by writing the wrong shape well.

subjects.name: English, language and literature
subjects.levels: DP SL and HL; Cambridge 0500 and 0990
subjects.description: Oral components and coursework sit at fixed points in the Diploma year and cannot be moved. For IGCSE the timed response is the examined skill, and the most common waste of tutoring is reading more texts instead of practising timed analysis of the ones already read.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: DP SL and HL; Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
subjects.description: Diploma Economics requires internal assessment commentaries built on current news articles, which means source selection is itself a deadline. Diagrams carry marks and are frequently drawn without labels, losing marks the student had earned.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in private schools regardless of the international curriculum, with separate class organisation for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. These subjects sit on the school timetable all year and are regularly the ones a family forgets to plan around.

subjects.name: Diploma internal assessments across subjects
subjects.description: Each subject's internal assessment has a school draft deadline that arrives before the IB's submission date. Taken together they are the single largest predictable pressure point in the Diploma year, and they cluster rather than spread out.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core carries up to three points on the 45-point total and runs on interim deadlines set by the school. Support here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts; no part of either may be written for a student, and the supervisor signs to that effect.

subjects.name: Mock examinations and predicted grades
subjects.description: The January mock window produces the predicted grade universities see. Students treat it as practice; admissions treat it as evidence. Preparing specifically for a school's own mock papers is a legitimate, bounded piece of tutoring with an obvious finish line.

subjects.name: Past-paper technique
subjects.description: The skill of reading a mark scheme and seeing where method marks were available. It is learnt by marking one's own paper, not by being told the answer, and it is reliably worth a grade band to a student who has never been shown how.

subjects.description: Shorter school hours and post-Iftar scheduling make this a window for review, past-paper marking and light consolidation rather than new content. A plan that ignores it collapses in practice, and a plan built around it does not.

sections.heading: What an Al Wahda family is asking for when they search near me mid-term
paragraphs: The direct answer: through IB Gram, an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Wahda means a subject specialist matched to your child's Diploma course or IGCSE syllabus code, teaching one-to-one over live video at an Abu Dhabi-friendly hour, starting this week rather than next month, with a free trial lesson first. There is no travel, no package bought in advance, and no tutor arriving at a UAE address, because in-home visits are a service we run only in India.

What makes a mid-term search different from a start-of-year one is that the scope is already fixed. In September a family can plan a year. In February they are standing between a mock result and a deadline, and the only useful question is what can be changed in the time left. A tutor who answers that question with a two-year plan has not listened. A tutor who answers it by asking which date is closest has.

The honest range of outcomes in a short window is worth setting out. Eight weeks of weekly sessions can reliably change examination technique, clear the three or four recurring topic errors an error log identifies, and get an internal assessment finished to a standard the criteria reward. It cannot reliably move a student who has understood little of two years of content, and anyone promising that is selling hope by the hour.

The geography question deserves a straight answer too. Al Wahda is central, which helps with everything except specialism. The adult who has taught Diploma Chemistry Higher Level, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, or Diploma Economics internal assessment commentaries, may not be within a twenty-minute drive of Hazza Bin Zayed Street, and in an exam term you need that person this week rather than a nearer person next month.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi school year, term by term, and what each term is actually for
paragraphs: Private schools here run three terms with a long summer break, a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break later in the year. Each term has a distinct function, and tutoring that ignores the function wastes money. Term one teaches new content and produces the first real assessment evidence. Term two carries mocks, predicted grades and most coursework deadlines. Term three is examinations and the window for technique only.

Term one is the cheapest term to buy tutoring in and the one families most often skip. A gap identified in October costs a handful of sessions. The same gap discovered in a January mock costs considerably more, because by then it sits underneath newer content that also needs attention. For a DP1 student coming from the Middle Years Programme, term one is where the timed-writing habit is built, and it cannot be built in term three.

Term two is where the calendar bites hardest. Internal assessment drafts cluster, the mock window arrives, and predicted grades are produced from internal evidence rather than from potential. Students routinely treat the mock as a rehearsal and discover afterwards that it was the evidence. A family who knows this in October treats January differently.

Term three narrows to technique. Whole papers under timing, marked against the official scheme, with an error log deciding what the next session covers. This is also the term when the honest advice is sometimes to stop adding sessions: a student with four tutors and no time to practise is being managed rather than taught, and the practice between lessons is where the marks are made.

sections.heading: Eight weeks: what a single block of weekly sessions can honestly achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the most commonly bought block and the least honestly described. Here is what it actually contains: eight sessions, perhaps twelve hours of contact if they run ninety minutes, and whatever the student does in between. That final part is the variable that decides the outcome, and it is the part no tutor controls.

Used well, the block follows a shape. Weeks one and two diagnose: a marked past paper, an error log started, the two or three recurring failures named. Weeks three to six attack those failures specifically and introduce whole papers under timing. Weeks seven and eight consolidate, re-test the same error types, and check the internal assessment is finished rather than hovering. By week eight the log should look different from week one, and if it does not, the diagnosis was wrong and should be redone rather than continued.

Used badly, the same eight weeks become a tour of the syllabus in chapter order, which feels productive and changes nothing. The tell is a session plan that could have been written before meeting the student. A plan that names frequency density, reverse percentages, uncertainty treatment in a physics graph or unlabelled economics diagrams is a plan built from evidence; a plan that says revise algebra is not.

What eight weeks cannot do is also worth stating plainly, because an Al Wahda parent deciding in March deserves it. It cannot convert a student who has not engaged with two years of content into a top-band candidate. It cannot produce an internal assessment from nothing in a way that is permissible, since the work must be the student's own. And it cannot substitute for the practice the student does alone, which is where almost all of the improvement happens.

sections.heading: The IGCSE series calendar for a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only. An Abu Dhabi candidate therefore sits the June series, with the November series available as the resit route, and any revision plan built around a February window has been copied from advice written for a different country.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each. Its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Since your child's school is the centre, the only timetable worth planning from is the one the school issues.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates are in the past, which is exactly why they are quoted: they can be checked. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, and because provisional dates are revised, a plan should link the live official timetable rather than repeat a date from a tutoring page.

The planning consequence is simple arithmetic. Entries are made months before the papers, results arrive months after, and a November resit decision has to be made while the June result still feels raw. A family that knows the shape of that cycle in advance makes a calmer decision than one meeting it for the first time in August.

sections.heading: The Diploma year: the deadlines that arrive before the IB's do
paragraphs: Diploma families often ask when the examinations are and plan from there. That is the wrong anchor, because the dates that constrain a DP student's year are set by the school rather than by the IB. Internal assessment draft deadlines, Extended Essay interim deadlines, the Theory of Knowledge essay timeline and the mock window are all school decisions, and they arrive first.

This page does not print IB session or results dates. The IB publishes them and revises them, and a wrong date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date at all. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the current internal calendar and confirm session dates against the IB's own assessment pages. Two Al Wahda students at different schools can genuinely have internal deadlines a month apart, so there is no general answer to give.

What can be said generally is the sequence. Internal assessment topics are agreed, drafts are submitted to the school, feedback is given once in most subjects, final versions are uploaded by the coordinator, mocks produce predicted grades, and then the session itself. The expensive mistake is treating the school's draft deadline as soft. In most subjects a student gets one round of formal teacher feedback, and a late draft forfeits it.

The implication for tutoring is that internal assessment coaching is seasonal and should be booked ahead of the school's date, not after it. Four to six weeks before the draft deadline is the useful window: enough time to narrow a question, gather data where the subject needs it, and act on criterion-level feedback. Two weeks before, the only honest service is helping a student finish what they have.

sections.heading: Ramadan, school hours and where the revision actually goes
paragraphs: Ramadan falls inside the UAE academic year and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which means it drifts across the second and third terms over time. School hours shorten, late-afternoon concentration drops, and family routines shift to the evening. A revision plan written in September that does not account for it does not survive contact with it.

The workable pattern is to front-load. Heavy new content and the hardest technique work belong in the weeks before Ramadan. During it, sessions move to post-Iftar slots, run shorter, and concentrate on consolidation: marking past papers already attempted, reviewing the error log, tidying an internal assessment that is substantially written. Afterwards, intensity resumes with the series in sight.

There is a scheduling advantage to online delivery here that is worth naming without overselling it. A post-Iftar session at an unusual hour is easy to arrange when nobody has to travel to it, and easy to move when the evening runs late. An in-home arrangement at the same hour depends on a tutor crossing Abu Dhabi after a long day, which is both more expensive and more fragile.

The same logic applies to the other fixed points in the UAE calendar: national holidays, school breaks, and the family travel that is common in this community. A student who is out of the country for three weeks in term two does not need a cancelled block; they need sessions on Gulf Standard Time wherever they are, which is a straightforward thing to arrange when the lesson is a video call rather than a visit.

sections.heading: What a term of tutoring costs, counted as a term rather than an hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tutoring look cheap and term costs make it look real, so here is the term view. A term of roughly twelve weeks at one session a week is twelve to eighteen hours of contact depending on session length. Taking the market bands below, that puts a qualified online subject tutor somewhere between the low thousands of dirhams for a term and roughly double that for exam-year specialist work, before any decision about a second subject.

The published bands behind that arithmetic, read in October 2026: budget online tuition from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350; IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; and premium named or examiner-led tuition at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Seen by the term, two decisions matter more than the hourly rate. The first is how many subjects, because two subjects doubles the cost and halves the student's time to practise either. The second is when in the year you buy. A term-one block that prevents a gap costs less than a term-two block that closes one, for the simple reason that the term-two gap now sits under newer content that also needs attention.

For context rather than comparison, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fees are regulated separately by ADEK. The reason to mention a fee decision at all is that tutoring is usually judged against the school fee it supplements, and families rarely have both numbers in front of them at once. Every figure here is a market rate from a named source; IB Gram's own fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach privately here, and what to do when nobody is free
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask any independent tutor to show the permit; it is free, so there is no cost reason to lack one. In Abu Dhabi there is an additional rule worth knowing: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to do likewise, so avoid engaging your child's own classroom teacher privately.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what those bodies do because it helps a parent judge what they are being sold; a page implying endorsement is misrepresenting itself. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal, and which should never be implied by anyone who does not hold it.

On availability, the honest position in an exam term is that specialists get booked. When no tutor for a particular Diploma course or syllabus code is free, you are told the expected wait and given the alternatives in writing: a different qualified tutor on the same course in another slot, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course on Gulf Standard Time and disclosed before booking, shorter and more frequent sessions while the preferred slot clears, or waiting. The last option is sometimes right, particularly in term one.
