process.title: Name the nearest date
process.description: The mock window, the internal assessment draft deadline, the series. Everything else in the plan is built backwards from whichever is closest, so that is the first thing to tell us, along with the subject, the level or syllabus code and the school.

process.title: We match to the course and the clock
process.description: A specialist for that Diploma course or IGCSE code, in a slot that works for an Al Wahda school day. If the right specialist cannot start in the week you need, you are told the wait rather than offered a substitute without being asked.

process.title: Free trial lesson used to diagnose, not to sell
process.description: One full lesson, no card required. The tutor works recent material and a marked paper to name the real failures, then says what is achievable in the time available, including when the honest answer is less tutoring than you expected.

process.title: A dated plan with a finish line
process.description: A short written plan that runs from today to the deadline, with the error log deciding the order of topics. Where a block is bought for one event, the plan ends on that event rather than rolling into the next term by default.

process.title: Review at the deadline, then stop or renew deliberately
process.description: After the dated event, the log is compared with where it started. If the recurring failures are gone, the recommendation is to stop or reduce. Renewal should be a decision made on evidence rather than a default that nobody revisits.

whyPoints.title: Plans built from your school's calendar
whyPoints.description: Two Al Wahda students at different schools can face internal deadlines a month apart. A plan built from the school's own written calendar beats a generic twelve-week template, and asking the coordinator for that calendar in September costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: The UAE-correct exam calendar
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's February and March series is India-only. Abu Dhabi candidates sit June and November, and Pearson runs May and June plus November. A page that gets this wrong gives a parent a date they will plan around, which is the worst kind of error to publish.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on what a short block can do
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks reliably changes technique and clears logged errors. It does not re-teach two years of content, and it cannot produce an internal assessment that must be the student's own work. Saying so before payment is more useful than saying it after.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and location stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes; that service runs only in India. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE, you hear it before booking.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources and dates attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is a market rate read from a named published source in October 2026, not an IB Gram price. Our own fee is quoted after the free trial lesson, once subject, level and session length are known.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives Ramadan and travel
whyPoints.description: Post-Iftar slots and sessions during family travel are straightforward when the lesson is a video call. Front-loading content before Ramadan and consolidating during it is a plan that holds rather than one that collapses.

faqs.question: We are halfway through the term. Is it sensible to start tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the scope matches the time left. A mid-term start works best when it targets one dated event: the mock window, an internal assessment draft deadline, or the series itself. The first session should produce a diagnosis from a marked paper rather than a syllabus tour, and the plan should run from today to that date and then stop. What does not work is attempting to cover a two-year course in the remaining weeks, which produces anxiety without producing marks.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the Abu Dhabi school year are the expensive ones to leave alone?
faqs.answer: Term two, almost always. Internal assessment drafts cluster there, the mock window arrives, and predicted grades are produced from internal evidence rather than from potential. A gap noticed in October costs a few sessions; the same gap discovered in a January mock costs more, because newer content now sits on top of it and both need attention. Term one is the cheapest term to buy help in and the one families most often skip.

faqs.question: Why are no IB session dates printed anywhere on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the IB publishes them and revises them, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around does more harm than no date. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the current internal calendar and confirm session and results dates against the IB's own assessment pages. The dates that actually constrain a Diploma student's year are set by the school anyway: internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay interim deadlines and the mock window all arrive before anything the IB sets.

faqs.question: Does my child in Al Wahda sit the February Cambridge exams?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. An Abu Dhabi candidate sits June, with November available as the resit route. A good deal of revision advice online is written for Indian candidates and quotes a February window, so check that any timetable you are working from matches the series your school has actually entered your child for.

faqs.question: How do we make sure we are using the right exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Use the one your school issues. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's school is the centre, so the school's version is the authoritative one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that are later revised, so work from the live official timetable rather than a copy.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of weekly sessions realistically change?
faqs.answer: Technique, logged errors and the completion of an internal assessment that is already substantially written. Eight sessions and perhaps twelve hours of contact is enough to fix recurring habits, build the discipline of writing a setup before calculating, and get whole papers completed under timing. It is not enough to re-teach two years of content, and it cannot substitute for the practice the student does alone between lessons, which is where most of the improvement is actually made.

faqs.question: When should we book internal assessment coaching for a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks before the school's own draft deadline, not the IB's submission date. That window gives time to narrow a question to something finishable, gather data where the subject requires it, and act on criterion-level feedback. Two weeks out, the only honest help is getting the student to finish what they have. Remember that in most subjects a student receives one round of formal teacher feedback, and a late draft forfeits it entirely.

faqs.question: Will a January mock really affect my child's university offer?
faqs.answer: It affects the predicted grade, which is what a university sees at the point of making an offer, so in practice yes. Schools produce predicted grades from internal evidence, and the mock is usually the largest single piece of it. Students treat the mock as a rehearsal because it does not appear on a certificate. Admissions read it as evidence. Preparing specifically for a school's own mock papers is a legitimate and bounded piece of tutoring with an obvious finish point.

faqs.question: Where do the Ramadan weeks fit into a revision timetable?
faqs.answer: They move, usually to post-Iftar slots, and the content changes rather than the frequency. School hours shorten and late-afternoon concentration drops, so the sensible pattern is to front-load heavy new content into the weeks before, use the period itself for consolidation, past-paper marking and error-log review, then resume full intensity afterwards. An unusual evening hour is easy to arrange when nobody has to travel for it, which is one practical advantage of a session delivered over video.

faqs.question: If we are abroad for three weeks in term two, is the block lost?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions are booked on Gulf Standard Time and delivered over live video, so a student travelling for two or three weeks in term two does not have to lose the block. The timing can also shift to suit the destination time zone for the duration. This is one of the clearer practical differences from an in-home arrangement, which simply stops when the family is away and then has to be restarted, often at the worst point in the term.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives in Al Wahda better than one who does not?
faqs.answer: Only if proximity solves your problem, and in an examination term it usually does not. The adult who has taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, or Economics internal assessment commentaries, may not live within a short drive of Hazza Bin Zayed Street. Online delivery changes the question from who is nearest to who has taught this exact course, and in a term where you need someone this week rather than next month, that is the question that matters.

faqs.question: What does a full term of weekly tutoring cost here?
faqs.answer: Counted as a term, roughly twelve sessions, or twelve to eighteen hours of contact depending on length. Using market bands read in October 2026, a qualified subject tutor online is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an examination-year specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. These are market figures from named sources; our own fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor is allowed to teach here?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tutor work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted at you. Since the permit is free, there is no innocent reason to lack it.

faqs.question: What happens if the specialist we need is fully booked this term?
faqs.answer: You are told, with an expected wait and the alternatives written down: a different qualified tutor on the same course in another slot, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course on Gulf Standard Time and disclosed before you book, shorter and more frequent sessions until the preferred slot clears, or waiting. Specialists genuinely do fill up in the weeks before mock windows and series. In term one, waiting is often the right choice rather than a disappointment.

faqs.question: Should we book two subjects at once or one at a time?
faqs.answer: One at a time, in most cases. Two subjects doubles the cost and halves the time the student has to practise either, and practice between lessons is where improvement is actually made. The exception is a student with two genuinely independent problems and enough free evenings to work on both, which is rarer than it sounds. Start with the subject carrying the nearest deadline or the largest recoverable gap, and add the second only if the first is clearly under control.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-z.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE subjects and IB Diploma courses at both levels. For a household choosing where to spend a limited budget, the match is made per subject and per level, with a view given on whether tuition is the right purchase at all.

intro.heading: The real question is how much, not how near
paragraphs: By the time a parent in Al Zahiyah types this phrase, the decision to spend something has usually been made and the harder questions are still open. Which child, if there are two. Which subjects, out of eight or nine. One session a week or two. For how long. And how you will know whether it is working, rather than feeling like it is working. None of those is answered by a list of tutors sorted by distance.

Al Zahiyah, the district still widely called the Tourist Club Area, occupies the dense north-eastern corner of Abu Dhabi island. Households here are typically running apartment living, more than one child, two different schools and often two different examination systems, because several schools in the emirate offer a British lower school and an IB Diploma above it. That combination produces the specific confusion this page is written for: two children on incompatible reporting scales, two sets of deadlines, and one household budget.

The single most useful thing a parent can internalise is that tuition has sharply diminishing returns across subjects and sharply increasing returns within one. Funding one subject properly, with marked written work and a specialist who knows the specification, reliably changes a grade. Funding four subjects thinly, with a generalist checking homework in each, reliably changes nothing and costs four times as much. Most of the disappointment in this market comes from the second pattern, and almost nobody selling tuition will tell you so.

On delivery, stated plainly rather than discovered later: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Independent tutors in the emirate do travel, and the market prices that loading in figures we attribute further down. The relevant consequence here is simply that proximity is not one of the five things that decide whether this spend works.

What follows is the decision material. The two systems set side by side on what each actually rewards. A table on how many subjects to fund and when to stop. The resit and retake routes by board, which parents almost always discover too late. What progress reporting you should insist on. How access arrangements work and who decides them, because that is a question families ask tutors and should be asking schools. What to do when a match is wrong, and the early signals that tell you so in week three rather than week ten. And the limits of this platform, written down, including the things we decline to sell at any price. Nothing on this page requires you to know the syllabus. It assumes only that you have a finite budget, more than one child, and a reasonable wish to be able to tell afterwards whether the money did anything.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-z.programmesIntro: An Al Zahiyah household running both systems is managing three different assessment logics at once. The point of setting them out is that a tuition plan drawn for one is wrong for the other.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal written papers, tiered Core and Extended by Cambridge and Foundation and Higher by Pearson. Almost everything rides on a fortnight of examinations, with practical skills in the sciences examined on paper. Coursework is minimal or absent in most subjects, which makes the tuition pattern steady and the deadline single.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Zahiyah family the planning implication is that the IGCSE child's year has one cliff edge. Work spread evenly across the two years is worth more than any concentration of effort, and the school's final entry deadline — months before the papers — is the date that fixes the tier and therefore the grade ceiling.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, graded one to seven per subject against a forty-five point total. Every subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria, so the year is a chain of deadlines rather than a single examination event.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the Diploma above a British lower school, which is exactly how a household ends up with two boards. The Diploma child's tuition needs to be lumpier — clustered around internal deadlines — while the IGCSE child's needs to be steady, and trying to run both on one pattern fails for one of them.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in several Abu Dhabi schools, with narrower subject choice, greater depth per subject and staged assessment across AS and A2. For families weighing it against the Diploma, the trade is breadth and coursework load against depth and a smaller number of examinations.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or grade 3 or better. Verify current requirements through the official channel.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-z.subjectsIntro: The courses below are the ones Al Zahiyah households most often weigh against each other when deciding where a limited budget goes, with an honest note on how much difference tuition tends to make in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics, IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: High return where the problem is procedural: scale factors, frequency density, rounding, command terms. Lower return where the problem is underlying fluency in Year 11, because the week has no room left for the practice volume required.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Diploma
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Consistently the highest-return Diploma subject for tuition, because the failure modes are specific and the exploration is twenty marks the student fully controls. Higher Level Paper 3 is the component least often practised and worth a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Good return at both levels. At IGCSE the marks sit in calculation chains and particle-level explanation; at Diploma level in organic mechanisms and the reasoning Paper 2 demands. The scientific investigation is marked on design rather than on tidy results.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Strong return where mathematics is the hidden obstacle, which it often is. A physics problem a student cannot start is frequently an algebra problem, and a tutor who checks that first saves a term of teaching the wrong subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Return depends on method rather than content. Students who revise by reading plateau; students who write answers against mark schemes improve. A tutor whose lessons are explanation rather than marked writing adds little here.

subjects.name: English, First Language and Diploma Language A
subjects.description: High return per hour where feedback is on the student's own writing, low return where lessons are about technique in the abstract. The Diploma's Individual Oral is a specific, trainable task that students rarely practise under conditions.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Good return because the common faults are structural: describing rather than evaluating, diagrams drawn imprecisely, commentaries that summarise an article instead of applying a theory to it. All three are correctable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: A distinct case. Content for these subjects is tightly prescribed and schools must ensure their teachers hold the regulator's approval to teach them. Any provider offering a bespoke alternative syllabus for them is describing something that should not be done.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Twenty marks across the essay and the exhibition, with strict word limits, and almost no household budgets for it. Support here is cheap relative to its effect on the points total, because students rarely receive any structured teaching on how the instrument is applied.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Thirty-four marks, with critical thinking alone worth twelve. Sessions are best clustered at the research-question and first-draft stages. The tutor questions and feeds back; the student produces every word, and we state that boundary to them directly.

sections.heading: The two systems side by side, on what each actually rewards
paragraphs: Parents running both boards tend to assume the Diploma is simply harder. It is more demanding in breadth and in the volume of internally assessed work, and less demanding in the single respect that matters to a nervous student: it does not place the entire grade on one fortnight. IGCSE does. Those are different kinds of pressure and they call for different tuition patterns.

The reward structures differ too. IGCSE rewards completeness and accuracy: a full, correct, well-expressed answer earns the marks. The Diploma rewards judgement — a position taken, supported with named evidence, with a limitation acknowledged. A student who writes excellent IGCSE answers in DP1 is marked down for exactly the qualities that previously earned top grades, which is disorienting unless somebody explains the change early.

Coursework is the third divergence and the one that reshapes a household's week. An IGCSE student's week is homework plus revision. A Diploma student's week is homework, revision and a portfolio of long internally assessed pieces, each with its own criteria, word limit and internal deadline. Those deadlines, not the examination window, are what a Diploma tuition plan must be built around, and they are published by the school at the start of the year if you ask.

The table sets the two out on the points that change a parent's decision. The last column is the practical one: what each difference means in a house where both systems are running at once, which is the situation a large share of Al Zahiyah families are actually in.

sections.heading: How many subjects should you fund, and when should you stop?
paragraphs: This is the question families most want answered and the one providers have the least incentive to answer honestly, because every additional subject is additional revenue. The honest answer is that the return falls off quickly, for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality: the student's own week is finite.

Tuition works through the work done between lessons. A session that teaches something and sets marked written practice produces improvement when that practice actually happens. Add a second subject and the student still has roughly the same number of free evenings. Add a third and the practice for all three gets thinner. By the fourth, the lessons continue and the written work has effectively stopped, at which point you are paying for attendance.

So the sequence we recommend is: fund one subject properly, see whether it moves within the review period, and only then consider a second. For a student in a terminal examination year with two genuinely failing subjects, two is defensible. Beyond two in the same term, the limiting factor is the child, and the right purchase is often not more tuition but a conversation with the school about workload, or a short bounded block on one neglected high-leverage component such as Theory of Knowledge.

The table gives a view by situation, including the two rows nobody writes down: when tuition adds very little, and when to stop. A provider willing to say 'this subject does not need us' is giving you information you can use, and a provider who recommends four subjects on a first phone call has told you how they decide things.

sections.heading: Resit and retake routes, by board
paragraphs: Parents usually learn about resits after results day, under time pressure, which is the worst moment to understand a system. The routes exist and they differ by board, and knowing them in advance changes how a family reacts to a disappointing grade — from panic to a plan with dates on it.

For Cambridge, the structure is straightforward: IGCSE examinations run in a June series and a November series, and those are the two series available to UAE candidates. A June candidate's resit route is November, and a November candidate's is the following June. The February and March series is offered in India only, so it is not a route for a student in Abu Dhabi, whatever a generic revision website says. Entries close well ahead of the papers, and the centre's internal deadline is earlier again than the board's.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The published schedule is a useful illustration of how far ahead the machinery runs: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well in advance, so the live official timetable is the only document worth planning from.

For the Diploma, a candidate may sit a subsequent session, and the handling of internally assessed marks between sessions is a question for the school's Diploma coordinator rather than for a tutoring page. We do not publish Diploma session or results dates here, because the organisation's own site is the only place they can be confirmed and a wrong date is worse than no date. The session UAE schools sit is the May one. Ask your coordinator for the exact windows and deadlines.

sections.heading: What progress reporting should you actually receive?
paragraphs: Most tuition is sold with a vague promise of progress updates and delivers a cheerful message after each lesson. That is reassurance, not reporting, and it is specifically designed not to be falsifiable. A parent paying for a term is entitled to something a sceptic could check.

The minimum useful set is small. A written diagnosis at the start, naming the specific faults found and the category of each. The student's own marked work, with the marks against the published scheme rather than a tick. An error log maintained across papers showing whether the named faults are recurring less often. And a review at a fixed date at which the question asked is whether the marks moved, not whether the lessons were enjoyable.

The reason to insist on marked work in particular is that it is the only artefact that cannot be dressed up. A student who was losing nine marks to command-term misreads and now loses three has improved by a number you can see. A student whose tutor reports growing confidence has produced nothing checkable, and in our experience that is exactly the language used when the written work has quietly stopped.

There is a privacy dimension worth stating as well, because tuition involves data about a minor. A provider should tell you what it collects, why, and how to have it deleted, and should keep a privacy link on every page. The UAE has a federal personal data protection law, and a lead form that gathers a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose is a problem regardless of how helpful the intent was. Ask what happens to the marked work and the diagnosis when you stop.

sections.heading: Access arrangements, learning support, and who actually decides
paragraphs: Families frequently ask a tutor whether their child can have extra time in examinations, and a tutor is the wrong person to ask. Access arrangements are applied for by the school to the examination board, on evidence, within the board's published rules and deadlines. No tutor arranges them, authorises them or can predict the outcome, and any provider implying otherwise is selling something they do not control.

What a parent can usefully do is start the conversation early and with the right person, which is the school's learning support lead or inclusion coordinator, not the subject teacher and not a tutoring platform. Evidence requirements and deadlines are real and the deadlines are earlier than families expect, frequently a full year before the examination. A request raised in the term of the papers is usually too late even when it is entirely justified.

Where tuition genuinely helps a student with additional learning needs is in the ordinary work: smaller steps, more repetition, explicit structure, written models, and a tutor who adapts pace without commentary. That is teaching rather than accommodation, and it is worth having on its own terms. We will say honestly when a student's needs are beyond what one-to-one subject tuition can address, because the alternative is taking money for the wrong intervention.

One further honest note. Lessons here are delivered over live video, which suits many students and genuinely does not suit all of them. Younger children, students who need physical supervision to stay on task, and those for whom a screen is itself a barrier may do better with something else. We would rather say that during a free trial than discover it in month three, and the trial exists partly for exactly this.

sections.heading: The Al Zahiyah week, and what changes it
paragraphs: Everything above assumes a week that can hold the plan. In a dense island district with more than one child, that assumption deserves checking before anything is booked, because the most common reason a sound tuition plan fails has nothing to do with the teaching.

Three features of an Al Zahiyah week recur. Journeys back into the district in the late afternoon are slow and variable, so a child's actual arrival time is later and less predictable than the school's published finish. Sibling collections at two different times usually bind the parent for an hour in the middle of the useful window. And the mandatory UAE subjects sit on the timetable alongside everything else, so a student's homework load is heavier than a count of their international subjects suggests.

The practical response is to design the week rather than hope for it. Record actual arrival times for five days and use the latest. Place the session where it survives a bad traffic day rather than where it fits a good one. Put written work in a fixed daily slot — twenty minutes of retrieval practice does more than a weekend batch — and accept a weekend session where the weekday arithmetic genuinely does not work. During Ramadan, agree a post-Iftar time in advance instead of watching the existing slot get cancelled.

None of this is sophisticated and all of it is skipped. A tuition arrangement that has been designed around the household's real week survives the term; one booked at a convenient-sounding time is being rescheduled by week four and abandoned by week eight, at which point the money has bought three lessons and a bad experience of tutoring in general.

sections.heading: When the match is wrong, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Sometimes a tutor and a student do not work, and the signal is not always poor results. The useful early warnings are specific: the student cannot say what the last lesson was about, there is no written work to look at, the tutor has not asked to see a marked paper, or every update is positive while the school's assessments are not. Any one of those is worth acting on in week three rather than week ten.

Our position is that a replacement should be straightforward and should not require an argument. Say the match is not working, and we match again. We would also rather hear it early, because a family that waits out a bad match for a term concludes that tutoring does not work, which is a reasonable conclusion from the evidence they have and the wrong one in general.

What a parent should not have to do is diagnose the problem. That is our job, and the usual answers are mundane: a specification mismatch nobody caught, a slot that is too late in the day for this particular child, a cadence too thin for the size of the gap, or a tutor whose strength is explanation when this student needs structured drilling. Each of those has a different fix and only one of them involves replacing the person.

The honest limit on all of this is that no replacement recovers time. A term spent with the wrong match in an examination year is a term gone, which is why the review date is set at the start and why the diagnosis is written down in the first week. A plan with a date and a measure in it fails visibly and early. A plan without one fails invisibly and late.

sections.heading: What this platform is, and the limits we will not cross
paragraphs: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform. It holds no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and is not a registered examination centre. It has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Naming a regulator on this page explains what that body does; it implies nothing about us, and the phrase describing a tutoring service as approved by one of them is the most dangerous sentence available in this market.

On tutors and permits: any paid private tutor in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so a specific figure quoted as the penalty is invention. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school; verify the current document before relying on the wording.

On assessed work: a tutor teaches, explains the criteria, questions a student's draft and marks practice against the published scheme. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, provide solutions for live assessed work, or sit beside a student during an assessment. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; we decline to produce assessed work at any price, and the consequences of buying it land on the student.

On claims: no tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university outcome, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism. We publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic, because we would have to produce the underlying data and the n, the date and the method with it. Market rates quoted on this page belong to the market and are dated October 2026. Board material is referenced and linked rather than reproduced, because specifications and mark schemes belong to the boards that publish them.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we fund for one child in Al Zahiyah?
faqs.answer: Start with one and review it. Tuition works through the marked written practice done between lessons, and a student's free evenings do not multiply when you add subjects. One subject funded properly, with a specialist and marked work, reliably moves a grade. Four funded thinly reliably move nothing and cost four times as much. For a student in a terminal examination year with two genuinely failing subjects, two is defensible. Beyond two in a term, the limiting factor is the child.

faqs.question: Is there an IB and IGCSE tutor based near Al Zahiyah?

IB Gram is not among them: we teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and do not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah or anywhere in the UAE, since home visiting is an India-only service for us. The reason we think that trade favours a household here is that proximity is not one of the things that decides whether the spend works. Specification match, marked work and cadence are.

faqs.question: What is my child's resit route if a Cambridge IGCSE grade disappoints?
faqs.answer: The November series for a June candidate, and the following June for a November candidate. Those are the two series available to UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered in India only, whatever a general revision website suggests. Entries close months ahead of the papers and your centre's internal deadline is earlier again, so the first call is to the exams officer rather than to a tutor. Cambridge also allocates centres to administrative zones with their own timetables.

faqs.question: When do Pearson International GCSE results and timetables fall?
faqs.answer: On a published schedule that runs further ahead than families expect. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well in advance of each series, which means the live official timetable is the only document worth planning a resit or an application deadline against.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get my child extra time in examinations?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone implying otherwise is selling something they do not control. Access arrangements are applied for by the school to the examination board, on evidence, within the board's published rules and deadlines. The right first conversation is with the school's learning support or inclusion lead, and it should happen early, because the deadlines frequently fall a full year before the examination. A request raised in the term of the papers is usually too late even when entirely justified.

faqs.question: What progress reporting should I expect from a tutor?
faqs.answer: Something a sceptic could check. A written diagnosis in the first week naming the specific faults found. The student's own work marked against the published scheme rather than ticked. An error log across papers showing whether those faults recur less often. And a review at a fixed date where the question is whether the marks moved. Cheerful messages after each lesson are reassurance by design, and in our experience that language appears exactly when the written work has stopped.

faqs.question: Does online tuition suit every student in a two-board household?
faqs.answer: No, and we would rather say so during a free trial than in month three. Live video works well for most secondary students and genuinely does not suit some: younger children, students who need physical presence to stay on task, and those for whom a screen is itself an obstacle. That is one of the things the trial lesson tests. Where a student's needs go beyond what one-to-one subject tuition can address, we say that too, because taking money for the wrong intervention helps nobody.

faqs.question: How do I know when to stop paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: When the marked evidence shows the gap has closed, not when the lessons feel better. That is the entire purpose of fixing a review date and a measure at the start. The three honest outcomes at a review are that the marks moved and the arrangement can taper, that the diagnosis was right but the cadence was too thin, or that the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing. A provider who never reaches the first of those has an incentive problem.

faqs.question: What should I do if the tutor and my child are not working out?
faqs.answer: Say so in week three rather than week ten, and we match again without an argument. The early signals are specific: your child cannot say what the last lesson covered, there is no written work to look at, the tutor never asked to see a marked paper, or every update is positive while school assessments are not. Diagnosing why is our job, and the usual causes are a specification mismatch, a slot too late in the day, or a cadence too thin for the gap.

faqs.question: Why should I not convert my children's grades between the two systems?
faqs.answer: Because the scales are not commensurable and the attempt causes domestic friction without producing information. Cambridge reports A* to G, Pearson nine to one, the Diploma one to seven per subject against a forty-five point total, and the Middle Years Programme one to eight against criteria. The only comparison that supports a decision is each child against their own earlier marked work on the same course, which is also the only comparison a tutor can act on.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by ADEK or KHDA to provide tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring platform should tell you otherwise without showing you a permit number. IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no UAE office, centre or branch, and no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises. We name regulators on this page to explain what they do, not to borrow their authority.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory UAE subject load affect a tuition plan?
faqs.answer: It reduces the homework headroom parents assume their child has. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum and adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So a Diploma student carrying six subjects plus the core plus the mandatory subjects is busier than the subject count suggests, which is a real argument for funding one subject properly rather than three thinly.

faqs.question: What is the honest return on paying for Theory of Knowledge support?
faqs.answer: Disproportionately good, and almost nobody buys it. The essay and the exhibition carry ten marks each against published instruments, both with strict word limits — sixteen hundred words for the essay, nine hundred and fifty for the exhibition commentary. Students receive little structured teaching on how the instrument is applied, so three to five sessions on exactly that tend to return more per dirham than the same spend added to a fourth subject. Markers stop at the word limit.

faqs.question: What does the data you collect about my child get used for?
faqs.answer: Matching a tutor and running the lessons, and you are entitled to ask what is held and have it deleted. The UAE has a federal personal data protection law and a tuition provider handling information about a minor should state what it collects, why, and how to remove it, with a privacy link on every page. A lead form gathering a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose is a problem regardless of intent, and it is reasonable to ask what happens to the marked work when you stop.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE subjects for students in Baniyas and the surrounding mainland communities. Each works to the exam series your child is entered for, and each session is scheduled around the school day rather than against it.

intro.heading: Start with the date, not the tutor
paragraphs: Most tutoring searches in Baniyas happen in the fortnight after a report card. A parent reads a 4 in IGCSE Maths or a predicted 4 in an IB HL subject, opens Google, and types a phrase with "near me" in it because proximity feels like the thing that can be fixed quickly. Proximity is rarely the constraint. The constraint is the calendar, and the calendar is already fixed by the time anyone starts searching.

Here is what that means in practice. A Year 11 student in Baniyas following Cambridge IGCSE sits papers in the June series. The school's final entry to Cambridge goes in months earlier, so by the time a report card triggers a search, the subject list, the tier and the paper combination are usually locked. What remains adjustable is how many marks that student can collect from the papers they are already entered for. An IB Diploma student in DP2 is in a tighter position again: the Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay all have internal school deadlines that arrive well before the written papers, and those deadlines are set by the coordinator, not by the IB.

So the first question a useful tutor asks is not "which topics are weak". It is "what is the next hard date". For a DP2 student in November that date is almost always an IA draft; for a Year 11 student it is a mock paper; for a Year 10 student it is the first full past paper under timed conditions. Each of those has a different shape of preparation, and treating them as the same job is the commonest way families waste money on tuition.

Baniyas adds one practical wrinkle. It is a mainland community, well inland from the island, and most secondary students here travel to school by bus along the Dubai road corridor. A bus that leaves at 06:40 and returns at 15:50 leaves a real window between roughly 16:30 and 20:00 on weekdays, but it also leaves a tired student. A session at 16:00 straight off the bus and a session at 18:30 after a break are not equally productive, and the difference shows within three weeks. Scheduling is part of the academic plan, not an administrative afterthought.

IB Gram works as a matching platform rather than a tuition centre. For families in the UAE every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Emirates, because home visits are a service offered only in India. That is the honest position, and the rest of this page explains why it usually produces a better subject match for a Baniyas family than a short driving radius would.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for almost every tutoring request from Baniyas: the IB Diploma, the IB Middle Years Programme that feeds it, and international GCSE under either Cambridge or Pearson. Each has its own clock, and the clock is what decides how a term of tuition is planned.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Written papers sit at the end of DP2 in the May session that UAE schools use. The internal components arrive much earlier: a Maths exploration, science practical work, a Language A written task and the Extended Essay all have school-set deadlines across DP1 and early DP2. Marks lost there cannot be recovered in the exam hall.
programmes.countryNote: Baniyas DP students mostly travel to IB schools on the island or in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, which means a long bus day. The practical effect is that DP2 students here arrive at tuition already behind on sleep. Sessions that work are shorter, more frequent, and pinned to the next internal deadline rather than to a topic list.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked A to D with band descriptors rather than percentages. MYP 5 ends with a Personal Project and, in some schools, eAssessment. The criterion structure is where families get confused: a child can produce competent work and still score in the middle band because the task asked for evaluation and the answer offered description. Reading the criterion wording is half the skill.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the single most common reason a Baniyas family looks for a tutor in the summer term of MYP 5. Students arrive in DP1 having been assessed against criteria for five years and meet a paper that wants method marks, units and a conclusion in a fixed form. Eight weeks of structured practice in that term closes most of the gap.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, with Cambridge offering Core and Extended tiers in several subjects and Pearson offering a single tier in most. Cambridge syllabus codes identify the course precisely: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry. Pearson numbers run differently, 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1 for Physics. Knowing the code matters because the past papers, the formula sheet and the command-term conventions all differ.
programmes.countryNote: Baniyas students sit in both board camps depending on which school the family chose, and some sit subjects split across boards. A tutor who assumes Cambridge conventions for a Pearson paper will teach the wrong structure for the longer six-mark questions, and the student will lose marks for a reason nobody explains to them.

programmes.name: November resit route
programmes.description: Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in November as well as May/June. For a student who misses a grade needed for a Diploma place or a sixth-form entry condition, the November route is a real second attempt rather than a wait of a full year. Entry goes through a centre, and private candidates must find a centre that accepts them.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Baniyas usually discover the November option too late, because the result and the resit decision land in the same August fortnight. Planning it in advance changes the tuition shape entirely: a resit block is about paper technique and the two or three topics that actually cost the grade, not a re-teach of the course.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of the mainland cluster around maths and the sciences, with English Language and Business Studies close behind. The descriptions below say what each subject assesses and where marks go missing, because that is what a first session has to diagnose.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the whole course. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any weakness in manipulation that a calculator has been hiding since MYP. HL students lose most marks in proof, complex numbers and the harder calculus, and in the exploration when the mathematics is correct but thin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. Every paper assumes graphical calculator competence, and students who learned maths by hand often score below their ability simply because they do not use the machine fast enough. The exploration rewards a real data set and a genuine question.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 is where grades are decided. Recurring losses sit in bounds and accuracy, similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, and the longer problems that need two steps linked. Working shown badly costs method marks even when the final answer is right.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, both with a calculator. The Higher tier asks more algebraic proof and more multi-stage ratio than students expect from the textbook, and the mark schemes credit a clear method line that many candidates never write down.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism produce the widest spread of marks at every level. IB students lose marks in the long-answer questions by describing instead of explaining; IGCSE candidates lose them on practical-method questions where a named control variable is required and only a vague answer is given.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry gate everything after them, so a student weak there appears weak across the paper. Organic mechanisms at HL and electrolysis at IGCSE are the two topics that most often need rebuilding from first principles rather than revising.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume misleads students into reading rather than writing. Marks go in data-analysis questions and in anything asking for a comparison with a stated measure. Command terms matter more here than in any other science: outline, describe, explain and evaluate each carry different mark expectations.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0500 and 4EA1
subjects.description: Analysis of unseen text is the trainable part. Students in Baniyas who read widely in English still lose marks for writing about content rather than about technique and effect. IB Paper 1 guided analysis and the IGCSE directed writing task reward a planned structure above vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish general answers. Marks come from applying a named tool to the stimulus firm and then judging it, and most candidates stop at the application step. HL has the additional burden of the extension topics and a longer research-based component.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are the mark-earning unit. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram with a sentence of explanation scores where three paragraphs of prose do not. HL calculation papers need practice under timed conditions because the arithmetic is simple but the question wording is not.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in UAE private schools as a mandatory subject, and the first-language and additional-language routes are genuinely different courses with different expectations. Support here is about reading fluency and written register rather than conversation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written paper rewards precision about algorithms and data representation more than coding ability. IGCSE candidates lose marks on pseudocode conventions and on trace tables; IB students lose them in the paper-two option and in a solution that is built but barely documented.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.regionsIntro: Baniyas sits inland on the Abu Dhabi mainland, with Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shawamekh to one side and the Dubai road corridor on the other. The notes below cover the communities whose school runs and session windows overlap with Baniyas.

regions.note: Older mainland housing in distinct sectors, with Bawabat Al Sharq as the local centre. Most secondary students travel out by school bus, which makes the 16:30 to 20:00 window the realistic slot for weekday tuition.

regions.note: Immediately adjacent, with a similar bus pattern and a heavy mix of Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum enrolment. Families here often need support split across two boards within the same household.

regions.name: Al Shawamekh
regions.note: Newer villa housing to the south of Baniyas. The commute to island schools is long enough that evening sessions after 18:00 are the norm rather than the exception.

regions.name: Khalifa City

regions.note: The island holds the oldest and best-known private schools in the emirate, and a Baniyas family that enrols there accepts an hour of travel each way as the price.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: This is the cluster most Baniyas secondary students travel to. It holds British-curriculum and IB provision within a few kilometres of each other, which is why two neighbours on the same street can be following completely different assessment calendars.

schoolClusters.city: The island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: The longer commute, chosen for programme rather than convenience. Several of these schools run the full IB continuum, so a Baniyas family that starts here in primary tends to stay through DP2 regardless of the travel.

schoolClusters.city: Baniyas and the near mainland
schoolClusters.note: Schools within a short drive of Baniyas itself, serving families who chose proximity over programme breadth. Most follow British or Indian curricula, and IGCSE entries from this cluster are concentrated in Cambridge subjects.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every request from Baniyas, and the right one depends entirely on how far away the next hard date is. All three run one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: A fixed slot each week with the same tutor, working through the school's scheme of work a fortnight ahead of the class. This is the shape that suits a Year 10 or DP1 student where the next exam is a long way off and the aim is to stop a gap forming. Progress is measured against the school's own assessment points rather than an external plan.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, usually 60 or 90 minutes
Work set between sessions and marked at the start of the next
Pauses available around school assessment weeks

modes.title: Deadline block for an IA, EE or coursework stage
modes.description: A short run of sessions timed to a specific internal deadline. The tutor works on the student's own research question, their own data and their own draft, giving feedback and teaching the criteria. No part of an assessed piece is written or produced for the student, because that is malpractice under IB rules and would put the Diploma at risk.
bullets: Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Method and data-handling teaching rather than content supply
Clear boundary stated at the first session and kept to

modes.title: Intensive run before a June or November series
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week for six to ten weeks, built around past papers under timed conditions. Each session marks a paper, isolates the two or three recurring mark losses, and drills those. This is the shape that fits the eight-week window most Baniyas families arrive with, and it is measured in marks per paper rather than topics covered.

Mark-scheme walkthrough on the student's own script

sections.heading: What a Baniyas parent is actually asking when they search for a tutor near me
paragraphs: The phrase means two things at once. The literal reading is geographic: who teaches this syllabus and lives close enough to reach Baniyas on a weekday evening. The real question underneath is about reliability — can someone competent be in front of my child this week, at a time that works, without the whole thing collapsing because of traffic on the Dubai road.

Answering the geographic version honestly is awkward, because the honest answer is that the pool of people living within fifteen minutes of Baniyas who can teach IB Chemistry HL or mark a Pearson 4MA1 Higher paper to the scheme is small. Abu Dhabi's specialist tutoring supply concentrates near the island and the Khalifa City corridor, where the schools are. A family that insists on a short radius ends up choosing from whoever is available rather than from whoever knows the subject, and that trade is invisible until the third session.

The reliability version has a better answer. A live video lesson removes travel from both sides of the arrangement. The tutor is not driving across the mainland at 17:00, so the session starts when it is supposed to and does not shorten when the road is slow. The student is not waiting for a doorbell. For a household where the school bus returns at 15:50 and dinner is at 20:00, that predictability is worth more than physical presence, and it is the reason the delivery model for UAE families is online one-to-one rather than a home visit.

So the page you have landed on answers the search properly and then declines part of it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Baniyas address — home visits are an India-only service — and the comparison later on this page sets out what you get instead, in money, in subject match, and in how often a session actually happens as planned.

sections.heading: The term counted backwards from the exam series
paragraphs: Every useful tuition plan is built from the last hard date backwards, and for IGCSE candidates in Abu Dhabi that date belongs to the board. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February/March series exists but is offered to candidates in India only, so no Baniyas student sits it and no page should tell a UAE parent otherwise.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. That single operational detail matters more than most revision advice: a family that plans around a timetable copied from a different zone can lose a paper outright. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone your centre sits in, and work from the timetable they hold.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results follow in January — November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The June picture is quicker: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, which is why any session plan should link the live official timetable rather than lean on dates restated on a tutoring page.

The table below is the shape of a term read backwards. Fill the date column from your own school's examinations officer and the board's published timetable, because entry deadlines are set by the centre and vary between schools.

sections.heading: Eight weeks: what can actually change, and what cannot
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most families arrive with, and it is enough to move some things and not others. What moves is anything mechanical: formula recall, the order a paper is attempted in, the habit of writing a method line, accuracy and rounding, calculator fluency on a Paper 2 that permits one. These are skills with short learning curves and they are worth real marks because they are lost on questions the student can already do.

What does not move in eight weeks is a missing foundation two years deep. A Year 11 student who never secured index laws will not become fluent in algebraic manipulation by June, and pretending otherwise wastes the window. The honest plan in that case is to triage: pick the topics with the highest mark density on the papers actually being sat, secure those completely, and accept that two or three topics will be left as guesses. A tutor who claims to re-teach a whole syllabus in eight weeks is selling comfort.

The diagnostic that makes this work is a marked script, not a conversation. Session one takes the student's most recent mock or past paper and goes through it question by question, separating three kinds of loss: did not know it, knew it and wrote it badly, knew it and ran out of time. Those three have different fixes, and families routinely spend eight weeks on the first when two thirds of the lost marks were in the second and third.

For a DP2 student the eight-week calculation is different again, because internal components are already submitted or nearly so. The marks still in play are in the written papers, and the fastest gains there are in Paper 2 and Paper 3 structure — knowing what an eight-mark question wants, and stopping at the point where the mark scheme stops. That is teachable quickly, and it is the part school classes rarely have time to drill.
bullets: Movable in eight weeks: timing, method lines, accuracy, command-term response, paper order
Partly movable: two or three named topics, rebuilt properly rather than skimmed
Not movable: a two-year foundation gap across the whole subject
Diagnosed from a marked script in session one, not from a parent's summary

sections.heading: What tuition costs around Abu Dhabi, and what the travel premium is paying for
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest end rather than the premium end, because that is where most families begin and where most of the disappointment happens. Online tutoring from university-student or generalist tutors is advertised in the UAE from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour — EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that rate you are buying homework supervision. It can be exactly right for a Year 9 student who needs company and structure, and it is the wrong purchase for a DP2 Chemistry HL student eight weeks from papers.

A qualified subject tutor working online sits in a different band. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted from about AED 200 to 450 and upwards; TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. At the top, named or examiner-level tutors are advertised far higher — BartyED quotes AED 650. These are market figures published by those providers, not IB Gram's prices.

In-home visits carry a premium that is easy to misread. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors in the Emirates are quoted between AED 200 and 500 including travel. For a Baniyas address the travel component is not small: a tutor crossing from the island or Khalifa City in the early evening spends forty minutes or more each way, and that time is priced into the hourly rate whether or not it appears as a separate line. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What the travel premium buys is physical presence and a tutor drawn from a radius rather than from a subject. For Baniyas that radius is the problem. The table below sets the three formats against each other on the terms that matter to a mainland household.

sections.heading: ADEK, your child's school and what an inspection band actually tells you
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Sharjah schools to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Baniyas families sit squarely under ADEK, which is worth knowing because almost no tutoring page in this market names it at all.

An inspection band is a judgement about a school, not about a cohort or a child. A strong band tells you the systems work: assessment is moderated, teaching is monitored, data on individual students exists and is used. A weaker band tells you those systems are patchy, which changes what a tutor is for. In a well-run school the tutor's job is usually narrow and technical, because the school has already identified the gap. In a school with weaker internal assessment, a tutor often has to do the diagnosis the school has not done.

Two ADEK-related points affect tutoring arrangements directly. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours is expected to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct carries the same restriction. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document, but the direction is clear and it means the phrase "your child's own teacher, privately" should set off an alarm rather than sound like a convenience.

IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring platform in this market should claim one it cannot evidence. What a platform can do is name the regulator correctly, explain what it governs, and point you to the authority's own listing when you want to check a school.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in the final weeks, when the temptation is highest
paragraphs: The eight weeks before a deadline are when boundaries get tested. A DP2 student with an unfinished Maths exploration and a mock week in the same fortnight is under real pressure, and the market contains providers who will take advantage of it. One operation in this SERP advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller.

The line a tutor works to is simple to state and worth stating to the student directly. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion asks for, read a draft the student wrote and say where it does not yet meet the criterion, ask questions that make the student find the weakness themselves, and teach method — how to structure an argument, how to present data, how to reference. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft, produce or supply any part of an assessed piece, may not invent or supply data, and may not edit a draft into something the student could not have written.

The practical test is whether the student can explain every sentence of the submitted work and every step of the reasoning. If they cannot, the work is not theirs, and an IB coordinator conducting a viva on an Extended Essay will find out. Supervisors are experienced at spotting a draft whose voice shifts, and the authenticity declaration the student signs is not a formality.

This boundary is also the most useful thing to ask a prospective tutor about. A tutor who answers vaguely, or who offers to "polish" a draft, is offering something that puts a Diploma at risk. A tutor who states the boundary before you ask is telling you they have worked with coordinators before.
bullets: Allowed: teaching content, explaining criteria, feedback on the student's own draft, method coaching
Not allowed: writing or rewriting any assessed text, supplying data, editing to completion
Test: can the student explain every sentence and every step without help
Ask any tutor where the line sits before the first paid session

sections.heading: Permits, and how a Baniyas parent can check a tutor is working legally
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

Two parts of that are worth holding on to. The permit costs nothing, so a tutor who says the paperwork is too expensive is not describing the UAE system. And individuals offering private tuition without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The ministry has not published a fine schedule — Khaleej Times reported that it did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties — so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified rather than repeated.

The official route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. A parent can reasonably ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit and under which category. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again and needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute; that is a permit issued to institutions with a physical centre, not something a matching platform holds.

For an online tutor based outside the Emirates the permit question changes shape, and the honest answer is that a UAE permit governs tuition provided in the UAE. What a family can still check is subject credentials, experience with the specific board and syllabus code, and whether the tutor can talk fluently about the mark scheme for the papers their child is sitting. That last test filters more effectively than any document.
