sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, the deadline nobody counts backwards from
paragraphs: Families plan carefully for exams and then meet equivalency as a surprise. If your child will apply to a UAE university or needs a UAE-recognised secondary certificate, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules decide which subjects and grades count, and they do not match the entry requirements of the university prospectus.

For the British track the requirements have been set out publicly: a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is where a competing tutoring page in this market publishes a wrong subject count, telling UAE candidates they need six IGCSE subjects. Five is the published figure.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold has been verified from the Ministry's own pages, so this page publishes none; if your child is on the Diploma and equivalency matters, check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly rather than trusting a number on a tutoring site.

What this changes about tuition planning is subject selection, not technique. A Year 10 student in Baniyas dropping a subject to lighten the load can quietly fall below the five-subject count, and nobody notices until the attestation stage. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees, and tuition is not a requirement for it. Knowing the rule early is what matters.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The Abu Dhabi academic year has features no generic revision plan accounts for. Working and school hours shorten during Ramadan, the school day ends earlier, and families restructure their evenings around iftar. For a DP2 or Year 11 student whose papers fall after Ramadan, that month sits in the middle of the most important revision block of the two-year course, and treating it as a normal six weeks is why plans fail.

What works is moving sessions rather than skipping them. A slot that ran at 17:30 moves to after iftar, often between 20:30 and 22:00, and students are noticeably sharper then than in the late afternoon of a fasting day. Session length drops and frequency holds. The alternative — pausing for a month and resuming three weeks before papers — loses the compounding that makes revision work.

Term holidays matter in the other direction. The winter break and the spring break are the only stretches in the year where a student can do sustained work on a weak topic without school homework competing for the same evening. A Baniyas family planning a June series properly uses one of those breaks for foundation repair and leaves the final eight weeks for paper technique. Families who do the reverse arrive in May still learning content.

Travel is the other common disruption. Many households here spend part of the summer and part of the winter break abroad, and a lesson delivered over live video follows the student to wherever they are, which a home visit cannot. Timezone shifts need planning rather than cancellation: a session at 18:00 Gulf Standard Time is mid-afternoon in London and late evening in Manila, and both can be made to work if the slot is agreed in advance.
bullets: Move sessions to after iftar rather than pausing through Ramadan
Use the winter or spring break for foundation work, not for paper drills
Keep the final six to eight weeks for timing and mark-scheme technique
Online delivery follows a travelling student; a home visit does not

process.title: Tell us the date, not just the subject
process.description: The enquiry form asks for year group, board, syllabus code if you know it, and the next hard date — a mock, an IA deadline, a June or November entry. That last field changes the match more than anything else, because an exam-series run and a term-long support arrangement need different tutors.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: A recent marked mock or past paper is worth more than a description of the problem. It shows where marks were actually lost and separates knowledge gaps from technique gaps, which is the difference between a term of re-teaching and six weeks of targeted drilling.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: The trial is a real diagnostic session, not a sales call. The tutor works through part of that marked script with your child and then tells you plainly what the eight or twelve weeks should contain. You judge the teaching before any block is agreed.

process.title: Agree the plan and the slot
process.description: Frequency, session length and a weekday window that survives the Baniyas school bus. Plans are written against your school's assessment dates, with pauses built in around mock weeks and internal deadlines rather than discovered when they arrive.

process.title: Review against marks, then adjust
process.description: Every few weeks the measure is a marked paper, not a feeling. If the recurring loss has moved, the plan moves with it; if the match is not working, you say so and a different tutor is proposed without an argument about the remaining block.

whyPoints.title: A subject specialist instead of a short radius
whyPoints.description: Matching by subject and level rather than by driving distance means a Baniyas student can work with a tutor who teaches Chemistry HL every week, rather than the best generalist who happens to cover the mainland on a Tuesday evening.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that start when they are meant to
whyPoints.description: No travel on either side means no session shortened by the Dubai road at 17:30. Over a twelve-week block the difference between a reliable sixty minutes and an unpredictable forty-five is several full sessions of teaching.

whyPoints.title: Board and syllabus code matched properly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different courses with different paper structures and different mark-scheme conventions. The match records which one your child sits, including the split-board cases that are common in this part of Abu Dhabi.

whyPoints.title: An honest academic-honesty line
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own work. Nothing assessed is written or produced for a student, and that boundary is stated at the first session rather than negotiated at a deadline.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to the providers and rate tables that published them, with the month they were read. You can check them before you decide what a fair price is for your own household.

whyPoints.title: A free trial before any commitment
whyPoints.description: The first lesson is free and is a working diagnostic. If the teaching is not right for your child, nothing has been spent and no block has been bought.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Baniyas who can start this week?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes — but not by travelling to you. Matches for Baniyas families are made by subject and level and the lessons run one-to-one over live video, so the constraint is tutor availability in your subject rather than whether anyone covers the mainland. A common subject such as IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or IB Maths AA SL can normally be matched within a few days, including a free trial lesson. Narrow combinations take longer: Chemistry HL eight weeks before papers, or a less common Group 2 language, may need a week or more. Tell us the next hard date in your enquiry and the match is prioritised around it.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Baniyas actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE candidates at UAE centres sit the June series, with November available as a resit or second-chance route. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to candidates in India only, so it does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. IB Diploma students at Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that you must use the timetable for your own zone, so ask your school's examinations officer which zone your centre is in and work from the timetable they hold rather than a date copied from a website.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series should a Baniyas student start tutoring?
faqs.answer: For technique work, eight to twelve weeks is the useful window: long enough to rehearse timing, method lines and command-term responses across several marked papers, short enough that the drilling stays sharp. For content repair the answer is a term earlier, because rebuilding a weak foundation takes sustained weekly work rather than an intensive run. If you are already inside eight weeks, the plan should be triage rather than coverage — identify the topics with the highest mark density on the papers being sat, secure those completely, and accept that two or three will be left. That is a smaller promise than a full re-teach and it produces more marks.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to a villa in Baniyas or Mohammed Bin Zayed City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service offered only in India. Every lesson for a family in Baniyas or the neighbouring mainland communities runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is practical rather than ideological: the specialist tutor pool for IB and IGCSE subjects in Abu Dhabi clusters near the island and the school corridor, so matching by driving radius would mean choosing from a much smaller group of people. Online delivery also removes the forty minutes each way that a mainland visit costs, which is why the market prices in-home sessions higher.

faqs.question: What does the in-home travel premium really buy a family on the mainland?
faqs.answer: Physical presence, and a tutor chosen from whoever covers your area. Published market rates put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Dubai table, and independent home tutors in the Emirates are quoted between AED 200 and 500 including travel. Qualified online subject tutors sit lower, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. For a Baniyas address the travel component is real — forty minutes or more each way from the island at 17:00 — and it is inside the hourly rate whether or not anyone itemises it. Whether that is worth paying depends on whether your child needs supervision or expertise.

faqs.question: My child is in DP2 and the Maths exploration is not finished. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the mathematics the exploration needs, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for in plain language, read what your child has written and say where it does not yet meet the criterion, and coach the process of refining a research question into something answerable. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot supply data, and cannot edit a draft into work your child could not have produced. That boundary is set by IB academic-honesty rules and the consequences of crossing it fall on the student. The practical test is whether your child can explain every step of the submitted exploration unaided.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around the Baniyas school bus and a long commute?
faqs.answer: That is the main scheduling problem for this community, and it is solvable. Secondary students bussing to Khalifa City, Al Raha or the island typically get home between 15:30 and 16:15, and a session straight off the bus is less productive than one after a break and some food. Most Baniyas families settle on a weekday slot between 17:30 and 20:00, with longer weekend sessions for paper practice that needs an uninterrupted two hours. Because lessons run over live video there is no travel on the tutor's side, so a 17:30 start is a 17:30 start rather than an estimate that depends on the Dubai road.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees my child's school in Baniyas?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Sharjah schools under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. ADEK is worth naming because almost no tutoring site in this market mentions it. IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK or any other regulator, and you should treat any claim of regulator approval by a tutoring provider with caution.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Baniyas families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any amount quoted online is unverified. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: Can a Baniyas teacher tutor my child if they teach at the same school?
faqs.answer: You should avoid that arrangement. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document, but the direction is unambiguous. Beyond the rule there is a practical reason: a tutor who also marks your child's school assessments cannot give independent feedback on them, which removes most of the value of having a second pair of eyes.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects must a Baniyas student pass for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring page in this market states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and tuition is not required for it — verify your own case on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What should a first session look like if we are eight weeks from papers?
faqs.answer: It should open the student's most recent marked script and work through it question by question, sorting every lost mark into one of three boxes: did not know it, knew it but wrote it badly, knew it but ran out of time. Those three have different remedies, and families often spend the whole window on the first when most of the marks sat in the second and third. By the end of the session the tutor should be able to name the two or three recurring losses and say what the next six weeks will drill. If a first session is spent on general discussion, ask for the script to be looked at instead.

faqs.question: How do lessons work during Ramadan for a student in Baniyas?
faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than stop. School hours shorten during Ramadan and household routines reorganise around iftar, so the slot that ran at 17:30 usually shifts to somewhere between 20:30 and 22:00, where students on a fasting day are measurably sharper than in the late afternoon. Session length often drops while frequency holds, which keeps the compounding that makes revision work. Pausing for the month and resuming a few weeks before papers is the pattern that costs the most, particularly for a DP2 or Year 11 student whose series falls soon after. The slot is agreed in advance rather than renegotiated weekly.

faqs.question: What happens if no Baniyas-matched specialist is free for a niche subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than matched with whoever is available. For a niche combination — a less common Group 2 language, a specific Pearson science option, or Chemistry HL in the weeks before papers — the honest options are a short wait for the right tutor, a different tutor with a strong adjacent specialism and a clear statement of what they do not cover, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. Quietly substituting a generalist is how families lose a term. Because delivery is over live video the pool is not limited to people who can reach the Abu Dhabi mainland, which makes a genuine match more likely than a radius search would.

faqs.question: Is a resit in the November series worth planning for before results arrive?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, because the result and the resit decision land in the same fortnight in August and a rushed decision is a worse one. Cambridge runs a November series and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in November as well as May/June, with November results following in January — November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. If a grade is a condition for a Diploma place or sixth-form entry, knowing the route in advance means the plan can start immediately rather than after three weeks of deliberation. A resit block is about paper technique and the two or three topics that cost the grade, not a re-teach.

faqs.question: How do we judge a tutor before committing money?
faqs.answer: Use the free trial as a test of three things. Can the tutor talk specifically about the paper structure and mark-scheme conventions for your child's board and syllabus code, not just the subject. Can they look at a marked script and name the recurring loss rather than describe the topic as weak. And will they state the academic-honesty boundary on coursework before being asked. A tutor who passes those three is worth paying; one who talks mainly about motivation and rapport may still be right for a younger student, but is unlikely to add marks in an exam year.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.closingHeading: Start from the next hard date in Baniyas
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-bani.closingBody: Send the year group, the board and syllabus code if you have it, and the one date that matters next — a mock, an IA deadline, a June or November entry. Attach the most recent marked paper if you can find it. The free trial lesson is a working diagnostic with the proposed tutor, who will look at that script with your child and then tell you plainly what the coming weeks should contain and what they cannot change. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Baniyas school run rather than against it. Nothing is booked until you have seen the teaching.

intro.heading: Two systems, two results seasons, two short windows
paragraphs: A Corniche household running both the British pathway and the IB Diploma gets two sets of results within a few weeks of each other in the summer, each with its own options and each with a window that closes faster than parents expect. The two systems publish differently, they repair differently, and the paperwork afterwards differs too. Treating them as one process is where families lose outcomes, usually by missing a deadline on one side while attending to the other.

The IGCSE side is published and citable. Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with different timetables.

The IB side cannot be published here with the same confidence. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session date, results date or enquiry deadline in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and secondary sources disagree with one another. UAE schools sit the May session; everything more precise should come from your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative version for your child's cohort.

What both systems share is a repair structure with three broad options: a review of the marking, a resit in a later session, or acceptance. What differs is the timing and therefore which option is realistic. An IGCSE November resit produces a grade the following January, which suits a conditional post-16 place and not a firm one. An IB retake sits in a later session with its own implications for a university offer, and whether an internal assessment mark carries forward changes the work involved substantially.

The Corniche contributes a practical layer rather than an academic one. This is apartment living along the waterfront with schools a short drive inland towards Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and Al Khalidiyah. Journeys are short, which means the limiting factor is the week rather than the road, and tower logistics mean visitor parking, reception and lift waits all consume paid minutes that no quoted rate itemises.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to the Corniche is one-to-one teaching over live video, which makes a two-system household easier to run: two specialists in consecutive slots on one evening, with nobody travelling between them and neither session starting late. One night of the week is committed rather than three, which in a household already managing two examination calendars is worth more than it sounds.

sections.heading: Two results seasons in one summer
paragraphs: The practical difficulty of a two-system household is that August contains two sets of decisions rather than one, and each has a short window. The IGCSE side is dated and public: Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The IB side arrives earlier in the summer, and its dates come from your school rather than from this page.

Each set of results then opens the same three broad questions in different forms. Is the marking worth reviewing. Is a resit realistic, and when would the grade arrive. Does the result actually meet the requirement that applies, rather than the one the household had in mind. The third question is the one most often skipped and most often the answer.

Timing is what separates the two systems. An IGCSE November resit produces a grade the following January, as happened when November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026. That suits a post-16 place that can hold a conditional and does not suit one requiring a firm grade in September, which is the common case for a school's own sixth form.

Use it in the spring rather than in August, because the single most useful thing a two-system household can do is agree in advance what grade would trigger each response. Decisions made calmly in March are better than decisions made in the forty-eight hours after a result, when nobody in the house is thinking clearly.

sections.heading: The IGCSE repair routes, with their real timings
paragraphs: Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable. An enquiry about results is submitted by the school within a board deadline on defined grounds; it is a clerical and marking review rather than a general appeal. A November resit produces a grade the following January. A retake in the next June series gives a full year of preparation and a grade the following August.

The enquiry is worth considering where a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary and the paper in question felt strong to the student. Mathematics is a reasonable candidate because the marking is comparatively objective. It is not a route to a better grade where the student simply underperformed, and schools will say so, usually correctly.

The November resit is the route families underuse and the one with the clearest arithmetic in some subjects. In mathematics the content is already taught, the gap is usually technique, and three focused months can move a boundary. In content-heavy subjects like Biology the same three months are rarely enough, because the specification is large and the student is also starting a new course.

The question that should precede all three is whether the grade meets the requirement that actually applies. Several schools reachable from the Corniche offer both A Levels and the Diploma, and their subject entry grades differ. A student short of one school's threshold may meet another's, and a place secured in September is often worth more than a better grade in January.

sections.heading: The IB repair routes, and why no dates appear here
paragraphs: The Diploma has its own repair structure and it runs through the school rather than directly. An enquiry upon results asks for a review of marking on a specific component. A retake in a later session allows a subject to be sat again. Acceptance is a legitimate third option and is more often correct than families assume in the week a result lands.

What this page will not do is publish the dates. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session date, results date or enquiry deadline in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and the secondary sources available disagree with one another. A wrong deadline on a tutoring page could cost a household an entire option, which is a worse outcome than an incomplete page.

Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative version: the results date for your cohort, the enquiry window and its grounds, the retake arrangements, and critically what happens to internal assessment marks in a retake. That last point varies by arrangement and changes the arithmetic of a retake considerably, because redoing an internal component is a different undertaking from resitting a paper.

The practical advice for a Corniche household is therefore procedural rather than informational. In the spring, email the coordinator and ask three questions: when results are released for this cohort, what the enquiry window and grounds are, and what a retake would involve for a named subject. Write the answers down. In August you will be glad you did not have to find them in a hurry.

sections.heading: What an enquiry about results actually is
paragraphs: Families often hear enquiry about results as appeal, and the mismatch causes disappointment. It is a review of whether the marking and the clerical process were correct, submitted by the school within a board deadline on defined grounds. It is not an opportunity to argue that the student is better than the grade suggests, and it is not a second marking from scratch in most circumstances.

The circumstances where it is genuinely worth pursuing are narrow and identifiable. A grade sitting one or two marks below a boundary. A paper the student felt went noticeably better than the result implies. A subject where the marking is comparatively objective, which favours mathematics and the quantitative sciences over extended-essay subjects. Where two or three of those apply, the case is worth putting to the school.

There is a cost dimension schools will explain and families should ask about early, because it varies by board, by type of review and by whether the request is made for a cohort or an individual. Ask what the school's own policy is, what the board charges, and whether the charge is refunded if the grade changes. Those are reasonable questions and they are rarely volunteered.

The thing to avoid is treating an enquiry as the default response to disappointment. It consumes the days immediately after results, which are also the days in which post-16 or university options need settling, and the chance of a change is modest unless the specific circumstances above apply. A clear-eyed conversation with the school in the first forty-eight hours usually settles it.

sections.heading: What a resit actually costs in time
paragraphs: Resit decisions are usually made on hope rather than arithmetic, and the arithmetic is straightforward enough to do in half an hour. A resit costs a defined number of weeks of a student's time, during which they are almost always also starting a new course. That double load is the real cost, and it is not reflected in any fee.

A November IGCSE resit gives roughly twelve usable weeks once the spring break, study leave and travel are subtracted, and those weeks run alongside the first term of a post-16 course. For mathematics that is often enough, because the content is taught and the gap is technique. For a content-heavy subject it usually is not, and attempting it can damage the new course as well as failing to fix the old grade.

A June retake gives a full year but costs a year of attention in a subject the student has moved past, which has its own motivational problem. A Diploma retake sits in a later session and may require an internal component again depending on the arrangement, which can double the work involved. Establish that with the coordinator before deciding.

Use it with the original script in front of you, because the script tells you whether the losses were procedural or content-based, and that single distinction is the best available predictor of whether a resit will work. sections.heading: Equivalency after results, and the subject count that catches families out
paragraphs: Once results are in, the paperwork question for families planning on a UAE university is certificate equivalency, which the Ministry of Education administers. On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail most often got wrong is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. At least one competitor ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. For a household deciding whether a resit is necessary, getting that right can remove the question entirely.

For the American track the requirements are different: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. For the IB track, no points threshold for equivalency has been read on a Ministry source, so this page publishes none; an invented figure would be worse than nothing.

Equivalency is a Ministry process rather than something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own site or with the attestation authority before acting on any version of it, including this one, and treat a provider claiming to secure equivalency for you as a reason for caution rather than confidence.

sections.heading: Decide the triggers in March, not in August
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a two-system household can do is agree in advance what each result would trigger. Which grade would prompt an enquiry request. Which would prompt a resit, and in which subject. Which would simply be accepted. Written down in March, those answers turn a stressful August week into an administrative one.

The reason this works is that the windows are short and the decisions are not. An enquiry has a board deadline measured in days or a few weeks. A November entry has to be made in time for the series. Meanwhile the same week contains post-16 or university decisions that cannot wait. A household making all of that up in forty-eight hours will make at least one choice it regrets.

The conversation also exposes the question that most often resolves everything: what requirement actually applies. Families frequently hold a target grade that is higher than the one the course they want needs. Checking the stated entry requirement for each option, for each child, before results arrive, routinely removes the resit question entirely and saves a whole term of work.

A tutor's role in this is narrow and useful. Read the previous mock or the original script, say honestly whether a resit would be likely to move the grade, and give an estimate of the weeks required. That is a judgement about evidence rather than a promise, and no provider can guarantee a grade or an improvement, including us.

On the Corniche that scheduling saving is larger than elsewhere, because tower logistics mean every visit carries a parking, reception and lift cost, and two visits on one evening carry it twice. Consecutive online slots remove it entirely.

Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above.

In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. None of these figures is our price list. They are the market, published with attribution so that any quote, including ours, can be measured against something checkable.

What we will not claim: no provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including us. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, we hold no ADEK, MoHRE, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, and there is no Abu Dhabi office. faqs.question: Can one IB IGCSE tutor near me in the Corniche handle both children after results?
faqs.answer: For a decision session, sometimes; for the teaching that follows, rarely. The decision work is procedural and transfers: reading a script, listing the options with their deadlines, checking the requirement that actually applies. The teaching does not transfer, because IGCSE and Diploma courses differ in content, component structure and what the questions ask for. faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one to one over live video. For a two-system household that is a genuine advantage: two specialists can take consecutive slots on one evening, which commits one night rather than three, and because nobody travels between them neither hour is shortened by parking or a lift wait.

faqs.question: When do the two sets of results arrive in a two-system household?
faqs.answer: Within a few weeks of each other. On the IGCSE side the dates are published: Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. On the IB side results arrive earlier in the summer, and the date for your child's cohort comes from the school's Diploma coordinator rather than from this page, because no IB date here has been verified.

faqs.answer: Because it has not been verified. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session date, results date or enquiry deadline in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and the secondary sources available disagree with one another. A wrong deadline on a tutoring page could cost a household an entire option, which is a worse outcome than an incomplete page. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative version.

faqs.question: Is an IGCSE November resit worth doing?
faqs.answer: It depends what the losses were. November gives roughly twelve usable weeks once breaks and travel are subtracted, and those weeks run alongside the first term of a post-16 course. For mathematics and the procedural sciences that is often enough, because the content is already taught and the gap is technique. For content-heavy subjects it usually is not, and attempting it can damage the new course as well as failing to fix the grade.

faqs.question: What exactly is an enquiry about results?
faqs.answer: A review of whether the marking and clerical process were correct, submitted by the school within a board deadline on defined grounds. It is not an appeal about the student's ability and it is not a fresh marking from scratch in most circumstances. It is worth pursuing where a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary on a paper the student felt went well, and it favours objectively marked subjects over extended-writing ones.

faqs.question: Does an enquiry cost anything, and is it refunded?
faqs.answer: That varies by board, by type of review, and by whether the school requests it for a cohort or an individual, so ask the school three questions: what the board charges, what the school's own policy is, and whether the charge is refunded if the grade changes. Those are reasonable questions and they are almost never volunteered. Ask them in the first forty-eight hours after results, because the window is short.

faqs.question: Which subjects resit well and which do not?
faqs.answer: Procedural subjects resit well. Mathematics is the clearest case: content already taught, technique the usual gap, and technique improves quickly with timed practice. Physics and Chemistry resit well where the losses were units, rearrangement or data handling. Biology resits least well because the specification is large and three months rarely rebuilds unseen content. The original script tells you which category you are in far better than the grade does.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma retake require the internal assessment again?
faqs.answer: It depends on the arrangement, and this is the single most important thing to establish before deciding, because redoing an internal component is a very different undertaking from resitting a paper. Ask the Diploma coordinator directly for a named subject rather than assuming either answer. The reply changes the time cost of a retake substantially and therefore changes whether the retake is a reasonable idea at all.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a UAE university actually need?
faqs.answer: On the published British-track rule, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one site ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule, and the difference can remove a resit question entirely.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points figure for equivalency we should plan around?
faqs.answer: Not one this page will publish, because no IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on a Ministry of Education source. The British-track numbers are sourced and quotable; the IB figure is not, and publishing an unverified number on a page a family might act on would be worse than publishing nothing. Equivalency is a Ministry process rather than something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees, so verify it directly with the Ministry.

faqs.answer: Three triggers per child, written down in March. Which grade would prompt an enquiry request. Which would prompt a resit, and in which subject. Which would simply be accepted. The windows after results are measured in days, and the same week contains post-16 or university decisions that cannot wait. faqs.answer: By reading the requirement that applies rather than the target you had in mind. Several schools reachable from the Corniche offer both A Levels and the Diploma, and their subject entry grades differ, so a student short of one school's threshold may meet another's. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a resit build alongside a new course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the common case, but the double load has to be acknowledged rather than ignored. Two sessions a week built entirely from the original script, working on conversion rather than coverage, is what fits alongside a first post-16 term. If the student is also starting Diploma Internal Assessments, we would usually recommend one subject rather than two, because the limiting resource is their hours rather than your budget.

intro.heading: Two curricula, one term, one evening
paragraphs: The phrase "near me" is doing something specific in this search. It is shorthand for a practical worry: can anybody competent actually reach us, and will the logistics work? Families at Eastern Mangroves ask it more often than most, because this is a compact residential pocket on the channel with no school inside it, and the children living here are bussed in four different directions. The honest answer is that proximity stopped being the binding constraint once lessons moved to video, and that the binding constraint is now the calendar.

Households here frequently run two examination systems at once. An older child in the Diploma, with the Exploration, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and six subjects to carry, sitting the May session. A younger one in Year 10 or 11 on Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, heading for a June paper with a mock in the winter. Both children are under pressure in the same weeks, from different directions, and the family has one evening schedule to fit it all into.

That collision is predictable and therefore plannable, which is the whole premise of this page. The Diploma pressure peaks when internal deadlines for coursework components land, typically clustered in the middle of the second year. The IGCSE pressure peaks around the mock window and again in the final weeks before study leave. Those peaks do not coincide exactly, which means a family that maps them in advance can usually stagger its spending rather than paying for two intensive blocks in the same month.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is something we run only in India. For a two-curriculum household that model is not a compromise, it is the thing that makes the arrangement possible: two children can be taught at 4.30pm and 6pm on the same evening by two different specialists, with no travel for anybody and no shared tutor pretending to cover both programmes.

What follows is the planning material rather than the sales pitch. A term-by-term map of what each programme demands and when. What an eight-week block can realistically achieve at each stage of each course. The questions to ask a tutor to establish within five minutes whether they know the syllabus they claim to teach. And the regulatory facts for Abu Dhabi, including the permit position, stated accurately rather than vaguely.

A note on how this page is organised, because it is not organised like the others competing for the same phrase. There is no section arguing that tutoring is valuable and no list of adjectives about our tutors. What there is instead is a calendar you can put next to your own school calendars, a table of what a block of sessions can and cannot do at each stage, and the questions that separate a specialist from a pleasant generalist in the first five minutes of a trial lesson. If you read only one part, read the calendar.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, a fixed specification per subject, no coursework on most mainstream boards, and a grade decided entirely by written papers. The tier on the entry sets a ceiling that no amount of revision lifts. Year 10 is content delivery; Year 11 is practice, technique and the mock that fixes a predicted grade. Everything in this programme is recoverable by practice, which is why it responds quickly to a focused block.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. programmes.countryNote: Option blocks at Abu Dhabi Diploma schools frequently constrain the subject combination a student wanted, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. programmes.name: Diploma Year 2

Strong IGCSE grades do not guarantee a comfortable DP1, because the Diploma asks for independent reading, extended writing and sustained coursework rather than examination recall. abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-east.subjectsIntro: Requests from two-curriculum households cluster in the subjects where both children need help at once, usually mathematics and the sciences. The list below names the component that generates the request in each case.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework, with tiering that caps the grade. Marks are lost in non-calculator arithmetic, in method lines never written down, and in the final parts of multi-part questions where two topics are combined deliberately.

subjects.name: Diploma Mathematics AA and AI
subjects.description: Four distinct routes across two courses and two levels. Paper 3 at Higher Level carries twenty per cent and is the component students discover late. The Exploration carries another twenty and is marked out of twenty across five criteria.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences
subjects.description: Chemistry, Physics and Biology with Core and Extended tiers. Cambridge candidates sitting the practical-skills paper need to write a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat, which is a writing skill rather than a laboratory one.

subjects.name: Diploma Sciences
subjects.description: Content volume plus an internally assessed investigation. The common failure is a student who understands the science and cannot structure a data analysis or evaluate a method, which costs marks in both the paper and the coursework.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language
subjects.description: Two distinct qualifications with different mark schemes and different recognition. Directed writing and composition carry the paper, and the marks go on planning rather than on vocabulary.

subjects.name: Diploma English A and B
subjects.description: Literature and language routes with oral components assessed internally. Students lose marks by describing a text rather than analysing how it works, and the oral is often the least rehearsed component in the whole Diploma.

subjects.name: Diploma core: TOK, EE and CAS
subjects.description: The core carries points and can cost a diploma. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are both coachable in the legitimate sense: the thinking is taught and questioned, and the student writes every word themselves.

subjects.name: Humanities across both systems
subjects.description: Business, Economics, History and Geography. The transferable skill is argument structure under time pressure, and it is the single most portable thing a tutor can teach a household running both curricula.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum under federal rules, taught in separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students. These subjects sit outside the five the Ministry of Education counts for British-track equivalency.

subjects.name: Bridging work between the systems
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, extended writing stamina and research-question design. A short summer block that removes most of the autumn shock, bought by far fewer families than need it.

sections.heading: What "near me" actually buys, and what it costs you
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor near me in Eastern Mangroves is a reasonable instinct and a poor filter. The instinct is about reliability: somebody local will turn up, will understand the school, will be reachable. The filter is the problem, because on this part of the island it reduces the available pool to whoever happens to live within a short drive, at the exact hour your child is free, for the specific course your child takes. For a Diploma Higher Level subject that intersection is frequently empty.

IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. What that removes is a person in the room, and it would be dishonest to pretend some families do not want that. What it adds is the ability to choose a tutor by programme, course and component rather than by driving distance, and the ability to run two children's sessions on the same evening without anyone in a car.

The local knowledge worry is worth answering directly rather than dismissing. A tutor who has never heard of ADEK, cannot say which series a UAE candidate sits, and does not know that Cambridge runs its February and March series for India only is not a good match for an Abu Dhabi family, wherever they live. That knowledge is testable in five minutes, and the section below gives you the questions. Proximity is a poor proxy for it; several pages ranking for this search are run from outside the country with a foreign phone number as the contact route.

So the useful substitution is this: stop asking who is near, and start asking who teaches this course, at this level, at the hour my child is actually home. That question has good answers for a family on the mangrove channel, and the rest of this page is about using them well.

sections.heading: Two calendars in one household, month by month
paragraphs: The reason a two-curriculum household feels permanently behind is that it is being squeezed from two directions on a staggered schedule. Mapping that squeeze is the single most useful planning exercise available, and it takes one sitting with both children's school calendars open.

The Diploma year runs on internal deadlines set by the school rather than by the board: coursework drafts, the Extended Essay milestones, Theory of Knowledge components, and the mock examinations. Those cluster in the middle of the second year and they are non-negotiable, because a missed internal deadline becomes a problem with the school before it becomes a problem with the board. The IGCSE year runs on a different rhythm: entries submitted months ahead, a mock around the winter break that fixes a predicted grade, then study leave and the June papers, with November available as a resit route.

The table below sets the two side by side as a planning skeleton rather than as dates, which is deliberate: dates get revised and a page that restates them goes stale without anyone touching it. Use it with your own schools' calendars. The pattern most families find is that there are two genuinely hard months and three relatively quiet ones, and that tutoring bought in the quiet months costs less and achieves more than tutoring bought in the hard ones.

One caution worth repeating. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones with its own version of the timetable, states that using the correct version is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Confirm the zone with your school rather than working from a date found online.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can do, by stage
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block families in this emirate most commonly buy, and its usefulness varies enormously by where the student is. A page that implies the same block does the same work for a Year 10 student and a DP2 student in March is not helping anybody plan.

The honest version is a range. For a Year 10 student, eight weeks of weekly sessions can genuinely teach content and rebuild a topic from the ground up, because there is a whole year still ahead in which the gain compounds. For a Year 11 student before the mock, it can change technique and recover marks the student can already earn. For a DP2 student in the spring, it can sequence the remaining work, rehearse Paper 3 and clear a coursework bottleneck — but it cannot teach a Higher Level option that was never covered.

Buying the wrong eight weeks is the commonest expensive mistake in this market, and it goes in both directions. Families buy a term of general support in Year 9 when three sessions on algebraic fluency would have done, and then buy three sessions in April of DP2 when a term in September was the real need. The corrective is to decide what the block is for before buying it, in writing, with a stated end date.

sections.heading: Six questions that test whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Parents are routinely told to check qualifications, and qualifications turn out to be a weak signal. A mathematics degree says nothing about whether somebody has taught Cambridge 0580 or Diploma Applications and Interpretation. What does signal competence is specificity, and specificity is testable in a few minutes by anyone, including a parent with no background in the subject.

Ask six things. Which syllabus code does my child's school enter for this subject? What are the papers and what is each one worth? Which series will my child sit, and which series does this board not run in the UAE? What are the assessment criteria for the coursework component, and how many marks does each carry? Where do students most often lose marks in this subject? And what will you refuse to do with my child's coursework?

The answers sort people quickly. A specialist names codes and weightings without hesitating, and answers the series question correctly — Cambridge runs its February and March sitting for India only, so a UAE candidate sits June and November. A generalist talks about building confidence and covering the basics. Neither answer is dishonest; they describe different products, and knowing which one you are buying is the point of asking.

The sixth question is the most revealing. A tutor who says they will not write any part of the coursework, will not rewrite the student's sentences, and will give feedback only on work the student has produced is describing the only defensible position under board rules. A tutor who is vague about it, or who offers to help get it finished, is a risk you are passing on to your child.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and what nobody should claim
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools, including every school a family here is likely to use, sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Across the country the map is: KHDA in Dubai, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and by a different body. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount is inventing it.

This emirate adds one rule a family should know. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. The arrangement that looks most convenient — your child's own teacher, paid, in the evening — is the one to avoid, and it is poor practice besides, since the person marking the work should not also be paid to prepare it.

Finally, what nobody should claim. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and claims none. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We also do not name any school as a client or partner, do not publish ratings we cannot evidence, and do not quote statistics without the number, the date and the method behind them.

sections.heading: Coursework, honesty and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Both systems contain work a student submits rather than sits, and the Diploma contains a great deal of it: the Exploration or its subject equivalent, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and internally assessed components in the sciences and languages. This is where the market in this region contains genuinely dangerous providers, including one which sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

The defensible boundary is specific and easy to state. A tutor may teach the skill the component assesses, explain the published criteria and what their command words mean, question a student about their own reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor does not write any part of the work, does not rewrite the student's sentences into better prose, and does not supply content for submission. We set that out before coursework support begins rather than when a deadline is close.

The same restraint applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. They belong to the boards, they are published on the boards' own sites, and the right thing to do is cite and link them. A provider offering a library of copied mark schemes is offering a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

There is a positive version of this, and it is worth saying. The legitimate coursework help is the valuable kind. Testing whether a research question can actually carry an Extended Essay, or whether an investigation has enough depth for the top criterion band, is the intervention that changes a grade — and it happens weeks before writing starts, which is exactly when families do not think to ask for it.

sections.heading: What a two-curriculum household should actually spend
paragraphs: Published market figures, read in October 2026, frame the decision. Qualified online subject tutors advertise from around AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270 and premium examiner-led provision advertised as high as AED 650. Entry-level online sessions are advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65. In-home visits including travel run from about AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Emirates rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350.

For a household with two children, the arithmetic gets uncomfortable quickly. Two weekly specialist hours across a term is a serious commitment at those rates, which is exactly why staggering matters. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Advertised packages in this market have included AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

The planning principle that saves the most money is simple: buy for the child whose deadline is nearest, finish that block, then buy for the other. Two staggered eight-week blocks across a term cost the same as one simultaneous pair and produce more, because each child gets a tutor's full attention in the weeks when the work matters and neither family evening carries two sessions plus homework.

IB Gram publishes no tariff here. Rates depend on programme, level, scarcity and session length and are quoted after a free trial lesson for each child. Every figure above belongs to the provider or survey named beside it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both my Diploma child and my Year 11 child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, in a shared subject at the lower end of the Diploma, but it is usually a false economy. The mark schemes, command terms and assessment structures are different enough that a tutor strong in one system tends to default to its habits in the other. The better arrangement in a household like yours is two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, which costs no more in travel because there is none, and gives each child somebody who marks to their own board.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB or IGCSE specialist available near Eastern Mangroves?
faqs.answer: If the filter is driving distance, the pool is small and gets smaller once you add a specific course, level and hour. If the filter is the course itself, the pool is large. IB Gram teaches over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the practical answer is that a specialist is available for most courses at most sensible hours. Test their knowledge instead of their postcode: ask for the syllabus code, the paper weightings and which series your child sits.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the Abu Dhabi school year are the expensive ones for a two-curriculum family?
faqs.answer: The weeks where the Diploma child's internal coursework deadlines overlap with the IGCSE child's mock preparation, which for most schools means the period around the winter break and the fortnight after it. That is when families buy two intensive blocks at once and spend the most for the least. Mapping both school calendars in the autumn and staggering the blocks typically halves the simultaneous load without reducing the total number of sessions bought.

faqs.question: Does my child in Abu Dhabi sit the Cambridge February series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only, so a candidate at a UAE centre sits the June series, with November available as a resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. This matters because several tutoring pages aimed at Gulf families quote the Indian dates, and an entry deadline acted on in the wrong country is a serious error. Confirm the paper dates with your school's examinations officer and the official timetable for your centre's zone.

faqs.question: How do I plan the summer between Year 11 and DP1?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions, spread across the break, on three things: algebraic fluency, extended writing stamina and what a research question looks like. Strong IGCSE grades do not guarantee a comfortable DP1, because the Diploma asks for independent reading and sustained coursework rather than examination recall. Where the student is also changing school, add a mapping session against the receiving school's DP1 expectations. It is the cheapest useful block in the entire two-year Diploma and very few families buy it.

faqs.question: What should a DP2 student do if three subjects are in trouble at once?
faqs.answer: Triage, not heroism. Identify which subjects sit nearest a grade boundary, which have coursework still outstanding, and which contribute most to the points total being targeted. Then fund the one or two where movement is plausible and deliberately leave the third alone for now. Spreading a limited number of sessions across three subjects in the spring of DP2 reliably produces no visible change anywhere. A tutor who agrees to cover all three without discussing priority is not planning, they are accepting an order.

faqs.question: How late can we leave the Extended Essay before it becomes a real problem?
faqs.answer: The deadline that matters is the school's internal one, not the board's, and schools in this emirate set them earlier than students expect. The genuinely valuable intervention happens before any writing: testing whether the research question can carry four thousand words of argument and whether the sources exist. A question that cannot do that caps the essay no matter how well it is written. Once a draft is in progress the help available is feedback on the student's own work, which is worth much less than the earlier conversation.

faqs.question: Can both children be taught on the same evening without a second commute?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most households at Eastern Mangroves that is the arrangement that actually survives a term. Two consecutive slots, two different specialists, nobody travelling. The sequencing usually follows arrival times: the child on the short Al Mushrif or Al Bateen run takes the earlier slot, and the child crossing the bridge from Saadiyat or coming up the highway takes the later one. Fixing the slots after you know real arrival times, rather than before, is what stops the weekly renegotiation.

faqs.question: Should an ADEK inspection band change which subject we buy tutoring for?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. The rating judges a school, and a highly rated school can still have a weak department while a lower-rated one can have an outstanding one. The useful reading is the subject-level commentary inside the report, where you can see whether the problem you are noticing at home was visible to inspectors too. That is a far better basis for deciding whether to buy tutoring, and for which subject, than the headline band on the front page.

faqs.question: Are the tutors teaching Eastern Mangroves students based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Some are and some are not, and we tell you which before the trial lesson rather than after. For common subjects at common hours a UAE-based match is usually available. For scarce Higher Level subjects, or for an unusual time slot, the specialist may be elsewhere, teaching in your time zone. We state the tutor's location up front because concealing it is a trust failure, and because two pages competing for this search route UAE parents to foreign phone numbers without mentioning where anyone is.

faqs.question: Do my children have to study Arabic alongside the IB or IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under the federal position, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Schools run separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students, with different expectations and languages of instruction. These subjects also sit outside the five that the Ministry of Education counts for British-track equivalency, which surprises most families the first time they read the requirement.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a household with two children commit to?
faqs.answer: Start with one per child, not two, and review after four weeks against marked work. The temptation in a pressured term is to buy more hours, and the effect is usually to crowd out the independent practice that converts teaching into marks. Where one child genuinely needs two sessions, the right move is often to pause the other child's block rather than to run four sessions a week. Staggering across the term is cheaper and more effective than running everything at once.

faqs.question: What happens if the specialist we need has no slot at our hour?
faqs.answer: You hear it immediately, with three options rather than a vague promise. A different time with the right specialist, which is usually the correct answer. A wait with an actual date attached, if the subject is scarce. Or a tutor based outside the UAE, with their location and working hours stated before the trial lesson. Nobody is placed into a course they do not teach to fill a slot, because a mismatched tutor in a Higher Level subject costs a family weeks they cannot get back.

faqs.question: How will we know after a month that both blocks are worth continuing?
faqs.answer: Each block should produce its own evidence, reviewed separately. For the IGCSE child, a second timed paper marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic. For the Diploma child, a specific deliverable: a coursework section completed to criteria, or a Paper 3 attempt that shows recovery from an early error. You should also hear each child name their own weakest area without prompting. Where one block shows that and the other does not, only one should continue.

intro.heading: Every quote has three things inside it
paragraphs: A tutoring rate is not one price. It is at least three components bundled into a single number: the teaching hour itself, whatever happens outside the hour, and travel. Providers quote the total and almost never break it down, which is why two quotes that look twenty per cent apart can be buying entirely different things. Learning to decompose a quote takes one conversation and is the most useful consumer skill available in this market.

Hudayriyat Island makes the travel component unusually visible. It is a recently developed island off the western side of Abu Dhabi, reached by bridge, with leisure and residential districts and no school or tuition centre on it. Every student here travels, mostly across to Al Bateen and Al Mushrif, and any visiting tutor is making a bridge crossing in both directions for a single lesson. That is a real cost and it sits inside whatever rate you are quoted, undeclared.

The second component — what happens outside the hour — is the one that decides whether the money does anything. Written work set with an instruction about what to show, that work returned marked against the published scheme rather than ticked, an error log kept across papers, and a diagnosis in writing. None of that is visible in a rate, all of it is askable in advance, and in our experience the presence or absence of it explains more variation in outcome than the price does.

Published rate information in this market is also thinner and less reliable than it appears, which is worth knowing before comparing numbers. Of six researched competitor pages in this cluster, three publish no price at all — one asks the price in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it — and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So a parent comparing quotes is often comparing a real figure with an absence.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits on Hudayriyat Island or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. From an island with bridge access and no local provision, the cost case for that is strong and the choice case is stronger: requiring a specialist in a given course and level to also cross the bridge at five in the afternoon frequently leaves nobody at all.

What follows is the pricing material. A quoted rate decomposed, with the question that exposes each component. The travel premium worked through for bridge access. programmes.description: Terminal written papers across eight or nine subjects, tiered by board, with coursework minimal or absent in most. The spend tends to be steady and the pressure terminal, which makes a fixed weekly arrangement a reasonable fit where one is genuinely needed.
programmes.countryNote: The rationing problem is at its sharpest here because of the number of subjects. The cheapest effective spend in the IGCSE years is early: work in Year 9 or early Year 10 can change which tier a school enters a student for, and the tier sets the grade ceiling.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work in every subject with published criteria and word limits, which makes the spend lumpy rather than even and clusters it around school deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: The best value purchase in the Diploma is usually a core component rather than a subject. Theory of Knowledge carries twenty marks across two assessments with word limits of sixteen hundred and nine hundred and fifty words, and almost no household budgets for it.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Staged assessment across AS and A2, narrower subject choice, greater depth per subject. Fewer subjects to fund than IGCSE and more depth in each, which usually means fewer and longer arrangements rather than more of them.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE subjects at grade E or grade 3 or better. Verify current requirements officially.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-huda.subjectsIntro: These notes are about what a pound of effort returns in each subject, which is what a household comparing quotes across subjects actually needs to weigh.

subjects.name: Mathematics, IGCSE and Diploma
subjects.description: The clearest value across both systems, because faults are specific and diagnosable. Higher Level Diploma Paper 3 is worth a fifth of the grade in a single hour and is the least practised component anywhere in the programme.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Good value where the hour produces marked written answers. The Diploma investigation is marked on the design of the investigation rather than on how tidy the results are, which is a correctable misunderstanding worth a session on its own.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Good value with a caveat that saves money: a physics difficulty is often an algebra difficulty, and a tutor who establishes that first avoids a term spent teaching the wrong subject at the wrong rate.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Value is a function of method, not of price. The subject responds to written answers marked against the scheme and barely at all to explanation, so a knowledgeable tutor who does not mark represents poor value at any rate.

subjects.name: English, First Language and Language A
subjects.description: High value per hour where feedback is on the student's own writing. The Diploma's Individual Oral is a bounded, trainable task that students almost never rehearse under conditions, which makes it unusually cheap to improve.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Good value because the faults are structural: evaluation missing, diagrams imprecise, commentaries summarising an article rather than applying a theory. A handful of sessions produces visible change in marked work.

subjects.name: The science practical component
subjects.description: Strong value and rarely bought, because families do not realise practical skills are examined in writing. Method descriptions, graph scales and error questions respond to four marked attempts.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The best value component in the Diploma and the least purchased. Twenty marks against published instruments with strict word limits, and very little structured teaching on how the instrument is applied.

subjects.name: Extended Essay support
subjects.description: Thirty-four marks with critical thinking alone worth twelve. Best bought at the research question and first draft stages; money spent in the final week mostly rearranges an argument that is already fixed.

subjects.name: A subject already at the top of its range
subjects.description: No value at any rate, and we say so. The question worth asking any provider is which subject they would refuse, because the answer reveals how they make decisions about somebody else's money.

sections.heading: Decomposing a quoted rate
paragraphs: The first thing to do with any quote is to ask what is inside it, because the single number conceals three separable components and the proportions differ wildly between providers. The teaching hour. Whatever happens outside the hour. And travel, where applicable, which from Hudayriyat Island is never zero for a visiting arrangement.

The teaching hour is the part everybody assumes they are buying and the part that varies least. A competent subject teacher delivering an hour is roughly a comparable thing across the middle of the market. What differs enormously is the second component — marking, diagnosis, logging, review — which is invisible in a rate and decisive in an outcome. At the budget end it is absent by necessity, because nobody paid AED 45 to 150 an hour is being paid for time outside the session.

The third component is travel. Published in-home rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online on agency rate pages, all read in October 2026. From an island reached by bridge, the gap between those bands is largely a crossing in each direction plus the risk that it goes badly.

The table gives the question that exposes each component. None is awkward, all are factual, and asking them before paying is considerably cheaper than discovering the answers afterwards. A provider who answers all four plainly is describing a service. One who treats them as distrust is describing something they would rather you did not look at closely.
