sections.heading: The travel premium, worked through for bridge access
paragraphs: Hudayriyat Island is reached by bridge from the western side of Abu Dhabi island, and a visiting tutor is therefore making two crossings and two approach drives for a single hour of teaching. That is a straightforward cost and it has to be recovered somewhere: either in the rate, in the length of the session, or in the tutor accepting a lower effective hourly return, which they will not do indefinitely.

Decompose it against the published figures. If a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a visiting tutor at AED 180 to 500, the difference at comparable teaching quality is the journey. For a bridge crossing with an afternoon approach, the loading will sit toward the upper part of that range rather than the lower, because the tutor is pricing unpaid time as well as fuel.

What the premium buys is physical presence in the room, and that genuinely matters for some students: younger ones, students who need supervision rather than teaching, and students for whom a screen is itself an obstacle. We say that plainly, because a page which pretends one format suits every child is not useful to anybody. What the premium does not buy is better teaching, better marking or a better match.

What it costs, beyond money, is choice — and on this island that is the decisive point. Take the set of people who can teach a given Diploma course at Higher Level or a given IGCSE specification at Extended tier. Intersect it with the set willing to cross the bridge at five in the afternoon. Intersect that with the set free on the specific weekday your household can hold. The result is frequently empty, and a family facing an empty set substitutes a generalist who is available. A generalist at specialist prices is the worst transaction in this market.

sections.heading: Where the published AED figures come from
paragraphs: Comparing rates assumes there are rates to compare, and in this market that assumption is shakier than it looks. Of six competitor pages examined in this cluster, three publish no price at all. One of those lists the price among its own frequently asked questions and then does not answer it. Two of the three that do publish quote in US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in, so a parent has to convert before comparing and is converting somebody else's undated figure.

That leaves a small number of usable sources, and it is worth knowing what each one is. Cost-estimate survey sites compile ranges across providers and publish them as market rates; the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table is the one most often cited and is the source for most of the banded figures on this page. Agency rate pages publish their own prices, which are real but self-interested and specific to one provider's model. Platform rate cards publish entry-level figures that often describe a different product from the one a family ends up buying. Marketplace listings vary tutor by tutor and frequently in other currencies.

The limitation common to all of them is dating. A rate published two years ago and never revised is still sitting on a page being read today, and one researched competitor's comparison panel was twenty-one months out of date when examined. Any figure worth using carries the date it was read, which is why every band on this page says October 2026. A number without a date is not evidence; it is decoration.

The practical use of the table is as a sanity check rather than a guide. If a quote sits far outside the published bands in either direction, ask why. Far above usually means a journey, a premium positioning or both; far below usually means the marking is absent. Neither is disqualifying and both are worth knowing before the first invoice.

sections.heading: A new community with no school and no centre
paragraphs: Hudayriyat Island is a recently developed part of the emirate, with leisure, sporting and residential districts and no school or tuition centre on the island itself. For a family thinking about education costs, that has three consequences and all of them are financial.

The first is that every student travels, so a school choice is also a daily journey and the journey is paid for in study hours as well as fuel. A student crossing the bridge to Al Bateen or Al Mushrif each way has materially less usable study time than one who walks to school, and that matters for which tuition purchases are realistic. A Higher Level Diploma subject is the least tolerant of a thin practice schedule.

The second is that there is no local provider pool. A tuition centre serves a catchment and no centre serves this island; an independent tutor builds a local client base and there is not yet a local base to build. So the in-person options are people travelling in, at a premium, from a limited set of those willing to do it. That is simply the state of a new community and it will change as the island develops.

The third is that the free options still exist and are unaffected by any of this. The school's own intervention or support class is at the school, which the student attends anyway, and it is free, taught by somebody who knows the specification and has seen the work. Reading three published mark schemes costs nothing. Twenty minutes a day of retrieval practice — writing an answer on an old topic without notes, then marking it against the scheme — costs nothing and outperforms the rereading most students do. On an island with no local provision those three are the first things to exhaust, not the last.

sections.heading: The cost of a wasted first month
paragraphs: Families budget for tuition and almost never budget for a bad start, which is the most common single loss in this market. A month spent with the wrong match, the wrong format or the wrong diagnosis costs the fees plus something considerably more expensive, and the arithmetic is worth seeing.

Take a mid-market weekly arrangement. On published monthly estimates of roughly AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly hour, a wasted month is that figure in cash. It is also four sessions of a student's limited evening capacity, a month of written practice that did not happen or happened unmarked, and — most expensively — a month closer to a fixed deadline. In an examination year, where the entry deadline and the series are immovable, a month is a measurable fraction of the time available, and no refund recovers it.

There is a further cost that does not appear on any invoice. A family that endures a poor arrangement for a term concludes that tutoring does not work. That is a reasonable conclusion from their evidence and a wrong general one, and it often means the student receives no further support at all. The damage of a bad first month therefore extends beyond the month.

All of which argues for the cheap protections rather than the expensive ones. A free trial lesson tests the match and the format before any commitment. A written diagnosis in week one makes the plan falsifiable. A review date with a stated measure means the arrangement fails visibly in week three or four rather than invisibly in week ten. And a stated replacement policy means a wrong match can be corrected without an argument. The table puts the figures against the weeks.

sections.heading: What to put in writing before paying
paragraphs: Almost nothing in this market is written down, and almost everything that matters could be. A short written exchange before the first invoice prevents most of the disputes and all of the ambiguity, and no legitimate provider should object to any of it.

Six items cover it. Whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, and the length of a lesson. Whether marking of written work between sessions is included or charged separately. What notice is required to cancel a session, on both sides, and what happens to a session cancelled late. Whether the first payment commits you to a block, and whether anything renews automatically. What happens if the match is wrong and a replacement is needed. And the date and measure of the first review.

Two further items are specific to this market and worth adding. The conditions attached to any free trial should appear on the same screen as the offer: ours is one lesson, no card required, no block commitment afterwards and nothing renewing, and that is the whole of it. And the data question, because tuition involves information about a minor — what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted, with a privacy link available. The UAE has a federal personal data protection law, and a form gathering a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose is a problem regardless of intent.

None of this requires a contract or a lawyer. A message with six numbered questions and the answers kept is sufficient, and it changes the dynamic: a provider who has written down what they will deliver is accountable to it, and a parent who has the answers can tell at the review whether it happened. The absence of any of this is the single clearest signal that an arrangement is being sold on reassurance rather than on substance.

sections.heading: The three purchases worth making at any budget
paragraphs: Whatever a household can spend, three purchases return more than their cost almost regardless of the student, and they are rarely the ones families buy first. Each is bounded, each is cheap relative to a term, and each addresses something the school is unlikely to cover in depth.

The first is a diagnosis. One session in which a specialist reads the last marked script against the published scheme and categorises every lost mark — content never learned, method misapplied, notation or calculator, command word misread, exact form not given, ran out of time — produces a plan that a family can act on with or without further tuition. Many families then find the plan is executable at home for free, and we would rather that than sell a term against a guess.

The second is a mark scheme session. Published schemes are free on the boards' own sites and almost no student has read one. One or two sessions reading real schemes alongside the student's own script, identifying the credit that was available and unclaimed, changes the shape of their written answers permanently. It is the single cheapest intervention with a durable effect that we know of in this subject area.

The third depends on the programme. For a Diploma student it is Theory of Knowledge, which carries twenty marks across two assessments against published instruments with strict word limits and receives very little structured teaching. For an IGCSE science student it is the practical paper, where method writing, graph scales and error questions are examined in writing and almost nobody practises them. Both are three to five session blocks and both address marks nobody else is competing for.

sections.heading: The permit, our status and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Since this page is about pricing, the permit position matters: it is free, so no part of any rate should be attributed to it. The UAE private tuition work permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with the ministry's own service page listing no fee and a two working day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published and press reporting states that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a specific dirham figure quoted as the penalty is invention, and a useful test of whether a provider's other claims are sourced. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school.

An operation with premises needs its own permit from the emirate regulator; in Dubai that is an educational services permit for a training institute issued by KHDA, obtained through initial approval followed by permit and licence steps with annual renewal. IB Gram holds none because it has no premises: it is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, holding no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and it is not a registered examination centre.

On claims: we publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic, because stating one honestly requires the sample size, the date and the method alongside it, and because providers in this market display ratings that contradict each other on the same page. Every AED figure here is attributed and dated October 2026 and none is our price list. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind at any price, and no tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university outcome.

Elsewhere, ask for the conditions on the same screen as the offer, because an offer described as free with an undisclosed requirement attached is not free. intro.heading: What the search results are actually sorted by
paragraphs: A proximity search ranks by two things: how close somebody is, and what their reviews look like. Both are measurable, which is why they are used, and neither is correlated with the thing that decides whether tuition works. Nobody in the list is ranked by whether they have taught Cambridge 0580 Extended, supervised a Diploma exploration, or marked a script against a published mark scheme. Those facts exist and are easy to establish, and no search interface asks for them.

Hydra Village makes this unusually visible. It is a small gated villa community on the mainland side of Abu Dhabi, out towards Al Shamkha and Al Reef, with no school inside it and no tuition provision. A proximity search from here returns either very little or a list of people a long way away, which is at least honest. Families in the island communities get a longer list and the same underlying problem, dressed up as choice.

Reviews are the second signal and they deserve a specific warning, because this market is full of unverifiable ones. Several providers in the UAE publish star ratings and review counts that do not match each other on the same page, and at least one shows a figure in its structured data that differs from the number a visitor sees. A rating that cannot be traced to real, countable, attributable reviews is a marketing device rather than evidence, which is why IB Gram publishes none at all.

Delivery here, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Hydra Village or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. From a community like this one that is less a preference than arithmetic: the set of people who can teach a given Diploma course at Higher Level, intersected with the set willing to drive out here in the late afternoon, is frequently empty.

Because families in Hydra Village are often comparing schools as well as tutors — the community sits between several clusters and a school choice here determines an hour of every day — a substantial part of this page is about reading a school rather than reading a tutor. What an inspection band means. What it cannot tell you. The questions to put to an admissions office that a published rating will never answer. And what happens when a child transfers school or country mid-course, which is a common pattern in the Emirates and is handled badly almost everywhere.

Everything factual here is attributable or marked as something to confirm, and the figures quoted belong to published sources with their dates. No examination or results date for the IB appears, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one, and no grade boundary appears, because boundaries are set after each session and published afterwards.

sections.heading: The ranking signals, and a better question for each
paragraphs: A search result is a set of signals, and it is worth knowing which ones are doing the sorting. Distance, review score, review count, response speed and sometimes price. Each is cheap to compute and each is silent about the one thing that determines whether tuition works, which is whether this person has taught and marked your child's specification.

Distance is the clearest example. From Hydra Village it filters out almost everybody who can teach a Higher Level Diploma course, because the intersection of 'can teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level' and 'will drive out past Al Shamkha at five in the afternoon' is nearly empty. The filter is doing real work; it is simply removing the wrong people. A family that relaxes it and solves the time of day instead has a far larger choice set.

Review scores deserve more scepticism than they get in this market. Providers in the UAE publish ratings and review counts that contradict each other on the same page, and at least one publishes a figure in its structured data that differs from the one a visitor can see. Google's own structured-data policy takes a dim view of self-serving review markup. A rating that cannot be traced to real, countable, attributable reviews is a device, which is why we publish none and would rather be judged on a free trial lesson.

The table gives each signal with what it genuinely tells you, what it cannot, and the question to ask instead. None of the better questions requires any subject knowledge, and all of them can be asked in a single message before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: What an inspection band actually means
paragraphs: Families in the Emirates use school inspection outcomes as the primary school-choice signal, and ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection results. Using them is sensible. Reading them as a proxy for the quality of a specific subject set is not, and that gap causes a great many misplaced decisions.

The band names used in UAE school inspection frameworks run from the highest rating down through a middle set of judgements to the lowest, and the current wording and criteria should be read from the regulator's own published framework rather than from any summary, including this one. What they describe is whole-school performance against a documented framework across several domains: student outcomes, teaching, curriculum, protection and leadership. They are compiled on a cycle and they describe the school as it was inspected.

What follows is that a band is an average over a large institution at a particular moment. A school rated at the top of the scale can have a Higher Level Chemistry set taught by a non-specialist this year, because a department carries a vacancy. A school in the middle of the scale can have an outstanding mathematics department. Neither fact is visible in the band, and both are decisive for one child in one subject.

The table sets out what each level of judgement broadly implies, what it cannot tell you, and the question that gets at the thing you actually need. Note the pattern in the third column: it is identical in every row, because the limitation is structural rather than band-specific. An inspection outcome is about the school; a tuition decision is about one child in one subject.

sections.heading: Comparing two schools for one child
paragraphs: From Hydra Village a school choice is also a choice about an hour of every day, which raises the stakes. Families here routinely weigh a nearer mainland school against a longer journey to the island, and the published information will not settle it. A short list of specific questions will get much closer.

Ask about the subject, not the school. How many students sat this course last year, at what levels, and what was the spread of outcomes. Is it taught by a subject specialist this year, and has that person changed recently. For the Diploma, which Higher Level combinations actually run, because a combination offered in a brochure may not run if too few students choose it, and discovering that in September is a serious problem.

Then ask about the things that only matter to a commuting family. What time does the day end, and what time does the bus reach this community. Are there compulsory after-school commitments, and when. How much homework is set in Year 10 or DP1 on an average evening. For Diploma students, when are the internal deadlines for the exploration and the Extended Essay, and are they published at the start of the year. Those answers determine whether your child has a usable evening, which determines whether any tuition plan can work.

For context on scale, the published figures are worth knowing. Dubai's private school sector in 2024-25 contained 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7, according to the government media office. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, with six schools having opened during 2025-26 and enrolment up 6 per cent. Those are Dubai rather than Abu Dhabi figures, and they indicate the pace of change in the sector a family is choosing within.

sections.heading: Hydra Village, Al Reef and Al Ghadeer: three communities, one tutor pool
paragraphs: This page is written from a comparison angle, so it is worth testing the comparison properly. Three small mainland communities, each with different neighbours and journeys, and the question is whether any of the differences changes what a family should buy.

Hydra Village is a gated villa community with no school and no tuition provision inside it. Al Reef is nearer the Khalifa City cluster and has more within a short drive. Al Ghadeer sits on the emirate boundary, and some of its households use Dubai-side schools, which means a different regulator, potentially different term dates and a wider nominal choice of everything. Three genuinely different positions.

What is identical is the tutor pool for the thing that matters. A specialist in Higher Level Diploma Chemistry is scarce across the whole emirate, and no address among these three improves access to one in person. Published in-home visiting rates run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, read in October 2026, with the longest journeys at the upper end — so the nominal choice in Al Ghadeer comes with the same loading as the nominal scarcity in Hydra Village.

The conclusion is the same from all three. Stop using distance as the first filter, because it removes the specialists rather than the weak candidates. Filter instead by course, level and whether written work gets marked against a published scheme, and then solve the time of day, which is a solvable problem in every one of these communities. sections.heading: The two-board household's week
paragraphs: A household with one child on IGCSE and another in the Diploma has a timetabling problem rather than a curriculum problem, and in a community like Hydra Village the timetable is the binding constraint on everything. Two children, two different finish times, one adult doing the collecting, and a long journey at both ends.

The practical solution is usually consecutive slots on the same evening, with a different specialist for each child. That keeps the household to one disrupted evening rather than two, keeps both matches specific, and means written work for both children lands on the same rhythm. It is a mundane arrangement and it is the single most common thing families here ask for once they realise it is possible.

What does not work is the instinct to find one tutor for both children. The temptation is obvious — one point of contact, one invoice, one evening — and the result is a tutor stretched across two assessment systems with different command vocabulary, different internal assessment rules and different examination calendars. One of the two children is always underserved, and it is usually the Diploma student, because their needs are less visible week to week.

The other reliable error is funding both children thinly in the same term. Tuition works through the marked written practice between lessons, and two children in one household with a long commute have a limited combined supply of usable evenings. Funding the child in an examination year properly, and leaving the other to the school and their own retrieval practice for a term, produces more than splitting the budget. That is unwelcome advice and it is what the evidence in this market supports.

sections.heading: Transfers: changing school or country mid-course
paragraphs: Mid-course transfers are common in the Emirates and handled poorly almost everywhere, which makes them one of the clearest cases where a short, bounded piece of tuition is genuinely the right purchase. The problems a transfer creates are specific and finite, which is what makes them addressable.

The first is content sequence. Schools teach the same syllabus in different orders, so a student arriving in January may have covered topics the new class did months ago and missed topics it has already finished. Nobody usually audits this, and the student discovers it in an assessment. A comparison of the two schemes of work takes an hour and identifies exactly what is missing, which turns a vague sense of being behind into a list.

The second is a board change, which happens more often than families expect. A student can move from Cambridge to Pearson, or between Cambridge specifications, without anyone flagging it as significant. The content is broadly the same; the paper structures, calculator rules, formula provision, tiering vocabulary and grading scale are not. A student revising for the wrong assessment shape is doing real work in the wrong direction.

The third applies to Diploma transfers and is the most serious. Internally assessed work, supervisor relationships and the school's own deadline chain do not transfer cleanly, and a student moving in DP2 loses time at the worst possible point. The honest advice for a family considering a mid-Diploma move is that it is expensive in a way fees do not capture, and that where a move has already happened, the first fortnight should be spent auditing exactly where the student stands on every internal assessment rather than catching up on content.

sections.heading: What we can and cannot see about your child's school
paragraphs: It is worth being explicit about the limits of what a tutoring platform knows, because providers in this market routinely imply more. We can read the same published inspection outcomes a parent can read. We can see patterns across the marked scripts families send us, which is genuinely informative about where a syllabus tends to go wrong. We cannot see inside a school.

Specifically, we do not know who teaches a particular set this year, whether a department is carrying a vacancy, what a school's internal assessment data shows, or how a particular teacher marks. Any provider claiming familiarity with your child's school's internal standards is either guessing or describing a relationship they should not have. The people who hold that information are the head of department and the subject teacher, and they will usually share it if asked a specific question.

Nor do we have any relationship with schools. Students we support attend a wide range of schools in Abu Dhabi, and the school names on this page are listed as context for parents comparing provision. IB Gram claims no affiliation, partnership, endorsement or client relationship with any named school or group, and several competitors in this market list twenty or more schools as trusted partners with no relationship whatsoever behind the claim.

What we can do is specific and bounded. Read a marked script against the published mark scheme and name the faults. Match a specialist to a named specification, course and level. Mark written work and maintain an error log so that progress is visible to a parent with no subject knowledge. State honestly what the remaining time can and cannot achieve. And tell you when the better next step is a conversation with the school rather than a purchase from us.

sections.heading: The permit, our status and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: A 'near me' search in Hydra Village surfaces a person long before it surfaces a permit, so start with the permit. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation states a two working day completion time for a private tutor work permit and lists no fee whatsoever, with the application running through the ministry's smart app, its website or its e-services system. A tutor who tells a family here that the paperwork is slow, costly or not worth the trouble is contradicting the service page they would be applying on. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, which means anyone who has taught across both an IB Diploma and an IGCSE cycle in this community has already renewed at least once. Eligibility is drawn widely: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published — press reporting states that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties — so a figure quoted to you as the penalty is invention. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current ADEK document before relying on the wording.

The regulator map is worth knowing because families move. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK; Dubai with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority; Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so their remit extends well beyond inspection.

On status and claims: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, holding no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from any of those bodies or from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind, to supply answers for live assessed tasks, or to reproduce board material. Our tutors are not described as current examiners for any board, and no tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university outcome.

faqs.answer: Whole-school performance against a documented framework at the time of inspection, across domains including student outcomes, teaching, curriculum, protection and leadership. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes the results, and reading them is sensible. What a band cannot tell you is who teaches your child's set this year, whether a department is carrying a vacancy, or how one subject group has performed over three years.

faqs.question: What should I ask a school that the rating will not tell me?
faqs.answer: Subject-level questions. How many students sat this course last year, at what levels, and with what spread of outcomes. Is it taught by a subject specialist this year, and has that person changed recently. For the Diploma, which Higher Level combinations actually run rather than which are advertised. Then the commuting questions: when the day ends, when the bus reaches your community, and when the internal deadlines for the exploration and Extended Essay fall.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Reef or Al Ghadeer give more tutoring choice?
faqs.answer: More nominal choice and the same real choice. Al Reef is nearer the Khalifa City cluster and Al Ghadeer sits on the boundary with some Dubai-side options, so both have more within a short drive than Hydra Village does. What is identical across all three is that a specialist in a Higher Level Diploma subject is scarce across the whole emirate, and published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour carry the journey either way.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my IGCSE and Diploma children?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and we would rather say so. The two systems have different command vocabulary, different internal assessment rules and different examination calendars, and a tutor stretched across both leaves one child underserved — normally the Diploma student, whose needs are less visible week to week. What works instead is two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, which keeps the household to one disrupted evening without compromising either match.

faqs.question: Should we fund both children or just one this term?
faqs.answer: Usually one, properly. Tuition works through marked written practice between lessons, and two children in a household with a long commute have a limited combined supply of usable evenings. Funding the child in an examination year at specialist level, and leaving the other to the school and their own retrieval practice for a term, produces more than splitting the budget. It is unwelcome advice and it is what the pattern in this market supports.

faqs.question: What goes wrong when a child transfers school mid-course?
faqs.answer: Three specific things. Content sequence, because schools teach the same syllabus in different orders, so topics get duplicated or missed and nobody audits it. A board or specification change that nobody flags, which leaves a student revising for the wrong paper structure, calculator rule or formula provision. And for Diploma students, internally assessed work and supervisor relationships that do not transfer cleanly, which is why a DP2 move is expensive in a way fees do not capture.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist be matched from Hydra Village?
faqs.answer: For mathematics at any tier or level, usually within a few days in term time. For Higher Level sciences and Economics it is longer, and the binding constraint is the late-afternoon window every household wants rather than the number of specialists. Where a subject or slot is thin we say so and offer the alternatives — a different weekday, a weekend session, or a short wait for a named tutor — rather than substituting a generalist who is free.

faqs.question: Do you know how my child's school marks internally?
faqs.answer: No, and nor does any other platform that tells you it does. We can read the same published inspection outcomes you can, and we see patterns across the marked scripts families send us, which is genuinely informative about where a syllabus goes wrong. We cannot see inside a school: who teaches a set, whether a department has a vacancy, or what internal data shows. The head of department holds that and will usually answer a specific question.

faqs.question: Which regulator applies if we move within the UAE?
faqs.answer: Five bodies cover private schools. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Dubai with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so their remit goes well beyond inspection.

faqs.question: How large and how fast-changing is the private school sector here?
faqs.answer: Large and changing quickly, which is worth factoring into a school choice. Dubai's sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7, per the government media office. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven schools and 16,846 places. Those are Dubai figures, and they indicate the pace of change across the sector.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram partnered with any Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: No. We have no affiliation, partnership, endorsement or client relationship with any school or school group, and the school names on this page are listed only as context for parents comparing provision. Students we support attend a wide range of schools in the emirate. Several competitors in this market list twenty or more schools as trusted partners with no relationship behind the claim, and at least one has listed a school that appears not to exist.

faqs.question: What will you tell me if the tuition is not working?
faqs.answer: Which part of the plan was wrong, and what we propose instead. A review date and a measure are set at the start, and the measure is marked evidence rather than how the lessons felt. The three honest outcomes are that the arrangement is working and can taper, that the diagnosis was right but the cadence is too thin for the gap, or that the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing. Sometimes the answer is that the next step is not a purchase.

Both are facts, both take one message, and neither appears anywhere in a search ranking. Then read your school's published inspection outcome and go past it, asking whether the course is taught by a specialist this year. intro.heading: What proximity actually buys a Khalifa City family, and what it costs
paragraphs: A near-me search is a request for reassurance, and it is a reasonable one. Somebody local can be met in person, has probably taught children from the same school, and will not disappear into a different time zone. For primary-age support, for a child who needs an adult physically present, and for general homework accountability, nearness is a genuine advantage and worth paying the travel premium for.

The difficulty begins the moment the requirement gets specific. Khalifa City is a villa community between the island and the airport road, and the tutors who serve it in person are drawn from whoever lives within a workable drive and still has a free evening. That is a sufficient pool for Year 7 maths. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, for Chemistry 0620 Extended, for Edexcel 4CH1, or for Arabic as a first language, it can be a pool of nobody at all, and the family never learns that. They are simply offered the nearest person who says yes.

The arithmetic is worth seeing plainly. Widening a search from five kilometres to twenty does not multiply the number of specialists; it multiplies the number of generalists and adds forty minutes of driving to the price. Widening it to the whole emirate adds tutors who live on the island and will quote a Khalifa City rate that includes a bridge crossing. None of those steps solves the original problem, which was never distance. It was depth in one specific course, taught to an examination, by somebody who has marked the paper your child will sit.

Online delivery changes the filter rather than the standard. The lesson arrives at a desk in Khalifa City over live video, on a shared whiteboard, with the school's own worksheet open, and the constraint on who teaches your child becomes the syllabus they have actually taught to an examination. IB Gram sends nobody to Abu Dhabi addresses: home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that position is the same on every country page we publish. The lesson arrives at a desk, not at a gate, and the only thing that travels is the worksheet on the shared screen.

What follows is written for a household that may well have both boards running at once, which is common in this corridor. It compares what the IB Diploma and IGCSE actually demand, maps which authority regulates your child's school and what that means in practice, sets out the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements a British-track certificate has to satisfy for UAE universities, states where a tutor must stop on assessed work, and explains how to verify that the person you are paying is permitted to tutor in the UAE at all. A near-me search answers none of those questions.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-khal.programmesIntro: Khalifa City households commonly run two curricula at once, because siblings end up at different schools and because families transfer between boards mid-school. These are the four programmes that produce most requests in this corridor, with what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, and the workload is distributed across two years rather than concentrated in a terminal examination series. Support concentrates on internal assessment design, command-term discipline and Paper 3 technique at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB session or results dates appear on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a wrong date in an answer a parent acts on is worse than no date. Your Khalifa City school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadline calendar, which is the document that actually binds a student's work.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment graded 1 to 8 against four criteria per subject, with no terminal written papers in most schools. Parents arriving from a British-track school often read the absence of examinations as an absence of rigour. It is a different evidence base: the work is judged against descriptors rather than against a mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Khalifa City run MYP to Year 11, so a child moving into an IGCSE school at Year 10 meets structured written papers for the first time. The gap is specific rather than general, and it is cheapest to close in the term after the move rather than in the run-up to a series.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written assessment with syllabus codes that determine everything: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500. Most subjects tier into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings and different content, not merely harder questions.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates each exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered in India only and belongs in no Abu Dhabi revision plan.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track route in this corridor, with codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1, tiered Foundation and Higher. Paper structures, question wording and formula provision all differ from Cambridge, so revision material does not transfer cleanly between the two boards even where the content overlaps.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Link the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-khal.subjectsIntro: IB Diploma subjects first, since these are the requests where a near-me search most often fails. Each note describes what the subject assesses and where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with SL Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Higher Level adds complex numbers, vectors, proof by induction and substantially harder calculus, and it is the single hardest Diploma course to staff locally in any Abu Dhabi community.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route, calculator permitted throughout, with statistics and regression central. Higher Level adds matrices and graph theory. Students who chose it as the easier option often need statistics support rather than algebra support.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and the energetics calculations decide most grades, with the internal assessment needing a research question narrow enough to generate usable data. Higher Level Paper 3 rewards experimental reasoning rather than recall.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields carry the paper, and the common failure is mathematical rather than conceptual: a student who understands the physics and cannot rearrange the expression quickly loses the mark. Uncertainty handling is routinely under-taught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with extended-response questions that reward structure as much as knowledge. The internal assessment is where most available improvement sits, because experimental design errors cap the mark regardless of how good the write-up is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline decide the grade. An evaluate question answered with explanation scores a fraction of the credit. Gulf-specific examples are legitimate, memorable and under-used by candidates in this region.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis and the individual oral carry the course, with the oral in particular rewarding a global issue that is genuinely arguable rather than merely topical. Structure is teachable; reading taste is not, and most marks sit in structure.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, both assessed against published criteria and both routinely left too late. Tutoring works here as questioning and criteria coaching, never as drafting, because every word must be the student's own.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research with a supervisor at school. Support means helping the student narrow a research question, interrogate method and reference properly, with the writing done entirely by the student.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio and Arabic B
subjects.levels: SL, and HL for Arabic B
subjects.description: Relevant across this corridor, and a course where consistent short sessions beat intensive blocks. Oral assessment carries weight that students tend to discover late, so speaking practice should start early rather than in the final term.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-khal.igcseSubjectsIntro: And the IGCSE side of the same household, where the syllabus code matters more than the subject name because the code determines the papers, the formula sheet and the mark scheme.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Circle theorems, trigonometry diagrams and histograms with unequal intervals return the most marks per hour. Practice must come from the board the child is entered for, because question styles differ enough to mislead.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cost more marks than any other topic, followed by uncertainty and graph gradient work in the practical paper. Many candidates state the physics correctly and lose the mark on units or significant figures.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and organic pathways decide the grade, and the paper rewards precise language. Writing that a reaction is faster rather than naming the increased frequency of successful collisions earns the idea and not the mark.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Approachable enough to be under-revised. The extended-response questions on transport, homeostasis and inheritance are where structured answers separate from merely correct ones, and structure is quick to teach.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the extended reading response carry the paper. Students who read well still lose marks for ignoring audience, form and purpose, which the mark scheme credits explicitly and visibly.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Formulaic, highly trainable exercises across reading, writing and listening, with speaking in 0511. Most of the available improvement is technique and timing rather than general language ability.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Both assessed on application rather than recall. Business Studies is entirely case-study driven, so practice has to be done on real inserts; revising definitions collects the smallest share of the available marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: The bridge into Diploma or A-Level mathematics, introducing calculus and advanced algebra a year early. The strongest preparation available for Analysis and Approaches, and worth taking if the school offers it.

sections.heading: What a widening search radius actually adds
paragraphs: Try the experiment honestly and the result is consistent. Search within a few kilometres of Khalifa City and you find people who can help with primary numeracy, lower secondary maths and general study habits. Extend it across Al Raha and Mohammed Bin Zayed City and the count rises while the specialism does not, because the additional names are mostly generalists serving a bigger population. Extend it to the island and you reach genuine Diploma depth, at which point the price includes two bridge crossings and the 16:00 slot becomes impossible.

The requests where this breaks down are predictable. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Chemistry at Higher Level with an internal assessment deadline in the same month. Edexcel-specific science codes where the family has assumed Cambridge. Arabic as a first language. Theory of Knowledge, which almost nobody advertises because almost nobody teaches it. For each of these the local pool in any single Abu Dhabi community is thin, and widening the radius dilutes rather than concentrates it.

The honest way to run the search is to invert it. Decide the course and level first, including the syllabus code where there is one, then ask who can teach that, then ask how the lesson reaches your child. Done in that order, proximity turns out to be a delivery question rather than a quality question, and it has a straightforward answer that does not involve anybody driving to a Khalifa City gate at five o'clock.

sections.heading: IB and IGCSE in one household: what each actually demands
paragraphs: Families running both boards at once usually discover that the two children need entirely different kinds of help, and that the word tutor covers both badly. IGCSE is a terminal examination qualification: the grade is produced by written papers in a single series, so the work is content coverage, paper technique and timing, and progress is measurable against past papers from the correct board. The diagnostic document is a marked mock script, and the plan runs backwards from the first paper.

The Diploma is a two-year portfolio with examinations at the end. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit outside any single subject, and school internal deadlines bind harder than anything the board publishes. The diagnostic documents are the school's internal calendar and the published assessment criteria, and the plan runs forwards from the criteria rather than backwards from a paper.

That difference has a practical consequence for hiring. A tutor who is excellent at IGCSE paper technique may have no useful opinion about whether a research question can carry a Higher Level internal assessment, and a Diploma specialist may be an expensive way to teach circle theorems. Hiring one person for both children because they live nearby is the specific mistake a near-me search encourages, and it is usually the more expensive option once the wasted sessions are counted. Two matched tutors on one family schedule cost roughly the same and waste fewer hours, because neither is learning the other child's course on your time.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it matters
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi families often assume a single national regulator and there are five. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The practical content differs by emirate, and not only in inspection. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate rather than only with the school. The federal baseline underneath all of it is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

For a Khalifa City family this matters in two concrete ways. Inspection ratings for your child's school are published by ADEK, not by a Dubai body, so a rating quoted from a KHDA report is about a different school system. And no tutoring provider, including this one, holds approval from any of these authorities. A platform offering private tuition is not inspected by ADEK, and any claim of regulator approval should be treated as a reason to look elsewhere.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what a certificate has to show
paragraphs: Families planning on UAE universities meet equivalency late, and it is one of the few genuinely rule-bound things in this market. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last detail is where a widely-read competitor page gets it wrong, publishing a requirement for six IGCSE subjects. The correct figure is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, which changes subject-choice planning in Year 9 for a Khalifa City family. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying.

For the IB, no points threshold is published here, and that is deliberate. The article these requirements come from states no IB threshold, and no figure should be put in front of a parent without having been read on the Ministry's own site or the emirate attestation authority's page. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or expedites. Describe it, check it against the official channel, and treat anybody offering to secure it as a warning sign.

sections.heading: The line a near-me search never tells you about
paragraphs: One part of this market sells finished assessed work, and at least one provider visible in UAE search results advertises completed Internal Assessments at a stated price. It is worth naming plainly what that is. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under IB rules and a disciplinary matter at every board, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. No tutor may write an internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any coursework component, at any price, for any deadline.

What a tutor may do is substantial, legitimate and worth buying. Teaching what each assessment criterion credits, so the student knows where the marks are. Stress-testing a research question before weeks are invested in it. Reading a draft and saying where the argument thins. Questioning a method until the student finds the flaw themselves. Modelling an analysis on different data so the technique transfers. Marking against descriptors. Checking referencing and data provenance before submission.

The boundary is also practical rather than merely ethical. Schools in this corridor run originality checks as routine, internal assessments are submitted with declarations, and a draft that reads nothing like a student's class work is the easiest thing in the world to notice. A family paying for genuine criteria coaching gets a mark that survives scrutiny. A family paying for a document is buying an exposure it cannot withdraw once the submission is made.

sections.heading: Is the person you found permitted to tutor here?
paragraphs: A near-me search returns names, not permissions, and private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source and is left out deliberately. MoHRE's own service page for the permit lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. The permit attaches to the individual, which means no agency or platform can hold it on a tutor's behalf, and a tutor who holds one can simply say so.

There is a second rule a Khalifa City family should know. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy text, so verify it against the current ADEK document. The principle is sound regardless: the person who marks the school assessment should not be paid privately to prepare your child for it.

sections.heading: What to send when you ask anybody for a quote
paragraphs: Quotes in this market are not comparable because the requests are not. One family asks for a maths tutor and another asks for a tutor who has taught Cambridge 0580 Extended to the examination and can mark a full paper against the scheme within the fee. They get very different answers, and the second family can actually compare the replies. Writing the request properly takes five minutes and is the highest-return effort available before any money is spent.

Include six things. The board and syllabus code, or the Diploma course and level, with the tier where one exists. The school and the year group. What the most recent marked assessment shows, with the script attached if possible. The window your week genuinely has, not the one you would prefer. Whether marking and written feedback are expected inside the rate. And the deadline that actually matters, which for a Diploma student is usually a school internal deadline rather than an examination.

Then ask every provider the same two closing questions. What happens if the match is wrong, and what will you refuse to do. The first tells you whether you are buying a relationship or a subscription. The second tells you whether you are dealing with a teaching service or an essay mill. Both answers arrive quickly from anybody serious, and the comparison between three replies is usually decisive without any further research. Keep the replies, too: a provider who answers precisely in writing before any payment tends to keep answering precisely afterwards, and one who answers vaguely has told you how the arrangement will feel in month three.

sections.heading: When nearness genuinely matters
paragraphs: This page argues against proximity as a filter, and there are cases where that argument does not hold. A young child who needs an adult physically in the room, a student with a learning need where in-person support has been recommended by a professional, and a household with unreliable connectivity are all situations where a local tutor is the right answer and the travel premium is money well spent. Saying otherwise would be selling rather than advising.

For a Khalifa City family with a Diploma or Extended-tier requirement, the calculation runs the other way. The specialist who has taught your child's exact course is unlikely to live within a workable drive, and insisting that they do means accepting a generalist instead. Live video with a shared whiteboard and the school's own worksheet open loses very little for an academic subject at this level, and it gains the one thing that actually moves a grade, which is somebody who knows the paper.

The way to resolve it is to test rather than theorise. One free hour over live video, no card details, no commitment, working on the problem your child is currently stuck on. Either the explanation lands and the format turns out to be irrelevant, or it does not and you have learned something real for nothing. That is a better basis for a decision than a search radius, and it is available before any Abu Dhabi tutor would have finished the drive to your gate.

faqs.question: Is there an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: For primary and lower secondary support, almost certainly: the local pool handles general maths, science and English well. For a Diploma Higher Level course, an Extended-tier science, an Edexcel-specific code or Arabic as a first language, the in-person pool in any single Abu Dhabi community is thin, and widening the radius towards Al Raha or Mohammed Bin Zayed City adds generalists rather than specialists. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring in the UAE at all; lessons are one-to-one over live video, matched on course and syllabus code.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work as well as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For academic subjects at IGCSE and Diploma level, the loss is small and the gain is specific. A shared whiteboard, the school's own worksheet and a marked script on screen cover what a desk covers, and the hour buys a teacher who knows the exact paper rather than the nearest available graduate. Where a professional has recommended in-person support, or where a child genuinely needs an adult in the room, a local tutor is the right answer. The way to settle it is the free trial hour rather than an argument in advance.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle my Diploma child and my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: It is usually the wrong economy, even though it looks like the convenient one. IGCSE work is content coverage, board-specific paper technique and timing, measured against past papers. Diploma work is internal assessment design, criteria discipline and school internal deadlines. Those are different jobs, and somebody strong at one often has no useful opinion about the other. Two matched tutors on one family schedule, with back-to-back slots if that suits the household, costs about the same and wastes fewer sessions than a single generalist covering both.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects schools in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain. Dubai schools are overseen by KHDA, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the Ministry of Education. Inspection ratings for a Khalifa City school come from ADEK, so a rating quoted from a Dubai report describes a different system. ADEK does not inspect or approve tutoring providers, including this one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a Khalifa City leaver need for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects passed at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One widely-read competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong, and the difference changes subject planning from Year 9. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry's own channel before acting, and treat any provider offering to secure equivalency as a reason for caution.

faqs.answer: None is published on this page, deliberately. The source that sets out the British and American track requirements states no IB threshold, and putting an unsourced points figure in front of a parent is the kind of error that gets acted on. Check the Ministry of Education's own site or the emirate attestation authority's page, or ask your child's IB coordinator, who deals with the process for the school's leavers each year. Treat any number quoted without a government source attached as unverified, wherever it appears.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Abu Dhabi need a licence or permit?
faqs.answer: A permit, yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years. faqs.question: Could we just pay the class teacher at my child's Khalifa City school?
faqs.answer: They should not. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than taken from the policy text, so verify it against the current ADEK document. faqs.answer: Six things, and the replies become comparable. The board and syllabus code, or the Diploma course and level, with the tier. The school and year group. And the deadline that genuinely binds, which for a Diploma student is usually a school internal deadline. Then ask everybody the same two closing questions: what happens if the match is wrong, and what will you refuse to do.

faqs.question: What will a tutor refuse to do on an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Write, draft, rewrite or edit to submission any part of it. A tutor may teach what each criterion credits, stress-test a research question before weeks go into it, question a method until the student finds the flaw, model an analysis on different data, mark drafts against the descriptors and check referencing. At least one provider advertising in UAE search results sells completed Internal Assessments, which is malpractice under IB rules and falls on the student rather than the seller. Asking the question directly is the fastest way to sort a teaching service from an essay mill.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a Khalifa City household?
faqs.answer: Mainstream requests move in a few days: Cambridge 0580 Extended, 0625, 0500, Applications and Interpretation at either level. Tighter requests take up to a week or more, particularly Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge and Edexcel-specific science codes, and they get tighter again near school internal deadlines. You are told which category your request falls into before the trial, along with where the tutor is based, rather than being given a fast general match that produces repeated diagnosis later.

faqs.question: Is there a Khalifa City centre or branch we can walk into?
faqs.answer: No, and it would be worth asking any provider the same question. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE, and nothing on this page should suggest otherwise. Two competitor pages studied for this search route UAE parents to a foreign phone number without saying where teaching happens, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. Delivery for Khalifa City is one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and that is the whole of the arrangement.

faqs.question: My child is switching from MYP into an IGCSE school. What changes?
faqs.answer: The evidence base changes, and that is the whole difficulty. MYP assesses against four criteria graded 1 to 8, with investigation and communication credited heavily and no terminal written papers in most schools. IGCSE produces the grade from written papers in a single series. Students arrive able to reason about unfamiliar problems and unfamiliar with structured paper technique, timing and the habit of showing ordered working. The gap is specific and closes fastest in the term after the move, especially in maths and the sciences.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this corridor?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, consistently. Then Theory of Knowledge, which almost nobody advertises because almost nobody teaches it. Then Extended-tier chemistry and physics tied to an internal assessment or coursework deadline in the same month, Edexcel-specific science codes where a family had assumed Cambridge, and Arabic as a first language. These are exactly the requests where distance is the wrong filter, because the number of people who can teach them well in any one Abu Dhabi community is small regardless of how wide the search gets.

faqs.question: If the first match misses, who pays for the second one?
faqs.answer: The next match is arranged at no additional cost, and the trial is repeated with the new tutor. That is a deliberate part of the arrangement rather than a concession, because the only reliable test of a match is whether the explanation lands for your particular child, and no profile or review predicts it. Say so early: the arrangements that fail are the ones where a family keeps a poor match out of politeness for half a term. Each child's match is reviewed separately after four sessions.

intro.heading: What 'near me' is really asking, and the honest answer for Madinat Zayed
paragraphs: The search is about logistics rather than geography. A parent in Madinat Zayed does not especially want a tutor who lives nearby; they want a session that happens reliably, at a time the child is awake and home, without one more car journey in an afternoon that already contains two. 'Near me' is shorthand for 'without adding another drive'. Once that is the actual requirement, an online session is not a compromise on proximity — it is the only version that fully satisfies it.

Start with the real timetable. Most Abu Dhabi secondary schools finish between 14:30 and 15:30, and a Madinat Zayed child attending a school in the central island corridor is home between 15:15 and 16:00. A child at a school in Khalifa City, Al Raha or Saadiyat is home between 16:00 and 16:45, later if the bus route is long. Add a prayer, a meal and some decompression, and the realistic first session slot sits between 16:30 and 18:00 on the island and between 17:30 and 19:00 off it.

Now put a driving tutor into that window. They are serving several families in one afternoon, which means their arrival time is set by the slowest leg of their route, not by your child's day. A 16:30 booking becomes 16:50, then 17:10, and by half term the session has quietly moved to the hour your child is least able to concentrate. Nothing dishonest has happened. The Abu Dhabi afternoon simply does this to a schedule, and it does it more in the cooler months when the school-run traffic around the central grid is heaviest.

The second thing 'near me' usually hides is that the household is running two systems. It is common in this area for an older child to be in the IB Diploma Programme while a younger one sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE, sometimes at different schools with different finish times. One in-home tutor can rarely serve both well, because the subject knowledge is different and the two children's slots do not line up. Two separate online tutors at two separate times costs the household nothing extra in travel and solves both problems properly.

IB Gram delivers to Madinat Zayed as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What that buys a family here is specific: a session fixed at the time your child is genuinely available, with a tutor matched to the programme and level rather than to a driving radius, and no slow drift of the slot across the term. The hour you agree in September is the hour you still have in February, and that single fact matters more to a result than almost anything else a parent chooses.

The year is paced by entry deadlines and mock windows rather than by continuous coursework.

For scheduling, the point is that Year 11 collapses into the eight weeks before the series, and a family that has held a steady weekly slot since September arrives there in a different state from one booking emergency sessions in April. The slot matters more than the intensity.

Content is narrower and deeper than the IB Diploma's six-subject spread, which makes the weekly commitment lower in number of subjects and higher in depth per subject. Students here can usually hold a later slot than a DP candidate because there are fewer competing internal deadlines.

sections.heading: Finish times around Madinat Zayed and the slot each one leaves
paragraphs: The useful planning number is not the school's published finish time; it is the time your child is home, fed and able to think. Across Abu Dhabi, secondary schools finish between 14:30 and 15:30. A Madinat Zayed child at a central island school is home by 15:45 or so. A child bussed to Khalifa City, Al Raha or Saadiyat is home between 16:00 and 16:45, and later again if the route has several stops before theirs.

Subtract the rest of the afternoon honestly. A prayer, a meal, twenty minutes of decompression and any sport or service commitment, and the realistic first slot lands between 16:30 and 18:00 for island-schooled students and between 17:30 and 19:00 for the off-island group. Younger children in the Middle Years Programme can usually manage the earlier end; a Diploma Programme student with service hours and a coursework deadline cannot, whatever the family intends in September.

This is where a visiting tutor's schedule and your child's day quietly diverge. The tutor's arrival time is set by their route across several families, so your slot is downstream of someone else's traffic. The shift is gradual and nobody is at fault — but by half term the session has moved to the hour your child is least able to use it. A fixed online slot has no upstream journey feeding into it, so there is nothing for a delay to propagate through. That is the whole of the argument, and it is a scheduling argument rather than a quality one.

sections.heading: Why a 16:30 in-home booking becomes a 17:10 session by half term
paragraphs: A tutor driving between families in central Abu Dhabi is solving a routing problem, not a teaching one. They have four or five slots in an afternoon and each is separated by a journey whose length they do not control. A delay in the first slot propagates through every subsequent one, and the family with the earliest booking absorbs the least while the family with the latest absorbs the most. If your child is the third stop, your 16:30 is structurally a 16:50.

The second mechanism is the end of the session rather than the start. A tutor with a 17:30 booking elsewhere has to leave your building at a fixed time whether or not the hour finished well. So a late start quietly shortens the lesson, and the part that gets cut is the end — which is where the consolidation, the homework setting and the question your child was building up the courage to ask all live. A nominal hour becomes forty-five useful minutes.

The third is attrition across the term. In September every booking is honoured precisely. By November the tutor has absorbed a dozen small delays, a parking problem near the Madinat Zayed grid, and a week of heavier school-run traffic, and the schedule has shifted permanently later to accommodate reality. None of this reflects badly on the tutor. It is simply what a fixed set of appointments and a variable set of journeys produce, and the family only notices once the slot has moved past the hour their child can use.
