sections.heading: Two boards, one household: what changes between IB and IGCSE
paragraphs: A Madinat Zayed family often needs both systems at once, and they are not two versions of the same thing. The IB Diploma Programme examines six subjects with internal assessments spread across two years, school-set deadlines throughout, and a single May examination session. IGCSE concentrates almost everything into terminal papers in a June or November series, with tiered entries that carry grade ceilings and, on Cambridge mathematics, one non-calculator paper per tier.

The scheduling consequence is the part parents care about. A Diploma student's pressure is continuous and lumpy: quiet weeks interrupted by deadline weeks when every evening disappears. An IGCSE student's pressure is flat for months and then vertical for eight weeks. Running both children on the same weekly rhythm therefore fails one of them. The IGCSE child needs a steady slot that intensifies in the spring; the Diploma child needs a slot that can move around a known deadline calendar and then return.

The tutoring consequence is that one person rarely serves both well. A tutor fluent in the Diploma's internal assessment criteria and in Higher Level Paper 3 technique is not automatically fluent in Cambridge tier ceilings or Pearson Edexcel's 9-to-1 scale, and the reverse is equally true. Two matched tutors at two staggered hours is the version that works, and online it costs a household nothing extra because nobody is driving anywhere. A visiting tutor serving two children in one appointment is also quietly halving each child's attention, which is rarely what the booking intended.

sections.heading: What proximity costs in this market, and what it actually delivers
paragraphs: Proximity has a price and it is visible in the published figures. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home tutoring in Dubai and Abu Dhabi at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors in the emirate advertise AED 200 to 500. Comparable online tuition sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher and AED 200 to 450-plus for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and TutorChase quoting AED 270.

What the premium buys is a person in the room. What it costs is a narrower choice of person, a slot that drifts, and a session that shortens from the end when the tutor has somewhere else to be. For a seven-year-old needing an adult alongside them, that trade can be worth making. For a Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a Pearson Edexcel Higher paper, or a Diploma student who needs Paper 3 technique, the premium is paying for travel at the exact moment specialist knowledge matters most.

Monthly figures make the comparison plainer. Packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. Those are other providers' published rates, named so you can check them; they are not an IB Gram price list, and we quote after a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the UAE academic calendar
paragraphs: A weekly slot that ignores the UAE calendar does not survive the year. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the household's useful evening shifts entirely: the productive window moves to after Iftar, and a session scheduled at 17:00 is a session nobody attends. Moving sessions to post-Iftar timing for the month is straightforward online and close to impossible for a tutor who has to drive between four families in a compressed evening.

Daily prayer timings also shape the afternoon more than most tutoring sites acknowledge. The Maghrib and Asr timings move through the year, and a fixed 17:30 that works in December lands differently in June. Families who set a slot with those timings in mind keep it; families who set it by convenience renegotiate it every few weeks. Asking about this at the start, rather than discovering it in week four, is the difference between a stable arrangement and a recurring conversation.

Then there is the shape of the UAE school year itself. The long summer break runs from late June into August or early September, and for a Diploma student the summer between DP1 and DP2 is the single most valuable block of unpressured time in the whole programme — the right moment to get the mathematics exploration or the Extended Essay substantially done. It is also the block most commonly lost entirely. Continuity across it costs little and is worth more than an equivalent number of sessions in March.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may do with coursework, and what nobody may do
paragraphs: Both systems in this household put assessed work in the student's hands, and both treat outside interference as malpractice. The IB internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. IGCSE coursework and the Cambridge 0607 investigation are the same. The research behind this page found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is an integrity breach whose consequence lands on the candidate, not the seller.

What a tutor may legitimately do is considerable and worth knowing precisely. They may teach the content the work requires. They may interrogate a research question until it is answerable at the right level. They may ask why a method was chosen and whether the assumptions hold. They may read a draft the student has written and give feedback against each published criterion. They may help map deadlines against the school's own calendar. All of that is teaching.

What no tutor may do is write, redraft to completion, or supply material for a student to transcribe. The test is not how much help was given but whose work the submitted document is, and the version a parent can apply at home is simple: ask your child to explain, unprompted, why each step is there. Nor will any tutor here supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads — those are the boards' copyright and the correct route is the official site or the school.

sections.heading: ADEK, inspection bands and what to ask the school
paragraphs: Private schools serving Madinat Zayed are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education each govern elsewhere. Advice written for Dubai, which is most of what ranks for these searches, does not describe your child's school or its inspection regime.

An inspection band is a statement about a whole school rather than a department. A strongly rated school can be short of Higher Level specialist teaching in one subject in one year, usually because an experienced teacher left and the timetable absorbed the gap. That is the most common honest reason a family in this area starts searching, and naming it sharpens the request: not general tutoring, but cover for a specific programme and level the school is temporarily thin in.

On credentials there are two things worth knowing. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation, claims none, and operates no UAE office.

sections.heading: Setting a slot that survives to February
paragraphs: Pick the hour from the hardest week rather than the easiest. A family that sets 16:30 in a quiet September, then discovers that every deadline week pushes the session to 19:00, has in practice chosen 19:00. A family that sets 17:45 — after the off-island journey, after a meal, before the evening collapses — keeps 17:45 in November, in Ramadan with a post-Iftar variant, and in the spring. The right question is not 'when is convenient' but 'when is this possible in a bad week'.

Protect it in the calendar as a fixed commitment, and keep the same tutor across it. Every change of tutor costs a re-diagnosis, a fortnight of rapport-building and usually a restart on whatever was half-fixed. That is the hidden cost in cheap hourly rates with rotating staff: the arithmetic looks better and the progress does not, because nobody holds a continuous picture of the student. Consistency is the single cheapest thing a parent can supply.

Review it against a timed paper every six weeks rather than against a feeling. A past paper under real conditions, marked to the published scheme, with the component breakdown compared to the previous one. If nothing has moved in twelve weeks, the plan is wrong and should change — possibly the tutor, possibly the target, possibly the slot. That review is also the honest moment to decide whether to keep paying, which is exactly when a family should be deciding it.

process.title: Tell us the finish time as well as the subject

That shapes the match as much as the subject does, because a tutor who cannot hold your real hour is not a match however good their teaching is.

process.description: IB Middle Years or Diploma, or Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE with the syllabus code and tier. Two children on two boards get two matches rather than one compromise. For Diploma students, say which Higher Level subject is weakest; for IGCSE, say whether the non-calculator paper is the problem.

process.title: Sit a free trial lesson in the real slot
process.description: Sixty minutes, no charge, scheduled at the hour you intend to keep rather than at whatever is free this week. That tests the slot and the tutor at the same time. If your child is too tired at that hour, you have learned something useful before paying for anything.

process.title: Fix the hour and get the plan in writing
process.description: After the trial you should have the weekly slot agreed and a short written statement of what the first eight sessions target, split by component where possible. This is also when a rate is quoted for the level and session length, against the market bands published on this page.

process.title: Flag the deadline and exam calendar early
process.description: Internal assessment deadlines, mock windows, and whether an IGCSE entry is for the June or November series. Those dates come from the school rather than from us, and knowing them in September is what lets a block of intensive work be planned rather than improvised in April.

process.title: Review on a paper every six weeks
process.description: A timed past paper marked against the published scheme, with the component breakdown compared to last time. If a component has not moved in twelve weeks, we change the plan, the target or the tutor. That review is the point at which a family decides whether to continue, and it should be.

whyPoints.title: The slot does not drift
whyPoints.description: An online session has no upstream journey, so the hour you agree in September is the hour you have in February. In-home bookings slide later across a term because the tutor's arrival is downstream of someone else's traffic, and the part that gets cut is the end of the lesson, where consolidation lives.

whyPoints.title: Both systems covered properly, separately
whyPoints.description: IB Middle Years and Diploma on one side, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE on the other, with a tutor matched to each rather than one generalist straddling both. Households in this area frequently run both at once, and the two children need different rhythms as well as different knowledge.

whyPoints.title: Matched on programme, not on driving distance
whyPoints.description: The set of tutors who can reach a Madinat Zayed building between 16:00 and 19:00 is small. The set available at 17:45 Gulf Standard Time is not. For a narrow need — Higher Level Paper 3, Cambridge 0607, Pearson Edexcel 4PM1 — that difference decides whether the right person is available at all.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider or rate table it came from and the month it was read. Three of six competitor pages researched publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. A number you can check is worth more than a reassurance you cannot.

whyPoints.description: Lessons to Madinat Zayed run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. We state it rather than leave it to be discovered, because two competitor pages route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where delivery happens.

Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work; they do not produce assessed components or distribute board materials.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB or IGCSE tutor near Madinat Zayed?
faqs.answer: There are tutors in and around central Abu Dhabi, yes. The more useful question is whether the ones who can reach your building between 16:00 and 19:00 include a specialist in your child's exact programme and level — Higher Level Paper 3, Cambridge 0607, Pearson Edexcel 4PM1 — because that pool is small in any one neighbourhood. IB Gram delivers to Madinat Zayed online, one-to-one over live video, and does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The match is made on programme rather than on postcode.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after the Abu Dhabi school run?
faqs.answer: For a child at a central island school, home by about 15:45, a 16:30 start is genuinely achievable. For a child bussed to Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas or Saadiyat, home between 16:00 and 16:45, the honest answer is 17:30 or 18:00 once a prayer and a meal are allowed for. Middle Years students manage the earlier end; Diploma students with service hours or sport rarely do. Choose the hour that works in a difficult week rather than a quiet one, because that is the hour you will actually keep.

faqs.question: Why do in-home tutoring slots keep slipping later through the term?
faqs.answer: Because a visiting tutor is solving a routing problem across four or five families in one afternoon, and a delay in the first slot propagates to every one after it. If your child is the third stop, your 16:30 is structurally a 16:50. A fixed onward booking also shortens the session from the end, which is where consolidation and homework-setting sit. By November a dozen small delays have become a permanently later slot. An online session has no upstream journey, so the hour holds.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover my Diploma child and my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and usually badly. The knowledge is different: Diploma internal assessment criteria and Higher Level paper technique on one side, Cambridge tier ceilings, non-calculator papers and Pearson Edexcel's 9-to-1 scale on the other. The rhythms are different too — Diploma pressure is lumpy around deadlines, IGCSE pressure is flat then vertical before a series. Two matched tutors at two staggered hours serves both children properly, and online that costs the household nothing extra because nobody is driving anywhere.

faqs.question: Which schools do Madinat Zayed children usually attend?
faqs.answer: Within the central island corridor, ten to twenty minutes away, sit schools including Abu Dhabi International School, Al Bateen Academy, Cambridge High School Abu Dhabi, Al Ittihad National Private School and the American Community School of Abu Dhabi. Many families also bus off-island to Al Yasmina Academy, GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi, Raha International School, Cranleigh Abu Dhabi or Brighton College Abu Dhabi. All are licensed and inspected by ADEK, and provision changes between intakes, so confirm with the school. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named.

faqs.question: Does the extra cost of a tutor who comes to the house buy better teaching?
faqs.answer: It buys presence, not expertise. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home tutoring in Abu Dhabi at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 200 to 450 for an online IB or IGCSE specialist. The premium pays for a car, a parking search and a journey. For a young child who needs an adult alongside them that can be worth it. For a Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a paper, it is paying for travel at the moment specialist knowledge matters most.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: They move to post-Iftar timing for the month. School hours shorten, the household's productive window shifts to the evening, and a session left at 17:00 is a session nobody attends. Rescheduling a whole month of slots is straightforward online and close to impossible for a tutor driving between four families in a compressed evening. Daily prayer timings also move through the year, so a slot set with Asr and Maghrib in mind from the start survives, and one set purely for convenience gets renegotiated every few weeks.

faqs.question: Should we keep tutoring going through the UAE summer break?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma student, yes, and the reason is specific rather than general. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the only long block of unpressured time in the programme, and it is the right moment to get the mathematics exploration or the Extended Essay substantially drafted by the student, with a tutor teaching the content and questioning the method. It is also the block most commonly lost entirely. For an IGCSE student the case is weaker; short maintenance sessions prevent the September restart, which is worth something but not everything.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a Madinat Zayed family?
faqs.answer: For mainstream needs — Diploma Standard Level sciences, Cambridge 0580, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 — usually within a few days, including the free trial lesson. For narrow ones, which is where honesty matters, it can be two to three weeks: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with Paper 3 experience, Cambridge 0607 Extended and Further Pure 4PM1 are the thinnest pools. We will tell you that rather than fill the slot with the nearest available person, and we will not charge an interim match as though it were the one you asked for.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's school before booking a tutor?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. First, the exact programme, level, syllabus code and tier — written down, not remembered. Second, the most recent mock or internal assessment score broken down by component rather than as a single grade, because a split between papers diagnoses the problem. Third, the deadline calendar: internal assessment dates, the mock window, and whether an IGCSE entry targets the June or November series. Those three answers define what tuition should buy, and they are more useful than any rate comparison.

faqs.question: Does my child in Abu Dhabi sit the February/March IGCSE series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers the February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, with November functioning as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong one. Take dates from the school's examinations officer, not from a tutoring website.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring effective for a younger Middle Years student?
faqs.answer: For most, yes, with two conditions. The session needs to be shorter — 45 minutes rather than 90 — and it needs to happen in a shared room rather than behind a closed door, so a parent can see that it is happening. A shared whiteboard shows the student's working line by line, which is what a tutor needs to see, and the recording lets a parent check what was covered. For a child who genuinely cannot stay with a screen, in-home tuition is the better answer, and we will say so.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my Diploma child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the content the assessment needs, interrogate the research question until it is answerable at the right level, challenge the assumptions, give criterion-by-criterion feedback on a draft the student has written, and map the work against the school's internal deadlines. A tutor may not write any of it, redraft it to completion, or supply material to transcribe. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the consequence of that falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: What happens if the slot we chose turns out to be too late in the day?
faqs.answer: We move it, and this is where the online format earns its place. Changing a weekly hour is an administrative matter rather than a routing problem, so a family who discovers in week three that 18:30 is past their child's useful concentration can shift to 17:30 without renegotiating a tutor's whole afternoon. The same applies in reverse when a school changes its finish time or a bus route is redrawn. Tell us early; the sunk cost of a bad slot is sessions nobody benefits from.

faqs.question: How can I check that a tutor is legally permitted to teach my child here?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one exposes the tutor to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. ADEK's ethics rules separately bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

intro.heading: "Near me" is the wrong question, and the right one is easy to answer
paragraphs: Masdar City is a clean-technology and research district near Abu Dhabi International Airport, built around a university campus, with a pedestrianised core and a small residential population of researchers, postgraduates and professionals. No private school sits inside it. Every school-age child here commutes, most often to the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and families arrive and leave on research and employment cycles rather than on school ones.

That last point explains why this particular search phrase comes from this particular district. Families move in mid-key-stage from British, American, Indian, Australian and continental European systems, and their children land in whichever Abu Dhabi school had a place. A parent six weeks into that may genuinely not know whether their Year 10 child is being prepared for Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE or the IB Middle Years Programme, and a Year 12 sibling may be on something different again.

So the honest starting point is not a list of tutors near you. It is a question you can answer for nothing: ask the school for the qualification name and, for IGCSE, the syllabus code. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for maths and 0625 for physics. Pearson codes look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. IB courses are named by subject and level — Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Biology SL. Once you have that, every other decision becomes answerable.

On the geography, the direct answer. There is no meaningful resident pool of IB or IGCSE subject specialists inside Masdar City, because teaching those qualifications is an occupation and it clusters where the schools are. What the district has in unusual density is mathematical and scientific ability, which is genuinely useful for understanding a topic and not the same as knowing how an IB or Cambridge mark scheme pays out.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor will travel to a Masdar City address. Lessons are live one-to-one video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with each tutor chosen for the specific qualification in front of them. For a household with two children on two curricula that is the practical difference: two specialists on two different evenings rather than one person who can reach the district.

There is also a budgeting consequence that a mixed household feels and a single-curriculum household does not. The two systems put their pressure in different places in the year: an IGCSE child's demands concentrate in Year 11, while a Diploma child's internal deadlines for coursework arrive steadily across two years. Treating both as one line in the household budget reliably produces a shortage in the fortnight when both land at once.

What follows is the detail a mixed household needs: how the two systems actually differ in what tutoring has to do, how to establish which board each child is on for nothing, the two exam calendars set side by side, where the transition gaps sit when a child moves between curricula mid-key-stage, the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside either curriculum, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges for running two arrangements at once.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-masd.programmesIntro: A mixed household may be tracking any combination of these. They are not variations on one qualification; they are assessed in genuinely different ways.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade on school-set boundaries, with no timed external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. Students become fluent at extended investigation and inexperienced at speed, which is the opposite profile to an IGCSE cohort of the same age.
programmes.countryNote: This is the qualification parents most often mistake for IGCSE, because a Year 10 or 11 child in an Abu Dhabi school may be on either. If your child is producing extended projects marked against lettered criteria rather than sitting past papers, they are in the MYP. The distinction decides whether tutoring targets criteria or mark schemes, so it is worth one email to the school.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations at the end of Year 11, identified by syllabus code: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology; Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1. Cambridge tiers many subjects as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher. Several Pearson subjects allow modular unit entry.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and is not available in Abu Dhabi. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of its grade. Forty-two subject points plus three core points gives the maximum of 45.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. IB exam and results dates are set and periodically revised by the IB, and none are published here — confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator. What governs a Diploma term in practice is the school's internal deadline calendar for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which bites months before anything external.

programmes.name: A Level, as the other post-16 route
programmes.description: The alternative sixth-form pathway after IGCSE, with three or four subjects examined in depth. Several schools in the corridors Masdar City families use offer both A Level and the IB Diploma, which makes the Year 11 grade set a genuine fork rather than a formality.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to a mixed household because the decision is often made for two children at once, and the answer may differ between them. A student who thrives on depth in three subjects and a student who needs breadth and a structured core are not the same case, and the IGCSE grade set constrains which options are open. Ask the sixth form directly rather than inferring from a prospectus.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-masd.subjectsIntro: These are the IB courses a Masdar City household most often needs, with what each assesses and where marks go. The IGCSE grid follows separately because the assessment model is different.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with HL adding a third paper of extended investigations. Technically able students lose marks to compressed working rather than to the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. The calculator is examined, and a correct result with no stated model behind it earns a fraction of the marks offered.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and nuclear physics with HL extensions. Marks go on unit prefixes, unstated assumptions in extended responses, and uncertainty treatment in the Internal Assessment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic pathways are the usual breaking point, and an IA with a clean graph still scores poorly if the method does not justify the range chosen.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology and physiology. The data-based paper separates grades, and the loss is describing a trend when the command term asked for a mechanism.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and development. Diagrams carry heavy credit and must be referenced in the prose; the IA commentaries are marked on explicit theory applied to real published articles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Literary and non-literary texts, the Individual Oral, the HL Essay and guided analysis. Paper 1 marks go to description of content instead of analysis of technique.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, networks, abstract data structures at HL and the solution-development IA. The IA scores on documented design and testing rather than on how impressive the program is.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the IA suite
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, a 4,000-word independent essay, and a per-subject Internal Assessment. Our role on all of these is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts.

subjects.name: Group 2 languages
subjects.description: Language acquisition across productive and receptive skills. Coverage is genuinely thinner for less-taught languages, and we say so before you pay rather than offering a near miss.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-masd.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of a mixed household, by syllabus code where it matters. Cambridge and Pearson examine the same subjects differently, so the code decides the revision.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics. Algebraic manipulation is the main loss at the higher tiers, since almost every multi-step question routes through it.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. Circuits are the standard breaking point and the practical-skills component rewards precise method description.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, electrolysis and organic chemistry. Moles and ionic equations concentrate the marks; qualitative analysis rewards learned observations.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, inheritance and ecology. Large content, and the losses are command-term failures rather than gaps in knowledge.

igcseSubjects.name: English First and Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, directed writing and composition, or the four skills for additional-language candidates. A repeatable writing structure moves this grade faster than more reading does.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Markets, the macroeconomy, business functions and finance. Diagram accuracy carries marks, and extended answers lose credit for listing points without evaluating them in context.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
igcseSubjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, algorithms and programming. Pseudocode and trace tables are reliable marks that students treat as optional.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional and further mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Material overlapping early AS content: advanced algebra, series, identities and calculus foundations. A short, cheap bridge into sixth-form maths for a secure student.

sections.heading: What a "near me" search returns in Masdar City, and what it means
paragraphs: A location search assumes the answer is a person within driving distance, and in most neighbourhoods that assumption is roughly sound. In Masdar City it is not, for a structural reason rather than a reputational one. The district was built as a research and clean-technology hub around a university campus. It has a small residential population, a pedestrianised core and no school inside its boundary. Teaching the IB or IGCSE for a living clusters where the schools are.

What the search will return is agencies willing to send someone from the Khalifa City corridor or Al Reef, with the airport-road journey and the walk into the pedestrian core priced into the hourly rate. That is a legitimate service. What it does not tell you is whether the person sent teaches your child's named qualification at your child's level, which is the question that actually determines whether the money does anything.

The gap is particularly wide in a household tracking two curricula. One visiting tutor covering a Year 10 IGCSE physicist and a Year 12 Diploma mathematician is, by arithmetic, a generalist in at least one of those roles. Online delivery breaks the constraint: two specialists, two slots, one household, and nobody driving anywhere.

So the useful reframing is to stop asking who is near and start asking who teaches the qualification. That reordering is available to a family in this district precisely because the local pool is thin, which turns an apparent disadvantage into a free decision.

sections.heading: Two curricula under one roof: how they actually differ
paragraphs: Families moving into Abu Dhabi mid-key-stage often assume IB and IGCSE are two brands of the same thing. They are not, and the differences change what tutoring should do. IGCSE is a terminal examination system: content is taught across two years and assessed by papers at the end, with tiered entries capping or opening the grade range. The skills that pay are recall under timing, mark-scheme phrasing and paper technique.

The IB is a programme rather than a set of subjects. The Middle Years Programme assesses against lettered criteria with no external papers in most schools. The Diploma combines externally examined papers with an Internal Assessment in every subject plus a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The skills that pay include independent written work produced over months, which has no IGCSE equivalent.

That asymmetry has a practical consequence for a mixed household. The IGCSE child needs timed practice and error correction, concentrated in the final year. The Diploma child needs that too, plus process coaching on independent work spread across two years with internal deadlines set by the school. The two children need different kinds of hours at different points in the calendar, and budgeting for them as one line produces a shortage at the worst moment.

It also means the two children should not share a tutor. Reading an Internal Assessment draft against published criteria and drilling a Cambridge 0625 physics paper are different professional skills, and someone doing both for one household is doing at least one of them adequately rather than well.

sections.heading: Finding out which board your child is on, for nothing
paragraphs: This takes one email and it is the precondition for every other decision on this page. Ask the school office or the head of year for the qualification name and, where it is an IGCSE, the syllabus code. The code is unambiguous in a way a subject name never is.

Cambridge codes are four digits: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language. Pearson Edexcel codes carry a number and letters: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. IB Diploma courses are named by subject and level, so the answer should come back as, for instance, Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL rather than as "IB maths". MYP subjects come back as subject groups with criteria.

Then use the answer as a filter on anyone you speak to. Give a prospective tutor the code and the level. If they ask which tier applies and which paper pattern governs your child's exam year, they know the qualification. If they treat IGCSE as a single thing, or offer to cover both your children, you have learned what you are being sold before paying for it.

There is a second reason to get this right which has nothing to do with tutoring. Entry administration, tiering and timetabling are the school's responsibility, and a parent who knows the exact qualification is in a much better position to ask sensible questions at a parents' evening about tier decisions, option blocks and whether a set has a settled teacher this year. Those conversations are free and they are frequently more consequential than the tutoring.

sections.heading: Two exam calendars, side by side
paragraphs: A household tracking both systems is tracking two calendars, and the planning error is treating them as one. Here is what is fixed. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi — a point worth stating because it circulated widely in the wrong direction.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November. Pearson's published history gives the shape of the wait: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so open the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date.

On the IB side, Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. We publish no IB exam or results dates on this page: the IB sets them, revises them periodically, and our sources for them could not be verified directly, so the only safe route is your school's IB coordinator. What does govern a Diploma term is the school's own internal deadline calendar for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and those deadlines usually land well before anything external.

The practical move for a mixed household is to put both calendars on one sheet in September, mark the school's internal deadlines on it, and look for the collisions. There is usually one: an Extended Essay draft due in the same fortnight as an IGCSE mock. Knowing that in September is worth more than any number of tutoring hours bought in that fortnight.

sections.heading: Transition gaps: moving between systems mid-key-stage
paragraphs: This is the section most relevant to a research district, because families here move on employment cycles. A child arriving in Year 10 from a different system, or moving from IGCSE or MYP into the Diploma, has a specific and findable set of gaps rather than a general deficit. Treating it as a general deficit is how families end up buying a year of tutoring for a problem that needed eight sessions.

The gaps are structural as often as they are topical. A student from a system with continuous assessment moving into terminal IGCSE examinations has rarely sat a full paper under timing. A student moving from MYP into Diploma maths or sciences is fluent at investigation and inexperienced at speed and at presenting method for a mark scheme. A student moving from IGCSE into the Diploma meets an Internal Assessment in every subject with no equivalent in their previous experience.

There are topical gaps too and they are usually narrow. A syllabus taught in a different order leaves one or two units untouched rather than a year missing. The efficient approach is a diagnostic against the new syllabus — a past paper or a criterion-marked task — which identifies exactly which units and which skills are absent, followed by a short block aimed only at those.

The expensive version is to start at the beginning of the new course and work forwards, which re-teaches material the student already holds. Ask any tutor how they will establish what is missing before teaching anything. If the answer is not a diagnostic task, the plan is a guess.

sections.heading: Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside either curriculum
paragraphs: A family new to the UAE is often surprised that their child studies Arabic, social studies and Islamic education alongside a British or IB curriculum. This is a federal requirement rather than a school policy: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Every emirate's requirement sits on that federal baseline.

The emirate regulator then implements it. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain that is ADEK, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's regulator KHDA publishes detailed mandatory-subject guidelines, which are a useful illustration of the kind of detail these requirements carry: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction; Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs; instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with an advised minimum lesson length of 25 minutes; and a prohibition on using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry.

Those specifics are Dubai's published implementation, not Abu Dhabi's, and they are quoted here only to show the shape of the obligation. For your own school, ask ADEK's requirements through the school rather than assuming the Dubai detail applies.

The point for a tutoring decision is a planning one. These subjects occupy real timetable hours and real homework time alongside the examined curriculum, which is part of why a Year 11 or Diploma week fills up faster than parents expect. One further detail is worth knowing for the equivalency count: for the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education requires.

sections.heading: Covering two children from one district, and what it costs
paragraphs: The operational question a mixed household actually has is how to run two different arrangements without the week collapsing. The answer is two slots on two evenings with two specialists, which is straightforward online and genuinely difficult in person. An in-home arrangement means two journeys, or one tutor stretched across two qualifications, and from Masdar City each journey carries the airport road plus the walk into the pedestrian core.

On cost, the published market bands for this emirate, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300. An in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500 with the journey inside the fee. A named IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates put mid-range weekly sessions at AED 600 to 1,200 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above.

Two children at mid-range weekly sessions therefore sits somewhere around AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month, and that is the figure a household should decide about rather than the hourly rate. The useful discipline is to stagger rather than to double: one child on a weekly arrangement where the gap is broad, the other on a defined block where it is narrow, with the heavier spend placed in the term each child's calendar demands it rather than in both at once.

IB Gram publishes no hourly price here. There is a free trial lesson and a consultation per child, and the figures above are the market's, included so you can price any quote you receive, ours among them.

What that requires from you is modest and worth getting right in the first session. A table rather than a bed. Headphones. For maths and the sciences, a camera angled at paper or a tablet and stylus so the tutor can see handwritten working as it happens. For written subjects, the draft in a form the tutor can read on screen alongside the student. The district supplies the rest: reliable connectivity, a quiet building, and no visitor to walk through a pedestrianised core.

On coverage, the honest position rather than a claim to cover everything. Common IB courses and both IGCSE boards in the main subjects are well covered, and a trial lesson is usually arranged within a few days to a week. Narrow Higher Level combinations and less-taught Group 2 languages are genuinely thinner. If the right specialist is not free we say so before you pay, and name the options: wait for a slot, start on a related component, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening.

faqs.question: Are there IB or IGCSE tutors actually based in Masdar City?
faqs.answer: Very few, for a structural reason. The district was built as a research and clean-technology hub around a university campus, with a small residential population, a pedestrianised core and no school inside its boundary. Teaching the IB or IGCSE for a living clusters where schools are — mainly the Khalifa City corridor and the island districts. What a local search returns is agencies willing to send someone in from there, with the airport-road journey and the walk priced into the rate, which answers a logistics question rather than an academic one.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on IGCSE or the IB MYP?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the qualification name and, if it is an IGCSE, the syllabus code. Cambridge codes are four digits such as 0580 Mathematics or 0625 Physics; Pearson codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. IB courses come back as a subject and level. A quick behavioural test also works: a child producing extended projects marked against lettered criteria is in the MYP, while a child sitting past papers under timing is being prepared for a terminal IGCSE. The distinction decides what tutoring should target.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a Year 10 IGCSE child and a Year 12 Diploma child?
faqs.answer: They can be booked to, and it is not what you want. Drilling a Cambridge 0625 physics paper and reading an Internal Assessment draft against published criteria are different professional skills, and one person doing both for one household is doing at least one of them adequately rather than well. Online delivery removes the compromise: two specialists on two evenings, one point of contact for scheduling. An in-home arrangement forces either a generalist or two separate journeys into a district with a pedestrianised core.

faqs.question: What actually differs between IGCSE and IB for tutoring purposes?
faqs.answer: IGCSE is terminal: two years of content assessed by papers at the end, with tiered entries that cap or open the grade range, so tutoring targets mark schemes, timing and paper technique, concentrated in Year 11. The IB Diploma combines external papers with an Internal Assessment in every subject plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, so tutoring also has to coach independent written work across two years against school-set internal deadlines. Different kinds of hours, at different points in the calendar, which matters when budgeting for two children.

faqs.question: Which exam series does each system use in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series; its February and March series is offered to India only and is not available here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Abu Dhabi schools enter the IB May session. We publish no specific IB dates because the IB sets and revises them and our sources could not be verified directly, so confirm those with your school's IB coordinator. For both IGCSE boards, open the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date.

faqs.question: How long is the wait for IGCSE results?
faqs.answer: Pearson's published history gives the pattern. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, roughly eight to nine weeks after the summer window. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, about two months after that series. The November 2026 final timetable itself ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are backward-looking dates quoted so you can plan the wait; future series dates get revised, so check the board's live timetable before acting on anything.

faqs.question: We have just moved to Abu Dhabi mid-year. What should we buy first?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic, not a course. A child arriving mid-key-stage has findable gaps rather than a general deficit: usually one or two untouched units because the previous syllabus ran in a different order, plus a structural gap such as never having sat a full paper under timing. One session on a diagnostic task against the new syllabus identifies exactly what is missing, and a short block of six to eight sessions closes it. Starting at the beginning of the new course re-teaches material your child already holds, at full price.

faqs.question: What is the hardest part of moving from IGCSE into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The Internal Assessment in every subject, which has no real IGCSE equivalent. A student arriving from terminal examinations is practised at recall under timing and inexperienced at producing independent written work over months against published criteria, with a research question they chose themselves. That is a process skill, and it is the one where early help is cheap and late help is expensive. A block early in DP1 on how the criteria work across subjects is worth more than the same hours spent in DP2 on a draft already due.

faqs.question: Why does my child study Arabic and Islamic education alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Because it is a federal requirement rather than a school choice. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, and each emirate's regulator implements that baseline. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain that regulator is ADEK. Dubai's KHDA publishes detailed guidelines on class organisation, language of instruction and lesson length as an illustration of the obligation's shape. Ask your own school what ADEK requires rather than assuming the Dubai detail transfers.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic education count towards Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not towards the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education requires on the British track. The published requirement is five accredited subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education expressly excluded from that count, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. A page currently ranking in this market states six subjects are needed, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry.

faqs.question: What does it cost to support two children on two curricula?
faqs.answer: Price the monthly figure rather than the hourly one. Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and a named IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with Bestimate's 2026 estimates giving AED 600 to 1,200 a month for mid-range weekly sessions. Two children at that level sits around AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month. The sensible discipline is to stagger rather than double: weekly where the gap is broad, a defined block where it is narrow.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Masdar City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. For this district the case is unusually clear: an in-home tutor faces the airport-road journey plus a walk into the pedestrianised core, two children on two curricula would mean two journeys or one generalist, and the market premium for the format pays for logistics rather than teaching. Online, you get a specialist per qualification.

faqs.question: What if nobody covers one of my children's subjects?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. Common IB courses and both IGCSE boards in the main subjects are well covered, with a trial usually arranged within a few days to a week. Narrow Higher Level combinations and less-taught Group 2 languages are genuinely thinner. In those cases we name the options: wait for a slot, begin on a related component such as an Internal Assessment with a specialist in that part, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening, disclosed before the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees the school my child attends?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai sits with KHDA; Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods, so a regulator's remit can extend well beyond inspection.

faqs.question: What should we send before free trial lessons for two children?
faqs.answer: Per child: the qualification name, the syllabus code and tier for an IGCSE or the subject and level for an IB course, the school name, and the last two marked assessments with teacher comments. Plus any Internal Assessment or Extended Essay draft in progress. And one household detail: the time each child is actually home, since the commute from Al Raha is twenty minutes and from Saadiyat closer to an hour. With that we can propose a specialist per qualification and two slots that do not collide.

We teach Masdar City students live over one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, cover IB programmes and both IGCSE boards, state coverage limits before you pay, and run no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Send the qualifications, the marked work and the arrival times, and take a free trial lesson per child.

intro.heading: The honest version of what is available near Mohammed Bin Zayed City
paragraphs: Start with what is true. For Year 7 to Year 9 mathematics, for mainstream IGCSE subjects at Core tier, for English support and for general study skills, Mohammed Bin Zayed City has a reasonable local supply of competent tutors, and a family that wants somebody in the room can find one. Nothing on this page argues otherwise, and a provider who pretends the local market is useless is selling rather than advising.

Then the part nobody publishes. There is a specific list of courses where the pool in any single Abu Dhabi community is thin to the point of being empty in a given term, and where widening the search adds travel time rather than expertise. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Theory of Knowledge. Extended-tier chemistry tied to an internal assessment or coursework deadline in the same month. Edexcel-specific science codes in a family that assumed Cambridge. Arabic as a first language. Coordinated Sciences, where the syllabus version determines half the content.

What happens when a family searches for one of those locally is predictable. They are not told the pool is empty. They are offered the nearest person who says yes, which is usually a capable graduate who has never taught that course to an examination, and the gap surfaces three or four sessions later when the explanation of a mark scheme does not match what the school said. By then the diagnostic hours have been paid for and will have to be paid for again.

Mohammed Bin Zayed City makes this worse for a structural reason rather than a reputational one. It is a large mainland community whose population is spread across several curricula, so the Diploma cohort in particular is distributed thinly between schools rather than concentrated in one. Thin demand produces thin local supply. That is arithmetic, not a judgement about the area, and it applies equally to several of the newer communities in the emirate.

This page is written to be useful whoever you hire. It names the scarce courses and says what to do about each. It maps the transition gaps between curricula, subject by subject, because transfers are common in these zones. It collects the word and page limits for assessed components into one reference table, which almost no competitor publishes. It explains how Ramadan and the UAE academic calendar move revision windows. And it states the honesty boundary on assessed work. IB Gram provides no home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, and that has been the position on every country page we publish since the first one went live. The lesson reaches a desk in your own home over live video, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own worksheet open, which is a different proposition from a car at the gate and should be judged as one.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-moha.programmesIntro: Four programmes account for nearly every request from these communities, and a dual-board household often runs two of them at once. The notes below describe what each one actually demands of a tutor.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries weight in every subject, and school internal deadlines govern the year more tightly than anything the board publishes. Support concentrates on assessment criteria, research design and command-term discipline rather than on content coverage alone.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a wrong date acted on by a family is worse than no date. The internal deadline calendar held by your school's IB coordinator is the document that actually binds, and it is worth requesting in writing at the start of Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment against four criteria per subject, graded 1 to 8, with no terminal written papers in most schools. Students develop investigation and communication strongly and meet structured examination technique late, which is the single most common transition problem in this corridor.
programmes.countryNote: Because MYP cohorts here are smaller than the British-track ones, a student moving from MYP into an IGCSE school is often the only one in the room with that background. Their specific gap, which is paper technique rather than content, goes unnoticed in a class where most students have the opposite profile.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written assessment organised by syllabus code, with most subjects tiered into Core and Extended. The code determines the paper structure, the formula provision and the mark scheme, which is why a tutor should be matched to 0620 Extended rather than to chemistry.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered in India only and belongs in no Abu Dhabi plan.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track route here, with codes including 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, tiered Foundation and Higher. Question phrasing, paper structure and formula provision differ from Cambridge, so revision material does not transfer cleanly between boards even where content overlaps.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those lead times are why resit planning precedes the first result.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-moha.subjectsIntro: Diploma courses first. The notes say what the course demands of a tutor, which is the relevant question when deciding whether a local generalist will do.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The hardest Diploma course to staff locally in any Abu Dhabi community. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers, vectors and substantially harder calculus, and Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so a tutor needs the course rather than the mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Easier to staff, because statistics and modelling are more widely taught, but Higher Level carries matrices and graph theory that a generalist will not have met. Students who chose it as the lighter route need statistics support, not algebra support.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Scarce when tied to an internal assessment deadline, because the research-design conversation needs somebody who has supervised one. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations decide most grades, and Higher Level Paper 3 rewards experimental reasoning over recall.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Reasonably available at Standard Level, thinner at Higher Level. The usual failure is mathematical rather than conceptual: a student who understands the physics and cannot rearrange quickly loses marks that algebra work recovers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most widely available of the sciences locally. Content is heavy and learnable independently, so paid hours are best spent on extended-response structure and on internal assessment design, where experimental errors cap the mark whatever the write-up looks like.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Almost nobody advertises it and almost nobody teaches it, which makes it the second scarcest request after Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay are both assessed against published criteria and both routinely started far too late.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research with a school supervisor. Useful support is narrowing the research question, interrogating method and checking referencing. The writing is entirely the student's, which is a boundary worth confirming with any provider before you hire.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Available locally in reasonable numbers. Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline decide the grade, and Gulf-specific examples are legitimate and under-used by candidates in this region, which makes them a cheap source of marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis and the individual oral carry the course. The oral rewards a global issue that is genuinely arguable rather than merely current, and structure is far more teachable than reading taste.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.levels: SL, and HL for Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic as a first language is the scarcer request; Arabic B and ab initio are more findable. All of them reward short frequent practice over intensive blocks, and the oral component carries weight students discover late.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-moha.igcseSubjectsIntro: And the IGCSE side of a dual-board household, where the syllabus code governs everything and the board question has to be settled before any revision set is built.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Widely available locally. Circle theorems, trigonometry with a drawn diagram and histograms with unequal class widths return marks fastest, and practice must come from the board the child is entered for.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Available at Core, thinner at Extended. Moles calculations and organic pathways decide the grade, and the paper rewards exact wording, so a student with the right idea and loose language is losing recoverable marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cost the most marks, then uncertainty handling and graph gradients in the practical paper. Units and significant figures account for a surprising share of the rest.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: The easiest science to find a tutor for and often the one that needs the fewest paid hours, because the content is learnable alone. Extended-response structure is the exception worth buying.

igcseSubjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
igcseSubjects.description: A scarce request, because the double award cuts specific sub-topics rather than simplifying everything, and a tutor working from the single-science syllabus wastes hours on content this course does not assess.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Widely available and the highest-yield English option for paid hours, since the exercises are formulaic and most of the gain sits in technique and timing rather than general language ability.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Both assessed on application rather than recall, and both findable locally. Business Studies is entirely case-study driven, so practice has to use real inserts rather than definitions.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
igcseSubjects.description: One of the scarcest requests in the corridor, and a subject where KHDA's published guidance for Dubai schools requires teachers of Arabic to hold the authority's approval, which indicates how specialised the teaching is treated as being.

sections.heading: The scarcity map, named rather than implied
paragraphs: No competitor page studied for this search discloses a coverage limit. Several route UAE parents to a foreign phone number without saying where teaching happens, and one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. The useful alternative is to publish the limit, because a family who knows which requests are hard can plan around it instead of discovering it in week four.

The courses below are scarce for reasons that have nothing to do with their difficulty. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is scarce because the number of people who have taught it to an examination is genuinely small everywhere. Theory of Knowledge is scarce because it is nobody's degree subject. Coordinated Sciences is scarce because the syllabus version determines half the content and most tutors have only taught the single sciences. Arabic as a first language is scarce because it is treated as a specialism by the regulators themselves.

What to do about each differs, and that is the point of naming them. Some are worth waiting a week for, because the alternative is paying twice for the same diagnosis. Some can be started with a narrower piece of work while the specialist frees up, such as paper technique or criteria coaching. Some are better served by a referral elsewhere, and saying so costs a provider a booking and saves a family a term. The table sets out which is which. Read the fallback column before the match-time column, because the fallback is the part that determines whether a wait costs you anything.

sections.heading: Transition gaps, mapped subject by subject
paragraphs: Transfers are routine in these communities, and the resulting difficulty is almost always specific rather than general. A student who moves systems does not become worse at a subject. They arrive missing one identifiable thing, and the useful work is naming it rather than restarting the subject. Families who get the diagnosis right spend weeks on it; families who do not spend terms.

The patterns repeat often enough to be predictable. Moving from an Indian or Ministry curriculum into IGCSE, the gap is structured question technique and showing working in a form that earns method marks, not content. Moving from MYP into IGCSE, it is terminal paper technique and timing. Moving from IGCSE into the Diploma, it is open-ended investigation, early calculus in mathematics, and the entirely unfamiliar genre of independent assessed writing. Moving from an American curriculum into the Diploma, it is the weight placed on internal assessment and the discipline of command terms.

The transition block should have a stated end. A tutor who diagnoses the gap in the first session, writes it down, works through it and then says the work is finished has done the job. One who converts a six-week transition into an indefinite weekly arrangement has quietly changed what you are buying. Ask for the diagnosis in writing and for a session count at the start, and ask for a short handover note at the end that you can give the school. A school that knows what was closed and what remains can pick the work up in class, which is free and often more effective than another paid hour.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, in one place
paragraphs: Assessed components carry limits, students routinely discover them late, and exceeding one is a self-inflicted loss that no amount of good content recovers. Collecting the limits into a single reference is the kind of thing almost no tutoring page bothers with, and it is among the most useful fifteen minutes a Diploma family can spend. Verify every figure against the current subject guide through your school's coordinator, because limits and guidance are revised and the school holds the governing version.

The ones that matter most are easy to remember. The Extended Essay is a maximum of four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is a maximum of sixteen hundred. The exhibition commentary is a maximum of nine hundred and fifty. The mathematical exploration is guided by a recommended page range rather than a hard word count, which students often read as having no limit at all, and then produce something unreadable that loses presentation and communication marks.

The practical discipline is to write to the limit from the first draft rather than cutting at the end. A student who drafts six thousand words for a four-thousand-word Extended Essay has to delete a third of their argument under deadline pressure, and what gets deleted is usually the analysis rather than the description, because description is easier to see as necessary. Planning to the limit is a structural decision made at the outline stage, and it is one of the few places where a tutor's intervention is both entirely legitimate and immediately worth money.

sections.heading: Ramadan and the shape of the UAE academic year
paragraphs: Revision planning in the UAE has a variable nobody outside the region accounts for. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the school year shifts, and in some years it lands close to mock examinations or to internal assessment deadlines while in others it sits comfortably clear of both. A tutoring plan made in September without checking where Ramadan falls is a plan with a hole in it.

Schools in the UAE commonly shorten the day during the month, which changes the shape of the afternoon rather than freeing it: children are home earlier but the household rhythm shifts later, with evenings reorganised around Iftar. For a Mohammed Bin Zayed City family the practical consequence is that a 16:30 session may work better than usual for part of the month and that a post-Iftar slot is often the most productive hour available, provided it is agreed in advance rather than improvised weekly.

The other calendar features worth planning around are more stable. School examination weeks are better used for short reviews of just-sat papers than for new content. The long summer break is the cheapest time to close a transition gap, because nothing competes with it. And the weeks immediately after results arrive are when resit decisions have to be made quickly, which is why those decisions are better pre-agreed. Because nobody travels to a UAE address for these lessons, every one of those adjustments costs nothing to make.

sections.heading: The boundary, for a household running both boards
paragraphs: A dual-board family meets two different versions of the academic-honesty question, and both deserve a plain answer. On the Diploma side the exposure is large: internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge components are all submitted as the student's own work, with declarations, and schools in this corridor run originality checks as routine. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, not on whoever sold them the document.

At least one provider visible in UAE search results advertises completed Internal Assessments at a stated price. The honest description of that transaction is that the student takes all of the risk for a mark that may be withdrawn. No tutor may write, draft, rewrite or edit to submission any part of an assessed component, at any price, under any deadline pressure, and a provider who will not say that plainly has answered a question you did not have to ask twice.

On the IGCSE side the exposure moves to materials rather than writing. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and reproducing or distributing them as downloads is copyright infringement, with unreleased material carrying a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor should link the official source and mark your child's own attempt against the published scheme. What both sides share is a simple test: ask any provider what they will refuse to do, and listen to how quickly the answer arrives. Somebody who has thought about it answers in one sentence; somebody who has not starts explaining how flexible they can be, which is the answer in a different form.

Marking done on the student's own attempt, with lost marks named in writing

sections.heading: Using one free hour as a test
paragraphs: A free trial is only useful if you know what you are testing. Used well it answers three questions in sixty minutes that no profile, review or phone call can answer, and it costs nothing, takes no card details and creates no commitment. Used badly it becomes an introductory chat, and the family ends up making the decision on exactly the impressions they were trying to get past.

Send the material first: the marked script for an IGCSE student, or the criteria and the school's internal dates for a Diploma student, plus the course, level, board and code. Then watch for three things in the hour. Does the tutor work on something from that material rather than on a generic topic? Can they say which lost marks are content, which are method and which are timing? And does your child follow the explanation, which is a question only your child can answer and is worth asking them directly afterwards.

Finish by asking the two closing questions. What happens if the match is wrong, and what will you refuse to do. The first tells you whether a replacement costs anything. The second sorts a teaching service from the other kind. Three providers tested the same way in a week give you a genuine comparison, which is a better basis for a decision than a search radius and considerably quicker than driving around Abu Dhabi meeting people. Keep the written replies as well, because a provider who answers precisely before any money changes hands tends to keep answering precisely afterwards.
