sections.heading: When a local tutor is the right answer
paragraphs: This page has argued that proximity is the wrong primary filter, and that argument has limits worth stating. A young child who needs an adult physically present, a student for whom in-person support has been recommended by a professional, and a household with unreliable connectivity are all cases where a local tutor is correct and the travel premium is money well spent. Pretending otherwise would be selling rather than advising, and it would be obvious.

For the courses on the scarcity map, the calculation inverts. The specialist who has taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level or supervised a chemistry internal assessment is unlikely to live within a workable drive of these zones, and insisting that they do means taking a generalist instead. For an academic subject at this level, a shared whiteboard with the school's own worksheet open loses very little, and it gains the one thing that actually moves a grade.

The honest resolution is not an argument but a test. One free hour, structured as described above, settles it for your particular child in less time than it would take an in-home tutor to reach Mohammed Bin Zayed City from the Corniche. If the format does not work, you have learned that for nothing. If it does, the scarcity map stops being a constraint and becomes a list of courses you can now actually staff. That is the whole of the argument, and it rests on one free hour rather than on anything this page has claimed.

faqs.question: Which subjects genuinely have no local tutor around MBZ City?
faqs.answer: In any single term, the thinnest are Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, Arabic as a first language, Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Edexcel-specific science codes where a family had assumed Cambridge. Extended-tier chemistry becomes scarce at internal assessment deadline season. None of that is about the area: these communities have a curriculum-mixed population, so the Diploma cohort is spread thinly between schools, and thin demand produces thin local supply. Mainstream IGCSE subjects and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level are adequately covered locally.

faqs.question: What should I do if the course I need is on that scarce list?
faqs.answer: Three options, and which one applies depends on the course. Wait a week for the right specialist, which is usually cheaper than paying twice for the same diagnosis. Start with a narrower piece of work with another tutor in the meantime, such as paper technique or criteria coaching, so the time is not lost. Or take a referral elsewhere if the wait is unreasonable. What you should not accept is a fast general match presented as a specialist, because the gap surfaces in session four and the diagnostic hours get repeated.

faqs.question: How long is an IB Extended Essay allowed to be?
faqs.answer: A maximum of four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at sixteen hundred, and the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty. Verify all of these against the current subject guide through your school's coordinator, because guidance is revised and the school holds the governing version. The practical discipline is to plan to the limit at outline stage rather than cutting at the end, because a student deleting a third of a draft under deadline pressure almost always cuts analysis and keeps description, which is the wrong way round.

faqs.question: My child just moved from an Indian curriculum into IGCSE. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Usually question technique rather than content. Students arriving from Indian or Ministry curriculum schools typically have strong procedural arithmetic and algebra and little experience of the structured multi-step question style an IGCSE paper uses, or of showing working in a form that earns method marks rather than simply reaching an answer. An explain question answered with a description earns a fraction of the credit however well the material is known. Four to six weeks of focused work closes it, and it is cheapest immediately after the move.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a revision plan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It moves roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so in some years it sits close to mock examinations or internal assessment deadlines and in others it is clear of both. Schools commonly shorten the day, which reorganises the afternoon rather than freeing it, and household evenings reshape around Iftar. The productive move is to agree a revised slot before the month rather than during it, often post-Iftar, and to use the period for technique work rather than new content. None of those changes costs anything when nobody is travelling.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting Theory of Knowledge support at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, and earlier than most families do. Both components are assessed against published criteria, both reward a specific kind of argument that is unlike any other subject, and almost nothing in a student's other five subjects prepares them for it. The difficulty is supply: almost nobody advertises Theory of Knowledge because it is nobody's degree subject, so expect a longer match. Start with criteria coaching rather than content, because the most common cause of a weak essay is not understanding what the prescribed title is asking for.

faqs.question: Do I need one tutor or two for a Diploma child and an IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Two, in almost every case, run as separate matches on one family schedule. IGCSE work is content coverage, board-specific paper technique and timing, measured against past papers. Diploma work is internal assessment design, criteria discipline and school internal deadlines. Somebody strong at one frequently has no useful opinion about the other, and hiring a single person because they live nearby is the specific error a near-me search encourages. Back-to-back slots on one evening give you the convenience without the compromise.

faqs.question: Why does the syllabus code matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it determines the paper structure, the formula provision and the mark scheme, all of which differ between Cambridge and Pearson even where the content is nearly identical. A tutor matched to chemistry rather than to 0620 Extended or 4CH1 Higher will teach correct chemistry against the wrong question style, and the first visible symptom is a mock result that makes no sense given the hours invested. Confirm the code and tier in writing from the school and hand that answer to every provider you speak to.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of my child's internal assessment if we are out of time?
faqs.answer: No, at any price and under any deadline. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge components are submitted as the student's own work with declarations, schools here run originality checks as routine, and a malpractice finding falls on the candidate rather than on whoever supplied the text. One provider in UAE search results sells completed Internal Assessments; the student carries all of that risk. What a tutor can legitimately do under time pressure is prioritise which criteria to rescue first.

faqs.question: What does ADEK actually do, and does it approve tutors?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain, and publishes inspection ratings for them. It does not approve, accredit or inspect private tutoring providers, and IB Gram holds no approval from ADEK, KHDA, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any provider claiming regulator approval for tutoring is making a claim worth checking carefully, because a KHDA educational services permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises and is not what a tutoring platform holds.

faqs.question: How should I use the free trial hour to actually learn something?
faqs.answer: Send your material first: the marked script for an IGCSE student, or the criteria and the school's internal dates for a Diploma student, with the course, level, board and code. Then watch three things. Does the tutor work from that material or from a generic topic? Can they separate content losses from method losses from timing losses? And ask your child afterwards whether the explanation landed, because that is the one judgement nobody else can make. Finish with the two closing questions about replacement and refusal.

faqs.question: Is online tuition a compromise for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For an academic subject at this level, very little is lost. A shared whiteboard, the school's own worksheet and a marked script on screen cover what a desk covers, and the hour buys somebody who has taught the exact course rather than the nearest available graduate. The genuine exceptions are a child who needs an adult physically present, a case where in-person support has been professionally recommended, and unreliable connectivity. Test it with the free hour rather than deciding in advance; it settles faster than any argument about the format.

faqs.question: When should we book help for internal assessment season?
faqs.answer: A term before the school's internal deadline, not in the month of it. Every Diploma cohort in the corridor hits those dates at roughly the same time, so the specialists who can supervise a research design well are committed early and what remains in deadline month is whoever is free. Get the internal calendar in writing from your coordinator at the start of the year and work backwards from it. Topic choice is where most of the grade is decided, and it is the step that cannot be rescued later.

faqs.question: What if we try a tutor and my child simply does not warm to them?
faqs.answer: Say so in week one or two and take a replacement, which costs nothing and repeats the trial with somebody else. Rapport is not a soft consideration at this level: a student who will not ask a question in the session is paying for a monologue. The arrangements that waste the most money are the ones a family keeps out of politeness, cancels twice, and then abandons without explaining why. Each child's match is reviewed separately after four sessions, and changing one does not disturb the other.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors actually based in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Some tutors are in the UAE and some are not, and you are told which before the trial rather than after it. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE, and no page here will suggest one exists. What is guaranteed about scheduling is the time zone: sessions are timed to Gulf Standard Time so they fit a Mohammed Bin Zayed City evening rather than somebody else's working day. Two competitor pages studied for this market route UAE parents to a foreign number without saying any of that.

intro.heading: The real question behind near me: what does this cost, and is the cheap version a saving?
paragraphs: A Mussafah parent searching for a tutor nearby is rarely indifferent to price. School fees are already the largest line in the household budget, two or three children may need support in the same term, and the published tutoring rates in this emirate span a factor of fourteen from bottom to top. The useful answer is not the cheapest number or the most impressive one. It is a clear account of what each band of spending buys, which bands are fine for which situations, and which purchases reliably waste money.

Start with the figures, because most pages in this search refuse to. Three of the six competitor pages measured for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no Abu Dhabi family transacts in. Against that, the market is actually quite legible. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

What separates those bands is not enthusiasm. It is whether the person has taught the specific syllabus to a grade boundary and read the mark scheme that decides the marks. A graduate who is good at maths can keep a Year 9 student company through practice and that is worth AED 50 an hour. The same person in front of a Year 12 Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student, eight weeks before the papers, is not cheap support; it is a wasted term. The reverse is also true, and worth saying: paying AED 650 an hour for a premium name to drill arithmetic with a Year 8 student is money spent on a mismatch.

The second thing this page does is count in hours rather than in rates. A single hourly figure hides the only number that matters to a household: the total across a course. A two-year IB Diploma with weekly support in two subjects is a different financial object from a six-session IGCSE diagnostic block, and families who compare hourly rates between the two are comparing nothing. There is a cost model further down that lays both out.

One point of honesty before the numbers. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The phrase people search is tutor near me, so that is the phrase this page uses, but the delivery for Mussafah families is one-to-one live video. That is also the cheaper half of the comparison, and the tables below show by how much, with every figure attributed to the provider that published it.

The first useful spend is two sessions explaining how criterion marks differ from percentages, because parents reading an MYP report as though it were a percentage grade make poor decisions about what to buy.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in external papers, with no Internal Assessment on most mathematics syllabuses. Spending is therefore concentrated and short: a diagnostic block to establish what is wrong, then a term or two of weekly sessions, then timed-paper work before the series. It is the best value programme to support because the target is narrow and measurable.
programmes.countryNote: Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entries exist across Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City schools. Before spending anything, get the syllabus code and the tier in writing, because a Core or Foundation entry caps the grade and no amount of late tutoring changes that. Checking the entry costs one email and can save a full term of fees.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muss.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject varies with how much of the grade sits in coursework and how scarce the specialism is. These are the subjects Mussafah families most often pay for, with the cost driver named.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested and among the most expensive to support, because Higher Level adds a third paper and the exploration carries a fifth of the grade. Two years of fortnightly support usually costs less than one panicked exam term of twice-weekly sessions.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches at the same level, because much of the work is modelling and interpretation that a student can practise independently once the method is taught. The exploration is still a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Cost is driven by the scientific investigation and by organic chemistry, which almost every student needs taught twice. Families who book supervision hours for the investigation early pay less than those who book crisis hours a fortnight before the internal deadline.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: The algebra is the bottleneck rather than the physics, so a maths repair block often does more for a physics grade than physics sessions do. That substitution is one of the cheapest wins available in an IB budget.

subjects.name: IB Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the difference between explain and evaluate carry the marks, and the portfolio commentaries need structured feedback rather than many hours. A short, well-timed block is better value than a continuous arrangement.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The cheapest subject to fix well, because the target is specific: non-calculator fluency, visible method, and the back-of-paper multi-step questions. Six to ten sessions often moves a grade when the losses are method rather than content.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Usually bought alongside maths, and the overlap makes them better value together than separately. Equation rearrangement, mole arithmetic and command-term discipline cover most of the marks at stake.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two calculator papers graded 9 to 1. Cost is lowest when the tier is confirmed early, because a Foundation entry caps the grade at 5 and a family paying for Higher-level preparation on a Foundation entry is paying for nothing.

subjects.name: IB Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge supervision
subjects.description: Priced by the block rather than by the hour in most of the market. The work is teaching the criteria and giving feedback on the student's own drafts; nobody should be paying anyone to produce this work, and one provider in this search sells exactly that.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, and a hidden cost in timetable terms rather than in fees. Budget the hours, not just the dirhams, when planning a Year 11 or Diploma Year 2 revision programme.

sections.heading: What each AED band actually buys, from the bottom up
paragraphs: The published bands in this market are not arbitrary and they are not a quality ladder either. Each one corresponds to a different thing being sold. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, which is where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise their entry tiers, you are buying supervised practice: someone able to do the work, keep a student on task, and answer questions. For a Year 8 or Year 9 student who will not sit down without company, that is correctly priced and genuinely useful.

At AED 150 to 300, the band where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, you are buying subject teaching: someone who knows the syllabus, has taught it before, and can explain the same idea three different ways when the first two fail. This is the band most exam-year students actually need. Above it, at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, you are buying mark-scheme knowledge: someone who has marked the paper, knows what each mark is awarded for, and can tell a student exactly why a correct answer scored two out of four. At AED 500 to 650, where BartyED publishes AED 650, you are buying scarcity and reputation, which is sometimes worth it for a narrow, late, high-stakes repair and is otherwise a transfer of money.

The practical rule that follows is about matching rather than about maximising. Pay the practice band for practice, the teaching band for teaching, and the mark-scheme band in the final term of an exam year when the difference between a 6 and a 7 is technique rather than content. Families who pay the top band all the way through, and families who pay the bottom band all the way through, both overspend; the first in dirhams, the second in outcomes. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page. The trial lesson is free with no card required, and the quote follows the diagnosis so it is attached to a plan.

sections.heading: Five ways tutoring money is wasted in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is buying hours before a diagnosis. A family notices a grade slipping, buys twelve sessions, and the tutor spends them re-teaching the syllabus because nobody established what was actually wrong. In most cases the losses were method, pacing and reading rather than content, and six sessions aimed at those would have moved the grade. A diagnostic block of four to six sessions costs less than half the twelve and tells you where to spend the rest.

The second is paying for the wrong tier. An IGCSE candidate entered for Cambridge 0580 Core cannot be awarded above a C, and a Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation entry caps at grade 5. A family paying for top-grade preparation on a capped entry is buying something that cannot be delivered, and the fix is an email to the exams officer in Year 10 rather than a term of fees in Year 11. The third is the mismatch in either direction: a premium examiner-led tutor drilling arithmetic with a Year 8 student, or a budget tutor sitting with a Diploma Higher Level candidate eight weeks before the papers.

The fourth is the slot that nobody can keep. A weekly session at a time the household cannot protect becomes fortnightly, then monthly, and the money already committed buys a fraction of the intended teaching. In this part of the emirate that is usually a scheduling arithmetic failure rather than a commitment failure. The fifth is late coursework supervision. An IB Internal Assessment is worth around a fifth of the subject grade, and buying crisis hours a fortnight before the internal deadline costs several times what the same hours cost spread across the months when the work was being planned and drafted. Of the five, this is the one with the largest gap between the cheap version and the expensive version of the same outcome.

sections.heading: Counting in hours: a two-year Diploma plan against one IGCSE term
paragraphs: Hourly rates make incomparable things look comparable. The question a household actually faces is what the whole course costs, and the two common shapes are completely different financial objects. An IGCSE intervention is short and narrow: a diagnostic block, a term of weekly sessions, then timed-paper work before the series. Call it twenty to thirty hours in total, concentrated inside one academic year.

A two-year IB Diploma plan with support in two subjects is a different order of commitment. Fortnightly across two years in two subjects is roughly eighty hours, plus supervision blocks for two Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay. Spread across twenty-four months, however, the monthly figure is often lower than the exam-term intensive a panicking family buys in the final spring, and the internal marks are better because the coursework was supervised while it was being produced rather than reviewed after it was finished.

The table sets both out at the published mid band so a family can see the shape rather than the slogan. Two cautions on reading it. These are market rates from provider pages and not IB Gram prices; our trial is free and our quote follows a diagnosis. And no plan of any size should be bought on the promise of a grade. Nobody can promise an outcome in an externally assessed qualification, and a provider who does is telling you something about their marketing rather than about their teaching. Read the table as a shape rather than as a quotation: the hours in the left column are what these plans typically take, and a household with a clear diagnosis often needs fewer, while a student who changed curriculum mid-course usually needs more.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, since near me includes four different businesses
paragraphs: A Mussafah search for a tutor nearby returns at least four kinds of business, and they are priced differently because they sell different things. An agency matches you to a tutor and takes a margin for vetting and replacement; a marketplace lists tutors and leaves the choice to you at a lower price and a higher risk of mismatch; an independent freelance tutor is usually cheapest for the same qualification level and carries no replacement arrangement if it goes wrong; a tuition centre with premises sells group teaching at a low per-student rate and a correspondingly low level of individual attention.

The right comparison is therefore not price against price but what happens when something fails. If the tutor is competent and wrong for the student, who changes them, and at whose cost? If a session is cancelled, is the hour lost? If the subject specialism turns out to be approximate, is there a second option? Those questions cost nothing to ask and they are the difference between a term of teaching and a term of politeness.

Two cautions worth more than any price comparison. First, a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a regulated entity: in Dubai that means a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, and in Abu Dhabi the emirate regulator is ADEK. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years. Ask which applies to whoever you are paying. Second, be sceptical of self-published ratings. Competitor pages in this research showed two different review totals on the same page, and one showed a perfect score from twenty reviews alongside a far larger claim about the number of students taught. A rating nobody can audit is decoration.

sections.heading: IB and IGCSE side by side: what the money is preparing for
paragraphs: A page covering both boards owes a parent the difference, because the spend follows the assessment design. IGCSE mathematics on Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 is externally assessed by written papers, with no Internal Assessment on the main mathematics syllabuses. All the preparation value therefore sits in paper technique, which is why short, well-aimed interventions work so well and why the total cost is low relative to the stakes.

The IB Diploma is a different object. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is assessed by two papers, one without a calculator and one with, each carrying forty per cent, with the exploration carrying the remaining twenty. At Higher Level there are three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty per cent, with the exploration again at twenty. Applications and Interpretation permits a calculator in both Standard Level papers. The consequence for a budget is that a fifth of the grade is produced at home over months, under supervision, and cannot be revised for in a final sprint.

That single structural fact explains most of the spending mistakes this page warns about. Families budget for exams and get surprised by coursework. The Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word ceiling and the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 words, both produced across months. Supervision of those is cheap when planned and expensive when urgent. One more boundary, stated plainly: a tutor teaches the criteria, works comparable examples and gives feedback on your child's own drafts. Nobody should be paying anyone to produce coursework, and one provider in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which exposes the student to malpractice proceedings rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before you pay anyone in this market
paragraphs: Most of the risk in this purchase can be removed with six questions, and none of them is about price. The first is which syllabus code and tier the tutor has taught, and when. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0580 Extended and marked it is a different proposition from one who is good at mathematics generally, and the difference is invisible in a profile description. The second is whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. If a fee is quoted for the permit itself, that tells you something.

Third, what happens if the match is wrong, and who bears the cost of changing. Fourth, how progress will be reported, and in what units. An answer about confidence is not a measurement; an answer about timed questions and classified errors is. Fifth, what the provider will not do: ask directly whether they will help with an Internal Assessment, and listen carefully to the answer. The right answer involves teaching criteria and giving feedback on the student's own work. Any version that involves producing, drafting or completing it should end the conversation.

Sixth, ask what any statistic on their page is based on. Several providers in this market publish satisfaction percentages, student counts and ratings with no sample size, date or method, and at least one shows two contradictory review totals on a single page. We publish none of those figures for the same reason we would not accept them from anyone else: we could not show you the underlying data. What we will show you is a free diagnostic trial, a written plan with a topic order, and a review at six sessions measured on timed questions, with the tutor changed if the match is wrong.

sections.heading: Why distance is a price signal in Abu Dhabi, not a quality signal
paragraphs: The near me search assumes proximity is a proxy for something. In this market it is a proxy for one thing only: the travel cost embedded in an in-home rate. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the clearest evidence that the gap is travel rather than teaching is that in-home quotes sit lower on the island, where journeys are short, and higher in Al Shamkha and Al Wathba, where they are long.

Proximity does not improve the teaching, because the syllabus, the papers and the grade boundaries are identical for every candidate in the emirate. What proximity constrains is choice. A Mussafah family choosing in-home is choosing among tutors willing to drive into the belt at the evening peak, which is a much smaller group than the set of people who teach that syllabus well. The usual outcome is a competent generalist rather than a specialist, and that substitution is the one trade in this market that reliably costs marks rather than dirhams.

There are real losses in going online and they deserve naming rather than burying. A young or distractible student is harder to supervise through a screen. Written working needs a tablet and stylus, or a phone propped over paper, for the tutor to see method as it forms. Both are worth testing in a free trial rather than assuming. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service available only in India, so if a physical presence in the room is what your child needs, buy it from the local market with the travel premium understood. This page would rather tell you that than take the booking.

faqs.question: What does an IB or IGCSE tutor near Mussafah actually cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Abu Dhabi market bands run wide. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Those are provider figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutoring in Abu Dhabi a saving or a false economy?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the student needs. At AED 33 to 65 an hour you are buying supervised practice: someone who can do the work and keep a student on task. For a Year 8 or Year 9 child who will not start without company, that is correctly priced and useful. For an exam-year candidate who needs to know why a correct answer scored two out of four, it is a wasted term, because mark-scheme knowledge is what the higher bands are selling. Match the band to the need rather than maximising or minimising the rate.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home tutor in Mussafah cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because travel is inside the price. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The clearest proof that the gap is travel rather than teaching is that in-home quotes sit lower on Abu Dhabi island, where journeys are short, and higher in Al Shamkha and Al Wathba, where they are long. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; home visits are available only in India.

faqs.question: How much should a Mussafah family budget for two years of IB Diploma support?
faqs.answer: At the published mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, fortnightly support in one subject across two Diploma years is roughly forty to forty-four hours, or about AED 6,000 to 13,200 in total. Two subjects doubles that. A supervision block for the Extended Essay adds eight to ten hours. Spread across twenty-four months the monthly figure is often lower than a single twice-weekly exam term bought in panic, and the internal marks tend to be better because coursework was supervised while it was being written.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way tutoring money is wasted here?
faqs.answer: Buying hours before a diagnosis. A grade slips, a family buys twelve sessions, and the tutor spends them re-teaching a syllabus the student mostly knows, because nobody established what was actually going wrong. In most cases the losses are method, pacing and reading rather than content, and six well-aimed sessions would have moved the grade. A four-to-six session diagnostic block costs less than half of the twelve and tells you where the rest of the money should go, or whether it is needed at all.

faqs.question: Could we be paying for a grade my child's exam entry cannot award?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens regularly. Cambridge grades the 0580 Core route C to G, so an A is unavailable on that entry. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 caps the Foundation tier at grade 5 while Higher runs 9 to 4. A family paying for top-grade preparation on a capped entry is buying something that cannot be delivered. Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code and the tier in writing during Year 10, while a change is still administratively possible. That email costs nothing and can save a full term of fees.

faqs.question: Does the Internal Assessment change how much IB support costs?
faqs.answer: Substantially, because around a fifth of each IB subject grade is produced at home across months rather than in an exam hall. That part cannot be revised for in a final sprint, so a budget built only around exam term will be surprised. Supervision is cheap when it is planned into the months the work is being drafted and expensive when bought as crisis hours a fortnight before the internal deadline. The Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word ceiling and the Theory of Knowledge essay to 1,600 words, both on the same long timescale.

faqs.question: Can I pay someone to write my child's Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: You should not, and we will not. A tutor teaches what the criteria reward, works a comparable example on a different problem, and gives feedback on your child's own drafts. Producing the work, supplying submittable text or editing a draft until the thinking is no longer the student's crosses into malpractice, and the consequences fall on the student rather than on the seller. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Treat that as a reason to avoid them rather than as a service option.

faqs.question: Which is better value for a Year 11 student: a tuition centre group or one-to-one?
faqs.answer: A group at a centre is cheaper per student and cannot follow one student's gaps, which is the whole point of the purchase when losses are specific. If the diagnosis says the student is broadly behind across a syllabus, a group can work. If it says the losses are method, pacing and three named topics, group pace will not touch them. The honest sequence is a short diagnostic block first, then choose, because the diagnosis also tells you whether the cheaper option would work.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in this market before I pay anything?
faqs.answer: Six questions, none about price. Which syllabus code and tier have you taught, and when? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Who changes a poor match, and at whose cost? How is progress reported, and in what units? What will you not do with an Internal Assessment? And what is the sample size, date and method behind any statistic on your page? A provider who answers all six clearly is a different proposition from one who answers on price alone.

faqs.question: Is the private tutor permit something I pay for as the parent?
faqs.answer: No. The private tuition work permit is the tutor's responsibility, it was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. If anyone asks you to cover a permit fee, that is a clear warning sign about the arrangement rather than a cost of tutoring.

faqs.question: Are the ratings and student numbers on tutoring sites in this market reliable?
faqs.answer: Treat them with caution. In the pages researched for this project, one provider showed two different review totals on the same page, and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews alongside a far larger claim about the number of students taught. A rating nobody can audit is decoration, and self-asserted review markup is against Google's structured-data policy as well as being a commercial representation. Ask for the sample size, the date and the method. We publish no such figures ourselves, for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: Do group discounts or sibling rates exist for Mussafah households with two children?
faqs.answer: In the wider market, yes, and the published monthly packages are the usual form: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, or AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Read the terms rather than the headline. The questions that matter are whether unused sessions roll over, how long a package stays valid, whether both children must take the same subject, and what happens if one child needs a different tutor. A package that cannot be split across two needs is cheaper per hour and more expensive per useful hour.

faqs.question: If we only have budget for six sessions, what should they be spent on?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic block, which is the highest-value six hours available in this market. The first session sits a full paper cold. Every lost mark is then classified as a method error, an arithmetic slip, a misread question or genuine unknown content. The remaining sessions attack whichever category is largest, and the block ends with a written statement naming the three topics still losing the most marks and whether the entry tier or level is right. You can take that to the school and spend nothing further.

faqs.question: Does paying more improve the odds of a particular grade?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise an outcome in an externally assessed qualification, and a provider who does is describing their marketing rather than their teaching. What more money reliably buys is a closer match: someone who has taught and marked the exact paper, who can explain why a correct answer scored two out of four, and who can say which three topics are still costing marks. That raises the quality of the work and still leaves the grade with the student on the day. We publish no score-improvement figures because we could not evidence one.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muss.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis before you buy the hours
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muss.closingBody: If you are weighing up what tutoring should cost for a Mussafah household, the cheapest useful move is also the first one. Ask the school for the syllabus code and the tier, or the IB subject and level, in writing. Then book a free trial lesson with no card required and let the tutor sit your child at the right level and watch the method. At the end you will know which error category is costing the most marks, whether the entry can deliver the grade you are aiming at, and how many hours the plan actually needs. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If the written diagnosis is all you want, take it and spend nothing further.

intro.heading: What proximity actually costs a Saadiyat Island family
paragraphs: Start with what you can verify, because that is the part of this decision you control. Three of the six competitor pages we examined for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. One page's structured data contradicts the price printed on the page itself. Another publishes a star rating it awarded itself. In a market where the basic numbers are withheld or inconsistent, the useful skill is knowing which claims can be checked.

None of that is an argument for distrust. It is an argument for arithmetic. A tutoring arrangement is one of the few education purchases a family makes entirely on its own judgement, without a regulator setting the price or a school vouching for the person, and the only protection available is knowing what each component of a quote is for before agreeing to it.

Four can. Whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, valid for two years, and applied for through MoHRE's own service page with a stated two-working-day completion time. Whether a named regulator approval exists, which is a specific licence rather than an adjective. Whether an AED figure has a source and a date attached. And whether the delivery format described matches what you are actually buying, which on a UAE page is the claim most often blurred.

Now the price of being near. Published market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, at AED 180-500. Bestimate's 2026 rate table quotes AED 180-350 for in-home; independent home tutors quote AED 200-500. The arithmetic that matters is the difference. Somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 of an in-home hour is not teaching. It is the journey, the waiting, and the second booking the tutor could not take.

On Saadiyat Island that component is structurally larger than it is on the mainland, because access is across a bridge and because the afternoon window when sessions happen is the same window the roads are busy. A tutor coming from Khalifa City, Al Reef or Mohammed Bin Zayed City is committing most of an afternoon to one hour of teaching. They are entitled to charge for that. The question for a parent is whether presence in the room is worth what it costs when the alternative is choosing from everyone who teaches the subject rather than the few who will make the trip.

IB Gram answers that question by not selling the option. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, which removes the travel component from the rate entirely and widens the pool from a neighbourhood to a profession. The rest of this page sets out the numbers, the provider models, the verification checklist and the two-programme household case, where the cost arithmetic changes again.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed rather than examined by terminal paper, which makes the cost question different: there is no past-paper diet to buy, and the value of tutoring sits in understanding how the four criteria in each subject are actually awarded. abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-saad.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects a combined IB and International GCSE household most often asks about, with what each assesses. Use them to decide which subject earns a paid hour this term and which can wait.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IB AA and AI; Cambridge 0580; Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The subject with the highest tutoring demand on both tracks, because every Diploma student takes it and every International GCSE student is tiered. Non-calculator fluency is the recurring gap at both levels, and it is cheap to fix early and expensive to fix late.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward algebraic fluency, so Physics marks often move when maths tutoring works. The practical-skills component at International GCSE is a written paper about method and error, which teaches well on a shared screen.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, energetics and electrolysis half-equations carry the quantitative load. At Diploma level the internal assessment adds a design and data-analysis demand that is a separate skill from the taught content and worth a bounded block of its own.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Highest content volume on either track, and the subject where command terms decide grades. Describe and explain carry different marks for the same knowledge, which is a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: English A and English Language
subjects.description: Marks sit in the guided analysis, the individual oral at Diploma level, and directed writing at International GCSE. All are taught techniques. Students can be articulate and score mid-band for not answering the exact brief that was set.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation decide the top bands on both tracks. Case-study application at International GCSE is the equivalent skill: theory recited without reference to the business in the paper caps a candidate mid-band.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Assessed by exhibition and essay against published criteria, and worth real points in combination. Support is process coaching and feedback on the student's own draft. No tutor writes, rewrites or supplies text for either.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: At International GCSE, pseudocode and trace tables are the most reliable mark-gainers and the most commonly skipped revision. At Diploma level the higher-level case study carries its own preparation load that is separate from the taught syllabus.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Language B, ab initio, First and Foreign Language
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules for Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. First-language and additional-language routes are different courses, and placement in the wrong one is a common and correctable problem.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Both reward case studies carried with their specific figures rather than named in passing. Source-handling in History and skills questions in Geography are examinable in their own right and respond quickly to targeted work.

sections.heading: The travel premium, itemised
paragraphs: An in-home hour and an online hour are not the same product, and the difference is not teaching quality. Published bands put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150-300 and an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500. Monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Break the in-home figure into what it pays for. There is the teaching hour itself, which is the same hour either way. There is the outbound journey, which from the Khalifa City corridor to Saadiyat Island in the late afternoon is not short. There is the return journey. There is waiting time, because a school run that overruns by fifteen minutes is the tutor's time, not yours. And there is opportunity cost: a tutor who spends two and a half hours delivering one hour on the island cannot take a second booking that evening, and that lost booking is priced in.

That is a defensible charge. A tutor is entitled to be paid for an afternoon. The question is what the parent gets for it, and the honest answer is presence in the room plus a smaller choice of tutors. On a specification like Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics or a Diploma higher level science, the smaller choice is the expensive part, because the premium buys a journey from someone who may not be the right specialist.

IB Gram removes the component rather than discounting it. We do not sell home visits in the UAE at all, and lessons for Abu Dhabi families are delivered one-to-one over live video. The table below separates the parts of an in-home rate so that a quote can be read rather than accepted.

sections.heading: Provider models compared on what you can actually check
paragraphs: Every competitor page in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms. A neutral comparison is more useful, and it should compare models rather than brands: an agency, an international marketplace, a freelance tutor, a tuition centre, a platform, and your child's own school. Each has a different cost structure, a different pool, and a different level of verifiability, and the last of those is the one nobody discusses.

A freelance tutor is the cheapest to engage directly and the hardest to verify, because there is nothing to check except the person in front of you and their permit. A tuition centre is verifiable in a different way: premises mean a licence, and in Dubai a training institute needs an educational services permit with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An international marketplace is often the least verifiable of all, quoting in dollars and routing UAE enquiries to non-UAE phone numbers.

Two patterns in this market are worth naming as warnings rather than as competitor criticism. Published structured data that contradicts the price on the page, which we found on one ranking site, means at least one of the two numbers is wrong. A self-awarded star rating, which we found on another, is not evidence of anything and is against Google's own structured-data policy. Neither tells you the tutoring is bad. Both tell you the page's numbers cannot be relied on.

sections.heading: Four claims you can check in ten minutes
paragraphs: Verification is the cheapest money-saving tool available in this market, and it takes less time than reading a pricing page. There are four claims worth checking on any quote, including ours.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and fast, an independent tutor without one has no cost excuse, and individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

The approval. Regulator approval is a specific licence, not a descriptor. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute, which is a documented thing with a permit number. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre. Any provider claiming otherwise can be asked for the number.

The figure and the format. An AED figure without a source and a date is not a market rate, it is an assertion; every figure on this page carries the name of the page or survey that published it. And the delivery format should be stated plainly rather than implied by a page title. A UAE page whose conversion path is a non-UAE phone number is telling you where the service actually sits, which is the detail two ranking competitors leave for the parent to discover.

sections.heading: The two-programme household: costing IB and IGCSE together
paragraphs: A Saadiyat Island family with a Year 11 International GCSE candidate and a DP2 Diploma student is running two different cost curves at once, and treating them as one budget is where the overspend happens. The International GCSE child needs terminal paper practice, which is intensive, short and finishes on results day. The Diploma child needs internal-assessment support at a fixed point and technique work in the final two terms, with a long content stretch in between where the school is doing most of the work anyway.

Those curves peak at different times, which is useful. If one child's intensive is in the spring and the other's assessment block falls in the autumn, a household can run a single specialist rate sequentially rather than two simultaneously. Families who book both children into weekly sessions for the whole year are paying through the trough of both curves, which is the least efficient possible allocation.

The temptation is to put one tutor on both children to save money. For mathematics at International GCSE and Diploma standard level there is a case for it, because the content genuinely adjoins. For most other combinations there is not: a Diploma higher level science specialist teaching International GCSE Extended content is being paid a specialist rate to do generalist work, and a generalist covering a Diploma internal assessment will not know the criteria.

The table sets out the two curves against each other so a household can see where the peaks fall. It is a planning tool rather than a price list, and the hourly bands behind it are the published market figures already cited.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of everything else you pay
paragraphs: Tutoring is never the only education line in a household budget, and the comparison is clarifying. Dubai's regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fee rules sit with ADEK rather than KHDA, so confirm your own school's position directly with the school.

Against a private school fee, a mid-band weekly session at a published AED 150-300 an hour is a visible addition rather than a transformative one. Two children at the specialist band for a full academic year is a different proposition, and it is the scenario a family should decide deliberately rather than arrive at by adding one arrangement to another. Bestimate's monthly estimates make the shape clear: AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, per child, per subject.

There are costs that are not tutoring and are often forgotten. Exam entry as a private candidate is arranged with an exam centre and priced by that centre, never by a tutor. Equivalency and attestation for a UAE university application are Ministry processes with their own requirements, and nothing on this page is performed or guaranteed by IB Gram. And a school's own catch-up provision is usually included in fees already, which makes it the first thing to ask about rather than the last.

The practical conclusion is unglamorous. Ask the school first, buy a diagnosis second, buy bounded blocks where the grade share is fixed and large, buy the intensive where the marks are terminal, and stop paying when the work is done. That sequence costs less than a two-year weekly arrangement and in most cases achieves more.

sections.heading: What a free trial is actually for
paragraphs: A trial lesson is often described as a chance to meet the tutor, which undersells it. Used properly it is a diagnostic session you did not pay for, and it answers three questions that no amount of reading can.

First, whether your child will admit confusion to this person. A student who performs understanding rather than reporting it will cost you a term of comfortable sessions and no movement, and you can see which it will be in forty minutes. Second, whether the tutor works from evidence. A tutor who has read the marked paper you sent and opens by naming two or three specific topics is working from evidence; one who opens by asking your child how they feel about the subject is working from a script.

Third, whether they asked the structural questions. For a Diploma student: which route, which level, which internal assessment deadline. For an International GCSE student: which board, which code, which tier. A tutor who has not asked those before the trial began will not ask them afterwards either, and the hours will be spent at slightly the wrong depth from beginning to end.

One caution about free offers generally, including ours. Anything described as free should state its conditions in the same place: how long the trial is, who is eligible, and whether card details are required. Ours is a full one-to-one session over live video, at no cost, with no card details taken. If any provider's free offer has a condition you had to find elsewhere, that is itself a piece of information about the provider.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's role ends on both programmes
paragraphs: Both tracks put a share of the grade inside work the student must author, and both treat authorship as non-negotiable. In the Diploma that is the internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition. At International GCSE it is the coursework or controlled assessment components where a school enters them. The boundary is the same in each case and it is worth stating in writing rather than leaving a parent to assume it.

A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, discuss topic ideas the student has proposed, teach techniques the student has chosen to use, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is substantial work and it is where a bounded assessment block earns its cost, because most marks in these components are lost to criteria nobody read rather than to content nobody knew.

No tutor may write the work, rewrite a draft into its final form, or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student, whose Diploma is the thing at risk rather than the provider's. We are explicit about this because in this market the position is not universal.

The same limit applies to materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. They belong to the boards, they are published on the boards' own sites, and the useful skill is teaching a student to work with them rather than handing over a copy.

process.title: Say who needs what, and when
process.description: Tell us which children, which programmes, which subjects, and when each one's pressure point falls. A household with a Year 11 candidate and a DP2 student has two different cost curves, and knowing where the peaks sit is what stops both running at full rate all year.

process.title: Send one marked paper per child
process.description: A marked mock, a returned assessment or an annotated draft. It converts the first session from an interview into teaching, and it is the single piece of evidence that tells a tutor whether the problem is two topics or something structural.

process.title: Use the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video, at no cost, with no card details taken. Judge it on whether the tutor read what you sent, named specific topics, and asked about route, level, board, code and tier before starting.

process.title: Agree the shape, not just the rate
process.description: Weekly across a course, a bounded assessment block, a final-term intensive, or a single diagnostic. Each has a different hour count and therefore a different total, and the shape matters more to the final bill than the hourly figure does.

process.title: Review on measurable things
process.description: A short written note follows each session. The tests are whether the named topic list is shrinking and whether timed-paper scores are moving. If neither has changed in six weeks, change the plan. Momentum is the most expensive thing in this market.

process.title: Stop when the work is done
process.description: The honest end point of a bounded block is the end of the block. We would rather a family finished a repair and stopped than continued a weekly arrangement out of habit, and we will say so when the evidence says the work is finished.

whyPoints.title: No travel component, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That removes the AED 30-200 of an in-home hour that pays for a bridge crossing, a return trip and a booking the tutor could not take.

faqs.question: What does "tutor near me" actually get a Saadiyat Island family?
faqs.answer: A shorter list and a higher rate. Published bands put a qualified tutor working online at AED 150-300 an hour and an in-home visit at AED 180-500 with travel included, and the gap pays for a journey rather than for teaching. On an island reached by a single bridge, that component is structurally larger than on the mainland. What proximity buys is presence in the room. What it costs is choice, which matters most for the scarcest specialisms.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home tutoring rate in Abu Dhabi is travel?
faqs.answer: Somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 an hour, taking the published online band of AED 150-300 against the in-home band of AED 180-500. Bestimate quotes AED 180-350 for in-home and independent tutors quote AED 200-500. That component covers the outbound and return journey, waiting time when a school run overruns, and the second booking the tutor could not take that evening. It is a defensible charge. It simply buys no additional teaching.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put one tutor on both my IB and IGCSE children?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per week, usually worse value. For mathematics at International GCSE and Diploma standard level there is a reasonable case, because the content genuinely adjoins. For most other combinations there is not: a Diploma higher level science specialist teaching Extended International GCSE content is being paid a specialist rate for generalist work, and a generalist supporting a Diploma internal assessment will not know how the criteria are awarded. A better saving is to stagger the two children's intensive phases.

faqs.question: Which claims in a tutoring quote can I verify myself?
faqs.answer: Four. Whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, valid for two years and applied for through MoHRE's own service page with a two-working-day completion time. Whether any claimed regulator approval is a real permit with a number. Whether each AED figure carries a source and a date. And whether the delivery format is stated plainly, since a UAE page whose contact route is a non-UAE number is telling you where the service actually sits.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any UAE regulator approval?
faqs.answer: No, and we say so rather than letting the question go unanswered. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. We name those bodies on this page to explain what each one governs. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai would need an educational services permit for a training institute, which is a documented thing with a number you could ask for.

faqs.question: Why do some tutoring sites in this market publish no prices at all?
faqs.answer: We cannot speak to their reasons, only to what we measured. Of six competitor pages examined for this market, three publish no price whatsoever, and the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. One page's own frequently-asked-questions section raises the price question and then declines to answer it. One site's structured data contradicts the figure printed on the page. The practical effect for a parent is that comparison becomes impossible, which is why every band on this page carries its source.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Abu Dhabi better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, and with two real costs for a Saadiyat Island household. The first is a second evening journey, usually to central Abu Dhabi, at the hour your child should be eating. The second is that a group cannot be matched to one student's syllabus code or Diploma route, because the room contains several entries. For general content coverage in an early year it can work. For terminal paper technique, where the value is in marking one student's own paper with them, it does not.

faqs.question: When should a household spend the most on tutoring?
faqs.answer: At the points where a grade share is fixed and large, and in the final term where marks are terminal. For a Diploma student that means the internal assessment block and the last two terms of technique work. For an International GCSE candidate it means the timed-paper intensive before the series. The low-value period is the long content stretch in the first year, where the school is covering the same material at the same time, and where a weekly arrangement quietly consumes most of a budget.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, including Saadiyat Island; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. The reason is stated throughout this page: the travel component of an in-home rate buys no teaching, and on an island it narrows the pool to those willing to make the crossing rather than those who know the subject best.

faqs.question: What is the free trial lesson and what are its conditions?
faqs.answer: A full one-to-one session over live video, at no cost, with no card details taken. Its honest purpose is to act as a diagnostic you did not pay for. Watch whether your child will admit confusion to this person, whether the tutor read the marked paper you sent and named specific topics, and whether they asked about route, level, board, code and tier beforehand. Any free offer, including ours, should state its conditions in the same place it is advertised rather than somewhere you have to find.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Saadiyat Island family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, treat any amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: How do school fees compare with what tutoring costs?
faqs.answer: Against a private school fee, a single mid-band weekly session is a visible addition rather than a transformative one. Two children at the specialist band across a full year is a different proposition. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, per child and per subject. Dubai's regulator confirmed a fee freeze for 2026-27 in that emirate on 22 May 2026; Abu Dhabi fee rules sit with ADEK, so ask your school.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing I can buy before committing?
faqs.answer: A single diagnostic session built around one marked paper, with a written output: named topics rather than general weaknesses, and an honest estimate of how many hours the repair needs. Some families take that list to their child's school and use the school's own catch-up provision, which is usually already included in fees. That is a legitimate outcome and it is a far cheaper answer than a year of weekly sessions bought on a hunch about what the problem is.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Diploma internal assessment or IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: Within a stated boundary, yes, and that work is often the best value in the whole arrangement. A tutor may explain each criterion and its mark allocation, test topic ideas the student has proposed, teach the techniques the student has chosen, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write the work, rewrite it into its final form, or supply text for submission. Most marks in these components are lost to criteria nobody read, not to content nobody knew.

faqs.question: How will I know when to stop paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the named topic list is empty and the timed-paper scores have stopped moving upward, which for a bounded repair block is usually a matter of weeks rather than terms. The honest end point of a block is the end of the block. We would rather tell a family the work is finished than let a weekly arrangement continue from habit, which is how a household ends up with two years of comfortable sessions, a large total, and a grade that moved early and then stayed still.

intro.heading: Six different businesses, one search result
paragraphs: Shakhbout City is a mainland villa community inside the Khalifa City corridor, built as family housing, with the emirate's densest school belt a few minutes away. It is a good place to find tutoring, which is the problem: a local search returns a long list, and the list conceals the fact that the entries are not comparable with one another at all.

There are six models in that list and they are genuinely different businesses. A freelance tutor who lives nearby and works for themselves. An agency that recruits, screens and allocates tutors and takes a margin. An international marketplace where tutors list themselves and set their own prices. A tuition centre with premises, employed staff and group classes. An online platform like this one. And the support your child's school already provides, which is in your fees and which most families use inconsistently.

They differ on the things that matter after the first lesson rather than before it. Who employs the tutor. Who screens them. What happens when the match is wrong in week three. Whether anybody holds a private tuition permit. Whether the price is per hour, per month or per package. Whether there is anyone to complain to. A search result flattens all of that into a row of similar-looking names.

The most useful single question to ask any of them is: who employs this person, and what happens if it does not work? A freelance tutor is both the service and the complaints department. An agency can replace a tutor and has a reason to. A marketplace will let you rebook and holds no view on quality. A centre will keep your child in the class. Those are four different risk positions at broadly similar prices.

The second most useful question is about the permit, because private tutoring in the UAE is regulated and almost nobody in this market mentions it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. It costs the tutor nothing to hold, which makes not holding one a choice rather than a hardship.

On our own model, stated plainly: IB Gram is an online platform. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-home visits are a service we run in India only — and no tutor will travel to a Shakhbout City address. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, matched on the named qualification, with a free trial lesson first. We hold no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership and operate no UAE office.

What follows is the comparison: the six models set against each other, what each one is genuinely good at, what your school already gives you for nothing, how a household with two children on two boards should think about it, the permit position by tutor category, and what each model costs in AED with the source for every figure.
