programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations at the end of Year 11, identified by syllabus code: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology; Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1. Cambridge tiers many subjects as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher, and allows modular unit entry in several subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only — not available to an Abu Dhabi candidate. Pearson runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Use the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade on school-set boundaries, with no timed external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. The Personal Project runs through Year 10 or 11 and carries real weight with no external examination attached.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in this corridor run MYP alongside or into the Diploma, so a Year 10 child here may be on MYP or on IGCSE and parents sometimes do not know which. A behavioural test works: extended projects marked against lettered criteria means MYP; past papers under timing means IGCSE. The answer decides whether tutoring targets criteria or mark schemes.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of its grade, with school-set internal deadlines across both years.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. We publish no IB exam or results dates — the IB sets and revises them, so confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator. What governs a Diploma term is the school's internal deadline calendar, which is also the thing to give any tutor you are assessing, because a good one will plan against it rather than against a syllabus.

programmes.name: A Level, as the other post-16 route
programmes.description: The alternative sixth-form pathway after IGCSE, with three or four subjects examined in depth. Several schools in and around this corridor offer both A Level and the IB Diploma, which makes the Year 11 grade set a genuine fork rather than a formality.
programmes.countryNote: Worth naming here because tutor models differ in how well they handle it. An agency or platform with a wide pool can cover both pathways across a household; a single freelance neighbour usually cannot. If you have one child heading for A Level maths and another for IB Higher Level, that is two specialisms and the provider model determines whether both are available.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-shak.subjectsIntro: These are the IB courses households in this corridor most often need, with where the marks go. The IGCSE grid follows separately because the assessment model differs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with HL adding a third paper of extended investigations. Marks go to compressed working rather than to the mathematics in most cases.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. A correct calculator result with no stated model earns a fraction of the available credit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields and nuclear physics with HL extensions. Unit prefixes, unstated assumptions and uncertainty treatment in the investigation are the recurring losses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic pathways break first, and an investigation with a clean graph still scores poorly if the method does not justify the range.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology and physiology. The data-based paper separates grades, and the loss is describing a trend where a mechanism was asked for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and development. Diagrams carry heavy credit and must be referenced in the prose; the portfolio commentaries need explicit theory applied to real articles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Literary and non-literary texts, the Individual Oral, the HL Essay and guided analysis. Paper 1 marks go to content description instead of technique analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. Numerical questions on ratios and investment appraisal are reliable marks students skip entirely.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the IA suite
subjects.description: An exhibition and prescribed-title essay, a 4,000-word independent essay, and a per-subject Internal Assessment. Our role is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts only.

subjects.name: Group 2 languages
subjects.description: Language acquisition across productive and receptive skills. Coverage is genuinely thinner for less-taught languages, and this is one of the places where provider model matters most.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-shak.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side, by syllabus code where it matters. The code is the only unambiguous way to brief any provider.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics. Algebraic manipulation dominates the losses at the higher tiers because every multi-step question routes through it.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. Circuits break first; the practical component rewards precise method and control-variable description.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, electrolysis and organic chemistry. Moles and ionic equations concentrate the marks; qualitative analysis rewards learned observations.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, inheritance and ecology. Large content, and the losses are command-term failures rather than gaps in knowledge.

igcseSubjects.name: English First and Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, directed writing and composition, or the four skills for additional-language candidates. A repeatable writing structure moves this grade faster than reading more does.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Markets, the macroeconomy, business functions and finance. Diagram accuracy carries marks and extended answers lose credit for listing without evaluating in context.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
igcseSubjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, algorithms and programming. Pseudocode and trace tables are reliable marks that students treat as optional.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional and further mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Advanced algebra, series, identities and calculus foundations overlapping early AS content. A short bridge into sixth-form maths for a secure student.

sections.heading: What "near me" returns, model by model
paragraphs: A local search in this corridor returns six businesses that look alike and behave differently. Knowing which one you are talking to is more useful than any claim on their page, because it tells you in advance what they can and cannot do.

The freelance local tutor is an individual working for themselves, usually resident in Khalifa City, Shakhbout City or Al Reef. The agency recruits and allocates tutors and takes a margin for doing so. The international marketplace lists tutors who set their own prices and manage their own quality. The tuition centre holds premises and employs staff, selling mostly group classes. The online platform matches and delivers over video. And your school's own support sits inside your fees.

The differences that matter appear in week three rather than week one. If the tutor is ill, who teaches? If the match is wrong, who replaces them and at whose cost? If the subject turns out to be outside their strength, who says so? If you want a second child covered on a different qualification, can they? If something goes wrong, is there anybody other than the tutor to raise it with?

The comparison table below sets the six against each other on exactly those questions. We have included ourselves in it, with the limitations stated rather than omitted, because a comparison that puts the author at the top of every column is not a comparison.

One note on how to read it. No row is the right answer for every household. A freelance neighbour suits a single-child, single-subject case well; a centre suits broad revision at low cost; the school's own provision suits almost everything first. The table is there to let you ask each model the question it is weakest on.

sections.heading: The freelance tutor who lives nearby
paragraphs: This is the option a local search surfaces most and the one worth understanding properly, because it is genuinely good at some things. A freelance tutor living in this corridor can be excellent, is often known to other families, builds a long relationship with a child, and charges without a margin on top. For a household with one child, one subject and a tutor who happens to own that exact qualification, it is hard to beat.

What you carry in exchange is everything an organisation would otherwise carry. Screening: you are verifying the qualification claim yourself, and the way to do that is to ask for the syllabus code and the level and judge the answer. Continuity: if they are ill or leave the country, the arrangement stops that week. Scope: one person has one or two specialisms, so a second child on a different board is usually out of reach. And quality assurance: if the sessions drift into homework supervision, the person you would raise it with is the person doing it.

There is also the permit question, which is more relevant to this model than to any other. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge and valid for two years, and tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it costs nothing, a freelance tutor who does not hold one has chosen not to, and asking to see it is a reasonable, non-confrontational request before a first paid session.

One Abu Dhabi-specific caution. ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as prohibiting private and charter school staff from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit code of conduct is reported to bar the same. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document if it applies to you. A teacher from your child's own school is not the shortcut it appears to be.

sections.heading: Agencies and marketplaces: who is accountable
paragraphs: These two are often confused and they sit at opposite ends of the accountability spectrum. An agency recruits, screens and allocates, holds a relationship with both sides, and can replace a tutor when a match fails. A marketplace is a listing: tutors advertise themselves, set their own prices, and the platform's role ends at introduction and payment.

The agency margin buys something real, and the thing to test is whether that something is being delivered. Ask what screening consists of, whether tutors are matched by syllabus code and level or by subject name, what the replacement policy is in writing, and whether anybody reviews whether the sessions are working. An agency that cannot answer those is charging a margin for an introduction, which is a marketplace with an office.

Marketplaces are good for breadth and poor for assurance, and in this market they have a specific local failing: several price in US dollars, a currency no family in Shakhbout City pays a tutor in, and some route UAE parents to contact numbers outside the country without stating where the teaching comes from. Both are discoverable in advance and both tell you that localisation was not a priority.

A related caution applies across these models. Self-asserted ratings are common and some are internally inconsistent — competitor pages in this market display different review counts and scores in different places on the same page, and one shows a rating drawn from twenty reviews alongside a far larger claimed student count elsewhere on the same page. A rating nobody can audit is not evidence. We publish none, which is why there is no star rating anywhere on this page.

sections.heading: The tuition centre a few minutes away
paragraphs: Centres are the model most under-rated by parents who have decided they want one-to-one, and most over-rated on price. The honest position is that a centre is good value for broad content coverage and shared revision, and poor value for a diagnosed individual weakness, which is the opposite of how families usually deploy it.

Price per hour makes a centre look decisively cheaper. Price per minute of attention directed at your child's specific error does not: a group class at a fraction of the one-to-one rate may give a student five to fifteen minutes of individual correction in an hour, with the pace set by the group. If the problem is that your child has not covered a topic, that is fine. If the problem is a habit of compressing working, a group class will not see it.

The costs a centre does not quote are worth counting. Two car journeys per session at the hour this corridor's roads are busiest, which is a parent's time as well as a student's. A fixed timetable, so a clash with a school activity is a paid session lost and not recovered. And a class composition you do not control, which may mix boards and tiers.

There is a regulatory distinction worth knowing, because it is the source of the most dangerous claim in this market. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. A centre holding that permit can say so and show the number. An individual or a platform cannot, and any provider implying regulator approval it does not hold is making a claim you should ask to see evidenced.

sections.heading: What your school already gives you for nothing
paragraphs: This belongs in the comparison because it is the cheapest entry on the list and the least used. Your fees already buy subject teaching, a revision programme, access to past papers through the exams officer, departmental advice on tier and option choices, and the attention of a teacher who sees your child three or four times a week.

Families in this corridor commonly skip straight past it, partly because asking feels like a complaint. It is not. The questions that get the most useful answers are specific and administrative: which tier is my child provisionally entered for and what would change that decision; which syllabus code and which paper pattern applies for their exam year; does this set have a settled teacher this year; what does the department's own revision provision contain and when does it run; and for a Diploma student, what are the internal deadlines across all six subjects and the core.

That last one is worth a paragraph of its own. A Diploma student carries well over twenty school-set dates across two years, set independently by different departments with no coordination around your child's particular combination. Collecting them on one sheet in September and finding the fortnight where three collide prevents more damage than any amount of tutoring bought in that fortnight. It is free and it takes one meeting.

Only after those questions does paid help become efficient, because by then you know what it is for. A tutor's hour is worth a great deal aimed at a named weakness and very little spent covering ground the school is already covering adequately.

sections.heading: Two children, two boards, one household
paragraphs: This is where the provider models separate most sharply, and it is common in this corridor because the school belt runs both British and IB pathways within minutes of each other. A household can easily have a Year 11 sitting Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and a Year 12 on IB Chemistry Higher Level with an Internal Assessment due.

Those are different professional skills. Drilling a 0620 paper against a Cambridge mark scheme and reading an IB investigation draft against published criteria are not variations of one job. A single freelance tutor covering both is, by arithmetic, a generalist in at least one of the two roles, and the weaker role is usually the one with coursework attached because it is harder to fake.

The models that handle this well are the ones with a pool: an agency with depth, a marketplace if you are willing to do the selecting, or a platform that matches per qualification. The models that handle it badly are a single freelance arrangement and a centre, where the two children end up in whatever classes exist rather than in the ones they need.

The practical household point is scheduling rather than cost. Two specialists on two evenings is straightforward online and genuinely awkward in person, where it means two separate journeys or one compromise. And the two children's calendars peak at different times — IGCSE pressure concentrates in Year 11, Diploma internal deadlines arrive steadily across two years — so the budget should stagger rather than double.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market answers this, so here it is. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than parents assume. Applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. So a university student tutoring in Khalifa City is expressly eligible, which also means they have no excuse for not holding one.

The consequence of not holding one is stated and the amount is not. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating in this market could not be verified, so any specific amount quoted to you should be treated with suspicion. This page quotes none.

The useful parental action is simple and polite: ask to see the permit before the first paid session. It is free to hold, quick to obtain and the person either has it or does not. For a centre, ask instead for the institute permit number and check it with the regulator. And be clear that naming a regulator is not the same as being approved by one — IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, MoHRE, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no office or centre in the UAE.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, whichever model you choose
paragraphs: This boundary is set by the examination boards rather than by any provider, so it applies identically to a freelance neighbour, an agency, a centre and us. A tutor may teach the content a task rests on, explain what each criterion or mark scheme rewards, question a method until the student finds its weakness, read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion it undersells, teach referencing and honest method description, and run timed practice on a different task.

A tutor may not write any part of assessed work, draft a paragraph for the student to adapt, edit a draft to completion, rewrite sentences so the final text is partly theirs, generate a research question and hand it over, supply data the student did not gather, or provide a worked model of the live task. There is an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than the seller, and it is not a service we offer at any fee.

There is a copyright boundary too, worth using as a test when comparing providers. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. We reference them and link the official source rather than redistributing them. A provider handing you a folder of scans is not giving you a bonus; they are distributing somebody else's copyrighted material, which also tells you how they treat rules generally.

Two more comparison tests. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, and we do not use examiner status to imply access to marking or boundaries. And we publish no statistic without a sample size, a date and a method, which is why there are no satisfaction percentages or median-score claims anywhere on this page.

intro.heading: Start by comparing everything, including the options you already pay for
paragraphs: Almost every page competing for this search assumes that the problem is solved by hiring a tutor. That is a convenient assumption for a tutoring platform and it is not always true. A Yas Island family facing a disappointing report has six genuine options, and two of them are already included in the school fees they pay. Starting with those is not modesty; it is the cheapest sensible first move, and it also sharpens what a paid tutor should then be asked to do.

The six are these. The school's own support, which usually includes departmental catch-up sessions, teacher clinics and access to the class teacher's marking. Self-study using the board's own published materials, which are free and which most students never open. A peer study group, which on a small island with a concentrated cohort is more practical than it sounds. A tuition centre group class. An online group course. And one-to-one tuition, in person or over video.

Each of those solves a different problem. School support is the right answer when a student has missed content through absence, or has one specific misunderstanding a teacher can clear in ten minutes. Self-study with official materials is the right answer when the student is capable and disorganised rather than confused. A peer group works when the issue is motivation and pace. A group class works for content coverage at a low price. One-to-one works when the problem is specific, diagnosed, and requires somebody to watch an individual student work.

The expensive mistake is buying one-to-one tuition for a problem that one of the cheaper options would solve. A student who is coping but not doing their homework does not need a specialist at an hourly rate; they need structure, and a parent can provide it. A student who has missed three weeks with illness needs the school's catch-up provision, which is free and which is also better informed than any external tutor about what was actually covered in those weeks.

There is one Yas Island specific point in this comparison. The island has a concentrated resident cohort and a leisure-led built environment, which makes a peer study group unusually workable and a second evening commute to a mainland tuition centre unusually tedious. It also hosts large-scale events, including the Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, which affect anything requiring travel on those weekends. Those facts change the ranking of the six options rather than the options themselves.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video. Market figures quoted on this page are published rates attributed to the sources that produced them, not our prices.

sections.heading: The six options, side by side
paragraphs: Set out together, the options separate cleanly by the kind of problem they solve. Two are already paid for. Two are cheap. Two are expensive. The ranking that matters is not by price but by fit, and a family that works down the list in order usually spends less and gets more than one that starts at the bottom.

School support is first because it is already bought, and because the class teacher knows what was covered in the lessons your child missed, which no external tutor does. Self-study with the boards' own published materials is second because the materials are free, authoritative and barely used: a student who has never opened a mark scheme for their own specification has an unused resource of real value sitting on a public website.

A peer study group is third, and it is underrated in a community like this one. Three students from the same class testing each other on recall-heavy content is genuinely effective, costs nothing, and solves the motivation problem that no paid arrangement reliably solves. A tuition centre group class is fourth: cheap per hour, good for content coverage, and unable to match one student's specification or diagnose an individual error.

One-to-one tuition sits at the bottom of the list by cost and at the top by capability. It is the only option in which somebody watches an individual student work and can see where a procedure breaks. That is worth paying for when the problem is individual and diagnosed. It is poor value when the problem is absence, disorganisation or motivation, which are better addressed higher up the list.

sections.heading: What the school already provides, and why to use it first
paragraphs: School provision is the most underused support available to a UAE family, partly because it is invisible: it does not advertise, it has no pricing page, and nobody follows up. It is also, for several specific problems, strictly better than anything a parent can buy.

The clearest case is absence. A student who has missed two or three weeks needs to know exactly what was covered, which examples were used, and what the class is assumed to know now. The class teacher has that information and an external tutor does not. A tutor filling that gap will cover the topic as they would normally teach it, which may be at the wrong depth or in a different order, and the student will then be slightly out of step rather than caught up.

The second case is a single specific misunderstanding. A student who cannot see why a particular step works usually needs five minutes with the person who taught it, not an hour with a stranger. Most departments run clinics, drop-ins or catch-up sessions after the taught day, and a student already on site can attend without any additional journey, which for a Yas Island household travelling back from the mainland is a material advantage.

The third is Diploma-specific. Every Diploma student has a supervisor for the Extended Essay and a subject teacher responsible for internal assessment guidance. Those people know the school's internal deadlines, have seen previous cohorts' submissions, and are accountable for the student's work in a way no external provider is. A paid coaching block should supplement that relationship rather than replace it, and a tutor who implies otherwise is overselling.

sections.heading: The free materials almost nobody uses
paragraphs: The examination boards publish a substantial body of material through their own channels, and students across this market reach the end of a two-year course without opening most of it. That is the single largest piece of unused value in the whole comparison, and it costs nothing to correct.

What exists varies by board and by qualification, and the reliable route is the board's own site plus whatever your school distributes. Syllabus or subject guide documents set out exactly what is examinable and, in the IB's case, the assessment criteria with their mark allocations. Past papers and mark schemes show what the examiner rewards, which is different from what a student assumes is wanted. Specimen and provisional timetable material shows the structure and the dates of a series.

Two cautions matter here, and they are the reason this section is a signpost rather than a library. These documents belong to the boards. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, and a provider offering a downloadable collection of them is offering something that is not theirs to give. Reference them, read them on the board's own site, and get them from your school.

The useful skill, and the thing a tutor can genuinely add here, is teaching a student to read a mark scheme critically: to see where method marks sit, how follow-through works, and why a description question is marked by element. A student who can do that gets more from every past paper they attempt afterwards, including the ones they attempt alone. That is a transferable gain rather than a dependency, which is the right thing for a paid hour to produce.

sections.heading: Group classes and peer groups compared honestly
paragraphs: A tuition centre group class is cheaper per hour than one-to-one and is frequently dismissed too quickly by families and oversold by providers. What it does well is deliver structured content coverage to a group at a low price. What it cannot do is match one student's syllabus code, route or tier, because the room contains several entries, and it cannot diagnose an individual's procedural error because nobody is watching one student's working.

For a Yas Island family there is a specific cost beyond the fee. Most of the emirate's centres are concentrated in central Abu Dhabi, which means a second journey off the island at the hour a student should be eating, on top of a school run that may already have taken an hour. Across a term that is a substantial amount of time in a car for content a student could read.

A peer study group is the option this market never mentions and it deserves to be named. Three or four students from the same class, same board, same tier, testing each other on recall-heavy content, works well for Biology, Geography case studies, Chemistry qualitative tests and the factual side of Economics. It costs nothing, it solves motivation and pace, and on an island with a concentrated cohort the logistics are trivial compared with a mainland commute.

Its limits are real. A peer group cannot diagnose, it cannot teach a procedure none of them has secured, and it can confidently reinforce a shared misunderstanding. The honest division of labour is that a peer group handles recall and pace, a paid hour handles diagnosis and technique, and a family that uses both spends less than one that uses one-to-one for everything.

sections.heading: When one-to-one tuition is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: Saying this plainly is unusual on a tutoring page and it makes the rest of the page more useful. There are four situations in which paying for one-to-one tuition is poor value, and recognising them saves a family a great deal of money.

The first is short absence. A student who has missed two or three weeks needs the school's own catch-up provision, because the class teacher knows what was covered and an external tutor does not. The second is disorganisation. A student who understands the work and is not completing it has a structure problem, and structure is supplied by a parent, a timetable and a quiet room rather than by an hourly rate. Paying a specialist to supervise homework is the most common overspend in this market.

The third is motivation. A student who has decided they dislike a subject will sit politely through an expensive hour and absorb very little, and a peer group or a conversation with the school will usually do more. The fourth is undiagnosed general worry. "They are struggling" is not a problem a tutor can solve efficiently; it is a description that needs a marked paper and fifteen minutes of analysis before anyone is paid for anything.

Where one-to-one genuinely outperforms everything else is narrow and valuable. A diagnosed, specific procedural failure that somebody has to watch the student make. An internal assessment where published criteria need explaining and a draft needs individual feedback. A timed-paper block where one student's own script is marked with them. And a scarce specification the local market does not cover, where the problem is availability rather than attention. Those are the four cases, and they are what a block should be bought for.

sections.heading: Comparing two tutors once you have decided to buy one
paragraphs: Having established that a paid hour is the right purchase, the next comparison is between providers, and the published rates will not help: the bands overlap completely. Entry-level online runs AED 45-150, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors listing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home runs AED 180-500 with travel included, per Bestimate's AED 180-350. Specialists run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Five questions separate a specialist from a generalist regardless of the figure. Which route, level, board, code or tier do you teach most weeks? What will you look for in a marked script? Which board's or guide's materials will we work from in session one? What is the end point of this block? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?

That last one is worth stating because it is free and checkable. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified.

One further check is about standing. Regulator approval is a numbered permit, not an adjective. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. We name those bodies on this page to explain what they govern, and any provider claiming otherwise about itself is making a statement you can ask them to evidence.

sections.heading: Why proximity drops out of the comparison entirely
paragraphs: Of the six options, three involve no travel at all and two involve travel that proximity does not improve. School support happens where your child already is. Self-study and online delivery happen at home. A peer group travels within the community. A tuition centre requires a mainland journey whether you live on Yas Island or Al Reem. Only in-home tuition is affected by how near a tutor lives, and that is the option with the smallest pool and the highest rate.

On this island the in-home pool is particularly thin. Yas Island is residential and leisure-led rather than a concentration of teaching staff, most of whom live in the inland communities. An in-home quote to the island therefore carries a substantial travel component and comes from a short list of people willing to make the journey, which is the opposite of a selection process based on specification knowledge.

The island's event calendar sharpens the point. Large-scale events, including the Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, change access and road conditions for residents, and anything that depends on somebody driving loses sessions on those weekends. A plan that runs for twelve weeks and loses two of them to traffic has lost a sixth of its value for a reason nothing to do with teaching.

IB Gram resolves this by not offering the affected option. We do not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, which means the comparison a Yas Island family makes is between school support, free materials, a peer group, a group class and one-to-one online, and in none of those five does the address of the teacher matter.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do on assessed work, and why that is a comparison point too
paragraphs: Both routes place some marks inside work the student must author, and this is a place where the options genuinely differ in what they are allowed to offer. A class teacher or Diploma supervisor can guide within the school's own framework, with accountability. A peer group can discuss. A tutor can teach, explain criteria and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. Nobody may produce the work.

Stated precisely: a tutor may teach the skills a task assesses, explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, discuss topic ideas the student has proposed, teach the techniques the student has chosen to use, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is substantial, and in the Diploma it is the highest-value paid hour available, because most marks in those components are lost to criteria nobody read rather than to content nobody knew.

No tutor may write the work, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion, or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price. The risk in that transaction falls on the student, whose Diploma is what a malpractice finding costs, and that asymmetry is the reason to state the boundary before anyone pays rather than after.

This is a comparison point because it is a reason to prefer the free option first. A Diploma supervisor's guidance carries the school's accountability and institutional knowledge of previous cohorts. A tutor adds criterion literacy and individual feedback on top. A provider offering to produce the work adds nothing and removes the only thing the student actually owns, which is authorship.

process.title: Ask the school first
process.description: Find out what departmental catch-up, clinics or revision provision already exists, and whether the class teacher can see your child for a specific question. It is included in your fees, it requires no journey, and for absence and single misunderstandings it is better than anything you can buy.

process.title: Get one marked paper analysed
process.description: Before buying a block of hours, have a marked script read properly. Clustered losses mean a short repair; scattered single marks usually mean method, rounding or timing. Those are different purchases, and the analysis can be a single session or a free trial.

process.title: Decide which of the six options fits
process.description: Absence points to the school. Disorganisation points to structure at home. Recall-heavy content points to a peer group or self-study with the board's own materials. A diagnosed procedural failure, an internal assessment or a scarce specification points to one-to-one.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no cost and with no card details taken. Judge it on whether the tutor named the route or code, read what you sent, and said plainly what the end point of a block would be.

process.title: Agree the end point before the start
process.description: A block that ends is a purchase; an open weekly arrangement is a subscription. Agreeing the end at the start is the single most effective way to avoid the main overspend in this market, and a tutor who cannot state one should be asked why.

faqs.question: What are all the support options a Yas Island family actually has?
faqs.answer: Six. School support including departmental clinics and the class teacher's marking, which is already inside your fees. Self-study using the boards' own published syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, which are free. A peer study group with classmates. A tuition centre group class. An online group course. And one-to-one tuition. Each solves a different problem, and working down the list in that order usually costs less and achieves more than starting with the most expensive.

faqs.question: When is paying for a one-to-one tutor the wrong decision?
faqs.answer: In four situations. Short absence, where the class teacher knows what was covered and an external tutor does not. Disorganisation, where a student understands the work and is not doing it, which needs structure rather than an hourly rate. Motivation, where a peer group or a conversation with the school usually does more. And undiagnosed general worry, where a marked paper and fifteen minutes of analysis should come before anyone is paid for anything.

faqs.question: What does my child's school already provide that I am not using?
faqs.answer: Usually more than families realise, because school provision does not advertise. Departmental catch-up sessions, subject clinics or drop-ins after the taught day, and the class teacher's own marking and feedback. For Diploma students there is also a named Extended Essay supervisor and a subject teacher responsible for internal assessment guidance. All of it is included, happens on site with no extra journey, and is better informed about the school's own deadlines than any external provider.

faqs.question: Is a peer study group genuinely worth organising on Yas Island?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this market never mentions it. Three or four students from the same class, board and tier testing each other works well for recall-heavy material: Biology content, Geography case studies with their figures, Chemistry qualitative tests, the factual side of Economics. It costs nothing, it solves motivation and pace, and on an island with a concentrated cohort the logistics beat a mainland commute easily. Its limit is that it cannot diagnose, and it can reinforce a shared misunderstanding.

faqs.question: What free material do the exam boards actually publish?
faqs.answer: Syllabus and subject guide documents setting out exactly what is examinable, assessment criteria with their mark allocations in the IB's case, past papers, mark schemes, and published timetables for each series. Most students reach the end of a two-year course without reading a mark scheme for their own specification. We do not reproduce or distribute any of it, because it belongs to the boards: read it on their own sites and get it through your school.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Abu Dhabi worth the journey from Yas Island?
faqs.answer: It depends what you want from it. It is cheaper per hour and genuinely useful for structured content coverage. What it cannot do is match one student's syllabus code, route or tier, because the room contains several entries, and it cannot diagnose an individual's procedural error. For a Yas Island household the real cost is a second journey to central Abu Dhabi at the hour a student should be eating, on top of a school run that may already have taken an hour.

faqs.question: What does one-to-one tuition do that nothing cheaper can?
faqs.answer: Four things. It watches an individual student work, which is how a procedural failure in the middle of a method is actually found. It explains published assessment criteria and gives feedback on that student's own draft. It marks that student's own script with them, question by question. And it covers scarce specifications the local market does not teach at all. Outside those four cases, something higher up the list usually does the job for less.

faqs.question: Is in-home tuition on Yas Island one of the six options IB Gram offers?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, including Yas Island; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video. On a comparison page that matters because in-home tuition is the only one of the six options where proximity helps at all, and on this island it has the thinnest pool and the largest travel component in its rate.

faqs.question: How should I compare two tutors when the rates are similar?
faqs.answer: Ask five questions. Which route, level, board, code or tier do you teach most weeks? What will you look for in a marked script? Which board's or guide's materials will we use in session one? What is the end point of this block? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? A specialist answers all five crisply. The published rate bands overlap completely, so the figure attached tells you almost nothing about which you are speaking to.

faqs.question: Why does the end point of a block matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because an arrangement without one becomes a subscription, and that is the largest avoidable cost in this market. A diagnostic is one session. A repair block is three to six and ends with a timed set on the problem it fixed. An assessment block ends at the school's internal deadline. A paper block ends at the series. Agreeing the end at the start also forces a tutor to say what success looks like, which is a useful thing to have in writing.

faqs.question: Do island event weekends really matter for a tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: For anything that depends on travel, yes. Yas Island hosts large-scale events, including the Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, and access and road management during those periods change what a weekday evening looks like for residents. A twelve-week plan that loses two weeks to traffic has lost a sixth of its value for reasons unconnected to teaching. A lesson delivered over live video is unaffected, as is school provision and self-study.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do on a Diploma internal assessment that the school cannot?
faqs.answer: Not more, but differently. The school's subject teacher and Extended Essay supervisor carry accountability and know what previous cohorts submitted, which is valuable and free. A tutor adds individual time on criterion literacy and feedback on a specific draft, which a teacher with a full class has less of. Both work within the same boundary: no tutor and no teacher may write the work, rewrite it into its final form or supply text for submission.

faqs.question: Should I buy a diagnostic session before committing to a block?
faqs.answer: It is usually the cheapest useful purchase available. One session, one marked paper, one written output: named topics rather than general weaknesses, plus an honest estimate of the hours a repair needs. Some families take that list to the school and use its free provision instead, which is a legitimate outcome. The list is worth having whatever you then do with it, because it converts a vague worry into something actionable.

faqs.question: Is self-study realistic for a Year 11 or Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For part of the job, yes, and it is the part most often outsourced unnecessarily. A capable student can work through past papers from their own specification, read the syllabus to see what is examinable, and read the criteria they are being marked against. What they cannot do alone is reliably tell why a mark was lost, which is where a paid hour earns its place. Teaching a student to read a mark scheme critically makes all their solo practice worth more.

faqs.question: What should a Yas Island family do first, this week?
faqs.answer: Two things that cost nothing. Email the school and ask what departmental support exists for the subject in question and whether the class teacher can see your child about one specific thing. And find your child's last marked paper and look at it: are the losses clustered in two or three topics, or scattered as single marks across the script, and were the final questions attempted? Those two steps determine which of the six options you actually need.

abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-yas-.closingHeading: Work down the list, not up it
abu-dhabi/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-yas-.closingBody: Ask the school what it already provides, look at one marked script properly, point your child at the board's own published materials, and see whether three classmates will test each other once a week. If a specific, diagnosed problem survives all of that, then buy a bounded block of one-to-one with a stated end point. intro.heading: Internal assessment is six tasks wearing one name
paragraphs: A family searching for Internal Assessment support usually has one specific crisis in mind and a general anxiety about the rest. That is reasonable, because the Diploma's internally assessed components share a name and almost nothing else. A science investigation has a 3,000-word ceiling and four criteria worth six marks each. An economics Internal Assessment is three separate commentaries of 800 words, each on a different unit of the syllabus and each built on a different published news source. A mathematics exploration has a recommended page range rather than a word count and five criteria, lettered A to E. A history investigation is a different task again.

Those differences are not administrative detail. They determine what can go wrong and therefore what support is worth buying. A science investigation fails most often because the research question cannot generate enough varied quantitative data. An economics commentary fails because the article chosen does not contain enough economics to analyse. A mathematics exploration fails because the chosen topic cannot carry mathematics at the level of the course. Three subjects, three completely different first conversations, and a provider offering generic Internal Assessment support has not had any of them.

The second thing a family needs is the criteria, by letter, with their mark allocations. This is where the market is strangely silent: competitor pages in this cluster discuss Internal Assessment at length and name not a single criterion, which is difficult to explain given that the criteria are the entire basis on which the mark is awarded. A student who knows that use of mathematics carries six of the twenty marks in a mathematics exploration, or that evaluation carries six of twenty-four in a science investigation, works differently from one who has been told to make it interesting.

The third is the record. Internal assessment is produced over weeks without time pressure, which makes it the most recoverable part of the Diploma and also the easiest place for drift to go unnoticed. The record this plan keeps is a dated version history of the student's own document: the research question at each narrowing, the feedback given at each stage, the criterion each comment refers to. A parent can read it. More importantly, it demonstrates that the thinking was the student's, which matters if anyone ever asks.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For Internal Assessment work the format is the correct one rather than a compromise: comments sit in the margin of the student's own file, the subject guide's criteria are visible alongside the text, every version is saved, and a family in Khalifa City or on Al Reem Island gets a tutor matched to the specific subject guide rather than to a driving radius.

abu-dhabi/ib-internal-assessment-help.programmesIntro: Internal assessment sits inside a two-year Diploma and the point in that course determines what help is useful. These are the four stages that matter to an Abu Dhabi family.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1, before any Internal Assessment starts
programmes.description: The cheapest and most useful moment to intervene, and the one families almost never use. Establishing what each subject's Internal Assessment requires, what its limits are and which criteria carry the most marks takes one session per subject and removes most of the later crises.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma programmes vary in when they introduce Internal Assessment work, and the variation is wide enough that a parent cannot assume. Asking the IB coordinator for the school's internal deadline schedule in September of Diploma Year 1 is the single most useful administrative act available.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1, research question and feasibility
programmes.description: Most science and mathematics Internal Assessment work begins late in Year 1. This is the stage where feasibility is settled: can this question generate the data the criteria need, and does the school hold the apparatus. Changing a question here costs one session; changing it after data collection costs the component.
programmes.countryNote: The Abu Dhabi academic year typically runs from late August to late June, with a long winter break. That break falls at a useful point for Internal Assessment reading and planning, and it is the most commonly wasted three weeks in the two-year course.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 2, drafting and submission
programmes.description: The crisis stage, where two or three Internal Assessments arrive at draft stage at once alongside the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Support here is triage: which component is furthest from its criteria, which can be fixed within the school's deadline, and which has to be submitted as it stands.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools set their own internal deadlines ahead of the IB's own upload schedule, and those internal dates are the ones that bind a family. Ask the coordinator for them in writing rather than relying on a student's recollection of an assembly.

programmes.name: After submission
programmes.description: Once a component is submitted the work is finished, and the useful conversation moves to the written examinations. A provider offering to revisit a submitted Internal Assessment is offering something that cannot help and should not be bought.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB exam or results date appears on this page because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no date here has been confirmed from the IB itself. Confirm dates with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly.

abu-dhabi/ib-internal-assessment-help.subjectsIntro: Each subject's Internal Assessment is a different task with its own limits and criteria. These are the ones Abu Dhabi families most often ask about, with what the component actually is.

subjects.name: Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL · the scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation with a 3,000-word ceiling, around ten hours of class time and 24 marks across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, at six marks each. Fails most often on a research question that cannot generate enough varied quantitative data.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: An individual written mathematical investigation on a student-chosen topic, with a recommended page range rather than a word limit, assessed against five criteria lettered A to E. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation, which is why topic choice caps the mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same component shape and the same five criteria, with the mathematics expected drawn from a modelling and statistics syllabus rather than an algebraic one. A topic that suits the Analysis route often will not suit this one, and the reverse.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: SL and HL · the portfolio of commentaries
subjects.description: Three commentaries of up to 800 words each, every one on a different unit of the syllabus and each built on a different published news article. Fails when the chosen article does not contain enough economics to analyse, which is a selection problem rather than a writing one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.levels: SL and HL · the research project
subjects.description: A written research project on a real organisation, with different word limits and research expectations at the two levels. The binding constraint is access: a student needs an organisation that will actually supply the information the project requires.

subjects.name: History
subjects.levels: SL and HL · the historical investigation
subjects.description: A written investigation on a student-chosen historical question, structured in defined sections with a stated word limit. Fails on a question too broad to answer in the space, and on source evaluation written as description rather than as assessment of value and limitation.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.levels: SL and HL · the experimental study
subjects.description: A report on a replication of a published experimental study, with a stated word limit and defined sections. Ethical constraints shape what is possible, and a student who chooses a study that cannot be ethically replicated has to start again.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.levels: SL and HL · the fieldwork report
subjects.description: A written report based on primary fieldwork data collected by the student, with a stated word limit. The constraint is the fieldwork itself: a question requiring data the student cannot actually gather in the time and place available will not produce a report.

subjects.name: Language A: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: HL · the HL essay · and the Individual Oral at both levels
subjects.description: The Higher Level essay is an extended piece of 1,200 to 1,500 words on a work or text studied. The Individual Oral, assessed at both levels, is a timed assessed conversation built on a global issue and two works, which is a different kind of preparation entirely.

subjects.name: Visual Arts, Music and Theatre
subjects.levels: SL and HL · portfolio and process components
subjects.description: Portfolio-based components assessed across several tasks rather than as a single document, with their own criteria and their own submission requirements. Support here is process coaching against criteria rather than anything resembling essay feedback.

sections.heading: The limits, component by component
paragraphs: The first useful document for an Abu Dhabi Diploma family is a single page listing, for each of their child's six subjects, what the Internal Assessment actually is, what its limit is and how many criteria it carries. Almost no student has that page, and almost every Internal Assessment crisis involves a limit or a criterion the student discovered late. It takes an hour to produce from the subject guides and it prevents more problems than any amount of drafting advice.

The limits matter because they change the shape of the work rather than merely capping it. A 3,000-word ceiling on a science investigation sounds generous until a student realises that research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation all have to fit inside it, with tables and graphs. An 800-word economics commentary is short enough that a single paragraph of unnecessary context removes the room for a diagram and its analysis. A mathematics exploration with a recommended page range rather than a word count invites students to pad with screenshots, which earns nothing.

The criteria count matters for the same reason. Four criteria at six marks each in a science investigation means evaluation is worth exactly as much as research design, which is not how students allocate their effort. Five criteria lettered A to E in a mathematics exploration, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation, means a topic that cannot carry the mathematics caps the piece however well it is written. These are planning facts and they belong at the start.

The table below sets out the components Abu Dhabi families most often ask about. Subject guides are revised, so every limit should be confirmed against the current guide for the student's own cohort before drafting begins. The right source is the guide itself or the school's IB coordinator, not a tutoring page, and a provider who cannot say which guide version they are working from is not a safe source for a limit.

sections.heading: The criteria, named by letter
paragraphs: Internal assessment marks are awarded against criteria, and the criteria have names and allocations. Competitor pages in this market discuss Internal Assessment at length and name none of them, which leaves a student with advice to be original and interested rather than with a description of what the mark is for. Naming the criteria changes how a student works more than any other single intervention in this part of the Diploma.

In the sciences the four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six of twenty-four marks. The effect of knowing that is immediate: evaluation stops being the paragraph at the end and becomes a quarter of the grade, which means the uncertainty work has to be done during data collection rather than reconstructed afterwards. A student who learns this in week one of the process works differently for the whole of it.

In mathematics the five criteria are lettered: A presentation, B mathematical communication, C personal engagement, D reflection and E use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation of the twenty available. Personal engagement and reflection together carry a meaningful share, which stops a student treating both as decoration around the mathematics. And because criterion E rewards mathematics commensurate with the course, topic choice is a mark decision rather than a matter of taste.

In economics each commentary is assessed against criteria covering diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, and evaluation, which is why a commentary built on an article with little economics in it cannot score: there is nothing for most of the criteria to attach to. In history the criteria separate the identification and evaluation of sources from the investigation itself and from the reflection, which means source evaluation is a specific scored task rather than a paragraph of context. Every subject guide publishes its own; the point is to have read them before writing, not after.

sections.heading: The boundary, in operational detail
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that matters most, so it is stated as operations rather than principles. A tutor may read the student's draft and comment in its margin. A tutor may ask what the independent variable is, how many values of it will be tested, and whether the data will support a conclusion. A tutor may name the criterion a paragraph is failing and what that criterion rewards. A tutor may teach the subject content or the statistical method the component requires. A tutor may mark a draft against the criteria and say what band it currently sits in.

A tutor may not supply text that appears in the submission. A tutor may not rewrite a paragraph into its final form, which is the line most easily blurred: editing a sentence until it is correct produces the tutor's sentence, not the student's. A tutor may not choose the research question, perform the calculations, supply data, or design the experiment. The rewriting is always done by the student, in the session or afterwards, which is slower and is the only version that is theirs.

The reason for the strictness is the consequence. Work that is not the student's own produces a malpractice finding against the student, not against whoever sold the help, and the outcome at stake is the Diploma itself rather than a lower grade in one subject. The market in this region contains providers who sell exactly what is prohibited: one UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a premium service with a risk attached; it is a transfer of risk onto a seventeen-year-old.

Two further boundaries belong here. The school supervisor relationship is the school's, and a tutor should not present themselves as a supervisor or participate in the recorded reflection process that some components require. And subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the International Baccalaureate: they are referenced and linked at ibo.org rather than reproduced or circulated, and a provider distributing bundles of them is indicating how it treats rules generally.

sections.heading: The three failure modes, and when each is still fixable
paragraphs: Internal assessment failures are few in kind and consistent across subjects. The first is a question that cannot produce what the criteria reward. In a science investigation that is an independent variable with two or three usable values, which cannot produce a graph and therefore leaves data analysis with little to assess. In a mathematics exploration it is a topic permitting only arithmetic. In economics it is an article containing a price rise and no economics. In history it is a question too broad for the word limit.

The second is data that cannot be collected. A science question requiring apparatus the school does not hold. A geography question needing fieldwork at a site the student cannot reach. A business project depending on an organisation that will not answer. A psychology replication that cannot be run ethically by a school student. All four of those look fine on paper and fail at the moment of collection, which in Diploma Year 2 is usually too late to change.

The third is criteria never read. A student writes a competent, interesting piece and discovers afterwards that reflection was a scored criterion they treated as a conclusion, or that evaluation was worth a quarter of the marks and received one paragraph. This is the most frustrating of the three because the work was good and the allocation was wrong, and it is entirely preventable by reading the criteria before drafting.

The timing of each failure determines what help is worth buying. All three are cheap to fix before drafting and expensive to fix after data collection. That is the argument for the single feasibility session per component, placed early: one session per subject in Diploma Year 1 costs a handful of hours in total and removes the majority of the crises that otherwise arrive together in the second year.

A kept version history, which makes drift visible

sections.heading: The draft record, and why it protects the student
paragraphs: Every session on an Internal Assessment produces a dated version of the student's own document with comments in its margin, and all versions are kept. That record has two uses. The first is practical: it makes drift visible. A research question that was narrowed in October and quietly broadened again by January shows up as a comparison rather than as a vague sense that the piece has lost focus.

The second use is protective and worth stating plainly. A version history showing a question narrowing over weeks, with comments that ask questions rather than supply answers, is evidence that the thinking was the student's. A single polished document that appeared in one week is not evidence of anything. Schools and boards do occasionally ask how a piece was produced, and a student with a version history is in a very different position from one without.

The comments themselves follow a convention that keeps the boundary clean: they are written as questions and criterion references rather than as corrections. 'Which criterion is this paragraph addressing?' 'Criterion E rewards mathematics at the level of the course — which part of the course does this use?' 'What was the dominant source of uncertainty here, and how do you know?' A student who answers those questions in writing has done the work. A student handed a corrected paragraph has not.

Parents receive the version history rather than a summary of it. Internal assessment is produced over weeks without a mark attached, which makes it the easiest part of the Diploma for a family to be reassured about and the hardest to verify. A dated file is the verification, and reading it takes five minutes.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi deadlines, ADEK, and who may help
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages found in this research, which is a notable omission on pages addressed to Abu Dhabi families, and it is the body whose framework the school's own policies sit inside.

The deadline structure a family actually has to work to is the school's rather than the board's. Abu Dhabi Diploma programmes set internal submission dates ahead of the IB's own upload schedule, they differ between schools, and they sometimes differ between subjects in the same school. Ask the IB coordinator for the full internal deadline schedule in writing at the start of each Diploma year. A student's recollection of an assembly is not a planning document, and the most common Internal Assessment emergency is a deadline that was known to the school and not to the family.

There is one rule specific to this emirate that families should know before arranging help. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported rather than read from ADEK's current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication before relying on it; the practical point is that the arrangement a parent might think of first may not be permitted.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated more generally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

sections.heading: What Internal Assessment support costs in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: This is among the cheapest interventions in the Diploma measured per mark available, because it is block-booked rather than held weekly. A feasibility session is one hour per component. A drafting block is three or four sessions per component, placed against the school's deadlines. A triage session covering two or three components at once is a single piece of work. Nothing here is a year-long weekly commitment, and a provider proposing one for Internal Assessment is proposing the wrong shape.

Published rates in this market, read in October 2026: EdFlik lists online tuition from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate rate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Internal assessment work needs criterion-referenced reading, which places it at the qualified band or above rather than at the budget tier.

Set against the weightings, the arithmetic is favourable. A science investigation carries twenty per cent of a subject grade and is produced without time pressure; four sessions at the qualified band is a small outlay against a fifth of a grade. The same four sessions spent on examination technique in the same subject would be a reasonable purchase too, and would address a smaller share of the grade with less certainty, because examination performance depends on the day and Internal Assessment does not.

The in-home comparison is the same as across this market: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. For Internal Assessment the online format is also the correct one, because the work is margin comments on a shared document and a kept version history, neither of which survives a visit and a paper draft. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

sections.heading: What to refuse, at any price
paragraphs: A completed Internal Assessment. One UAE-facing site advertises them at AED 3,750, and what is being sold is a malpractice finding with a seventeen-year-old's name on it. The Diploma itself is the exposure, not a grade in one subject. No framing makes this a reasonable purchase, and a provider offering it has told a family everything they need to know about everything else it offers.

A guaranteed mark or band. Internal assessment is marked by the school and moderated externally, and no provider controls either step. A promise about an Internal Assessment band is a sales position rather than a description of how the component is assessed. What can be committed to honestly is that a draft will be read against the published criteria and that the criterion it falls short of will be named.

An editing service. This is the dangerous one because it sounds legitimate. Editing a draft until the sentences are correct produces the editor's sentences, and the student submits work that is partly not theirs without anybody intending malpractice. The honest version is feedback written as questions and criterion references, with the student performing every rewrite, which is slower and produces a defensible piece of work.

A bundle of exemplar Internal Assessments. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and exemplar material belong to the International Baccalaureate, and circulating copies is both a copyright matter and, where the exemplars are used as templates, a route to work that is not the student's own. The legitimate version is referencing the official material and linking to ibo.org. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and operates no UAE office or centre.
