process.title: Send the six subjects and the school's internal deadlines
process.description: The useful opening message lists the six subjects with their levels and attaches the school's internal Internal Assessment deadline schedule, obtained in writing from the IB coordinator. Without the dates a drafting sequence cannot be planned, and the deadline is the one variable a family cannot change.

process.title: Build the one-page limits document
process.description: For each subject, what the Internal Assessment is, its limit, how many criteria it carries and what each is worth, confirmed against the current subject guide for that cohort. One hour of work, and it prevents more problems than any amount of later drafting advice.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken, no obligation. It is spent reading the student's current research question against the criteria for their subject and saying plainly whether it can produce what those criteria reward.

process.title: One feasibility session per component, early
process.description: Placed before drafting and before any apparatus, fieldwork or organisation access is committed. The written outcome is one of three things: proceed, narrow, or choose a different question. This is the single cheapest intervention available in the Diploma.

process.title: Drafting block against the school's dates
process.description: Three or four sessions per component, each reading the student's current version against the criteria and commenting in the margin of their own file as questions rather than corrections. Every version is kept and dated, and the student performs every rewrite.

process.title: Triage if several arrive at once
process.description: Where two or three components land together in Diploma Year 2, one session produces a written order of work, including the honest recommendation to submit something as it stands. That recommendation is sometimes the most valuable thing in the report.

whyPoints.title: Criteria named by letter and allocation
whyPoints.description: Every comment refers to a specific criterion and what it is worth, because that is the basis on which the mark is awarded. Competitor pages in this market discuss Internal Assessment at length and name not a single criterion, which leaves students with advice instead of a specification.

whyPoints.title: Feasibility before drafting, always
whyPoints.description: One session per component, early, testing whether the question can produce what the criteria reward and whether the data can actually be collected. Every Internal Assessment failure is cheap to fix at that point and expensive to fix afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Comments are questions, not corrections
whyPoints.description: Feedback is written as questions and criterion references in the margin of the student's own document, and the student performs every rewrite. Editing a draft until it reads well produces the editor's sentences, which is the line most easily crossed without anyone intending to.

whyPoints.title: Version history kept and dated
whyPoints.description: The record makes drift visible and demonstrates that the thinking was the student's. A question narrowing over weeks with questioning comments is evidence; a polished document that appeared in one week is not.

whyPoints.title: The limits document comes first
whyPoints.description: One page per student listing each subject's component, its limit and its criteria, confirmed against the current guide. Most Internal Assessment crises involve a limit or a criterion discovered late, and the page costs an hour.

whyPoints.title: Abu Dhabi specifics stated
whyPoints.description: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of the emirate's private schools, its professional-ethics rules restrict school staff from paid tutoring of their own students, and the school's internal deadlines bind a family rather than the board's. None of that appears on competitor pages addressed to this emirate.

faqs.question: What exactly is an IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: It is the internally assessed component of a Diploma subject, marked by the school and moderated externally, and it is a different task in every subject. The sciences require an individual scientific investigation with a 3,000-word ceiling and 24 marks across four criteria. Mathematics requires a written exploration with five criteria lettered A to E. Economics requires three commentaries of 800 words each on different syllabus units from different published news sources. History, psychology, geography and business management each set something different again. The shared name is the only thing these components have in common.

faqs.question: What share of an Abu Dhabi student.s subject grade does the IA decide?
faqs.answer: In the sciences and in mathematics it is typically twenty per cent, and in several other subjects it is higher. The figure matters because of what it is twenty per cent of: a fifth of a subject grade awarded for work produced over weeks without time pressure, in conditions the student controls. That makes it the most recoverable portion of the Diploma and also the easiest place to give marks away, because nothing about the process generates a warning until the piece is submitted. Confirm the exact weighting for each of your child's subjects against the current guide.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria for an IB science investigation?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six of twenty-four marks, with the component weighted at twenty per cent of the subject grade and a 3,000-word ceiling. Research design rewards a focused question with a genuinely variable independent quantity and properly controlled variables. Data analysis rewards correct processing, graphing and treatment of uncertainty. Conclusion rewards a reading of the results related to accepted science. Evaluation rewards identifying which source of uncertainty actually dominated, which requires the uncertainty work to have been done during collection.

faqs.question: Which five criteria is the maths exploration marked against, and what is each worth?
faqs.answer: Five, lettered A to E across twenty marks: A presentation, B mathematical communication, C personal engagement, D reflection and E use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation. The practical consequence is that topic choice is a mark decision rather than a matter of taste, because criterion E rewards mathematics commensurate with the course and a topic that permits only arithmetic caps the piece however well it is written. Personal engagement and reflection together carry a meaningful share, which stops a student treating both as decoration around the mathematics.

faqs.question: Why do IB Internal Assessment research questions fail?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, consistent across subjects. The question cannot produce what the criteria reward — an independent variable with two or three usable values cannot produce a graph, so data analysis has little to assess. The data cannot be collected, because the apparatus is not held, the fieldwork site is unreachable, the organisation will not answer or the replication cannot be run ethically. Or the criteria were never read, so a competent piece allocated one paragraph to a criterion worth a quarter of the marks. All three are cheap to fix before drafting and expensive afterwards.

faqs.question: Exactly what may a tutor do with an Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Read it and comment in its margin. Ask what the independent variable is, how many values will be tested, and whether the data will support the conclusion. Name the criterion a paragraph is failing and state what that criterion rewards. Teach the subject content or the statistical method the component needs. Mark the draft against the criteria and say what band it currently sits in. What a tutor may not do is supply text that appears in the submission, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the research question, perform the calculations, supply data or design the experiment.

faqs.question: Is paying someone to edit an IB Internal Assessment allowed?
faqs.answer: Treat an editing service as the dangerous option, because it sounds legitimate and is not. Editing a draft until the sentences are correct produces the editor's sentences, and the student then submits work that is partly not their own without anybody intending malpractice. The defensible version is feedback written as questions and criterion references, with the student performing every rewrite themselves. It is slower and it produces a piece that is theirs. Ask any provider to state in writing where their line sits, and be cautious of one that describes its service as polishing.

faqs.question: What happens if a submitted Internal Assessment is not the student's own work?
faqs.answer: The consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever supplied the help, and what is at stake is the Diploma itself rather than a grade in one subject. That asymmetry is the whole argument for the strict boundary. The market in this region contains providers selling exactly what is prohibited: one UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a premium service with a risk attached; it is a transfer of risk onto a seventeen-year-old, and no price makes it a reasonable purchase.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi Diploma student start their Internal Assessments?
faqs.answer: Most science and mathematics Internal Assessment work begins late in Diploma Year 1, and the useful intervention comes earlier than that. A single feasibility session per component, placed before any drafting, apparatus booking or fieldwork commitment, removes most of the crises that otherwise arrive together in Year 2. The other early act is administrative: ask the IB coordinator in writing for the school's internal deadline schedule, because those dates differ between schools and sometimes between subjects within a school, and they are the dates that actually bind a family.

faqs.question: Why does a dated draft history matter?
faqs.answer: For two reasons. It makes drift visible: a research question narrowed in October and quietly broadened by January shows up as a comparison rather than as a vague feeling that the piece has lost focus. And it protects the student. A version history showing a question narrowing over weeks, with comments that ask questions rather than supply answers, is evidence that the thinking was the student's own. A single polished document that appeared in one week is evidence of nothing, and schools and boards do occasionally ask how a piece was produced.

faqs.question: Who sets the Internal Assessment deadlines in an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: The school, ahead of the IB's own upload schedule, and the school's dates are the ones a family has to work to. They differ between schools in the emirate and sometimes between subjects within the same school, which is why they should be obtained in writing from the IB coordinator at the start of each Diploma year rather than inferred. The most common Internal Assessment emergency in this market is a deadline that was known to the school and not to the family, and a student's recollection of an assembly is not a planning document.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher help with their Internal Assessment privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask the school before arranging anything. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That information is press-reported rather than read from the authority's current policy document, so verify it against ADEK's own publication. The school supervisor relationship for an Internal Assessment is in any case the school's and separate from any paid arrangement.

faqs.question: What does Internal Assessment support cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is block-booked rather than weekly, which keeps the total small. A feasibility session is one hour per component. A drafting block is three or four sessions per component against the school's deadlines. Published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The work needs criterion-referenced reading, so it sits at the qualified band rather than the budget tier. Measured against a fifth of a subject grade, four sessions is a favourable outlay.

faqs.question: Does online Internal Assessment support work as well as someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For this component it works better. The work is comments in the margin of the student's own document with the subject guide's criteria visible alongside, and every version saved and dated. A kept version history is the thing that makes drift visible and that demonstrates the work was the student's, and it does not survive a home visit and a paper draft. The published cost difference also runs one way: AED 180-350 for qualified in-home work against AED 150-300 online. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for our subject's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: You should be told, because a substitution does real damage here. A tutor who has not taught the specific subject guide will not know its criteria or its limits, and criterion-referenced reading is the entire service. Niche components run short — Higher Level Further Mathematics, Music, Theatre, Global Politics, a Group 2 language — and the honest options are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

abu-dhabi/ib-internal-assessment-help.closingHeading: Build the one-page limits document first
abu-dhabi/ib-internal-assessment-help.closingBody: Before buying any Internal Assessment help, make the page nobody has: each of your child's six subjects, what its internally assessed component actually is, its word or page limit, how many criteria it carries and what each is worth, confirmed against the current subject guide. Then ask the IB coordinator in writing for the school's internal deadlines. Those two documents prevent most Internal Assessment crises and cost nothing but an hour. After that, one feasibility session per component, early, is the cheapest useful purchase in the whole Diploma.
